# Accordion

Accordion: stacked headings that each open to show their content.

Also asked as: collapsible, expand collapse, disclosure, expandable sections, faq.

**Import:** `import { Accordion } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Accordion/Accordion.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Accordion/Accordion.stories.jsx` — Styles, Behavior, InteractionStates, Content, Overview, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Expanded, Disabled, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Accordion/Accordion.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Accordion` when a page carries several long, independent sections and only
one of them matters at a time — a settings page, a FAQ, the optional detail
under a form. Each item is collapsed until asked for, so the page keeps its
shape and the headers stay a readable index of what is there.

It is uncontrolled by default: give it `defaultActiveKey` and it tracks the open
item itself. Pass `activeKey` and `onSelect` together to control it. `alwaysOpen`
lets more than one item stay open at once, and `flush` removes the outer border
and rounded corners when the accordion sits inside a card or panel. Use an accordion for several long, independent sections where only one matters at a time.

## Motion

Accordion reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Height and chevron move together, opening down from the header and collapsing back into it. A section uses spatial.default; closing is one speed faster. |

## Alternatives

- For switching between alternative views of the same content, use `Tabs`.

## Best practices

### Open one section at a time. {#open-one-section-at-a-time}

A stack answers one question at a time; leaving every item open turns it into a long page.

Do: One section open, the rest closed.
Don't: Every section open at once.

### Keep titles to a few words. {#keep-titles-to-a-few-words}

The title is the only thing visible when closed, so it has to name the content at a glance.

Do: A short noun title.
Don't: A title that runs on and wraps.

### Stack the items in one accordion. {#stack-the-items-in-one-accordion}

Items share borders so the group reads as one control.

Do: Items touch, borders shared.
Don't: Items spaced apart like separate cards.

### Author items with either `items` or `children`; `children` wins. {#author-items-with-either-items-or-children-children-wins}

```jsx
// Incorrect — the items array is dropped when children exist.
<Accordion items={sections}>
    <Accordion.Item eventKey="0" header="One">…</Accordion.Item>
</Accordion>

// Correct — pick one:
<Accordion items={sections} />
```

### Pass an array key when `alwaysOpen` is set. {#pass-an-array-key-when-alwaysopen-is-set}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with alwaysOpen and a string key, opening another item replaces the selection.
<Accordion alwaysOpen defaultActiveKey="0" items={sections} />

// Correct.
<Accordion alwaysOpen defaultActiveKey={['0']} items={sections} />
```

### Use `flush` inside another bordered surface. {#use-flush-inside-another-bordered-surface}

`flush` removes the outer border and corner radius so the item rows sit flat
against a bordered container such as a card. On the bare page, keep the default
border.

## Accessibility

- **Each header is a real button.** It carries `aria-expanded` and
  `aria-controls`, wrapped in a heading. Tab reaches every header; Enter and
  Space toggle; the heading list shows the whole index.
- **The body is associated with its header.** The panel's `role="region"` is
  labeled by the header that opened it, so a screen reader can jump straight
  to it, not just land there in document order.
- **Write `header` as a heading.** It becomes the text of a heading, so it is
  read both in place and in the heading list.
- **`disabled` is a real disabled button.** It leaves the tab order and a press
  never opens it. Say why in text inside or beside the item, never in a tooltip
  on the header. The body stays in the DOM, so omit the item if its content is
  not for this reader.
- **Focus stays on the header after a toggle.** Opening an item does not move
  focus into the body and does not scroll it into view, so the user keeps their
  place.

## Related

- `Tabs`: use when switching between mutually exclusive views of the same area.
- [Section](?path=/docs/templates-section--docs): use when every section should stay visible at once so people can compare them without opening and closing rows.

Same group: `Carousel` · `PageHeader` · `ScrollBar`

## Parts

1. **Trigger.** The full-width button: the section title on the left, the chevron on the right.
2. **Chevron.** Turns up when the section is open, so the state reads without the body.
3. **Body.** The content, shown under an open trigger.
4. **Edge.** One border round the group, with the card corner radius on the first and last item. `flush` drops it for a divider line.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Surface ground, subtle text, chevron down. |
| Hovered | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring with no fill change; see Border. |
| Expanded | `--ds-background-selected`, and `--ds-background-selected-hovered` under the pointer. The chevron turns up. |
| Disabled | The item is dimmed to `--ds-opacity-disabled`. The trigger is announced as disabled, leaves the tab order, and a press never opens it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger ground | `--ds-surface`; `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` and `-pressed` under the pointer; open, `--ds-background-selected` and `--ds-background-selected-hovered`. |
| Trigger and chevron | `--ds-text-subtle`; title in `--heading-sm`; chevron at `--icon-sm`. |
| Body | `--body-lg` on `--ds-surface`, `--ds-text-subtle`, with a `--ds-border` rule above it. |
| Edge | `--ds-border` at `--stroke-1`, corners `--card-radius`. |
| Padding | `--card-pad` on every side. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` wide and offset. |
| Disabled | `--ds-opacity-disabled`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the section with a short noun phrase: "Session notes". | Write a sentence or a question as the header. |
| Lead the body with the answer or the content itself. | Repeat the header as the first line of the body. |
| Keep sibling headers parallel: all nouns, all the same case. | Mix "Goals", "How do I set goals?" and "SETTINGS". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | arrayOf | `[]` | Array of accordion item configurations |
| `children` | node | — | Child AccordionItem components (alternative to items array) |
| `defaultActiveKey` | string or array | — | Initially expanded item(s) - single key or array for alwaysOpen |
| `activeKey` | string or array | — | Controlled active key(s) |
| `flush` | bool | `false` | Remove borders for seamless/flush appearance |
| `alwaysOpen` | bool | `false` | Allow multiple items to be open simultaneously |
| `onSelect` | func | — | Callback when active item changes |
| `className` | string | `''` | Additional CSS classes |
| `id` | string | — | HTML ID attribute |

## Sub-components

### `Accordion.Item`

Implemented as `AccordionItem`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `eventKey` | string (required) | — | Unique key for this accordion item |
| `header` | node (required) | — | Header content (title text or node) |
| `children` | node | — | Body content when expanded |
| `disabled` | bool | — | Disable this item |
| `className` | string | — | Additional CSS classes |

## Tokens touched

`--body-lg` · `--border-width-default` · `--card-pad` · `--card-radius` · `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` · `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` · `--ds-background-selected` · `--ds-background-selected-hovered` · `--ds-border` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast-duration` · `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-spatial-fast-duration` · `--ds-opacity-disabled` · `--ds-surface` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--heading-sm` · `--icon-sm`

From `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Accordion/Accordion.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

# AiChat

AI chat on a Frame: a floating action button at the bottom right of the Page opens chat as a popup; from there it moves to the Frame's Panel or to full screen. It takes the Frame's props and adds the chat. - The button is the one way in. It hides while chat is open in the Panel or full screen. - The mode is remembered for the tab in sessionStorage (and an open Panel). - Under 768 the popup is shown full screen. - The conversation moves with the mode and is kept for the tab (the last 50 messages, under `${storageKey}-messages`), so a reload keeps it. There is no backend: `respond(text, history)` returns the reply, `history` being the turns before it as `{ role, text }`. A reply is text, or `{ text, sources }`: the pages or records it drew on list under it.

Also asked as: chat, assistant, chatbot, conversation.

**Import:** `import { AiChat } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiChat/AiChat.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiChat/AiChat.stories.jsx` — Overview, Popup, PanelMode, Fullscreen, Interactive, SwitchingModes, ConversationFollowsTheMode, RemembersThePanel, RemembersFullscreenClosed, PopupIsFullScreenUnder768, PopupStaysAPopupAt768, HeaderControls, ModalLeavesThePopupOpen, TrustMarks, RepliesWithSources, DocsAgent, DocsAgentFallback

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiChat/AiChat.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use AI chat to ask about the current page. Choose a mode for the task.

| Mode | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Popup | The default. A quick ask that keeps the page in view. |
| Panel | Ongoing work beside the page. The Frame docks it, or floats it over the Page when there is no room. |
| Full screen | Long answers that need room. It covers the window. |

Follow the six AI interaction guidelines for identity, answer marking, fallibility, sources, confirmation and feedback.
Call the chat "AI chat". Return `{ text, sources }` from `respond` for answers
based on records; `linkTarget` controls where source links open. `onFeedback`
receives the reply and its rating, which persists across modes.

### In the Storybook docs

The docs' floating button has an AI chat action that opens chat; the docs' chat keeps its mode under its own `storageKey`.
Set `launcher={false}` to omit chat's own button; the popup floats above the bottom right corner.

The docs answerer uses a server-side function grounded in the design-system index.
Credentials stay on the server. On errors or rate limits, it searches site pages
and the component index and names that fallback.

## Motion

AiChat reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |

## Best practices

### Use the popup for quick asks. {#use-the-popup-for-quick-asks}

A popup keeps the page in view. For ongoing work it covers the page and loses context: move it to the Panel.

### Use the Panel beside the page. {#use-the-panel-beside-the-page}

The Panel docks next to the work. For a quick ask it takes more room than the question needs.

### Use full screen for long work. {#use-full-screen-for-long-work}

Full screen gives long answers room. A docked Panel squeezes them.

### Mark every answer. {#mark-every-answer}

Do: Each reply is an AI message, led by the AI icon.
Don't: A reply in plain text reads as a person's.

### Say fallibility once. {#say-fallibility-once}

Do: One line, under the prompt input.
Don't: The line repeated under every reply turns into noise.

### List the sources an answer drew on. {#list-the-sources-an-answer-drew-on}

Do: The records the answer read, listed under it.
Don't: An answer from records with nothing to check it against.

## Accessibility

- The button is named by `title`, AI chat by default, and so is the Panel's complementary landmark unless `panelLabel` names it.
- The conversation is a log that announces new messages politely.
- Every reply carries one AI icon named "AI", so no answer reads as a person's to a screen reader.
- The thumbs are a group named "Rate this answer". A rated thumb is pressed, and a status line confirms the rating.
- The popup without the button (`launcher={false}`) takes focus in its prompt input on open, and Escape closes it.
- Full screen is a dialog named by `title`, and focus moves into it.

## Related

- Frame places the Panel the chat docks in.
- A Panel never draws a Blanket: it docks beside the Page or floats over it, and the Page stays in view.
- For one reply on its own, use `AiMessage`.
- For the field alone, use `PromptInput`; for suggested prompts, `PromptStarters`.

Same group: `AiIcon` · `AiMessage` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptInput` · `PromptStarters` · `Suggestion`

## Parts

1. **Button.** A primary circle Icon button with the AI icon, at the bottom right of the Page. It is the one way in, and it hides while chat is open in the Panel or full screen.
2. **Header.** The AI icon, the title and the controls: clear chat, switch mode (popup and Panel trade places), full screen, more and close.
3. **Conversation.** The person's messages on the sunken fill, and each reply as an AI message with its sources and thumbs.
4. **Prompt starters** (optional). Offered while the conversation is empty, from `starters`.
5. **Prompt input.** Where the person writes. While a reply is coming, its send button becomes Stop.
6. **Fallibility line.** One line under the prompt input.

The same surface fills every mode; the mode only changes which header controls show and where the surface sits.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Closed | Only the button shows. |
| Popup | The popup opens anchored to the button, over the Page. The button stays. |
| Panel | Chat docks in the Frame's Panel, or floats over the Page. The button hides. |
| Full screen | Chat covers the window, in a column capped at the reading width. The button hides. |
| Replying | A typing indicator stands in for the reply, and the prompt input's send button becomes Stop. |

Hover, pressed, focus and disabled belong to the Icon buttons in the header and the button, and are described on the Icon button page. Clear chat is disabled while the conversation is empty.

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Button | `--ai-chat-fab-size` square, `--page-pad` from the Page's bottom and right edges, `--ds-shadow-overlay`. |
| Popup | `--ai-chat-width` wide and `--ai-chat-height` high; without the button it floats `--stack-md` above where the button would be. |
| Floating popup fill | `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--popup-radius`. |
| Full screen | `--ds-surface`, on `--layer-dialog`; the conversation is capped at `--content-max-width-reading`. |
| Conversation | `--stack-md` between messages, `--body-default` in `--ds-text`. |
| The person's message | `--ds-surface-sunken`, `--pad-y-sm` by `--pad-x-md`, `--radius-md`. |
| Empty state and fallibility line | `--ds-text-subtle`; the line at `--body-sm`. |
| Footer | `--stack-sm` between the starters, the input and the line. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Call it AI chat, with the AI icon. | A persona name or an avatar. |
| Short starters that say what they ask: "Summarize this page". | Starters that are whole paragraphs. |
| Say "AI can make mistakes. Check important info." once, under the prompt input. | A warning on each message. |
| Name a source by its record: "Session notes, Oct 24". | Bare links or ids. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `defaultMode` | oneOf | `'popup'` | The mode a tab with nothing remembered starts in. |
| `defaultOpen` | bool | `false` | Whether chat starts open when the tab has nothing remembered. |
| `storageKey` | string | `AI_CHAT_STORAGE_KEY` | The sessionStorage key the mode and the conversation are kept under (the Storybook docs' chat passes its own); null keeps nothing. |
| `launcher` | bool | `true` | `false` leaves out the floating button: the popup then floats above the bottom right corner, and the host opens chat with `useAiChat().dispatch({ type: 'open' })`. |
| `linkTarget` | string | — | Where a reply's links and source links open, such as `_top` from inside a frame. |
| `resolveHref` | func | — | Rewrites a link's address in a reply's text: `(href) => href`, such as a page named by its title. |
| `onModeChange` | func | — | Called with the new mode whenever chat moves between popup, Panel and full screen. |
| `respond` | func | — | Returns the reply (or a promise of it) to a sent message: a string, or `{ text, sources: [{ title, href, type }] }`. Without it nothing answers. |
| `onFeedback` | func | — | Called with the answer and `{ rating }` (or `{ rating: 'down', comment }`) when a person rates it. Every answer offers thumbs. |
| `starters` | arrayOf | — | `{ id, label, text }` prompts offered in the empty conversation, under its opening line. |
| `title` | string | `'AI chat'` | The chat's name: the header title, the button's label and the Panel landmark. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Ask anything'` | The prompt input's placeholder: what this chat can be asked about. Keep it to one line. |
| `emptyText` | string | `'Ask about what you are working on.'` | The line an empty conversation opens with, above the starters. |
| `panelLabel` | string | — | Overrides the Panel landmark's name; defaults to `title`. |
| `children` | node | — | The Page content. |

## Variants

**`defaultMode`** — `popup` · `panel` · `fullscreen`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--ai-chat-fab-size` · `--ai-chat-height` · `--ai-chat-width` · `--body-default` · `--body-sm` · `--content-max-width-reading` · `--ds-shadow-overlay` · `--ds-surface` · `--ds-surface-overlay` · `--ds-surface-sunken` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--layer-dialog` · `--layer-navigation` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-y-sm` · `--page-pad` · `--popup-radius` · `--radius-md` · `--stack-lg` · `--stack-md` · `--stack-sm`

From `design-system/src/components/ai/AiChat/AiChat.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

entries.name: AiIcon

# AiIcon

An icon for an AI action: generate, ask, rewrite, summarize, plan, suggest or stop generating. Each icon with a sparkle mark is a Font Awesome Free glyph with one four-point sparkle in its top-right corner and a clean gap cut around it. Generate is the sparkle alone, and stop generating has none because stopping is not generative. - **name** picks the icon. - **size** is 16 (the default) or 24. Generate and stop generating also have 12. Asking another icon for 12 draws it at 16 and warns. - **label** names the icon for assistive technology. Without it the icon is hidden, so pair it with visible text. The shapes fill with `currentColor`, which starts at the icon color; set `color` to change it. Pair every icon with a label unless its meaning is obvious.

**Import:** `import { AiIcon } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiIcon/AiIcon.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiIcon/AiIcon.stories.jsx` — AllIcons, CloseUp, Labeled, Color, Interactive, Rest

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiIcon/AiIcon.mdx`

## Usage

Use `AiIcon` for AI actions. For other actions, use a plain Font Awesome Free glyph.

## Best practices

### Pair it with visible text, or give it a `label`. {#pair-it-with-visible-text-or-give-it-a-label}

Without `label` the icon is hidden from assistive technology.

Do: The icon beside the verb it stands for.
Don't: A bare icon with no text and no label, so it has no name.

### Pick `name` from the set. {#pick-name-from-the-set}

`generate`, `ask`, `rewrite`, `summarize`, `plan`, `suggest` and `stop-generating`.

Do: One icon for each action it names.
Don't: One icon reused for different actions.

### Use it for AI actions only. {#use-it-for-ai-actions-only}

An AI icon marks something generative. Use a plain Font Awesome icon for an action that is not.

Do: The sparkle marks something generative.
Don't: The sparkle on an action that is not AI.

## Accessibility

- **Labeled or hidden.** With `label` the icon is `role="img"` named by it. Without, it is `aria-hidden`.
- **Color follows the text.** It fills with `currentColor`, so it keeps contrast with its surroundings.

## Related

- For any non-AI icon, use a Font Awesome Free glyph.
- For the border that shows generation in progress, use `GenerativeBorder`.

Same group: `AiChat` · `AiMessage` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptInput` · `PromptStarters` · `Suggestion`

## Parts

1. **Glyph.** A Font Awesome Free shape for the action: generate, ask, rewrite, summarize, plan, suggest or stop generating.
2. **Sparkle.** One four-point sparkle at the top right, with a gap cut around it. Generate is the sparkle alone; stop generating has none.
3. **Size.** 12 (generate and stop generating only), 16 or 24.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. An icon is a picture, not a control. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused, disabled | None. Put the icon inside a button, which carries them. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill | `currentColor`, starting at `--ds-icon`. |
| Size | A square box of exactly its size: `--icon-sm` (12), `--icon-md` (16) and `--icon-lg` (24). |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Pair the icon with the verb: "Summarize". | An icon alone for an action that is not obvious. |
| Use the icon that names the action. | Reuse one icon for a different action. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | oneOf | `'generate'` | Which action the icon stands for. |
| `size` | enum | `16` | The icon's size in px. 12 exists for generate and stop-generating only. |
| `label` | string | — | An accessible name. Without it the icon is hidden from assistive technology. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

## Variants

**`name`** — `generate` · `ask` · `rewrite` · `summarize` · `plan` · `suggest` · `stop-generating`

**`size`** — `12` · `16` · `24`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--ds-icon` · `--icon-lg` · `--icon-md` · `--icon-sm`

From `design-system/src/components/ai/AiIcon/AiIcon.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

# AiMessage

An assistant reply, marked as AI by the small AI icon at its start (named "AI" for assistive technology), so no answer reads as a person's. Text is Markdown: paragraphs, lists, headings, code, bold, italic and links. The content is `text`, or `parts` when a reply mixes text with other content: a part is `{ type: 'text', text }` or any other `{ type, ... }`, which `renderPart` draws. - `status="complete"` is a finished message. - `status="streaming"` is text still arriving: a caret follows the last character and the message is marked busy for assistive technology. - `status="thinking"` is the typing indicator, before any text exists. `sources` lists what a finished answer read, folded under the message behind one toggle: the answer links what it names in its own text, so the list is there to check, not to read. `onFeedback` puts thumbs up and down under a finished answer; `feedback` holds the rating when the page owns it.

**Import:** `import { AiMessage } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiMessage/AiMessage.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiMessage/AiMessage.stories.jsx` — Message, Streaming, TypingIndicator, TypedOut, WithParts, Interactive, WithSources, WithMarkdown, WithFeedback

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/AiMessage/AiMessage.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · ready `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.ai.ready` · strong `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.ai.strong` · refine `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.ai.refine`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `AiMessage` for every AI reply, in chat, a panel or elsewhere. Choose its
status from the table below.

### Status guidance

| Status | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Thinking | From the moment a message is sent until the first text arrives. The typing indicator, with no text. |
| Streaming | While text arrives. A caret follows the last character, and the message is busy for assistive technology. |
| Complete | The default: a finished reply. Only a complete reply shows its sources and its thumbs. |

## Motion

AiMessage reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Load content | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Sources fade in place 20 ms apart, each tied to real work; the answer streams in chunks with no fade. |  |
| ready | Load content | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Feedback fades in over its Spinner. | `sound.ai.ready` on land: the feedback took over 1 s, so a Spinner showed |
| strong | Load content | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Strong feedback fades in over its Spinner. | `sound.ai.strong` on land: the feedback took over 1 s, so a Spinner showed |
| refine | Load content | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Refine feedback fades in over its Spinner. | `sound.ai.refine` on land: the feedback took over 1 s, so a Spinner showed |

## Best practices

### Stream the answer, then settle. {#stream-the-answer-then-settle}

Keep progress visible rather than leaving a blank; follow the status sequence
in Usage.

Do: The typing indicator, then the streaming state, shows the answer arriving.
Don't: Partial text shown as finished hides that it is still being written.

### List the sources whenever an answer draws on records. {#list-the-sources-whenever-an-answer-draws-on-records}

An answer built from sessions, students or reports passes them as `sources`,
so a person can open what the AI read. A general answer that read nothing
shows no list.

Do: The records the answer read, listed under it.
Don't: An answer from records with nothing to open.

### Offer feedback on every finished answer. {#offer-feedback-on-every-finished-answer}

Pass `onFeedback` for every answer; feedback appears only at `complete`, so
partial replies cannot be rated. See AI feedback
for rating changes and the optional, skippable comment.

Do: Thumbs under a finished answer.
Don't: A finished answer with no way to rate it.

## Accessibility

- **Marked as AI.** The AI icon at the start of every reply is an image named
  "AI", so a screen reader hears whose answer it is. Don't add a second icon
  beside the message.
- **Sources and feedback.** See AI sources
  for list naming and toggle semantics, and AI feedback
  for rating names, pressed states, focus and announcements.
- **Busy while arriving.** A streaming message is marked `aria-busy`, so a
  screen reader waits for the finished text. A typed-out reply carries its full
  text for assistive technology and hides the character-by-character copy.
- **Announced indicator.** The typing indicator is a status named "AI is writing";
  its visual marks are hidden from assistive technology.
- **Reduced motion.** The caret and progress indicator stop animating, and typed-out text
  shows at once.

## Related

- `AiChat`, which shows every reply in an `AiMessage`.
- `PromptInput`, which sends the message.
- AI sources and AI feedback, which sit under a finished reply.

Same group: `AiChat` · `AiIcon` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptInput` · `PromptStarters` · `Suggestion`

## Parts

1. **AI icon.** The small AI icon at 16, named "AI", centered on the first line, so no answer reads as a person's.
2. **Text.** The body style, keeping the reply's line breaks. With `parts`, text parts and other parts in order; `renderPart` draws a part that is not text.
3. **Caret.** Streaming only: a thin bar after the last character, blinking.
4. **Progress indicator.** Thinking only: three pulsing marks in place of the text.
5. **Sources** (optional). Complete only: a counted "Sources" toggle, closed by default, with linked titles and types inside.
6. **Feedback** (optional). Complete only, with `onFeedback`: thumbs up and down and a quiet thanks beside them.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Complete | The text, then the sources and the thumbs when they are passed. With `typeOut`, the text types out character by character (`TypingText` takes `speed`, in milliseconds per character, and `onComplete`). `linkTarget` sets where links open, such as `_top` from inside a frame, and `resolveHref` rewrites a link's address. |
| Streaming | A caret follows the last character, and the message carries `aria-busy`. No sources and no thumbs yet. |
| Thinking | The typing indicator, a status named "AI is writing", in place of the text. |
| Reduced motion | The caret and progress indicator stop animating, and typed-out text shows at once. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`. |
| Icon to text | `--inline-md`; the icon centers on the first line against `--icon-md`. |
| Between parts | `--stack-md`. |
| Progress indicator | `--ds-text-subtle`, `--radius-full`, `--stack-sm` apart. |
| Caret and progress indicator motion | `--ds-motion-loop`, with its three marks offset by a quarter and a half cycle. |
| Sources | Heading `--heading-xxs` in `--ds-text-subtle`; type `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`; rows `--stack-sm` apart. |
| Feedback | Thanks `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`; buttons `--inline-sm` apart. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name a source by its record: "Session notes, Oct 24", with its type, "Session". | Name a source by its address. |
| Put a table or a list the reply needs in a part that `renderPart` draws. | Draw a table out of characters inside the text. |
| Let the AI icon mark the reply. | Add a second icon beside the message. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | — | A single text reply; shorthand for one text part. |
| `parts` | arrayOf | — | Parts of a reply, in order: `{ type: 'text', text }` or another `{ type }` that `renderPart` draws. |
| `status` | enum | `'complete'` | `complete` is finished, `streaming` is text still arriving, `thinking` is the typing indicator. |
| `typeOut` | bool | `false` | Types a finished text out character by character, as a reply that has just arrived. |
| `renderPart` | func | — | Draws a part that is not text: `(part, index) => node`. |
| `sources` | arrayOf | — | What a finished answer read: one `{ title, href, type }` per source, listed under the message. |
| `linkTarget` | string | — | Where the reply's links and its source links open, such as `_top` from inside a frame. |
| `resolveHref` | func | — | Rewrites a link's address in the reply's text: `(href) => href`, such as a docs page named by its title. |
| `onFeedback` | func | — | Thumbs up and down under a finished answer: called with `{ rating }`, or `{ rating: 'down', comment }`. |
| `feedback` | enum | — | The rating, when the page owns it: `up`, `down` or null. |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`status`** — `complete` · `streaming` · `thinking`

**`feedback`** — `up` · `down`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--ai-message-caret-width` · `--ai-message-dot-size` · `--body-default` · `--body-sm` · `--code-default` · `--ds-background-neutral` · `--ds-motion-loop` · `--ds-motion-loop-duration` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--heading-xs` · `--icon-md` · `--inline-md` · `--inline-sm` · `--pad-x-lg` · `--pad-x-sm` · `--pad-x-xs` · `--pad-y-md` · `--plus-ai-message-caret` · `--plus-ai-message-dot` · `--radius-full` · `--radius-md` · `--radius-sm` · `--stack-md` · `--stack-sm`

From `design-system/src/components/ai/AiMessage/AiMessage.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Avatar

A person or an agent shown as a picture, initials or an icon. The picture wins when it loads, then the initials, then the icon, then a plain person glyph.

Also asked as: user photo, initials, profile image, user picture, tutor photo, student photo.

**Import:** `import { Avatar } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Avatar/Avatar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Avatar/Avatar.stories.jsx` — Initials, Sizes, DefaultSize, Shapes, Fallbacks, Colors, Status, Naming, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Avatar/Avatar.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Avatar` for a person's or an agent's profile picture, initials or icon
wherever they are named in a row, a thread or a list of attendees. Circles
represent people; squares represent teams and agents.

## Alternatives

- For a short set of people that would crowd a line, use `AvatarGroup`.
- For a school or tool or lesson in a square frame, use `Tile`.
- For a workflow state or condition beside a name, use `StatusTag`.

## Best practices

### Use a circle for people and a square for teams and agents. {#use-a-circle-for-people-and-a-square-for-teams-and-agents}

Keep one shape per kind within a list, so the shape tells a person from an
agent at a glance.

Do: A circle for a person, a square for an agent.
Don't: A person in a square and an agent in a circle.

### Keep the name beside bare initials. {#keep-the-name-beside-bare-initials}

Two people can share initials. The name tells them apart, so drop it only where
the person is already named nearby.

### Let `AvatarGroup` set the size and shape in a stack. {#let-avatargroup-set-the-size-and-shape-in-a-stack}

`AvatarGroup` passes its `size` and `shape` to every child avatar so the row
stays even.

```jsx
<AvatarGroup label="Session attendees" max={5}>
    {people.map((p) => <Avatar key={p.id} name={p.name} src={p.photo} />)}
</AvatarGroup>
```

### Use color for a category, never a status. {#use-color-for-a-category-never-a-status}

Keep one color per kind of person, or leave avatars blue. Green, yellow and red belong to the presence dot, so a green avatar reads as "online".

Do: One color for all people, or one per kind.
Don't: Green and yellow read as online and away.

### Show presence only where it helps. {#show-presence-only-where-it-helps}

Use the dot in a list a person scans for who is around. Leave it off a byline or a comment, where presence is not the question.

Do: The dot in a list that is scanned for who is around.
Don't: A dot on a tiny byline, where presence is not the question.

## Accessibility

- **Decorative by default.** An avatar with no `name` or `label` is hidden from
  assistive technology (`aria-hidden="true"`), for use beside a name that
  already says who it is.
- **A name makes it one image.** With a `name` or `label` it becomes
  `role="img"` with that name. A `status` is added to the name ("Jane Park,
  online"), since the dot's color alone says nothing to a screen reader.
- **Not a control.** An avatar has no hover or focus state of its own. To make
  one clickable, wrap it in a button or link that carries the name.

## Related

- `AvatarGroup`: use when overlapping a row of avatars and folding overflow into a `+n` menu.
- `Sidebar`: use when showing the signed-in person with a name and role in the account row.
- `Tile`: use when framing a school, tool or lesson in a square.

Same group: `AvatarGroup` · `Icon` · `Illustration` · `Image` · `Object` · `Tile`

## Parts

1. **Face.** The picture when it loads; otherwise the initials, then the icon, then a plain person glyph.
2. **Frame.** A circle for a person; a square for a team or an agent, with a radius of a quarter of its size.
3. **Presence dot.** Optional, a quarter of the avatar's size at the bottom right, ringed in the surface color.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. The ground and ink come from the Tag color set; a picture covers them. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. An avatar is a picture, not a control; wrap it in a button or link for a click. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A person is never dimmed; a state for the account belongs in the name or the page. |
| Presence | The dot takes the success, warning, danger or neutral bold fill for online, away, busy and offline. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Size | `--image-xxs` to `--image-lg` for 16 to 40; 96 and 128 are built from the large spacing primitives. |
| Ground and ink | `--ds-background-accent-blue-subtler` and `--ds-text-accent-blue` for blue, and the same pair for each other Tag color. |
| Radius | `--radius-full` for a circle; a quarter of the size for a square, capped at `--radius-xxl`. |
| Presence dot | `--ds-background-success-bold`, `-warning-bold`, `-danger-bold`, `-neutral-bold`; ring `--ds-surface`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use the person's full name: "Jane Park". | Initials alone, or a nickname, where a full name is known. |
| Name an agent by its job: "Study bot". | A generic "Bot" or "AI". |
| Write a `label` that says who or what it is. | "Avatar" or "Profile picture", which says nothing about whom. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `src` | string | — | The picture's URL. If it is missing or fails to load, the initials show. |
| `name` | string | — | The person's or agent's name. Gives the initials and, unless `label` is set, the accessible name. |
| `initials` | string | — | Overrides the initials taken from `name`. |
| `icon` | string or node | — | The fallback when there is no picture and no initials: a Font Awesome Free name (`robot`), a class list, or a node. Defaults to `user`. |
| `size` | enum | `32` | 16 to 40 follow the Media sizes; 96 and 128 are for profiles. |

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# AvatarGroup

A row of avatars that overlap, with the rest behind a `+n`. The group owns what one avatar cannot: the overlap, the ring that separates neighbors, and how many fit. Past `max`, the remaining people go into a menu under `+n`, the same overflow the tag group uses, so every person stays reachable by name.

**Import:** `import { AvatarGroup } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/AvatarGroup/AvatarGroup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/AvatarGroup/AvatarGroup.stories.jsx` — Group, GroupFits, Sizes, GroupSizeAndShape, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/AvatarGroup/AvatarGroup.mdx`

## Usage

Use `AvatarGroup` for a short set of people that would crowd a line: the
attendees of a session, the members of a team. Past `max`, the rest fold into
a `+n` menu, reachable by name.

## Alternatives

- For a single person or agent with room to name each person beside their picture, use `Avatar`.
- For the signed-in person with a name and a role, use `Sidebar`.

## Best practices

### Let the group set the size and shape. {#let-the-group-set-the-size-and-shape}

`AvatarGroup` passes its `size` and `shape` to every `Avatar` child, so the
row stays even even when a child sets its own.

Do: The group sets one size and shape for every child.
Don't: Children that set their own size and shape, which the group ignores.

### Count the `+n` slot inside `max`. {#count-the-n-slot-inside-max}

Five people with `max={5}` show all five; a sixth pushes one into the overflow
slot — `max` is the most slots the row ever shows, the `+n` included.

Do: Three people fit in the cap with no +n.
Don't: A fourth person shows two avatars and +n, because the +n takes a slot.

### Keep the group short. {#keep-the-group-short}

Use it for a handful of people. For a roster, link to the list instead of folding sixty names behind `+n`.

Do: A handful, with the rest behind the +n.
Don't: Folding most of a roster behind +n: link to the list instead.

## Accessibility

- **Name the group.** `label` names the group for assistive technology —
  "Session attendees" — the same way `Avatar`'s `label` names a person.
- **The `+n` is a named button.** It announces the count of hidden people and
  opens a menu of their names, reached with Tab and closed with Escape.
- **Every shown avatar keeps its own name.** The group changes `size` and
  `shape`, never an avatar's accessible name.

## Related

- `Avatar`: use when configuring each child avatar's name, picture, initials or fallback.
- `Popup`: use when building a custom anchored overlay outside an avatar stack.

Same group: `Avatar` · `Icon` · `Illustration` · `Image` · `Object` · `Tile`

## Parts

1. **Avatars.** Up to `max`; when people overflow, `max` minus one plus the `+n`. Each takes the group's size and shape, overlapping by a quarter.
2. **Ring.** A surface-colored ring around each avatar that separates neighbors.
3. **Overflow.** A gray `+n` button that opens a menu of the people left out, by name.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Overlapping avatars; the `+n` in `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler`. |
| Hovered | The `+n` takes `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtle`. The avatars do not change. |
| Pressed | Opens the menu and sets `aria-expanded`. Escape closes it. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the `+n` for keyboard focus; see Border. |
| Disabled | None. With nothing to fold there is no `+n`, only pictures. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Avatar size | `--image-xxs` to `--image-lg`, from the group's `size`. |
| Overlap | A quarter of the avatar size. |
| Overflow fill | `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler`; hovered `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtle`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the group for what it holds: "Session attendees". | "Avatars" or "People", which names the picture, not the set. |
| Let `+n` count only the people left out. | Write your own count in the label; it will drift from the menu. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | `Avatar` elements. |
| `max` | number | `5` | The most avatars on the row, counting the `+n`. Default 5. |
| `size` | oneOf | `32` | One size for the whole row; it overrides each avatar's own. |
| `shape` | oneOf | `'circle'` | One shape for the whole row. |
| `label` | string | — | Names the group for assistive technology: "Session attendees". |
| `overflowLabel` | func | — | Formats the overflow's visible text. Defaults to `+n`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the group element beside the component's own. |

## Variants

**`size`** — `16` · `24` · `32` · `40` · `96` · `128`

**`shape`** — `circle` · `square`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Banner

Banner: a prominent message at the top of a page. No dismiss and no side stripe — the caller mounts and unmounts it, and meaning comes from the fill and the icon alone.

Also asked as: announcement, top of page, system message, outage.

**Import:** `import { Banner } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Page (`ds guide page`)

**Governed by:** Errors (`ds guide errors`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Warning, Danger, Announcement, WithoutIcon, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Banner/Banner.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.default` · exit `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Banner` for a condition that applies to the whole page, for as long as it
holds: scheduled maintenance, an outage, an account-wide notice. It has no
timeout and no dismiss, so only mount it while the condition is true.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Warning | The default, cautionary form. Example: "Scheduled maintenance begins tonight." |
| Danger | Something that needs immediate attention, such as an outage. |
| Announcement | A general notice with nothing wrong. No icon and no severity. |

## Motion

Banner reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | Pushes the page down, then fades in. |
| exit | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades, then the page closes the gap. |

## Alternatives

- For a message scoped to one region of the page that stays until resolved or dismissed, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a timed confirmation that something already happened, use `Flag`.
- For a short note tied to one control or field, use `Popup` or `Tooltip`.

## Best practices

### Use the danger banner only when action is needed now. {#use-the-danger-banner-only-when-action-is-needed-now}

Routine news belongs in an announcement.

Do: Danger for a canceled session.
Don't: Danger for a feature announcement.

### Show one banner at a time. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time}

Stacked banners compete and push the page down.

Do: A single announcement.
Don't: A warning and a danger banner stacked.

### Keep it to one line. {#keep-it-to-one-line}

A banner is read at a glance; long copy belongs on the page.

Do: One short sentence.
Don't: A paragraph in the banner.

## Accessibility

- **Announced as a status.** The banner's role is `status`, so assistive
  technology reports its content without interrupting the current task.
- **Severity needs more than color.** `warning` and `danger` pair their fill
  with a leading icon, but the icon is decorative, so say the severity in the
  words of the message. Only `announcement` relies on fill alone, which suits
  a notice with no severity.
- **No focus trap.** A banner never captures focus or keyboard navigation; it
  sits in the page's reading order like any other content.
- **A banner link takes focus like any link.** It shows the focus ring and
  its text names the destination.

## Related

- `Link`: use when embedding an inline action or destination inside the banner message.
- Frame: use when placing a site-wide banner above the application layout.

Same group: `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Icon.** Leading glyph for `warning` and `danger`; `announcement` has none.
2. **Message.** Short text that fits on one line. A link inside inherits the banner's text color and is underlined, so it stays visible on every fill.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Fill and text per appearance. |
| Hovered | Not a control, so nothing changes. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes; there is no pressed layer. |
| Focused | Tab skips the banner; a link inside shows the focus ring. |
| Disabled | Not supported. Unmount the banner once the condition clears. |
| Truncated | Not supported. Keep the message short enough to fit. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Warning | `--ds-background-warning`, `--ds-text-warning`, `--ds-icon-warning` |
| Danger | `--ds-background-danger`, `--ds-text-danger`, `--ds-icon-danger` |
| Announcement | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--ds-text` |
| Message | `--body-default`; a link at `--type-weight-medium` |
| Padding, gap | `--pad-y-md`, `--pad-x-md`, `--inline-md` |
| Icon | `--icon-md` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use concise, scannable language that states the problem. | Write a long message; there is no way to expand it. |
| Say the severity, what is affected and what to do. | Leave out what the person should do next. |
| Own the problem when it is ours: "We lost the connection." | Blame the person: "Something is wrong with your connection." |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `appearance` | enum | `'warning'` | `warning` (default form), `danger` (critical, needs immediate attention) or `announcement` (general, no icon). |
| `icon` | string or node or enum | — | A Font Awesome Free solid glyph name or a node. `false` removes the appearance's default icon. |
| `children` | node (required) | — | Message content. Typically text, optionally with a link. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `warning` · `danger` · `announcement`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--body-default` · `--ds-background-danger` · `--ds-background-neutral` · `--ds-background-warning` · `--ds-icon-danger` · `--ds-icon-warning` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-danger` · `--ds-text-warning` · `--icon-md` · `--inline-md` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-y-md` · `--type-weight-medium`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Breadcrumb

Universal element component for navigation breadcrumbs. / /* `items` defaults to `[]` even though its prop type is `isRequired`. A required prop is a lint, not a guarantee: React renders anyway, and `items.map` on `undefined` took the whole page down rather than the one breadcrumb. Found by `DocumentedContract.stories.jsx`, and only once this component's page gained a Usage tab: the guard renders each DOCUMENTED prop against fabricated required props, and it cannot fabricate an `arrayOf(shape)`. So documenting `separator` is what first rendered a Breadcrumb with no items, and the crash had been reachable by any caller all along.

Also asked as: path, navigation trail.

**Import:** `import { Breadcrumb } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Page (`ds guide page`)

**Governed by:** Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb.stories.jsx` — Standard, Short, Overview, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Breadcrumb/Breadcrumb.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Breadcrumb` when a page sits inside a hierarchy the user needs to see and
climb — a student inside a cohort inside a program, a lesson inside a unit. It
answers two questions at once: where am I, and what is one level up. When the
hierarchy is one level deep, a single "Back to X" `Link` says the same thing
with less furniture.

It takes a single `items` array, ordered root first. Each item is `{ text, href,
onClick }`. The last item is the current page and is rendered as plain text; every
item before it is a link.

## Motion

Breadcrumb reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Arrives with its page, one level longer; its row opens from its seam once, at Drill depth 1. |
| exit | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Leaves with its page. |

## Alternatives

- For progress through a sequence of steps, use `ProgressTracker`.
- For moving between sibling views of the same subject, use `Tabs`.
- For a persistent hierarchy the user browses rather than retraces, use `Sidebar`.

## Best practices

### End the trail on the current page. {#end-the-trail-on-the-current-page}

```jsx
// Incorrect — the href is dropped. The last item is rendered active
// unconditionally, and an active item is plain text with aria-current="page",
// never an anchor.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026', href: '/cohorts/a26' },
]} />

// Correct — the trail ends at where you are.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### Pass `href` alongside `onClick` on ancestor items. {#pass-href-alongside-onclick-on-ancestor-items}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no href the item is rendered active, which means it is an
// li rather than a link. The click handler still fires for a mouse, and is
// unreachable by keyboard.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />

// Correct — the href makes it a real, focusable link; onClick intercepts it
// for the router. The component calls preventDefault for you.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### Pass a string to `separator`, not a node. {#pass-a-string-to-separator-not-a-node}

Despite the `node` prop type, the value is written into the breadcrumb's
divider custom property, and a custom property holds text. A string is quoted
for you and works; a React element is stringified by CSS and disappears. Pass
`'/'`, `'›'`, `'—'`.

Do: A string separator is quoted for you.
Don't: A React element is stringified by CSS and disappears.

### Show the whole path, root first. {#show-the-whole-path-root-first}

A trail that starts mid-hierarchy leaves people unsure where they are. List every level from the top down to the current page, and let the row wrap rather than dropping a level.

Do: Every level from the root to the current page.
Don't: The trail starts mid-hierarchy, so the top is missing.

### Use it for position, not for history. {#use-it-for-position-not-for-history}

A breadcrumb shows where a page sits in the hierarchy, never the pages the person happened to visit. The trail for a page is the same whichever way they arrived.

### Name each level literally. {#name-each-level-literally}

Use the page's own title, not a direction or a pointer.

Do: Short, literal names that match the page titles.
Don't: Names that mean nothing out of context.

## Accessibility

  `aria-describedby` or a test at the trail as a whole, use `className`.

- `PageHeader`: use when placing `Breadcrumb` in the page header's `breadcrumbs` slot above the page title.

| --- | --- |

| Pressed | No change of its own. |

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |

rankedText.usage:
Use `Breadcrumb` when a page sits inside a hierarchy the user needs to see and
climb — a student inside a cohort inside a program, a lesson inside a unit. It
answers two questions at once: where am I, and what is one level up. When the
hierarchy is one level deep, a single "Back to X" `Link` says the same thing
with less furniture.

It takes a single `items` array, ordered root first. Each item is `{ text, href,
onClick }`. The last item is the current page and is rendered as plain text; every
item before it is a link.
rankedText.best:
### End the trail on the current page.

```jsx
// Incorrect — the href is dropped. The last item is rendered active
// unconditionally, and an active item is plain text with aria-current="page",
// never an anchor.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026', href: '/cohorts/a26' },
]} />

// Correct — the trail ends at where you are.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts' },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### Pass `href` alongside `onClick` on ancestor items.

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no href the item is rendered active, which means it is an
// li rather than a link. The click handler still fires for a mouse, and is
// unreachable by keyboard.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />

// Correct — the href makes it a real, focusable link; onClick intercepts it
// for the router. The component calls preventDefault for you.
<Breadcrumb items={[
    { text: 'Cohorts', href: '/cohorts', onClick: goToCohorts },
    { text: 'Autumn 2026' },
]} />
```

### Pass a string to `separator`, not a node.

Despite the `node` prop type, the value is written into the breadcrumb's
divider custom property, and a custom property holds text. A string is quoted
for you and works; a React element is stringified by CSS and disappears. Pass
`'/'`, `'›'`, `'—'`.

Do: A string separator is quoted for you.
Don't: A React element is stringified by CSS and disappears.

### Show the whole path, root first.

A trail that starts mid-hierarchy leaves people unsure where they are. List every level from the top down to the current page, and let the row wrap rather than dropping a level.

Do: Every level from the root to the current page.
Don't: The trail starts mid-hierarchy, so the top is missing.

### Use it for position, not for history.

A breadcrumb shows where a page sits in the hierarchy, never the pages the person happened to visit. The trail for a page is the same whichever way they arrived.

### Name each level literally.

Use the page's own title, not a direction or a pointer.

Do: Short, literal names that match the page titles.
Don't: Names that mean nothing out of context.

# Button

Button: triggers an action.

Also asked as: cta, submit.

**Import:** `import { Button } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Modal (`ds guide modal`); Panel (`ds guide panel`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`); +1 more

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Spacing, Icons, WithCount, States, Default, Primary, Subtle, Warning, Danger, Link, DangerLink, Discovery, Ai, Compact, Spacious, Selected, Disabled, Loading, ExplainsOnPress, FitContainer, Truncation, Interactive, StateSteps, LinkStates, KeyboardFocus, AnchorKeyboard, AnchorHref, Anatomy, FooterLayouts

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Button/Button.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Button` for an action on the current page: submit a form, mark attendance, close a dialog.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most actions that are not the main call to action of a page or area, and the secondary half of a footer. Draws a soft neutral fill with no outline. Example: "Reschedule session". |
| Primary | The main call to action or a form submission. One per page or area. Example: "Book session". |
| Subtle | Secondary actions in headers, toolbars and button groups. Example: "Learn more" in a toolbar. Never "Not now": a declining action is a Default secondary in the left half of a footer. |
| Warning | Confirms an action that may cause a significant change or a loss of data, often in a confirmation modal. Example: "Remove from this week". |
| Danger | The final confirmation of a destructive, irreversible action. Example: "Delete session recording". |
| Link | An action that leaves: text in the brand color with no fill, underlined on hover. It fills a footer's leading slot. Use it on a `LinkButton` to leave the page, or on a `Button` to leave the task. Examples: "Save and exit", "Open profile". |
| Danger link | A footer's leading destructive action: danger-colored text with no fill, so every leading action lines up as text. Example: "Delete", "Discard". Use Danger for the final confirmation. |
| Discovery | The call to action for a new experience. Example: "Try the new schedule view". |
| AI | The one primary AI action in a region. Draws the sparkle before its label. Example: "Generate summary". |

## Motion

Button reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Hover and press change color, 90% by about 110 ms. |

## Alternatives

- For navigation to another page or site in the look of a button, use `LinkButton`.
- For an action shown as an icon with no visible label, use `IconButton`.
- For a primary action joined to a menu of related variations, use `SplitButton`.
- For a menu of actions behind one trigger, use `DropdownMenu`.

## Best practices

### Use one primary action per area. {#use-one-primary-action-per-area}

Do: One primary button, with the secondary action subtle beside it.
Don't: Two primary buttons in one area compete for attention.

### Use one primary AI action per region. {#use-one-primary-ai-action-per-region}

The `ai` appearance marks the main AI action in a region, such as "Generate summary" on session notes. Use it only for actions that call AI, and leave its look as shipped (the sparkle is always drawn and a label is required). Every other AI action in the region is a `default` or `subtle` button with an AI icon.

Do: One AI button for the region's main AI action, with the other actions subtle.
Don't: A second AI button competes with the first, and Save notes is not an AI action.

### Pick the spacing for the surrounding space. {#pick-the-spacing-for-the-surrounding-space}

Use `default` spacing in most places, `compact` for tables, headers and inline popups, and `spacious` in modal and panel footers.

### Keep an action enabled and explain on press. {#keep-an-action-enabled-and-explain-on-press}

An action that is not ready stays enabled. When pressed, move focus to the first field that needs attention and show the reason there, or in a warning `SectionMessage` above when it blocks the main action. Disable a button only while it is sending (`isLoading`), or when the reason is self-evident, such as Back on the first step. A button for something a role can never do is left out. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Enabled, with the reason shown as text when the button is pressed.
Don't: A disabled submit button gives no direction and leaves the tab order.

### Align the primary button with its group. {#align-the-primary-button-with-its-group}

In Modal and Panel footers, `FooterActions` places the primary action in the rightmost track. On single-page forms and full-page tasks, left-align buttons with the primary first.

## Accessibility

- **Action vs. navigation.** `Button` renders a `<button>`; use `LinkButton` for navigation so screen readers announce the right role.
- **Disabled state.** A disabled button leaves the tab order, receives no events, and never takes a tooltip or an `aria-disabled` stand-in. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).
- **Icon-only buttons.** A button with no visible label is an `IconButton`, which requires a `label`.
- **Focus.** The focus ring is 2px in `--ds-border-focused`. Never remove it.
- **Loading and selected.** `isLoading` blocks interaction, sets `aria-busy`, and keeps the label in the accessibility tree. `isSelected` sets `aria-pressed`.

## Related

- `FooterActions`: use when placing spacious buttons across the four-track footer slot of a Modal or Panel.
- `IconButton`: use when space allows only an icon with a tooltip label.
- `LinkButton`: use when the control navigates to another page or URL.
- `ButtonGroup`: use when related buttons sit together in a connected row.
- `DropdownMenu`: use when a trigger opens a list of actions.
- `ProgressBar`: use when showing progress on the page rather than inside the button.

Same group: `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Container.** Soft neutral fill (`--ds-background-neutral`) with no border on `default`, transparent on `subtle`, and bold semantic fills on `primary`, `warning`, `danger`, `discovery` and `ai`. Draws `32` high (`--control-md`) at `default` spacing, `24` (`--control-sm`) at `compact`, and `48` (`--control-xl`) at `spacious` inside `FooterActions`. Stretches to its parent's width with `shouldFitContainer`, keeping the label centered.
2. **Icon before** (optional). A Font Awesome Free glyph at `16` (`--icon-md`), before the label (`ai` always draws its sparkle).
3. **Label.** Body/default at the medium weight, centered in the container; truncates with an ellipsis when constrained.
4. **Icon after** (optional). A Font Awesome Free glyph at `16` (`--icon-md`), or `12` (`--icon-sm`) for a trailing chevron.
5. **Spinner** (loading only). A `16` `Spinner` in the label color that replaces the label and icons while the button is busy.

Most buttons need no icon. Add one only when the glyph has an established meaning, such as `plus` for add.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | The container takes the appearance's hovered fill. The label and icon keep their colors. |
| Pressed | The container takes the appearance's pressed fill. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | The selected role fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, label and icon. Applies to default and subtle, and sets `aria-pressed`. |
| Disabled | The disabled fill, label and icon: a change of color, not of opacity. Subtle stays transparent. |
| Loading | A 16 `Spinner` replaces the label and icons. The container keeps its fill, blocks interaction and sets `aria-busy`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill: default, subtle | `--ds-background-neutral` (default) and `--ds-background-neutral-subtle` (subtle), each with hovered and pressed steps. Neither draws an edge. |
| Fill: primary, warning, danger, discovery | `--ds-background-brand-bold`, `-warning-bold`, `-danger-bold`, `-discovery-bold`, each with hovered and pressed steps. |
| Fill: AI | `--ds-ai-background-bold`, with hovered and pressed steps. |
| Fill: selected, disabled | `--ds-background-selected` with hovered and pressed steps and a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge; `--ds-background-disabled`. |
| Label and icon | `--ds-text` and `--ds-icon` (default); `--ds-text-subtle` and `--ds-icon-subtle` (subtle); `--ds-text-inverse` and `--ds-icon-inverse` (primary, danger, discovery, ai); `--ds-text-warning-inverse` (warning); the selected and disabled roles. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |
| Height | Default 32: `--control-md`. Compact 24: `--control-sm`. Spacious 48: `--control-xl`. |
| Padding | Default 12: `--pad-x-md`. Compact 8: `--pad-x-sm`. Spacious 16: `--pad-x-lg`. |
| Radius | Default 6: `--button-radius-default`. Compact 4: `--button-radius-compact`. Spacious 10: `--button-radius-spacious`. |
| Icon-to-label gap | 4: `--inline-sm`. |
| Label | Body/default at the medium weight; icons at 16 (`--icon-md`), chevrons at 12 (`--icon-sm`). |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use sentence case: "Add student". | Title case or all capitals: "Add Student", "ADD STUDENT". |
| Keep the label short and free of punctuation: "Save notes". | "Save the notes for this session." |
| Start with a verb and name what is acted on: "Confirm session time". | Vague labels such as "OK", "Yes" or "Submit". |
| Use the same words as the heading and related text in view. | Different words for the same action within one view. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | — | The label. Children work too. |
| `children` | node | — | The label, used when `text` is not given. Omit both for an icon-only button. |
| `title` | string | — | The `title` attribute, a native tooltip on hover. It is left off while the button is disabled or loading. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | The visual style. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | Height and padding: `default` draws 32, `compact` draws 24, `spacious` draws 48. Compact is for tables and tight toolbars; spacious is for modal and panel footers. |
| `shouldFitContainer` | bool | `false` | Stretches the button to the width of its container, with the label centered. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the button element beside the component's own. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event when the button is activated by mouse or keyboard. It does not fire while `isDisabled` or `isLoading` is set. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction. Avoid it; see Usage. |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | Marks the button selected and sets `aria-pressed`. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | Shows a spinner in place of the label and blocks interaction. |
| `type` | string | `'button'` | The native button `type`: `button` (default), `submit` or `reset`. Used only when the button renders as a `button` element. |
| `as` | elementType | — | Renders the button as this element or component instead, such as a router link. Without it the button is an anchor when `href`, `target` or `rel` is set, otherwise a `button`. |
| `href` | string | — | Renders as an anchor when set (and no `as` overrides it). |
| `target` | string | — | The anchor `target` attribute, such as `_blank`. Used only when the button renders as an anchor. |
| `rel` | string | — | The anchor `rel` attribute. Used only when the button renders as an anchor. |
| `role` | string | — | Overrides the default `"button"` ARIA role an anchor-rendered Button takes (e.g. `LinkButton`'s own `"link"`). |
| `iconBefore` | string or node | — | A Font Awesome Free glyph name, or a node, before the label. |
| `iconAfter` | string or node | — | A Font Awesome Free glyph name, or a node, after the label. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the rendered element. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `primary` · `subtle` · `warning` · `danger` · `discovery` · `ai` · `link` · `danger-link`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact` · `spacious`

# ButtonGroup

Button group: a visually connected row of related actions. A plain container for `Button` children, each keeping its own `appearance` and `spacing`. `label` names the group for assistive technology.

**Import:** `import { ButtonGroup } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.stories.jsx` — Overview, Seams, Appearances, Spacing, IconOnly, Selected, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.mdx`

## Usage

Use `ButtonGroup` for a short row of related actions or view toggles that read as one unit.

## Alternatives

- For a single standalone action, use `Button`.
- For one primary action joined to a menu of variations, use `SplitButton`.
- For mutually exclusive form answers, use `RadioGroup`.
- For large illustrated choices with a title and an illustration, use `ChoiceGrid` (or `RadioGroup` / `CheckboxGroup` in `tile` appearance).

## Best practices

### Group related actions only. {#group-related-actions-only}

A group reads as one control. Every button in it works on the same object.

Do: Day, Week and Month all change the same calendar.
Don't: Save, Delete and Help act on different things.

### Give the group an accessible name. {#give-the-group-an-accessible-name}

`ButtonGroup` has no visible title of its own. `label` names the whole group
for assistive technology, such as "Calendar view".

```jsx
<ButtonGroup label="Calendar view">
    <Button text="Day" isSelected={view === 'day'} onClick={() => setView('day')} />
    <Button text="Week" isSelected={view === 'week'} onClick={() => setView('week')} />
</ButtonGroup>
```

### Keep every button one size. {#keep-every-button-one-size}

Buttons in a group share one spacing so the outline stays continuous.

Do: Every button uses default spacing.
Don't: A compact button beside default ones breaks the outline.

### Make the labels parallel. {#make-the-labels-parallel}

Do: Every label is a noun of the same kind.
Don't: A noun, a phrase and a verb in one group.

### Selection state lives on each `Button`, not on the group. {#selection-state-lives-on-each-button-not-on-the-group}

`ButtonGroup` renders children as given — set `isSelected` on the `Button`
that should read as current, and manage which one that is yourself.

## Accessibility

- **A named group.** The row is `role="group"` with `label` as its accessible
  name, so assistive technology announces the buttons as one related set.
- **Each button keeps its own accessible name and state.** `ButtonGroup`
  adds no roles or attributes beyond the group wrapper.

## Related

- `Button`: use when an action stands alone or sits in a spaced row.
- `SplitButton`: use when one primary action pairs with a chevron menu.
- `ChoiceGrid`: use when offering illustrated choices (or `RadioGroup` / `CheckboxGroup` with `appearance="tile"`).

Same group: `Button` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Container.** Groups its children with `role="group"` and the `label` as its name. It paints nothing of its own.
2. **Buttons.** Button or Icon button children that hug their labels. Each keeps its own appearance, spacing and state.
3. **Seam.** Inner corners are square and neighbors overlap by one edge, so the row reads as one control and a selected item's 1px border stays unbroken.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | The hovered button rises above its neighbors so its fill is not covered. |
| Focused | The focused button rises above its neighbors so its ring is not covered. |
| Selected | Set on each button with `isSelected`, which sets `aria-pressed`, draws `--ds-background-selected`, `--ds-text-selected` and a 1px `--ds-border-selected` border, and rises above its neighbors. The group has no selection logic. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Outer corners | 6: `--button-radius-default`. Compact 4: `--button-radius-compact`. |
| Seam overlap | 1: `--border-width-default`. |
| Selected border | 1px `--ds-border-selected` over `--ds-background-selected`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Give the group a label that names the choice: "Date range". | A generic label such as "Buttons" or "Group". |
| Keep each button label to one or two words in sentence case: "Week", "Month". | Long or sentence-length labels that make the group wrap. |
| Make the labels parallel: all nouns or all verbs. | A mix such as "Week", "Show all" and "Choose". |
| Order the buttons the way people read the choice, such as smallest to largest. | An arbitrary order. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | The buttons to render inside the group. |
| `label` | string | — | The group's accessible name. Strongly recommended. |
| `testId` | string | — | A `data-testid` hook for automated tests. |
| `className` | string | — | Additional CSS classes. |
| `id` | string | — | HTML ID attribute. |

## Tokens touched

`--border-width-default` · `--button-radius-default`

From `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ButtonGroup/ButtonGroup.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.
