# Calendar

Calendar — the month grid DatePicker and DateTimePicker open (Figma `_Calendar`), public for a caller who wants the grid on its own rather than behind a field's popup. It is the same component the pickers use. - **Grid:** always six weeks, 42 cells, so the panel never changes height. Days of the months either side are drawn and can't be picked. - **Days:** each is a button named with its full date. `aria-pressed` marks the picked day, or both ends of a range; `data-in-range` marks the days between; `aria-current="date"` marks today. - **Bounds:** days before `minDate` or after `maxDate` are disabled. - **Size:** a pixel width, 24, 32 or 40, drawn from the `--calendar-day-*` tokens.

**Import:** `import { Calendar } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Calendar/Calendar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Calendar/Calendar.stories.jsx` — Size24, Size32, Size40, PickADay, TurnMonths, TurnMonthsReduced, Default, Selected, Range, Disabled, HoveredState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Calendar/Calendar.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Calendar` directly only when a month grid must stay visible on the page without a field or popup around it, such as an embedded scheduling view.

## Motion

Calendar reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |
| change | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | A month change slides the grid flat. |

## Alternatives

- For a date or date range field that opens this grid in a popup, use `DatePicker`.
- For a combined date and time answer, use `DateTimePicker`.

## Best practices

### Name the month in full, with the year. {#name-the-month-in-full-with-the-year}

The header states the full month name and year rather than numeric month codes so people do not have to count.

### Dim unavailable days, do not hide them. {#dim-unavailable-days-do-not-hide-them}

A dimmed day tells people why a slot is missing; a day that looks pickable but is not wastes a tap. Set `minDate` and `maxDate` to the span that can be chosen.

Do: Days outside the span that can be chosen are dimmed and disabled.
Don't: Every day looks pickable, and the limit is found only after an error.

### Show the selected date as one filled day. {#show-the-selected-date-as-one-filled-day}

In single mode one day carries the selected fill. A second fill reads as a range.

Do: One picked day carries the fill.
Don't: Two filled ends for a single answer read as a range.

### Say which dates can be chosen. {#say-which-dates-can-be-chosen}

Put the limit in text near the calendar, so people do not find it by trying disabled days.

Do: A line above the grid states the span.
Don't: No text: the limit shows only as dimmed days.

### Let the caller own the month on show. {#let-the-caller-own-the-month-on-show}

`Calendar` holds no state of its own. The caller owns `viewDate` and updates it when `onViewDateChange` fires, the same pattern Date picker uses internally.

```jsx
const [viewDate, setViewDate] = useState(new Date());

<Calendar
    viewDate={viewDate}
    onViewDateChange={setViewDate}
    selected={selectedDate}
    onPick={setSelectedDate}
/>
```

### Keep the grid at six weeks. {#keep-the-grid-at-six-weeks}

Six weeks render every month, including the days of neighboring months that fill the remaining cells. This keeps the panel's height constant as someone pages through months, at the cost of occasionally showing a mostly empty week.

## Accessibility

- **Each day is a real, named button.** The accessible name is the day's full date, not just a number, so a screen reader announces an unambiguous date on every cell.
- **State is marked, not just styled.** `aria-pressed` marks the picked day or a range's ends, `aria-current="date"` marks today, and `data-in-range` marks the days between. None of this relies on color alone.
- **Out-of-range and out-of-month days are truly disabled**, not just dimmed: they take no focus and fire no `onPick`.
- **The month buttons are named** "Previous month" and "Next month".

## Related

- `DatePicker`: use when a single date or date range field opens the calendar in a popup.
- `DateTimePicker`: use when a date and a time are answered together.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Header.** The month and year in full, with Previous month and Next month buttons.
2. **Weekday row.** Seven short day names.
3. **Day cells.** Forty-two buttons in six weeks. Days of neighboring months fill the spare cells.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Day text in `--ds-text` on no fill. |
| Hovered | An enabled day takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. A picked day keeps its fill. |
| Pressed | No look of its own: pressing an enabled day picks it. |
| Focused | The month buttons and the days draw a 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge. |
| Disabled | Faded to `--ds-opacity-disabled`; no focus, no `onPick`. |
| Today | A 1px `--ds-border-brand` edge and `--ds-text-brand` text. |
| In range | `--ds-background-selected`. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected-bold` with `--ds-text-inverse`, and `aria-pressed`. |
| Outside the month | `--ds-text-subtle`; not pickable. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Month | `--heading-xs` in `--ds-text`. |
| Month buttons | Compact `IconButton` (`--control-sm` square), `--ds-icon-subtle`, hovered `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Weekday names | `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Day text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`. |
| Day size | `--calendar-day-sm` (24), `--calendar-day-md` (32), `--calendar-day-lg` (40). |
| Day radius | `--radius-md`. |
| Gaps | `--stack-md` between header, weekdays and days; `--stack-sm` between rows. |
| Padding | `--space-025` top and bottom, `--pad-x-md` either side. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say which dates can be chosen in text near the calendar: "Pick a day between October 12 and 25." | Leave people to find the limit by trying disabled days. |
| Name the choice by its role: "Session date". | "Calendar" or "Pick a date". |
| Write dates in full where text names them: "October 21, 2026". | All-numeric dates that read differently by locale: "10/11/12". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `viewDate` | instanceOf (required) | — | Any day in the month on show. |
| `onViewDateChange` | func (required) | — | `(firstOfMonth)` when Previous month or Next month is pressed. |
| `selected` | string or instanceOf | — | The picked day, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. |
| `rangeStart` | string or instanceOf | — | A range's first day; with `rangeEnd`, the days between are marked. |
| `rangeEnd` | string or instanceOf | — | — |
| `minDate` | string or instanceOf | — | The earliest day that can be picked, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. Earlier days are disabled. |
| `maxDate` | string or instanceOf | — | The latest day that can be picked, as ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` or a Date. Later days are disabled. |
| `size` | enum | — | Day width in pixels: 24, 32 or 40. |
| `onPick` | func (required) | — | `(date)` when an enabled day is pressed. |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`size`** — `24` · `32` · `40`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Figma

entries.summary: A container for one student, session, metric or other object, with slots for an image, header, body and footer.

props.name: title
props.description: The card's title, in the card title type (`styles/_card-title.scss`), tagged one heading level below its section

props.name: description
props.description: Body/default 14 under the title

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions at the end of the header row: buttons, a pager or an overflow

props.name: header
props.description: Custom header that replaces title, description and actions (tabs, a toolbar)

props.name: image
props.description: Image slot, full bleed: above the content, or at the start or end edge per `imagePlacement`

props.name: imagePlacement
props.description: Image position. Side placements apply from the 480 minimum width; narrower cards put the image on top.

props.name: imageRatio
props.description: Image shape on a top image: its height follows the card width at 16:9, 4:3 or 1:1, rounded to a multiple of 4, and the picture crops to cover. A side image fills the card height instead.

props.name: imageSplit
props.description: Side image share. One half also steps the title up to Heading md. Ignored for top placement.

props.name: footer
props.description: Footer slot: a link for one action that leaves, or a compact pair with no Primary, start-aligned, Card/stack-lg below the body

props.name: surface
props.description: Surface level: sunken (default, flat), default (page fill with a 1px border, flat), or raised (raised fill and shadow)

props.name: gap
props.description: Header-to-body stack: Card/stack-sm · md · lg (4 · 8 · 12)

props.name: minWidth
props.description: Minimum width constraint (number of px or any CSS length)

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler, passed to the card's root element. Its presence adds the clickable class: a pointer cursor and the hover lift. It adds no role or tab stop; pass `role` and `tabIndex` for a card clickable as a whole.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Key handler, passed to the card's root element. A card clickable as a whole takes Enter and Space here, beside its `role` and `tabIndex`.

props.name: dragging
props.description: The card is being dragged: it lifts to the overlay pair

props.name: children
props.description: Body content slot

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Card

PLUS card: an optional image, content and footer on a `sunken`, `default`, or `raised` surface. - **Surface**: `sunken` (default, flat), `default` (page surface with a 1px border, flat), or `raised` (raised surface and shadow). Every card carries a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) so forced colors draw its edge. - **Image placement**: `top` (default), `start` or `end`. Side images apply at the 480 minimum width and fill the height. `imageSplit` chooses one third (default) or one half; half uses Heading md on a side card. Below the 480 minimum width, the image returns to the top with its own ratio. - **Image ratio**: `imageRatio` is `16:9` (default), `4:3` or `1:1`. A top image's height is the card width times the ratio, rounded to a multiple of 4 so the card stays on the 4 px grid; the picture crops to cover and the text sets the rest of the height. - **Header** (`_Card header`): `title` (the card title type, shared with Card in `styles/_card-title.scss`, one heading level below its section) over an optional `description` (Body/default 14), with `actions` at the end of the row. `header` replaces that block with custom content, like the header's `custom` type, for tabs or a toolbar. - **Spacing** comes from the Card tokens: padding uses `--card-pad` and radius uses `--card-radius` at every size, the header sits Card/stack-md above the body (`gap` picks the stack step), and the footer sits Card/stack-lg below. The footer hugs the start: one action that goes somewhere is a link (`appearance="link"`), two are a compact pair with no Primary, and a card that is all one action is clickable with no buttons. - The card hugs its content; in a row it stretches to the tallest card. - **Elevation**: a clickable `sunken` or `default` card lifts to Raised on hover in place and settles to the raised shadow while pressed; a clickable `raised` card lifts to the raised hovered step under the overlay shadow and settles back onto the raised shadow while pressed; `dragging` puts any card on the overlay pair while it moves. The card also sets the current surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

Also asked as: summary card, object card.

**Import:** `import { Card } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.stories.jsx` — Overview, Interactive, Elevation, Anatomy, Jobs, MinWidth224, MinWidth304, MinWidth480, ImageWide, ImageStandard, ImageSquare, ImageRatioGrid, ImageRatioDefault, ImageTop, ImageTopHovered, ImageTopPressed, ImageTopDragging, ImageStart, ImageStartHovered, ImageStartPressed, ImageStartDragging, ImageEnd, ImageEndHovered, ImageEndPressed, ImageEndDragging, ImageStartHalf, ImageEndHalf, ImageTopIgnoresSplit, BodyOnly, WithFooter, CustomHeader, SurfaceSunken, SurfaceDefault, SurfaceRaised, Static, Clickable, Dragging, ForcedColors, LoadingCard, Rows, PlacementBoundary

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · milestone `spatial.default`, sound `sound.done.milestone`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use a card when one object needs its own container on the page. Pick `surface` by the card's role: `sunken` (default) groups static content on `--ds-surface-sunken` without a shadow; `default` pairs `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border` on the Frame, on Sunken or colored areas, and for dense rows; `raised` pairs `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised` for the one primary card per view, first in reading order. A card holds a heading, content and an optional footer for actions. Fill its slots with your own parts.

1. Pick the size by what the card holds.
2. Choose a header, or omit it when the body carries its own title.
3. Fill the body slot. Add spacing only inside slot content, using Card stack tokens.
4. Add a footer only for actions that commit.

### Color

To give a card a semantic or accent fill, swap its surface token for a solid brand (`--ds-background-brand-subtlest`, or `--ds-background-brand-bold` with `--ds-text-inverse`), status (`--ds-background-information`, `--ds-background-success`), accent-subtlest (`--ds-background-accent-teal-subtlest`), or selected (`--ds-background-selected`) background token. `surface="raised"` keeps `--ds-shadow-raised`. On a clickable colored card, hovered and pressed states use that same token's `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps.

### Width guidance

Content picks the minimum width. Choose the narrowest card that holds the content without clipping, then let the row decide how many fit. Height always hugs the content, and a card in a row stretches to the tallest card.

| Minimum width | When to use | Pad | Radius | Token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224 | One number or one line. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-sm` |
| 304 | A short list or a few lines. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-md` |
| 480 | A summary with several parts. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-lg` |

`minWidth` sets the minimum width; every width uses `--card-pad` (16) and `--card-radius` (16). The text sets the height, and a top image takes its `imageRatio` height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4. Set a height cap with `style`'s `maxHeight`; the card clips what passes it.

### Cards in a row

In a row, place the most cards that keep each card at its minimum width. Each row is the content width of its mode, with a 16 gutter. The count switches between viewport widths of 1224 and 1256 with the sidebar docked.

| Mode | Content width | Min 224 | Min 304 | Min 480 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium, 768 | 720 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Large, 1024 | 736 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| X-Large, 1440 | 1152 | 4 | 3 | 2 |

## Motion

Card reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | It changes color on hover and press like a Button. Opening a clickable card is Drill. |  |
| milestone | Load content | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The one card in a milestone page entrance is Expressive and leaves by the exit rules. | `sound.done.milestone` on land: onboarding complete, first session, goal reached, term start or end, achievement claimed; goal reached is shared, so the student hears it |

## Best practices

### Fit the width to what the card holds. {#fit-the-width-to-what-the-card-holds}

Visible empty space inside the card means a narrower minimum width. A clipped or crowded body means a wider one.

Do: One number fits the 224 minimum; the card is only as wide as it needs, so a row of them stays tidy.
Don't: The same number at 480 leaves most of the card empty; narrow it instead of filling the space.

### Never put a card inside a card. {#never-put-a-card-inside-a-card}

A card's fill and edge are its own object boundary. Group related cards in a Section instead.

Do: One card; three metrics stacked in its body, split by dividers.
Don't: Three mini cards inside the card; borders and shadows pile up and the hierarchy flattens.

### Keep the card in place while it loads. {#keep-the-card-in-place-while-it-loads}

Do: Loading keeps the card in place: a skeleton fills the body, so the layout does not jump when data arrives.
Don't: A bare loading line takes the card away; the row collapses and everything below it moves.

### Let the footer's job pick its buttons. {#let-the-footer-s-job-pick-its-buttons}

A card's footer actions hug the start, under the content. One action that goes somewhere, such as View session, is a link. Two actions are a compact Default pair with no Primary. A card that is all one action is clickable and has no buttons. Only a Modal or Panel footer, on FooterActions, fills tracks and ends in a Primary. The whole rule: Common actions.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading one level below the section the card sits in: an h3 in a section, an h2 straight on a page. Nest the card in a Section rather than choosing a tag.
- A card that is clickable as a whole needs a role and a tab stop, and it must answer Enter and Space. When the card has one action, put a Button in the footer instead.
- Mark the card `aria-busy` while it loads. The skeleton bars are hidden from assistive technology.
- The hover lift is never the only cue that a card is clickable. Pair it with a visible action or a link in the card.
- Every card keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) so forced colors draw its edge.
- Text sits on each surface in `--ds-text` and `--ds-text-subtle`, which meet contrast in every color mode.
- The card sets `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` to its chosen surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

## Related

- Section for a region that holds cards under one heading.
- Table for many objects of the same shape that people compare across columns.
- Page for the content area's own fill, header and elevation.
- Modal for something that must be decided before the page can continue.

Same group: `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Parts

1. **Image** (optional). A slot above everything else, or beside the content in a side layout. It runs edge to edge, outside the pad, and the card radius clips its corners. On top, `imageRatio` (16:9 default, 4:3 or 1:1) sets its height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4, and the picture crops to cover; beside the content it fills the full height at one third or one half of the width and crops to cover.
2. **Header.** The title, an optional description and an optional actions slot. A custom `header` replaces all three. The title uses Heading xs at every heading level, stepping up to Heading md for a half side image. The description uses Body default. In Figma the title truncates to one line and the description's `text` variant truncates at three lines or wraps; code leaves wrapping to CSS.
3. **Body.** A slot for text, a list or media.
4. **Footer** (optional). A start-aligned slot for the card's actions: one link, or a compact pair with no Primary.

The image sits above (or, in a side layout, beside) a padded frame, and the header, body and footer sit inside it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `sunken` (default): `--ds-surface-sunken`, flat. `default`: `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border`, flat. `raised`: `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. Every surface keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) for forced colors. |
| Hovered | A clickable card only: `sunken` and `default` lift in place to `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`; `raised` lifts to `--ds-surface-raised-hovered` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`. A card with no `onClick` does not change. |
| Pressed | A clickable card only: settles to `--ds-surface-raised-pressed` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. |
| Focused | The card has no focus style of its own. A card made clickable as a whole takes `role` and `tabIndex` from you. |
| Disabled | A card is never disabled. Disable the controls inside it. |
| Dragging | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, held under hover and press. |
| Loading | Skeleton bars in the body, with `aria-busy` on the card. Figma's `loading?` has no prop in code. |

### Tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--card-pad` | 16 | Padding inside a card at every width. |
| `--card-radius` | 16 | Corner rounding of a card at every width. |
| `--card-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 4 · 8 · 12 | Title to description; header to body, set by `gap`; body to footer. |
| `--card-inline-md` | 8 | Items on a row, such as actions in the header. |
| `--card-min-width-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 224 · 304 · 480 | The minimum width of each card width. |
| `--card-surface-sunken`, `-default`, `-raised` | color | The card fill at rest (`--ds-surface-sunken`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-raised`). |
| `--card-border-default`, `--card-border-width` | border | The 1px `--ds-border` on `default` cards, and the 1px width kept on every card for forced colors. |
| `--card-shadow-raised`, `-overlay` | shadow | `--ds-shadow-raised` on raised and hovered clickable cards; `--ds-shadow-overlay` while dragged or hovering a raised card. |
| `--card-surface-raised-hovered`, `-pressed`, `-overlay` | color | Clickable hover/press steps and the dragged overlay surface. |
| `--heading-xs`, `--card-description-font` | type | The regular title and the description (`--body-default`). |
| `--card-title-font-lg` | type | The title beside a half-width side image (`--heading-md`). |
| `--card-text`, `--card-text-subtle` | color | The title and the description (`--ds-text`, `--ds-text-subtle`). |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the card with the object it holds, in sentence case: "Ana Ruiz", "Sessions this week". | A generic title such as "Details" or "Info". |
| Keep the description to one line that adds something, such as "Lincoln Middle · Thu 4:00 PM". | A description that repeats the title. |
| Name a footer action for what it does: "Save note", "View session". | "OK" or "Submit". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `title` | node | — | The card's title, in the card title type (`styles/_card-title.scss`), tagged one heading level below its section |
| `description` | node | — | Body/default 14 under the title |
| `actions` | node | — | Actions at the end of the header row: buttons, a pager or an overflow |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header that replaces title, description and actions (tabs, a toolbar) |
| `image` | node | — | Image slot, full bleed: above the content, or at the start or end edge per `imagePlacement` |
| `imagePlacement` | enum | `'top'` | Image position. Side placements apply from the 480 minimum width; narrower cards put the image on top. |
| `imageRatio` | enum | `'16:9'` | Image shape on a top image: its height follows the card width at 16:9, 4:3 or 1:1, rounded to a multiple of 4, and the picture crops to cover. A side image fills the card height instead. |
| `imageSplit` | enum | `'1/3'` | Side image share. One half also steps the title up to Heading md. Ignored for top placement. |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer slot: a link for one action that leaves, or a compact pair with no Primary, start-aligned, Card/stack-lg below the body |
| `surface` | enum | `'sunken'` | Surface level: sunken (default, flat), default (page fill with a 1px border, flat), or raised (raised fill and shadow) |
| `gap` | enum | `'md'` | Header-to-body stack: Card/stack-sm · md · lg (4 · 8 · 12) |
| `minWidth` | number or string | — | Minimum width constraint (number of px or any CSS length) |
| `onClick` | func | — | Click handler, passed to the card's root element. Its presence adds the clickable class: a pointer cursor and the hover lift. It adds no role or tab stop; pass `role` and `tabIndex` for a card clickable as a whole. |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Key handler, passed to the card's root element. A card clickable as a whole takes Enter and Space here, beside its `role` and `tabIndex`. |
| `dragging` | bool | `false` | The card is being dragged: it lifts to the overlay pair |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | Body content slot |

## Variants

**`imagePlacement`** — `top` · `start` · `end`

**`imageRatio`** — `16:9` · `4:3` · `1:1`

**`imageSplit`** — `1/3` · `1/2`

**`surface`** — `sunken` · `default` · `raised`

**`gap`** — `sm` · `md` · `lg`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--card-border-default` · `--card-border-width` · `--card-description-font` · `--card-inline-md` · `--card-pad` · `--card-radius` · `--card-shadow-overlay` · `--card-shadow-raised` · `--card-stack-lg` · `--card-stack-md` · `--card-stack-sm` · `--card-surface-default` · `--card-surface-overlay` · `--card-surface-raised` · `--card-surface-raised-hovered` · `--card-surface-raised-pressed` · `--card-surface-sunken` · `--card-text` · `--card-text-subtle` · `--card-title-font-lg` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast-duration` · `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current`

From `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Carousel

A centered stage of slides: the active one full size and, with `peek`, one neighbor on each side in the same flat row, smaller and faded. Under it, a play button whose ring fills over the slide's time, a progress indicator whose current dot stretches into a bar that fills on the same clock, and a caption that changes with the slide. Autoplay holds while the pointer rests on the stage, keyboard focus is inside, the carousel is out of view or the tab is hidden. Under reduced motion it never moves on its own: arrows replace the play button, the current bar shows full and every move is instant.

Also asked as: slideshow, gallery.

**Import:** `import { Carousel } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Carousel/Carousel.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Carousel/Carousel.stories.jsx` — Overview, Static, NoLoop, CaptionFadesInPlace, FewSlides, ReducedMotion, Interactive, NoPeek, PauseStopsProgress, DotRestartsClock, ArrowKeysMove, HoverHolds, InactiveSlidesHidden, RegionIsNamed, NeighborsWrap, DotFills, StaticBarFull, DotTargets

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/Carousel/Carousel.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.default` · enter `appearance.default` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Carousel` for a few equal panels a person is invited to look through: what is
new, a short tour, a handful of featured items. Every slide but one is hidden at
any moment, so nothing a person must read or act on belongs in it.

`slides` takes `{ media, title, description }`. `media` is the card; `title`
and `description` fill the caption under the controls and name each step in the
progress indicator. Autoplay is on by default (`interval` `5000`), and loops.
`peek` shows the neighbors; turn it off to show the current slide alone.
`onSlideChange` gets the new index. Give the region a name with `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`.

## Motion

Carousel reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | No autoplay by default; if it plays, it has a visible pause. |
| enter | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | The caption fades in place with no vertical travel. |
| exit | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The caption fades out in place before the next words swap in. |

## Alternatives

- For switching between alternative views of the same content, use `Tabs`.
- For a short guided tour of a new feature, use `Spotlight`.

## Best practices

### Keep it to three to six slides. {#keep-it-to-three-to-six-slides}

The progress indicator is the map. Past six, nobody gets to the end.

Do: Three slides, each worth seeing.
Don't: Ten slides and a long progress indicator to match.

### Give every slide a title. {#give-every-slide-a-title}

The title is the caption a sighted reader sees and the name a screen reader hears on each step button.

Do: A title and one line for each slide.
Don't: No titles: the step buttons say only the slide number.

### Keep the caption to one line. {#keep-the-caption-to-one-line}

The caption holds two lines of room so the page does not jump. A paragraph pushes the page down every time the slide changes.

### Leave autoplay to slides that can be missed. {#leave-autoplay-to-slides-that-can-be-missed}

Autoplay moves on whether or not a person finished. Turn it off with `autoplay={false}` when a slide asks someone to read closely.

## Accessibility

- **The region needs a name.** It is a `region` announced as a carousel; pass
  `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- **The pause control comes first.** Autoplay can always be stopped from the
  play button, which is the first control in the row. Its name says what a
  press will do: Pause, then Play.
- **Each indicator step is a button.** The `ProgressIndicator` is a group named
  "Choose a slide"; each button is named with the slide number and title, and
  the current one carries `aria-current="step"`.
- **Only the active slide is read.** Each slide is a group; the others are
  `aria-hidden` and inert, so focus never lands behind the front card.
- **Keyboard focus holds the clock.** Tabbing into the carousel stops
  autoplay so nothing moves under a keyboard user; pressing Play starts it
  again. A mouse click on a control does not hold it.
- **Arrow keys move the stage.** With focus on the region or a control,
  ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move a slide either way.
- **The caption speaks only when asked.** It is a polite live region while the
  carousel is paused or does not autoplay, and silent while it plays, so it
  never talks over a screen reader on its own.
- **Reduced motion is respected.** When the viewer asks for less motion, the
  carousel does not autoplay, shows arrows and moves in one step.

## Related

- `ProgressIndicator`: use when displaying step indicators below the stage.
- [Card](?path=/docs/templates-card--docs): use when laying out a few items side by side in a grid so nothing is hidden and nothing moves.

Same group: `Accordion` · `PageHeader` · `ScrollBar`

## Parts

1. **Stage.** Full width, with the edges fading out.
2. **Slide.** A card, centered. A neighbor on each side sits in the same row, scaled down and faded; clicking one brings it to the front.
3. **Play button.** A subtle circle `IconButton`, Pause while playing and Play while paused, inside a ring whose arc fills over the slide's time.
4. **Progress indicator.** A selectable `ProgressIndicator`, one step per slide. The current step stretches into a bar (`--control-md`) whose fill grows from the start edge over the slide's time. Choosing a step moves to its slide and restarts the clock.
5. **Arrows.** Circle `IconButton`s, shown when the carousel does not autoplay, in place of the play button.
6. **Caption.** The active slide's title as a `Heading` and one line of body text, centered under the controls.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Playing | The ring arc and the bar fill together in `--ds-background-brand-bold`. |
| Paused | The play icon shows. The arc and the bar hold where they stopped. |
| Held | The clock stops while the pointer rests on the stage, keyboard focus is inside, the carousel is out of view or the tab is hidden. It resumes where it held. Pressing Play starts it again even with focus inside. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused | The play button and the arrows keep the states of `IconButton`. The indicator steps keep the states of `ProgressIndicator`. |
| Reduced motion or no autoplay | No ring; the bar shows full. |
| Disabled arrow | Without `loop`, at the first or last slide. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Card | `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`, corners `--card-radius`. |
| Neighbors | Faded under `--ds-surface` at 45%, `--inline-2xl` apart (`--inline-lg` on a narrow stage). |
| Ring | `--control-lg` across, `--border-width-selected` wide. Track `--ds-border`; progress `--ds-background-brand-bold`. |
| Progress indicator | The default `ProgressIndicator`: steps `--progress-indicator-dot-size-8`, the bar `--control-md` long, each step a `--control-sm` target. |
| Motion | A move takes `--ds-motion-spatial-default`, fading on `--ds-motion-appearance-slow`. The caption fades out over `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` and fades in over `--ds-motion-appearance-default`, with no vertical travel. |
| Caption | `Heading` size sm; line in `--body-default` and `--ds-text-subtle`; at most `--content-max-width-reading` wide. |
| Spacing | `--section-stack-md` between the stage, the controls and the caption; `--inline-md` between controls. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `slides` | arrayOf | `[]` | The slides, in order. `media` is the card; `title` and `description` fill the caption and name the slide's dot. A string `media` renders as text, or as an image when it is a path ending in an image extension (`alt` describes it). |
| `autoplay` | bool | `true` | Moves to the next slide on its own, with a play button to stop it. Off under reduced motion, where arrows show instead. Defaults to `true`. |
| `interval` | number | `5000` | Milliseconds each slide shows before the next. Defaults to `5000`. |
| `peek` | bool | `true` | Shows the neighbors at each side, smaller and faded. Off, only the current slide shows. Defaults to `true`. |
| `loop` | bool | `true` | Lets the arrows and arrow keys wrap from the last slide to the first. Autoplay always wraps. Defaults to `true`. |
| `aspectRatio` | number | `16 / 10` | Width over height of a slide. Defaults to `16 / 10`. |
| `defaultIndex` | number | `0` | The slide shown first. Defaults to `0`. |
| `onSlideChange` | func | — | Called with the new index whenever the slide changes. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names on the root, beside `plus-carousel`. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles on the root. |
| `aria-label` | requireName | — | Names the carousel region. This or `aria-labelledby` is required. |
| `aria-labelledby` | requireName | — | Names the carousel region by another element's id. This or `aria-label` is required. |

rankedText.usage:
Use `Carousel` for a few equal panels a person is invited to look through: what is
new, a short tour, a handful of featured items. Every slide but one is hidden at
any moment, so nothing a person must read or act on belongs in it.

`slides` takes `{ media, title, description }`. `media` is the card; `title`
and `description` fill the caption under the controls and name each step in the
progress indicator. Autoplay is on by default (`interval` `5000`), and loops.
`peek` shows the neighbors; turn it off to show the current slide alone.
`onSlideChange` gets the new index. Give the region a name with `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`.
rankedText.best:
### Keep it to three to six slides.

The progress indicator is the map. Past six, nobody gets to the end.

Do: Three slides, each worth seeing.
Don't: Ten slides and a long progress indicator to match.

### Give every slide a title.

The title is the caption a sighted reader sees and the name a screen reader hears on each step button.

Do: A title and one line for each slide.
Don't: No titles: the step buttons say only the slide number.

### Keep the caption to one line.

The caption holds two lines of room so the page does not jump. A paragraph pushes the page down every time the slide changes.

### Leave autoplay to slides that can be missed.

Autoplay moves on whether or not a person finished. Turn it off with `autoplay={false}` when a slide asks someone to read closely.

# Cascader

Cascader: a field that picks one path through nested options, one level at a time.

**Import:** `import { Cascader } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Cascader/Cascader.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Cascader/Cascader.stories.jsx` — Overview, EmptyPath, PreselectedPath, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled, FieldInvalid

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Cascader/Cascader.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Cascader` when a single path through a hierarchy is chosen one level at a time in sequence, such as district, then school, then grade.

## Motion

Cascader reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |
| change | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Columns and branches expand. |

## Alternatives

- For a hierarchy where someone may pick or view several nodes across branches at once, use `TreeSelect`.
- For a flat list of options with no hierarchy, use `Select`.

## Best practices

### Show the path while choosing. {#show-the-path-while-choosing}

An open cascader shows each level beside the last, so the path stays visible. Reopening a field with a path reveals every column up to its level, so any step can be changed without starting from the top.

### Disable a field that has nothing to offer yet. {#disable-a-field-that-has-nothing-to-offer-yet}

A dependent field stays disabled until its earlier answer exists.

Do: Disabled until the earlier answer is set.
Don't: An enabled field with no options to show.

### Show the chosen path in the field. {#show-the-chosen-path-in-the-field}

A filled field shows the choice; an empty one cannot confirm it. `value` is the whole path, outermost value first, and `onChange` fires with the path as each column is chosen. Pass and read the whole array, since the levels between are part of the answer.

Do: The field shows the whole chosen path.
Don't: An empty field after a choice cannot confirm it.

### Mark a failed pick on the field. {#mark-a-failed-pick-on-the-field}

With `isInvalid`, the field draws the danger border and `errorMessage` replaces the caption.

Do: A failed pick draws the danger border, so the error is seen at the field.
Don't: A failed pick still draws the normal border, so nothing marks the error.

## Accessibility

- **The field states the full path**, not just the deepest choice, so its
  accessible value matches what's visibly shown.
- **Without a visible label, name the field explicitly** with `aria-label`
  or `aria-labelledby`.
- **Disabled nodes are skipped, not just dimmed** — they take no focus and
  can't be chosen at any column.

## Related

- `TreeSelect`: use when expanding branches in place or selecting multiple nodes across a tree.
- `Select`: use when choosing from a flat list of options.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Field.** The box that shows the chosen path, its levels joined with a slash.
2. **Label.** Names the field. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text.
3. **Columns.** One column per level, opening to the right of the last.
4. **Caption.** Helper text, or the error that replaces it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge; the placeholder until a path is chosen. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down, and the press opens the columns. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Side padding | `--pad-x-md`. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Label and caption | `--body-sm`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`, error `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Menu | `--ds-surface-overlay` with a `--ds-border` edge, `--popup-radius` and `--ds-shadow-overlay`. |
| Column rule | `--border-width-default` in `--ds-border` between columns. |
| Option | `--control-md` high; hovered `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, chosen `--ds-background-selected` with `--ds-text-selected`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each level by what it is: "District", "School". | Names that only make sense at one level. |
| Keep each level's options short and parallel. | Mixed kinds of option in one column. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Pick a location". | "Required" or "Invalid". |
| Label the field with the whole path's subject: "Location". | A label for just the first level. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `name` | string | — | Submitted with a form through hidden inputs, one per path segment. |
| `label` | node | — | The visible label above the field. Without one, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `caption` | node | — | Help under the field. With `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` takes its place and is announced. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for the info tooltip beside the label. |
| `value` | arrayOf | `NO_PATH` | — |
| `options` | arrayOf | `[]` | — |
| `onChange` | func | — | — |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Please select'` | Hint text shown in the field while no path is selected. Defaults to `Please select`. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 40 and `compact` draws 32. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | — |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border, sets `aria-invalid`, and `errorMessage` becomes the announced caption. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | — |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

# ChangeTag

A small label for change over time, such as "+3 vs last week". The sign sets the arrow, `goodDirection` sets the tone, and the change is spoken in words. It is never a button.

Also asked as: delta tag, trend indicator.

**Import:** `import { ChangeTag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.stories.jsx` — Overview, Styles, Formats, CustomIcon, ValueChange, NeverAButton, UnknownValuesFallBack, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/ChangeTag/ChangeTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `ChangeTag` beside a number to say how it moved since the last period: in
a card header, a table cell or a chart tooltip. For the number itself, use plain text.

### Good direction

`goodDirection` says which way is good for this metric. The tone follows from
it, never from the arrow alone.

| Good direction | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Up | More is better: sessions held, reflections completed. Up is success, down is danger. |
| Down | Less is better: no-shows, absences, missed reflections. Down is success, up is danger. |
| None | The change has no value judgment: hours tutored, students assigned. Neutral either way. |

## Alternatives

- For a count on its own, use `CountTag`.
- For the condition something is in, use `StatusTag`.

## Best practices

### Set the tone from the metric, not the arrow. {#set-the-tone-from-the-metric-not-the-arrow}

Pass the signed change as a number and set `goodDirection` once per metric. When less is better, up is bad: say so with `goodDirection="down"`.

Do: More no-shows reads as danger.
Don't: More no-shows reads as success.

### Keep a change with no value judgment neutral. {#keep-a-change-with-no-value-judgment-neutral}

Not every change is good or bad. Leave `goodDirection` at `none` for those.

Do: Neutral: more hours is neither good nor bad.
Don't: Success implies a judgment nobody made.

### Never make a change tag a button. {#never-make-a-change-tag-a-button}

It renders a `span` with no role and no click handler: `onClick`, `role` and
`tabIndex` are dropped with a console warning in development.

## Accessibility

- **The change is spoken in words.** A screen reader hears "Up 3 vs last
  week" or "Down 12% vs last month"; the visible pill and comparison are
  `aria-hidden`, so nothing is read twice.
- **Color never carries it alone.** The arrow and the sign say the direction;
  the tone only reinforces it.
- **Not a control.** No role, no tab stop, no click handler.
- **Reduced motion.** The fade and the color change read the motion duration
  tokens, which drop to 0ms when reduced motion is on.

## Related

- `Sparkline`: use when showing the shape of a trend beside a metric and its `ChangeTag`.
- `CountTag`: use when showing an absolute count rather than a delta.

Same group: `CompetencyTag` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `StatusTag` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Arrow.** Up, down or flat, from the sign of `value`. `iconBefore` replaces it. It is decoration; the value and the spoken text say the direction.
2. **Value.** Signed: "+3", "−12%", "+4.5 pts". An em dash when there is nothing to compare.
3. **Pill.** A filled ground in the tone, with an inset border so the height stays exact.
4. **Comparison.** Optional, such as "vs last week", in subtle text after the pill.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. The tone (neutral, success, danger) comes from the sign and `goodDirection`. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. It is a label, not a control. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A label is never dimmed. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Height | `--label-height-sm` (16). |
| Padding and gap | `--pad-x-xs` on both sides, 2 between arrow and value, `--inline-sm` before the comparison. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`. |
| Neutral | `--ds-background-neutral` fill, `--ds-text` words, `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` edge. |
| Success | `--ds-background-success` fill, `--ds-text-success` words, `--ds-background-success-pressed` edge. |
| Danger | `--ds-background-danger` fill, `--ds-text-danger` words, `--ds-background-danger-pressed` edge. |
| Comparison | `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Motion | `--ds-motion-appearance-default` for both the value and the color. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the period: "vs last week", "vs last term". | Leave a change with no baseline when the period is not clear from the page. |
| Pass the raw signed number: `value={-12}` with `format="percent"`. | Pass a formatted string such as "-12%". |
| Use `null` when there is nothing to compare. | Show 0 for a missing comparison: 0 means no change. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | — | The signed change. Above zero is up, below is down, zero is flat; `null` shows an em dash and reads "No change data". |
| `format` | enum | `'number'` | `number` (+3), `percent` (+12%) or `points` (+3 pts). Always signed. |
| `goodDirection` | enum | `'none'` | Which way is good: `up` or `down` turn the tag success or danger; `none` keeps it neutral for a change with no value judgment. |
| `comparison` | node | — | What the change is measured against, such as "vs last week", in subtle text after the tag. |
| `iconBefore` | string | — | Replaces the direction arrow: a Font Awesome Free name (`arrow-trend-up`). Decorative; the words carry the direction. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the tag element beside the component's own. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the tag element. |

## Variants

**`format`** — `number` · `percent` · `points`

**`goodDirection`** — `up` · `down` · `none`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Checkbox/Checkbox.stories.jsx` — Overview, States, Content, Invalid, SelectAll, CheckboxGroup, Interactive, ReadOnly, DescriptionAndCard, KeyboardFocus, Keyboard, HoverStep, Unselected, Selected, Mixed, Disabled, DisabledWithReason, Required, Description, Card, Soft, Tile, TileNarrowLargeIllustrations

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Checkbox/Checkbox.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · goal `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.goal`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Checkbox` when a person needs to select one or more options from a list of related items, or when a setting needs an explicit confirmation before it applies. Checkboxes let a person choose many options, or none, from a short list they can see whole, and a parent checkbox shows the mixed (`isIndeterminate`) state while some of its children are selected.

## Motion

Checkbox reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |  |
| goal | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A session goal set or checked off together: the mark and fill change color, like any change. | `sound.goal` on land: only the session goal check-in done together, shared with the student; other checkboxes stay silent |

## Alternatives

- For a question offering a list of checkboxes under a shared legend and error, use `CheckboxGroup`.
- For a setting that takes effect immediately without submitting a form, use `Toggle`.
- For mutually exclusive answers where only one may be chosen, use `RadioGroup` or `Radio`.
- For a long list of multi-select options, use `Select` with `isMulti`.
- For a rows-by-columns matrix of checkboxes, use `ChoiceGrid`.

## Best practices

### Reserve choice tiles for one big question with two to four pictured options. {#reserve-choice-tiles-for-one-big-question-with-two-to-four-pictured-options}

Use `appearance="tile"` when a step asks one focal question with two to four options and every option carries an `illustration`. Keep ordinary form lists and sets of five or more options in `plain` or `card`.

Do: Two pictured tiles with top-end checkboxes for one focal question.
Don't: Plain text options without illustrations drawn as tiles.

### Say what is being agreed to. {#say-what-is-being-agreed-to}

The label states the commitment in a full phrase. "Yes" or "OK" hides what the person is accepting.

Do: The label names the agreement.
Don't: The label says nothing about what is accepted.

### Keep the label beside the box, in sentence case. {#keep-the-label-beside-the-box-in-sentence-case}

Sentence case reads as a statement. All caps and a trailing period read as a warning.

Do: Sentence case, no period.
Don't: All caps with a period.

### Keep each label to one line. {#keep-each-label-to-one-line}

A short label sits level with the box. A long one wraps and pushes the box away from its first line.

Do: One short line.
Don't: A label that wraps into a paragraph.

### Name the choice, not the instruction. {#name-the-choice-not-the-instruction}

Do: The label names the choice.
Don't: The label tells the person what to do with the box.

### Explain an invalid box; do not disable it. {#explain-an-invalid-box-do-not-disable-it}

Do: The invalid box keeps full contrast and stays in the tab order.
Don't: A disabled box cannot be tabbed to.

### Use read-only for fixed answers and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-answers-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` shows an answer that cannot be changed: the box stays in the tab order at full contrast with no hover (`aria-readonly`), ignores clicks and Space, and takes the neutral fill when unchecked. `isDisabled` removes it from the tab order and grays it when a prerequisite on the same screen is unmet. Put the reason in `description`, which stays at full contrast, never a tooltip. When it blocks the main action or several boxes, add a warning `SectionMessage` above that says how to turn them on. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

### Keep extra detail in `description`. {#keep-extra-detail-in-description}

`description` renders under the label and is wired with `aria-describedby`, so it is read after the name.

### Pick controlled or uncontrolled and stay there. {#pick-controlled-or-uncontrolled-and-stay-there}

```jsx
// Incorrect: `isChecked` being defined puts the component in controlled mode,
// which makes `defaultChecked` dead. The two never apply together.
<Checkbox id="terms" label="I accept" isChecked={accepted} defaultChecked />

// Correct: controlled needs a handler; uncontrolled needs neither.
<Checkbox id="terms" label="I accept" isChecked={accepted} onChange={onAccept} />
```

### Treat `isIndeterminate` as display only. {#treat-isindeterminate-as-display-only}

The underlying value is still checked or unchecked. Clicking a mixed box resolves it like any other, so it cannot be used as a third stored value.

## Accessibility

- **Label association.** The component derives an id for the input and label automatically; pass `aria-label` only when there is no visible label.
- **Do not disable a box that must stay reachable.** Use `isInvalid` with a message linked by `aria-describedby`, so a screen reader user hears why the option cannot be chosen. Include an error message for a required or invalid box, for example "Select an option".
- **`isRequired` sets `aria-required` on the checkbox**, whether or not `labelMarker="required"` is shown for a minority required field.
- **`isIndeterminate` is set on the DOM node** and announced as "mixed".
- **Keyboard.** `Space` toggles the focused checkbox; `Enter` does not. Keyboard focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the box; pointer focus draws none.

## Related

- `CheckboxGroup`: use when grouping checkboxes under a shared legend, value array and error.
- `Toggle`: use when turning a setting on or off takes effect immediately.
- `RadioGroup`: use when only one option may be chosen from a short list.
- `ChoiceGrid`: use when asking the same checkbox question across multiple rows.
- `Select`: use when choosing from a long list of options (`isMulti`).

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Box.** An 18 square with a 2px edge in `plain`, `card` and `tile`; visually hidden in `soft` while keeping native checkbox semantics, keyboard navigation, and form submission.
2. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the box in a 24 row. It names the checkbox. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text.
3. **Description.** Optional 12/16 text under the label that describes the choice. It does not name it.
4. **Appearances.** `plain` draws the box and label inline; `card` wraps them in a bordered surface row; `soft` draws a `--ds-background-neutral` row without a checkbox box (selected row shows `--ds-background-selected`, a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing `fa-solid fa-check` icon) for the majority selection type in a choice flow while the minority selection type keeps its visible control; `tile` draws a 224px pictured card with the checkbox at the top end.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-input` fill with a `--ds-border-input` edge; in `soft`, `--ds-background-neutral` fill with no border. |
| Hovered | Unselected: `--ds-background-input-hovered` with a `--ds-border-brand` edge (or `--ds-background-neutral-hovered` in `soft`). Selected: the hovered step of the selected bold fill (or `--ds-background-selected-hovered` in `soft`). |
| Pressed | In `soft`, an unselected row takes `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` and a selected row takes `--ds-background-selected-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the box (or around the row in `soft` and `tile`), for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill and `--ds-border-selected` edge; the check is `--ds-icon-inverse`. In `soft`, `--ds-background-selected` fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Mixed | The same fill and edge as selected; the mark is a dash in `--ds-icon-inverse` (or `fa-solid fa-minus` in `--ds-icon-selected` in `soft`). |
| Invalid | The unselected box or tile takes `--ds-border-danger` (in `soft`, both unselected and selected rows take `--ds-border-danger`). |
| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, `aria-readonly`, no hover; an unchecked box takes the `--ds-background-neutral` fill. Ignores clicks and Space. In `soft`, a checked row keeps its selected fill, edge and trailing check. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill, `--ds-border-disabled` edge, `--ds-icon-disabled` mark. Out of the tab order. In `soft`, the row takes the disabled fill and edge, with the check in `--ds-icon-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box fill | `--ds-background-input`; selected `--ds-background-selected-bold`. |
| Box edge | `--ds-border-input`; selected `--ds-border-selected`; invalid `--ds-border-danger`. |
| Box size, radius | `--checkbox-control-size` (18); `--radius-md`; `--border-width-selected` edge. |
| Row | `--control-sm` (24); gap `--inline-md`. |
| Label | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |
| Soft row | `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-background-neutral` fill at rest; selected `--ds-background-selected` fill, `--border-width-default` `--ds-border-selected` edge, and `--icon-sm` trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Choice tile | `--choice-tile-width` (224px), `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-surface` fill; selected 2px `--ds-border-selected` and `--ds-background-selected`, with the Checkbox at the top end. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write the label as the choice: "Email me a summary". | An instruction: "Check this box to receive an email summary." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Phrase every label in the positive: "Send reminders". | A negative that makes selecting mean "no": "Do not send reminders". |
| Say what to do in an error: "Select an option". | "Required" or "Invalid". |
| Put extra detail in the description: "Sent the evening before." | Stretch the label into a sentence. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` of the checkbox; the label points at it. Generated when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | The form key the box submits under, and sent in the `onChange` payload. |
| `label` | node | — | Text that names the checkbox |
| `value` | string or number | — | The value submitted with a form when the box is selected, and sent in the `onChange` payload. |
| `isChecked` | bool | — | Whether the box is selected. Pass it, with `onChange`, to control the checkbox. |
| `defaultChecked` | bool | — | Whether the box starts selected, when `isChecked` is not controlling it. |
| `isIndeterminate` | bool | `false` | Mixed state, for a parent of partly selected children |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Marks the unselected box as failing validation |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disable the checkbox |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shown and announced, not changeable |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Minority marker after the label |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Set aria-required on the checkbox |
| `description` | node | — | Secondary text under the label. It describes the box and does not name it. |
| `illustration` | node | — | Decorative picture shown above the label when `appearance` is `tile`. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'plain'` | `plain` (default) draws the box and label inline; `card` draws a bordered row; `soft` draws a neutral row without a checkbox; `tile` draws a centered pictured tile with the checkbox at its top end. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with `{ target: { name, value, checked } }` when the box is toggled. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the checkbox gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the checkbox loses focus. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event on the checkbox. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the field wrapper beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the field wrapper. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

**`appearance`** — `plain` · `card` · `soft` · `tile`

# CheckboxGroup

CheckboxGroup — one question and its checkbox answers, any number of which may be chosen. Mirrors `RadioGroup` on `Fieldset`: a `<fieldset>` named by `legend`, stacked or inline (wrapping 224px tiles when `appearance` is `tile`), with an array `value`, `onChange(nextArray)`, and one group `error` announced via `Fieldset`. `isDisabled` on the group overrides every `Checkbox`'s own.

**Import:** `import { CheckboxGroup } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CheckboxGroup/CheckboxGroup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CheckboxGroup/CheckboxGroup.stories.jsx` — Overview, Orientation, Descriptions, Reveal, Soft, Tiles, Unselected, Selected, Required, Invalid, ReadOnly, Disabled, TileRest, TileHovered, TileSelected, TileFocused, TileInvalid, TileReadOnly, TileDisabled, SoftRest, SoftHovered, SoftPressed, SoftSelected, SoftSelectedHovered, SoftFocused, SoftInvalid, SoftInvalidSelected, SoftReadOnly, SoftDisabled, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CheckboxGroup/CheckboxGroup.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `CheckboxGroup` for one question where a person may pick several answers — or none — from a short list visible all at once. It mirrors `RadioGroup` on `Fieldset`, owning the `legend`, the array `value`, and a single group `error` so each option stays a plain `Checkbox`.

## Motion

CheckboxGroup reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |

## Alternatives

- For a single standalone confirmation or a select-all tree, use `Checkbox`.
- For mutually exclusive answers where only one may be chosen, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a long list of multi-select options, use `Select` with `isMulti`.

## Best practices

### Mark the minority selection type in a flow of choice questions. {#mark-the-minority-selection-type-in-a-flow-of-choice-questions}

In a flow of choice questions (onboarding, quizzes, check-ins, surveys), pick one default selection type for the flow: the majority type uses `appearance="soft"` without a visible radio dot or checkbox box, while the minority type keeps its visible control (`card` or `plain`) so people notice when a question works differently, following the same exception-marking rule as required and optional fields on [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs).

Do: In a mostly single-select flow, the minority multi-select question keeps its visible checkboxes so multi-select is unmistakable.
Don't: Both the majority single-select questions and the minority multi-select question hide their controls, so nothing signals that multiple answers work here.

### Name the question with a legend. {#name-the-question-with-a-legend}

The `legend` tells people what the checkboxes answer and names the `<fieldset>` for assistive technology.

Do: A visible legend names the question.
Don't: Checkboxes with no visible question.

### Reserve choice tiles for one big question with two to four pictured options. {#reserve-choice-tiles-for-one-big-question-with-two-to-four-pictured-options}

Use `appearance="tile"` when a step asks one focal question with two to four options and every option carries an `illustration`. Keep ordinary form lists and sets of five or more options in `plain` or `card`.

Do: Two pictured options for one focal question.
Don't: An ordinary list without illustrations drawn as tiles.

### Explain an error once under the group. {#explain-an-error-once-under-the-group}

Pass `error` on `CheckboxGroup` so one message explains what to fix, rather than repeating an error under every box.

Do: One error explains what to select.
Don't: Invalid borders with no explanation.

## Accessibility

- **Native `<fieldset>` grouping.** `Fieldset` wires the `legend` to name the group so screen readers announce the question when entering the checkboxes.
- **Standard checkbox keyboard behavior.** `Tab` moves between checkboxes in the group and `Space` toggles the focused checkbox, in plain, card and tile appearances alike.
- **Decorative illustrations.** In `tile` appearance, `illustration` is marked `aria-hidden="true"` so each tile is announced by its `label`, `description` (`aria-describedby`), and checked state.
- **One error, announced once.** `error` renders a single `role="alert"` message linked to the `<fieldset>` via `aria-describedby`.

## Related

- `Checkbox`: use when there is a single confirmation or a parent-child select-all list.
- `RadioGroup`: use when only one option may be chosen.
- `Select`: use when the list is too long to show all at once, with `isMulti`.
- `Fieldset`: use when grouping mixed form controls under a legend.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Legend.** The question. It names the `<fieldset>` and carries an optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) in plain text.
2. **Options.** Checkboxes in a stacked list, an inline row, bordered `card` rows, `soft` rows without a visible checkbox box, or 224px `tile` cards.
3. **Tile checkbox and illustration.** When `appearance` is `tile`, each tile centers its decorative `illustration`, `label`, and `description`, and anchors its `Checkbox` at the top end so multi-select is clear before clicking.
4. **Reveal.** Optional content under an option, shown while that option is selected.
5. **Error.** One message under the group, tied to the `<fieldset>` with `aria-describedby`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Plain/card as Checkbox; `soft` uses `--ds-background-neutral` with no border; tile uses `--ds-surface` fill and 1px `--ds-border` edge. |
| Hovered | Plain/card as Checkbox; unselected `soft` uses `--ds-background-neutral-hovered`; unselected tile uses `--ds-surface-hovered` and `--ds-border-brand`; selected `soft` and tile use `--ds-background-selected-hovered`. |
| Selected | Each selected Checkbox takes `--ds-background-selected-bold`; a selected `soft` row takes `--ds-background-selected`, a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing `fa-solid fa-check` icon in `--ds-icon-selected`; a selected tile takes `--ds-background-selected` and a 2px `--ds-border-selected` edge. |
| Pressed | In `soft`, an unselected row steps to `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` and a selected row steps to `--ds-background-selected-pressed`. |
| Focused | 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`: around the box in plain/card, and outside the row or tile in `soft` and `tile` appearances. |
