# ChoiceGrid

ChoiceGrid — the same question asked of several rows, as a table. Each cell is the real Checkbox or Radio, named by its row and its column.

Also asked as: matrix question.

**Import:** `import { ChoiceGrid } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.stories.jsx` — Overview, Variants, Layout, Size, InteractionStates, TwoGridsWithoutIds, ReadOnly, Interactive, Keyboard, Unselected, Selected, Hovered, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/ChoiceGrid/ChoiceGrid.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `ChoiceGrid` when the same question is asked of several items at once, as a matrix with the answer scale in the column headers and one subject per row.

It is fully controlled: `values` is `{ rowId: columnId }` in `radio` mode and `{ rowId: { columnId: boolean } }` in `checkbox` mode, and the component holds no state of its own.

## Motion

ChoiceGrid reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |

## Alternatives

- For a single question with mutually exclusive answers, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a single question with multi-select answers, use `CheckboxGroup`.
- For displaying rows and columns of read-only data, use `Table`.

## Best practices

### `onChange` has two shapes, and only one of them is the new state. {#onchange-has-two-shapes-and-only-one-of-them-is-the-new-state}

```jsx
// radio: the two ids that changed. Merge them yourself.
<ChoiceGrid type="radio" values={v} rows={rows} columns={cols}
            onChange={(rowId, columnId) => setV({ ...v, [rowId]: columnId })} />

// checkbox: the whole new values object, already merged.
<ChoiceGrid type="checkbox" values={v} rows={rows} columns={cols}
            onChange={(next) => setV(next)} />
```

In checkbox mode the merge copies the top level and the row it changes, so the `values` you passed in is left as it was and can be compared against the next one.

### A radio row cannot be unanswered again. {#a-radio-row-cannot-be-unanswered-again}

Selecting a column always sets it; there is no path back to "not answered". If that state is meaningful, add a column for it. "Not applicable" as a real option is better than a row the user cannot clear.

### Keep the grid small. {#keep-the-grid-small}

Every cell is a control, so a six-by-five grid is thirty tab stops. Past that, ask the questions one at a time with Radio group.

### Give the grid a question above it. {#give-the-grid-a-question-above-it}

Do: A question above the grid that every row answers.
Don't: The same grid with no question: nothing says what the scale measures.

### Radio grid for one answer per row. {#radio-grid-for-one-answer-per-row}

The control type tells people how many answers a row takes.

Do: Radios, for one preferred time each day.
Don't: Checkboxes for the same single-answer rows.

### Checkbox grid for several answers. {#checkbox-grid-for-several-answers}

Checkboxes signal that a row accepts more than one answer.

Do: Checkboxes, for every tool each tutor uses.
Don't: Radios, where several tools apply to a row.

### Keep one size per grid. {#keep-one-size-per-grid}

Mixed control sizes make a grid hard to scan. `size` is set per grid, so grids that sit together in one form share it too.

Do: One size (`size={14}`) across both grids.
Don't: A `size={12}` grid under a `size={14}` grid.

## Accessibility

- **Every cell is named by its row and its column.** Each input carries `aria-labelledby` pointing at both the row label and the column header, so it is announced as "Punctuality, Agree" rather than as an unnamed radio in a table.
- **Every cell is the real control.** Cells render Checkbox and Radio, so focus, states and read-only behave as they do anywhere else.
- **Radio rows are grouped per row.** Each row's inputs share a `name` built from the grid's id and the row's id, which makes one answer per row and arrow-key movement along it. With no `id` or `name` the grid generates its own base, so two grids on a page never share ids or radio groups.
- **The grid itself has no name.** There is no caption and no `aria-label` on the table. Put the question above it as a heading, and describe the scale in the column headers.
- **The row-header column is empty on purpose.** It carries a visually hidden "Row" so the header row is not a blank cell.
- **On a narrow screen this is a wide table.** Put it in a horizontal scroll area rather than letting the columns crush.

## Related

- `RadioGroup`: use when asking a single radio question or a linear scale (`leadingText` and `trailingText`).
- `CheckboxGroup`: use when asking a single multi-select question.
- `Table`: use when displaying data rather than collecting answers.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Column headers.** The answer scale. They name every cell in their column.
2. **Row labels.** The subject of each row. They name every cell in their row.
3. **Cells.** A real Radio or Checkbox, centered, with no visible label of its own.
4. **Row-header corner.** Empty on purpose; it carries a visually hidden "Row".

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Each cell shows its Radio or Checkbox at rest, unselected. |
| Hovered | As the Radio or Checkbox in the cell: the input hovered fill and a brand edge. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered look holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | As the control in the cell: a 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Selected | As the control in the cell: the selected bold fill. |
| Read-only | Full contrast, cells stay in the tab order with `aria-readonly`; changes are ignored. |
| Disabled | Cells take the disabled fill and edge and leave the tab order; header text uses a solid muted token, not opacity. |
| Invalid | Not drawn by the grid. Put the message above it and mark the question there. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `--ds-surface-sunken` on the table, headers, labels and cells. |
| Padding | `--pad-y-md` and `--pad-x-md` on headers, labels and cells. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`. |
| Text | `--ds-text`, body default, or the label font `size` picks. |
| Control | `--checkbox-control-size`, or `--choice-grid-control-size-10` and `-12` through `size`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write column headers as the scale: "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often". | Bare numbers with no meaning attached. |
| Keep row labels short and parallel; they do not wrap. | A sentence per row. |
| Phrase the question above the grid so every row answers it. | A different question in each row. |
| Keep column headers short and the same length. | A header the person cannot read at a glance. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `name` | string | — | — |
| `type` | enum | `'radio'` | Type of selection: radio (single) or checkbox (multiple) |
| `rows` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | — |
| `columns` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | — |
| `values` | object | `{}` | Radio: `{ rowId: columnId }`. Checkbox: `{ rowId: { columnId: boolean } }`. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disable the choice grid |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shown and focusable, not changeable. |
| `size` | enum | — | Option-label font size in px, and the control width that goes with it. Unset keeps the default rendering. |
| `onChange` | func | — | — |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

## Variants

**`type`** — `radio` · `checkbox`

**`size`** — `12` · `14` · `16`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

`--body-default` · `--body-lg` · `--body-sm` · `--checkbox-control-size` · `--choice-grid-control-size-10` · `--choice-grid-control-size-12` · `--ds-surface-sunken` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-y-md` · `--table-radius`

# CloseButton

The one dismiss control for a surface that closes as a whole — Modal, Section message, Flag. An Icon button, subtle, fixed to the × glyph. `label` is required: "Close" for a surface that blocks (Modal), "Dismiss {what}" for a message. `appearance="inverse"` is for colored or dark grounds, where the subtle appearance's own hover and pressed read as nearly invisible. There is no disabled state: a close control is always available.

**Import:** `import { CloseButton } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Spacing, Tones, Focus, InverseGrounds, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/CloseButton/CloseButton.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `CloseButton` wherever a surface closes as a whole, such as the corner of a `Modal`, the end of a `SectionMessage`, a `Flag` or a `Panel`.

## Motion

CloseButton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Hover and press change color, 90% by about 110 ms. |

## Alternatives

- For removing one item from a set or using a different glyph, use `IconButton`.
- For a labeled Cancel action in a footer, use `Button`.

## Best practices

### Sit top-right in its container. {#sit-top-right-in-its-container}

The close button anchors the top-right corner of the modal, panel or message it closes.

Do: Top-right of the message.
Don't: Bottom-left, under the content.

### Name what it closes. {#name-what-it-closes}

Use "Close" for a surface that blocks, like a Modal, and "Dismiss" plus what goes away for a message: "Dismiss update", "Dismiss message". The × glyph is the same either way, so `label` is the only thing that tells a screen reader user what just went away.

```jsx
<CloseButton label="Dismiss update" onClick={dismiss} />
```

### Use inverse only on colored grounds. {#use-inverse-only-on-colored-grounds}

The inverse appearance is for the declared colored and dark grounds. Neutral surfaces use default.

Do: Default appearance on a neutral surface.
Don't: Inverse appearance on a neutral surface: the glyph disappears.

### Close a whole surface, not one item. {#close-a-whole-surface-not-one-item}

A close button dismisses the surface it sits on. To remove one item from a set, use an `IconButton` with its own icon and label.

Do: One close button for the whole message.
Don't: A close button on each item inside the message.

### Keep the close button enabled. {#keep-the-close-button-enabled}

A close control stays available even while the surface it closes is loading or in error. `CloseButton` has no disabled prop.

## Accessibility

- **A real, always-focusable button.** Reached with Tab and activated with Enter or Space, same as any `IconButton`.
- **The accessible name is the whole contract.** The `xmark` glyph is decorative; `label` is the accessible name and hover title, so it must say what closes.
- **The inverse appearance preserves contrast** on dark or bold-colored surfaces.

## Related

- `IconButton`: use when removing a single item or using a glyph other than `xmark`.
- `Modal`: use when a dialog closes from its corner.
- `SectionMessage`: use when an in-page notice can be dismissed.
- `Flag`: use when a corner notification can be dismissed.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Container.** A subtle Icon button, 32 at default spacing and 24 at compact.
2. **Glyph.** The `xmark` glyph at 16, always drawn.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill: the glyph alone, in either appearance. |
| Hovered | Default: the neutral subtle hovered fill. Inverse: `--ds-interaction-inverse-hovered`. |
| Pressed | Default: the neutral subtle pressed fill. Inverse: `--ds-interaction-inverse-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`; `--ds-border-focused-inverse` for the inverse appearance. |
| Disabled | There is none. A close control is always available. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill, default appearance | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle`, hovered and pressed steps. |
| Glyph, inverse appearance | `--ds-icon-inverse`; text `--ds-text-inverse`. |
| Size | 32: `--control-md`. 24: `--control-sm`. Square. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say what closes: "Close filters", "Dismiss message". | A bare "Close", or a label that repeats the glyph: "X icon". |
| Use "Close" for a surface people can reopen and "Dismiss" for a message they are done with. | The same word for both, or "Cancel", which names a different action. |
| Use sentence case. | Title case or all capitals. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | string | `'Close'` | "Close" for a surface that blocks; "Dismiss {what}" for a message |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | `default` on neutral surfaces; `inverse` only on the declared colored and dark grounds |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event. The surface that owns the close button closes itself here. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the button beside the component's own. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `inverse`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

Use "Close" for a surface that blocks, like a Modal, and "Dismiss" plus what goes away for a message: "Dismiss update", "Dismiss message". The × glyph is the same either way, so `label` is the only thing that tells a screen reader user what just went away.

```jsx
<CloseButton label="Dismiss update" onClick={dismiss} />
```

### Use inverse only on colored grounds.

The inverse appearance is for the declared colored and dark grounds. Neutral surfaces use default.

Do: Default appearance on a neutral surface.
Don't: Inverse appearance on a neutral surface: the glyph disappears.

### Close a whole surface, not one item.

A close button dismisses the surface it sits on. To remove one item from a set, use an `IconButton` with its own icon and label.

Do: One close button for the whole message.
Don't: A close button on each item inside the message.

### Keep the close button enabled.

A close control stays available even while the surface it closes is loading or in error. `CloseButton` has no disabled prop.

# Code

An inline snippet for a short piece of code inside a sentence. It is a `code` element in the code typeface at 0.875 of the text around it, on a neutral fill, so it follows a paragraph or a heading without a size of its own.

**Import:** `import { Code } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`)

**Governed by:** Empty (`ds guide empty`); Errors (`ds guide errors`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Code/Code.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Code/Code.stories.jsx` — Overview, InHeading, WrapsAtTheEdge, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, NotAControl

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Code/Code.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Code` for a name, command, value or snippet that sits inside a sentence:
a function, a file path, a flag, a token.

The typeface and size come from the `--code-default` text style (`0.875em`, scaling
with the surrounding text).

## Alternatives

- For several lines of code or a snippet with line numbers, use `CodeBlock`.

## Best practices

### Keep inline code to a short phrase. {#keep-inline-code-to-a-short-phrase}

A long inline span wraps awkwardly and loses its structure. A block keeps lines and scroll.

Do: Several lines go in a code block.
Don't: A whole instruction in inline code.

### Do not use it for emphasis. {#do-not-use-it-for-emphasis}

`Code` tells readers "this is literal text to type". Use bold or a button label for emphasis.

Do: Bold for emphasis, in the reader's words.
Don't: Inline code on a word that is not code.

### Write it as the reader would type it. {#write-it-as-the-reader-would-type-it}

Do: The exact name, with its brackets.
Don't: A trailing period inside the span, which the reader may type.

## Accessibility

- **Announced as text.** `Code` renders a `code` element; screen readers read it as
  ordinary text, so write the code so it makes sense spoken.
- **Contrast.** The ink on the fill passes in every color mode, because both
  come from the neutral background and code ink tokens.
- **It wraps.** Long values break inside the element, so reflow at narrow widths and
  200% zoom does not scroll the page.

## Related

- `CodeBlock`: use when displaying several lines of code with line numbers or line highlights.

Same group: `CodeBlock` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `StaticTable` · `TreeTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Element.** A `code` element in the code typeface at `0.875` of the text around it.
2. **Fill.** The neutral ground (`--ds-background-neutral`), with `--radius-md`.
3. **Text.** The code ink (`--ds-text-code-default`); long values wrap inside the span.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Neutral fill with the code ink. |
| Hovered, pressed | Does not react. |
| Focused | Not a control; Tab skips it. |
| Disabled | Not applicable; never dimmed. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Typeface, size | `--code-default` |
| Fill | `--ds-background-neutral` |
| Ink | `--ds-text-code-default` |
| Padding, radius | `--space-025`, `--radius-md` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use it for a name, command, value or flag: `getSession()`. | Use it for emphasis or a product name. |
| Write the code exactly as the reader would type it. | Add punctuation or a trailing period inside the element. |
| Keep it to a short phrase. | Put several lines in it; use a code block. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | The code, as text. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra classes for placement, such as spacing. |

## Tokens touched

`--code-default` · `--ds-background-neutral` · `--ds-text-code-default` · `--pad-x-xs` · `--radius-md`

From `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/Code/Code.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

# CodeBlock

A block of code in the code typeface on the code surface, with optional line numbers and highlighted lines. Long lines scroll sideways inside a focusable, named region, or fold onto the next line when `wrap` is on. It does not color syntax: the text is one ink, and `language` is recorded for tools.

**Import:** `import { CodeBlock } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.stories.jsx` — Overview, WithoutLineNumbers, HighlightedLines, SeparateHighlights, ScrollsLongLines, WrapsLongLines, BlankLines, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, WrapNotFocusable

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/CodeBlock/CodeBlock.mdx`

## Usage

Use `CodeBlock` for code a reader may copy or follow line by line: an example,
a command sequence, a config file.

## Alternatives

- For a name or short phrase inside a sentence, use `Code`.

## Best practices

### Scroll commands, wrap prose. {#scroll-commands-wrap-prose}

Scroll keeps line structure, which matters for shell commands and config, where a fold could read as a new line. Wrap suits prose-like output in a narrow column.

Do: A command scrolls, so one line stays one line.
Don't: A command folded onto a second line reads like two commands.

### Name each block when there are several on a page. {#name-each-block-when-there-are-several-on-a-page}

Do: Each region says what it holds: Install command.
Don't: Every block named Code snippet.

### State what a highlight points at in prose. {#state-what-a-highlight-points-at-in-prose}

Do: The sentence says which line to read, and the highlight supports it.
Don't: The fill is the only cue.

### Keep line numbers for code you discuss. {#keep-line-numbers-for-code-you-discuss}

Do: A one-line command with no gutter.
Don't: A line number beside a single command.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard scroll.** A scrolling block is a focusable region with a name, so a
  keyboard user can scroll it with the arrow keys. A wrapping block has nothing
  to scroll and is not a tab stop.
- **Highlights are spoken.** Each highlighted run is bracketed by "Highlight
  start" and "Highlight end" for screen readers, because fill alone says nothing
  to them. Those words are not selectable, so they stay out of a copy.
- **Line numbers are skipped.** The gutter is hidden from assistive technology and
  cannot be selected, so a copy is the code alone.
- **Contrast.** Ink, gutter and highlight come from the code color roles and keep
  their contrast in every color and contrast mode.

## Related

- `Code`: use when formatting a short identifier or command inline within prose.

Same group: `Code` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `StaticTable` · `TreeTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Surface.** The code ground with a hairline edge and `--radius-md`.
2. **Gutter.** Optional line numbers, skipped by screen readers.
3. **Line.** One per line of text; a highlighted line has its own ground.
4. **Region.** The scrolling block, focusable and named when it does not wrap.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Code ground and ink; highlighted lines on the highlight fill. |
| Hovered, pressed | The block does not react. |
| Focused | A scrolling block shows the focus ring inset; a wrapping block is not focusable. |
| Disabled | Not applicable. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Typeface | `--code-default` at `--type-size-0875`, line height `--type-line-height-125` |
| Surface, ink | `--ds-background-code-default`, `--ds-text-code-default` |
| Gutter | `--ds-background-code-gutter`, `--ds-text-code-gutter` |
| Highlight | `--ds-background-code-highlight` |
| Edge, radius | `--ds-border`, `--radius-md` |
| Ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Show the smallest snippet that makes the point. | Paste a whole file. |
| Name the language in prose before the block. | Leave the reader to guess the language or the file name. |
| Highlight the lines the text is about. | Highlight most of the block. |
| Give each block a `label` when a page has several. | Leave several blocks with the same name. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | `''` | The code, with lines separated by newlines. |
| `language` | string | — | The language, recorded as a `language- ` class for tools that read it. It does not color the text. |
| `showLineNumbers` | bool | `true` | Whether each line is numbered in a gutter that screen readers skip. |
| `highlight` | string or number or arrayOf | — | Lines to highlight: a string such as "2,4-6", or an array such as [1, 3]. Start and end are announced to screen readers. |
| `wrap` | bool | `false` | Fold long lines onto the next line instead of scrolling sideways. |
| `label` | string | `'Code snippet'` | The name of the scrolling region a screen reader announces. Unused when `wrap` is on. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra classes for placement, such as spacing. |

## Tokens touched

`--body-default` · `--border-width-default` · `--card-radius` · `--ds-background-code-default` · `--ds-background-code-gutter` · `--ds-background-code-highlight` · `--ds-border` · `--ds-border-focused` · `--ds-text-code-default` · `--ds-text-code-gutter` · `--focus-ring-width` · `--pad-x-lg` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-y-lg` · `--plus-code-block-digits` · `--plus-code-block-gutter` · `--type-family-code` · `--type-line-height-125`

# Comment

Comment: one entry in a threaded discussion, with slots for the author, time, content, actions and replies.

**Import:** `import { Comment } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Comment/Comment.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Comment/Comment.stories.jsx` — Basic, Saving, Highlighted, Edited, Restricted, WithNestedReplies, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Comment/Comment.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Comment` for one entry in a threaded discussion, such as a note on a session or a reply in a review thread.

## Alternatives

- For a plain multi-line input with no author or thread context, use `TextArea`.
- For formatted notes with lists or links, use `RichTextEditor`.

## Best practices

### Nest replies through `nestedReplies`, not by composing comments yourself. {#nest-replies-through-nestedreplies-not-by-composing-comments-yourself}

Passing replies through `nestedReplies` opens a heading context at `headingLevel`, so any `Heading` inside the reply tree nests one level deeper automatically. Composing comments directly without this prop skips that step.

```jsx
<Comment
    author="Jane Park"
    time="2h ago"
    content="Looks good to me."
    nestedReplies={<Comment author="Sam Lee" time="1h ago" content="Agreed." />}
/>
```

### Swap `actions` for `savingText` with `isSaving`; do not hide them yourself. {#swap-actions-for-savingtext-with-issaving-do-not-hide-them-yourself}

Set `isSaving` rather than conditionally rendering `actions`. It keeps the saving state in one prop instead of two places making the same decision.

Do: While the reply saves, the saving text replaces the Reply action.
Don't: The Reply action stays live, with nothing to say a reply is saving.

### Show who wrote it and when. {#show-who-wrote-it-and-when}

Every comment names its author and time. Anonymous, undated comments cannot be trusted or followed up.

Do: Author and time are both present.
Don't: No name, no time.

### Write the comment as a plain sentence. {#write-the-comment-as-a-plain-sentence}

Sentence case, normal punctuation. Capitals and stacked marks read as shouting.

Do: A plain question.
Don't: All caps, stacked marks.

### Ask for one clear thing. {#ask-for-one-clear-thing}

Name the action and the detail. An open "Thoughts?" leaves the reader guessing.

Do: One action, one detail.
Don't: No action named.

## Accessibility

- **A real article.** Each comment is an `<article>`, giving assistive technology a landmark per entry in the thread.
- **Replies nest their headings correctly.** Because `nestedReplies` opens its own heading context, a reply thread's headings read in the right outline order rather than all landing at the same level.
- **Restricted visibility is stated, not just implied.** `restrictedTo` renders as visible text in the header, so who can see the comment is not communicated by color or icon alone.

## Related

- `Avatar`: use when rendering the author's image beside the comment.
- `TextArea`: use when collecting a plain multi-line reply or note.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Avatar.** Sits beside the comment's content.
2. **Header.** The author, the time, an edited marker and, when restricted, who the comment is visible to.
3. **Content.** The comment body.
4. **Actions**, or **saving text** in their place while a change is in flight.
5. **Nested replies.** Sit below, indented, at one heading level deeper through `headingLevel`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Saving | The actions give way to the saving text in `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Highlighted | The comment takes `--ds-background-selected`. |

A comment has no hover, pressed, focus or disabled state of its own. The actions a caller passes in carry theirs.

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Author | Body default, semibold. |
| Time, edited, restricted, saving | `--ds-text-subtle`, body small. |
| Highlight fill | `--ds-background-selected`. |
| Padding and gaps | `--comment-pad`, `--comment-gap`, `--inline-lg`, `--stack-md`, `--stack-sm`. |
| Replies indent and rule | `--comment-replies-stack`, `--comment-replies-indent`; `--ds-border`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Show the author's name as people know them: "Ari Patel". | A username or an id. |
| Write the time as relative or dated text: "2h ago", "Oct 21". | A raw timestamp: "2026-10-21T14:03:11Z". |
| State who can see a restricted comment: "Visible to staff only". | A lock icon with no words. |
| Name the action in the saving text: "Saving your reply…". | A bare "Loading". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `avatar` | node | — | — |
| `author` | node | — | — |
| `time` | node | — | — |
| `edited` | node | — | — |
| `content` | node | — | — |
| `actions` | node | — | — |
| `nestedReplies` | node | — | — |
| `isSaving` | bool | `false` | Hides `actions` and shows `savingText` instead. |
| `savingText` | node | `'Saving…'` | — |
| `isHighlighted` | bool | `false` | — |
| `restrictedTo` | node | — | — |
| `type` | string | — | — |
| `headingLevel` | enum | `2` | The heading level `nestedReplies` opens at, via HeadingContextProvider. |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`headingLevel`** — `1` · `2` · `3` · `4` · `5` · `6`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

# CompetencyTag

A tag for one of the five competency areas. The `subject` fixes its color and leading icon, and the rest is passed to Tag.

Also asked as: skill tag.

**Import:** `import { CompetencyTag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CompetencyTag/CompetencyTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CompetencyTag/CompetencyTag.stories.jsx` — Overview, CustomLabel, PassesThroughTagProps, UnknownSubjectFallsBack, BesideHeading, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CompetencyTag/CompetencyTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `CompetencyTag` wherever training content, a tutor's strengths or a feedback
item is tagged by competency area. `CompetencyTag` fixes the color and icon per
subject and delegates every other behavior to `Tag`.

### Subject guidance

| Subject | Icon | Default label |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `social-emotional` | heart | Social-emotional |
| `mastering-content` | book | Mastering content |
| `advocacy` | bullhorn | Advocacy |
| `relationship` | handshake | Relationship |
| `technology-tools` | laptop-code | Technology tools |

Each subject's color and icon are fixed: there is no prop to mix a subject's
meaning with a different color.

## Alternatives

- For a category outside the five competency areas, use `Tag`.
- For a workflow condition such as "Completed" or "Needs review", use `StatusTag`.

## Best practices

### Keep the subject's own name. {#keep-the-subject-s-own-name}

The label defaults to the subject name; a long rewrite breaks the one-line tag. Override it with `children` or `text` only when the surrounding content needs a shorter or longer phrasing.

Do: The subject name.
Don't: A long custom label.

### Show each subject once. {#show-each-subject-once}

Repeating a subject adds nothing; a row lists the different subjects.

Do: Distinct subjects.
Don't: The same subject three times.

### Keep the icon with its label. {#keep-the-icon-with-its-label}

The icon is part of the subject's identity, so it is never dropped. A plain `Tag` in the subject's color loses it.

Do: Icon and label.
Don't: Label without the icon.

### Write the current spelling. {#write-the-current-spelling}

`socio-emotional` and `relationships` are accepted and map to
`social-emotional` and `relationship`. Write new code with the current
spelling; the aliases exist for content written before it changed.

## Accessibility

- **Inherits `Tag`'s accessibility.** Selection, removal and link behavior
  are unchanged; see `Tag`'s Accessibility section for the full contract.
- **The subject icon is decorative.** It is `aria-hidden`; the subject's name
  is carried by the visible label, not the icon.

## Related

- `Tag`: use when configuring selection, removal, links or elevation on a `CompetencyTag`.
- `TagGroup`: use when laying out a set of competency tags with shared spacing and overflow.

# CountTag

CountTag: a number on its own, as a near-square countTag.

Also asked as: counter, unread count, numeric badge.

**Import:** `import { CountTag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CountTag/CountTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CountTag/CountTag.stories.jsx` — Appearances, Size, Max, Zero, Ring, Styles, DotNeedsALabel, LabeledNumber, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/CountTag/CountTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `CountTag` for a number on its own: unread messages on a nav item, results on a
tab, errors in a section header, a notification on a bell. It is always `16` tall,
including inside `Button`, `Tabs`, `Sidebar` rows, `StatusTag` (`trailingMetric`)
and selectable `Tag` (`trailingMetric`).

## Alternatives

- For the condition something is in, use `StatusTag`.
- For a change over time such as "+3 vs last week", use `ChangeTag`.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a category or subject or person, use `Tag`.
- For progress toward a total, use `ProgressBar`.

## Best practices

### Keep most counts quiet. {#keep-most-counts-quiet}

Subtle neutral is the default. Bold asks for action now, so use at most one bold count per area.

Do: Subtle neutral by default, with bold only where something needs doing now.
Don't: Bold on every item in a list: when every count shouts, none of them does.

### Let the component decide zero and overflow. {#let-the-component-decide-zero-and-overflow}

It renders nothing at `value={0}` and caps past `max` with a `+`, so pass the raw number.

Do: Pass the raw number: at zero the tag leaves the empty tab bare.
Don't: Force a zero onto an empty tab, unless the zero is the news.

### Show the bare number, and put the meaning in the label. {#show-the-bare-number-and-put-the-meaning-in-the-label}

The tag shows the number alone, never words alongside it; `label="4 unread messages"` tells a screen reader what it counts.

### Use inverse on filled buttons and dark surfaces. {#use-inverse-on-filled-buttons-and-dark-surfaces}

Inverse is a solid light ground with dark text, so it passes contrast on any fill. On a light surface use subtle.

Do: Inverse on a filled, dark ground.
Don't: Inverse on a light surface, where it barely separates from the page.

### Give a dot a name. {#give-a-dot-a-name}

A dot has no number, so `label` is its accessible name; without one it is announced as nothing.

## Accessibility

- **A dot needs a name.** It has no number, so `label` is its accessible name,
  exposed as an image with that name. Without one it is announced as nothing,
  and the component warns in development.
- **A label turns a digit into information.** "Messages 4" is ambiguous; with
  `label="4 unread"` a screen reader hears "Messages 4 unread", while the tag
  still shows 4.
- **The count is not a control.** It is a `span` that sits inside buttons, tabs
  and nav items; whatever is pressable is the thing around it.
- **Contrast.** Subtle uses each appearance's text color, and bold warning uses the
  warning inverse pair so it clears AA. Inverse clears AA on any bold fill, including
  a primary button.

## Related

- `StatusTag`: use when nesting a `CountTag` inside a condition label through `trailingMetric`.
- `Tag`: use when nesting a `CountTag` on a selectable filter tag through `trailingMetric`.

Same group: `ChangeTag` · `CompetencyTag` · `DateTag` · `StatusTag` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Number.** The count in the body-sm size with tabular digits, hidden at 0 unless `showZero`, capped at `max` with a `+`.
2. **Pill.** `16` tall, `24` wide at minimum, so one digit is a small rectangle and more digits grow it from the trailing edge.
3. **Dot.** Presence without a number: an `8` circle that needs a `label` for its name.
4. **Ring.** Optional, in the surface color, for a count pinned to the corner of an icon or an avatar.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. Subtle neutral by default; bold, inverse and the dot are choices of ground, not states. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. It is a label, not a control; the thing around it is what responds. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A label is never dimmed; a disabled thing is described by the control beside it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Height | `--label-height-sm` (16). |
| Width and padding | `--control-sm` for the minimum, `--pad-x-xs` either side. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`; the dot is `--radius-full`. |
| Subtle | `--ds-background-neutral` with `--ds-text`, and the same pair for each other appearance. |
| Bold | `--ds-background-neutral-bold` with `--ds-text-inverse`; warning takes `--ds-text-warning-inverse`. |
| Inverse | `--ds-surface` with `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Ring | `--count-tag-ring-width` in `--ds-surface`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Show the bare number: 4, 12, 99+. | Add words or units to the tag: "4 unread". |
| Put the meaning in `label`, which a screen reader reads: "4 unread messages". | Write "04" or pad with zeros. |
| Leave a zero out. An empty tab needs no count tag. | Show "0" unless the zero is the news. |
| Give a dot a `label` that says what it marks: "New message". | Ship a dot with no name. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number or string | — | The number. Hidden at 0 (and below) unless `showZero`. Ignored by `isDot`. |
| `max` | number | `99` | Above this the count shows `{max}+`. |
| `showZero` | bool | `false` | Render a count of 0 instead of nothing. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'neutral'` | The intent. Use one only when the number carries it. |
| `isBold` | bool | `false` | The solid fill: asks for action now (at most one per area). |
| `isInverse` | bool | `false` | A solid white countTag with dark text, for filled buttons and dark grounds. Always neutral. |
| `isDot` | bool | `false` | Presence without a number. Needs `label`. |
| `hasRing` | bool | `false` | A 2px ring in the page color, for a count pinned to the corner of an icon or avatar. |
| `label` | string | — | The accessible name. Required for `isDot`; on a number it replaces the bare digits for screen readers. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `neutral` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` · `info` · `discovery`

# DatePicker

DatePicker — a date field that opens a month calendar (Figma `DatePicker`). Built from the shared parts: the field is `FieldBox` with the calendar icon in Trailing, and the calendar is the shared `Calendar` on the `_Listbox` surface, which DateTimePicker opens too. - **Typing:** the field takes MM/DD/YYYY (and, with `range`, two dates joined by a dash). It is checked when you press Enter or leave the field: a real day inside `minDate`…`maxDate` is picked, anything else is kept as typed and marked invalid, and `onChange` is not called. - **Range:** the first click sets the first day, the second the last; a click before the first day starts again. `onChange` receives `[start, end]`. - **Clearing:** when a value or typed text is in a live field, a subtle `xmark` icon button (`tabIndex={-1}`) sits before the calendar icon and a subtle "Clear" button (in the tab order) sits in the calendar footer. Both empty the field, call `onChange` with `''` (or `[null, null]` with `range`) when a pick was set, and keep focus in the input. - **Popup:** opens 4px (`--stack-sm`) below the field, left-aligned (or as `calendarAlign` asks), and flips above with the same gap when there is no room below. Props it does not name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `data-*`) go to the input, which is the control a screen reader lands on: DatePicker has no `label` prop, so that is how a caller names it.

Also asked as: calendar input, date field, date input, date selector.

**Import:** `import { DatePicker } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DatePicker/DatePicker.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DatePicker/DatePicker.stories.jsx` — Overview, Spacing, InteractionStates, PickDate, PickRange, Bounds, Interactive, CalendarColors, Default, WithValue, Compact, Invalid, ReadOnly, Disabled, HoveredState, KeyboardFocus, CalendarOpensFourPixelsBelow, CalendarFlipsAboveNearTheBottom, RangePicksASpan, BoundedDatesBehavior, TypedEntry, DaysAnnounceTheirDate, ClearControl, MonthTurnKeepsPopupHeight, RangePopup, RangePopupPresetKeyboard, RangePopupClearCommits, RangePopupPresetBounds, RangePopupReadOnly

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DatePicker/DatePicker.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `DatePicker` for a single date or a date range typed or chosen from a popup calendar, such as a session date or a billing period.

## Motion

DatePicker reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |
| change | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | A month change slides the grid flat. |

## Alternatives

- For a time of day with no date, use `TimePicker`.
- For a combined date and time answer, use `DateTimePicker`.
- For an always-visible month grid on the page, use `Calendar`.

## Best practices

### Typing is checked on Enter or on leaving the field. {#typing-is-checked-on-enter-or-on-leaving-the-field}

A real day inside `minDate` to `maxDate` is picked; anything else is kept exactly as typed and marked invalid, and `onChange` is not called until the text reads as a real date.

```jsx
<DatePicker
    value={date}
    onChange={setDate}
    minDate="2026-01-01"
    maxDate="2026-12-31"
/>
```

### A range is two clicks, not a drag. {#a-range-is-two-clicks-not-a-drag}

The first click sets the first day, the second sets the last day, and `onChange` receives `[start, end]`. A click before the first day starts the range again rather than erroring.

### Name the field. {#name-the-field}

There is no `label` prop. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; both go straight to the input.

### Show the date format as a hint. {#show-the-date-format-as-a-hint}

The field says how to type the date before anyone types it. Without a hint people guess the order. The placeholder is MM/DD/YYYY unless you replace it, so leave it.

Do: The format is shown.
Don't: No format given.

### Show dates in one format everywhere. {#show-dates-in-one-format-everywhere}

Use the same order and separators in the field, the calendar and any message. Mixed formats read as different dates.

Do: One format throughout.
Don't: A second format appears in the message.

### Use one range field, not two dates. {#use-one-range-field-not-two-dates}

A range picks start and end in one field and one calendar. Two separate fields split one decision in two.

Do: One range field.
Don't: Two separate fields.

### Use read-only for fixed dates and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-dates-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` keeps the date focusable, selectable and at full contrast (`aria-readonly`); `isDisabled` removes the field from the tab order when it does not apply yet. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value; content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

## Accessibility

- **The input is the named control.** `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` are forwarded to the text input (`role="combobox"`), which tracks the popup with `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`.
- **The popup is a labeled dialog.** It opens as `role="dialog"` with `aria-label` "Choose a date" or "Choose dates".
- **Clearing by keyboard and screen reader.** When a live field holds a value or typed text, the field's plain ✕ `IconButton` (`xmark` at `--icon-sm`) is named `"Clear <noun>"` in lowercase (such as `"Clear start date"`, `"Clear date"` or `"Clear dates"`) and sets `tabIndex={-1}` so `Tab` moves past the field in one stop, while the popup footer's subtle "Clear" `Button` stays in the tab order. Keyboard users clear the text and press `Enter`, or `Tab` through the open calendar dialog to the footer "Clear" button; pointer and screen-reader users can activate either button. Both empty the field, call `onChange` with `''` (or `[null, null]` with `range`) when a pick was set, and return focus to the input.
- **Invalid input stays editable.** An invalid typed date keeps the typed text and sets `aria-invalid` so the person can correct it.

## Related

- `TimePicker`: use when selecting a time of day without a date.
- `DateTimePicker`: use when selecting a date and a time together.
- `Calendar`: use when rendering the month grid inline on the page.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Field.** A 40 box (32 at compact) on the input fill, with the date as text.
2. **Clear button.** A subtle `IconButton` (`xmark` at `--icon-sm`) before the calendar icon when a date, range or typed text is in a live field (not read-only or disabled).
3. **Calendar icon.** Opens the calendar. Decoration for assistive technology; the input is the control.
4. **Calendar.** A month grid of 24px day cells (`--calendar-day-sm`) in a popup `--stack-sm` below the field, flipped above when there is no room. A picked day or range end is a filled square; days between form a continuous band that rounds where a week starts or ends.
5. **Presets and footer.** With `presets`, a 160px (`--width-1000`) column of 32px radio rows (`All time`, `Today`, `Last 7 days`, `Last 30 days`) sits beside the calendar with arrow-key navigation and `Enter`/`Space` selection, and presets outside `minDate`–`maxDate` are disabled. Compact `Clear` and `Apply` buttons sit below: `Clear` commits `[null, null]` immediately while `Apply` stays disabled until an in-bounds complete range (or `All time` over a non-empty filter) is ready. Otherwise, a compact subtle "Clear" `Button` sits at the end of the popup footer while a value or typed text is in the field.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-input` fill with a `--ds-border-input` border. |
| Hovered | The border takes `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the box. |

| Read-only | The box takes `--ds-background-neutral`, at full contrast with no hover. The clear button and calendar icon are not drawn and a press opens no calendar (nor does a read-only filter trigger). The date can be read, selected and copied. |
| Disabled | The box fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled`, hides the clear button, and leaves the tab order. |

| Popup gap | `--stack-sm`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the date by its role: "Session date", "Start date". | A generic name: "Date", or "Pick a date". |
| Leave the placeholder as the format, MM/DD/YYYY. | Put an instruction in the placeholder: "Click to choose". |

rankedText.usage: Use `DatePicker` for a single date or a date range typed or chosen from a popup calendar, such as a session date or a billing period.
rankedText.best:
### Typing is checked on Enter or on leaving the field.

A real day inside `minDate` to `maxDate` is picked; anything else is kept exactly as typed and marked invalid, and `onChange` is not called until the text reads as a real date.

```jsx
<DatePicker
    value={date}
    onChange={setDate}
    minDate="2026-01-01"
    maxDate="2026-12-31"
/>
```

### A range is two clicks, not a drag.

The first click sets the first day, the second sets the last day, and `onChange` receives `[start, end]`. A click before the first day starts the range again rather than erroring.

### Name the field.

There is no `label` prop. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; both go straight to the input.

### Show the date format as a hint.

The field says how to type the date before anyone types it. Without a hint people guess the order. The placeholder is MM/DD/YYYY unless you replace it, so leave it.

Do: The format is shown.
Don't: No format given.

### Show dates in one format everywhere.

Use the same order and separators in the field, the calendar and any message. Mixed formats read as different dates.

Do: One format throughout.
Don't: A second format appears in the message.

### Use one range field, not two dates.

A range picks start and end in one field and one calendar. Two separate fields split one decision in two.

Do: One range field.
Don't: Two separate fields.

### Use read-only for fixed dates and disabled for unavailable ones.

`isReadOnly` keeps the date focusable, selectable and at full contrast (`aria-readonly`); `isDisabled` removes the field from the tab order when it does not apply yet. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value; content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

# DateTag

An outlined label for a due or event date, such as "Due tomorrow". The app picks the appearance from how close the date is; it is never a button.

Also asked as: date pill.

**Import:** `import { DateTag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/DateTag/DateTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/DateTag/DateTag.stories.jsx` — Overview, Styles, Truncation, NeverAButton, UnknownAppearanceFallsBack, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/DateTag/DateTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `DateTag` for a due or event date beside the thing it belongs to: an
assignment, a session, a report. Write `children` as people say the date, such as "Due tomorrow" or "2 days overdue", never a raw timestamp. `DateTag`'s outline, icon and three
appearances are reserved for dates.

### Appearance guidance

The app derives `appearance` from the date and a due-soon window it defines.

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Neutral | The date is not close. Draws a calendar. Example: "Due next week". |
| Warning | The date is near, before it turns overdue. Draws a clock. Example: "Due tomorrow". |
| Danger | The date has passed. Draws a triangle. Example: "Overdue". |

## Alternatives

- For a workflow condition such as "Completed" or "Needs review", use `StatusTag`.
- For a category or subject or person, use `Tag`.
- For a numeric count, use `CountTag`.

## Best practices

### Reserve danger for overdue dates. {#reserve-danger-for-overdue-dates}

The app picks the appearance from the date and its due-soon window, never from taste. Danger means the date has passed; a far-off date stays neutral.

Do: Danger when it is overdue.
Don't: Danger on a date far in the future.

### Use warning for dates that are close. {#use-warning-for-dates-that-are-close}

Warning tells people the date is near, before it turns overdue.

Do: Warning when it is due soon.
Don't: Neutral hides that it is due soon.

### Show one date tag per row. {#show-one-date-tag-per-row}

A row carries one date; extra tags compete for attention.

Do: One date per row.
Don't: Several dates in one row.

### Never make a date tag a button. {#never-make-a-date-tag-a-button}

It renders a `span` with no role and no click handler: `onClick`, `role` and
`tabIndex` are dropped with a console warning in development. The one time it
takes focus is when its text is truncated, so a keyboard user can still reach
the tooltip holding the full date.

## Accessibility

- **Not a control.** No role, no tab stop, no click handler: assistive
  technology reads it as plain text beside whatever it labels.
- **Truncated text stays reachable.** When the label is clipped, the tag
  takes a tab stop and its full text is available as a tooltip on hover or
  focus.
- **The icon is decorative.** It is `aria-hidden`; the appearance's meaning
  lives in the text, not the icon alone.

## Related

- `DatePicker`: use when the person picks or edits a date in a form field.
- `StatusTag`: use when showing the workflow state of a dated item.

Same group: `ChangeTag` · `CompetencyTag` · `CountTag` · `StatusTag` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Icon.** Fixed by the appearance: a calendar for neutral, a clock for warning and a triangle for danger. It is decoration; the date says the rest.
2. **Date.** One short string, set by the app: "Due tomorrow", "Mar 4".
3. **Outline.** An inset border, so the height stays exact. A date tag has no fill.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. The appearance (neutral, warning, danger) is chosen from the date and the due-soon window. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. It is a label, not a control; the thing around it is what responds. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. A truncated label takes focus only so a keyboard user can reach the tooltip with its full text. |
| Disabled | None. A label is never dimmed; a disabled thing is described by the control beside it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Height | `--label-height-md` (20), or `--control-md` (32) when spacious. |
| Padding and gap | `--pad-x-xs` on the leading edge, 2 on the trailing edge and between icon and label, `--stack-sm` inside the text; spacious `--pad-x-md` with 6 behind. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`; spacious `--radius-lg`. |
| Neutral | `--ds-border` edge, `--ds-text-subtle` words. |
| Warning | `--ds-border-warning-subtle` edge, `--ds-text-warning` words. |
| Danger | `--ds-border-danger-subtle` edge, `--ds-text-danger` words. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say it in the reader's terms: "Due tomorrow", "Mar 4". | Write a timestamp: "2026-03-04T09:00". |
| Keep one date to a tag. Use two tags for a range. | Pack a range or a time zone into one tag. |
| Let the app turn the tag warning or danger from the date. | Pick a color for emphasis. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node (required) | — | The date, as people say it: "Due tomorrow", "2 days overdue". |
| `appearance` | enum | `'neutral'` | `neutral` (not close), `warning` (due soon) or `danger` (overdue). Drives the fixed icon too. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` (20) in rows, lists and sentences; `spacious` (32) beside a heading. |
| `maxWidth` | number or string | `200` | The widest the Date tag grows, in px or any CSS length, and never wider than its container. Past it the label ends in an ellipsis and the full text is a tooltip. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the tag element beside the component's own. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the tag element. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `neutral` · `warning` · `danger`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `spacious`

# DateTimePicker

DateTimePicker — a date field and a time field read as one moment. Composed from DatePicker and TimePicker, laid out as labeled sections with a shared time-zone caption under the time.

Also asked as: date and time, schedule.

**Import:** `import { DateTimePicker } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DateTimePicker/DateTimePicker.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DateTimePicker/DateTimePicker.stories.jsx` — Overview, Spacing, Validation, InteractionStates, TimeZones, Interactive, Default, WithValue, Compact, Invalid, Valid, ReadOnly, Disabled, HoveredState, KeyboardFocus

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DateTimePicker/DateTimePicker.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `DateTimePicker` when a date and a time are one combined answer, such as a session's start or a deadline.

## Motion

DateTimePicker reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |
| change | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | A month change slides the grid flat. |

## Alternatives

- For a date or date range with no time, use `DatePicker`.
- For a time of day with no date, use `TimePicker`.

## Best practices

### `onChange` reports the date, the time and the combined moment. {#onchange-reports-the-date-the-time-and-the-combined-moment}

Each field's change calls `onChange` with `{ date, time, utc }`. `date` and `time` are the two fields' own display values, and `utc` is the ISO moment once both halves are set, computed from `timeZone`. Store `utc`; show `date` and `time` back to the person who typed them.

```jsx
<DateTimePicker
    label="Session start"
    dateValue={date}
    timeValue={time}
    onChange={({ date, time, utc }) => {
        setDate(date);
        setTime(time);
        setStartUtc(utc);
    }}
/>
```

### `label` names the whole field, not either input. {#label-names-the-whole-field-not-either-input}

The label's text is read as the group's accessible name, and the date and time inputs are additionally named off the "Date" and "Time" section headings. `isLabelHidden` only hides the label visually.

### A time-zone mismatch adds the other person's time, it does not replace yours. {#a-time-zone-mismatch-adds-the-other-person-s-time-it-does-not-replace-yours}

`otherTimeZone` only changes the caption when it differs from the viewer's own zone, and then it adds the other person's time rather than converting the field. The fields always show the viewer's local time.

### Show the date and the time in one pattern. {#show-the-date-and-the-time-in-one-pattern}

Date comes first, followed by time with `AM` or `PM` (`MM/DD/YYYY, h:mm AM`). Write the moment in the same order wherever else it appears, "10/21/2026, 3:30 PM" and not "2026-10-21 15:30", so people do not have to reread it.

### Always show AM or PM. {#always-show-am-or-pm}

A time without AM or PM can mean two times a day apart. Every time in the time field's list carries its period, so the field always shows it; keep it in any message that repeats the time.

### Name the time zone when it can differ. {#name-the-time-zone-when-it-can-differ}

Tutors and students can sit in different zones. Name the zone next to the time so a session is not missed. `showTimeZone` is on by default.

Do: The zone is named under the time.
Don't: The zone is not named.

### Label the moment by its role. {#label-the-moment-by-its-role}

Do: The label says which moment this is.
Don't: The label names the two halves, not the moment.

### Say what to fix in an error. {#say-what-to-fix-in-an-error}

Do: The message says what to change.
Don't: A bare 'Invalid' does not say what to change.

## Accessibility

- **One group, two named inputs.** The wrapper is `role="group"` named by `label`; the date and time inputs are each named by that label plus their own section heading, so a screen reader announces "Session start, Date" and "Session start, Time".
- **Validation and the time-zone caption are both wired through `aria-describedby`**, composed with anything already passed in rather than overwriting it.
- **`isLabelHidden` never removes the accessible name**, only its visible text.

## Related

- `DatePicker`: use when selecting a date or date range without a time.
- `TimePicker`: use when selecting a time of day without a date.
- `Calendar`: use when embedding a standalone month grid on the page.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Label.** Names the whole group. `isLabelHidden` hides it visually and keeps the name.
2. **Section labels** (optional). "Date" and "Time" captions above each field.
3. **Date field.** The Date picker, on its own calendar.
4. **Time field.** The Time picker: a list of the day's times, each with its period.
5. **Caption.** One line under the pair: the validation message, or the viewer's time zone and the other person's time.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-input` fill with a `--ds-border-input` border. |
| Hovered | The hovered half's border takes `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the focused half. |
| Invalid | Both borders take `--ds-border-danger`; the caption shows the error message. |
| Valid | Both borders take `--ds-border-success`; the caption shows the success message. |
| Read-only | Both boxes take `--ds-background-neutral`, at full contrast with no hover. The calendar icon and the chevron are not drawn. |
| Disabled | Both boxes fade to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leave the tab order. |

### Tokens

rankedText.usage: Use `DateTimePicker` when a date and a time are one combined answer, such as a session's start or a deadline.
rankedText.best:
### `onChange` reports the date, the time and the combined moment.

Each field's change calls `onChange` with `{ date, time, utc }`. `date` and `time` are the two fields' own display values, and `utc` is the ISO moment once both halves are set, computed from `timeZone`. Store `utc`; show `date` and `time` back to the person who typed them.

```jsx
<DateTimePicker
    label="Session start"
    dateValue={date}
    timeValue={time}
    onChange={({ date, time, utc }) => {
        setDate(date);
        setTime(time);
        setStartUtc(utc);
    }}
/>
```

### `label` names the whole field, not either input.

The label's text is read as the group's accessible name, and the date and time inputs are additionally named off the "Date" and "Time" section headings. `isLabelHidden` only hides the label visually.

### A time-zone mismatch adds the other person's time, it does not replace yours.

`otherTimeZone` only changes the caption when it differs from the viewer's own zone, and then it adds the other person's time rather than converting the field. The fields always show the viewer's local time.

### Show the date and the time in one pattern.

Date comes first, followed by time with `AM` or `PM` (`MM/DD/YYYY, h:mm AM`). Write the moment in the same order wherever else it appears, "10/21/2026, 3:30 PM" and not "2026-10-21 15:30", so people do not have to reread it.

### Always show AM or PM.

A time without AM or PM can mean two times a day apart. Every time in the time field's list carries its period, so the field always shows it; keep it in any message that repeats the time.

### Name the time zone when it can differ.

Tutors and students can sit in different zones. Name the zone next to the time so a session is not missed. `showTimeZone` is on by default.

Do: The zone is named under the time.
Don't: The zone is not named.

### Label the moment by its role.

Do: The label says which moment this is.
Don't: The label names the two halves, not the moment.

### Say what to fix in an error.

Do: The message says what to change.
Don't: A bare 'Invalid' does not say what to change.

# Dialog

The dialog panel itself: header (title, optional description, header actions, close button, or custom header / tabs), scrolling body, and optional footer slots. Sizes from the screen grid (`4-col · 6-col · 8-col · 10-col`) and renders inline with no Blanket and no modal behavior. For a blocking overlay dialog with Blanket, portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock, use the `Modal` template from `@/templates`.

Also asked as: dialog panel, dialog layout.

**Import:** `import { Dialog } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Modal (`ds guide modal`)

**Governed by:** Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Dialog/Dialog.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Dialog/Dialog.stories.jsx` — Width4Col, Width6Col, Width8Col, Width10Col, HeightHug, HeightFill, HeaderOptions, WithoutCloseButton, Tabs, Loading, Content, Layout, Interactive, Overview, FooterLayouts, SizeToContent, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Dialog/Dialog.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Dialog` as the panel inside the Modal template, or when a docs illustration or mockup draws the dialog panel inline with no Blanket and no modal behavior. For a working overlay over the page (Blanket, portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock), use the `Modal` template from `@/templates`.

The footer runs on `FooterActions`: pass `primaryButton` and `secondaryButton`
as objects for a `50/50` pair (or `primaryButton` alone for the right half), or
pass `footer` with `<FooterActions>` for three actions or a leading action
(a `danger` side action or a link).

### Width guidance

`width` takes a step of `DIALOG_WIDTHS` (4-col · 6-col · 8-col · 10-col): that
many columns of the screen grid plus the dialog pad.

| Width | When to use | `DIALOG_WIDTH_PX` at 768 · 1024 · 1280 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4-col | A compact confirmation. | 269 · 355 · 440 |
| 6-col | A confirmation or a short question. | 392 · 520 · 648 |
| 8-col | A short form. | 515 · 685 · 856 |
| 10-col | A table or an editor. | 637 · 851 · 1064 |

`Dialog` draws `--ds-surface-material-overlay` and a `--ds-border-material` edge with `--dialog-shadow` (`--ds-shadow-blocking`) in every width. A `Select` list opened inside it keeps `--ds-shadow-overlay`.

The width grows with the screen, never shrinks, and ignores the Sidebar. The
height hugs its content up to the cap (`--dialog-max-height`);
`height="fill"` sits at that cap.

## Alternatives

- For a blocking overlay over the page with Blanket, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock, use `Modal` (`@/templates`).
- For a message the person only reads, use `SectionMessage` in the page or `Flag` at the screen corner.
- For a task that keeps the page in view, use `Panel`, floating: a row's details, filters, a short edit.
- For a small aside anchored to a control, use `Popup`.
- For a list of actions or a value to pick, use `DropdownMenu` or `Select`.

## Best practices

### Size the Dialog to its content with a step of `DIALOG_WIDTHS`. {#size-the-dialog-to-its-content-with-a-step-of-dialogwidths}

A short confirmation takes `6-col`, a short form `8-col`, a table or an editor
`10-col`. A step grows with the screen; a fixed number keeps one size on every
screen.

Do: The narrowest step for a short question.

Don't: The widest step around one sentence.

### Keep Close on a Dialog unless the person has to answer it. {#keep-close-on-a-dialog-unless-the-person-has-to-answer-it}

An informational `Dialog` keeps its close button; `showCloseButton={false}` is
for a decision that has to be answered from the footer.

Do: Close stays on an informational dialog.
Don't: No way out of an informational dialog.

### Add `dividers` when the Dialog body scrolls. {#add-dividers-when-the-dialog-body-scrolls}

The rules mark where the header and footer stay put while the body scrolls; a
short body reads cleaner without them.

Do: Dividers around a scrolling body.
Don't: Dividers around a short body.

### Give the Dialog footer a button. {#give-the-dialog-footer-a-button}

`showBottomButtons` defaults to true, and the footer renders only when
`primaryButton`, `secondaryButton` or `footer` is given; describe the actions as
objects and the component renders the `FooterActions` pair.

Do: Pass `primaryButton` or `footer` when the dialog asks for a decision.

Don't: Leave a confirm dialog with no footer action.

### Use `Modal` from `@/templates` when a task needs a Blanket and focus trap. {#use-modal-from-templates-when-a-task-needs-a-blanket-and-focus-trap}

`Dialog` draws the panel inline; `Modal` places it on a Blanket with Base UI
focus management, Escape dismissal and scroll lock.

Do: Use `Modal` for live overlay confirmations and short forms.

Don't: Render a bare `Dialog` over page content on your own.

## Accessibility

- **The close button is labeled `Close`**, hard-coded. Its icon is
  `aria-hidden`. `showCloseButton={false}` removes it.
- **The title is the dialog's h1 and its accessible name**, through
  `aria-labelledby`: the panel reads as its own page. The `description`
  describes it, through `aria-describedby`. A `Dialog` with no title takes
  `ariaLabel`.
- **A body that scrolls is focusable.** Once the content runs past the cap, the
  body gets `tabIndex={0}` so a keyboard user can scroll it.
- **Loading is announced as busy.** `loading` sets `aria-busy` on the body while
  the skeleton bars stand in for it.
- **`Dialog` has no Blanket, focus trap or Escape handling.** Use
  Modal for live blocking dialogs over
  the page.

## Related

- `Modal` template: places `Dialog` on a Blanket with portal, focus trap, Escape and scroll lock.
- `FooterActions`: use when placing three actions or a leading action across the Dialog's four-track footer slot.
- Templates: use when choosing between a Modal and a full page; its Usage section weighs the two.

Same group: `Banner` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Header.** Title, optional description, header actions and the close button, or a custom `header` and optional `tabs`.
2. **Body.** Text, tabs panel, or any content; scrolls when it overflows.
3. **Footer.** Appears only when a button or `footer` is given: `FooterActions` divides the width inside container padding into four equal tracks.
4. **Dividers.** Optional rules under the header and over the footer.

The tokens each part draws are read from `Dialog.scss` and listed under Tokens
touched in the Harness tab.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Drawn inline with the title naming the dialog. |
| Hovered | The close button takes the subtle hovered step. |
| Pressed | The close button takes the subtle pressed step. |
| Focused | The close button shows the focus ring. |
| Disabled | The dialog has no disabled state; disable a footer button instead. |
| Loading | The body shows a skeleton and sets `aria-busy`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Dialog with the action or decision: "Delete account?". | Use a vague title such as "Warning". |
| Say what happens and whether it can be undone. | Hide the consequence in the body. |
| Label buttons with verbs that match the title: "Delete recording", "Archive instead". | Use "Cancel", "Yes" or "No" in a Dialog footer. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the dialog panel. |
| `title` | node | — | The dialog's h1, and its accessible name. |
| `description` | node | — | A line under the title, read as the dialog's description. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | — | The dialog's accessible name when it has no visible `title` or uses a custom `header`. |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header slot replacing the title row (title and close button), so the caller owns both and names the dialog with `ariaLabel`. |
| `headerActions` | node | — | Icon buttons in the header, before the close button. |
| `showCloseButton` | bool | — | The header's close button. Off for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `tabs` | arrayOf | — | Tab group under the title (`{ key, label, content, disabled? }`). The body becomes the tab panel and shows the selected tab's `content`. |
| `activeTab` | string or number | — | Selected tab's key when controlled; update from `onTabChange`. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | string or number | — | Initial tab key when uncontrolled; defaults to the first enabled tab. |
| `onTabChange` | func | — | Called with the key of the selected tab. |
| `body` | string or node | — | The main content of the dialog. A string is drawn as body text; a node is drawn as given. `children` is rendered after it. |
| `height` | enum | — | `hug` grows with the content to the cap and then scrolls its body; `fill` sits at that cap. |
| `showBottomButtons` | bool | — | Show the footer: `footer`, or the secondary and primary buttons. |
| `footer` | node | — | Custom footer content in place of the built-in pair, such as a three-button or leading-text FooterActions layout. |
| `primaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The confirming footer button, drawn on the right. Takes `text` (default "Confirm"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `primary`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `secondaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The secondary footer button, drawn in the left half when a primary button is also given. Takes `text` (default "Discard"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `default`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `dividers` | bool | — | A rule under the header and over the footer. |
| `loading` | bool | — | Skeleton bars in place of the body while its content loads. |
| `onClose` | func | — | Called when the close button is clicked. |
| `width` | enum or number or string | — | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`: 4 · 6 · 8 · 10 columns of the screen grid plus the dialog pad. Grows with the screen, never shrinks, ignores the sidebar. A number or a length sets a fixed width. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the dialog panel beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the dialog panel. A fixed `width` is applied after them. |
| `children` | node | — | More content rendered in the body after `body`, for composing the dialog contents directly. |

## Variants

**`height`** — `hug` · `fill`

props.name: trigger
props.description: The element that opens the menu. A `Button` with a chevron is the default pattern.

props.name: children
props.description: The menu's rows: `Section`, `ButtonItem`, `LinkItem`, `CustomItem`.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state. Pair it with `onOpenChange`; leave it out for an uncontrolled menu.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next open state (a boolean) when the menu opens or closes: trigger press, outside click, Escape or picking a row.

props.name: placement
props.description: Side and alignment against the trigger, such as `bottom-start` (default), `top-end` or `right`. A bare side centers the menu on that side.

props.name: shouldFlip
props.description: Flips to the opposite side when there isn't room.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws 32px rows, `compact` draws 24px.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows one "Loading options" row, with a spinner, in place of the menu's rows while its options load. Never skeleton rows.
