props.description: Minimum width of the menu list, as a CSS length such as `240px`.

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/DropdownMenu/DropdownMenu.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `DropdownMenu` for a trigger that opens a menu of actions or navigation links (`Section`, `ButtonItem`, `LinkItem`, `CustomItem`).

`trigger` opens the menu and `children` supply its rows. Pass `isOpen` and `onOpenChange` for controlled mode, `placement` and `shouldFlip` for positioning (left uncontrolled, it opens and closes on its own), `spacing` for `default` (32 rows) or `compact` (24), `maxHeight` to cap height before scrolling, and `container` for the portal target. `isLoading` shows one "Loading options" row with a spinner; `hasError` shows "Couldn't load options" with a Retry row (`onRetry`). A menu never draws skeleton rows.

## Motion

DropdownMenu reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, with no clip or travel. From the keyboard it opens with no animation. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, the same as the enter. |

## Alternatives

- For picking a value in a form field, use `Select`.
- For picking a single view or filter value from a button, use `PopupSelect`.
- For one primary action joined to a chevron menu of related actions, use `SplitButton`.

## Best practices

### A row closes the menu unless it opts out. {#a-row-closes-the-menu-unless-it-opts-out}

```jsx
// Picking "Rename" closes the menu: the common case for an action list.
<DropdownMenu trigger={<Button text="Actions" iconAfter={<Icon name="chevron-down" size={12} />} />}>
    <ButtonItem onClick={onRename}>Rename</ButtonItem>
    <ButtonItem onClick={onArchive}>Archive</ButtonItem>
</DropdownMenu>

// A toggle row that should stay open across repeated picks carries
// `data-keep-open`, as a multi-select tag or filter row does.
<ButtonItem onClick={toggleStarred} isSelected={starred} data-keep-open="true">
    Starred
</ButtonItem>
```

### A static row never closes the menu. {#a-static-row-never-closes-the-menu}

A Custom item with no `component` override (its default, `div`) renders a row that only says its words: nothing to press, nothing to focus, and it leaves the menu open.

### Use a menu for actions and a select for a value. {#use-a-menu-for-actions-and-a-select-for-a-value}

Rows that set a value belong in a Select, which shows the chosen value on its trigger. A dropdown menu's rows do something: rename, archive, share.

### Group related items and keep destructive ones last. {#group-related-items-and-keep-destructive-ones-last}

Order items by task and put Delete at the bottom, away from the common actions.

Do: Delete sits last, after the common actions.
Don't: Delete first puts a risky action at the top.

### Start each item with a verb, in sentence case. {#start-each-item-with-a-verb-in-sentence-case}

Verb-first labels read as actions. All caps and noun-only labels slow scanning.

Do: Verb first, sentence case.
Don't: All caps and noun-only labels.

### Keep item labels short and distinct. {#keep-item-labels-short-and-distinct}

One or two words each. Long, near-identical labels make the choice harder and wrap.

Do: Short, distinct labels.
Don't: Long, near-identical labels.

### Keep menus one level deep. {#keep-menus-one-level-deep}

The Menu family has no submenu-trigger row. Flatten the choices or use sections.

## Accessibility

- **The trigger announces the menu.** Its trigger carries `aria-haspopup="menu"` and an `aria-expanded` that tracks the open state.
- **Arrow keys move between rows**, Enter and Space pick the row at the cursor, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
- **Disabled rows.** Arrow keys skip disabled rows (`aria-disabled`), which cannot be picked and carry no tooltip; put the reason in `description`. Menu rows are not tab stops. Disable a row only for something the person can fix on the same screen: leave an action enabled and explain on press when it is merely not ready, and leave out a row the role can never use. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

## Related

- `Select`: use when picking a value in a form field.
- `PopupSelect`: use when picking one view or filter value from a button.
- `PageHeader`: use when placing page-level actions and overflow menus in a header row.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Trigger.** Any element that opens the menu, usually a Button with a chevron.
2. **Menu.** A floating list 4px from the trigger, on the raised surface.
3. **Rows.** Button items, Link items or Custom items, 32 tall at default and 24 at compact.
4. **Section title and separator** (optional). Group related rows.

### Menu items

Dropdown menu exports the four row parts: `Section`, `ButtonItem`, `LinkItem` and `CustomItem`. `ButtonItem` runs an action and `LinkItem` navigates with `href`. `CustomItem` renders through a `component` of the caller's choosing, such as a `label` around a checkbox. All three take `elemBefore`, `elemAfter`, `description`, `isSelected` and `isDisabled`. `Section` takes a `title` and `hasSeparator` and groups rows. Arrow keys move between enabled rows and wrap at the ends. Standalone menus wrap rows in `MenuGroup`, which takes `spacing` (`default` 32, `compact` 24, `spacious` 40).

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered row | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed row | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Selected row | `--ds-background-selected`. |
| Focused trigger | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge, for keyboard focus only. |
| Disabled row | Text takes `--ds-text-disabled`; the row cannot be picked. Its description keeps `--ds-text-subtle`, so the reason stays readable. |
| Loading | One "Loading options" row with a 16 spinner replaces the rows, in `--ds-text-subtle`. |
| Load failed | A "Couldn't load options" row with a Section message icon, then a Retry row. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface padding | `--dropdown-menu-pad` (4). |
| Row height | `--control-md` (32) default; `--control-sm` (24) compact; `--control-lg` (40) spacious on `MenuGroup`. |
| Row text | `--ds-text`, `--body-default` (14); disabled `--ds-text-disabled`. |
| Row icon | `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Row padding, gap, radius | `--pad-x-md` and `--pad-y-md` (12 × 6); gap `--inline-md` (8); `--radius-control-md` (8). |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Start each row with a verb: "Rename", "Archive". | A noun with no action: "Name". |
| Use sentence case: "Open report". | Title case: "Open Report". |
| Name the trigger for what the menu holds: "Actions", "Views". | "Menu" or "Click here". |
| Keep section titles to one or two words: "Manage", "Go to". | Sentences as section titles. |
| Put the most common action first. | Order rows alphabetically when use is uneven. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `trigger` | element (required) | — | The element that opens the menu. A `Button` with a chevron is the default pattern. |
| `children` | node | — | The menu's rows: `Section`, `ButtonItem`, `LinkItem`, `CustomItem`. |
| `isOpen` | bool | — | Controlled open state. Pair it with `onOpenChange`; leave it out for an uncontrolled menu. |
| `defaultOpen` | bool | `false` | Whether an uncontrolled menu starts open. |
| `onOpenChange` | func | — | Called with the next open state (a boolean) when the menu opens or closes: trigger press, outside click, Escape or picking a row. |
| `placement` | oneOf | `'bottom-start'` | Side and alignment against the trigger, such as `bottom-start` (default), `top-end` or `right`. A bare side centers the menu on that side. |
| `shouldFlip` | bool | `true` | Flips to the opposite side when there isn't room. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 32px rows, `compact` draws 24px. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | Shows one "Loading options" row, with a spinner, in place of the menu's rows while its options load. Never skeleton rows. |
| `hasError` | bool | `false` | Shows "Couldn't load options" with a Retry row in place of the menu's rows, after loading failed. |
| `onRetry` | func | — | Called when Retry is pressed. The menu stays open. |
| `minWidth` | string | — | Minimum width of the menu list, as a CSS length such as `240px`. |
| `maxHeight` | string | — | Maximum height of the menu list, as a CSS length such as `320px`. |
| `container` | object | — | Where the menu portals to. Defaults to the page. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid` on the menu popup, for test queries. |
| `id` | string | — | Id set on the menu popup. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the menu popup, beside `plus-dropdown-menu`. |

## Variants

**`placement`** — `top` · `bottom` · `left` · `right` · `top-start` · `top-end` · `bottom-start` · `bottom-end` · `right-start` · `right-end` · `left-start` · `left-end`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

`--body-default` · `--border-width-default` · `--dropdown-menu-max-height` · `--dropdown-menu-max-width` · `--ds-shadow-overlay` · `--ds-surface-overlay` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--layer-popup` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-y-md` · `--popup-radius` · `--stack-md`

entries.summary: Dynamic table. A table people sort, page or act on, built on the table shell: its `footer` and `emptyState` slots, sortable `HeadCell`s in the head row and the shared `TableRow` and `TableCell` parts in the body. - **Data.** `head.cells` is one `{ key, content, isSortable, width, align }` per column; `rows` is `{ key, cells, onClick }` with one `{ key, content }` per column. A column sorts by its cells' `key`. - **Stateful or stateless.** Left alone it holds its own sort and page, seeded by `defaultSortKey`, `defaultSortOrder` and `defaultPage`. Pass `sortKey` and `sortOrder`, or `page`, and the page owns that state: the table reports a press through `onSort` or `onSetPage` and draws only what it is given. With `totalRows`, `rows` is already the current page (paged on a server) and the footer counts against `totalRows`. - **States.** `default`, `empty`, `no results`, `loading`, `refreshing` and `error`. `empty` and `no results` replace the whole table (no head row, footer or pagination) with `EmptyState`; `loading` and `error` keep the head row and swap the body for one message row; `refreshing` keeps the rows at the loading opacity under a spinner. `isLoading` and an empty `rows` choose the state on their own; `state` names one outright (`no results` and `error` are only ever named). - **Selection.** `isSelectable` adds a checkbox column as wide as the row is tall: "Select row N" on each row, "Select all rows" in the head, which is checked when every row on the page is selected and mixed when only some are. A selected row carries `aria-selected` and the selected fill. The keys come back through `onSelectionChange`; pass `selectedRowKeys` to own them. - **Bulk bar.** While rows are selected, the head row becomes the bulk bar: select-all stays in its cell, and one cell across the columns says "N selected" and holds `bulkActions` at the start. The labels cross-fade in place and the row keeps its height. There is no Clear: the checkboxes clear the selection, and the head row comes back when none are left. - **Sticky header and frozen column.** `stickyHeader` pins the head row inside the table's own scroll region, bounded by `maxHeight`. `isFrozen` pins the first column (with the checkboxes, the title column beside them) on an opaque surface, with a stronger divider and the overflow shadow only while the table is scrolled sideways. - **Width.** Under the content minimum the table scrolls sideways instead of squeezing. The first column fills the room and the rest size to their content, unless a head cell sets `width`; `isFixedSize` holds every column to its set width.

# DynamicTable

Dynamic table. A table people sort, page or act on, built on the table shell: its `footer` and `emptyState` slots, sortable `HeadCell`s in the head row and the shared `TableRow` and `TableCell` parts in the body. - **Data.** `head.cells` is one `{ key, content, isSortable, width, align }` per column; `rows` is `{ key, cells, onClick }` with one `{ key, content }` per column. A column sorts by its cells' `key`. - **Stateful or stateless.** Left alone it holds its own sort and page, seeded by `defaultSortKey`, `defaultSortOrder` and `defaultPage`. Pass `sortKey` and `sortOrder`, or `page`, and the page owns that state: the table reports a press through `onSort` or `onSetPage` and draws only what it is given. With `totalRows`, `rows` is already the current page (paged on a server) and the footer counts against `totalRows`. - **States.** `default`, `empty`, `no results`, `loading`, `refreshing` and `error`. `empty` and `no results` replace the whole table (no head row, footer or pagination) with `EmptyState`; `loading` and `error` keep the head row and swap the body for one message row; `refreshing` keeps the rows at the loading opacity under a spinner. `isLoading` and an empty `rows` choose the state on their own; `state` names one outright (`no results` and `error` are only ever named). - **Selection.** `isSelectable` adds a checkbox column as wide as the row is tall: "Select row N" on each row, "Select all rows" in the head, which is checked when every row on the page is selected and mixed when only some are. A selected row carries `aria-selected` and the selected fill. The keys come back through `onSelectionChange`; pass `selectedRowKeys` to own them. - **Bulk bar.** While rows are selected, the head row becomes the bulk bar: select-all stays in its cell, and one cell across the columns says "N selected" and holds `bulkActions` at the start. The labels cross-fade in place and the row keeps its height. There is no Clear: the checkboxes clear the selection, and the head row comes back when none are left. - **Sticky header and frozen column.** `stickyHeader` pins the head row inside the table's own scroll region, bounded by `maxHeight`. `isFrozen` pins the first column (with the checkboxes, the title column beside them) on an opaque surface, with a stronger divider and the overflow shadow only while the table is scrolled sideways. - **Width.** Under the content minimum the table scrolls sideways instead of squeezing. The first column fills the room and the rest size to their content, unless a head cell sets `width`; `isFixedSize` holds every column to its set width.

Also asked as: data table, interactive table.

**Import:** `import { DynamicTable } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); Search (`ds guide search`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/DynamicTable/DynamicTable.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/DynamicTable/DynamicTable.stories.jsx` — Default, Stateless, States, Empty, NoResults, EmptyNothingYet, EmptyHiddenByFilter, EmptyNothingToCreate, Widths, Selection, StickyHeaderAndFrozenColumn, SortableHeadCells, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, DisabledRow, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/DynamicTable/DynamicTable.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast` · roster `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.roster`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `DynamicTable` for a table of sessions or records where people act on the
data: sort a column, filter or search the rows, select some for a bulk action,
or split a long result across numbered pages. It holds its own sort and page until the page passes `sortKey` or `page`.

## Motion

DynamicTable reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Rows are added, removed and reordered; sort is Reorder, a filter is Swap content. Ticking rows cross-fades the head row into the bulk bar, same height, nothing slides. |  |
| roster | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A student joins or leaves the session roster: the row is added or removed. | `sound.roster` on land: in a session; changes within 2 s play once |

## Alternatives

- For a fixed grid people only read or a nested hierarchy, use `Table`.

## Best practices

### Give a column a sortable key. {#give-a-column-a-sortable-key}

A date needs a key that sorts, such as `20261024`, and its readable text as `content`.

Do: A key per cell sorts chronologically rather than alphabetically.
Don't: No key, so the formatted strings sort alphabetically instead.

### Say what an empty table is for. {#say-what-an-empty-table-is-for}

`empty` and `no results` replace the whole table (header row, footer and pagination included) with `EmptyState`. Word the message with `emptyView`.

Do: A message that says what is missing and what happens next.
Don't: No data, with no hint of why.

### Page on the server when the list is long. {#page-on-the-server-when-the-list-is-long}

With `totalRows`, `rows` is the current page only (`rowsPerPage`), and the footer counts against the total.

Do: One page of rows, counted against the total.
Don't: The whole list loaded to page on the screen, when it is thousands of rows.

## Accessibility

- **Sorting is announced.** A sortable header carries `aria-sort` (`none`, `ascending` or `descending`) and holds a real button, so a keyboard reaches it with Tab and a press asks for the next sort.
- **Focus is a ring.** The ring is inset in the cell and focus never changes the fill.
- **The arrow is decorative.** The sort state is in `aria-sort`, so color and the arrow never carry it alone.
- **A disabled row is announced.** It is `aria-disabled` and takes no pointer events.
- **Row selection is named and announced.** Each checkbox is "Select row N" and the head's is "Select all rows", mixed when only some rows are selected; a status says how many are selected, from the first one. The bulk bar's count is not announced a second time.

## Related

- `Pagination`: use when splitting a long result set across numbered pages.
- Table: use when choosing between Static, Dynamic and Tree tables.
- Section: use when placing search, filters and actions in the toolbar above the table; selected rows never change it.

Same group: `Code` · `CodeBlock` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `StaticTable` · `TreeTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Head cell.** A label with an optional type icon; a sortable one holds a button across the whole cell.
2. **Sort arrow.** `12` tall; hidden until hover or focus, kept once sorted.
3. **Row.** Cells in a band, with hover and selected grounds.
4. **Footer.** States the range on a table that pages.
5. **Message row.** The `loading` and `error` states, spanning every column under the head row. `empty` and `no results` replace the whole table with `EmptyState`.
6. **Checkbox column.** With `isSelectable`: as wide as the row is tall, select-all in the head.
7. **Bulk bar.** While rows are selected, the head row itself: select-all in its cell, then the count and `bulkActions` in one cell across the columns. The labels cross-fade in place and the row keeps its height.
8. **Frozen column.** With `isFrozen`: an opaque first column with a stronger divider while scrolled sideways.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Head cells clear; sorted columns keep their arrow. |
| Hovered | A sortable head cell takes the subtle hovered ground and shows its arrow. |
| Pressed | A sortable head cell takes the subtle pressed ground. |
| Focused | The sort button shows the focus ring inset; focus is never a fill. |
| Disabled | A row takes the disabled ink and ignores the pointer; there is no disabled sort. |
| Rows selected | The head row becomes the bulk bar, at the same height; selected rows keep the selected ground. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |

# EmptyState

What a view shows when it has nothing to show yet: a picture, a short header, one line saying what goes here, and the action that fills it. It invites; it does not apologize. It also fills the slot when content cannot be shown: a load failure ("Couldn't load sessions" with Try again) or no access (the plain reason and who can help). Those are the same parts with different words, so they need no props of their own. - **image** is a slot for an Illustration or any picture. Without it, `icon` (a Font Awesome Free solid name) stands in. Both are decorative. - **header** is a heading one level below the section that holds the EmptyState, so it joins the page's outline. - **primaryAction** is one filled Button; **secondaryAction** an optional outlined one after it. - **spacing** `default` centers in a view on Heading/medium 20; `compact` fits a table body or a card on Heading/small 16 with a smaller picture. Pass it to a Table's `emptyState` slot.

Also asked as: no data, zero state, blank slate.

**Import:** `import { EmptyState } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Empty (`ds guide empty`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Search (`ds guide search`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/EmptyState/EmptyState.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/EmptyState/EmptyState.stories.jsx` — Overview, WithIcon, Default, Compact, InATable, LoadFailure, NoAccess, LoadFailureInATable, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/EmptyState/EmptyState.mdx`

## Usage

Use `EmptyState` when a view, panel, card or table has no content yet, in place
of a blank area or a bare "No results". It carries a picture, a header, one line
and one primary action.

Use `EmptyState` too when content cannot be shown. A view, panel or table that
fails to load shows the failure in the same slot, with a filled **Try again**.
A view the person may not open says so plainly and names who can help. A
rejected form submit is not one of these: a danger `SectionMessage` at the top
of the form summarizes it. A failure in the background is a `Flag`.

### Kind guidance

| The view is | The slot says |
| --- | --- |
| Empty | What goes here and the action that fills it. Example: "No students yet", Add student. |
| Failed to load | What failed and a filled Try again. Example: "Couldn't load sessions". |
| No access | The plain reason and who can help, with no action. Example: "Only supervisors can see session notes. Ask your supervisor to add you." |

### Spacing guidance

| Spacing | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | A whole view or panel, with the header at `--heading-md`. |
| Compact | A table body or a card, with the header at `--heading-sm` and a smaller picture. |

## Alternatives

- For a rejected form submit at the top of a form, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a background failure such as a sync or autosave that failed out of sight, use `Flag`.
- For a view that is still fetching its data, use `Skeleton` or `Spinner`.

## Best practices

### Use default spacing for a whole view. {#use-default-spacing-for-a-whole-view}

Compact spacing is for a table body or a card.

Do: Default spacing fills a view or panel.
Don't: Compact spacing leaves a full view cramped.

### Lead with one filled action. {#lead-with-one-filled-action}

The second action is outlined and never stands alone.

Do: A filled action leads.
Don't: An outlined action with nothing to lead.

### Invite with the next step. {#invite-with-the-next-step}

Say what goes here and what to do, in a warm voice. Never apologize.

Do: What goes here and what to do.
Don't: A cold label with no way forward.

### Show a load failure in the slot, with Try again. {#show-a-load-failure-in-the-slot-with-try-again}

State what failed and offer the retry. Never leave the view blank or send the
person to a message above it.

Do: What failed, with Try again.
Don't: An empty-view invitation when the load failed.

### Replace a Table with it, never stack it under one. {#replace-a-table-with-it-never-stack-it-under-one}

Pass `EmptyState` to `DynamicTable`'s `emptyView` (or the Table template's `emptyState` with `empty`) so it replaces the whole table, header row and footer included. Never stack an `EmptyState` under an empty Static table.

Do: An EmptyState in DynamicTable's emptyView replaces the whole table.
Don't: An EmptyState under a Static table with an empty body.

## Accessibility

- **A real heading.** The header is one level below the section that holds the
  EmptyState, so it joins the page outline.
- **Decorative picture.** The image and icon are hidden from screen readers; the
  words carry the meaning.
- **Contrast.** Header and description use the text roles, which pass in every
  color mode.
- **Reflow.** The text wraps inside a column no wider than
  `--section-min-width-main`.

## Related

- `DynamicTable`: use when passing `EmptyState` into a table's `emptyView` or `noResultsView` slot.
- `Illustration`: use when placing a PLUS character in the `image` slot.
- Empty: use when choosing empty and error states across pages, sections and tables.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Picture.** An `image` slot or a Font Awesome Free `icon`. Decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
2. **Header.** A heading one level below the section that holds it.
3. **Description.** One line on what goes here and what to do.
4. **Actions.** One primary `Button` and an optional secondary one.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Header, description and picture on their text and icon tokens. |
| Hovered | The message is not a control; its Buttons carry their own hovered state. |
| Pressed | The message is not a control; its Buttons carry their own pressed state. |
| Focused | Tab moves through the actions only. |
| Disabled | Not supported on the message; disable an action Button instead. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Header | `--heading-md` (default), `--heading-sm` (compact), `--ds-text` |
| Description | `--body-default`, `--ds-text-subtle` |
| Icon | `--ds-icon-subtle` |
| Spacing | `--stack-sm`, `--inline-md`, `--section-stack-sm`, `--stack-xl`, `--page-stack-sm`, `--page-stack-md`, `--page-stack-lg` |
| Width | `--section-min-width-main` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the header short and specific to what is missing. | Apologize or blame: "Oops, nothing here." |
| Use the description for context that helps someone decide what to do. | Repeat the header in the description. |
| Make the primary action name the next step: "Add student". | Use a generic label such as "Continue". |
| Add a secondary action only for a real alternative, such as importing. | Add a second action just to fill space. |
| For a failure, say what happened in plain words and offer Try again. | Show an error code or "Something went wrong" with no next step. |
| For no access, give the reason and who can help. | Offer an action the person is not allowed to take. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `header` | node | — | What this view is, as a heading: "No students yet". |
| `description` | node | — | One line on what goes here and what to do, in an inviting voice. |
| `image` | node | — | Picture slot, such as an Illustration. Takes the place of `icon`. |
| `icon` | string | — | A Font Awesome Free solid name, such as "user-group", shown when there is no `image`. |
| `primaryAction` | node | — | The one action that fills the view: a filled Button. |
| `secondaryAction` | node | — | An optional second action: an outlined Button. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` for a view or panel; `compact` for a table body or a card. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--body-default` · `--ds-icon-subtle` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--heading-md` · `--heading-sm` · `--icon-lg` · `--image-md` · `--inline-md` · `--page-stack-lg` · `--page-stack-md` · `--page-stack-sm` · `--screen-pad-x` · `--section-min-width-main` · `--stack-md` · `--stack-sm` · `--stack-xl`

# Fieldset

Fieldset — a legend plus the fields it groups. A thin, token-styled wrap around Base UI's Fieldset: `Root` renders the `<fieldset>`, `Legend` renders a `<div>` already wired to `aria-labelledby` the fieldset. `RadioGroup` builds on this; a "Checkbox group" is the same composition with `Checkbox` instead.

Also asked as: field group.

**Import:** `import { Fieldset } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Fieldset.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Fieldset.stories.jsx` — Default, CheckboxGroup, WithRequiredAndError, Required, Invalid, Disabled, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Fieldset.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Fieldset` when a set of mixed controls shares one legend and one validation message, such as related text fields asked together.

## Alternatives

- For a group of radio buttons under one question, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a group of checkboxes under one question, use `CheckboxGroup`.
- For a single field with its own label and caption, use `TextField` or `Select`.

## Best practices

### One `error` covers the whole group. {#one-error-covers-the-whole-group}

Pass `error` on the Fieldset, not on each field inside it, when the validation applies to the set as a whole: "Choose at least one", for example, rather than a field-by-field message.

```jsx
<Fieldset legend="Notify me by" isRequired error={error}>
    <Checkbox label="Email" />
    <Checkbox label="Text" />
</Fieldset>
```

### Build on a fieldset rather than reimplementing it. {#build-on-a-fieldset-rather-than-reimplementing-it}

`RadioGroup` and `CheckboxGroup` already compose `Fieldset` with `Radio` and `Checkbox` children. Reach for those directly for single-question choice sets, and use `Fieldset` on its own when grouping custom or mixed fields.

Do: A fieldset with one legend for the set.
Don't: Loose boxes in a plain container, with no legend.

### Group related fields under one legend. {#group-related-fields-under-one-legend}

The legend names what the fields have in common. Without it a screen reader hears loose, unrelated fields.

Do: The legend names the group.
Don't: A legend that says nothing.

### Keep the legend to a few words. {#keep-the-legend-to-a-few-words}

A legend is a label, not an instruction. Two or three words stay on one line.

Do: One short line.
Don't: A whole sentence as the legend.

### Name the group, not the action. {#name-the-group-not-the-action}

The legend says what the fields are. The button says what to do with them.

Do: A noun phrase.
Don't: An instruction.

## Accessibility

- **A real `fieldset` and `legend` pair.** The legend is tied to the group through native HTML semantics, which every screen reader already understands.
- **The error is announced once.** `role="alert"` on the error message means assistive technology hears it as soon as it appears, without needing focus to move there.
- **`isRequired` is spoken even when unmarked.** When most fields in the form are required and `labelMarker` is omitted, a visually hidden `"(required)"` is added to the legend's accessible name; when `labelMarker="required"` is set, the visible `"(required)"` text already names it.

## Related

- `RadioGroup`: use when grouping radio buttons under a shared legend and error.
- `CheckboxGroup`: use when grouping checkboxes under a shared legend and error.
- [Form](?path=/docs/components-forms-and-inputs-form--docs): use when reviewing the label and caption rules for individual fields.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Legend.** Names the group, in body default. An optional `"(optional)"` or `"(required)"` minority marker follows it in the same type style.
2. **Fields.** The grouped fields, stacked with `--stack-md` between them.
3. **Error.** One message under the fields, in body small.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Required | `isRequired` adds a visually hidden `"(required)"` to the legend's accessible name when no visible `labelMarker="required"` is shown; pass `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| Invalid | The error shows in `--ds-text-danger`, announced with `role="alert"` and linked with `aria-describedby`. |
| Disabled | The native `disabled` attribute disables every field inside. |

A fieldset has no hover, pressed or focus state of its own. The fields inside carry theirs.

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Legend and minority marker | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Error | `--ds-text-danger`, body small. |
| Gap | `--stack-md`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write the legend as the question or topic: "Notify me by". | A generic legend: "Options". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a colon after the legend. |
| Say what to do in the error: "Choose at least one." | "Required" or "Invalid". |
| Keep the legend short enough to read as a heading. | A paragraph of instructions in the legend. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the fieldset. The legend and error ids derive from it. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `legend` | node | — | Labels the fieldset's contents. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the legend: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables the fieldset and every control inside it. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Announces the group as required to assistive technology. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `error` | node | — | One error for the group, announced when it appears. |
| `children` | node | — | The fields the legend groups. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the `<fieldset>`, beside `plus-fieldset`. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the `<fieldset>`. |

A legend is a label, not an instruction. Two or three words stay on one line.

### Name the group, not the action.

The legend says what the fields are. The button says what to do with them.

# FileItem

`FileItem` — one 56px row representing a file or a folder in a `FileUpload` list or as a standalone attachment on a note, comment or message. Anatomy (`start`, `label`, `description`, `end`) is structured for reuse: a 20px lead status/type indicator, middle-truncated name with a full-name tooltip, one status/meta line, and at most one removal control (preceded by Retry on `error`).

**Import:** `import { FileItem } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FileItem/FileItem.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FileItem/FileItem.stories.jsx` — Overview, Queued, Uploading0, Uploading40, Uploading80, DoneRemove, DoneDelete, ErrorWithRetry, FolderUploading, FolderDone, ReadOnly, Disabled, LongName, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FileItem/FileItem.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · progress `linear`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `FileItem` inside `FileUpload`'s `children` slot to represent every chosen file or folder, or standalone to display attachments on session notes, comments, and messages. Every row stays locked to `--file-item-height` (`56px`) across `queued`, `uploading`, `done`, and `error` so a list never shifts height as uploads progress.

## Motion

FileItem reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Row state and action hover transitions. |
| progress | Load content | `--ds-motion-linear` | The uploading ProgressRing fills clockwise with the upload. |

## Alternatives

- For choosing or dropping files from a device, use `FileUpload`.
- For overall progress across a checklist or page section rather than a row's lead slot, use `ProgressBar`.
- For a compact inline token representing a person or category rather than an attachment, use `Tag`.

## Best practices

### Match the removal mode to whether the file is already saved. {#match-the-removal-mode-to-whether-the-file-is-already-saved}

Use `removal="cancel"` while uploading and `removal="remove"` in an unsaved form so an accidental click is reversible, and reserve `removal="delete"` for saved attachments where removing deletes stored data.

Do: Saved attachment uses trash and asks to confirm before deleting.
Don't: Saved attachment removed immediately with an X and no confirmation.

### State both the cause and the fix on upload errors. {#state-both-the-cause-and-the-fix-on-upload-errors}

Write `error` as one sentence naming why the upload failed and what the person can do next alongside `Retry`.

Do: Names the limit and the next step beside Retry.
Don't: Leaves the user guessing why Retry will or will not work.

### Represent a chosen folder as one folder row with its file count. {#represent-a-chosen-folder-as-one-folder-row-with-its-file-count}

Keep the file list scannable by collapsing a dropped or picked folder into one `kind="folder"` row that reports its item count in `meta`.

Do: One folder row with its file count in meta.
Don't: Folder row hides how many files were included.

## Accessibility

- **Full file name stays accessible.** Visually truncated names expose a single unbroken accessible text node for screen readers and Links, and reveal the full name in a `Tooltip` on hover or focus.
- **Determinate upload progress.** While `status="uploading"`, `ProgressRing` announces `role="progressbar"` with `aria-label="Uploading <name>"` and `aria-valuenow`.
- **Named per-file actions.** Cancel, Remove, and Delete `IconButton` controls include the file name in their accessible label (`"Remove zoom_0.mp4"`, `"Delete signed_consent.pdf"`) so screen-reader users can distinguish rows in a batch.
- **Keyboard-accessible delete confirmation.** `removal="delete"` opens a Base UI `Popup` dialog that traps Escape and outside clicks to cancel cleanly and returns focus to the trigger.

## Related

- `FileUpload`: use when letting a user pick or drop files and folders into a form field.
- `ProgressRing`: use when showing determinate 0–100% progress inside a compact slot.
- `Popup`: use when anchoring lightweight confirmation or secondary detail to a trigger control.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Lead (`start`).** A `--image-xs` (`20px`) slot: a `subtlest` clock when `queued`, a `ProgressRing` when `uploading`, a danger icon on `error`, a folder icon when `kind="folder"` is `done`, or the matching file-type icon when `kind="file"` is `done`.
2. **Name (`label`).** Single-line name that truncates before the extension so `.mp4` or `.pdf` remains readable, wrapped in a `Tooltip` with the full name. Opens via `Link` when `href` is set on a `done` item.
3. **Meta (`description`).** Single-line secondary status: `Waiting` when `queued`, `Uploading · <n>%` when `uploading`, `meta` (or `Uploaded`) when `done`, and the `error` message in danger text on `error`.
4. **Actions (`end`).** Omitted when `isReadOnly` or `isDisabled`. Draws a compact subtle X `IconButton` for `cancel` and `remove`, or a trash `IconButton` that confirms via `Popup` for `delete`. On `error`, a compact subtle `Retry` `Button` precedes the X control.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Queued | Clock icon in `--ds-icon-subtlest`, `Waiting` in `--ds-text-subtle`, and Cancel X. |
| Uploading | `ProgressRing` at `--image-xs`, `Uploading · <n>%` in `--ds-text-subtle`, and Cancel X. |
| Done | File-type or folder icon in `--ds-icon-subtle`, `meta` (size, count, or date), optional `href` link, and Remove X or Delete trash with confirmation. |
| Error | Danger icon in `--ds-icon-danger`, cause-and-fix message in `--ds-text-danger`, and `Retry` before Remove X. |
| Read-only | Full contrast and openable `href` link, with all end actions hidden. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled`, `--ds-border-disabled`, and `--ds-text-disabled`; end actions hidden and links disabled. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Row height and padding | `--file-item-height`, horizontal padding `--pad-x-lg`, gap `--inline-lg`. |
| Row surface and border | `--ds-surface`, `--ds-border`, radius `--radius-control-md`; list dividers use `--border-width-default` in `--ds-border`. |
| Lead slot | `--image-xs`; icons use `--ds-icon-subtlest`, `--ds-icon-subtle`, and `--ds-icon-danger`. |
| Name and meta | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; meta in `--body-sm` and `--ds-text-subtle` (or `--ds-text-danger` on error). |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the real file name and extension intact so middle truncation preserves the type. | Strip the extension from `name`. |
| Write error messages with cause and fix: "Connection dropped. Check your network and retry." | "Error" or "Failed". |
| Include file count on folders: "6 files · 142 MB". | Show a folder name with no count. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `name` | string (required) | — | File or folder display name. Truncates in the middle so the extension stays visible, with the full name in a tooltip. |
| `meta` | node | — | Secondary metadata such as file size (`"14.2 MB"`), folder item count (`"6 files"`), or saved date (`"Added Nov 12"`). |
| `status` | enum | — | Current upload lifecycle state of the item. |
| `progress` | number | — | Upload percent from 0 to 100 while `status` is `uploading`. |
| `error` | node | — | One-sentence cause and fix shown on `status="error"`. |
| `kind` | enum | `'file'` | `file` (default) or `folder` (uses the folder icon when done and shows file count in `meta`). |
| `fileType` | string | — | Explicit file category or extension (`pdf`, `video`, `audio`, `image`, `archive`, `word`, `spreadsheet`, `presentation`, `code`, `text`, `file`). Inferred from `name` when omitted. |
| `removal` | enum | — | `cancel` (in-flight upload X), `remove` (unsaved form X), or `delete` (saved attachment trash icon that confirms first). |
| `onRemove` | func | — | Called when the user cancels, removes, or confirms deleting the item. |
| `onRetry` | func | — | Called when the user presses Retry on an `error` item. |
| `href` | string | — | Destination URL that opens a completed (`status="done"`) file. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Hides all end actions while keeping full contrast, for read-only views and static attachments. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Hides end actions, disables opening links, and dims the row. |
| `id` | string | — | Element id on the row container. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the row container. |

## Variants

**`status`** — `queued` · `uploading` · `done` · `error`

**`kind`** — `file` · `folder`

**`removal`** — `cancel` · `remove` · `delete`

# FilterButton

Filter button: opens or toggles a filter. It shows the filter's name, an optional count of what is applied, and a chevron when it opens a menu.

Also asked as: filter chip, filter control.

**Import:** `import { FilterButton } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Label, Metric, Appearances, Spacing, States, Selected, Disabled, Loading, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterButton/FilterButton.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `FilterButton` for a control in a view bar that opens a filter's options or toggles a filter on and off.

## Motion

FilterButton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The count hugs the label: the button widens, the number fades in. |

## Alternatives

- For a single-list filter menu that applies on pick, use `PopupSelect`.
- For several filter categories staged and applied together from one trigger, use `FilterMenu`.
- For showing a chosen filter value that can be removed directly, use `Tag`.
- For a general action that is not a filter, use `Button`.

## Best practices

### Keep space between filter buttons. {#keep-space-between-filter-buttons}

Leave a gap so neighboring filter buttons read as separate targets.

Do: A clear gap between filter buttons.
Don't: Filter buttons touching.

### Show the active count. {#show-the-active-count}

When a filter is applied, the trailing count says how many values are
active. Pass `trailingMetric` once at least one value is selected, and leave
it out when none is: `0` renders as a visible count of zero, not an empty
state.

Do: Subject shows its three applied values; Grade, with none, shows no count.
Don't: Subject has three values applied but shows no count.

```jsx
<FilterButton text="Status" trailingMetric={selected.length || undefined} />
```

### Let it hug its label. {#let-it-hug-its-label}

Keep the natural width, so the chevron stays right after the name. Filter
button has no prop to fill its container; don't stretch it across a wide row
with your own styles.

### Fold into one menu on narrow screens. {#fold-into-one-menu-on-narrow-screens}

Below the desktop breakpoint (`768px`), a row of filter buttons does not fit. Fold them into one filter `IconButton` whose `FilterMenu` stacks the categories, and pass the total applied count as `trailingMetric`.

```jsx
<IconButton icon="filter" label="Filters" trailingMetric={applied} />
```

### Use the filter's name as the label. {#use-the-filter-s-name-as-the-label}

Do: The label is the filter's name.
Don't: A verb phrase repeats what the button already does.

### Turn off the chevron only when the button doesn't open a menu. {#turn-off-the-chevron-only-when-the-button-doesn-t-open-a-menu}

`hasChevronDown` defaults to `true`. Set it `false` only for a filter that
toggles directly on click, with nothing to open.

## Accessibility

- **A real button, unchanged.** `FilterButton` renders a `Button`
  underneath, so focus, activation and disabled/loading states all follow
  `Button`'s own contract.
- **The chevron is decorative.** It signals that a menu opens, but the
  accessible name comes from `text` and, when present, the applied count.

## Related

- `PopupSelect`: use when the filter button opens a single list that applies on pick.
- `FilterMenu`: use when several filter categories stage and apply together.
- `Tag`: use when displaying an applied filter value as a removable tag.
- `Button`: use when the control triggers a general action rather than a filter.

## Parts

1. **Container.** A Button, 32 at default spacing and 24 at compact.
2. **Label** (optional). The field the filter narrows, in subtle text before the text; the button then reads "Field: value".
3. **Text.** The filter's name, or its value when there is a label, in ink.
4. **Metric** (optional). The count of applied values, after the name. `0` shows; leave it out to hide it.
5. **Chevron** (optional). Drawn by default; turn it off when the button toggles instead of opening a menu.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | The container takes the hovered fill of its appearance. |
| Pressed | The container takes the pressed fill of its appearance. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge, for keyboard focus only. |

| Use sentence case: "Grade level". | Title case or all capitals: "Grade Level". |

| `isDisabled` | bool | — | — |
| `isLoading` | bool | — | — |
| `onClick` | func | — | — |

# FilterMenu

Filter menu: several filter categories in a Popup, held until Apply. - **Held until Apply.** Ticking a box changes the menu, not the content. Apply hands the values to `onApply`, closes the menu with a fade, and the content behind swaps in place once. Escape or a click away drops what was ticked; the next open starts from what is applied. - **Clear** clears every box in the menu without applying. Apply then applies the empty set. Both are compact (24) at the end of the menu: Clear is Subtle, Apply is Default, with no Primary. - **Layout follows the count.** Two or three categories sit side by side at `3-col`; four or more stack, at `3-col` or `4-col`. - **The trigger** is the Filter icon button, its count the number of values applied, on the selected fill once any is. It opens `bottom-end`, the end of the bar where filters sit.

Also asked as: filter dropdown.

**Import:** `import { FilterMenu } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.; Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterMenu/FilterMenu.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterMenu/FilterMenu.stories.jsx` — Overview, OpensWithAFade, Staging, Stacked, Placement, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/FilterMenu/FilterMenu.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `FilterMenu` when a section's content takes two or more filter categories staged and applied together from one Filter icon trigger.

- **Two or three categories with short lists:** side by side.
- **Four or more, or long lists:** stacked (`layout="stacked"`).

## Motion

FilterMenu reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, with no clip or travel. From the keyboard it opens with no animation. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, the same as the enter. |

## Alternatives

- For one category in a menu that applies as you pick, use `PopupSelect`.
- For one to three quick filter triggers in a bar, use `FilterButton`.

## Best practices

### Show the applied count on the trigger. {#show-the-applied-count-on-the-trigger}

The trigger's `trailingMetric` is the only place applied filters show; never add a row of filter tags under the bar, and never combine quick `FilterButton` triggers with a `FilterMenu` in the same bar.

### Apply changes only when Apply is pressed. {#apply-changes-only-when-apply-is-pressed}

The content behind the menu updates once on Apply, not on each checkbox tick, so the page does not jump while someone is still choosing.

### Stack categories when lists are long. {#stack-categories-when-lists-are-long}

Pass `layout="stacked"` when a few categories have long option lists so each category gets the full menu width.

## Accessibility

- **The trigger is a real button** that says a popup opens and whether it is
  open. Its name carries the count: "Filters, 2 applied".
- **The popup is named** by `label`, and each category is a group named by
  its legend.
- **Focus moves into the menu** on open and **returns to the trigger** after
  Apply or Escape.

## Related

- `PopupSelect`: use when one filter category applies immediately on pick.
- `FilterButton`: use when placing one to three quick filter triggers directly in a bar.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Trigger.** The Filter `IconButton`. Once any value is applied it shows the count on the selected fill and reads "Filters, 2 applied".
2. **Popup.** A `Popup` at a column step: `3-col` side by side; `3-col` or `4-col` stacked.
3. **Categories.** A `Fieldset` per category, its label the legend, its options `Checkbox`es. Pick as many as apply.
4. **Footer.** Clear (subtle) and Apply (default), compact, at the end. No Primary.

### Placement

| Trigger | `placement` |
| --- | --- |
| At the end of a bar, where filters sit | `bottom-end` (default): the menu's end edge meets the trigger's. |
| At the start of a bar | `bottom-start`: the menu's start edge meets the trigger's. |

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Open | The menu fades in place, on the values applied. A keyboard open is instant. |
| Ticked | The box changes color. The content behind does not change. |
| Clear | Every box clears with the same color change. Nothing is applied yet. |
| Applied | The menu fades, the content behind swaps in place once, and the trigger's count changes. Nothing slides. |
| Dismissed | Escape or a click away closes it and drops the ticks; the next open starts from what is applied. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | Those of `Popup`: `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--popup-radius`. |
| Pad, and the gap above the footer | 16: `--popup-pad`. |
| Gap between categories | `--inline-lg` across, `--stack-lg` down. |
| Height of the categories | Scroll past 320: `--dropdown-menu-max-height`. |
| Gap to the trigger | 4: `--popup-offset`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| "Clear" in the menu. | "Reset", "Reset filters" or "Clear all" in the menu. "Reset filters" is for everywhere else, such as a No matches state. |
| Name a category by what it holds: "Status", "Subject". | A verb phrase such as "Filter by status". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `container` | object | — | Where the open menu mounts: an element. Leave it out for the page's overlay layer; name one to keep the menu inside a picture or a scrolling region. |
| `categories` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | The filter categories, in order: `{ id, label, options }`. Options are strings, or `{ value, label, isDisabled }`. Each category is a list of checkboxes; pick as many as apply. |
| `value` | objectOf | — | The applied values, `{ [categoryId]: value[] }`. Leave it out to let the menu keep its own. |
| `defaultValue` | objectOf | — | The values applied at first, when `value` is left out. |
| `onApply` | func | — | `(value)`, called on Apply with every category, an empty list for a category with nothing picked. Nothing is called while boxes are ticked. |
| `label` | string | `'Filters'` | Names the menu and the Filter icon button: "Filters", read "Filters, 2 applied" once two are. |
| `trigger` | node or func | — | A trigger of your own, or `({ isOpen, count }) => node`. Without it the Filter icon button is drawn. |
| `placement` | enum | `'bottom-end'` | `bottom-end` (default) for a trigger at the end of a bar, `bottom-start` for one at its start. |
| `layout` | enum | — | Leave it out to follow the count: two or three categories side by side, four or more stacked. Set `stacked` for a few categories with long lists. |
| `width` | enum | `'3-col'` | The column step of a stacked menu, `3-col` (default) or `4-col`. A side-by-side menu is always `3-col`. |
| `isOpen` | bool | — | Whether the menu is open. Leave it out to let the trigger open and close it. |
| `defaultOpen` | bool | `false` | Opens the menu on first render, when `isOpen` is left out. |
| `onOpenChange` | func | — | `(open)`. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | The Filter icon button's spacing: `default` draws 32, `compact` 24. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra classes on the popup. |
| `id` | string | — | The popup's id. |

## Variants

**`placement`** — `bottom-start` · `bottom-end`

**`layout`** — `side-by-side` · `stacked`

**`width`** — `3-col` · `4-col`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--dropdown-menu-max-height` · `--heading-xs` · `--inline-lg` · `--inline-md` · `--plus-filter-menu-columns` · `--popup-pad` · `--stack-lg`

One surface, 400 wide, padded 16: a 16 icon on the title's first line, the title and its optional description, actions, and the controls. `appearance` alone decides the kind: `normal` is the default flag (overlay surface, a status icon or an avatar, always the dismiss ×, actions as links); every other appearance is bold (its bold fill, no ×, collapsed to its title behind a chevron, actions as buttons).

props.name: id
props.description: Id set on the flag surface.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `normal` (default), `information`, `warning`, `error` or `success`.

props.name: title
props.description: What happened, in a few words.

props.name: children
props.description: An optional description under the title.

props.name: actions
props.description: Actions under the description, in the order given, at most two. Links on a default flag, buttons on a bold one. An action with an `href` on a bold flag draws a button that navigates.

props.name: icon
props.description: The default flag's leading icon: a status icon name, or an element such as an Avatar. Unset, the information icon in the subtle icon color. Ignored on a bold flag, which shows its appearance's icon.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Whether a bold flag starts expanded.

props.name: show
props.description: Whether the flag renders. Defaults to true; false renders nothing and stops the auto-close timer.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called with no arguments when the dismiss button is pressed and when the auto-close timer ends. The caller sets `show` to false.

props.name: delay
props.description: How long it stays before closing itself, in ms. 8000 by default; keep it at 8000 or more so a slow reader is not cut off.

props.name: autohide
props.description: Close itself after `delay`. Defaults to true for normal, information and success; warning and error never close themselves.

props.name: timer
props.description: Draws a 4 px countdown bar as the flag's top cap, emptying over `delay`, and steps the corners from 12 to 4. For a timed action such as Undo: the first action undoes, `onDismiss` commits. The bar and the wait pause while the flag is hovered or focused.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class on the flag surface.

props.name: headerClass
props.description: Extra class on the header row that holds the title and timestamp.

props.name: bodyClass
props.description: Extra class on the description container.

props.name: timestamp
props.description: Small text beside the title, such as "11 mins ago".

props.name: sound
props.description: The sound token it plays as it lands, through the app's sound setting, or `false` for none. Unset, an `error` flag plays `error` and every other appearance plays `notify`. Pass `false` when a flag should stay quiet, such as during a session.

props.description: Hold reduced motion on or off for this flag. Unset, it follows its FlagGroup, then the person's setting.

props.name: staggerDelayMs
props.description: Optional entrance stagger delay in ms when arriving as part of a burst.

props.name: onExited
props.description: Called once the leaving flag's exit animation finishes and it unmounts.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles applied to the flag surface.

# Flag

The Popup family's Flag (Figma Pattern/Flag). One surface, 400 wide, padded 16: a 16 icon on the title's first line, the title and its optional description, actions, and the controls. `appearance` alone decides the kind: `normal` is the default flag (overlay surface, a status icon or an avatar, always the dismiss ×, actions as links); every other appearance is bold (its bold fill, no ×, collapsed to its title behind a chevron, actions as buttons).

Also asked as: notification, snackbar, success message, undo, temporary message, notify, save confirmation.

**Import:** `import { Flag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Flag/Flag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Flag/Flag.stories.jsx` — Overview, Normal, Information, Success, Warning, ErrorAppearance, BackgroundFailure, Bold, Interactive, Dismiss, UndoTimer, FlagContent, UnknownAppearance, ActionKinds, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, LandsWithNotify, StackClosesUp, StackClosesUpReduced, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced, MotionExitCompletes, MotionQueueStack, MotionQueueStackReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Flag/Flag.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.default`, sound `sound.notify` · exit `spatial.exit` · dismiss `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.default` · milestone `spatial.fast`, sound `sound.done.step` · prompt `spatial.default` + `appearance.default`, sound `sound.prompt` · failed `spatial.default` + `appearance.default`, sound `sound.error`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Flag` to confirm something that has already happened and needs no reply:
saved, sent, copied. `show` and `onDismiss` are yours; the component holds no
state. `FlagGroup` positions a stack of them.

`appearance` alone decides the kind of flag and its controls. A **default flag**
(`normal`) is for passive news a person can clear: the overlay surface, an `icon`
that carries the meaning (a status icon name or an element such as an `Avatar`), the
dismiss × and actions as links. A **bold flag** (`information`, `warning`, `error`,
`success`) takes the appearance's bold fill, starts collapsed to its title, and
opens its description and actions behind a chevron; its actions are buttons.

### The dismiss rule

- The × is on default flags only, never on bold.
- A bold flag leaves when its action resolves it, or, for information and success,
  when it times out. Warning and error never close themselves and offer a next action.
- A `FlagGroup` never mixes dismissible and non-dismissible flags: a stack is all
  default flags or all bold.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Normal | The default flag, for passive news a person can clear. Closes itself after `delay` (default `8000`). Example: "Notes copied". Set `icon` to a status icon or an `Avatar`. |
| Information | Bold. Something worth knowing, on the dark neutral fill. Times out. |
| Success | Bold. A finished action. Times out. |
| Warning | Bold. Something to check before going on. Never closes itself; offers a next action. |
| Error | Bold. Something that failed. Never closes itself; offers a next action. |

### Sound

A flag plays a sound as it lands: Error for an error flag, Notify for every other appearance, through the app's sound setting. Pass `sound={false}` where a flag should stay quiet, such as during a session.

## Motion

Flag reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | Slides in from the top-right corner. | `sound.notify` on land: outside a session; any appearance but error, which plays Error (the failed event); Flags that arrive together play once |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-exit` | Timed out: leaves the way it came, toward the top-right corner, on spatial.exit aimed 3.8× past the edge; the stack then closes up. |  |
| dismiss | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Closed by hand: a quick fade in place. |  |
| change | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The stack closes up when one leaves. |  |
| milestone | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Finishing a reflection: inside an Expressive container, slides in from the top-right corner with one overshoot; leaves by the exit rules. | `sound.done.step` on land: a reflection is complete |
| prompt | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A Flag that asks for action now enters like any Flag. | `sound.prompt` on land: session link ready, a lead with an empty tutor, wrap-up, few students at 10 min; an app passes sound="prompt"; plays when the tab is hidden |
| failed | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A danger Flag for a failed background job enters like any Flag and stays until closed. | `sound.error` on land: an error Flag, the default for that appearance: a background job the person started failed |

## Alternatives

- For something the user must read or act on in the page flow, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a decision that blocks the task until answered, use `Modal`.
- For help attached to a specific control, use `Tooltip` or `Popup`.

## Best practices

### Match the appearance to the outcome. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-outcome}

Success for a finished action; error only when something failed.

Do: Success appearance for a saved session.
Don't: Error appearance on good news.

### Keep routine news on the default flag. {#keep-routine-news-on-the-default-flag}

A bold flag competes with the page; routine news stays quiet and can be cleared.

Do: Default flag for routine news.
Don't: Bold fill on a routine confirmation.

### Say what happened and what to do next. {#say-what-happened-and-what-to-do-next}

A title names the event; the description gives the next step.

Do: Event in the title, next step below.
Don't: A bare title with no next step.

### Show a background failure as an error Flag with Try again. {#show-a-background-failure-as-an-error-flag-with-try-again}

When work fails out of sight, such as a sync or an autosave, use an error flag.
It stays until the action resolves it and carries **Try again** as its action, so the person can
retry without leaving what they are doing. A failure to load a view is not a
flag: it takes the view's `EmptyState`.

Do: Error flag with Try again; it stays until the action resolves it.
Don't: A failure with no next action.

### Never put required information only in a flag. {#never-put-required-information-only-in-a-flag}

The user can dismiss a flag before reading it, and that takes the only copy
with it. A rejected form submit stays on the form, in a danger `SectionMessage`
at the top with an error on each field.

### Turn off autohide for anything the user might need to re-read. {#turn-off-autohide-for-anything-the-user-might-need-to-re-read}

With `autohide={false}`, or `delay={0}`, a default flag waits for its ×.

### Do not mix dismissible and non-dismissible flags in one stack. {#do-not-mix-dismissible-and-non-dismissible-flags-in-one-stack}

The × is on default flags only, so a stack is all default flags or all bold.

## Accessibility

- **Only warning and error interrupt.** Those two appearances are `role="alert"`
  with `aria-live="assertive"`. Every other appearance is `role="status"` with
  `aria-live="polite"`, so a success flag waits for the screen reader to finish
  what it is saying. Every appearance is `aria-atomic`, so the flag is read as one
  message.
- **The timeout is a timing limit.** Content that disappears on its own has to
  be dismissible or extendable to satisfy WCAG's timing rule. The ×
  is what does that on a default flag; a bold flag that times out is information or
  success, and one that does not is warning or error, which offer an action.
- **Announcement needs the region to already exist.** A flag mounted at the same
  moment as its container may not be announced at all. Render `FlagGroup`
  with the page and put flags into it.
- **The dismiss button is the shared `CloseButton`** on a default flag's surface, with an `aria-hidden` ×. The × and its focus ring are at least 3:1 on that surface.
- **The appearance icon is decorative.** It is `aria-hidden`, so the title beside it
  carries the meaning; the color and icon should never carry it alone.
- **The chevron reports its state.** It sets `aria-expanded`, so a screen reader
  hears whether a bold flag is expanded or collapsed.

## Related

- `CloseButton`: use when rendering the dismiss control on a default flag.
- `EmptyState`: use when a whole view fails to load rather than a background sync.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Icon.** On a default flag the `icon` (the information icon unless set); on a bold flag the appearance glyph. Decorative.
2. **Title.** What happened, in a few words, in `--heading-xs` whatever level the page around it is at.
3. **Timestamp.** Optional, subtle, after the title.
4. **Description.** At most one line.
5. **Actions.** At most two, under the description: links on a default flag, compact `Button`s on a bold one; an action with an `href` navigates either way.
6. **Expand toggle.** Only on a bold flag that has a description or actions; it starts collapsed to its title.
7. **Dismiss.** The shared `CloseButton`, named "Dismiss flag", on default flags only.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The appearance icon color on the overlay surface; a bold flag fills the surface instead. |
| Hovered | The flag does not react; Dismiss and the toggle take the subtle hovered step. |
| Pressed | Dismiss and the toggle take the subtle pressed step. |
| Focused | Dismiss, the toggle and each action show the focus ring; the ring is inverse on a bold fill. |
| Disabled | Not supported. |
| Expanded | A bold flag shows its description and actions; collapsed, only the title. |
| Autohide | Normal, information and success close after `delay` (default `8000`; keep any `delay` at 8000 or more); warning and error never close themselves. |
| Dismissed | The flag leaves the stack. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--popup-radius`, `--popup-pad`, `--flag-width` |
| Title, description | `--heading-xs`, `--ds-text`; `--body-default`, `--ds-text-subtle` |
| Icon | `--ds-icon-subtle`, `--ds-icon-information`, `--ds-icon-success`, `--ds-icon-warning`, `--ds-icon-danger`, at `--icon-md` |

| Gaps | `--inline-lg` before Dismiss, `--inline-md`, `--stack-sm`; `--flag-stack` between flags |
| Group | `--layer-flag`, `--popup-gap-screen` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say what happened in the title, in a few words. | Put the only copy of important information in a flag. |
| Add one line of description at most. | Write a paragraph in the description. |
| Write actions as verbs: "Undo", "View session". | Use "Click here" or "OK" as an action. |

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id set on the flag surface. |
