# InlineEdit

InlineEdit — text that reads as text and becomes a field when it is pressed. The read view and the edit view are drawn at the same size, so opening the editor does not move anything around it. Enter or leaving the editor confirms; Escape cancels. Confirm and cancel buttons sit under the edit view and can be left off. `validate` can refuse a value with a message, and the editor stays open. The parent holds the value. `defaultValue` is what the edit view starts with each time it opens, and `onConfirm` is where the new value goes. Not for use inside a form: it saves on its own and has no say in the form's submit. Use `Input` there.

**Import:** `import { InlineEdit } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/InlineEdit/InlineEdit.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/InlineEdit/InlineEdit.stories.jsx` — Textfield, LeavingConfirms, KeepOpenOnBlur, Validation, FailedConfirm, WithoutButtons, StartsOpen, SameHeight, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, ButtonsDoNotMoveThePage, WithAnotherEditView, Placeholder, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/InlineEdit/InlineEdit.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · rejected `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `InlineEdit` for a value that is read far more often than it is changed and
that can be saved on its own: a title, a name or a short note on a record or a
profile page.

## Motion

InlineEdit reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Read and edit states swap in place. |
| rejected | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A blocked save shakes the field and its button once. |

## Alternatives

- For a field in a form where a Save button submits every field together, use `TextField`: an inline edit saves when confirmed and has no say in the form's submit, so placing one in a form leaves two ways to save.
- For several lines edited in a form, use `TextArea`.

## Best practices

### Keep the read view plain text. {#keep-the-read-view-plain-text}

The whole read view is one button. A link or a button inside it cannot be
reached or pressed, so put those beside it.

Do: Plain text in the read view.
Don't: A link inside the read view, which cannot be reached or pressed.

### Confirm on Enter and on leaving. {#confirm-on-enter-and-on-leaving}

Both save; Escape cancels. The inline edit saves itself, so it needs no Save button of its own.

Do: Enter or leaving the field saves the title.
Don't: A separate Save step beside an inline edit.

### Use compact spacing in dense lists. {#use-compact-spacing-in-dense-lists}

`spacing="compact"` draws both views at `--control-md`, to sit in a table cell or a dense row.

Do: Compact rows in a dense list.
Don't: The default height spreads a dense list out.

### Let the parent hold the value. {#let-the-parent-hold-the-value}

`defaultValue` is what the edit view starts with each time it opens. Update it
in `onConfirm`, or the next edit starts from the old value.

### Say why a value was refused. {#say-why-a-value-was-refused}

Return the reason from `validate`, in the words a tutor would use. A refused
value leaves the editor open, so the person can fix it without retyping.

### Leave the editor open for long text. {#leave-the-editor-open-for-long-text}

Set `keepEditViewOpenOnBlur` where a stray click would publish an unfinished
thought, and keep the buttons so there is a clear way out.

## Accessibility

- **The read view is a button.** It is named by the label and the text ("Display
  name Ada Lovelace") and described as "Edit" (`editLabel`).
- **Focus follows the editor.** Opening it puts the caret in the field. Enter,
  the check or Escape returns focus to the read view. Leaving the field
  confirms and leaves focus where the person sent it.
- **Enter confirms and Escape cancels.** In a multi-line edit view, Enter adds a
  line and Cmd or Ctrl and Enter confirms.
- **Refusals are announced.** The message is in the field's caption with
  `role="alert"`, and the field is `aria-invalid`.
- **The buttons are named.** The check and the cross are icon-only, named by
  `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel`.

## Related

- `TextField`: use when configuring the text input inside `InlineEditableTextfield` or editing in place with `appearance="subtle"`.
- `TextArea`: use when passing a multi-line edit view to `InlineEdit`.

Same group: `Code` · `CodeBlock` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `StaticTable` · `TreeTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Label** (optional). Shown above both views.
2. **Read view.** The value as plain text on the field's own box. The whole view is one button.
3. **Edit view.** The field it opens into: a `TextField` in `InlineEditableTextfield`, or any edit view passed to `InlineEdit`.
4. **Actions.** The confirm and cancel icon buttons, on an overlay under the field. `hideActionButtons` leaves them off.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The read view: text on a transparent box with a transparent `--border-width-default` edge. |
| Hovered | The read view takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | Pressing the read view opens the edit view in the same box, with the caret in it. |
| Focused | The read view draws the focus ring; see Border. |
| Disabled | None. An inline edit has no disabled state. |
| Editing | The field's fill and `--border-width-default` input edge appear; nothing else moves. |
| Invalid | The field stays open with the danger edge and the message in its caption. |
| Placeholder | An empty read view shows the placeholder in `--ds-text-subtlest`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Read view height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. |
| Read view box | `--radius-control-lg`, a `--border-width-default` transparent edge, `--pad-x-md` either side. |
| Read view text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Read view hovered | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Actions | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--radius-md`, `--stack-sm` padding and gap. |
| Gap under the label | `--stack-sm`. |

The edit view takes the field's own tokens: see Text field.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label the value it holds: "Display name". | Label the action: "Edit name". |
| Give an empty value a placeholder that says what to add: "Add a nickname". | Leave an empty read view blank, with nothing to press. |
| Say why a value was refused: "Enter a name." | "Invalid" or "Error". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Base id for the edit view's control; the label points at it while editing. |
| `label` | node | — | Shown above both views. |
| `defaultValue` | any | — | What the edit view starts with each time it opens. The parent updates it after a confirm. |
| `readView` | func (required) | — | Returns the read view's content. Keep it to plain text: the whole view is one button. |
| `editView` | func (required) | — | Returns the edit view, given `{ id, value, onChange, validation, validationMessage, isSaving }`. `onChange` takes a value or a change event. |
| `onConfirm` | func | — | Called with the value on Enter, on leaving the editor and on the confirm button. Throw or reject to keep the editor open with the error. |
| `onCancel` | func | — | Called when Escape or the cancel button closes the editor. |
| `onEdit` | func | — | Called when the editor opens. |
| `validate` | func | — | Returns a message to refuse the value, or nothing to accept it. May be async. |
| `keepEditViewOpenOnBlur` | bool | `false` | Leaving the editor no longer confirms; only Enter and the confirm button do. |
| `startWithEditViewOpen` | bool | `false` | Opens in the edit view and puts the caret in it. |
| `hideActionButtons` | bool | `false` | Leaves off the confirm and cancel buttons. Enter, Escape and leaving the editor still work. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | Field and button height: `default` (40) or `compact` (32). |
| `readViewFitContainerWidth` | bool | `false` | The read view fills its container, so the whole row is one press target. |
| `editLabel` | string | `'Edit'` | What a screen reader hears after the read view, naming what pressing does. |
| `confirmLabel` | string | `'Confirm'` | — |
| `cancelLabel` | string | `'Cancel'` | — |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

`--body-default` · `--border-width-default` · `--control-lg` · `--control-md` · `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast-duration` · `--ds-shadow-overlay` · `--ds-surface-overlay` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtlest` · `--pad-x-md` · `--radius-control-lg` · `--radius-md` · `--stack-sm`

# InlineMessage

InlineMessage: a compact icon trigger that opens a Popup carrying the full message. Built on Popup so placement, dismissal and focus return are shared with every other popup in the system.

Also asked as: field error, helper error, inline error, form validation.

**Import:** `import { InlineMessage } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/InlineMessage/InlineMessage.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/InlineMessage/InlineMessage.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Info, Warning, Danger, Success, WithSecondaryText, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, BestPracticesLive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/InlineMessage/InlineMessage.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast` · exit `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `InlineMessage` for a note that explains or qualifies something right
beside it, such as why a field is required or what a score means, without
taking up space until someone asks. Pass `defaultOpen` when the message popup
should start open on first render. It is built on `Popup`, so placement,
dismissal and focus return are shared with every other popup in the system.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Info | The default, for a neutral explanation. |
| Warning | The note is cautionary: say what happens if they proceed. |
| Danger | The note explains something that failed or is blocked. |
| Success | The note confirms an outcome. |

## Motion

InlineMessage reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Makes room, then fades in. |
| exit | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades, then the room closes. |

## Alternatives

- For a message that belongs to a page or section and should always be visible, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a short plain-text label on hover or focus over a control, use `Tooltip`.

## Best practices

### Match the tint to the meaning. {#match-the-tint-to-the-meaning}

Info for a neutral note; danger only when something failed. The icon is a
second cue, not a style choice.

Do: Info for a neutral note.
Don't: Danger for a neutral note.

### Keep it to one short line. {#keep-it-to-one-short-line}

It sits beside a field; long copy pushes the form around.

Do: One short sentence.
Don't: A paragraph beside a field.

### Show one message per field. {#show-one-message-per-field}

Two messages on one field leave no clear next step.

Do: A single message.
Don't: An info note and a warning together.

### Write the label as the question the popup answers. {#write-the-label-as-the-question-the-popup-answers}

The trigger is an icon button with no text of its own, so `label` carries its
accessible name and its tooltip. Write "Why this field is required", not
"info" or "more".

## Accessibility

- **The trigger is a real button.** It is reached with Tab and opens with
  Enter or Space, same as any `IconButton`.
- **`label` is required.** It is the trigger's only accessible name; a vague
  label like "info" tells a screen reader nothing about what the popup holds.
- **Focus and dismissal follow `Popup`.** Opening moves focus into the popup;
  Escape or a click outside closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

## Related

- `Popup`: use when configuring the anchored overlay surface this component is built on.
- `IconButton`: use when rendering the compact icon trigger button.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Trigger.** A subtle, compact icon button in the appearance color, named by `label`.
2. **Popup.** Opens on press — or on first render with `defaultOpen` — with a `title`, optional `secondaryText` and body `children`, positioned by `placement`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The icon in its appearance color; the popup closed. |
| Hovered | The subtle neutral fill behind the icon button. |
| Pressed | A stronger neutral fill. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the trigger for keyboard focus; see Border. |
| Disabled | Not supported. |
| Open | The Popup is shown with its own fill, shadow and radius. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Trigger icon | `--ds-icon-information`, `--ds-icon-warning`, `--ds-icon-danger`, `--ds-icon-success`, set on the icon in the jsx rather than the scss |
| Title | `--heading-sm` |
| Secondary text | `--body-default`, `--ds-text-subtle` |
| Spacing | `--stack-sm` |

The popup surface is Popup's; see `Popup`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Warning: say what happens if they proceed and offer an alternative. | Alarm without a next step. |
| Error: explain the problem and give a next step. | Use technical detail or blame the person. |
| Confirmation: confirm the outcome and get out of the way. | Add detail the person did not ask for. |
| Keep the title concise, in sentence case. | Let the message run past five lines. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |

# Link

Link: an inline navigation anchor.

**Import:** `import { Link } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Frame (`ds guide frame`); Modal (`ds guide modal`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.stories.jsx` — Appearances, OpenInNewWindow, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Link/Link.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Link` for navigation inside a sentence or a block of text — "see the
session report," "read more." `Link`'s appearances are for inline text, not
for a control that stands on its own.

## Motion

Link reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Color only, on the fast fade. |

## Alternatives

- For a standalone navigation action styled like a button, use `LinkButton`.
- For an action that triggers in-page behavior rather than navigating to a URL, use `Button`.
- For a trail of links showing where a page sits in a hierarchy, use `Breadcrumb`.

## Best practices

### Pick the appearance for the surface it sits on, not for emphasis. {#pick-the-appearance-for-the-surface-it-sits-on-not-for-emphasis}

`default` is for a link on the page's own background, `subtle` for one on a
muted surface where less contrast reads better, and `inverse` for a link on a
dark or colored fill. None of the three changes the link's meaning.

### Make the link text name the destination. {#make-the-link-text-name-the-destination}

Do: The words say where the link goes.
Don't: Link text that means nothing out of context.

### Let `isOpenInNewWindow` manage `target` and `rel` together. {#let-isopeninnewwindow-manage-target-and-rel-together}

Setting `isOpenInNewWindow` adds the external-link glyph, appends spoken text to the accessible name, and defaults `target="_blank"` with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. Pass `target` or `rel` directly only when the default pairing does not fit.

Do: The glyph and the spoken warning come with the prop.
Don't: Warning typed into the text: the glyph is missing and it reads twice.

### Keep the link inside the sentence it finishes. {#keep-the-link-inside-the-sentence-it-finishes}

A link is inline text. When the action stands alone, such as Save or Continue, it is a button, not a link.

Do: The link sits on the words that name the destination.
Don't: A standalone action dressed as a link; use a button.

## Accessibility

- **A real anchor.** `Link` renders an `<a>`, reachable with Tab and
  activated with Enter, with no extra role needed.
- **New-window links say so.** The glyph is decorative, but the accessible
  name gains "(opens in a new tab)" through visually hidden text, so a screen
  reader announces the behavior before it happens.
- **`children` is required.** A link always needs visible or accessible text
  — there is no icon-only mode.

## Related

- `LinkButton`: use when rendering a standalone navigation control with button sizing and padding.
- `Breadcrumb`: use when rendering a hierarchy trail of ancestor links above a page title.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Pagination` · `Sidebar` · `Tabs`

## Parts

1. **Text.** The link's name, in the appearance's ink.
2. **Underline.** Always on for `default` and `inverse`; `subtle` shows it on hover.
3. **New-window glyph.** Added by `isOpenInNewWindow`, with “(opens in a new tab)” appended to the accessible name.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Default in the link ink, underlined; visited in the visited ink. |
| Hovered | Subtle is underlined; default keeps its ink. |
| Pressed | The pressed link ink on default and subtle. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the link; the inverse ring on a dark fill. See Border. |
| Disabled | Not a state. A link with nowhere to go is plain text, not a dimmed link. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Default | `--ds-link`, `--ds-link-visited`, `--ds-link-pressed` |
| Subtle | `--ds-text`, `--ds-link-pressed` |
| Inverse | `--ds-text-inverse`, ring `--ds-border-focused-inverse` |
| Corners | `--radius-md` |
| New-window glyph | `--icon-sm`, `--inline-md` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Make the text say where it goes: “View the full report”. | Use “click here” or “read more”. |
| Put the link on the words that name the destination. | Stretch it over a whole sentence. |
| Write it in sentence case, without ending punctuation inside the link. | Add an arrow or “>” to the text; the glyph does that job. |
| Warn about a new window with `isOpenInNewWindow`. | Say “(opens in new tab)” in the text yourself. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `href` | string (required) | — | The destination URL of the anchor. Required. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | `default` for links in body text; `subtle` for links inside secondary or quiet text; `inverse` for links on dark or colored grounds. |
| `target` | string | — | Pass-through to the anchor; `isOpenInNewWindow` sets `_blank` when neither is given. |
| `rel` | string | — | The anchor `rel` attribute. Defaults to `noopener noreferrer` when the link opens in a new tab. |
| `isOpenInNewWindow` | bool | `false` | Draws the new-window glyph and appends it to the accessible name. Also defaults `target` to `_blank`. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the anchor beside the component's own. |
| `children` | node (required) | — | The link text. Required, since it names the link. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `subtle` · `inverse`

# LinkButton

Link button: navigates, and looks like a button. It renders an anchor, so it has no disabled or loading state.

**Import:** `import { LinkButton } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkButton/LinkButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkButton/LinkButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Spacing, WithIcons, Selected, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkButton/LinkButton.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `LinkButton` to open another page, site or section when the link needs the visual weight of a button.

## Motion

LinkButton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Hover and press change color, 90% by about 110 ms. |

## Alternatives

- For an action on the current page, use `Button`.
- For navigation shown as an icon alone, use `LinkIconButton`.
- For a link inside a sentence or paragraph, use `Link`.

## Best practices

### Keep space between link buttons. {#keep-space-between-link-buttons}

Leave a gap so neighboring link buttons read as separate targets.

Do: A clear gap between link buttons.
Don't: Link buttons touching.

### Use it to go somewhere, not to act. {#use-it-to-go-somewhere-not-to-act}

`LinkButton` renders an anchor so assistive technology announces a link. Actions that save, delete or submit belong on `Button`.

Do: Open session notes goes to the notes page.
Don't: Delete session acts on the page, so it belongs on a button.

### Let it hug its label. {#let-it-hug-its-label}

Keep the natural width. Reserve `shouldFitContainer` for narrow containers, such as a mobile sheet.

Do: Natural width.
Don't: Stretched across a wide row.

### Align with the button group. {#align-with-the-button-group}

Right-align in multi-step tasks and Modals; left-align on full-page forms and content-heavy screens.

## Accessibility

- Renders an `<a>` element so assistive technology announces a link and browser link shortcuts work.
- Has no disabled state. A disabled link leaves the tab order and does not say why; omit unavailable links or use validation and error messages, and never attach a tooltip to a disabled control.
- `target="_blank"` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; indicate the new tab in the label or with an external-link icon.
- The focus ring is 2px in `--ds-border-focused`. Never remove it.

## Related

- `Button`: use when the control performs an action on the current page.
- `LinkIconButton`: use when navigating with an icon and no visible label.
- `Link`: use when linking inline within text.
- `ButtonGroup`: use when grouping related link buttons.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Container.** An anchor (`<a>`) drawn as a button: 32 high at default spacing and 24 at compact.
2. **Icon before** (optional). A Font Awesome Free glyph at 16, before the label.
3. **Label.** Body/default at the medium weight. It names the destination.
4. **Icon after** (optional). A Font Awesome Free glyph at 16, after the label, such as `arrow-up-right-from-square` for an external link.

### Appearance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most links that need button weight. Example: View sessions. |
| Primary | The main way forward to another page. Example: Start onboarding. |
| Subtle | Navigation inside toolbars and headers. Example: Back to lessons. |
| Warning, danger | Rare for a link; a destination that leads to a risky area. Prefer default. |
| Discovery | The call to action for a new experience. Example: Try the new schedule view. |

### Spacing

Default spacing suits most places. Use compact in table rows and inline toolbars.

### States

Hover, pressed and focus are the browser's own. A link button has no `ai`, disabled or loading state.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | The container takes the appearance's hovered fill. |
| Pressed | The container takes the appearance's pressed fill. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | The selected role fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, label and icon, with `aria-current`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill, label, icon | The same named tokens as Button for each appearance, with hovered and pressed steps. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |
| Height | 32: `--control-md`. 24: `--control-sm`. |
| Radius | 6: `--button-radius-default`. Compact 4: `--button-radius-compact`. |
| Padding | 12: `--pad-x-md`. Compact 8: `--pad-x-sm`. |
| Icon-to-label gap | 4: `--inline-sm`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Describe the destination: "View sessions". | "Click here" or "Go". |
| Use sentence case, short and without punctuation. | Title case, or a full sentence. |
| Match the words of the surrounding UI. | Different words for the same destination in one view. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `href` | string (required) | — | Where the link goes. |
| `target` | string | — | The anchor `target` attribute, such as `_blank` to open a new tab. |
| `rel` | string | — | The anchor `rel` attribute. Defaults to `noopener noreferrer` when `target` is `_blank`. |
| `text` | string | — | The label as a string. Wins over `children`. |
| `children` | node | — | The label, used when `text` is not given. |
| `appearance` | oneOf | — | The button's look, the same as Button. Use `primary` for the one main navigation on a view, `default` or `subtle` for the rest, and `link` for a text link that leaves. |
| `spacing` | enum | — | `default` draws 32. `compact` draws 24. |
| `iconBefore` | string or node | — | An icon before the label: a Font Awesome Free glyph name (`calendar`) or a node. |
| `iconAfter` | string or node | — | An icon after the label: a Font Awesome Free glyph name (`arrow-right`) or a node. |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | Marks the link as the current page: sets `aria-current` and draws the selected look on `default` and `subtle`. |
| `shouldFitContainer` | bool | — | Stretches the link to the full width of its container. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event when the link is activated. The link still navigates to `href` unless the handler prevents it. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the anchor beside the component's own. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `primary` · `subtle` · `warning` · `danger` · `discovery` · `ai` · `link` · `danger-link`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

# LinkIconButton

Link icon button: an icon that navigates. It renders an anchor with an accessible `label`, and has no disabled or loading state.

**Import:** `import { LinkIconButton } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkIconButton/LinkIconButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkIconButton/LinkIconButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Spacing, Selected, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/LinkIconButton/LinkIconButton.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `LinkIconButton` when an icon alone opens another page or site and space is limited, such as a Help Center link in a toolbar.

## Motion

LinkIconButton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Hover and press change color, 90% by about 110 ms. |

## Alternatives

- For an icon that performs an action on the current page, use `IconButton`.
- For a button-styled link with a visible text label, use `LinkButton`.
- For an inline text link, use `Link`.

## Best practices

### Keep space between link icon buttons. {#keep-space-between-link-icon-buttons}

Leave a gap so neighboring link icon buttons read as separate targets.

Do: A clear gap between link icon buttons.
Don't: Link icon buttons touching.

### Say where the link goes. {#say-where-the-link-goes}

The `label` is the accessible name and the tooltip. Name the destination ("Open Help Center"), not "Link" or a bare "Help".

```jsx
// Incorrect: says nothing about the destination.
<LinkIconButton href="/help" icon="circle-question" label="Link" />

// Correct.
<LinkIconButton href="/help" icon="circle-question" label="Open Help Center" />
```

### Keep it square. {#keep-it-square}

Link icon buttons stay square at `--control-md` (`default`) or `--control-sm` (`compact`), and round only in top navigation (`shape="circle"`). Never stretch one to fill a row.

### Use a link for navigation and a button for an action. {#use-a-link-for-navigation-and-a-button-for-an-action}

If the icon acts on the current page, use `IconButton`. Navigation uses `LinkIconButton` so assistive technology announces a link and browser link shortcuts work.

### Pick a glyph people recognize at a glance. {#pick-a-glyph-people-recognize-at-a-glance}

Do: A question mark reads as help.
Don't: A star does not read as the Help Center.

### Give each destination its own glyph. {#give-each-destination-its-own-glyph}

Do not reuse one glyph for several links in the same area.

Do: Help Center and settings each have their own glyph.
Don't: One link glyph for two destinations.

## Accessibility

- `label` is required and names the destination. A missing label fails `check:icon-button-name`.
- Has no disabled state. A disabled link leaves the tab order and does not say why; omit unavailable links or use validation and error messages.
- `target="_blank"` adds `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; say so in the label if it opens a new tab.
- The focus ring is 2px in `--ds-border-focused`. Never remove it.

## Related

- `IconButton`: use when the icon performs an action on the current page.
- `LinkButton`: use when navigating with a visible text label.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Container.** An anchor (`<a>`) drawn as a square button: 32 at default spacing and 24 at compact. `shape="circle"` rounds it.
2. **Icon.** A Font Awesome Free glyph at 16.
3. **Label.** Not drawn. It is the accessible name and the tooltip, and says where the link goes.

### Appearance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most link icon buttons: a destination with a clear, familiar glyph. Example: Open Help Center. |
| Subtle | Links in toolbars, table rows and headers where it is already clear they are interactive. |
| Primary | The main way forward from a small area when space allows no label. Use sparingly. |
| Discovery | The way into a new experience. |

### Spacing

Default spacing suits most places. Use compact in table rows and inline toolbars.

### States

Hover, pressed and focus are the browser's own. A link icon button has no disabled or loading state.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | The container takes the appearance's hovered fill. |
| Pressed | The container takes the appearance's pressed fill. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the edge, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | The selected role fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge and icon, with `aria-current`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill: default, subtle | `--ds-background-neutral` (default) and `--ds-background-neutral-subtle` (subtle), each with hovered and pressed steps. Neither draws an edge. |
| Fill: primary, discovery | `--ds-background-brand-bold`, `--ds-background-discovery-bold`, each with hovered and pressed steps. |
| Fill: selected | `--ds-background-selected` with hovered and pressed steps and a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge. |
| Icon | `--ds-icon` (default), `--ds-icon-subtle` (subtle), `--ds-icon-inverse` (primary, discovery); the selected role. 16, `--icon-md`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |
| Size | 32: `--control-md`. 24: `--control-sm`. Square. |
| Radius | 6: `--button-radius-default`. Compact 4: `--button-radius-compact`. Circle 50%. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say where the link goes: "Open Help Center". | A bare "Help", or "Link". |
| Use sentence case. | Title case. |

## Props

| `href` | string (required) | — | — |
| `target` | string | — | — |
| `rel` | string | — | — |
| `icon` | string or node | — | — |
| `label` | string (required) | — | The accessible name and tooltip. Say where the link goes ("Open Help Center"). |
| `appearance` | oneOf | — | — |
| `spacing` | enum | — | — |
| `shape` | oneOf | — | — |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | — |
| `onClick` | func | — | — |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `subtle` · `primary` · `discovery`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`shape`** — `default` · `circle`

### Keep space between link icon buttons.

Leave a gap so neighboring link icon buttons read as separate targets.

Do: A clear gap between link icon buttons.
Don't: Link icon buttons touching.

### Say where the link goes.

The `label` is the accessible name and the tooltip. Name the destination ("Open Help Center"), not "Link" or a bare "Help".

```jsx
// Incorrect: says nothing about the destination.
<LinkIconButton href="/help" icon="circle-question" label="Link" />

// Correct.
<LinkIconButton href="/help" icon="circle-question" label="Open Help Center" />
```

### Keep it square.

Link icon buttons stay square at `--control-md` (`default`) or `--control-sm` (`compact`), and round only in top navigation (`shape="circle"`). Never stretch one to fill a row.

### Use a link for navigation and a button for an action.

If the icon acts on the current page, use `IconButton`. Navigation uses `LinkIconButton` so assistive technology announces a link and browser link shortcuts work.

### Pick a glyph people recognize at a glance.

Do: A question mark reads as help.
Don't: A star does not read as the Help Center.

### Give each destination its own glyph.

Do not reuse one glyph for several links in the same area.

Do: Help Center and settings each have their own glyph.
Don't: One link glyph for two destinations.

# Logo

The PLUS logo: the mark, or the lockup of mark and wordmark. Seven sizes, six appearances. At 24 and below the mark uses its small-size drawing, and below 24 the lockup gives way to the mark alone.

**Import:** `import { Logo } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/assets/Logo/Logo.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/assets/Logo/Logo.stories.jsx` — Playground, Sizes, SizesDark, SmallSizeDrawing, Lockup, LockupDark, Appearances, LightAndDark, Construction, ClearSpace

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/assets/Logo/Logo.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Logo` to mark PLUS in the sidebar header, sign-in, email headers and the loading screen. Brand rules, color options, clear space and construction live on Logos.

## Alternatives

- For partner or tool logos or school crests or lesson thumbnails, use `Tile`.
- For a person or team or agent, use `Avatar`.
- For an action or object glyph, use `Icon`.

## Best practices

### Pick a `LOGO_SIZES` step rather than scaling by hand. {#pick-a-logosizes-step-rather-than-scaling-by-hand}

`size` takes a step from `LOGO_SIZES`; never stretch or resize the SVG with custom CSS.

### Use `wordmark` from `LOCKUP_MIN_SIZE` up. {#use-wordmark-from-lockupminsize-up}

Below `LOCKUP_MIN_SIZE` (`24`), `Logo` renders the mark alone even when `wordmark` is set.

## Accessibility

- **Labeled SVG.** `Logo` renders an SVG with `role="img"` and `aria-label="PLUS"`.
- **Alt-text and link rules.** When the logo sits beside a visible PLUS title or inside a home link, follow the alt-text table on Logos.

## Related

- Logos: use when checking brand rules, color options, clear space or construction geometry.
- `Sidebar`: use when rendering the application navigation rail that holds `Logo` in its header row.
- `Tile`: use when framing a third-party tool or school logo.

## Parts

1. **Logomark.** The PLUS plus-sign tile at height `size` (`16` to `96`). At `SMALL_MAX_SIZE` (`24`) and below, it uses the small-size drawing.
2. **Wordmark** (optional). Shown beside the logomark when `wordmark` is true and `size` is at least `LOCKUP_MIN_SIZE` (`24`).

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. The logo is brand artwork, not a control. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused | None on `Logo` itself; when the logo links home, the wrapping link or button carries focus and interaction states. |

### Tokens

The logomark's glows and fills use fixed `--ds-logo-*` brand tokens (`Logo.scss`); in the colored appearance the wordmark follows `--ds-text`, so it tracks the color mode.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `appearance` | enum | `'colored'` | One of six appearances |
| `size` | enum | `32` | Height of the mark in pixels |
| `wordmark` | bool | `false` | Show the lockup. From size 24; below that the mark stands alone |
| `className` | string | `''` | Additional CSS classes |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `colored` · `colored-dark` · `filled` · `dark` · `outlined` · `outlined-reversed`

**`size`** — `16` · `20` · `24` · `32` · `48` · `64` · `96`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Modal

`@base-ui/react` Dialog (portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock, and the blanket-press rule). One Modal is open at a time (`useOverlaySlot`). `inline` renders the Blanket + Dialog in flow for docs previews and static stages without a portal, focus trap, Escape handling or scroll lock.

Also asked as: confirm, confirmation dialog, destructive confirm, popup window.

**Import:** `import { Modal } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Modal (`ds guide modal`); Panel (`ds guide panel`); Popup (`ds guide popup`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Modal/Modal.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Modal/Modal.stories.jsx` — Overview, Widths, Heights, Tabs, BodyMinHeight, CustomHeader, Divider, Loading, WidthsAtEveryScreen, Width4Col, Width6Col, Width8Col, Width10Col, HugLong, HeightFill, TabsStill, Interactive, LiveBehavior, StaticBlanketRefusesToClose, BlockingShadow, SelectKeepsOverlayShadow, TypePassive, TypeActive, TypeAcknowledge, TypeSteps, AnatomyActive, WidthStrip, ResponsiveWidth, TierActive, TierDanger, TierTypeName, FooterOne, FooterTwo, FooterThree, FooterLeadingAction, FooterDestructive, FooterNarrow, KeyLongContent, KeyLoading, KeyWithForm, KeyConfirmInside, StackConfirmOverPanel, StackModalOnModalRefused, BlanketInline, BlanketPads, BlanketScreenGrid, BlanketInteractive, BlanketLayers, BlanketConfirmOverPanel, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced, BlanketMotionOpenClose, BlanketMotionReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Modal/Modal.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.default` · exit `spatial.exit` + `appearance.fast` · swap `appearance.fast` · rejected `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use a Modal when the next step has to happen before anything else can: a confirm, a rare critical task with fewer than five fields, something to read before going on. It is always centered over a Blanket. A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal.

| Type | Use when | Footer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive | Something to read, with nothing to decide | None; Close only |
| Active | A choice, a confirm or a short form | Secondary (such as Discard or Keep) and the action; no Cancel |
| Acknowledge | One thing to read and accept | One button |
| Steps | A short ordered sequence | Back and Next |

## Motion

Modal reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | Scales from 96% and fades in; the Blanket dims on appearance.default. It opens only from something the person did, and focus moves to its first input as the motion starts. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-exit` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Leaves at 98%, fading; stays mounted until the exit completes. |
| swap | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | One Modal at a time: a confirm replaces the content in place, never a second Modal. |
| rejected | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A blocked submit shakes it once; never in reduced motion. |

## Alternatives

- For the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, use `Dialog` (`@/components`).
- For content read beside the page, use `Panel`.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For a long or stepped task, use `Frame`.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Open a Modal only from a person's action. {#open-a-modal-only-from-a-person-s-action}

**Checked:** Review

A button, a link, an icon. Never on its own.

Do: Open a Modal when a person clicks an action or trigger.

Don't: Open a Modal automatically on page load.

### Size a confirm at the smallest step and step up with a detail line or a field. {#size-a-confirm-at-the-smallest-step-and-step-up-with-a-detail-line-or-a-field}

**Checked:** Review

A confirm takes 4-col or 6-col; a short form is 8-col; a table, editor or steps is 10-col. Choose width by task.

Do: A confirm at the narrow step: the title, one line and two buttons.
Don't: The same confirm at a wide step: empty width around one line, picked to make it look a certain way.

### Confirm inside the Modal, and never open a Modal on another Modal. {#confirm-inside-the-modal-and-never-open-a-modal-on-another-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Stacking holds the rule. The overlay module keeps a second Modal closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: One Modal that confirms inside itself, with a message and its own buttons.
Don't: A Modal opened on another Modal, a second Blanket dimming the first.

### Scroll the body between a fixed header and footer. {#scroll-the-body-between-a-fixed-header-and-footer}

**Checked:** Automatic

Each width has a maximum height, the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below. Header and footer are pinned and the footer never moves. Actions never sit in the body, which scrolls away; a missing-field error shows on the field and the body scrolls to it, and a rejected submit shows its message at the top of the body.

Do: Past the cap the body scrolls; the footer stays pinned with its buttons.
Don't: The button inside the scrolling body: it scrolls out of reach.

### Use tabs for views, not steps. {#use-tabs-for-views-not-steps}

**Checked:** Review

Two to five views of one thing opened in any order; one footer saves them all. Views in order are Steps, with Back and Next in the footer.

Do: Views in order are Steps: Back and Next split across the footer.
Don't: Numbered tabs as steps: any order, one Save, nothing to go back to.

Footer buttons, real actions and Close, and which destructive tier, including type the name: Common actions. A blocked submit: Forms. The sending button: Loading.

## Accessibility

- The Modal is a dialog named by its title, which is its h1; a Section inside opens at h2. A Modal with a custom header needs its own name.
- Focus moves into the Dialog on open (to the first input or control) and stays trapped until it closes, while the page behind stops scrolling. Escape, Close and the Blanket close it, and focus returns to what opened it.
- Set `blanket="static"` (or `false`) for an inline confirmation of a destructive action so a stray click outside does not abandon it.
- A body that scrolls is a tab stop. With tabs, Left and Right move between tabs and the panel is named by its tab.
- A blocked submit announces the first error; with reduced motion the color, icon, message and focus move carry it without the shake.
- Close is named "Close". The Danger button in a type-the-name confirm stays disabled until the name matches, and the caption carries the reason.

## Related

- Dialog: use when drawing the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, such as in docs and mockups.
- Forms: use when the Modal holds fields.
- Panel: use when the page must stay usable.
- Popup: use when the content is a menu or a short list.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules across Modals: Common actions, Forms, Errors, Loading.

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Types

Picked by what the person has to do. The Dialog component page holds the panel's props and states; these are the filled Modal layouts.

- **Passive.** Information only, with Close. No footer.
- **Active.** A choice, a confirm or a short form. Discard (or a real alternative) and the action; no Cancel.
- **Acknowledge.** One thing to read and one button that fills the footer.
- **Steps.** A short sequence at 10-col: Back and Next, split 50/50.

## Anatomy

An Active Modal at 8-col with a short form. Every part once; the pad is 20 on every side, the radius 16, and the parts sit 16 apart.

1. **Blanket.** Dims the page and holds the Modal centered.
2. **Header.** The title at 20/24, whatever the level around it, and the Close icon button. With tabs, the tab group sits 8 under the title.
3. **Body.** Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap and never draws under 96 tall.
4. **Footer** (optional). Full-bleed buttons; secondary (Default) left, Primary right. A declining action such as "Not now" is the secondary. Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel.

## Slots

```jsx
import { Modal } from '@/templates';
import { Button } from '@/components';
```

`Modal` places `Dialog` (`@/components`) on the Blanket with Base UI portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return.

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `onClose` | The h1 and the Close icon button. |
| `width` | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`. |
| `body` | Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap. |
| `footer` or `primaryButton` · `secondaryButton` | The footer's buttons. Leave them out for Passive. |
| `blanket` · `keyboard` | Whether a Blanket press or Escape closes the Modal (`true` by default; `blanket="static"` keeps it open). |
| Full-bleed footer | Planned. Cells that fill the footer edge to edge and never change the Modal's height, with the inner corners squared. Today the page composes it from Button. |
| `tabs` | Two to five views of one thing under the title. |
| `confirmView` | Planned. The swapped title, body and footer for a confirm about the Modal itself. Today the caller swaps them in place. |
| Blocked-submit shake | Planned. The Modal's single shake when a submit is blocked. |

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--modal-pad` | 20 | Pad on every side. |
| `--modal-radius` | 16 | Corner radius at every width. |
| `--modal-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 8, 16, 24 | Title to tabs; header, body and footer; groups of fields. |
| `--modal-body-min-height` | 80 | The least the body draws. |
| `--ds-surface-material-overlay`, `--ds-border-material`, `--ds-shadow-blocking` | pair | The Modal's fill, edge and elevation, the one surface that lifts above a Blanket. The fill is translucent with no blur, and turns solid under reduced transparency and increased contrast. |
| `--ds-blanket` | color | The Blanket's fill. |

The Modal's maximum height is the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Delete this session?" | "Are you sure?" or "Warning". |
| Give the consequence in one line: "This cannot be undone." | A paragraph that repeats the title. |
| Name the action after the question: "Delete session". | "OK" or "Yes". |
| On the last step, name Next after the outcome: "Schedule". | "Finish". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the dialog panel. |
| `title` | node | — | The dialog's h1, and its accessible name. |
| `description` | node | — | A line under the title, read as the dialog's description. |
| `ariaLabel` | string | — | The dialog's accessible name when it has no visible `title` or uses a custom `header`. |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header slot replacing the title row (title and close button), so the caller owns both and names the dialog with `ariaLabel`. |
| `headerActions` | node | — | Icon buttons in the header, before the close button. |
| `showCloseButton` | bool | `true` | The header's close button. Off for a dialog that has to be answered. |
| `tabs` | arrayOf | — | Tab group under the title (`{ key, label, content, disabled? }`). The body becomes the tab panel and shows the selected tab's `content`. |
| `activeTab` | string or number | — | Selected tab's key when controlled; update from `onTabChange`. |
| `defaultActiveTab` | string or number | — | Initial tab key when uncontrolled; defaults to the first enabled tab. |
| `onTabChange` | func | — | Called with the key of the selected tab. |
| `body` | string or node | — | The main content of the dialog. A string is drawn as body text; a node is drawn as given. `children` is rendered after it. |
| `height` | enum | `'hug'` | `hug` grows with the content to the cap and then scrolls its body; `fill` sits at that cap. |
| `showBottomButtons` | bool | `true` | Show the footer: `footer`, or the secondary and primary buttons. |
| `footer` | node | — | Custom footer content in place of the built-in pair, such as a three-button or leading-text FooterActions layout. |
| `primaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The confirming footer button, drawn on the right. Takes `text` (default "Confirm"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `primary`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `secondaryButton` | buttonShape | — | The secondary footer button, drawn in the left half when a primary button is also given. Takes `text` (default "Discard"), `onClick`, `appearance` (default `default`), `spacing` and `icon`. |
| `dividers` | bool | `false` | A rule under the header and over the footer. |
| `loading` | bool | `false` | Skeleton bars in place of the body while its content loads. |
| `show` | bool | `false` | Whether the modal is open. Controlled by the parent: set it to false in `onClose` to close. |

rankedText.usage:
Use a Modal when the next step has to happen before anything else can: a confirm, a rare critical task with fewer than five fields, something to read before going on. It is always centered over a Blanket. A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal.

| Type | Use when | Footer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive | Something to read, with nothing to decide | None; Close only |
| Active | A choice, a confirm or a short form | Secondary (such as Discard or Keep) and the action; no Cancel |
| Acknowledge | One thing to read and accept | One button |
| Steps | A short ordered sequence | Back and Next |
rankedText.best:
### Open a Modal only from a person's action.

A button, a link, an icon. Never on its own.

Do: Open a Modal when a person clicks an action or trigger.

Don't: Open a Modal automatically on page load.

### Size a confirm at the smallest step and step up with a detail line or a field.

A confirm takes 4-col or 6-col; a short form is 8-col; a table, editor or steps is 10-col. Choose width by task.

Do: A confirm at the narrow step: the title, one line and two buttons.
Don't: The same confirm at a wide step: empty width around one line, picked to make it look a certain way.

### Confirm inside the Modal, and never open a Modal on another Modal.

Stacking holds the rule. The overlay module keeps a second Modal closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: One Modal that confirms inside itself, with a message and its own buttons.
Don't: A Modal opened on another Modal, a second Blanket dimming the first.

### Scroll the body between a fixed header and footer.

Each width has a maximum height, the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below. Header and footer are pinned and the footer never moves. Actions never sit in the body, which scrolls away; a missing-field error shows on the field and the body scrolls to it, and a rejected submit shows its message at the top of the body.

Do: Past the cap the body scrolls; the footer stays pinned with its buttons.
Don't: The button inside the scrolling body: it scrolls out of reach.

### Use tabs for views, not steps.

Two to five views of one thing opened in any order; one footer saves them all. Views in order are Steps, with Back and Next in the footer.

Do: Views in order are Steps: Back and Next split across the footer.
Don't: Numbered tabs as steps: any order, one Save, nothing to go back to.

Footer buttons, real actions and Close, and which destructive tier, including type the name: Common actions. A blocked submit: Forms. The sending button: Loading.
rankedText.related:

- Forms: use when the Modal holds fields.
- Panel: use when the page must stay usable.
- Popup: use when the content is a menu or a short list.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules across Modals: Common actions, Forms, Errors, Loading.

# NotificationItem

`NotificationItem` — one row for an update that arrived over time, shared by the Inbox, a Home card and a full notifications page. The whole row is a single link (`href`). When `unread` is true, the row shows the selected fill and an unread dot paired with the visually hidden word "Unread" so assistive technology announces it. When `onMarkRead` is also passed, a compact "Mark as read" `IconButton` sits as a sibling of the link over the trailing slot and appears on hover and keyboard focus. Anatomy (`__start`, `__body` [`__label`, `__description`], `__end`) matches `FileItem` and `SettingRow` so all three can lift onto a shared row base.

**Import:** `import { NotificationItem } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/NotificationItem/NotificationItem.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/NotificationItem/NotificationItem.stories.jsx` — Overview, Actors, Unread, Read, Hovered, Focused, Pressed, Motion, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/NotificationItem/NotificationItem.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `NotificationItem` for updates that arrived over time: in the Inbox Notifications panel, in a recent-updates card on Home, or on a full notifications page. Every row says who, what, where and when in two compact lines and opens its destination as one link.

## Motion

NotificationItem reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Row fill and Mark as read fade on hover, press and read state changes. |

## Alternatives

- For a passing confirmation of an action that just finished, use `Flag`.
- For something to read or act on inside part of a page, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a condition that holds across a whole surface, use `Banner`.

## Best practices

### Keep the whole row a single link. {#keep-the-whole-row-a-single-link}

Put the destination on `href` and never nest links inside `title` or `meta`. A single link gives one clear target for pointers and one stop per row for keyboard users.

Do: One link opens the session; Mark as read sits beside it as a sibling button.
Don't: Missing actor name and context forces opening the notification to tell who and where.

### Pair Avatar for people and Tile for the system. {#pair-avatar-for-people-and-tile-for-the-system}

Circles represent people; rounded squares represent tools, reminders and system events.

Do: System reminder uses a 32px Tile so people and automated events scan apart.
Don't: Person Avatar initials on an automated system reminder.

## Accessibility

- **One link per row.** `NotificationItem` renders a single `<a>` element for the row and keeps the `"Mark as read"` `IconButton` as a sibling outside the link so interactive controls never nest.
- **Unread state announced in words.** The unread dot is `aria-hidden="true"` and paired with visually hidden `"Unread"` inside the link, so assistive technology announces unread status without relying on color or shape.
- **No duplicate actor announcement.** `actor` sits in an `aria-hidden="true"` start slot because `title` names who acted.
- **Keyboard-reachable Mark as read.** Focusing the row link triggers `:focus-within`, revealing `"Mark as read"` as the next Tab stop.

## Related

- Notifications: use when choosing between a Flag, Banner, SectionMessage, Modal or the Inbox.
- `Avatar`: use when a person triggered the notification (`actor`).
- `Tile`: use when the system triggered the notification (`actor`).
- `EmptyState`: use when all unread items in the Inbox have been cleared.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `SectionMessage` · `Spotlight`

## Parts

1. **Actor (`actor` at `start`).** A `32px` (`--image-md`) `Avatar` for a person or `Tile` for the system. Hidden from the link's accessible name because `title` already says who acted.
2. **Title (`title` at `label`).** Who and what on `--body-default` in `--ds-text`, promoted to `--type-weight-medium` while `unread` is true.
3. **Meta (`meta` at `description`).** Context and relative time separated by a middle dot (`"Sessions · 2m"`) on `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`.
4. **Unread indicator and action (`end`).** An `8px` (`--count-tag-dot-size`) dot in `--ds-background-brand-bold` paired with visually hidden `"Unread"`, replaced on hover and keyboard focus by a compact `"Mark as read"` `IconButton` when `onMarkRead` is provided.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Unread | `--ds-background-selected` fill, `--type-weight-medium` title, `--ds-background-brand-bold` dot, and `Unread` announced in the link name. |
| Read | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle` fill, regular title weight, no dot and no `Mark as read` button. |
| Hovered | `--ds-background-selected-hovered` (unread) or `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` (read); on actionable unread rows the dot hides and `Mark as read` appears. |
| Focused | 2px `--ds-border-focused` ring on the row link, with `Mark as read` visible and reachable on the next Tab press. |
| Pressed | `--ds-background-selected-pressed` (unread) or `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` (read). |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Row padding, gap and radius | `--pad-y-lg` × `--pad-x-md`, gap `--inline-lg`, radius `--radius-control-md`. |
| Row state fills | `--ds-background-selected` / `-hovered` / `-pressed` when unread; `--ds-background-neutral-subtle` / `-hovered` / `-pressed` when read. |
| Actor and trailing slots | `--image-md` (`32px`) start slot; `--control-sm` (`24px`) end slot with `--count-tag-dot-size` (`8px`) dot in `--ds-background-brand-bold`. |
| Title and meta | `--body-default` (`--type-weight-medium` when unread) in `--ds-text`; `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`; stack gap `--stack-sm`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say who and what in `title`: "Ana Ruiz moved Thursday's session". | "New update" or "Session notification". |
| Pair where and when in `meta`: "Sessions · 2m", "Notes · Yesterday". | Full timestamps down to the second on every row. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `actor` | node | — | Leading actor visual: an `Avatar` for a person or a `Tile` for the system. Hidden from the link's accessible name because `title` names who acted. |
| `title` | node (required) | — | Who did what, such as `"Ana Ruiz moved Thursday's session"`. |
| `meta` | node | — | Context and relative time on one line, such as `"Sessions · 2m"`. |
| `unread` | bool | `false` | Marks the row unread with the selected fill, an unread dot and an announced `"Unread"` state. |
| `href` | string | `'#'` | Destination URL for the notification row. |
| `onMarkRead` | func | — | Called when the user activates the `"Mark as read"` button on an unread item. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Click handler forwarded to the row link. |
| `onPointerEnter` | func | — | Pointer-enter handler on the row container. |
| `onPointerLeave` | func | — | Pointer-leave handler on the row container. |
| `id` | string | — | Optional `id` on the row container. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names on the row container. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the row container. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid` on the row container. |

# Object

Object: a fixed Font Awesome glyph that marks the kind of thing a row or reference names, one component per kind (`TaskIcon`, `BugIcon`, …) built by `createObjectIcon`.

> Implemented as `createObjectIcon` in the source and exported as `Object`. Import the exported name; read the source under the implementation name.

**Import:** `import { Object } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Panel (`ds guide panel`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Object/Object.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Object/Object.stories.jsx` — Kinds, Sizes, Decorative, Rest, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Object/Object.mdx`

## Usage

Use an `Object` icon (`TaskIcon`, `BugIcon`, `IdeaIcon`, `PullRequestIcon`,
`ProjectIcon` or `PageIcon`) beside the name of the record it represents — a
task in a list, a bug in a reference, a page in a breadcrumb. Each kind is its
own fixed Font Awesome Free glyph (`size` is `12` or `16`, and `label` defaults
to the kind's name unless `label=""` marks it decorative) — there is no `icon`
prop to swap it for another kind.

## Alternatives

- For a larger square picture of a school or tool or lesson, use `Tile`.
- For a general-purpose Font Awesome Free glyph, use `Icon`.
- For a bitmap photo or screenshot, use `Image`.
- For a person or an agent, use `Avatar`.

## Best practices

### Pick the component for the kind. {#pick-the-component-for-the-kind}

`TaskIcon`, `BugIcon`, `IdeaIcon`, `PullRequestIcon`, `ProjectIcon` and
`PageIcon` each draw a fixed glyph. Reach for the component that names the
record rather than passing a custom glyph name.

Do: The Task glyph beside the task name.
Don't: The Bug glyph on a task.

### Override `label` only when the default name does not fit. {#override-label-only-when-the-default-name-does-not-fit}

Each kind defaults its accessible name to its kind ("Task", "Bug"). Set
`label=""` when the kind is already stated in visible text beside it, so
assistive technology does not hear it twice.

Do: An empty label when the kind is written beside it.
Don't: Both the default name and the visible kind, so it reads twice.

### Keep the glyph at its kind and put status in `StatusTag`. {#keep-the-glyph-at-its-kind-and-put-status-in-statustag}

Each kind has one glyph and color. Do not swap the glyph to indicate workflow state; pair it with `StatusTag`.

Do: The kind stays a Task; the status goes in a Status tag.
Don't: A second glyph to hint at a status.

## Accessibility

- **Named by default.** Each icon's default `label` makes it `role="img"`
  with that name, read by assistive technology.
- **Decorative with an empty label.** `label=""` sets `aria-hidden="true"`
  and drops the accessible name, for use beside visible text that already
  names the kind.

## Related

- `StatusTag`: use when pairing a record's kind with its workflow state.
- `Breadcrumb`: use when showing a page or project icon in a hierarchy trail.

Same group: `Avatar` · `AvatarGroup` · `Icon` · `Illustration` · `Image` · `Tile`

## Parts

1. **Glyph.** A fixed Font Awesome Free glyph for the kind: task, bug, idea, pull request, project or page.
2. **Size.** `12` or `16`, in `--ds-icon-subtle`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. An object icon is a picture, not a control. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused, disabled | None. It sits beside the name of the thing, which carries any interaction. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Size | `--icon-sm` for 12; `--icon-md` for 16. |
| Color | `--ds-icon-subtle`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the visible name beside the glyph: "Fix the broken sync". | A glyph alone where the kind is not obvious. |
| Set `label=""` when the kind is already written beside it. | Leave both the label and the visible kind, so it reads twice. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `size` | enum | — | `12` or `16` (the default), in pixels. |
| `label` | string | — | The accessible name. An empty string marks the glyph decorative. |
| `testId` | string | — | — |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`size`** — `12` · `16`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

# Page

The Page surface: paints `--ds-surface` edge to edge with `--page-pad` (24) on every side and no radius, border, or shadow; children fill the content slot. A Page can carry its `title`: the page's one h1, at Heading/large 24, above the content. Sections inside it open at h2.

Also asked as: surface.

**Import:** `import { Page } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Modal (`ds guide modal`); Page (`ds guide page`); Panel (`ds guide panel`); Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); +1 more

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Page/Page.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Page/Page.stories.jsx` — Overview, WithTitle, HeaderAndBanner, OptionalSlots, ColorModes, MediumPad, Interactive, TypeDefault, TypeFullWidth, TypeReading, AnatomyRecord, ScenarioArea, ScenarioSeveralSections, ScenarioRecordTabs, ScenarioTwoLevels, KeyBanner, ResponsiveWidth, MotionSwitchViews, MotionSwitchViewsReduced, MotionScrollToSpot, MotionScrollToSpotReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Page/Page.mdx`

**Motion:** title `linear` · anchor `linear` · tabs-shadow `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use Page for the content of every default Frame. It carries the page header, the one h1, and the Sections under it. The default type caps the grid at 1232; full width is for a page that fills the window, such as chat, a board or a wide table; reading caps it at 864 for text people read through.

## Motion

Page reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The header is scroll-linked: the small title fades in at the end of the Breadcrumb row, its opacity mapped to the next 24 px of scroll. No spring, no timer, no snap when scrolling stops. |
| anchor | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The actions and the tabs ride up with the page and anchor: the actions at the end of the Breadcrumb row, the tabs under it. One copy of every control. |
| tabs-shadow | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The tabs' shadow appears when they stick, a single moment. In Reduced mode nothing changes: every movement is the person's own scroll. |

## Alternatives

- For one task that takes the whole window, use `Frame`.
- For a region of the page with its own heading, use `Section`.
- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.

## Best practices

### Make the page header the page's one h1. {#make-the-page-header-the-page-s-one-h1}

**Checked:** Automatic

A Section never stands in for it. Sections inside open at h2.

Do: The page header is the one h1; the Section under it opens at h2.
Don't: Sections standing in for the page title: two page-title-sized headings and no page header.

### Show the breadcrumb by the Navigation pattern. {#show-the-breadcrumb-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

When it shows and what it holds: the Navigation pattern.

Do: An area page: the title alone.
Don't: A breadcrumb on a top-level area page, repeating the Sidebar's place.

### Place page actions and the add action by the Navigation pattern. {#place-page-actions-and-the-add-action-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

Page actions sit at the end of the title row and are about the page only. Where an add action goes: the Navigation pattern.

Do: "Add" is the Section's one action, in its title row; the page header carries only page actions.
Don't: The same Primary twice: in the page header and in the Section's title row.

### Keep the description to one line. {#keep-the-description-to-one-line}

**Checked:** Review

Anything longer moves into the first Section.

Do: One detail line under the title.
Don't: A paragraph under the title pushes the first Section down.

### Keep one tab system per page. {#keep-one-tab-system-per-page}

**Checked:** Review

The rule and its reasons: the Navigation pattern. Page tabs name views of one subject; the Section's views become one labeled PopupSelect.

Do: Under page tabs the Section's views are one labeled PopupSelect in its views row.
Don't: Pill views under page tabs: two tab systems on one page.

### Shrink the scrolled header to one sticky row. {#shrink-the-scrolled-header-to-one-sticky-row}

- The Page is the `main` landmark. Its header's title is the one h1; Sections open at h2.

- Page tabs are a tablist; the selected tab names its panel. Views swap in place and are announced.
