<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# PageHeader

PageHeader: a page's title row, with an optional breadcrumb trail above it, actions to its side, and a bottom bar below.

Also asked as: heading with buttons, header actions, page heading.

**Import:** `import { PageHeader } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Page (`ds guide page`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/PageHeader/PageHeader.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/PageHeader/PageHeader.stories.jsx` — Basic, SecondaryLevel, WithBreadcrumbsActionsAndBottomBar, DisableTitleStyles, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/PageHeader/PageHeader.mdx`

**Motion:** change `linear`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `PageHeader` once per page layout, at the top of the Page template's body,
to carry the page's title and primary action or page-level actions. Pass a
`Breadcrumb` in `breadcrumbs` above the title, page-level controls in `actions`
at the end of the title row, and `Tabs` or a filter bar in `bottomBar` below it.
`disableTitleStyles` lets a custom node such as `InlineEdit` replace the default
heading wrapper.

## Motion

PageHeader reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The small title fades over 24 px of scroll; actions and tabs travel up and pin. It follows the scroll one to one. |

## Alternatives

- For a heading inside a region of the page rather than the page itself, use `Heading`.

## Best practices

### Show the trail on nested pages. {#show-the-trail-on-nested-pages}

Breadcrumbs tell the person where they are; on a page two levels down they are the way back.

Do: Breadcrumbs on a nested page.
Don't: Nested page with no way back.

### Name the page in a word or two. {#name-the-page-in-a-word-or-two}

The title shares a row with actions, so it has to stay on one line.

Do: A short noun.
Don't: A title that wraps and pushes actions down.

### Use only the parts the page needs. {#use-only-the-parts-the-page-needs}

Every extra row pushes content down; add a part only when the page uses it.

Do: Title and one action.
Don't: Breadcrumbs, actions and bottom bar all on.

### Pass the title through `title` or `children`, not both. {#pass-the-title-through-title-or-children-not-both}

Pass the title through `title`, or through `children` when that reads more
naturally in the surrounding code; `children` is only used when `title` is
not given.

```jsx
<PageHeader
    title="Session plans"
    breadcrumbs={<Breadcrumb items={trail} />}
    actions={<Button text="New plan" />}
/>
```

### Pass `titleAs="h2"` when the header sits below another page title. {#pass-titleas-h2-when-the-header-sits-below-another-page-title}

A page has one `h1`. When a `PageHeader` sits under an existing page heading or
inside a dialog below its `h1` title, pass `titleAs="h2"` so the heading
outline keeps one `h1`.

### Reach for `disableTitleStyles` only when the title is not plain text. {#reach-for-disabletitlestyles-only-when-the-title-is-not-plain-text}

The default renders the title in a `Heading`. Turn styling off only when the
title is a custom element already carrying its own heading semantics.

## Accessibility

- **A real heading.** The title renders as a `Heading` (`h1` by default),
  giving the page one clear entry point for assistive technology navigating by
  heading; see Best practices when a second header needs `titleAs="h2"`.
- **Breadcrumbs keep their own semantics.** `PageHeader` does not wrap
  `breadcrumbs` in extra markup — pass a `Breadcrumb` component, which
  carries its own navigation landmark.

## Related

- [Section](?path=/docs/templates-section--docs): use when heading a section inside a page.
- `Breadcrumb`: use when rendering the hierarchy trail above the page title.

Same group: `Accordion` · `Carousel` · `ScrollBar`

## Parts

1. **Breadcrumbs.** Optional, above the title.
2. **Title.** The page's `h1` by default, or any node with `disableTitleStyles`.
3. **Actions.** Optional, at the end of the title row.
4. **Bottom bar.** Optional, under the row: tabs, a filter bar or a status line.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A title row with its actions, no ground of its own. |
| Hovered | Nothing changes. Hover belongs to the breadcrumbs, actions and tabs inside. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes. |
| Focused | Not focusable. Focus goes to the controls in the slots. |
| Disabled | A header has no disabled state. Disable the controls in it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Title | `Heading` at `lg` (24/28); see Best practices for heading level. |
| Rows | `--page-header-stack` between breadcrumbs, title row and bottom bar. |
| Title row | `--page-header-gap` between the title and its actions; `--inline-lg` between actions. |
| Breadcrumbs | `--body-sm`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the page for what a person does or sees: "Session plans". | Use the product name or "Page" as the title. |
| Keep the title to a few words. | Write a sentence with a verb and a full stop. |
| Put the one main action first in the actions. | Fill the actions with every command the page has. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | node | — | The page title. Drawn as a `lg` `Heading` (at the ambient heading level, `h1` by default) unless `disableTitleStyles` is set. `children` is used when it is omitted. |
| `children` | node | — | `children` is the title when `title` is not given. |
| `breadcrumbs` | node | — | A breadcrumb trail shown above the title row. Pass a `Breadcrumb`. |
| `actions` | node | — | Controls shown at the end of the title row, such as a primary button or a menu. |
| `bottomBar` | node | — | Content in a bar below the title row, such as tabs or filters. |
| `titleAs` | oneOf | — | Overrides the HTML element the title's `Heading` renders as, e.g. `"h2"` when placed below another page title. A `Modal` or dialog body resets the heading level to 1, so a `PageHeader` inside one passes `titleAs="h2"`. |
| `disableTitleStyles` | bool | `false` | Renders the title as a plain node instead of a `Heading`, for a caller that styles it itself. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class names added to the header element beside the component's own. |

## Variants

**`titleAs`** — `div` · `h1` · `h2` · `h3` · `h4` · `h5` · `h6` · `span`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Pagination

A numbered page trail with Previous and Next controls. It shows a window of pages around the current one and always keeps the first and last reachable.

Also asked as: paging, pager, next page, page numbers.

**Import:** `import { Pagination } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Pagination/Pagination.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Pagination/Pagination.stories.jsx` — Content, Spacing, InteractionStates, Overview, Interactive, Accessibility, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Current, Disabled, OuterHeight

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Pagination/Pagination.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Pagination` when a list is split into numbered pages and the user needs to
move between them or jump to a known one — admin tables of sessions, students,
tutors. It is fully controlled: `currentPage` and `totalPages` are required, and
every click calls `onPageChange` with the target page. It holds no state.

Reach for it to page through results too many for one screen: a table's rows,
a search's matches, a long history.

The window of numbers is computed for you. `max` (default `5`) centers the
window on the current page, and first and last pages are pinned with an ellipsis
whenever the window does not reach them.

## Motion

Pagination reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Page segments change fill and ink in place; the paged body uses Step. |

## Alternatives

- For a step-by-step workflow rather than pages of results, use `ProgressTracker`.
- For a bounded list that scrolls inside a fixed region, use `ScrollBar`.
- For a continuously loading feed, use infinite scroll rather than pages.

## Best practices

### Pass both `currentPage` and `onPageChange`. {#pass-both-currentpage-and-onpagechange}

```jsx
// Incorrect — nothing happens on click. The component never tracks a page of
// its own, and without onPageChange each click is preventDefault and stop.
<Pagination currentPage={1} totalPages={12} />

// Correct.
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Use `navigator="text"` to show visible Previous and Next labels. {#use-navigator-text-to-show-visible-previous-and-next-labels}

```jsx
// Incorrect — in the default `icon` navigator, previousLabel and nextLabel are used only
// as the arrows' accessible names, so these strings are never visible.
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={9} onPageChange={setPage}
            previousLabel="Back a page" nextLabel="On a page" />

// Correct — navigator="text" renders the words; otherwise leave the defaults, which
// already label the arrows "Previous" and "Next".
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={9} onPageChange={setPage} navigator="text" />
```

### Name the navigation when there is more than one on the page. {#name-the-navigation-when-there-is-more-than-one-on-the-page}

```jsx
// Incorrect — two paginated tables produce two landmarks both called
// "Page navigation", the component's default.
<Pagination currentPage={p1} totalPages={4} onPageChange={setP1} />
<Pagination currentPage={p2} totalPages={7} onPageChange={setP2} />

// Correct.
<Pagination label="Sessions pages" currentPage={p1} totalPages={4} onPageChange={setP1} />
<Pagination label="Students pages" currentPage={p2} totalPages={7} onPageChange={setP2} />
```

Do: Each navigation landmark has its own name.
Don't: Two landmarks with the default name are indistinguishable to a screen reader.

### Show a window, not every page. {#show-a-window-not-every-page}

`max` keeps the row short. Page one and the last page stay reachable with an ellipsis between, so a long list never pushes the controls off the screen.

Do: A window of five pages, with the first and last pinned.
Don't: Every page in the row pushes the controls wide.

### Say how many pages there are. {#say-how-many-pages-there-are}

When the total matters, such as a table of sessions, show it beside the pagination. The row alone only shows a window.

Do: The total beside the row.
Don't: Only a window of numbers, with no total.

## Accessibility

- **The structure is right.** A `nav` labeled by `label` (default "Page
  navigation") wraps a `ul` of `li`s, and the current page carries
  `aria-current="page"`.
- **Every page has a name.** Each page button is labeled "Page 3", "Page 4", so
  a screen reader never reads a bare number. Naming the `nav` says which list
  the pages belong to.
- **Parts are buttons.** `Pagination.Page` and `Pagination.Navigator` are
  `button` elements: Tab reaches each, Enter and Space activate it, and none
  follows a link.
- **A disabled Navigator stays reachable.** At the first or last page the
  Previous or Next control keeps its tab stop and carries `aria-disabled="true"`;
  activating it does nothing. It is announced as unavailable rather than
  disappearing, which keeps the row from reflowing.
- **The ellipsis is hidden.** It is `aria-hidden`: the pinned first and last
  pages beside it carry the meaning.
- **Pages are not destinations.** If page numbers should be linkable or
  shareable, render your own anchors with real URLs.
- **Focus is a ring inside the segment** (`--focus-ring-width`), and the current page keeps an
  outline in forced-colors mode.

## Related

- `DynamicTable`: use when pairing `Pagination` with sorting and filtering on a multi-page table.
- [Table](?path=/docs/templates-table--docs): use when laying out a table footer with row counts and pagination.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Link` · `Sidebar` · `Tabs`

## Parts

1. **Navigator.** Previous and Next, as a caret alone (named by its label) or as the label text.
2. **Page.** A numbered button; the current one is selected.
3. **Gap.** An ellipsis where the window skips pages; hidden from assistive technology.
4. **Pill.** One bordered, fully rounded row holding every segment, divided by a hairline.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Subtle ink on the surface. |
| Hovered | The subtle neutral hovered fill. |
| Pressed | The subtle neutral pressed fill. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring inside the segment; see Border. |
| Current | The selected fill and ink, semibold; hover and press do not change it. |
| Disabled | The disabled ground, ink and caret; the control keeps its tab stop with `aria-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Row height | `--control-md` (default), `--control-sm` (compact) |

rankedText.usage:
Use `Pagination` when a list is split into numbered pages and the user needs to
move between them or jump to a known one — admin tables of sessions, students,
tutors. It is fully controlled: `currentPage` and `totalPages` are required, and
every click calls `onPageChange` with the target page. It holds no state.

Reach for it to page through results too many for one screen: a table's rows,
a search's matches, a long history.

The window of numbers is computed for you. `max` (default `5`) centers the
window on the current page, and first and last pages are pinned with an ellipsis
whenever the window does not reach them.
rankedText.best:
### Pass both `currentPage` and `onPageChange`.

```jsx
// Incorrect — nothing happens on click. The component never tracks a page of
// its own, and without onPageChange each click is preventDefault and stop.
<Pagination currentPage={1} totalPages={12} />

// Correct.
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={12} onPageChange={setPage} />
```

### Use `navigator="text"` to show visible Previous and Next labels.

```jsx
// Incorrect — in the default `icon` navigator, previousLabel and nextLabel are used only
// as the arrows' accessible names, so these strings are never visible.
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={9} onPageChange={setPage}
            previousLabel="Back a page" nextLabel="On a page" />

// Correct — navigator="text" renders the words; otherwise leave the defaults, which
// already label the arrows "Previous" and "Next".
<Pagination currentPage={page} totalPages={9} onPageChange={setPage} navigator="text" />
```

### Name the navigation when there is more than one on the page.

```jsx
// Incorrect — two paginated tables produce two landmarks both called
// "Page navigation", the component's default.
<Pagination currentPage={p1} totalPages={4} onPageChange={setP1} />
<Pagination currentPage={p2} totalPages={7} onPageChange={setP2} />

// Correct.
<Pagination label="Sessions pages" currentPage={p1} totalPages={4} onPageChange={setP1} />
<Pagination label="Students pages" currentPage={p2} totalPages={7} onPageChange={setP2} />
```

Do: Each navigation landmark has its own name.
Don't: Two landmarks with the default name are indistinguishable to a screen reader.

### Show a window, not every page.

`max` keeps the row short. Page one and the last page stay reachable with an ellipsis between, so a long list never pushes the controls off the screen.

Do: A window of five pages, with the first and last pinned.
Don't: Every page in the row pushes the controls wide.

### Say how many pages there are.

When the total matters, such as a table of sessions, show it beside the pagination. The row alone only shows a window.

Do: The total beside the row.
Don't: Only a window of numbers, with no total.

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# PopupSelect

Popup select: one list in a Popup, applied the moment a row is picked. - **One list, applied on pick.** Picking a row sets the value, the menu fades out, and focus goes back to the trigger. There is no Apply. - **Two triggers.** With `label` and no `trigger`, the labeled trigger reads "Status: Upcoming" with a chevron, as the view switch under page tabs. Pass `trigger` for anything else, such as a filter button in a section's view bar; a function gets `{ isOpen, option }`. - **Placement follows the trigger's side.** A trigger at the start of a bar opens `bottom-start` (the default); one at the end opens `bottom-end`. - **Width** is Popup's `auto`: at least the trigger, 160 to 320. - **Marker** is a radio before the label: one choice among several. `marker="check"` puts a check at the row's end. - **Search** sits above the list and filters it. Short lists turn it off with `isSearchable={false}`. The list is Select's own: the same rows, keys and messages.

**Import:** `import { PopupSelect } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Page (`ds guide page`); Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.; Navigation (`ds guide navigation`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/PopupSelect/PopupSelect.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/PopupSelect/PopupSelect.stories.jsx` — Overview, OpensWithAFade, Keyboard, Placement, Searchable, Spacing, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/PopupSelect/PopupSelect.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `PopupSelect` when one pick from one list immediately changes what the page shows, with no field and no Apply button:

- **A view switch** under page tabs, such as "Status: Upcoming" (pass `label` and no `trigger`).
- **One filter** in a section's view bar, such as Subject (pass a `FilterButton` as `trigger`).

## Motion

PopupSelect reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, with no clip or travel. From the keyboard it opens with no animation. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, the same as the enter. |

## Alternatives

- For a value that belongs to a form field, use `Select`.
- For several filter categories staged and applied together, use `FilterMenu`.
- For a menu of actions rather than values, use `DropdownMenu`.

## Best practices

### Line the menu up with its trigger's side. {#line-the-menu-up-with-its-trigger-s-side}

Start-of-bar triggers open `bottom-start` and end-of-bar triggers open `bottom-end`, so the menu never hangs past its own bar.

### Turn search off for a short list. {#turn-search-off-for-a-short-list}

Pass `isSearchable={false}` when a list has only a few options that scan at a glance.

### Show the active value on the trigger. {#show-the-active-value-on-the-trigger}

The built-in labeled trigger shows the value automatically; with a custom `FilterButton` trigger, pass the applied count as `trailingMetric`.

### Keep it to one list. {#keep-it-to-one-list}

Two lists, or picks that wait for an Apply, are a different menu.

## Accessibility

- **The trigger is a real button** that says a popup opens and whether it is
  open. The labeled trigger's name carries the value: "Status: Upcoming".
- **The popup is named** by `label`, and so is the list inside it.
- **The search field is the list's combobox.** Focus stays in it while the
  arrow keys move the highlighted row (`aria-activedescendant`). Without
  search, focus goes to the list itself.
- **Focus returns to the trigger** after a pick or Escape.

## Related

- `Select`: use when picking a value inside a form field.
- `FilterMenu`: use when staging and applying several filter categories together.
- `DropdownMenu`: use when opening a menu of actions rather than values.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Trigger.** The labeled trigger is a subtle `FilterButton` reading "Label: Value" with a chevron. Any other trigger is the caller's.
2. **Popup.** A `Popup` at `width="auto"`: at least the trigger's width, never under 160, up to 320. It sits 4 from the trigger.
3. **Search** (optional). A compact search field above the list, on by default. Turn it off with `isSearchable={false}` for a short list.
4. **List.** `Select`'s list: the same rows, groups, descriptions and messages. The picked row takes the selected fill and a radio before its label, since the menu picks one value. `marker="check"` draws a check at the row's end instead.

### Placement

| Trigger | `placement` |
| --- | --- |
| At the start of a bar, or alone | `bottom-start` (default): the menu's start edge meets the trigger's. |
| At the end of a bar | `bottom-end`: the menu's end edge meets the trigger's. |

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Open | The menu fades in place. A keyboard open is instant. |
| Hovered row | The row takes the hovered fill; it is also the keyboard cursor. |
| Picked | The row changes color, then the menu fades and the content behind it swaps in place. Nothing slides. |
| No match | One "No results" row; set your own with `emptyMessage`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | Those of `Popup`: `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--popup-radius`. |
| Inset of the rows | 4: `--dropdown-menu-pad`. |
| Width | `--popup-min-width` to `--popup-max-width`, and at least the trigger. |
| Height of the list | Scrolls past 320: `--dropdown-menu-max-height`. |
| Gap to the trigger | 4: `--popup-offset`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name what is picked: "Status", "Subject", "View". | A verb phrase such as "Filter by status". |
| Use short option labels in sentence case: "Upcoming". | Labels long enough to wrap or truncate. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|

# ProgressBar

`ProgressBar` — a determinate (or indeterminate) bar for a task whose proportion done is known. `value` is a percent (0 to 100); the drawn width and the announced `aria-valuenow` clamp together, so an out-of-range value never draws a full bar while reporting a number past its own `aria-valuemax` (#325) — a state no assistive technology can make sense of.

Also asked as: percent complete, determinate loading.

**Import:** `import { ProgressBar } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Default, Success, Inverse, WithACaption, Indeterminate, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.mdx`

**Motion:** change `linear` · success `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.done.step`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `ProgressBar` for progress through a task: an upload, a course, a
multi-step form. When the task's length is unknown, set `isIndeterminate`.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most bars: a brand fill on a neutral track. |
| Success | Marks completion. Show a finished task at `100` in success. |
| Inverse | On a bold or colored background. |

## Motion

ProgressBar reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Load content | `--ds-motion-linear` | Fills with the work, never ahead of it. |  |
| success | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The bar reaches its end and its fill changes to done. | `sound.done.step` on land: a module or lesson is done |

## Alternatives

- For an indeterminate wait with no track at all, use `Spinner`.
- For a compact determinate ring beside a title or a file row, use `ProgressRing`.
- For the outcome when a task finishes, use `Flag` or `SectionMessage`.
- For position in a hierarchy rather than progress through a task, use `Breadcrumb`.

## Best practices

### Use `isIndeterminate` when the length is unknown. {#use-isindeterminate-when-the-length-is-unknown}

A bar that fills implies a known total; use the moving bar when the work has
no measurable end. `isIndeterminate` drops `value` and the value attributes.

### Use inverse on bold surfaces. {#use-inverse-on-bold-surfaces}

The default track disappears on a bold ground; inverse keeps the bar readable.

Do: Inverse appearance on a bold surface.
Don't: Default appearance on a bold surface.

### Show one bar per task. {#show-one-bar-per-task}

Stacked bars for one task read as separate jobs; show a single bar for the whole.

Do: A single bar.
Don't: Three bars for one task.

### Put the number in text beside the bar. {#put-the-number-in-text-beside-the-bar}

The bar (`--progress-bar-height`) carries no visible text of its own.

Do: A caption beside the bar says what the fill means.
Don't: A bare bar leaves the reader to guess the number.

### Show a finished task as success. {#show-a-finished-task-as-success}

Do: When complete, the success appearance marks the task done.
Don't: A finished task left as a brand bar.

## Accessibility

- **The bar is a real progressbar.** `role="progressbar"` with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` when determinate, and
  an `aria-label` that defaults to "Progress".
- **Reduced motion is handled.** The indeterminate sweep stops under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Color is not the message.** `appearance` colors the bar and says nothing
  to a screen reader; `ariaLabel` and a caption carry the meaning.

## Related

- `ProgressRing`: use when showing determinate progress in a compact circular slot.
- `ProgressTracker`: use when showing discrete named steps in a multi-step flow.

Same group: `ProgressRing` · `Skeleton` · `Spinner`

## Parts

1. **Track.** The full-width bar the fill runs along, a pill (`--progress-bar-height` tall).
2. **Fill.** The done part, a percent of the track. Indeterminate, it is a moving segment.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Determinate: the fill width is `value`, clamped to `0` to `100` together with `aria-valuenow`. |
| Indeterminate | A segment slides along the track. No value is announced. Under reduced motion the segment holds still. |
| Hovered | None. It is not a control. |
| Pressed | None. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A bar has no disabled state. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Track | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--progress-bar-height` tall, `--radius-full`. |
| Fill | `--ds-background-brand-bold` through `--plus-progressbar-fill-color`; `--ds-background-success-bold` for `success`. |
| Inverse | Track `--ds-background-inverse-subtle`, fill `--ds-background-inverse-subtle-pressed`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the bar for what it measures: "68% of goals met". | Leave the default "Progress" label. |
| Use the same words in the caption and in `ariaLabel`: "68% of goals met". | Say one thing on screen and another to a screen reader. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `0` | A percent, 0 to 100 |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | success marks completion; inverse reads on a bold background |
| `isIndeterminate` | bool | `false` | The duration is unknown |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `'Progress'` | Names what the bar measures. "Progress" says nothing when a page has two bars. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `success` · `inverse`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# ProgressIndicator

A row of dots showing where you are along the steps of a journey. Unlike `ProgressTracker`, the steps carry no label of their own — only a position. `onSelect` makes every dot a button and lets a person jump to any step; without it the dots are decorative and `aria-current` on the active one is the only state a screen reader gets. A dot that is a button keeps a 24px target, so the gap between buttons widens to fit it. `progress` times the current step: its dot stretches into a bar whose fill tracks `progress`, from 0 to 1, as in a carousel that moves on its own. A step with no clock passes `1`, and the bar shows full; under reduced motion the bar always shows full.

Also asked as: dots, carousel dots, step dots, slide marker.

**Import:** `import { ProgressIndicator } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressIndicator/ProgressIndicator.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressIndicator/ProgressIndicator.stories.jsx` — Default, Interactive, Appearances, Sizes, Spacing, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Decorative, SizeTokens, Timed, Clock, TimedInteractive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressIndicator/ProgressIndicator.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `ProgressIndicator` for a short sequence where position matters more than
the name of each step — a carousel, an onboarding flight, a slide deck.

When each step lasts a set time and moves on by itself, pass `progress` so the
current marker shows how much of its time is left.

## Motion

ProgressIndicator reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Step states change in place: the step left becomes visited, the next current. |

## Alternatives

- For steps with their own visible labels, use `ProgressTracker`.
- For a single bar showing percent complete, use `ProgressBar`.

## Best practices

### Pass `onSelect` only when jumping ahead makes sense. {#pass-onselect-only-when-jumping-ahead-makes-sense}

Without `onSelect` the markers are decorative and only `aria-current` marks the active one. With it, every marker becomes a button a person can press to jump there directly. That suits a carousel, not a linear flow someone must complete in order.

Do: Interactive markers on a carousel, where any slide can be opened.
Don't: Interactive markers on a flow that must be finished in order.

```jsx
<ProgressIndicator
    values={slides}
    selectedIndex={index}
    onSelect={({ index }) => setIndex(index)}
    ariaControls="carousel-panel"
/>
```

### Keep the number of steps small. {#keep-the-number-of-steps-small}

A short row reads at a glance. With many steps, position stops being readable.

Do: A handful of steps, so the current one is easy to find.
Don't: Two dozen steps, where the current one is lost in the row.

### Match the appearance to the surface. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-surface}

`inverted` is for a dark surface; on a light one use `default`, `primary` or `help`.

Do: Inverted indicator on a dark ground.
Don't: Inverted indicator on a light surface, where it vanishes.

### Use `values` to supply the step count and each button's accessible name. {#use-values-to-supply-the-step-count-and-each-button-s-accessible-name}

The array's content never renders visually. Its length becomes the number of step markers, and when `onSelect` is set each entry becomes a button's accessible name.

## Accessibility

- **A named group.** The row has `role="group"` with a `label` ("Progress" by
  default), so a screen reader announces it as one control.
- **The current step is `aria-current="step"`.** This is the only state a
  non-interactive indicator exposes.
- **Interactive markers are real buttons**, each named from its `values` entry
  and linked to the content it controls with `ariaControls`.
- **The bar is hidden from assistive technology.** Its fill is a picture of
  time; `aria-current` still names the current step.
- **Reduced motion shows the bar full**, so nothing grows on screen.

## Related

- `Carousel`: use when pairing `ProgressIndicator` with an autoplaying slide stage.
- `ProgressTracker`: use when each step needs a visible label beside its marker.

Same group: `ProgressTracker`

## Parts

1. **Step marker.** One circle per step (`8` or `12` across).
2. **Current marker.** The brand ground (discovery for help, inverse icon for inverted), with `aria-current="step"`.
3. **Group.** The row, named by `label`.
4. **Bar.** With `progress`, the current marker stretches to `--control-md`: the subtlest icon ground is the track, and the fill grows from the start edge. Under reduced motion it shows full.
5. **Target.** A marker that is a button keeps a `--control-sm` target, so the gap between buttons widens to fit it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Subtlest icon ground; the current marker is on its appearance ground. |
| Hovered | Interactive only: an unselected marker takes the subtle icon ground. |
| Pressed | Interactive only: an unselected marker takes the default icon ground. |
| Focused | Interactive only: shows the focus ring; see Border. |
| Disabled | A progress indicator has no disabled state; without `onSelect` it is decorative. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Marker ground | `--ds-icon-subtlest`, `--ds-icon-subtle`, `--ds-icon` |
| Current marker | `--ds-background-brand-bold`, `--ds-background-discovery-bold`, `--ds-icon-inverse` |
| Inverted marker | `--ds-background-inverse-subtle` and its states |
| Size | `--progress-indicator-dot-size-8`, `--progress-indicator-dot-size-12` |
| Bar | `--control-md` long; track `--ds-icon-subtlest`, fill the current marker's color |
| Gap | `--inline-md`, `--inline-sm`, `--stack-sm`; between buttons at least `--control-sm` less the marker |
| Ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each entry for its step when the markers are buttons: "Step 2, Reflection". | Leave interactive steps unnamed or number them only. |
| Give the group a `label` that says what it tracks: "Carousel slides". | Keep the default "Progress" when a page holds two indicators. |
| Use it where steps have no labels of their own. | Use it where each step needs a title; use Progress tracker. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `values` | array (required) | — | — |
| `selectedIndex` | number (required) | — | — |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | — |
| `size` | enum | `8` | — |
| `spacing` | enum | `'spacious'` | — |
| `onSelect` | func | — | — |
| `ariaControls` | string | — | — |
| `label` | string | `'Progress'` | — |
| `progress` | number | — | Times the current step: its dot stretches into a bar filled to this fraction, 0 to 1. Pass `1` for a step with no clock. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `default` · `primary` · `help` · `inverted`

**`size`** — `8` · `12`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact` · `spacious`

# ProgressRing

`ProgressRing` — a determinate ring for a known amount of progress in a small slot. `value` is a percent (0 to 100); the drawn arc and the announced `aria-valuenow` clamp together to 0 to 100. A ring is never indeterminate; unknown time is `Spinner`'s job.

**Import:** `import { ProgressRing } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressRing/ProgressRing.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressRing/ProgressRing.stories.jsx` — Overview, Default, Inverse, Zero, Partial, Complete, Values, Sizes, Size16, Size20, Size24, WithInlineText, OutOfRangeValuesAreClamped, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, ReducedMotion

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressRing/ProgressRing.mdx`

**Motion:** change `linear`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `ProgressRing` when a task has a known percent done and sits in an
icon-sized slot, such as an uploading file row where a list of horizontal bars
would crowd the view. A ring is never indeterminate.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Standard surfaces: a brand-bold fill on a neutral track. |
| Inverse | On a bold or colored background. |

## Motion

ProgressRing reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Load content | `--ds-motion-linear` | Fills clockwise from twelve o'clock with the work, never ahead of it. |

## Alternatives

- For a wait whose duration is unknown, use `Spinner`.
- For progress where a horizontal track fits (such as a card header or a form step), use `ProgressBar`.
- For content loading into a layout that already has a shape, use `Skeleton`.

## Best practices

### Keep `ProgressRing` determinate and reach for `Spinner` when the total is unknown. {#keep-progressring-determinate-and-reach-for-spinner-when-the-total-is-unknown}

A ring with a track promises a known share of completion; spinning or freezing a
half-filled ring when there is no total misleads the tutor about how long is
left.

Do: Spinner when the wait has no measurable percent.
Don't: A fixed ProgressRing faking an unknown wait.

### Pair `ProgressRing` with visible percent text when exact progress matters. {#pair-progressring-with-visible-percent-text-when-exact-progress-matters}

At `PROGRESS_RING_SIZES` diameters (`16`, `20`, `24`), the center of the ring
cannot hold text; put the percent beside it on the row's meta line.

Do: The percent sits beside the ring.
Don't: A bare ring with no surrounding context.

an active upload never shifts the row, and `size={16}` beside compact text.

Don't: An undersized ring that shifts when replaced by the row's icon.

and fill to inverse roles that stay legible.

  one progressbar from another.

| Hovered | None. It is not a control. |
| Pressed | None. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |

| Inverse | Track `--ds-background-inverse-subtle`, fill `--ds-icon-inverse`. |

# ProgressTracker

The steps of a journey, each done, current or upcoming. Every item renders as a link (`href`), a button (`onClick`) or plain text, in that order of precedence; `disabled` items take neither. `status` alone drives how a step looks — a `visited` item still needs `onClick`/`href` to be reachable again.

Also asked as: steps, stepper, wizard, multi-step, checkout steps.

**Import:** `import { ProgressTracker } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressTracker/ProgressTracker.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressTracker/ProgressTracker.stories.jsx` — Default, Interactive, Vertical, Spacing, Clickable, Completed, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/status-indicators/ProgressTracker/ProgressTracker.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · success `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.done.step`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `ProgressTracker` when each step of a journey has its own name people
need to see and, often, jump back to — a multi-page form, a setup flow, a
reflection with named sections.

## Motion

ProgressTracker reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Step states change in place: the step left becomes visited, the next current. |  |
| success | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The last step changes to done in place. | `sound.done.step` on land: a module or lesson is done |

## Alternatives

- For a short sequence where position matters more than each step's name, use `ProgressIndicator`.
- For a single bar showing percent complete, use `ProgressBar`.

## Best practices

### Set an item's status and its action separately. {#set-an-item-s-status-and-its-action-separately}

`status` alone decides how a step looks. Give any non-`disabled` item an `href` or `onClick` to make it reachable; without either, it renders as plain text even if its status says it can be revisited.

```jsx
<ProgressTracker
    items={[
        { id: 'info', label: 'Session information', status: 'visited', onClick: goTo('info') },
        { id: 'reflection', label: 'Student reflection', status: 'current' },
        { id: 'feedback', label: 'Form feedback', status: 'disabled' },
    ]}
/>
```

### Let people go back to a step they finished. {#let-people-go-back-to-a-step-they-finished}

Give a `visited` step an action so it can be reopened. Leave a step that cannot be reached yet `disabled`.

Do: A finished step opens again; a step not yet reachable is disabled.
Don't: A finished step is plain text, while a step not yet ready can be opened.

### Keep labels short. {#keep-labels-short}

One line per step, a few words. A long label truncates with an ellipsis.

Do: Each label names the task in a word or two.
Don't: Sentence-length labels that cut off mid-word.

### Use the vertical orientation when the row will not fit. {#use-the-vertical-orientation-when-the-row-will-not-fit}

Stack the steps in a narrow column such as a sidebar; keep the row when there is width for it.

Do: Vertical steps in a narrow column, each label readable.
Don't: A row squeezed into a narrow column, so every label truncates.

### Mark unreachable steps `disabled`. {#mark-unreachable-steps-disabled}

A `disabled` item renders neither a link nor a button regardless of what `href` or `onClick` is passed, keeping a step someone cannot reach yet out of the tab order.

## Accessibility

- **A named landmark.** The tracker is a `nav` with `label` as its accessible
  name ("Progress tracker" by default), and its steps are an ordered list.
- **The current step is `aria-current="step"`.** Screen readers announce it
  as the one in progress.
- **Reachable steps are real links or buttons.** Tab reaches any non-`disabled`
  step that carries `href` or `onClick`; `disabled` steps are marked
  `aria-disabled` and are not in the tab order.

## Related

- Forms: use when pairing `ProgressTracker` with a multi-step form layout.
- `ProgressIndicator`: use when steps have no visible labels of their own.

Same group: `ProgressIndicator`

## Parts

1. **Marker.** A circle for unvisited, current and disabled steps; a success check for a visited step.
2. **Label.** One line, truncating with an ellipsis.
3. **Step.** A link, a button or plain text, with `aria-current="step"` on the current one.
4. **Rule.** A hairline joining horizontal steps.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Subtle text on no ground; the current step is on the selected ground in medium weight. |
| Hovered | A link or button step takes the subtle neutral hovered ground. |
| Pressed | A link or button step takes the subtle neutral pressed ground. |
| Focused | A link or button step shows the focus ring inset in the step; see Border. |
| Disabled | Disabled ink and icon; neither a link nor a button, and `aria-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Step text | `--ds-text-subtle`, `--ds-text-selected`, `--ds-text-disabled` |
| Current ground | `--ds-background-selected` |
| Hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` |
| Visited check | `--ds-icon-success` |
| Marker, rule | `--ds-icon-subtle`, `--ds-border` |
| Gap | `--stack-lg`, `--stack-md`, `--stack-sm` |
| Ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each step for the task it holds: "Student reflection". | Number the steps in the label or repeat "Step". |
| Keep each label to a few words. | Write labels that truncate. |
| Use the same names as the page titles they lead to. | Rename a step between the tracker and its page. |
| Give the nav a `label` that says what it tracks: "Reflection steps". | Keep the default when a page holds two trackers. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `items` | enum | — | — |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | — |
| `orientation` | enum | `'horizontal'` | — |
| `label` | string | `'Progress tracker'` | — |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact` · `spacious`

**`orientation`** — `horizontal` · `vertical`

# PromptInput

Where a person writes to the AI: a text area that grows from one line up to five, then scrolls, with an optional control before the text and one send action after it. - **value / defaultValue / onChange** control or seed the text. Uncontrolled, the field clears itself after a send; controlled, the owner clears it in `onSubmit`. - **onSubmit(value)** runs on Enter or the send button, with the text as typed. Shift+Enter starts a new line. Nothing sends while the field is empty, disabled, loading, or an input method is mid-composition. - **isLoading** turns the send button into Stop (`onStop`) and rings the field in a `GenerativeBorder`. - **startSlot** is one quiet control before the text, such as an attach button. **attachments** renders a row of staged files above the text. **actions** is a slot for extra controls beside the send button. A PLUS composition of `FieldBox`, `IconButton` and `GenerativeBorder`.

Also asked as: ask the assistant, prompt box, chat input.

**Import:** `import { PromptInput } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptInput/PromptInput.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptInput/PromptInput.stories.jsx` — Default, ButtonInside, ButtonStaysBottom, RingFollowsField, EnterSends, ShiftEnterStartsALine, CannotSendWhenEmpty, Loading, WithSlots, ComposingDoesNotSend, Focused, Disabled, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptInput/PromptInput.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `PromptInput` for AI chat or a feature that drafts from a free-text request.
For a plain multiline field without send-on-Enter or loading behavior, use `TextArea`.

`PromptInput` does not include the fallibility line.
`AiChat` supplies it; other consumers must place it under the field.

## Motion

PromptInput reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Send becomes Stop at once while the AI writes. |

## Best practices

### Keep the field visible while generating. {#keep-the-field-visible-while-generating}

Pair `isLoading` with `onStop` to show progress while keeping the question visible and Stop reachable. Keep the field enabled.

Do: The loading state shows progress inside the field.
Don't: A field emptied while generating loses the question.

### Show focus while typing. {#show-focus-while-typing}

Focus tells the user the field accepts input. The field draws its own focus ring; never remove it with custom styles.

### Hint at what can be asked. {#hint-at-what-can-be-asked}

Do: The placeholder hints at what can be asked.
Don't: The placeholder describes the control.

### Leave the field enabled when idle. {#leave-the-field-enabled-when-idle}

A disabled field blocks follow-up questions.

Do: An idle field takes the next question.
Don't: A disabled idle field blocks the next question.

### Send only real text. {#send-only-real-text}

`onSubmit` never fires for an empty, disabled or loading field, or on Enter during IME composition.

```jsx
<PromptInput
    label="Message to AI chat"
    placeholder="Ask anything about this session…"
    isLoading={isGenerating}
    onSubmit={sendMessage}
    onStop={cancelGeneration}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- **`label` is required** and is the field's only accessible name — there is
  no visible label by default.
- **Send and Stop are both labeled buttons**, each with its own
  `aria-label`, not just an icon.
- **Enter-to-send follows the platform convention for composed text**:
  Shift+Enter inserts a line break, and an in-progress IME composition never
  triggers a send.

## Related

- For a plain multi-line field with no AI behavior, use `TextArea`.
- For the border treatment shown while loading, see `GenerativeBorder`.
- For a short, tappable prompt suggestion, use `Suggestion` or `PromptStarters`.

Same group: `AiChat` · `AiIcon` · `AiMessage` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptStarters` · `Suggestion`

## Parts

1. **Attachments** (optional). A row of staged files above the text.
2. **Start slot** (optional). One quiet control before the text, such as an attach button.
3. **Text area.** Grows from one line to five, then scrolls. Named by `label`.
4. **Actions** (optional). Extra controls beside the send button.
5. **Send.** A default (32) primary icon button, 4 from the edge on every side and on the last line as the text grows; while loading it becomes Stop.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill and `--border-width-default` input edge. Send is held back until there is text. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own on the field; the send button takes its own pressed fill. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. |
| Disabled | The field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled`, and nothing sends. |
| Loading | Send becomes Stop, and a GenerativeBorder rings the field and sets `aria-busy`. Stop is never held back by `isDisabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`, `--radius-control-lg`. |
| Height | Starts at one line, `--height-250` (40, a single-line field), and grows to five lines: `--type-line-height-125` × 5 plus `--space-0375` top and bottom, then scrolls. |
| Padding | `--pad-y-md` top and bottom, `--pad-x-md` either side. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Attachments | `--stack-md` between files and under the row. |
| Actions and send | `--stack-sm` between them. |
| Loading ring | GenerativeBorder at `radius-control-lg`, the field's own radius. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the field for what it sends: "Message to AI chat". | A generic name such as "Text" or "Input". |
| Hint at what can be asked: "Ask about a student, a session or a lesson". | Describe the control: "Type here". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `label` | string (required) | — | The field's accessible name, such as "Message to AI chat". |
| `value` | string | — | The text, for a controlled field. |
| `defaultValue` | string | `''` | The starting text of an uncontrolled field. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with the change event as the text changes. |
| `onSubmit` | func | — | Called with the text on Enter or the send button. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | A reply is being generated: the send button becomes Stop and the field gets a GenerativeBorder. |
| `onStop` | func | — | What the Stop button does while `isLoading`. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | — |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | — |
| `startSlot` | node | — | One quiet control before the text, such as an attach button. |
| `attachments` | node | — | A row of staged attachments, shown above the text. |
| `actions` | node | — | Extra controls beside the send button. |
| `state` | enum | — | Draws focus still, for documentation. Live focus needs nothing. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | — |

## Variants

**`state`** — `default` · `focus`

# PromptStarters

A few things a person could ask the AI, as a wrapping row of prompt `Suggestion` tags. - **starters** are `{ id, label, text }`: the short `label` on the tag and the longer `text` it stands for. - **onSelect(starter)** runs when a tag is pressed, with the whole starter and nothing else. A starter suggests; it never sends on its own, so the caller decides what happens — usually putting `text` in a `PromptInput` for a person to read and send. - **label** names the group for assistive technology.

**Import:** `import { PromptStarters } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptStarters/PromptStarters.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptStarters/PromptStarters.stories.jsx` — Default, SelectHandsBackTheStarter, EmptyRendersNothing, FillsThePromptInput, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptStarters/PromptStarters.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `PromptStarters` before a person types into an empty chat, new reflection or
blank prompt field. For a single follow-up during a conversation, use `Suggestion`.

## Motion

PromptStarters reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fade in place, staggered; picking one fills the composer. |

## Best practices

### Keep the label short, and put the prompt in `text`. {#keep-the-label-short-and-put-the-prompt-in-text}

Use a few words for `label` and put the full request in `text`.

Do: A short label for a longer prompt.
Don't: The whole prompt as the label.

### Offer a few. {#offer-a-few}

Three to five starters fit a row and can be read at a glance.

Do: A few starters to choose from.
Don't: So many starters the row becomes a wall.

### Write each label as a request. {#write-each-label-as-a-request}

The label says what the person is asking for, starting with a verb.

Do: Labels that read as requests.
Don't: Topic names that don't say what will be asked.

### Let `onSelect` decide what happens. {#let-onselect-decide-what-happens}

Use `onSelect` to fill a `PromptInput` with the starter's `text` so the person
can read, edit and send it. Never send it on their behalf.

### Pass an empty list rather than a guard. {#pass-an-empty-list-rather-than-a-guard}

Pass an empty `starters` array to render nothing, including no empty group;
no conditional wrapper is needed.

## Accessibility

- **A named group.** The row is `role="group"` with `label` as its accessible
  name, required so assistive technology announces the set together.
- **Each tag is `Suggestion`'s own control.** Keyboard reach, focus and the
  accept action all follow `Suggestion`'s accessibility contract.

## Related

- For a single follow-up prompt once a conversation is underway, use `Suggestion` directly.
- For where a selected starter's text typically lands, see `PromptInput`.

Same group: `AiChat` · `AiIcon` · `AiMessage` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptInput` · `Suggestion`

## Parts

1. **Group.** A wrapping row with `role="group"`, named by the required `label`.
2. **Starter.** A prompt `Suggestion` per entry in `starters`: the sparkle wand, the short `label` on the tag, and the longer `text` it stands for.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A row of prompt tags. The group itself has no ground and no state. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused | Each tag reacts as a `Suggestion` does. |
| Empty | An empty `starters` array renders nothing. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Gap | `--stack-md` between tags and between rows, the same gap as a tag row. |
| Starter | A `Suggestion`, so its edge, words, grounds and focus ring are Suggestion's tokens. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write a label of a few words that reads as a request: "Summarize this session". | Put a whole paragraph on the tag. |
| Name the group for what it offers: "Suggested prompts". | Leave the group unnamed. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `starters` | arrayOf | `[]` | What to offer: `id` for the key, `label` on the tag, `text` for the prompt it stands for. |
| `onSelect` | func | — | Called with the starter that was pressed. It never sends anything itself. |
| `label` | string (required) | — | The group's accessible name, such as "Suggested prompts". |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |

## Tokens touched

`--stack-md`

From `design-system/src/components/ai/PromptStarters/PromptStarters.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

# Radio

Radio — single option within a named radio group. Supports controlled (`isChecked`) and uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`) usage. Built on Base UI's Radio, wrapped in `FieldFrame` (A7) for the label and the description caption. Base UI's Radio has no standalone `checked` prop — selection lives on a `RadioGroup` ancestor. `RadioGroup` renders one real, shared Base UI `RadioGroup` around all of its options and passes each one `grouped`, so the group gets Base UI's native roving-tabindex keyboard nav across options for free, same as `ChoiceGrid`'s radio-type rows. A `Radio` used on its own (no `grouped`, the default) — a lone question, a `ChoiceGrid` cell, or sibling Radios sharing a bare `name` the way the "Group" story composes them — owns a private, single-item group instead, so it stays independently controllable exactly like the native input it replaces. That private group keeps its own `role="radiogroup"` (axe rejects `aria-readonly`/ `aria-required` on a role-less `div`) but drops the `aria-labelledby` it would otherwise inherit from an ambient Fieldset legend it has no business naming itself after.

**Import:** `import { Radio } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Radio/Radio.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Radio/Radio.stories.jsx` — Overview, Content, States, Invalid, Interactive, ReadOnly, DescriptionAndCard, KeyboardFocus, HoverStep, Unselected, Selected, Hovered, Focused, Disabled, DisabledWithReason, Required, Soft, Tile, TileNarrowLargeIllustrations

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Radio/Radio.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Radio` directly only when options need custom layout, such as radio cells inside a table.

Make one option the default: the safest and lowest-risk one. If a person may decline all options, add a "None" option; if the list cannot be complete, add "Other".

## Motion

Radio reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |

## Alternatives

- For a standard radio question with a shared legend and error, use `RadioGroup`.
- For a question where several options may be chosen, use `CheckboxGroup` or `Checkbox`.
- For a list of six or more options, use `Select`.
- For a setting that turns on or off immediately, use `Toggle`.

## Best practices

### Reserve choice tiles for one big question with two to four pictured options. {#reserve-choice-tiles-for-one-big-question-with-two-to-four-pictured-options}

Use `appearance="tile"` when a step asks one focal question with two to four options and every option carries an `illustration`. Keep ordinary form lists and sets of five or more options in `plain` or `card`.

Do: Two pictured tiles for one focal question.
Don't: Plain text options without illustrations drawn as tiles.

### Show one answer selected at a time. {#show-one-answer-selected-at-a-time}

A radio group holds exactly one answer. Never show two selected.

Do: One radio selected in the group.
Don't: Two radios selected at once.

### Never preselect a high-risk answer. {#never-preselect-a-high-risk-answer}

Leave consequential choices, such as ones about privacy or payment, for the
person to make on purpose. When an option starts selected, make it the safe
one.

Do: The safe option, Keep my history, starts selected.
Don't: The high-risk option, Delete my history, starts selected.

### Keep labels short and parallel. {#keep-labels-short-and-parallel}

Short labels scan as a list; long ones wrap and blur the choices.

Do: Short, parallel labels.
Don't: Long labels that wrap, beside a one-word one.

### Order options by likelihood or risk. {#order-options-by-likelihood-or-risk}

Do: Order options from most to least likely, or from least to most risk.
Don't: Alphabetical order cannot be localized and says nothing about which option fits most people.

### A lone Radio is not a group. {#a-lone-radio-is-not-a-group}

Radios that share a `name` are one group; each option gets its own id. ARIA allows `aria-readonly` on a radiogroup and not on a radio, so a read-only question belongs in RadioGroup, which announces it.

### Avoid long lists and overlapping ranges. {#avoid-long-lists-and-overlapping-ranges}

For six or more options, use `Select`. Do not write numeric options that overlap (`0–20`, `20–40`) or skip a number.

### Keep extra detail in `description`. {#keep-extra-detail-in-description}

`description` renders under the label and is read after the name.

## Accessibility

- **Unique ids.** Each instance derives its own id so labels never resolve to the first radio of the group; pass `aria-label` only when there is no visible label.
- **Required or invalid group.** Include an error message, for example "Select an option".
- **Disabled options.** Disable an option only for something the person can fix on the same screen, and put the reason in `description` at full contrast, never a tooltip; a disabled option leaves the tab order. For a choice that must stay reachable, keep it enabled and use validation, so a screen reader user hears why it cannot be chosen. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).
- **Keyboard.** Arrow keys move between radios that share a `name`. Focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the radio.

## Related

- `RadioGroup`: use when asking a complete radio question with a legend, value and error.
- `CheckboxGroup`: use when any number of options may be chosen.
- `Select`: use when choosing one option from a list of six or more.
- `Toggle`: use when flipping a single setting on or off immediately.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Radio.** A 12 circle in `plain` and `card` appearances; visually hidden in `soft` and `tile` while keeping native radio semantics, keyboard navigation, and form submission.
2. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the radio in a 24 row. It names the option. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows a standalone radio's label in plain text.
3. **Description.** Optional 12/16 text under the label that describes the option. It does not name it.
4. **Appearances.** `plain` draws the circle and label inline; `card` wraps them in a bordered surface row; `soft` draws a `--ds-background-neutral` row without a radio dot (selected row shows `--ds-background-selected`, a 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing `fa-solid fa-check` icon) for the majority selection type in a choice flow while the minority selection type keeps its visible control; `tile` draws a 224px pictured card.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Hovered | Unselected: `--ds-background-input-hovered` with a `--ds-border-brand` edge (or `--ds-background-neutral-hovered` in `soft`). Selected: the hovered step of the selected bold fill (or `--ds-background-selected-hovered` in `soft`). |
| Pressed | No step of its own in plain/card. In `soft`, an unselected row takes `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` and a selected row takes `--ds-background-selected-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the radio (or around the row in `soft` and `tile`), for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill and `--ds-border-selected` edge; the dot is `--ds-icon-inverse`. In `soft`, `--ds-background-selected` fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Invalid | The unselected radio or tile takes `--ds-border-danger` (in `soft`, both unselected and selected rows take `--ds-border-danger`). |
| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, no hover; an unchecked radio takes the `--ds-background-neutral` fill. Not changeable. In `soft`, the selected row keeps its selected fill, edge and trailing check. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill, `--ds-border-disabled` edge, `--ds-icon-disabled` dot or check. Out of the tab order. In `soft`, the row takes the disabled fill and edge, with the check in `--ds-icon-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Circle fill and edge | `--ds-background-input` and `--ds-border-input`; selected `--ds-background-selected-bold` and `--ds-border-selected`. |
| Circle size, edge width | `--radio-control-size` (12); `--border-width-selected`. |
| Row | `--control-sm` (24); gap `--inline-md`. |
| Label | `--ds-text`, body default. |
| Card | `--radius-control-md`, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border`, `--ds-surface` fill. |
| Soft row | `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-background-neutral` fill at rest; selected `--ds-background-selected` fill, `--border-width-default` `--ds-border-selected` edge, and `--icon-sm` trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Choice tile | `--choice-tile-width` (224px), `--radius-control-md`, `--ds-surface` fill; selected 2px `--ds-border-selected` and `--ds-background-selected`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write each label as the option: "In person". | A sentence or an instruction: "Choose this if you meet in person." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Keep labels parallel in length and form. | Mix one word with a full clause. |
| Add "None" when a person may decline every option, "Other" when the list cannot be complete. | Force an answer that does not fit. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Select an option". | "Required" or "Invalid". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the radio button, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string (required) | — | Form key of the radio group. Options that belong together share it, and it is reported in `onChange`. |
| `label` | node | — | The text that names this option. |
| `value` | string or number | — | Form value of this option, and the `target.value` that `onChange` reports when it is chosen. |
| `isChecked` | bool | — | Controlled selected state. Pair it with `onChange`; when it is set, `defaultChecked` is ignored. |
| `defaultChecked` | bool | — | Whether an uncontrolled radio starts selected. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error state, for an option that fails validation. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Prevents interaction and dims this option. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the option without letting the user change it. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets the required constraint (`aria-required`) on a standalone radio. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `description` | node | — | Secondary text under the label. It describes the option; it does not name it. |
| `illustration` | node | — | Decorative picture shown above the label when `appearance` is `tile`. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'plain'` | `plain` (default) is a radio beside its label; `card` draws a bordered row; `soft` draws a neutral row without a radio dot; `tile` draws a centered pictured tile. |
| `grouped` | bool | `false` | Set by `RadioGroup`. Not for direct use. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with `{ target: { name, value, checked: true } }` when the option is chosen. A radio never reports being unchecked. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the radio gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the radio loses focus. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Called with the click event on the radio button. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the radio and its label. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

**`appearance`** — `plain` · `card` · `soft` · `tile`
