# RadioGroup

RadioGroup — one question and its radio answers. A `Fieldset` (legend plus grouped fields) holding one real Base UI `RadioGroup`, which carries the `role="radiogroup"`, the keyboard roving tabindex across options, and `aria-required`/`aria-readonly`; the Fieldset stays plain grouping and the legend, which the group inherits as its own accessible name. Lays them out stacked or inline, can put scale ends either side (`leadingText`, `trailingText` — see the "Linear scale" story), and shows one error for the group. `isDisabled` on the group overrides every `Radio`'s own. The value is the chosen option's value, or `null`/`undefined` while unanswered — a radio group does not fall back to its first option, so a response of `1` can be told apart from no response.

Also asked as: single choice, radio buttons, single select, multiple choice, radio list.

**Import:** `import { RadioGroup } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.stories.jsx` — Overview, Keyboard, Orientation, Size, LinearScale, Descriptions, Reveal, States, Validation, TwoGroupsWithoutIds, Interactive, Soft, Tiles, TileRest, TileHovered, TileSelected, TileFocused, TileInvalid, TileReadOnly, TileDisabled, SoftRest, SoftHovered, SoftPressed, SoftSelected, SoftSelectedHovered, SoftFocused, SoftInvalid, SoftInvalidSelected, SoftReadOnly, SoftDisabled, SoftMixedFlow, Unanswered, Selected, Hovered, Focused, Required, Invalid, ReadOnly, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RadioGroup/RadioGroup.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `RadioGroup` for one question with mutually exclusive answers visible all at once: a handful of options someone picks by scanning, not searching. The group owns the `legend`, the `value` and a single group `error` on `Fieldset`.

## Motion

RadioGroup reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Mark and fill change color. |

## Alternatives

- For a question where several answers may be chosen, use `CheckboxGroup`.
- For a list of six or more options, use `Select`.
- For asking the same radio question across multiple rows, use `ChoiceGrid`.
- For a single radio placed in a custom layout such as a table, use `Radio`.

## Best practices

### Mark the minority selection type in a flow of choice questions. {#mark-the-minority-selection-type-in-a-flow-of-choice-questions}

In a flow of choice questions (onboarding, quizzes, check-ins, surveys), pick one default selection type for the flow: the majority type uses `appearance="soft"` without a visible radio dot or checkbox box, while the minority type keeps its visible control (`card` or `plain`) so people notice when a question switches between single-select and multi-select, following the same exception-marking rule as required and optional fields on [Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs).

Do: Two single-select questions use soft rows without radio indicators; the one multi-select question keeps its visible checkboxes.
Don't: The two majority single-select questions keep their radio indicators while the minority multi-select question goes soft without checkboxes.

### Name the question with a group label. {#name-the-question-with-a-group-label}

The `legend` tells people what the options answer. A group with no visible
legend needs its own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`; the caller's wins over
the legend.

Do: The group has a visible question.
Don't: Options with no visible question.

### Stack three or more answers. {#stack-three-or-more-answers}

A stacked list scans faster than a row once options multiply. Keep `inline`
for short labels or a scale.

Do: A stacked list for several options.
Don't: A long row of options.

### Explain an error under the group. {#explain-an-error-under-the-group}

One message under the group says what went wrong and what to do; a bare error
state does not. Don't disable the group to block an answer instead: that hides
why and removes it from the tab order.

Do: The error is explained in one message.
Don't: The error state with no explanation.

### Leave the group unanswered until the person answers. {#leave-the-group-unanswered-until-the-person-answers}

`value` tells "answered zero" apart from "answered the first option." An unanswered group is `null` or `undefined` and never falls back to the first option. Check for that explicitly before treating the group as answered.

```jsx
<RadioGroup
    legend="How was the session?"
    leadingText="Not at all"
    trailingText="Very"
    options={['1', '2', '3', '4', '5']}
    value={rating}
    onChange={setRating}
/>
```

### Reserve choice tiles for one big question with two to four pictured options. {#reserve-choice-tiles-for-one-big-question-with-two-to-four-pictured-options}

Use `appearance="tile"` when a step asks one focal question with two to four options and every option carries an `illustration`. Keep ordinary form lists and sets of five or more options in `plain` or `card`.

Do: Two pictured options for one focal question.
Don't: An ordinary five-item list without illustrations drawn as tiles.

### Use `reveal` instead of a separate conditional field. {#use-reveal-instead-of-a-separate-conditional-field}

When choosing one option should show an extra field, such as "Other, please specify", pass that field as the option's `reveal` rather than rendering it outside the group. It stays scoped to the option that triggers it and disappears when another option is chosen.

## Accessibility

- **One real `radiogroup`, named by the legend.** The outer Fieldset supplies the `<fieldset>`/`<legend>` pair; the inner group repeats the legend's id as its own `aria-labelledby`, so assistive technology announces the question once, not twice.
- **Roving tabindex.** Tab enters and leaves the group as a single stop; arrow keys move the checked state between options, matching native radio button behavior.
- **A caller's own `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` wins over the legend**, for the rare case where the question is named another way.
- **One error, announced once.** `error` renders a single message tied to the group via `aria-describedby`, rather than repeating it per option.

## Related

- `CheckboxGroup`: use when any number of options may be chosen.
- `Radio`: use when placing individual radio controls in a custom layout.
- `Select`: use when choosing from six or more options.
- `Fieldset`: use when grouping mixed controls under a legend.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Legend.** The question. It names the group and carries an optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) in plain text.
2. **Options.** Radios in a stacked or inline set (`plain`, bordered `card`, `soft` without a visible dot, or pictured `tile`). Each has a label and an optional description.
3. **Scale ends.** Optional `leadingText` and `trailingText` either side of the options.
4. **Reveal.** Optional content under an option, shown only while that option is chosen.
5. **Error.** One message under the group, tied to it with `aria-describedby`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | As Radio; in `soft`, `--ds-background-neutral` fill with no edge and no radio dot. |
| Hovered | As Radio. Unselected: `--ds-background-input-hovered` with a `--ds-border-brand` edge (or `--ds-background-neutral-hovered` in `soft`). Selected: the hovered step of the selected bold fill (or `--ds-background-selected-hovered` in `soft`). |
| Selected | As Radio: `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill and `--ds-border-selected` edge; in `soft`, `--ds-background-selected` fill, 1px `--ds-border-selected` edge, and a trailing `fa-solid fa-check` icon in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own in plain/card; in `soft`, an unselected option steps to `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` and a selected option steps to `--ds-background-selected-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused` on the one tab stop (around the row in `soft` and `tile`). |
| Invalid | Unselected options take `--ds-border-danger` (and in `soft`, selected options do too), with one message for the group. |
| Read-only | Full contrast, focusable, no hover, `aria-readonly` on the group; unchecked radios take the `--ds-background-neutral` fill and the answer does not change. In `soft`, the selected row keeps `--ds-background-selected`, its `--ds-border-selected` edge and the trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`; unselected rows stay `--ds-background-neutral`, with no hover or pressed step and a default cursor. |
| Disabled | Every option takes the disabled fill and edge and leaves the tab order. In `soft`, every row takes `--ds-background-disabled` and a `--ds-border-disabled` edge; a selected row keeps its trailing check, in `--ds-icon-disabled`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Options gap | Stacked `--stack-md`; inline column gap `--radio-group-inline-gap`; tile gap `--inline-lg`. |
| Soft row | `--ds-background-neutral` fill at rest; selected `--ds-background-selected` fill, `--border-width-default` `--ds-border-selected` edge, and `--icon-sm` trailing check in `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Choice tile width | `--choice-tile-width` (224px), inline and wrapping. |
| Radio size | `--radio-control-size`, or `--radio-control-size-10` and `-14` through `size`. |
| Scale ends | `--ds-text`, body default; gap `--radio-group-inline-gap`. |
| Reveal indent | The radio width plus `--stack-md`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write the legend as the question: "Did the session happen?" | A label for the field: "Session status". |
| Keep option labels short, parallel and in sentence case. | Mix one word with a full clause, or end labels with periods. |
| Order options from most to least likely, or from least to most risk. | Alphabetical order. |
| Label the ends of a scale: "Not at all" and "Very". | Leave a 1 to 5 scale unlabeled. |
| Say what to do in the error: "Choose an answer." | "Required" or "Invalid". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Base for every id in the group. Generated when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | The form key the choices submit under. Defaults to the group's id. |
| `legend` | node | — | The question. Names the group. |
| `orientation` | enum | `'stacked'` | `stacked` (default) puts one option per line; `inline` lays them in a row, for short labels or a scale. |
| `options` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | The answers. A string is its own value and label. An object can add a `description` under the label, a decorative `illustration` (for `tile`), `isDisabled`, an `id`, and `reveal`: content shown under the option while it is chosen. |
| `value` | optionValueType | — | The answer: one option value, or `null`/`undefined` while unanswered. |
| `defaultValue` | optionValueType | — | The option value chosen at the start, when the group is uncontrolled. Leave it out for no answer. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Receives the next answer's value. |
| `leadingText` | node | — | Scale end before the options, e.g. "Not at all". Describes the group. |
| `trailingText` | node | — | Scale end after the options, e.g. "Very". Describes the group. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'plain'` | Passed to every Radio. `card` draws each as a bordered row; `soft` draws each as a neutral row without a radio dot; `tile` draws centered pictured tiles. |
| `size` | enum | — | Radio control (dot) width, in px; unset keeps today's rendering. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the legend: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the radiogroup. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Overrides every Radio's own `isDisabled`. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shown and focusable, not changeable. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | — | Marks every Radio as failing validation. Defaults to whether `error` is set. |
| `error` | node | — | One error for the group, announced when it appears. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the fieldset beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the fieldset. |

## Variants

**`orientation`** — `stacked` · `inline`

**`appearance`** — `plain` · `card` · `soft` · `tile`

**`size`** — `10` · `12` · `14`

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--body-default` · `--ds-text` · `--inline-lg` · `--radio-control-size` · `--radio-control-size-10` · `--radio-control-size-14` · `--radio-group-inline-gap` · `--stack-md`

# Range

Range — slider over a numeric span. A range input carries its value, never its meaning: "49" says nothing about what is being set. `label` is the only thing that names it, so it takes the same pair as `Input` — `label` for the text, `showLabel={false}` to hide that text without taking the name away (#213). Built on Base UI's Slider, wrapped in `FieldFrame` (A7) for the disabled fade. Base UI's Slider has no DOM-query label lookup the way Checkbox and Radio do — `Slider.Thumb`'s accessible name only ever comes from an explicit `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` or an ambient `Field.Label` registration — so the label here points at the thumb directly via `aria-labelledby` on `Slider.Root`, which `Slider.Root` forwards to every `Slider.Thumb` beneath it.

Also asked as: slider, range slider.

**Import:** `import { Range } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Range/Range.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Range/Range.stories.jsx` — Overview, Labels, Positions, Disabled, Interactive, Size, ReportsNumber, Aria, Keyboard, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, DisabledState

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Range/Range.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `linear`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Range` when an approximate value between a minimum and maximum is enough, such as a zoom level or volume. Avoid it for exact numbers, non-numeric choices, or spans under four steps or over a hundred steps.

## Motion

Range reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-linear` | The thumb follows the pointer; on release it settles on a spring that starts from the hand's speed. |

## Alternatives

- For an exact numeric value, use `TextField` with `type="number"`.
- For a five-point satisfaction score, use `Rating`.
- For a choice among a few discrete options, use `RadioGroup` or `Select`.

## Best practices

### Use the default `size={12}` in standard forms. {#use-the-default-size-12-in-standard-forms}

The `size={12}` handle and track are easy to read and grab in a standard form.

Do: Standard `size={12}` in a form.
Don't: Compact `size={8}` used for a primary input.

### Use one size per form. {#use-one-size-per-form}

Matching sizes keep several ranges aligned.

Do: Every range in the form uses `size={12}`.
Don't: Mixing `size={12}` and `size={8}` in the same form.

### Use `size={16}` for touch. {#use-size-16-for-touch}

A thicker track gives touch screens a larger target.

Do: Larger `size={16}` where touch is the main input.
Don't: Small `size={8}` on a touch screen.

### Put the label directly above the slider. {#put-the-label-directly-above-the-slider}

Keep it short and aligned left. Show it unless the layout already names the slider.

Do: The label sits above the slider and names it.
Don't: The label is hidden, so nothing on screen names the slider.

### Read the numeric value from the first argument of `onChange`. {#read-the-numeric-value-from-the-first-argument-of-onchange}

`onChange(value, event)` passes the new number first and the event second; a handler that wrote `event.target.value` reads the second argument instead.

### In a left-to-right layout the lowest value is on the left. {#in-a-left-to-right-layout-the-lowest-value-is-on-the-left}

In a right-to-left layout it is on the right.

### Use helper text to explain how. {#use-helper-text-to-explain-how}

If the slider needs explaining, put one line of helper text under it rather than a longer label.

## Accessibility

- **Label every slider.** `label` names the input; `showLabel={false}` visually hides the text while keeping the accessible name.
- **Keyboard.** Arrow keys step by `step`; `Home` and `End` jump to `min` and `max`. Focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the handle; pointer focus draws none.
- **Do not use a range where precision matters.** Offer a text field beside it, or use one instead.

## Related

- `TextField`: use when an exact numeric value is needed (`type="number"`).
- `Rating`: use when collecting a score out of five.
- `RadioGroup`: use when choosing among a few discrete options.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Label.** 14/20 text directly above the slider, aligned left. It names the slider.
2. **Track.** A 4 line showing the span (6 or 8 with `size` 12 or 16). It fills with the selected bold fill from the start to the handle.
3. **Handle.** A 20 circle, or 8, 12 or 16 when `size` is set, that the person moves along the track to change the value.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The track fills with `--ds-background-selected-bold` from the start to the handle. |
| Hovered | The handle takes `--ds-background-selected-bold-hovered`. |
| Pressed | While the handle is dragged it reads the same as hovered. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the handle, for keyboard focus only. |
| Disabled | Track and fill take `--ds-background-disabled`; the handle takes `--ds-icon-disabled` with no shadow. Out of the tab order. |
| Invalid, read-only | Not drawn. A range always holds a value, so there is nothing to mark invalid. |

### Tokens

### Use the default `size={12}` in standard forms.

The `size={12}` handle and track are easy to read and grab in a standard form.

Do: Standard `size={12}` in a form.
Don't: Compact `size={8}` used for a primary input.

### Use one size per form.

Matching sizes keep several ranges aligned.

Do: Every range in the form uses `size={12}`.
Don't: Mixing `size={12}` and `size={8}` in the same form.

### Use `size={16}` for touch.

A thicker track gives touch screens a larger target.

Do: Larger `size={16}` where touch is the main input.
Don't: Small `size={8}` on a touch screen.

### Put the label directly above the slider.

Keep it short and aligned left. Show it unless the layout already names the slider.

Do: The label sits above the slider and names it.
Don't: The label is hidden, so nothing on screen names the slider.

### Read the numeric value from the first argument of `onChange`.

`onChange(value, event)` passes the new number first and the event second; a handler that wrote `event.target.value` reads the second argument instead.

### In a left-to-right layout the lowest value is on the left.

In a right-to-left layout it is on the right.

### Use helper text to explain how.

If the slider needs explaining, put one line of helper text under it rather than a longer label.

# Rating

Rating component with 5 stars, supporting two types: 1. With "Comments" label below 2. With numeric labels (1-5) above each star

Also asked as: stars, score.

**Import:** `import { Rating } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.stories.jsx` — Overview, Content, Variants, InteractionStates, Interactive, PropsRender, Unrated, Rated, Hovered, Pressed, SelectedHovered, SelectedPressed, Focused, Disabled, UnratedNumeric, RatedNumeric, HoveredNumeric, PressedNumeric, SelectedHoveredNumeric, SelectedPressedNumeric, FocusedNumeric, DisabledNumeric, RatedThumbsUp, Required

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Rating/Rating.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Rating` for a five-point satisfaction score given in one gesture, such as end-of-session feedback. Five items is the whole scale; there is no other length. `type` is `comments` (one caption below the row) or `numeric` (1 to 5 above each item); `icon` is `star` or `thumbs-up`.

## Motion

Rating reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Stars fill with the brand selected color, staggered 20 ms. |

## Alternatives

- For a continuous or wider numeric span, use `Range`.
- For a labeled Likert scale or mutually exclusive options, use `RadioGroup`.
- For the written feedback that accompanies a score, use `TextArea`.

## Best practices

### Use stars for quality and thumbs for approval. {#use-stars-for-quality-and-thumbs-for-approval}

Match the icon to the question.

Do: Stars rate the quality of a session.
Don't: Thumbs on a graded five-point scale.

### Start empty for new input. {#start-empty-for-new-input}

A pre-filled rating biases the answer.

Do: No rating yet, so the person gives their own.
Don't: Four stars filled before the person has rated.

### Show a given rating as disabled. {#show-a-given-rating-as-disabled}

A rating that cannot change reads as a result.

Do: A recorded rating, disabled.
Don't: A recorded rating that still looks editable.

### It is always controlled. {#it-is-always-controlled}

```jsx
// Incorrect: the component holds no state. Without an onChange the items are
// clickable and nothing ever changes.
<Rating label="How was the session?" />

// Correct: onChange receives the number, not an event.
<Rating label="How was the session?" value={score} onChange={setScore} />
```

### It submits its value under `name`. {#it-submits-its-value-under-name}

A hidden input carries the score with its form, so `name` is how a server reads it.

```jsx
<form onSubmit={submit}>
    <Rating name="score" label="Rating" value={score} onChange={setScore} />
</form>
```

### Give it a `label`. {#give-it-a-label}

Do: A label names the row, so a page with two ratings tells them apart.
Don't: Without a label the row falls back to the generic name "Rating". `commentsLabel` is a caption, not a substitute.

## Accessibility

- **It is one value out of five, and says so.** The row is a `radiogroup` and each item is a `radio` carrying `aria-checked` and an `aria-label` of "Rate 1" through "Rate 5". The chosen value is in the accessibility tree, not only in the fill color.
- **One tab stop, arrow keys within it.** Tab reaches the group once, landing on the checked item, or the first when nothing is checked; Left/Right, Up/Down, Home and End move the value. Enter and Space still activate an item directly.
- **Moving the selection is changing it.** An arrow key calls `onChange`, so a keyboard user cannot browse the scale without setting it. That is the usual radio-group behavior.
- **Disabled stays announced.** The items keep their role, label and `aria-checked` and take `aria-disabled`, and drop out of the tab order.
- **The label is a `span`, deliberately.** There is no form control for a `label` element to point at, so the label has an id and the row is named by `aria-labelledby`.
- **`isRequired` sets `aria-required` on the radiogroup.** Pair it with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

## Related

- `Range`: use when choosing an approximate value along a continuous track.
- `RadioGroup`: use when choosing among labeled options or a custom linear scale.
- `TextArea`: use when collecting a written comment alongside the rating.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Label.** Text above the row that names the rating. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text.
2. **Items.** Five 32 circles, each drawing a 16 icon. Items up to the score are filled.
3. **Number.** In the numeric type, 1 to 5 above each item.
4. **Caption.** In the comments type, one line under the row.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-neutral` circle with the icon outlined in `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Hovered | The item takes `--ds-background-neutral-hovered`; a selected item takes `--ds-background-selected-bold-hovered`. |
| Pressed | The item takes `--ds-background-neutral-pressed`; a selected item takes `--ds-background-selected-bold-pressed`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the item, for keyboard focus only. |
| Selected | Every item up to the score takes a `--ds-background-selected-bold` fill with a filled icon in `--ds-icon-inverse`. Unselected items stay on the neutral circle with an outlined `--ds-icon-subtle` icon. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` fill and `--ds-icon-disabled` icon. Out of the tab order, still announced. |
| Invalid, read-only | Not drawn. Validate the answer in the form and explain the error beside the rating. |

The selected fill is the bold brand step because an item is a small filled control, the same ground Checkbox, Radio, Toggle, Range and Select draw when checked. The soft tint is for larger choice surfaces.

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Item | `--control-md` (32) circle on `--ds-background-neutral`; `--ds-background-selected-bold` when selected. |
| Icon | `--icon-md` (16). |
| Gaps | `--rating-gap` between items; `--stack-sm` inside an item group; `--stack-md` between label and row, plus `--stack-sm` under the label. |
| Label, minority marker, number | `--ds-text`, body default. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name what is rated, as a question: "How was the session?" | "Rating" alone, or an instruction: "Click a star." |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation except a question mark. | Title case. |
| Keep the comments caption to one short line. | A paragraph under the row. |
| Pair the rating with a comment box when you need the reason. | Ask for the reason in the label. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the star group, which the label names. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Form key under which the chosen rating is sent with its form. |
| `label` | node | — | Visible label above the stars. It names the group; without one the group is named "Rating". |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Marks the radiogroup required (`aria-required`). Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `value` | number | `0` | Current rating, 0 for none up to 5. Every star up to it is filled. Update it from `onChange`. |
| `type` | enum | `'comments'` | `comments` (default) shows the icons alone, with an optional comments label under them; `numeric` prints each number above its icon. |
| `showCommentsLabel` | bool | `true` | Shows `commentsLabel` under the stars. Applies to the `comments` type only. |
| `commentsLabel` | node | `'Comments'` | Text under the stars in the `comments` type. Defaults to "Comments". |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables every icon so no rating can be picked. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with the new rating (1 to 5) when the user picks a different star. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the wrapper around the label and stars. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the wrapper around the label and stars. |
| `icon` | enum | `'star'` | The glyph used for every choice: `star` (default) or `thumbs-up`. |

## Variants

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

**`type`** — `comments` · `numeric`

**`icon`** — `star` · `thumbs-up`

# RichTextEditor RichTextEditor: a text field with a formatting toolbar, for where the formatting is part of the meaning. **Import:** `import { RichTextEditor } from '@/components';` **Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.jsx` **Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.stories.jsx` — Overview, Interactive, BlockStyleMenu, Empty, Filled, BoxRadius, Focused, ReadOnly, DisabledState, Compact, FullToolbar, ToolbarButtonHovered, ToolbarButtonPressed **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.mdx` ## Usage Use `RichTextEditor` when formatting such as emphasis, lists or links is part of the content's meaning. `toolbarPreset` is `compact` or `full` (or pass `toolbarButtons` by name, which implies the full toolbar); `value` and `onChange` are HTML strings. Giving it a `name` also renders a hidden input, so the HTML posts with a plain form. ## Alternatives - For plain multi-line text with no formatting toolbar, use `TextArea`. - For single-line text, use `TextField`. - For a threaded discussion entry with an author and timestamp, use `Comment`. ## Best practices ### Use the compact toolbar for short notes. {#use-the-compact-toolbar-for-short-notes} Fewer tools keep a short field light. Do: The compact toolbar on a short note. Don't: The full toolbar on a short note. ### Use the full toolbar for long content. {#use-the-full-toolbar-for-long-content} Long-form writing needs the full set of tools. Do: The full toolbar for a long summary. Don't: Long-form writing limited to the compact toolbar. ### Use read-only for content people read. {#use-read-only-for-content-people-read} Set `isReadOnly` on content people need to read: it stays in the tab order at full contrast, so it can be selected and copied. Keep `isDisabled` for an editor that is unavailable; it steps down and leaves the tab order. ### Use the placeholder for a hint. {#use-the-placeholder-for-a-hint} Do: The placeholder hints at what to write. Don't: The placeholder repeats the label. ### `value` is written to the DOM as HTML. {#value-is-written-to-the-dom-as-html} ```jsx // Incorrect: the value is assigned to the editable region's innerHTML, so // anything a user can influence is executed as markup. // Correct: sanitize on the way in, and again on the way out before storing. setBody(sanitize(html))} /> ``` The same applies to what you receive: `onChange` hands you whatever the browser produced, which is markup from a paste as much as from the toolbar. ### It is built on a deprecated browser API. {#it-is-built-on-a-deprecated-browser-api} Formatting runs through `document.execCommand`, which every engine now documents as deprecated. It works today and its exact output differs between browsers: one may wrap a line in `
`, another in `

`. Do not depend on the shape of the HTML; store it and render it, or convert it once on save. ### Link and image ask with a browser prompt. {#link-and-image-ask-with-a-browser-prompt} Pressing those buttons opens the platform `prompt()` dialog for a URL. It is unstyled, it is not translatable, and some environments suppress it. Where that matters, leave those two buttons out of `toolbarButtons`. ### Label the editor. {#label-the-editor} Do: A label names the editor on screen and for assistive technology. Don't: No label, only a placeholder, which disappears as soon as someone types. ## Accessibility - **The editable region announces itself as a multi-line textbox.** `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline`, and `aria-readonly` while it is read-only and `aria-disabled` while it is disabled. - **`label` names it, and is effectively required.** The prop renders a `span` above the editor and the region points at it with `aria-labelledby`. A `label` element cannot be used, because `contentEditable` is not a form control for `htmlFor` to bind to. Without a `label` the region is a named role with no name, which a screen-reader user hears as nothing. - **The toolbar buttons are named.** Each carries an `aria-label` from its definition, and the bold, italic and underline set is a `role="group"` labeled "Bold, italic, and underline". Their pressed state is tracked internally and is not exposed as `aria-pressed`. - **The placeholder is CSS.** It is drawn from a `data-placeholder` attribute, so it is not part of the accessible name and may not be announced at all. - **Keep the formatting optional.** Anything that only exists as bold text or a color in the body is invisible to someone hearing the page. Structure it with lists and headings instead. ## Related - `TextArea`: use when plain multi-line text is enough. - `TextField`: use when collecting a single line of text. - To display formatted content the user cannot edit, render the HTML yourself after sanitizing it. - `Comment`: use when displaying a formatted note in a discussion thread. Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect` ## Parts 1. **Label.** Text above the box that names it. 2. **Box.** One edge around the toolbar and the writing area together. 3. **Toolbar.** Flat formatting buttons along the top of the box: block style, bold, italic, underline, lists, link and more. A keyline separates it from the writing area. 4. **Writing area.** The editable region, with a placeholder at the start of its first line while it is empty. ### States | State | What changes | | --- | --- | | Rest | A `--ds-background-input` box inside one `--ds-border-input` edge. | | Hovered | Toolbar buttons take `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. The writing area has no hover step. | | Pressed | Toolbar buttons take `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. | | Active format | The button takes `--ds-background-selected` with `--ds-text-selected` and `--ds-icon-selected`. | | Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused` wraps the box while the writing area has focus. | | Read-only | `--ds-background-neutral` box, `--ds-text` text at full contrast, the writing area in the tab order, toolbar faded and inert. | | Disabled | `--ds-background-neutral` box and `--ds-text-subtle` text, the writing area out of the tab order, and the toolbar faded to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and inert. | | Invalid | Not drawn. Mark the surrounding field and explain the error beside it. | ### Tokens | Part | Token | | --- | --- | | Fill, edge | `--ds-background-input`; `--ds-border-input` at `--border-width-default`; corner `--radius-control-lg`, the same as the 40-high fields. | | Toolbar | Subtle icon buttons; # ScrollBar

ScrollBar — a wrapper that applies the Design System's tokenized custom scrollbar styling (thin width, border-colored thumb, transparent track) to its scrollable content.

**Import:** `import { ScrollBar } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/ScrollBar/ScrollBar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/ScrollBar/ScrollBar.stories.jsx` — Overview, Layout, Content, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/ScrollBar/ScrollBar.mdx`

## Usage

Use `ScrollBar` when a region has to scroll inside a page that does not — a long
list in a fixed panel, a wide table in a narrow column. It caps the height,
turns on overflow, and applies the design system's thin scrollbar so the region
does not draw the platform's default one.

`maxHeight` (default twice `--size-1000`) caps a vertical region. `horizontal`
switches the axis, and in that mode `maxHeight` is ignored — the width comes
from the container.

## Alternatives

- For a long list that should page rather than scroll, use `Pagination`.
- For content the user opens rather than scrolls past, use `Accordion`.

## Best practices

### Use one scrollbar per region. {#use-one-scrollbar-per-region}

Two bars side by side suggest two scrolling areas where there is one. Do not nest one region inside another on the same axis.

Do: A single scrollbar.
Don't: A region nested in another: two scrollbars on one region.

### Keep the track thin. {#keep-the-track-thin}

The scrollbar stays at its natural width; stretching it competes with the content. It has no width prop, so leave its styling as shipped.

### Wrap only content that overflows. {#wrap-only-content-that-overflows}

A region around content that already fits shows no bar and still adds a tab stop with nothing to scroll.

Do: A region around a list that overflows.
Don't: A region around two short items.

### Use `maxHeight` to cap height, not to fill a taller container. {#use-maxheight-to-cap-height-not-to-fill-a-taller-container}

`maxHeight` is a cap. In a taller container, give the region the height you want it to take, such as `maxHeight="100%"`.

Do: The region fills its container and scrolls.
Don't: A smaller cap leaves the space below it empty.

### Name each region. {#name-each-region}

```jsx
// Incorrect — two scroll regions on a page, both announced as the default "Scrollable content".
<ScrollBar><SessionList /></ScrollBar>
<ScrollBar><NoteList /></ScrollBar>

// Correct.
<ScrollBar aria-label="Sessions"><SessionList /></ScrollBar>
<ScrollBar aria-label="Notes"><NoteList /></ScrollBar>
```

### Scroll on one axis, not both. {#scroll-on-one-axis-not-both}

`horizontal` chooses which axis is styled and which cap applies. A table that
needs horizontal scroll inside a page that scrolls vertically uses one axis on
each container.

## Accessibility

- **The region is focusable on purpose.** `tabIndex={0}` lets a keyboard user
  scroll it with the arrow keys and satisfies the scrollable-region-focusable
  rule.
- **Give multiple regions distinct names.** `aria-label` defaults to
  "Scrollable content". When a page has more than one scroll region, name each
  for what it holds.
- **Not a landmark.** It omits `role="region"` so multiple scroll areas on a
  page do not collide as landmarks; `aria-label` names the tab stop directly.
- **Do not hide the last row.** A scroll region whose content ends exactly at the
  cap looks finished. Leave the cut visible so the reader knows more content sits
  below.

## Related

- `StaticTable`: use when wrapping a wide table in a horizontal `ScrollBar` rather than shrinking its columns.
- `Panel`: use when scrolling body content inside `PanelBody`.

Same group: `Accordion` · `Carousel` · `PageHeader`

## Parts

1. **Region.** The wrapper that caps the height and scrolls.
2. **Track.** Transparent, so it never reads as a second edge.
3. **Thumb.** The border-colored bar, darker under the pointer.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A thin thumb in the border color on a transparent track. |
| Hovered | The thumb takes the bold border color. |
| Pressed | No pressed layer. |
| Focused | The region takes focus from Tab, named by `aria-label`. |
| Disabled | A scroll region has no disabled state. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Thumb | `--ds-border`; `--ds-border-bold` on hover. |
| Track and corner | Transparent. |
| Width | `--space-0375`. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`. |
| Height cap | twice `--size-1000` by default. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the region for what is in it: "Session notes". | Leave the region unnamed. |
| Give a horizontal region a width its content cannot fit. | Wrap content that already fits. |
| Keep the label short and specific. | Start it with "Scrollable". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | — |
| `maxHeight` | string or number | `'var(--scroll-bar-max-height)'` | Maximum height before vertical scrolling begins (e.g., "240px") |
| `horizontal` | bool | `false` | Scroll horizontally instead of vertically |
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `aria-label` | string | — | Names the scrollable region for assistive technology. Defaults to `Scrollable content`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

## Tokens touched

`--ds-border` · `--ds-border-bold` · `--radius-md` · `--scroll-bar-size`

From `design-system/src/components/layout-and-structure/ScrollBar/ScrollBar.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Names the scope ("Search students"). Required: the label is hidden, so this is what a sighted person reads, and it names the collapsed icon and its tooltip.

props.description: The accessible name, when it should differ from the placeholder.

props.name: mode
props.description: `active` filters on each keystroke through `onValueChange`. `basic` runs `onSearch` on Enter and nothing per keystroke. `focused` adds the results panel.

props.name: value
props.description: The search text, when the caller holds it. Pair with `onValueChange`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting text when the field holds its own.

props.description: `(text)`: called on every edit, on Esc and on the clear button.

props.description: `(text, { offset, limit, scope })` → `Promise<{ results, total }>`. Asked on first render (so `onResults` fires without typing) and after a short pause in typing; an older answer never replaces a newer one. `scope` is sent when `scopes` is set.

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# SearchField

Search field: find a record by typing. It is a TextField with a search icon before the text and a clear button after it, and its label is hidden: the placeholder names the scope ("Search students"). `mode="active"` reports the text on every keystroke through `onValueChange`. Hold the rows yourself and filter them (sync), or give `loadResults` for a list on a server (async): it is asked after a short pause, and what it returns goes to `onResults`. Results show in the results area, never under the field. While results load, a Spinner takes the search icon's place. `isCollapsible` starts as an icon button that grows into the field and collapses when left empty. Esc clears the text; a second Esc closes the field and returns focus to the icon. `scopes` puts a scope filter before the field, with "All" first and selected. `mode="basic"` runs `onSearch(text)` on Enter and does no work per keystroke. `mode="focused"` opens a panel (a Popup) under the field. On focus with no text it lists `recent` searches; while typing it lists matches grouped by type, then a last "See all" row that acts as a basic search. Arrow keys move through the rows, Enter chooses, Esc closes the panel. A `SearchFieldAction` child is the optional last row.

**Import:** `import { SearchField } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.; Search (`ds guide search`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SearchField/SearchField.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SearchField/SearchField.stories.jsx` — Overview, Active, Spacing, Filled, ButtonInside, Disabled, Loading, Async, Collapsible, Scopes, CollapsibleScopes, Basic, Focused, FocusedKeyboard, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SearchField/SearchField.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `SearchField` to find a record by typing. Matches appear in the table or list being searched, never under the field (except in `focused` mode): the count sits in that header, and the no-matches message in its body.

Pick the mode by where the answer lands:

- `active` (default): filters rows as you type through `onValueChange`.
- `basic`: runs on Enter through `onSearch`, for searches too heavy to run on every keystroke.
- `focused`: opens a panel under the field for jumping straight to a record from anywhere (`recent` searches on focus, matches grouped by type while typing, a "See all" row, and an optional `SearchFieldAction` child).

`isCollapsible` starts the field as an icon button (`defaultOpen` starts it open). Default strings can be overridden via `clearLabel` ("Clear search"), `panelLabel` ("Suggestions"), `recentLabel` ("Recent searches"), `noMatchesLabel` ("No matches for") and `seeAllLabel` ("See all results for").

## Motion

SearchField reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A collapsed search grows from its icon into the field, end edge fixed, so it opens to the left; focus moves in. The focused mode's panel is a Popup and takes the Popup row's open and close. |
| exit | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Left empty, the field narrows back into the icon and fades; Esc twice does the same. |

## Alternatives

- For picking a value from a known option list, use `Select`.
- For narrowing a list by a category in a view bar, use `FilterButton`, `PopupSelect` or `FilterMenu`.
- For general single-line text entry in a form, use `TextField`.

## Best practices

### Name the scope in the placeholder. {#name-the-scope-in-the-placeholder}

Do: The placeholder says what is searched.
Don't: A bare verb leaves the scope unsaid, and the label is hidden.

### Pass compact in a bar. {#pass-compact-in-a-bar}

A view bar holds 32-high controls, so pass `spacing="compact"`.

### Collapse only where the bar is tight. {#collapse-only-where-the-bar-is-tight}

Use `isCollapsible` when the bar keeps quiet until search is needed. Elsewhere
leave the field open.

## Accessibility

- **The hidden label still names the field.** The accessible name is the placeholder, or `label` when given.
- **The collapsed icon button is named** by the same words, and its tooltip shows them.
- **The scope filter has its own name**, "Search scope" unless `scopeLabel` says otherwise.
- **In `focused` the input is the combobox.** Focus stays in it and the highlighted row is its `aria-activedescendant`; the panel is a named listbox.
- **Loading is announced** through the spinner's status text.

## Related

- `Select`: use when picking a value from a list of options.
- `FilterButton`: use when narrowing a list by a category in a filter bar.
- `TextField`: use when collecting single-line text in a form.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Scope filter** (optional). A compact select before the field, with All first and selected.
2. **Field.** A text field, 40 at default spacing and 32 at compact.
3. **Search icon.** Before the text; a spinner takes its place while results load.
4. **Clear button.** After the text once it holds any.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Collapsed | An icon button named by the placeholder, with a tooltip. Only with `isCollapsible`. |
| Rest | The placeholder shows. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, for keyboard focus only. |
| Filled | The clear button appears after the text. |
| Loading | A spinner replaces the search icon. |
| Disabled | The disabled fill and text: a change of color, not of opacity. |

### Keyboard

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Esc | Clears the text. When already empty and starting as an icon, closes the field and returns focus to the icon. |
| Enter | In `basic`, runs `onSearch`. In `focused`, chooses the row under the cursor, or runs `onSearch` when none is. |
| Arrow down and up | In `focused`, move through the panel's rows and wrap. Inside the scope list, move and choose. |
| Esc in the panel | Closes the panel and keeps the text. The next Esc clears. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Field | Those of the text field. |
| Gap between scope and field | `--inline-sm`. |
| Width open | `--field-width-md`. |
| Collapsed width and height | `--control-md`. |
| Panel maximum height | `--dropdown-menu-max-height`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Start with a verb and name the scope: "Search students". | "Search…" or "Type here". |
| Use sentence case. | Title case: "Search Students". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `placeholder` | string (required) | — | Names the scope ("Search students"). Required: the label is hidden, so this is what a sighted person reads, and it names the collapsed icon and its tooltip. |
| `label` | string | — | The accessible name, when it should differ from the placeholder. |
| `mode` | enum | `'active'` | `active` filters on each keystroke through `onValueChange`. `basic` runs `onSearch` on Enter and nothing per keystroke. `focused` adds the results panel. |
| `value` | string | — | The search text, when the caller holds it. Pair with `onValueChange`. |
| `defaultValue` | string | `''` | Starting text when the field holds its own. |
| `onValueChange` | func | — | `(text)`: called on every edit, on Esc and on the clear button. |

rankedText.usage:
Use `SearchField` to find a record by typing. Matches appear in the table or list being searched, never under the field (except in `focused` mode): the count sits in that header, and the no-matches message in its body.

Pick the mode by where the answer lands:

- `active` (default): filters rows as you type through `onValueChange`.
- `basic`: runs on Enter through `onSearch`, for searches too heavy to run on every keystroke.
- `focused`: opens a panel under the field for jumping straight to a record from anywhere (`recent` searches on focus, matches grouped by type while typing, a "See all" row, and an optional `SearchFieldAction` child).

`isCollapsible` starts the field as an icon button (`defaultOpen` starts it open). Default strings can be overridden via `clearLabel` ("Clear search"), `panelLabel` ("Suggestions"), `recentLabel` ("Recent searches"), `noMatchesLabel` ("No matches for") and `seeAllLabel` ("See all results for").

# Section

Section: a span of the page grid under one heading, with its title row, views, search and filters.

Also asked as: page section, section header, block, region.

**Import:** `import { Section } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Frame (`ds guide frame`); Page (`ds guide page`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.; Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); +6 more

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Section/Section.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Section/Section.stories.jsx` — Overview, HeaderDefault, HeaderCustom, LayoutSingle, LayoutSplit, LayoutSubsections, SunkenCard, DetailIsSunkenCard, CardNesting, NoSurfaceNoPad, Footer, Anatomy, Levels, SearchInHeader, LoadingDefault, LoadingSearchAndFilters, LoadingViews, Interactive, ColorModes, SplitLayout, Spacing, Detail, TypeList, TypeQueue, TypeCards, TypeStats, TypeDetails, TypeMainAndSide, TypeForm, TypeSubsections, Full, FiltersApplied, NoViews, ViewsOnly, ManyFilters, WrappedFilters, RowsSelected, Narrow, Subsection, SideAtEnd, FilterSideAtStart, ResponsiveWidth, EmptyInTable, AnatomyQueue

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Section/Section.mdx`

**Motion:** view-bar `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast` · side-open `spatial.default` · side-close `spatial.default` · detail `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast` · body `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast` · footer `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Section` when content has a heading, shares actions, shows or hides as a unit, or takes its own span of the grid; otherwise the content belongs to the Section above it. The header is the Section's, not the Table's: the title row names it and carries its actions, and the header rows under it hold the views, then Search and the filters, so switching views can swap a table for cards while the rows stay put.

A Section takes no fill and no pad, and has five parts: header, body, side, detail and footer. The detail is an inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down.

## Motion

Section reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| view-bar | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Title row: nothing moves. The selected pill's fill and the format switch's indicator glide while the content swaps in place. Search and the Filter count grow to the left. |
| side-open | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The side opens and collapses as a section. Below 960 it hides with no animation. |
| side-close | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Collapses back the same way. Below 960 the side is gone in the same frame, with no animation. |
| detail | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. |
| body | Load content | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Content loads on arrival; add or remove, reorder and swap content as it changes. |
| footer | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Paging is Step. |

## Alternatives

- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.
- For a queue page or a quick look at a row from a table, use `Panel`.
- For the page's own title, use `PageHeader`; a Section stands under it.

## Best practices

### Make a Section only when it earns one. {#make-a-section-only-when-it-earns-one}

**Checked:** Review

A Section earns its own heading, its own actions or its own place in the grid. When its heading would repeat its only card's title, drop the Section and let the card stand on its own.

Do: A card with its own title stands on its own in the page.
Don't: A Section whose heading repeats its only card's title: two headings for one thing.

### Put the title row first and the header rows under it. {#put-the-title-row-first-and-the-header-rows-under-it}

**Checked:** Automatic

The title row sits `--section-stack-sm` above the header rows, and the header sits `--section-stack-md` above the body. The title, the first pill's label and the first column's text share one left edge. Actions that do not fit beside the heading drop under it, still at the end of the row. At every width the two stay separate rows. In a narrow Section the filters fold into one Filter button and the views scroll sideways.

Do: The title row first, the header rows under it, sharing one left edge.
Don't: The title pushed into the views row: the heading and the pills fight for the start, and the description has nowhere to go.

### Give each action one home: the title row. {#give-each-action-one-home-the-title-row}

**Checked:** Review

Actions sit at the end of the title row, More then the labeled Primary, whether or not the Section has views. The views row is for views and the format switch, the third for Search and filters, so an action there is a second home.

Do: The actions at the end of the title row, with the views under it.
Don't: Add students in the title row and again in the views row: one action, two homes.

### Keep views at the start as pills that hug their labels. {#keep-views-at-the-start-as-pills-that-hug-their-labels}

**Checked:** Review

Views are a fixed set the product defines, and one pill stays even with one view. The strip stays on one line and scrolls sideways when the pills do not fit. Under page tabs, the views become one labeled PopupSelect, so the page keeps one tab system.

### Order the header: actions, then views and format, then Search and filters. {#order-the-header-actions-then-views-and-format-then-search-and-filters}

**Checked:** Review

The title row ends with More, then the labeled Primary, which is last. The views row holds the views at the start and the format switch at the end. The filters row holds a compact `SearchField` (`spacing="compact"`, and `isCollapsible` where the row is tight), then the filter triggers; a trigger that opens a list takes a `menu`. More is an Icon button with a Tooltip. Fold extras into More.

Do: More and the labeled Primary in the title row; the format switch ends the views row; Search, then the filter, lead the filters row.
Don't: Five controls in no order, the Primary first, a second labeled button and a Filter icon in the title row: fold extras into More and give the filter its own row.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected. {#turn-the-head-row-into-the-bulk-bar-when-rows-are-selected}

**Checked:** Automatic

The part-ticked select-all, the count of selected rows, then the actions, all at the start. The checkboxes clear the selection, so the bar carries no Cancel. Selected rows take the selected fill and the header rows stay put. Only the Dynamic table selects rows.

### Drop the Filter icon while a filter side shows. {#drop-the-filter-icon-while-a-filter-side-shows}

**Checked:** Review

Each control has one home. The Filter button returns with its count once the side hides, below `SECTION_DETAIL_FLOOR`.

### Use a Section detail as an inline expand, never on a queue page. {#use-a-section-detail-as-an-inline-expand-never-on-a-queue-page}

**Checked:** Review

A **Section detail** is an inline expand: a row or card opens in place inside its Section and pushes the content below it down. It is never the detail view on a queue page — a queue page docks a `Panel` beside the list instead, and the record opens on demand.

### Keep the footer for paging and "View all". {#keep-the-footer-for-paging-and-view-all}

**Checked:** Review

Actions that commit changes belong in the card or form that holds the fields.

Do: The form card holds its own Save; the Section footer is for paging and "View all".
Don't: Cancel and Save in the Section footer, away from the fields they commit.

### Give a part a fill with a Card, not a Section. {#give-a-part-a-fill-with-a-card-not-a-section}

**Checked:** Review

A padded box with a fill is a Card. A Section takes no fill and no pad, so a part that stands apart from its neighbor, such as a detail, is a sunken Card.

### Nest a Section once at most. {#nest-a-section-once-at-most}

**Checked:** Review

A subsection is an h3. A Section that already has views holds subsections without them.

The table's empty state replaces the whole table, by the Empty pattern; elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading whose level follows nesting: h2 for a Section, h3 for a subsection. With a custom header the title stays in the page, hidden from sight.
- The pill views are a tablist; the selected tab says which rows the body shows. Views swap in place.
- Search, the filter triggers and More carry their names: "Search students", "Status: Upcoming", "More section actions". A trigger's selected state is announced as pressed.
- The table announces a selection politely, "2 selected", and the bulk bar's actions follow the select-all checkbox in the tab order.
- The detail is a collapsible region named by its title: the disclosure button toggles it with Enter or Space, and Escape inside the open detail closes it and returns focus to the button.

## Related

- Page: use when the heading is the page's own.
- Panel: use when a queue page docks the Panel beside the list, or for a quick look from a table.
- Popup: use when choosing the menu the labeled view trigger (`PopupSelect`) or a filter trigger opens.
- Table: use when the body is rows and columns.
- Filtering: use when picking a filter tier for the header.
- Patterns: use when the question is the search field's behavior (Search) or an empty body (Empty).

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Table`

## Types

Each Section type combines a header and body, with an optional side or detail. These are starting layouts of the same component.

- **List.** The views alone, one table, paging. The default for an area page.
- **Detail.** A list with a detail that opens an item in place.
- **Cards.** Title and actions, a grid of cards three across.
- **Stats.** A row of cards, each one number and its label, four at most.
- **Details.** Label and value pairs in two columns, with Edit in the title row.
- **Main and side.** A split with the side at the end and no fill: facts beside the main content.
- **Form.** Fields in a card, with the card's own Save and Cancel at its bottom.
- **Subsections.** Sections nested one level, each an h3, for a long settings page.

## Anatomy

A Section with its header rows, a detail and a footer. The title, the first pill and the first column share one left edge.

1. **Title row.** The h2, an optional one-line description, and the actions at the end: More and the labeled Primary.
2. **Header rows** (optional). Row 2 holds the pill views at the start and the format switch at the end. Row 3 holds Search, then the filter triggers.
3. **Body.** A Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. A Table's head row follows the header rows with nothing between.
4. **Detail** (optional). An inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel` beside the list.
5. **Footer** (optional). Paging or "View all".

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `description` · `actions` | The title row. |
| `views` · `format` · `search` · `filters` · `count` | Rows 2 and 3 of the header: pill Tabs and the format switch, then a compact Search and the "Field: value" triggers. A `filters` entry takes an optional `menu`, `(trigger) => node`, that wraps its trigger in a Popup select or a Filter menu. |
| `header` · `type` | With `type="custom"` the `header` slot replaces the title and description; `title` stays as the visually hidden heading. `type` is `default` or `custom`, and is read from the slots when left off. |
| `isLoading` | Swaps the header for skeleton bars while the Section loads. |
| `level` | `page` makes the Section the page header: an h1, and the Sections it holds are h2s. Left off, the title is one level below what holds it. |
| `named` | Makes the Section a region named by its title, for one that stands apart as a landmark. |
| `onClearAll` · `onMoreFilters` · `onOpenFilters` | Clear all, More filters, and the Filter button of a narrow Section. |
| `id` · `className` · `style` | Passed to the Section's root. |
| `spacing` | `compact`, `default` or `spacious`: the space between the header, the body and the footer. |
| `children` | The body: a Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. |
| `layout="split"` · `side` | A second column at the end, for a summary. |
| `sidePlacement` | Planned. `start` puts the side first, for a filter side or a step rail. |
| `detail` · `detailTitle` · `detailDescription` · `detailFooter` | An inline expand that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel`. |
| `detailOpen` · `defaultDetailOpen` · `onDetailOpenChange` | Open state of the inline detail expand. |
| `footer` | Paging or "View all". |

The bulk bar lives in the Dynamic table's head row, through its `bulkActions`, and the Section holds nothing for it: Dynamic table.

## Sizes

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--section-stack-sm` | Title row to header rows. |
| `--section-stack-md` | Header to body; body to footer. |
| `--section-stack-lg` | Between subsections. |
| `--section-min-width-main`, `--section-min-width-side` | The main and side columns of a split. |
| `--card-pad`, `--card-radius` | The detail, which is a sunken Card, on `--ds-surface-sunken`. |
| `--heading-md`, `--heading-sm` | A Section title and a subsection title. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Section with what it holds, in sentence case: "Upcoming sessions". | A title that repeats the only card inside it. |
| Keep the description to one line: "Lincoln Middle · 24 students". | A paragraph under the title. |
| Name views by the rows they show: "All students", "Needs follow-up". | Views of different things in one strip. |
| Name the scope in Search: "Search students". | A bare "Search". |

## Props

## Variants

**`layout`** — `single` · `split` · `subsections`

**`level`** — `page`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact` · `spacious`

rankedText.usage:
Use `Section` when content has a heading, shares actions, shows or hides as a unit, or takes its own span of the grid; otherwise the content belongs to the Section above it. The header is the Section's, not the Table's: the title row names it and carries its actions, and the header rows under it hold the views, then Search and the filters, so switching views can swap a table for cards while the rows stay put.

A Section takes no fill and no pad, and has five parts: header, body, side, detail and footer. The detail is an inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down.
rankedText.best:
### Make a Section only when it earns one.

A Section earns its own heading, its own actions or its own place in the grid. When its heading would repeat its only card's title, drop the Section and let the card stand on its own.

Do: A card with its own title stands on its own in the page.
Don't: A Section whose heading repeats its only card's title: two headings for one thing.

### Put the title row first and the header rows under it.

The title row sits `--section-stack-sm` above the header rows, and the header sits `--section-stack-md` above the body. The title, the first pill's label and the first column's text share one left edge. Actions that do not fit beside the heading drop under it, still at the end of the row. At every width the two stay separate rows. In a narrow Section the filters fold into one Filter button and the views scroll sideways.

Do: The title row first, the header rows under it, sharing one left edge.
Don't: The title pushed into the views row: the heading and the pills fight for the start, and the description has nowhere to go.

### Give each action one home: the title row.

Actions sit at the end of the title row, More then the labeled Primary, whether or not the Section has views. The views row is for views and the format switch, the third for Search and filters, so an action there is a second home.

Do: The actions at the end of the title row, with the views under it.
Don't: Add students in the title row and again in the views row: one action, two homes.

### Keep views at the start as pills that hug their labels.

Views are a fixed set the product defines, and one pill stays even with one view. The strip stays on one line and scrolls sideways when the pills do not fit. Under page tabs, the views become one labeled PopupSelect, so the page keeps one tab system.

### Order the header: actions, then views and format, then Search and filters.

The title row ends with More, then the labeled Primary, which is last. The views row holds the views at the start and the format switch at the end. The filters row holds a compact `SearchField` (`spacing="compact"`, and `isCollapsible` where the row is tight), then the filter triggers; a trigger that opens a list takes a `menu`. More is an Icon button with a Tooltip. Fold extras into More.

Do: More and the labeled Primary in the title row; the format switch ends the views row; Search, then the filter, lead the filters row.
Don't: Five controls in no order, the Primary first, a second labeled button and a Filter icon in the title row: fold extras into More and give the filter its own row.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected.

The part-ticked select-all, the count of selected rows, then the actions, all at the start. The checkboxes clear the selection, so the bar carries no Cancel. Selected rows take the selected fill and the header rows stay put. Only the Dynamic table selects rows.

### Drop the Filter icon while a filter side shows.

Each control has one home. The Filter button returns with its count once the side hides, below `SECTION_DETAIL_FLOOR`.

### Use a Section detail as an inline expand, never on a queue page.

A **Section detail** is an inline expand: a row or card opens in place inside its Section and pushes the content below it down. It is never the detail view on a queue page — a queue page docks a `Panel` beside the list instead, and the record opens on demand.

### Keep the footer for paging and "View all".

Actions that commit changes belong in the card or form that holds the fields.

Do: The form card holds its own Save; the Section footer is for paging and "View all".
Don't: Cancel and Save in the Section footer, away from the fields they commit.

### Give a part a fill with a Card, not a Section.

A padded box with a fill is a Card. A Section takes no fill and no pad, so a part that stands apart from its neighbor, such as a detail, is a sunken Card.

### Nest a Section once at most.

A subsection is an h3. A Section that already has views holds subsections without them.

The table's empty state replaces the whole table, by the Empty pattern; elevation and fills follow Elevation.

Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion. ## Usage Use `SectionMessage` for a message that belongs to the page and stays there until it is resolved or dismissed: why a session cannot be booked, a notice that a report is out of date, a confirmation that survives a scroll. It takes children, so the message can carry a link or emphasis, and up to two `actions` after the body. A section message always says something about state, so it has six styles and no others. Each style sets the ground to its role's background token and a default leading icon in the style's icon color. There is no border or side stripe: the fill and the icon carry the style. ### Appearance guidance | Appearance | When to use | Default icon | | --- | --- | --- | | Primary | The default, for a general message. | `circle-info` | | Secondary | A plain, neutral notice. | `circle-info` | | Success | Something went well. | `circle-check` | | Danger | Something failed and needs attention. | `circle-exclamation` | | Warning | A caution before something goes wrong. | `triangle-exclamation` | | Info | Something worth knowing. | `circle-info` | ## Motion SectionMessage reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve. | Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enter | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Makes room, then fades in. | | exit | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades, then the room closes. | ## Alternatives - For validation on a single field, use `TextField` or the field's own error state. - For a transient confirmation that needs no reply, use `Flag`. - For something that must be acknowledged before continuing, use `Modal`. - For a status label on a row, use `StatusTag`. ## Best practices ### Match the appearance to the meaning. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-meaning} Warning for a caution; danger only when something failed. Do: Warning for a provisional schedule. Don't: Danger for a caution. ### Add a title only when the body needs a heading. {#add-a-title-only-when-the-body-needs-a-heading} A short body speaks for itself. Do: A short body, no title. Don't: A title that repeats the body. ### Dismiss only what is optional. {#dismiss-only-what-is-optional} A blocking message stays until the problem is fixed. `dismissible` is on by default, so turn it off when the message must stay. Do: A blocking error cannot be dismissed. Don't: A blocking error that can be dismissed. ### Replace the icon through `icon`, not the children. {#replace-the-icon-through-icon-not-the-children} A Font Awesome Free solid name or a node replaces the default; `false` removes it. An icon in the children adds a second one, in the text. Do: icon replaces the default icon. Don't: An icon in the children, beside the default one. ### Put field errors on the field. {#put-field-errors-on-the-field} An error about one input belongs to that input's own error state, such as `TextField`'s `isInvalid` and `errorMessage`, not in a section message above it. A rejected submit is the exception: a danger section message at the top of the form says what was refused, and each field named still shows its own error. ### Remount with a new `key` to show a dismissed message again. {#remount-with-a-new-key-to-show-a-dismissed-message-again} The component keeps its own dismissed state, and `show` is not a prop. To bring a message back when it genuinely changes, remount it with a new `key`. ## Accessibility - **It announces assertively.** The message renders `role="alert"`, which implies `aria-live="assertive"`, so a screen reader interrupts to read it. That is right for something that just went wrong and wrong for ambient information; for the latter, prefer plain text on the page. - **A message rendered on mount may not be announced at all.** Live regions announce changes. If the message is present in the first paint, treat it as ordinary content and make sure the surrounding page still reads correctly. - **`title` renders as a real heading**, at `headingLevel` (default `h2`). It joins the page's outline, so pick the level that fits where it sits. - **The dismiss button is labeled `Dismiss message`**, rendered by the shared `CloseButton` whose × is `aria-hidden`. - **Say the meaning in the words.** The leading icon is `aria-hidden` and there is no text prefix, so `appearance="danger"` on its own does not say "error" to a screen reader. The icon differs in shape per style, so danger and warning do not rely on color alone to look different. - **Links keep the text color.** A link in the body is told from the text by its underline alone. ## Related - `CloseButton`: use when rendering the dismiss control on a dismissible message. - Forms: use when pairing a form-level danger `SectionMessage` with per-field validation errors.
