A link in it keeps the text color and is underlined. 4. **Actions.** Link buttons, separated by a divider. 5. **Dismiss.** The shared `CloseButton`, centered on the first line. ### States | State | What changes | | --- | --- | | Rest | The fill and icon of the appearance, text in the default color. | | Hovered | The message does not react; Dismiss takes the subtle hovered step. | | Pressed | Dismiss takes the subtle pressed step. | | Focused | Dismiss and each action show the focus ring; see Border. | | Disabled | Not supported. | | Dismissed | The message is removed and the page keeps no copy. | ### Tokens | Part | Token | | --- | --- | | Ground | `--ds-background-brand-subtlest`, `--ds-background-neutral`, `--ds-background-success`, `--ds-background-danger`, `--ds-background-warning`, `--ds-background-information` | | Icon | `--ds-icon-brand`, `--ds-icon-subtle`, `--ds-icon-success`, `--ds-icon-danger`, `--ds-icon-warning`, `--ds-icon-information` | | Title, body, link | `--heading-sm`, `--body-default`, `--ds-text`; actions at `--type-weight-medium` | | Divider | `--ds-border`, `--border-width-default` | | Padding, gaps, corner | `--card-pad`, `--card-stack-sm`, `--stack-md`, `--card-radius` | | Dismiss | `--control-md` | ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Write a title that states the issue or the reason for the message. | Repeat a field's error here; say it once. | | Keep the description to what the person needs to act. | Explain background the person does not need. | | Write actions as verbs: "Reschedule", "Get help". | Use "click here" as link text. | ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `id` | string | — | Unique identifier for the section message element | | `appearance` | enum | `'primary'` | Visual appearance | | `title` | string | — | Optional title/heading for the message | | `headingLevel` | enum | — | Heading level the title renders as, 1 through 6. props.name: id
props.description: The `id` of the combobox control; the label and the list ids are built from it. Generated when omitted.

props.name: name
props.description: Submitted with a form through hidden inputs, one per value.

props.name: label
props.description: The visible label above the field. Without one, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: caption
props.description: Help under the field. With `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` takes its place and is announced.

props.name: isMulti
props.description: Several values, shown as Tags in the field and checkboxes in the list.

props.name: options
props.description: Objects: `value` is the id, `label` (or `text`) what is shown. `group` puts consecutive options under a heading.

props.name: value
props.description: The picked id, or ids with `isMulti`. Pass it to control the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The picked id, or ids with `isMulti`, to start with when the field is uncontrolled.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: The text shown when nothing is picked. It names the field when there is no label.

props.name: isSearchable
props.description: Typing in the field filters the list. On by default; pass `false` for a short list, such as a filter menu's.

props.name: isCreatable
props.description: Offers "Create text " when nothing matches exactly, ignoring case. Implies typing.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: Called with the text of a created option, which is then picked.

props.name: createOption
props.description: `(text)` → the option a typed text creates, `{ value, label }`, or null to create nothing. Defaults to the text itself.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Holds the list open or shut. Controlled: Escape, a press outside and a pick ask through `onOpenChange`, and the list stays as it is until the parent changes `isOpen`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the list starts open, when `isOpen` is not controlling it.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: `(open)`: the list asks to open or close.

props.name: defaultSearchTerm
props.description: The text the search input starts with, so the list opens already filtered. Used by a searchable field.

props.name: displayMode
props.description: With `isMulti`: `tags` (Tag tags) or `text` (comma-separated).

props.name: lineWrap
props.description: With `isMulti`: wrap the picks onto more rows (the default). `false` keeps one row that scrolls sideways.

props.name: truncate
props.description: With `isMulti`: the tags collapse into a "+n" count until the field is focused. With `displayMode="text"` the row clips with a fade.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws 40 and `compact` draws 32.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Dims the field and blocks opening and changing it.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Shows the value, stays focusable, and cannot be changed.

props.name: labelMarker
props.description: Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

props.name: info
props.description: Text for the info tooltip beside the label.

props.name: isInvalid
props.description: Draws the error border, sets `aria-invalid`, and `errorMessage` becomes the announced caption.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: The caption shown under the field while `isInvalid` is set. It is announced.

props.name: isValid
props.description: Draws the confirmation border; `successMessage` takes the caption's place.

props.name: successMessage
props.description: The caption shown under the field while `isValid` is set.

props.name: commitOnClose
props.description: With `isMulti`: `onChange` fires once when the list closes, as a filter bar wants, not on each pick.

props.name: clearable
props.description: Shows the clear × (Figma `_Field Clear`), and lets Delete empty the field. Defaults to true with `isMulti` and to `!isRequired` otherwise; a sort passes `false`.

props.name: selectAll
props.description: With `isMulti`: a "Select all" button over the list, hidden past 50 matches.

props.name: maxSelections
props.description: With `isMulti`: the most values; past it the other rows are disabled and the list says why.

props.name: dependsOn
props.description: The field this one depends on: `{ value, label }`. Until `value` is set the field is disabled with "Choose {label} first"; when it changes, this field clears.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: The options are on their way: the list shows a loading row.

props.name: loadOptions
props.description: `(text, { offset, limit })` → `Promise<{ options, total }>`. Options load as the list opens, as you type and as you scroll, 50 at a time.

props.name: recent
props.description: Ids shown under "Recent" before typing, in a list of more than 50.

props.name: suggested
props.description: Ids shown under "Suggested" before typing, in a list of more than 50.

props.name: marker
props.description: How a single pick is marked: `check` (default) or `radio`. `isMulti` always draws checkboxes.

props.name: onChange
props.description: `(next)`: an id, or an array of ids with `isMulti`.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Focus entering the field from outside it.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Focus leaving the field and its list.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class names added to the field wrapper beside the component's own.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the field wrapper.

# Select

Select — pick one value, or several, from a list, on `_Field` with the internal `Listbox` under it. - **The field is the combobox.** Focus stays in it, and the highlighted row is its `aria-activedescendant`. The field is a text input: typing in it filters the list. With `isSearchable={false}` it is a select-only combobox. - **Values are ids; options are objects.** `value` is an option's `value` (an array with `isMulti`), controlled or not. - **`isMulti`** shows Tags in a TagGroup (`displayMode="tags"`). They wrap by default, so the field is as tall as its tag rows; `lineWrap={false}` keeps one row that scrolls sideways, and `truncate` collapses them into "+n" without focus. - **Trailing** holds the plain ✕ clear button (not a tab stop; Delete does the same) and the caret; the list's footer also carries a subtle "Clear" action (in the tab order) while a value is set.

Also asked as: combobox, picklist, option list, async select.

**Import:** `import { Select } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`design-system/agent-views/patterns/Filtering.md`, `ds guide filtering`) — Quick filters (1–3 categories, short lists) use `FilterButton`, not `Select`.; Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`); +1 more

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Select/Select.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Select/Select.stories.jsx` — Empty, Filled, Multi, MultiRows, OverflowWrap, OverflowNowrap, OverflowTruncate, Searchable, Marker, NotSearchable, Creatable, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Spacing, DependentFields, LongList, Async, AsyncCreatable, AsyncLoading, AsyncFailed, Overview, Interactive, Colors, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled, FieldInvalid, FieldReadOnly, FieldReadOnlyShowsLabel, FieldReadOnlyLongValue, OpenListEdge, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced, MotionKeyboardOpen

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Select/Select.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Select` for a form field with six or more options, where typing to filter helps more than scanning, such as a tutor roster or a school name.

| The choice is | Reach for |
| --- | --- |
| One pick, up to 5 options | `RadioGroup` |
| Several picks, up to 5 options | `CheckboxGroup` |
| 6 or more options | `Select`, searchable by default |
| A list held on a server, too large to ship | `Select` with `loadOptions` |
| Options in a hierarchy | `Cascader` or `TreeSelect` |
| Narrowing a table from a bar | `PopupSelect`, `FilterButton` or `FilterMenu` |
| An action run from a button | `DropdownMenu` |

## Motion

Select reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, with no clip or travel. From the keyboard it opens with no animation. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, the same as the enter; stays mounted until the exit completes. |

## Alternatives

- For up to five mutually exclusive options, use `RadioGroup`.
- For up to five multi-select options, use `CheckboxGroup`.
- For hierarchical options, use `Cascader` or `TreeSelect`.
- For free-form tags a person can create and manage in place, use `TagInput`.
- For switching a view or setting one filter from a button, use `PopupSelect`.
- For a menu of actions, use `DropdownMenu`.

## Best practices

### Keep option labels short and parallel. {#keep-option-labels-short-and-parallel}

Short, parallel labels scan as a list; a sentence in the field gets cut off.

Do: A short label names the value.
Don't: A sentence in the field does not fit.

### Use multi select when answers combine. {#use-multi-select-when-answers-combine}

Several answers belong in Tags, one per answer, not in one comma-joined value.

Do: One Tag per chosen answer.
Don't: Answers joined into one value.

### Show an error on the field itself. {#show-an-error-on-the-field-itself}

Mark the field with `isInvalid` so the message reads as an error; the same words as help text in a default field look fine.

Do: The field shows the error state.
Don't: The same words as plain help, in a default field.

### Pick the mode by the answer. {#pick-the-mode-by-the-answer}

`isMulti` shows picks as `Tag`s and checkboxes in the list; `selectAll` and `maxSelections` (the maximum number of picks) apply to it only. `onOpenChange` reports the list opening and closing. Typing filters the list unless you pass `isSearchable={false}`, and `isCreatable` adds a "Create" row when nothing matches. `createOption` turns the typed text into the created option, or refuses it with `null` (`TimePicker` uses it to parse `"1430"` as `"02:30 PM"`). `clearable` defaults to on with `isMulti` and off for a required single select.

### Mark a single pick with a check or a radio. {#mark-a-single-pick-with-a-check-or-a-radio}

A single `Select` marks its pick with a check at the end of the row. Pass `marker="radio"` to draw a radio before the label instead when the list reads as a set of alternatives, as in a view switch or filter menu. Several picks always use checkboxes, so `marker` has no effect with `isMulti`. The marker changes color on selection; it does not move.

### Show picks as text when Tags crowd the field. {#show-picks-as-text-when-tags-crowd-the-field}

`displayMode="text"` (with `isMulti`) shows picks as comma-separated text instead of `Tag`s. `isValid` with `successMessage` draws the success edge and message.

### Chain `dependsOn` for fields that filter each other. {#chain-dependson-for-fields-that-filter-each-other}

Pass the parent's `{ value, label }` as `dependsOn` on the child. The child disables itself and explains why until the parent has a value, and clears itself the moment the parent's value changes.

```jsx
<Select label="School" options={schools} value={school} onChange={setSchool} />
<Select
    label="Teacher"
    options={teachersFor(school)}
    value={teacher}
    onChange={setTeacher}
    dependsOn={{ value: school, label: 'a school' }}
/>
```

### Use `commitOnClose` for a filter bar, not a form field. {#use-commitonclose-for-a-filter-bar-not-a-form-field}

A form's multi-select should fire `onChange` on every pick. `commitOnClose` fires once on close to avoid re-querying on every checkbox click in a filter panel.

### Reach for `loadOptions` once a list is genuinely large or server-backed. {#reach-for-loadoptions-once-a-list-is-genuinely-large-or-server-backed}

`recent` and `suggested` only change the order past 50 static options; `loadOptions` is for a list too large to ship as a static array.

`loadOptions` is `(text, { offset, limit }) => Promise<{ options, total }>`. The first page loads when the list opens and whenever the typed text changes; the next page loads as the list scrolls near its end (50 at a time), and an older answer never overwrites a newer one. `isCreatable` works with it.

```jsx
<Select
    label="Student"
    isCreatable
    loadOptions={(text, { offset, limit }) => fetchStudents(text, offset, limit)}
/>
```

While a page is loading, the list shows one "Loading options" row rather than skeleton rows. If the request fails it shows "Couldn't load options" with a Retry button, and Enter in the field retries too. A later page that fails keeps the rows already loaded and puts the same message in the footer. Options fade in one after another, 20 ms apart, capped at 500 ms; reduced motion shows them at once.

### Turn typing off for a short set of choices. {#turn-typing-off-for-a-short-set-of-choices}

Typing is on because most lists are long enough to need it. A menu that holds a few choices, applied as you pick, has nothing to search: pass `isSearchable={false}` so the field stays a plain trigger and Space opens it.

### Use read-only for fixed values and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-values-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` keeps the value focusable, selectable and at full contrast (`aria-readonly`); `isDisabled` removes the field from the tab order when it does not apply yet. Say why in the caption. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value; content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

## Accessibility

- **A real combobox.** The field is `role="combobox"` with
  `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`/`aria-activedescendant` tracking the open
  list and its highlighted row.
- **The label is linked, or named explicitly.** Pass `label` for a visible
  one, or `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby` when there isn't a visible label.
- **Keyboard parity with a native select.** Arrow keys, Enter and Escape
  open, move through and close the list; Backspace removes the last Tag in a
  multi-select with an empty filter; Delete clears the field when
  `clearable`.
- **Clearing by keyboard and screen reader.** When a live field is `clearable`
  (on by default except on a required single `Select`) and holds a value, the
  field's plain ✕ `IconButton` (`xmark` at `--icon-sm`) is named
  `"Clear <noun>"` in lowercase (such as `"Clear school"` or
  `"Clear selection"`) and sets `tabIndex={-1}` so `Tab` moves past the field
  in one stop, while the list footer's subtle "Clear" `Button` stays in the
  tab order. Keyboard users press `Delete` to clear in place, or `Tab` into
  the open list to the footer "Clear" button; pointer and screen-reader users
  can activate either button. Both empty the value, call `onChange` with `''`
  (or `[]` with `isMulti`), and return focus to the combobox.
- **A waiting dependent field says why.** `dependsOn`'s disabled state pairs
  with a caption ("Choose a school first"), not silence.

## Related

- `RadioGroup`: use when choosing one option from up to five visible options.
- `CheckboxGroup`: use when choosing several options from up to five visible options.
- `TreeSelect`: use when options form an expandable hierarchy.
- `Cascader`: use when choosing a hierarchical path column by column.
- `TagInput`: use when picking and creating color-coded tags in place.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Field.** The box that shows the value, or the placeholder, the plain ✕ clear button when a value is set and clearable, and the caret.
2. **Label.** Names the field. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text.
3. **List.** The options, in a popup under the field. Groups carry a heading; when a value is set and clearable, a compact subtle "Clear" button sits at the end of the list footer.
4. **Caption.** Helper text, or the error that replaces it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge; the placeholder until a value is picked. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down, and the press opens the list. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Valid | With `isValid`, the edge takes `--ds-border-success` and `successMessage` shows under the field. |
| Read-only | The `--ds-background-neutral` fill, full contrast, no hover. The chevron is not drawn, a press opens nothing, and a long value wraps instead of clipping. The value can be read, selected and copied. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Caret and clear | Caret `--ds-icon-subtle` at `--icon-sm`; field clear icon `--icon-sm` on a subtle `IconButton`; footer Clear compact subtle `Button` in `--dropdown-menu-pad` under a `--ds-border` top edge. |
| Label and caption | `--body-sm`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`, error `--ds-text-danger`. |
| List | `--ds-surface-overlay` with a `--ds-border` edge, `--popup-radius` and `--ds-shadow-overlay`. |
| Option | `--pad-y-md` `--pad-x-md`, `--body-default`; hovered `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, picked `--ds-background-selected`. |
| Select all mark | `--ds-background-input` with a `--ds-border-input` edge and `--radius-md`; checked `--ds-background-selected-bold`, `--ds-border-selected`, `--ds-icon-inverse`. |
| Search hint | "Type to search" above a long list: `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`, `--pad-x-xs` `--pad-x-md`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write each option as the thing itself: "Lincoln Middle". | A sentence or an instruction: "Choose this for algebra". |
| Order options by how often they are picked, or alphabetically for a long list. | A random order that makes people scan. |
| Use a placeholder that names the action: "Select a school". | The label repeated as the placeholder. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Select a school". | "Required" or "Invalid". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` of the combobox control; the label and the list ids are built from it. Generated when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Submitted with a form through hidden inputs, one per value. |
| `label` | node | — | The visible label above the field. Without one, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `caption` | node | — | Help under the field. With `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` takes its place and is announced. |
| `isMulti` | bool | `false` | Several values, shown as Tags in the field and checkboxes in the list. |
| `options` | arrayOf | `[]` | Objects: `value` is the id, `label` (or `text`) what is shown. `group` puts consecutive options under a heading. |
| `value` | arrayOf | — | The picked id, or ids with `isMulti`. Pass it to control the field. |
| `defaultValue` | arrayOf | — | The picked id, or ids with `isMulti`, to start with when the field is uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Select...'` | The text shown when nothing is picked. It names the field when there is no label. |
| `isSearchable` | bool | `true` | Typing in the field filters the list. On by default; pass `false` for a short list, such as a filter menu's. |
| `isCreatable` | bool | `false` | Offers "Create text " when nothing matches exactly, ignoring case. Implies typing. |
| `onCreate` | func | — | Called with the text of a created option, which is then picked. |
| `createOption` | func | — | `(text)` → the option a typed text creates, `{ value, label }`, or null to create nothing. Defaults to the text itself. |
| `isOpen` | bool | — | Holds the list open or shut. Controlled: Escape, a press outside and a pick ask through `onOpenChange`, and the list stays as it is until the parent changes `isOpen`. |
| `defaultOpen` | bool | `false` | Whether the list starts open, when `isOpen` is not controlling it. |
| `onOpenChange` | func | — | `(open)`: the list asks to open or close. |
| `defaultSearchTerm` | string | `''` | The text the search input starts with, so the list opens already filtered. Used by a searchable field. |
| `displayMode` | enum | `'tags'` | With `isMulti`: `tags` (Tag tags) or `text` (comma-separated). |
| `lineWrap` | bool | `true` | With `isMulti`: wrap the picks onto more rows (the default). `false` keeps one row that scrolls sideways. |
| `truncate` | bool | `false` | With `isMulti`: the tags collapse into a "+n" count until the field is focused. With `displayMode="text"` the row clips with a fade. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 40 and `compact` draws 32. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Dims the field and blocks opening and changing it. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the value, stays focusable, and cannot be changed. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for the info tooltip beside the label. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border, sets `aria-invalid`, and `errorMessage` becomes the announced caption. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | The caption shown under the field while `isInvalid` is set. It is announced. |
| `isValid` | bool | `false` | Draws the confirmation border; `successMessage` takes the caption's place. |
| `successMessage` | node | — | The caption shown under the field while `isValid` is set. |
| `commitOnClose` | bool | `false` | With `isMulti`: `onChange` fires once when the list closes, as a filter bar wants, not on each pick. |
| `clearable` | bool | — | Shows the clear × (Figma `_Field Clear`), and lets Delete empty the field. Defaults to true with `isMulti` and to `!isRequired` otherwise; a sort passes `false`. |
| `selectAll` | bool | `false` | With `isMulti`: a "Select all" button over the list, hidden past 50 matches. |
| `maxSelections` | number | — | With `isMulti`: the most values; past it the other rows are disabled and the list says why. |
| `dependsOn` | shape | — | The field this one depends on: `{ value, label }`. Until `value` is set the field is disabled with "Choose {label} first"; when it changes, this field clears. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | The options are on their way: the list shows a loading row. |
| `loadOptions` | func | — | `(text, { offset, limit })` → `Promise<{ options, total }>`. Options load as the list opens, as you type and as you scroll, 50 at a time. |
| `recent` | arrayOf | — | Ids shown under "Recent" before typing, in a list of more than 50. |
| `suggested` | arrayOf | — | Ids shown under "Suggested" before typing, in a list of more than 50. |
| `marker` | enum | `'check'` | How a single pick is marked: `check` (default) or `radio`. `isMulti` always draws checkboxes. |
| `onChange` | func | — | `(next)`: an id, or an array of ids with `isMulti`. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Focus entering the field from outside it. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Focus leaving the field and its list. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the field wrapper beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the field wrapper. |

## Variants

**`displayMode`** — `tags` · `text`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

**`marker`** — `check` · `radio`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--body-default` · `--body-sm` · `--border-width-default` · `--ds-background-input` · `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` · `--ds-background-selected-bold` · `--ds-border-focused` · `--ds-border-input` · `--ds-border-selected` · `--ds-icon-inverse` · `--ds-icon-subtle` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--ds-text-subtlest` · `--focus-ring-width` · `--icon-sm` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-x-xs` · `--pad-y-md` · `--radius-md` · `--select-check-size` · `--stack-md` · `--stack-sm`

# SettingRow

SettingRow — puts a setting's name and one-line description at the start and its control (`Toggle`, compact `Select`, or `Button`) at the end, top-aligned to the label. Any `status` (`StatusTag`) sits beside the label so the end slot holds only the action. The row's `label` names `control` through `aria-labelledby`; controls that carry their own visible action text (such as a `Disconnect` `Button`) combine their own id with the row label id so both the action and the setting name are announced.

**Import:** `import { SettingRow } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SettingRow/SettingRow.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SettingRow/SettingRow.stories.jsx` — Overview, ToggleControl, SelectControl, ConnectionRow, Rest, Saving, Saved, ErrorState, DisabledWithReason, ReadOnly, Motion, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SettingRow/SettingRow.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `SettingRow` on settings and preference pages where each row adjusts one independent setting or external connection that takes effect immediately. Stack related rows directly under a section heading: adjacent `SettingRow` elements divide with a `1px` border at `--setting-row-pad-y` (`12px`) vertical padding, with no card per row.

## Motion

SettingRow reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Row state and inline control transitions. |

## Alternatives

- For fields edited and submitted together with a Save button, use stacked form fields inside `Fieldset` (see Forms).
- For an option inside a submitted form, use `Checkbox` rather than `Toggle` or `SettingRow`.
- For one value on a record page read far more often than edited, use `InlineEdit`.

## Best practices

### Omit Toggle's own label inside SettingRow. {#omit-toggle-s-own-label-inside-settingrow}

`SettingRow` wires its `label` to `control` through `aria-labelledby`. Passing a second `label` on `Toggle` repeats the text visually and at the end of the row.

Do: Row label at the start names the bare Toggle at the end.
Don't: Toggle repeats its own label in the end slot.

### Put connection status beside the label, never in the control slot. {#put-connection-status-beside-the-label-never-in-the-control-slot}

Pass `StatusTag` through `status` so every row's end slot holds only its action control.

Do: StatusTag sits beside the label; Disconnect stands alone at the end.
Don't: Status crowds the action at the end of the row.

### State the reason in description when a setting is disabled. {#state-the-reason-in-description-when-a-setting-is-disabled}

When a setting waits on another setting on the same page, explain how to unlock it in `description` rather than hiding it in a tooltip.

Do: Description names the prerequisite on the same page.
Don't: Disabled control gives no clue why it cannot be changed.

## Accessibility

- **Label names the control.** `SettingRow` links its `label` span to `control` via `aria-labelledby`, so a `Toggle` announces `"Session reminders, switch, on"` without needing its own visible label, and `status` text beside the label does not pollute the switch's accessible name.
- **Self-describing action buttons.** When `control` carries visible action text (such as a `Disconnect` `Button`), `SettingRow` combines the button's own id with the row label id in `aria-labelledby` (`"Disconnect Google Calendar"`), keeping multiple connection rows distinct for screen-reader users while satisfying WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name.
- **Readable descriptions and announced errors.** `description` and `error` link to `control` via `aria-describedby`; `error` renders with `role="alert"` and sets `aria-invalid="true"`.
- **DOM order matches reading order.** Label, status, description, and inline error precede the end control in the DOM so Tab and virtual-cursor order match visual reading order.

## Related

- `Toggle`: use as `control` when a setting turns on or off and applies immediately.
- `Select`: use with `spacing="compact"` as `control` when a setting picks one option from a short list.
- `StatusTag`: pass to `status` to show connection or feature state beside the setting name.
- `Flag`: use in `FlagGroup` to confirm background saves on a settings page.

## Parts

1. **Label (`label`) and status (`status`).** Strong `--body-default` setting name at the start, with an optional `StatusTag` beside it so the end slot holds only the interactive control.
2. **Description (`description`).** One line of `--body-sm` subtle context under the label, or the visible prerequisite/permission reason when disabled or read-only.
3. **Inline error (`error`).** Optional danger error message rendered directly under `description` when a background save fails.
4. **Control (`control` at `end`).** Top-aligned to the label row: a `Toggle` (with no `label` prop), a compact `Select` (`spacing="compact"`), or a compact `Button`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the setting as a noun phrase: "Session reminders", "Reminder lead time". | Phrase the row label as a question or command with punctuation. |
| Keep `description` to one sentence adding context the label does not already say. | Restate the label ("Turn session reminders on or off"). |
| Write `error` with cause and next step: "Could not save SMS alerts. Check your connection and try again." | "Save failed" or "Error". |

## Props

entries.summary: The PLUS sidebar: the app's navigation, 240 wide, padded 12, on the sunken fill. Every row sits on one grid: rows 32 high from x 12 to 228 with radius 8, a 24 icon slot centered on x 32, the label on x 48, and a trailing slot centered on x 208. By default it fills with the groups for `user` (`sidebarConfig.js`, defaulting to `'tutor'`), the signed-in person's account row, and open tabs from `useOpenTabs()`. Pass `user` and `groups` together to add or override a prototype's own area(s) by `id` while keeping the role's navigation; pass `groups` without `user` (and/or `tabs`) to render custom groups directly. - **Logo row**: the PLUS Logo lockup at height 24, a link to Home, and the sidebar toggle (`angles-left`) on the trailing column. Inside a Frame the toggle comes from the Frame; standalone, pass `onToggle`. - **Groups**: the first has no title (Home, Slack). Every other group has a title row, a full 32 row that collapses its group; an `angle-down` shows after the title on hover and focus and turns right while collapsed. Each person's collapsed sections are remembered in localStorage. - **Locked group**: while `modulesLeft` is above 0, a group marked `lockedDuringOnboarding` shows a lock in the title's caret slot, its rows in the subtlest text with no hover, and the tooltip "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit" (no number). It neither collapses nor opens. - **Training counts**: a row with `training: 'lessons'` shows the Count tag of `lessonsLeft` ("2 assigned lessons left"); `training: 'modules'` shows `modulesLeft` ("3 onboarding modules left"), only while onboarding is in progress. Zero shows nothing. - **Trailing slot**: a count, a dot, the external icon for a link that leaves the app, or a close button. - **Open tabs** (`useOpenTabs()` or `tabs[item.id]`): records a person opened (a session, a student) list under their row on a thread, one line on the icon column whose last row turns into the label column. Each tab shows a live dot at rest and Close on hover, focus and while selected; Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab. Three show, then "Show n more". On hover the row's icon slot turns into a collapse angle and its trailing slot into Close all. Exactly one row is selected: a selected tab takes the fill and its row goes to ink; collapsed, the row takes the fill and shows the tab count. - **Icons**: every row icon is outlined (Font Awesome Free regular) in the one subtle icon color. A selected row shows the fill and the selected icon color, never a solid icon; a brand mark (`fa-brands fa-slack`) is the only exception. - **Inner mode**: pass `inner` and the Sidebar's content swaps for an inner sidebar: one full-width Back button (`onBack`) with the area name centered, an optional full-width context dropdown (`inner.switcher`), then text-only rows (`inner.rows`: a record's stages, or a task's steps). The container, logo row and account row stay still; only the content swaps. The old content leaves at once and the new enters as one block, sliding 12 on `spatial.fast` from the end going in and from the start going back, and fading on `appearance.fast`, with no overshoot. Reduced motion keeps only the fade. Back shows the main Sidebar, where what was left sits as one open row (`tabs`) under its area. - **Account row**: `SidebarAccount`, under a divider: the account menu (Profile, Help Center, Sign out) and, at the end, the Inbox bell with its unread count. Content is data. Nothing here changes the URL.

Every row sits on one grid: rows 32 high from x 12 to 228 with radius 8, a 24 icon slot centered on x 32, the label on x 48, and a trailing slot centered on x 208. By default it fills with the groups for `user` (`sidebarConfig.js`, defaulting to `'tutor'`), the signed-in person's account row, and open tabs from `useOpenTabs()`. Pass `user` and `groups` together to add or override a prototype's own area(s) by `id` while keeping the role's navigation; pass `groups` without `user` (and/or `tabs`) to render custom groups directly. - **Logo row**: the PLUS Logo lockup at height 24, a link to Home, and the sidebar toggle (`angles-left`) on the trailing column. Inside a Frame the toggle comes from the Frame; standalone, pass `onToggle`. - **Groups**: the first has no title (Home, Slack). Every other group has a title row, a full 32 row that collapses its group; an `angle-down` shows after the title on hover and focus and turns right while collapsed. Each person's collapsed sections are remembered in localStorage. - **Locked group**: while `modulesLeft` is above 0, a group marked `lockedDuringOnboarding` shows a lock in the title's caret slot, its rows in the subtlest text with no hover, and the tooltip "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit" (no number). It neither collapses nor opens. - **Training counts**: a row with `training: 'lessons'` shows the Count tag of `lessonsLeft` ("2 assigned lessons left"); `training: 'modules'` shows `modulesLeft` ("3 onboarding modules left"), only while onboarding is in progress. Zero shows nothing. - **Trailing slot**: a count, a dot, the external icon for a link that leaves the app, or a close button. - **Open tabs** (`useOpenTabs()` or `tabs[item.id]`): records a person opened (a session, a student) list under their row on a thread, one line on the icon column whose last row turns into the label column. Each tab shows a live dot at rest and Close on hover, focus and while selected; Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab. Three show, then "Show n more". On hover the row's icon slot turns into a collapse angle and its trailing slot into Close all. Exactly one row is selected: a selected tab takes the fill and its row goes to ink; collapsed, the row takes the fill and shows the tab count. - **Icons**: every row icon is outlined (Font Awesome Free regular) in the one subtle icon color. A selected row shows the fill and the selected icon color, never a solid icon; a brand mark (`fa-brands fa-slack`) is the only exception. - **Inner mode**: pass `inner` and the Sidebar's content swaps for an inner sidebar: one full-width Back button (`onBack`) with the area name centered, an optional full-width context dropdown (`inner.switcher`), then text-only rows (`inner.rows`: a record's stages, or a task's steps). The container, logo row and account row stay still; only the content swaps. The old content leaves at once and the new enters as one block, sliding 12 on `spatial.fast` from the end going in and from the start going back, and fading on `appearance.fast`, with no overshoot. Reduced motion keeps only the fade. Back shows the main Sidebar, where what was left sits as one open row (`tabs`) under its area. - **Account row**: `SidebarAccount`, under a divider: the account menu (Profile, Help Center, Sign out) and, at the end, the Inbox bell with its unread count. Content is data. Nothing here changes the URL.

Also asked as: left nav, side nav, side navigation.

**Import:** `import { Sidebar } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Page (`ds guide page`); Panel (`ds guide panel`)

**Governed by:** Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Sidebar/Sidebar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Sidebar/Sidebar.stories.jsx` — Overview, Geometry, KeyboardDisclosure, Tutor, DefaultRole, PrototypeAreas, OnboardingInProgress, OnboardingDone, SectionsOpen, SectionsCollapsed, TabsNone, TabsFew, TabsMany, TabsClipped, TabRest, TabHover, TabFocus, TabSelected, TabsCollapsedWithSelection, ClosingTabs, AccountHug, AccountRow, SidebarOpen, SidebarClosed, SidebarFloating, InnerSidebar, RowsRoundEight, InnerSwapInAndBack, InnerTaskOpenRow, StudentBreadcrumb, InnerStepsDoneAndOff, InnerKeyboard, InnerSwapMotion, InnerSwapReducedMotion, Interactive, Light, Dark

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Sidebar/Sidebar.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` · exit `spatial.fast` · swap `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Sidebar` for the app's main areas. `Sidebar` (`@/components`) fills the
rail from the role's config (`user`), and a prototype passes `groups` to add
or override its own areas by `id` while keeping the role's navigation. The
Frame decides whether it docks, collapses or floats; this page covers what is
inside it.

A record with stages (a session) or a multi-step task swaps the Sidebar's
content for an **inner sidebar**: pass `inner` (`areaLabel`, `rows`, and an
optional `switcher`) and `onBack`. Only the content swaps; the logo row, the
account row and the page stay where they are. A record without stages, such as
a student, keeps the main Sidebar with a breadcrumb.

Content is data. The Sidebar draws the `groups` it is given and never changes
the URL: the caller handles `onSelect` and decides which groups a role sees.

## Motion

Sidebar reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Slides in from its edge while the Page narrows on the same clock; the Page toggle fades out. |
| exit | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Slides out to its edge and leaves nothing behind; the Page widens and its toggle fades in. |
| swap | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The Sidebar container stays still and only its content swaps between the main and the inner sidebar. The old content leaves at once; the new enters as one block, no stagger, sliding 12 from the end going in and from the start going back, fading in, with no overshoot. The page does not animate. Reduced motion keeps only the fade. |

## Alternatives

- For switching between views of a single subject inside a page, use `Tabs`.
- For showing position inside a deep hierarchy above the page title, use `Breadcrumb`.

## Best practices

### Mark one selected item at a time. {#mark-one-selected-item-at-a-time}

The Sidebar marks one current page. `activeId` takes one id, so exactly one row or tab carries the selected fill and `aria-current="page"`.

### Keep every row icon outlined. {#keep-every-row-icon-outlined}

Rows draw regular-style icons in the one subtle icon color, and a selected row shows its fill with the selected icon color, never a solid icon. A brand mark such as Slack is the only exception: it keeps its brand glyph.

### Highlight the ancestor without a fill when a child tab is selected. {#highlight-the-ancestor-without-a-fill-when-a-child-tab-is-selected}

A parent of the current page shows it without competing: when one of a row's tabs is selected, the tab takes the fill and the row goes to ink without it.

### Pass every open tab; the Sidebar folds them. {#pass-every-open-tab-the-sidebar-folds-them}

Past three open tabs the rest go behind Show n more. The Sidebar does this for you; pass every open tab and let it fold them.

### Name the area in a word or two. {#name-the-area-in-a-word-or-two}

Do: Sessions and Students: one word each, read at a glance.
Don't: A sentence for a label truncates and hides the area's name.

### Lock the Toolkit during onboarding, never hide it. {#lock-the-toolkit-during-onboarding-never-hide-it}

Do: The Toolkit shows, locked, so the tutor sees what training unlocks.
Don't: With the Toolkit left out, nothing says it is coming.

### Name a tab by when and who. {#name-a-tab-by-when-and-who}

Do: The time and the teacher; the school is in the tooltip.
Don't: Everything in the label, and the time is cut off.

## Accessibility

- The Sidebar is a `nav` named by `label`, Main by default. A titled group is a `group` named by its title.
- The selected row or tab carries `aria-current="page"`, so selection never rests on the fill alone.
- A section title is a button that reports whether its rows are expanded and points at them. It opens and closes with Enter and Space, as does "Show n more"; both are built on Base UI Collapsible, and the account button opens its menu on Base UI Menu.
- A locked group's lock is focusable and named "Locked. Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit".
- Delete or Backspace closes the focused tab, and focus moves to the next tab, else the one before it, else the tab's row.
- The toggle is named "Close sidebar", announces Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac) and reports that the Sidebar is expanded.
- The account button is named by the person's name and role, then "account menu".
- In the inner sidebar, focus lands on Back when it opens and returns to the open row when Back closes it. Back, then the context Select, then each row are reached with Tab; Enter picks a row.
- The swap slides 12 and fades. With reduced motion it only fades.

## Related

- Frame: use when docking, collapsing and floating the Sidebar beside the Page.
- `SidebarTab`: use when configuring a single row inside a custom sidebar section.
- `CountTag`: use when rendering a count on the trailing edge of a row.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Link` · `Pagination` · `Tabs`

## Parts

1. **Logo row.** The PLUS `Logo`, which goes Home, and the toggle at the end of the row.
2. **Group.** Rows under an optional section title. A group without a title has no title row and never collapses.
3. **Section title.** A full `--control-md` row in the subtlest text. On hover and focus the collapse angle shows after it.
4. **Row.** An icon slot, the label, and a trailing slot for a count, a dot, the external icon or Close.
5. **Open tabs.** Records a person opened, such as a session or a student, under their row on a thread. Three show, then Show n more.
6. **Account row.** The avatar, the name and the role, which open the account menu (Profile, Help Center, Sign out), and the bell with its unread count, which opens the Inbox beside the Sidebar, under a divider.

Every part sits on one grid: icon centers on x `32`, labels start on x `48`, trailing slots center on x `208`, and section titles start on x `20`.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The row in `--ds-text-subtle`, with no fill. |
| Hovered | The neutral hovered fill and ink text. A row with tabs swaps its icon for the collapse angle and its trailing slot for Close all; a tab swaps its live dot for Close. |
| Pressed | The neutral pressed fill. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring inside the row's edge and the same swaps as hover; see Border. |
| Disabled | Not used. A row the person cannot reach yet is locked instead. |
| Selected | The selected fill, ink text and icon and the medium weight, with `aria-current="page"`. A selected tab takes the fill and its row goes to ink without it. |
| Locked | While `modulesLeft` is above 0, a group marked `lockedDuringOnboarding` shows a lock and its rows take the subtlest text, with no hover and no press. |
| Collapsed | A collapsed section hides its rows and turns its angle right. Collapsed sections are remembered per person under `storageKey`. |

### Tokens

The Sidebar's width, 240, belongs to the Frame: see Frame.

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Pad | 12: `--frame-sidebar-pad`. |
| Row | 32: `--control-md`; radius 8: `--frame-sidebar-row-radius`; 2 apart: `--frame-sidebar-row-gap`. |
| Groups | 16 apart: `--frame-sidebar-group-gap`. |
| Row text and icon | `--ds-text-subtle` and `--ds-icon-subtle`, at `--body-default`. |
| Hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `-pressed`. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-selected` with hovered and pressed steps; `--ds-text-selected`, `--ds-icon-selected`. |
| Section title and locked rows | `--ds-text-subtlest`, `--ds-icon-subtlest`; titles at `--body-sm`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width`, inside the row. |
| Account row | 8 above: `--stack-md`; 12 below and at the start: `--frame-sidebar-pad`; 16 at the end: `--pad-x-lg`. |
| Account row divider | `--ds-border`. |

Docked, collapsed, peeking and overlay are the Frame's states, on the Frame page.

## Content guidelines

rankedText.usage:
Use `Sidebar` for the app's main areas. `Sidebar` (`@/components`) fills the
rail from the role's config (`user`), and a prototype passes `groups` to add
or override its own areas by `id` while keeping the role's navigation. The
Frame decides whether it docks, collapses or floats; this page covers what is
inside it.

A record with stages (a session) or a multi-step task swaps the Sidebar's
content for an **inner sidebar**: pass `inner` (`areaLabel`, `rows`, and an
optional `switcher`) and `onBack`. Only the content swaps; the logo row, the
account row and the page stay where they are. A record without stages, such as
a student, keeps the main Sidebar with a breadcrumb.

Content is data. The Sidebar draws the `groups` it is given and never changes
the URL: the caller handles `onSelect` and decides which groups a role sees.
rankedText.best:
### Mark one selected item at a time.

The Sidebar marks one current page. `activeId` takes one id, so exactly one row or tab carries the selected fill and `aria-current="page"`.

### Keep every row icon outlined.

Rows draw regular-style icons in the one subtle icon color, and a selected row shows its fill with the selected icon color, never a solid icon. A brand mark such as Slack is the only exception: it keeps its brand glyph.

### Highlight the ancestor without a fill when a child tab is selected.

A parent of the current page shows it without competing: when one of a row's tabs is selected, the tab takes the fill and the row goes to ink without it.

### Pass every open tab; the Sidebar folds them.

Past three open tabs the rest go behind Show n more. The Sidebar does this for you; pass every open tab and let it fold them.

### Name the area in a word or two.

Do: Sessions and Students: one word each, read at a glance.
Don't: A sentence for a label truncates and hides the area's name.

### Lock the Toolkit during onboarding, never hide it.

Do: The Toolkit shows, locked, so the tutor sees what training unlocks.
Don't: With the Toolkit left out, nothing says it is coming.

### Name a tab by when and who.

Do: The time and the teacher; the school is in the tooltip.
Don't: Everything in the label, and the time is cut off.

Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion. ## Usage Use `Skeleton` for a loading state while content loads, so the space it will fill is already on screen and the layout does not jump when it arrives. - **One label loading on its own** (a status calculated after the row appears, a tag group fetched separately): the matching preset. - **A thumbnail, avatar or header:** a rectangle or circle with its own size. ## Motion Skeleton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve. | Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | change | Load content | `--ds-motion-linear` | Shimmer from top-left to bottom-right; content fades in over it. | ## Alternatives - For an action in progress or a short wait with no layout shape yet, use `Spinner`. - For a wait whose percentage is known, use `ProgressBar` or `ProgressRing`. ## Best practices ### Shape the placeholder like its content. {#shape-the-placeholder-like-its-content} A paragraph placeholder promises lines of text; a block promises an image. Do: Paragraph preset for a paragraph. Don't: A rectangle standing in for text. ### Pair a circle with text for people. {#pair-a-circle-with-text-for-people} An avatar placeholder is round; a square one misleads about what will load. Do: Circle beside a text line. Don't: Rectangle beside a text line. ### Keep the shimmer on while loading. {#keep-the-shimmer-on-while-loading} The shimmer tells the person the content is still coming; a frozen skeleton reads as a broken page. Leave `isShimmering` at its default. ### Use a label preset when one label loads after its row is on screen. {#use-a-label-preset-when-one-label-loads-after-its-row-is-on-screen} A preset has the label's height and corners, so nothing moves when the value arrives. Do: The status preset, the size of the Status tag it stands in for. Don't: A free rectangle at its default size, so the row jumps when the status arrives. ### Use plain text bars inside a loading table or card. {#use-plain-text-bars-inside-a-loading-table-or-card} The container owns the skeleton. Labels become the same text bars as the rest, so a loading table does not fill with dozens of label shapes. Do: Text bars throughout the row. Don't: Label shapes inside a loading container. ### Skip the skeleton on a count in a button, tab or nav item. {#skip-the-skeleton-on-a-count-in-a-button-tab-or-nav-item} Show nothing until the number arrives; `CountTag` already renders nothing without a value. ### Skeleton the host, not a count inside it. {#skeleton-the-host-not-a-count-inside-it} For a `CountTag` inside a `StatusTag` or `Tag`, use one `preset="status"` for the whole label. ### Leave flags, modals, menus and spinners out. {#leave-flags-modals-menus-and-spinners-out} They appear when they have something to say. A `Tag` saving a change keeps its own spinner (`isLoading`), so saving and loading look different. ## Accessibility - **Every skeleton is hidden from assistive tech.** It renders `aria-hidden="true"` with no role, never takes focus and ignores the pointer, so a screen reader does not read a list of empty items and a placeholder cannot be clicked. - **The loading region carries the busy state.** Set `aria-busy="true"` once on the container that is loading, and remove it when the content arrives. - **Pair the busy state with a live label.** Render a visually hidden `role="status"` element **beside** the busy region, not inside it. Mount the status empty and set its text after mount ("Loading students…"), keep it mounted, and update its text when content arrives ("Students loaded"). `aria-busy` alone is not announced by every screen reader. - **Contrast in any theme.** The fill is `--ds-skeleton` and the shimmer `--skeleton-subtle`, both theme tokens. ```jsx const [message, setMessage] = useState(''); useEffect(() => { setMessage(loading ? 'Loading students…' : 'Students loaded'); }, [loading]);
{message}

Students

{loading ? : renderStudents(students)}
``` - **Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the shimmer stops and the fill is flat. ## Related - `StatusTag`: use when replacing a `preset="status"` placeholder once the status resolves. - `TagGroup`: use when replacing a `preset="tag-group"` placeholder once the tags load. - Loading: use when deciding between `Skeleton`, `Spinner` and `ProgressBar` across a view. # Spinner

`Spinner` — an animated ring that says a wait is in progress, with no duration to report. `size` is a pixel diameter; `appearance="inherit"` takes the surrounding text color, `"invert"` is for a bold or colored background.

Also asked as: loading, busy indicator, wait indicator, loading indicator.

**Import:** `import { Spinner } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Search (`ds guide search`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/loading/Spinner/Spinner.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/loading/Spinner/Spinner.stories.jsx` — Overview, Sizes, Size16, Size24, Size48, Invert, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, ReducedMotion

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/loading/Spinner/Spinner.mdx`

**Motion:** change `loop`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Spinner` when the wait is short, indeterminate, and the user has nothing
to do but wait: a submit in flight, a panel fetching on open. For a wait under
about 300 ms, show nothing so the indicator does not flicker.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Inherit | The default. The ring takes the surrounding text color, so it matches a label, a panel or a disabled control. |
| Invert | On a bold or colored background. |

## Motion

Spinner reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Load content | `--ds-motion-loop` | Swings on the loop spring while work runs and stops the moment it stops. A static label in reduced motion. |

## Alternatives

- For a wait whose percentage is known, use `ProgressBar` or `ProgressRing`.
- For content loading into a layout that already has a shape, use `Skeleton`.
- For a result once the wait ends, use `SectionMessage` or `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Size the spinner to its container. {#size-the-spinner-to-its-container}

A small control takes the `size={16}` spinner; `size={48}` dwarfs the label it replaces.

Do: Small spinner in a compact row.
Don't: Large spinner in a compact row.

### Use invert on dark surfaces. {#use-invert-on-dark-surfaces}

Inherit takes the text color around it; on a dark ground use invert so it
stays visible. There is no color prop: a spinner is not a status color.

Do: Invert on a dark surface.
Don't: Inherit on a dark surface.

### Show one spinner per wait. {#show-one-spinner-per-wait}

Several spinners on one view compete for attention; show one for the whole load.

Do: A single spinner.
Don't: A spinner on every block.

### Show a busy button with its own loading state. {#show-a-busy-button-with-its-own-loading-state}

Do: isLoading puts the spinner inside the button and blocks it.
Don't: A loose spinner beside a button that can still be pressed.

## Accessibility

- **It announces itself as a status.** `role="status"` is the default, with a
  visually hidden label: "Loading" unless `label` names something more
  specific.
- **A status region is only announced when it changes.** A spinner rendered
  into a region that was already on the page is announced; one that arrives
  with a whole new screen usually is not. If the wait matters, put the live
  region where it will still be there afterward and swap its contents.
- **Say what is loading when it is not obvious.** "Loading" beside a form is
  fine; "Loading" as the only thing on a page needs a specific `label`.
- **Reduced motion is handled.** The ring holds still under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, and the hidden status label still names the wait.

## Related

- `Button`: use when a button is busy by setting its `isLoading` prop rather than placing a loose `Spinner` beside it.
- Loading: use when choosing wait thresholds and loading states across a view.

Same group: `ProgressBar` · `ProgressRing` · `Skeleton`

## Parts

1. **Ring.** A circle with one side open, turning. Its stroke is an eighth of the diameter.
2. **Label.** Visually hidden text read as a status, "Loading" unless `label` names more.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The ring swings on the loop spring. Under reduced motion it holds still, and the hidden label still names the wait. |
| Hovered | None. It is not a control. |
| Pressed | None. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. Inside a disabled control, `inherit` takes that control's color. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Ring | `currentColor`; `--ds-icon-inverse` for `invert`. |
| Size | `--spinner-size-sm` (16), `--spinner-size-md` (24), `--spinner-size-lg` (48), on the size scale (`--size-100`, `--size-150`, `--size-300`), read through `--plus-spinner-size`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Say what is loading when it is not obvious: "Loading session plans". | Leave a bare "Loading" as the only thing on a page. |
| Keep the label to a few words. | Write a sentence in the label. |

## Props

|------|------|---------|-------------|

Use `Spinner` when the wait is short, indeterminate, and the user has nothing
to do but wait: a submit in flight, a panel fetching on open. For a wait under
about 300 ms, show nothing so the indicator does not flicker.

stays visible. There is no color prop: a spinner is not a status color.

Do: Invert on a dark surface.
Don't: Inherit on a dark surface.

Several spinners on one view compete for attention; show one for the whole load.

Do: A single spinner.
Don't: A spinner on every block.

# SplitButton

Split button: a primary action joined to a chevron that opens a menu of related actions. Composed from two children — a `Button` for the action and an `IconButton` (chevron) for the menu trigger — each carrying its own appearance, spacing and state; `SplitButton` only draws the seam between them and groups them for assistive tech.

**Import:** `import { SplitButton } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SplitButton/SplitButton.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SplitButton/SplitButton.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Spacing, MenuState, States, HoveredState, PressedState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/SplitButton/SplitButton.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `SplitButton` when one action is clearly primary and a few related variations belong in an attached menu, such as "Send" with "Send and close" or "Save as draft".

## Motion

SplitButton reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | As Button; its menu is a Popup. |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The menu fades in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The menu fades in place, the same as the enter. |

## Alternatives

- For a connected row of actions with no single primary, use `ButtonGroup`.
- For a single trigger that opens a menu of actions without a separate primary button, use `DropdownMenu`.
- For a single action with no menu, use `Button`.

## Best practices

### Keep the two halves joined. {#keep-the-two-halves-joined}

The primary action and the menu trigger share one outline and one height.

Do: One outline around both halves.
Don't: Two separate buttons with a gap.

### The menu holds related actions only. {#the-menu-holds-related-actions-only}

Every menu item is a variation of the primary action: "Save", then "Save as draft" and "Save as template". "Delete account" or "Invite tutor" belong somewhere else.

### Put the common action on the face. {#put-the-common-action-on-the-face}

The half people use most sits on the face; the rarer ones go in the menu.

Do: "Save" on the face.
Don't: The rarely used "Save as template" on the face.

### Match appearance and spacing on both children yourself. {#match-appearance-and-spacing-on-both-children-yourself}

`SplitButton` draws the seam but sets no styling of its own. Pass the same
`appearance` and `spacing` to the `Button` and the chevron `IconButton` so
the control reads as one piece.

Do: Both halves use the primary appearance.
Don't: The two halves disagree on appearance, so they read as two controls.

```jsx
<SplitButton>
    <Button text="Send" onClick={send} appearance="primary" />
    <IconButton icon={<Icon name="chevron-down" size={12} />} label="More send options" appearance="primary" onClick={openMenu} />
</SplitButton>
```

### Open the menu from the chevron's own click handler. {#open-the-menu-from-the-chevron-s-own-click-handler}

`SplitButton` has no menu logic itself — wire the chevron's `onClick` to open
a `Popup` or `DropdownMenu` positioned under it.

## Accessibility

- **A group of two controls.** The wrapper is `role="group"`, so
  assistive technology reads the action and its menu trigger as related. It
  has no name of its own; pass `aria-label` to give it one.
- **Each child keeps its own accessible name.** The primary action needs its
  own label; the chevron's `IconButton` needs a label describing what its
  menu holds, not a generic "more."

## Related

- `ButtonGroup`: use when grouping peer actions with no single primary.
- `DropdownMenu`: use when the chevron opens a menu of action items.
- `Popup`: use when the chevron opens a custom overlay panel.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Action.** A Button for the primary action.
2. **Seam.** The two children meet at a flat edge: inner corners are square, outer corners keep the button radius.
3. **Menu trigger.** An Icon button with a chevron that opens the related actions.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Each child draws its own rest look; the seam joins them. |
| Hovered | Set independently on each child. |
| Pressed | Set independently on each child. |
| Focused | The focused child rises above its neighbor so its ring is not covered. |
| Disabled | Set independently on each child. |
| Loading | Set independently on each child. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Seam | 1: `--border-width-default` in `--ds-border` (default) or `--ds-border-inverse` (primary). |
| Outer corners | 6: `--button-radius-default`. Compact 4: `--button-radius-compact`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label the main action with a verb and its object: "Publish page". | A bare "Go" or "More". |
| Name the menu trigger for what it opens: "More publish options". | "Menu", "Arrow" or "Chevron". |
| Use sentence case on both halves. | Title case or all capitals. |
| List the alternatives in the menu in the same voice as the main action: "Publish and notify". | Menu items that are not variations of the main action. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node (required) | — | Two Button-family elements: the primary action and the menu trigger. |
| `className` | string | — | — |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Tokens touched

`--border-width-default` · `--ds-border` · `--ds-border-inverse`

# Spotlight

Spotlight: a one-step onboarding callout anchored to a `SpotlightTarget`, drawn on `Popover.Positioner` from `@base-ui/react`.

Also asked as: onboarding, feature tour, coach mark, new feature highlight, walkthrough.

**Import:** `import { Spotlight } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.stories.jsx` — Basic, WithMedia, LinkAction, PrimaryAction, SecondaryAction, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, BestPracticesLive, MotionOpenAndClose, MotionReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `spatial.default` + `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Spotlight` to point out one feature the first time someone can use it:
a new button, a changed control, a place to start. It is a single step or a
short, explicit sequence with a `stepCount`, not an ongoing help system.

## Motion

Spotlight reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Each coachmark step is Step. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |

## Alternatives

- For a message that stays in the page until resolved, use `SectionMessage`.
- For a short label on hover or focus over a control, use `Tooltip`.
- For an interactive anchored overlay with arbitrary content, use `Popup`.

## Best practices

### Name the feature, then say what to do. {#name-the-feature-then-say-what-to-do}

A headline names the thing; the body is one sentence.

Do: Short headline, one-sentence body.
Don't: A greeting and a paragraph.

### Show a step count only in a tour. {#show-a-step-count-only-in-a-tour}

One step alone has nothing to count.

Do: Step count in a multi-step tour.
Don't: Step count on a single tip.

### Keep the secondary action quieter than the primary. {#keep-the-secondary-action-quieter-than-the-primary}

The primary action leads as the filled action; the secondary is the outlined one.
Either `SpotlightAction` can take `href` to navigate.

Do: The outlined secondary next to the filled primary.
Don't: Two filled, competing buttons.

### Wrap the target and the spotlight in one `SpotlightProvider`. {#wrap-the-target-and-the-spotlight-in-one-spotlightprovider}

`SpotlightTarget` and `Spotlight` share an anchor through context, so both
need to sit inside the same provider. Pass `target` directly only when the
anchor comes from outside that tree.

```jsx
<SpotlightProvider>
    <SpotlightTarget>
        <Button text="Create" />
    </SpotlightTarget>
    <Spotlight headline="Create a new board" onDismiss={() => setSeen(true)}>
        Start a new board from here.
    </Spotlight>
</SpotlightProvider>
```

### Dismiss it once, and remember that it was seen. {#dismiss-it-once-and-remember-that-it-was-seen}

`isOpen` is yours to control. Store whatever "seen" state applies, such as a
user preference or a session flag, so the same spotlight does not reopen on
every visit.

## Accessibility

- **A dialog, not a tooltip.** The spotlight is a `Popup` with a title and a
  description, read together when it opens.
- **The dismiss control is the first focusable element.** Tab reaches it
  before the body or the actions, so closing never requires finding the
  target again.
- **Escape closes it.** Dismissing with Escape or the close button calls
  `onDismiss`.

## Related

- `Popup`: use when anchoring an overlay dialog or panel to a trigger element.
- `CloseButton`: use when rendering the inverse dismiss control in the spotlight header.

Same group: `Banner` · `Dialog` · `EmptyState` · `Flag` · `InlineMessage` · `NotificationItem` · `SectionMessage`

## Parts

1. **Target.** `SpotlightTarget` wraps the element the spotlight points at and
   shares its anchor with the `Spotlight` through a `SpotlightProvider`.
2. **Headline.** The dialog title, read first.
3. **Dismiss.** The shared `CloseButton` in its `inverse` tone, in the header, the dialog's first focusable element. `dismissible={false}` leaves it out.
4. **Media.** An optional image above the body.
5. **Body.** The `children` text.
6. **Step count.** A short label like "1 of 3".
7. **Actions.** A secondary and a primary `SpotlightAction`, the secondary first. Each takes `onClick`, or `href` to render a link.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Popup on the brand bold fill with inverse text. |
| Hovered | Dismiss takes the inverse hovered layer. |
| Pressed | Dismiss takes the inverse pressed layer. |
| Focused | Dismiss and actions show the inverse focus ring; see Border. |
| Disabled | Not supported. |
| Dismissed | The popup closes and `onDismiss` fires. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Surface | `--ds-background-brand-bold`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--spotlight-width`, `--popup-radius`, `--spotlight-pad` |
| Text | `--ds-text-inverse`, `--heading-sm`, `--body-default`; step count `--body-sm` |
| Dismiss | `--ds-icon-inverse`, `--ds-interaction-inverse-hovered`, `--ds-interaction-inverse-pressed`, `--radius-md` |
| Primary action | `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-text` |
| Secondary action | `--ds-text-inverse` text and `--border-width-default` edge |
| Actions | `--radius-lg`, `--radius-lg`, `--radius-xxl`, `--inline-lg` between |
| Media | `--radius-lg` |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused-inverse` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the feature in the headline: "Create a new board". | Write a headline that only says "New". |
| Use one or two short lines in the body. | Explain the whole feature. |
| Label actions with verbs: "Next", "Skip", "Got it". | Use "OK" for every step. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `target` | object or func | — | The anchor element, when not read from the nearest SpotlightProvider's SpotlightTarget. |
| `placement` | enum | `'bottom'` | — |
| `headline` | node | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | — |
| `media` | node | — | — |
| `stepCount` | node | — | — |
| `primaryAction` | node | — | A `SpotlightAction`, rendered after `secondaryAction`. |
| `secondaryAction` | node | — | — |
| `dismissible` | bool | `true` | — |
| `onDismiss` | func | — | — |
| `isOpen` | bool | `true` | — |
| `className` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`placement`** — `top` · `top-start` · `top-end` · `bottom` · `bottom-start` · `bottom-end` · `left` · `right` · `auto`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

`--body-default` · `--body-sm` · `--ds-background-brand-bold` · `--ds-interaction-inverse-hovered` · `--ds-interaction-inverse-pressed` · `--ds-shadow-overlay` · `--ds-surface-overlay` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-inverse` · `--heading-sm` · `--inline-lg` · `--plus-overlay-origin` · `--popup-radius` · `--radius-lg` · `--spotlight-footer-stack` · `--spotlight-gap` · `--spotlight-media-height` · `--spotlight-pad` · `--spotlight-screen-pad` · `--spotlight-width` · `--transform-origin`
