# StaticTable

The Static table: a fixed grid people read. Rows rest or are highlighted (`rowStates`); there is nothing to sort, select, page or expand, so it takes no hover and no row click. Reach for the Dynamic table when rows act or people work the data. Takes `headers` and `rows`, plus `size`, `frame`, `titleColumn`, `summary`, `verticalLines` and `striped`.

Also asked as: basic table.

**Import:** `import { StaticTable } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Table (`ds guide table`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/StaticTable/StaticTable.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/StaticTable/StaticTable.stories.jsx` — Overview, Striped, Bordered, Sizes, FramedAndLines, Cells, RowStates, Summary, Static, HeadCells, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled, Invalid, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/StaticTable/StaticTable.mdx`

## Usage

Use `StaticTable` for a grid people only read: a record, a summary, a rate
card.

## Alternatives

- For a table people sort or filter or page, use `Table`.

## Best practices

### Right-align numbers. {#right-align-numbers}

Do: Numbers align by their digits, so the amounts line up.
Don't: Left-aligned numbers do not line up.

### Name the record in one column. {#name-the-record-in-one-column}

Do: `titleColumn` marks the one column that names the row.
Don't: Emphasis on every cell, so nothing stands out.

### Keep a cell to one line. {#keep-a-cell-to-one-line}

Do: Long text truncates with an ellipsis and shows in full in a tooltip.
Don't: Every cell wrapped, so rows grow uneven.

## Accessibility

- **It is a real table.** Headers are `th` in a `thead`, so a screen reader announces the column for each cell.
- **Rows are not controls.** Nothing in a Static table takes focus; a table people interact with is a Dynamic table.
- **State is not color alone.** A selected row sets `aria-selected`, a disabled row `aria-disabled`.
- **Truncated text keeps its full value.** A cell that ends in an ellipsis shows the whole text in a tooltip.

## Related

- `StatusTag`: use when showing a record's condition inside a cell.
- `CountTag`: use when showing a numeric count inside a cell.
- Table: use when choosing between Static, Dynamic and Tree tables.

Same group: `Code` · `CodeBlock` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `TreeTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Head cell.** A label with an optional type icon.
2. **Row.** Cells in a band; rest, highlighted, selected or disabled.
3. **Cell.** Text, a number, an icon or any node, with optional secondary text and an `elemBefore` slot.
4. **Summary row.** One calculation per column, muted, with no rule under it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Clear row; a striped table shades alternate rows. |
| Hovered | Not applicable; a Static table never hovers. |
| Pressed | Not applicable; a Static table never presses. |
| Focused | Not applicable; a row is not a control. |
| Disabled | Disabled ink, no pointer events, `aria-disabled`. |
| Invalid | A cell with `state: 'error'` takes the danger ink. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Row hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` |
| Selected row | `--ds-background-selected`, `--ds-background-selected-hovered`, `--ds-background-selected-pressed` |
| Highlighted row | `--ds-background-warning-bold` washed |
| Disabled ink | `--ds-text-disabled` |
| Error ink | `--ds-text-danger` |
| Hairlines | `--ds-border` |
| Row height | `--row-height-sm`, `--row-height-md`, `--row-height-lg` |

# StatusTag

A filled label for the condition something is in, such as "Needs review" or "Overdue". It is never a button; its appearance carries the meaning.

Also asked as: lozenge, pill, state label.

**Import:** `import { StatusTag } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Page (`ds guide page`); Panel (`ds guide panel`)

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/StatusTag/StatusTag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/StatusTag/StatusTag.stories.jsx` — ColoredMaterial, Styles, WithCount, TrailingMetricAppearance, IconBefore, Truncation, NarrowContainer, NeverAButton, PinnedWeight, UnknownValuesFallBack, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/StatusTag/StatusTag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `StatusTag` for the condition something is in when that condition can change:
completed, needs review, missed, in progress. It is the same component whether
the system calculated the state or a person set it.

Use `spacing="default"` (`20`) in rows, lists, tables and sentences, and
`spacing="spacious"` (`32`) beside a heading.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Neutral | Not started. |
| Success | Done. Example: "Completed". |
| Warning | Needs attention. Example: "Needs review". |
| Danger | Failed or missed. Example: "Missed". |
| Info | In progress. Example: "In progress". |
| Discovery | New. |

## Alternatives

- For a number on its own, use `CountTag`.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a change over time such as "+3 vs last week", use `ChangeTag`.
- For a category or subject or person, use `Tag` or `CompetencyTag`.

## Best practices

### Match the appearance to the meaning. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-meaning}

Color carries the verdict, so success never labels a problem. Each appearance
means one thing (see the guidance above). There is no color prop; a category
with a color is a `Tag`.

Do: Success for a finished thing.
Don't: Danger on a finished thing.

### Keep labels to one or two words. {#keep-labels-to-one-or-two-words}

A status is read at a glance; a sentence belongs in the row text.

Do: On track.
Don't: A sentence in the tag.

### Show one status per object. {#show-one-status-per-object}

Two statuses on one object force people to decide which is true.

Do: One status per row.
Don't: Two competing statuses.

### Nest a count instead of placing one beside it. {#nest-a-count-instead-of-placing-one-beside-it}

Do: One label; the number reads as part of it.
Don't: Two labels that read as unrelated.

### Give the metric its own appearance when it means something else. {#give-the-metric-its-own-appearance-when-it-means-something-else}

`trailingMetricAppearance` defaults to the Status tag's own appearance. Set it
only when the number carries a different meaning from the status, such as a
success status with a danger count of failures.

### Edit in the field, not on the label. {#edit-in-the-field-not-on-the-label}

A Status tag never opens a menu. Where a status can be changed, the field around
it uses a `Select` whose options are grouped To do · In progress · Complete ·
Exception · Failed, each group with one appearance (neutral · info · success ·
warning · danger).

## Accessibility

- **Read as its text.** A Status tag is a `span` with no role, so a screen reader
  announces its text and nothing suggests it can be pressed. An `onClick` is
  dropped with a development warning.
- **Not a tab stop, unless truncated.** When the label is clipped, the Status tag
  takes focus so a keyboard user can reach the tooltip holding the full text;
  pointer users get the same tooltip on hover. The full text is always in the
  DOM, so a screen reader hears all of it.
- **Not color alone.** A state can add `iconBefore` where color alone is
  not enough. Icons are decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
- **An edge on any surface.** The inset border keeps a pale fill visible
  on white and on gray; in forced-colors mode it becomes a real border.

## Related

- `CountTag`: use when nesting a metric inside `StatusTag` through `trailingMetric`.
- `Select`: use when letting a person change a record's status in a form or table cell.

Same group: `ChangeTag` · `CompetencyTag` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `Tag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Icon before.** Optional: a Font Awesome Free icon by name.
2. **Label.** The condition, in a word or two. Past `maxWidth` it ends in an ellipsis and the full text is a tooltip.
3. **Trailing metric.** Optional: a 16 `CountTag` nested inside, with its own appearance when it means something else.
4. **Fill.** The appearance's tinted ground with its words and an inset edge one step darker.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. A status that can change is edited in the field around it. |
| Hovered, pressed | None. It is a label, not a control; the thing around it is what responds. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. A truncated label takes focus only so a keyboard user can reach the tooltip with its full text. |
| Disabled | None. A label is never dimmed; a disabled thing is described by the control beside it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Height | `--label-height-md` (20), or `--control-md` (32) when spacious. |
| Padding and gap | `--pad-x-xs` on the leading edge, 2 on the trailing edge and between icon and label, `--stack-sm` inside the text; spacious `--pad-x-md` with 6 behind. |
| Corner | `--radius-md`; spacious `--radius-lg`. |
| Neutral | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--ds-text`, edge `--ds-background-neutral-pressed`. |
| Success, warning, danger | The same three for each: `--ds-background-success`, `--ds-text-success`, edge `--ds-background-success-pressed`. |
| Info and discovery | `--ds-background-information` and `--ds-background-competency-mastering-content`, with their text and pressed steps. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the condition: "In review", "Overdue", "Approved". | Write an action: "Review now". A status is not a button. |
| Use one or two words, in sentence case. | Write a sentence or end with a period. |
| Keep one wording for one condition across the product. | Use "Done" here and "Complete" there for the same state. |
| Let a trailing metric be a plain number. | Put words in the metric. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node (required) | — | The status text, as people say it: "Needs review", "Due tomorrow". |
| `appearance` | enum | `'neutral'` | The meaning. Info is Tertiary; discovery is the curriculum purple. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` (20) in rows, lists and sentences; `spacious` (32) beside a heading. |
| `material` | enum | — | Colored material for a status over media or a material surface: bold or subtle, in the appearance's color. Not for neutral. |
| `iconBefore` | string | — | One icon before the label: a Font Awesome Free name (`circle-check`). |
| `trailingMetric` | number or string | — | A small count at the end of the tag, a 16 Count tag nested inside it. Hidden at 0. |
| `trailingMetricAppearance` | oneOf | — | The Count tag's appearance. Defaults to the Status tag's own. |
| `maxWidth` | number or string | `200` | The widest the Status tag grows, in px or any CSS length, and never wider than its container. Past it the label ends in an ellipsis and the full text is a tooltip. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the tag element beside the component's own. |
| `id` | string | — | The `id` attribute of the tag element. |

## Variants

**`appearance`** — `neutral` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` · `info` · `discovery`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `spacious`

**`material`** — `bold` · `subtle`

**`trailingMetricAppearance`** — `neutral` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` · `info` · `discovery`

`--body-default` · `--body-sm` · `--border-width-default` · `--ds-background-competency-mastering-content` · `--ds-background-competency-mastering-content-pressed` · `--ds-background-danger` · `--ds-background-danger-pressed` · `--ds-background-information` · `--ds-background-information-pressed` · `--ds-background-neutral` · `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` · `--ds-background-success` · `--ds-background-success-pressed` · `--ds-background-warning` · `--ds-background-warning-pressed` · `--ds-text` · `--ds-text-competency-mastering-content` · `--ds-text-danger` · `--ds-text-information` · `--ds-text-success` · `--ds-text-warning` · `--icon-md` · `--icon-sm` · `--image-xs` · `--pad-x-md` · `--pad-x-xs` · `--plus-status-edge` · `--plus-status-height` · `--plus-status-icon-box` · `--plus-status-max` · `--radius-control-md` · `--radius-md` · `--stack-sm` · `--tag-gap` · `--tag-gap-compact` · `--tag-pad-x-end` · `--tag-pad-x-end-compact`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Suggestion

Suggestion: a tag for a value or question the system proposes, which a person accepts or leaves.

Also asked as: ai chip.

**Import:** `import { Suggestion } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/ai/Suggestion/Suggestion.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/ai/Suggestion/Suggestion.stories.jsx` — Types, InATagRow, Callbacks, StateLayers, FocusRing, DisabledBesideTags, AcceptIntoTags, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/ai/Suggestion/Suggestion.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Suggestion` when the system proposes a value and a person decides whether
to take it: an AI-suggested focus area beside the ones already chosen, or a
suggested question beside a chat box. Put it in the row where the accepted
value will land, after the tags already there.

### Type guidance

| Type | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Insert | The default. Adds a value to the field, in place; `onAccept` hands back the `value`. Leads with a plus. Example: "Fractions". |
| Prompt | Sends or fills text, starting a conversation; `onAccept` hands back the `text`. Leads with a sparkle wand. Example: "Summarize". |

Use `Tag` for a value that is already in the field. Use `Button` for an action
that is not a proposed value.

## Motion

Suggestion reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place. |
| exit | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Accepting folds it away; dismissing fades. |

## Best practices

### Name the action. {#name-the-action}

Name an insert suggestion for its value. Start a prompt label with a short verb
and pass the full request as `text`.

Do: A short verb.
Don't: A sentence in the tag.

### Pick insert or prompt by outcome. {#pick-insert-or-prompt-by-outcome}

Insert changes the content in place; prompt starts a conversation.

Do: Insert for an in-place edit.
Don't: Prompt for an in-place edit.

### Show an unavailable action as disabled. {#show-an-unavailable-action-as-disabled}

Keep unavailable suggestions visible and disabled. `isDisabled` disables one;
a disabled field or `TagGroup` disables all through `TagContext`, shared with Tag.

Do: Disabled when unavailable.
Don't: Active with nothing to do.

### Let the field decide what happens next. {#let-the-field-decide-what-happens-next}

`onAccept` returns the value (insert) or text (prompt). The field adds a Tag,
sends a message or fills the text box, then removes the suggestion; the suggestion
does not change itself.

Do: Insert hands back the value; the field turns it into a Tag.
Don't: A Tag styled as a suggestion is not a button, so nobody can accept it with a keyboard.

## Accessibility

- **A real button.** It takes focus, and Enter or Space accepts it.
- **Disabled is a disabled button.** It keeps its name, is announced as
  disabled, is skipped by Tab, and never calls `onAccept`.
- **Named for what pressing it does.** An insert suggestion is announced as
  `Add {label}, suggested`, so a screen-reader user knows pressing it adds a
  value. A prompt is not added to anything, so it is announced as
  `{label}, suggested`.
- **The glyph is decorative.** The plus and the sparkle wand are hidden from
  assistive technology; the name already says what the suggestion does.
- **Focus is a ring, not a fill**: a 2px Focus Ring 2px outside the edge, so
  focus never reads as pressed.

## Related

- For a value already in the field, use `Tag`, inside a `TagGroup`.

Same group: `AiChat` · `AiIcon` · `AiMessage` · `GenerativeBorder` · `PromptInput` · `PromptStarters`

## Parts

1. **Glyph.** A plus for an `insert` suggestion, a sparkles wand for a `prompt`. It says which kind of proposal this is.
2. **Label.** The proposed value or prompt, short.
3. **Edge.** Dashed, in the discovery border: the system proposed it, the person has not accepted it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A dashed edge on a clear ground. The accessible name is "Add Fractions, suggested" or "Summarize, suggested". |
| Hovered | `--ds-background-discovery`. |
| Pressed | `--ds-background-discovery-hovered`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring 2px off the dashed edge. The ground stays clear, so focus never reads as pressed. |
| Disabled | Disabled ground and words, no focus, and `onAccept` never fires. A disabled field or tag group disables every suggestion in it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Edge | `--ds-border-discovery`, dashed, `--border-width-default` wide. |
| Words and glyph | `--ds-text-discovery` and `--ds-icon-discovery`. |
| Hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-discovery` and `--ds-background-discovery-hovered`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` wide and offset. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled`, `--ds-text-disabled`, `--ds-icon-disabled`. |
| Box | The same height (`--label-height-md`, 20), padding (`--pad-x-xs`) and radius (`--radius-md`) as Tag, so it fits the row where the value will land. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use the value itself: "Fractions". | Write an instruction: "Click to add Fractions". |
| Keep a prompt to a few words that read as a request: "Summarize". | Send a whole paragraph as the label. |
| Offer a few. Three to five fit a row. | Fill a row with suggestions until the real tags are lost. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `label` | string (required) | — | The proposed value's words. The accessible name is built from it. |
| `type` | enum | `'insert'` | `insert` adds a value to the field; `prompt` sends or fills text. |
| `value` | any | — | `insert` only: what `onAccept` receives. Defaults to `label`. |
| `text` | string | — | `prompt` only: the text `onAccept` receives. Defaults to `label`. |
| `onAccept` | func | — | Called with the value (insert) or the text (prompt), then the click event. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | Disables this suggestion. A disabled field or TagGroup disables all of its suggestions through `TagContext`. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Fires on press, before `onAccept`. It never replaces `onAccept`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`type`** — `insert` · `prompt`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

# Table

Section header carries the title and the toolbar. Under the header come the table, then the `footer` slot (range, page size, Pagination), and the empty state box in place of both when there are no rows. The template draws no default footer: the slot is the contract. Pass the table as `children` (a `StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` or `TreeTable`), or name a `kind` and pass its props as `tableProps`. Choose the kind by what people do with the rows: nesting is a Tree table; sort, filter, select, page, expand or row actions is a Dynamic table; otherwise it is a Static table. A Dynamic or Tree table already draws its own footer and empty state, so the template's `footer`, `emptyState` and `empty` serve a Static table and are not drawn around the other two. Every other prop goes to the Section (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `views`, `search`, `filters`).

Also asked as: list of records, data table on a page, sortable list, records with filters, rows and columns, grid, table pattern.

**Import:** `import { Table } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Modal (`ds guide modal`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); Search (`ds guide search`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Table/Table.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Table/Table.stories.jsx` — StaticKind, DynamicKind, TreeKind, TableAsChild, EmptyState, EmptyHiddenByFilter, EmptyNothingToCreate, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Table/Table.mdx`

**Motion:** selection `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

A table sits in a Section and spans it. Its first and last cells sit flush with the section edge. The Section header carries the views, then Search and the "Field: value" filters, and once a filter is applied, the record count. The bulk bar is never in the Section header: while rows are selected, a Dynamic table's head row becomes it, so the header rows stay put. Empty and no results replace the whole table so the Section header stays usable; loading and error states happen inside the table, under its header. Paging stays under the rows, inside the same Section.

### Type guidance

Choose by what people do with the rows. Read the questions in order and stop at the first yes.

| Question | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Does any row nest under another? Nesting wins, even when the table is interactive. | Tree table |
| Can people act on the table: sort, filter, select, page, expand rows or use row actions? | Dynamic table |
| Otherwise, people only read it. | Static table |

Search, filters and actions sit in the Section header: `<Table title="Students" views={...} search={...} filters={[...]} count="340 students" kind="dynamic" tableProps={...} />`. Pass the table as `children` instead of `kind` when you build it yourself.

## Motion

Table reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| selection | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Ticking a row turns the head row into the bulk bar: labels cross-fade, same row, same height, nothing slides. Selected rows take the selected fill. The view bar above never moves. |

## Best practices

### Put a plain table in a Section. {#put-a-plain-table-in-a-section}

Do: The table spans the Section under its header: no frame, no card, no padding of its own.
Don't: The table sits inside its own frame with padding; it stops lining up with the Section and the Section header.

### Put nothing between the header and the head row. {#put-nothing-between-the-header-and-the-head-row}

Do: Search and filters live in the Section header rows, with the record count once a filter is applied; the head row follows directly.
Don't: A second toolbar sits between the Section header and the head row; the table has no toolbar of its own.

### One table per block. {#one-table-per-block}

Never mix a Static, Dynamic or Tree table in one Section either.

Do: One table per Section, with its own header, so people always know which rows its Search and filters act on.
Don't: Two tables share one Section and one header; search and filters no longer say which table they act on.

### Use a Dynamic table for rows people act on. {#use-a-dynamic-table-for-rows-people-act-on}

Do: A roster people act on as a Dynamic table: sortable heads, checkboxes, a pager, and bulk actions in the head row while rows are selected.
Don't: A roster people act on as a Static table; with no sort, selection or paging, 340 students become one long scroll.

### Use a Tree table for a hierarchy. {#use-a-tree-table-for-a-hierarchy}

Do: Classes nest under their school and students under their class; each level indents and keeps the columns.
Don't: A hierarchy faked with expandable rows: the classes and students lose their columns and can't be sorted or selected.

## Accessibility

- Name every column with a head cell. Head cells are labels for a column, so they use Heading/xxs rather than a heading level.
- Mark the sorted column with `aria-sort`, and give every icon-only control a name, such as "Actions for Ava Thompson".
- Mark a selected row with `aria-selected="true"`. That attribute belongs to a row of a table with `role="grid"`.
- Selection is never color alone. The row's checkbox is checked, and the head row says "2 selected".
- A region that scrolls takes keyboard focus, so people can scroll it without a pointer. That covers a region with `maxHeight` and one with a sticky column.
- When empty, the empty state replaces the table with no table roles left behind, and keeps the table's accessible name when one was provided.
- Name the table with its `label`, or `label` on the template for the empty state box, when no caption names it.

## Related

- Section: the header rows that sit above every table.
- Static table, Dynamic table and Tree table: the three table components the template takes.
- Pagination: the pager that fills the footer slot.
- Card: a table never sits inside a card.

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section`

## Parts

1. **Head row.** Names the columns. Its rule is the bold border.
2. **Rows.** The data you pass as `tbody`. Each draws a thin rule, and there is no zebra striping.
3. **Footer** (optional). The `footer` slot under the rows, aligned to the end: the range, the page-size Select and Pagination. The template draws no default footer: the slot is the contract. On a narrow screen its parts wrap onto lines of their own, and the pager stays at the end. It hides while the empty state shows. A Dynamic or Tree table draws its own footer and empty state, so the template's `footer`, `emptyState` and `empty` are for a Static table.
4. **Empty state.** The `emptyState` slot, which replaces the whole table (head row, caption and footer included) when `empty` is true; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally.

### States

Row states are layered over each cell's fill, never swapped for it.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill of its own: the table shows what it sits on. |
| Hovered | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Focused | A scroll region takes keyboard focus and draws the `--ds-border-focused` ring. |
| Disabled | A table has no disabled state. Disable the controls in a row. |
| Selected | A row with `aria-selected="true"` takes `--ds-background-selected` across the whole row, with `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps and no stripe on its leading edge. |
| Empty | The empty state replaces the whole table; no head row or footer stays. |

### Tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-border`, `--border-width-default` | color, 1 | The rule under each row. |
| `--ds-border-bold` | color | The rule under the head row. |
| `--ds-text`, `--body-default` | 14/20 | Body cells. |
| `--ds-text-subtle`, `--heading-xxs` | color, type | Head cells, message rows, and empty-state wrapper text. |
| `--table-pad-x-cell`, `--table-pad-y-cell` | length | Cell padding, message row padding, and plain empty-state wrapper padding. |
| Footer slot (Table template): `--table-inline`, `--table-footer-height` | 8, 48 | The gap between the table and the footer slot, the gap between controls in the footer, and the footer row height. |
| `--table-empty-surface`, `--table-empty-radius` | color, 16 | The sunken background and card-rounded corners of the empty state box. |
| `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `-pressed` | color | A hovered and a pressed row. |
| `--ds-background-selected`, `-hovered`, `-pressed` | color | A selected row. |
| `--ds-shadow-overflow` | shadow | A sticky edge, only while content is scrolled under it. |
| `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` | color | The fill of sticky cells, so they match what the table sits on. |
| `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` | focus ring | The ring of a scroll region. |
| `--row-height-md` | 40 | The least height of the message row. |
| Footer the shell draws (Dynamic/Tree): `--stack-md`, `--stack-sm` | 8, 4 | Gap between a Dynamic or Tree table and the footer it draws itself, and inside message and empty-state wrappers. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name every column with a short head, in sentence case: "Last session". | A blank head, or one in all caps. |
| Give the count in words in the header once a filter is applied: "340 students". | A count in the head row or under the table. |
| An empty message that says what will appear and the first action: "No members yet", "Invite a member". | An empty table body with no message. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `kind` | enum | — | The kind of table to draw when no table is passed as `children` |
| `tableProps` | object | — | Props for the table a `kind` draws: its head, rows, label and state |
| `children` | node | — | The table itself, a `StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` or `TreeTable`; wins over `kind` |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer slot under a Static table (range, page-size Select, Pagination); the template draws no default. Not drawn around a Dynamic or Tree table, which has its own; hidden while the empty state shows |
| `emptyState` | node | — | Empty-state slot: replaces a Static table and its footer when `empty` is true; a Dynamic or Tree table draws its own |
| `empty` | bool | `false` | Replace the table with the `emptyState` slot; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally |
| `label` | string | — | The table's accessible name, kept on the empty state box when the table is replaced |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `title` | node | — | The Section title above the table; passed to the Section |
| `actions` | node | — | Actions slot in the Section's title row; passed to the Section |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles on the Section; passed to the Section |

## Variants

**`kind`** — `static` · `dynamic` · `tree`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--table-inline`

<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# Tabs

A tab strip with its panels. Tabs go into the tablist and every other child, usually Panels, renders after it.

Also asked as: switch views, tab bar, segmented, view switcher.

**Import:** `import { Tabs } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Modal (`ds guide modal`); Page (`ds guide page`); Panel (`ds guide panel`); Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`)

**Governed by:** Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.stories.jsx` — Overview, Layout, Alignment, Appearance, UnderlineRadius, WithCount, WithPanels, InteractionStates, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Selected, SelectedPill, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/navigation/Tabs/Tabs.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Tabs` for the tab bar that switches between sibling views on the same page
— a student's Overview / Sessions / Progress, or the sections of an admin page.
Compose it from `Tabs.Tab` children, and declare a `Tabs.Panel` alongside each
one when the tab's content should be owned by the component rather than rendered
separately.

It can be uncontrolled (`defaultActiveKey`) or controlled (`activeKey` plus
`onSelect`). `alignment` covers left, center, right and `justified`, which
stretches the tabs to fill the bar. `appearance` is `default` (an underline) or
`pill` (a filled, rounded selected tab); `spacing` is `default` (`--control-md`) or
`compact` (`--control-sm`).

## Motion

Tabs reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Switch views | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | The indicator glides; both tab bodies slide together toward the chosen tab, no fade. Pill views: the fill glides and the content swaps in place. |

## Alternatives

- For navigating to a different page in a hierarchy, use `Breadcrumb` or `Sidebar`.
- For more options than fit on one strip without wrapping, use `Select`.
- For a second-level choice inside a view, use `PopupSelect`.
- For filtering a list rather than switching between views, use `FilterMenu` or `RadioGroup`.

## Best practices

### Pass `onSelect` whenever `activeKey` is controlled. {#pass-onselect-whenever-activekey-is-controlled}

```jsx
// Incorrect — activeKey pins the bar and nothing updates it.
<Tabs activeKey="overview">
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Give every `Tabs.Tab` an `eventKey`. {#give-every-tabs-tab-an-eventkey}

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no eventKey, there is no key to compare against activeKey,
// so the tab never shows as selected and onSelect fires with nothing useful.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab>Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Keep the labels short and parallel. {#keep-the-labels-short-and-parallel}

Each label is one or two words naming a view of the same subject: Overview, Sessions, Progress. Parallel wording lets people scan the strip without reading it.

Do: Short nouns for views of the same subject.
Don't: Mixed verbs and phrases that do not scan.

### Choose the appearance by weight, not taste. {#choose-the-appearance-by-weight-not-taste}

The underline suits a strip that sits above page content. The pill suits a strip inside a card or toolbar, where a filled selected tab reads as a control.

Do: A pill strip inside a card reads as a control.
Don't: The page-level underline inside a card, where it reads as a stray rule.

### Keep labels the same across visits. {#keep-labels-the-same-across-visits}

A label names a view. A count or status in it changes the name and breaks the parallel wording.

Do: The label names the view.
Don't: Counts and status in the label.

### Keep one tab system per page and use `PopupSelect` for a second-level choice. {#keep-one-tab-system-per-page-and-use-popupselect-for-a-second-level-choice}

A `pill` strip is a fixed set of views of one subject, decided when the page is designed, so it has no add-view control and people cannot create, rename, reorder or remove a tab. A strip that must grow with the data is a list or a `Select`, not tabs. A page has one tab system: the underline strip under the page header switches the page's sections, and a pill strip inside a card switches that card's views, without stacking two strips of the same kind. For a second-level choice inside a view, use the labeled trigger of `PopupSelect` ("Status: Upcoming") in the view's toolbar.

Do: One strip for the sections; a labeled PopupSelect for the choice inside one.
Don't: A second strip under the first, so two tab systems compete.

### Swap content in place without sliding. {#swap-content-in-place-without-sliding}

Switching tabs is a frequent action. The selected marker transitions quickly, and the content under the strip swaps in place with no slide or fade-through. Reduced motion removes the transition and the marker changes at once.

## Accessibility

- **A real tab widget, always.** `role="tablist"` on the strip, `role="tab"`
  and `aria-selected` on each tab, `aria-controls` pointing at the panel when
  one is declared, and roving tabindex: one stop for the whole strip, with
  Left, Right, Home and End moving selection and focus together. Tabs are real
  `<button>` elements, so activating one pushes no history entry and moves no
  scroll position.
- **A disabled tab stays reachable by the arrow keys**, so its existence is
  discoverable, but is never selected — `isDisabled` keeps it out of
  `activeKey` contention without removing it from the strip's keyboard path.
- **`aria-controls` is omitted rather than dangled.** A `Tabs.Tab` with no
  matching `Tabs.Panel` gets no pointer at all.

## Related

- `PageHeader`: use when placing a page-level `Tabs` strip in the header's `bottomBar` slot.
- `PopupSelect`: use when adding a second-level view choice inside a tab's toolbar.

Same group: `Breadcrumb` · `Link` · `Pagination` · `Sidebar`

## Parts

1. **Tab strip.** A `tablist` of buttons, aligned left, center, right or justified.
2. **Tab.** A button whose label names a view, on one line; the selected one is marked by an underline on the strip's baseline (`default`) or a filled pill (`pill`), whose strip has no baseline.
3. **Baseline.** The hairline under an underline strip that the selected bar sits on.
4. **Panel.** The content one tab controls, shown below the strip.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Subtle ink on a clear ground. |
| Hovered | The subtle neutral hovered fill. |
| Pressed | The subtle neutral pressed fill. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the tab with no fill; see Border. |
| Selected | Selected ink with the underline bar, or the neutral fill with the default ink in `pill`. |
| Disabled | Disabled ink; the tab cannot be pressed or selected. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Tab height | `--control-md` (default), `--control-sm` (compact) |
| Tab padding | `--pad-x-lg`, `--pad-x-md` |
| Ink | `--ds-text-subtle`, selected `--ds-text-selected`, disabled `--ds-text-disabled` |
| Baseline and bar | `--ds-border`, `--border-width-default`; `--ds-border-selected`, `--border-width-selected` |
| Hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed` |
| Selected pill | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--ds-text`; `--ds-background-neutral-hovered`, `--ds-background-neutral-pressed` |
| Gap | `--stack-md`, pill strip `--inline-lg` (12) |
| Panel offset | `--section-stack-sm` |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Use nouns that name the view: “Sessions”. | Use verbs or full sentences. |
| Write labels in sentence case, one to two words. | Use Title Case or labels that wrap. |
| Keep the same labels across visits. | Rename a tab to show a count or status. |
| Order tabs by how often people open them, most used first. | Hide the most used view in the last tab. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | `Tabs.Tab` elements, which fill the tablist, and the `Tabs.Panel` elements that follow it. |
| `alignment` | enum | `'left'` | Horizontal alignment of the tab strip |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | Underline indicator (default), or a pill-shaped selected fill. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` is a 32px tab; `compact` is 24px. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the tabs root, beside `plus-tabs`. |
| `id` | string | — | Id set on the tabs root. |
| `defaultActiveKey` | string or number | — | The `eventKey` of the tab selected at first, for uncontrolled use. |
| `activeKey` | string or number | — | The `eventKey` of the selected tab, for controlled use. Pair it with `onSelect`. |
| `onSelect` | func | — | Called with the newly selected `eventKey` whenever selection moves. |

## Variants

**`alignment`** — `left` · `center` · `right` · `justified`

**`appearance`** — `default` · `pill`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Sub-components

### `Tabs.Tab`

Implemented as `Tab`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `eventKey` | string or number | — | Identifies this tab; matched against the root's `activeKey`/`defaultActiveKey`. |
| `children` | node | — | The tab's label. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | Disables this tab: it cannot be selected. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class on the tab, beside `plus-tab`. |

### `Tabs.Panel`

Implemented as `Panel`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `eventKey` | string or number | — | Matches the `Tab` with the same `eventKey`. |
| `children` | node | — | The content shown while the matching tab is selected. |
| `className` | string | — | Extra class on the panel, beside `plus-tabs-panel`. |

Use `Tabs` for the tab bar that switches between sibling views on the same page
— a student's Overview / Sessions / Progress, or the sections of an admin page.
Compose it from `Tabs.Tab` children, and declare a `Tabs.Panel` alongside each
one when the tab's content should be owned by the component rather than rendered
separately.

It can be uncontrolled (`defaultActiveKey`) or controlled (`activeKey` plus
`onSelect`). `alignment` covers left, center, right and `justified`, which
stretches the tabs to fill the bar. `appearance` is `default` (an underline) or
`pill` (a filled, rounded selected tab); `spacing` is `default` (`--control-md`) or
`compact` (`--control-sm`).
rankedText.best:
### Pass `onSelect` whenever `activeKey` is controlled.

```jsx
// Incorrect — activeKey pins the bar and nothing updates it.
<Tabs activeKey="overview">
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="sessions">Sessions</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Give every `Tabs.Tab` an `eventKey`.

```jsx
// Incorrect — with no eventKey, there is no key to compare against activeKey,
// so the tab never shows as selected and onSelect fires with nothing useful.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab>Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>

// Correct.
<Tabs activeKey={tab} onSelect={setTab}>
  <Tabs.Tab eventKey="overview">Overview</Tabs.Tab>
</Tabs>
```

### Keep the labels short and parallel.

Each label is one or two words naming a view of the same subject: Overview, Sessions, Progress. Parallel wording lets people scan the strip without reading it.

Do: Short nouns for views of the same subject.
Don't: Mixed verbs and phrases that do not scan.

### Choose the appearance by weight, not taste.

The underline suits a strip that sits above page content. The pill suits a strip inside a card or toolbar, where a filled selected tab reads as a control.

Do: A pill strip inside a card reads as a control.
Don't: The page-level underline inside a card, where it reads as a stray rule.

### Keep labels the same across visits.

A label names a view. A count or status in it changes the name and breaks the parallel wording.

Do: The label names the view.
Don't: Counts and status in the label.

### Keep one tab system per page and use `PopupSelect` for a second-level choice.

A `pill` strip is a fixed set of views of one subject, decided when the page is designed, so it has no add-view control and people cannot create, rename, reorder or remove a tab. A strip that must grow with the data is a list or a `Select`, not tabs. A page has one tab system: the underline strip under the page header switches the page's sections, and a pill strip inside a card switches that card's views, without stacking two strips of the same kind. For a second-level choice inside a view, use the labeled trigger of `PopupSelect` ("Status: Upcoming") in the view's toolbar.

Do: One strip for the sections; a labeled PopupSelect for the choice inside one.
Don't: A second strip under the first, so two tab systems compete.

### Swap content in place without sliding.

Switching tabs is a frequent action. The selected marker transitions quickly, and the content under the strip swaps in place with no slide or fade-through. Reduced motion removes the transition and the marker changes at once.
rankedText.related:
- `PageHeader`: use when placing a page-level `Tabs` strip in the header's `bottomBar` slot.
- `PopupSelect`: use when adding a second-level view choice inside a tab's toolbar.

# Tag

A small outlined label that names a category, person, agent or team. It can also act as a link, a toggle or a removable tag, depending on its props.

Also asked as: label, keyword.

**Import:** `import { Tag } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/Tag/Tag.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/Tag/Tag.stories.jsx` — Colors, LeadingSwatchAndIcon, SwatchRefusesRawColor, NewColorsContrast, Behaviors, Types, AvatarFallback, TypeBehaviors, PersonFocusRing, RemoveFocusRingOnTypes, AvatarEdgeCases, AvatarFills, Selecting, StateLayers, Removing, RemoveNeedsANameForNodeLabels, FocusRing, LinkWithRemove, DisabledInField, CountOnSelectable, Saving, Truncation, OnImages, ColoredMaterial, ElevatedAvatarTypes, ElevatedDisabled, ElevatedRemoveFocus, ElevatedOnlyReadOnlyAndLink, AnswerTags, IsDisabled, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, Disabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/Tag/Tag.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Tag` for a subject, a focus area, a person, an agent, a team or a
category. A tag is outlined and a status is filled, so a reader tells a
category from a workflow state without reading the words.

- **Is it a number?** `CountTag`.
- **Is it a due or event date?** `DateTag`.
- **Is it the condition something is in, and can that condition change?** `StatusTag`.
- **Otherwise** (a subject, a focus area, a person, a category): `Tag`.

`color` is one of the ten tag hues (`gray`, `blue`, `green`, `purple`, `magenta`, `yellow`, `teal`, `orange`, `lime`, `brown`). `type` is `person`, `agent` or `team` for a tag that leads with an avatar. `isSelected` makes the tag a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); `isLoading` puts a spinner in the leading slot while a toggle or remove is saving.

## Alternatives

- For one of the five competency areas, use `CompetencyTag`.
- For the condition something is in when that condition can change, use `StatusTag`.
- For a number on its own, use `CountTag`.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a labeled field where the person picks and removes tags, use `TagInput`.

## Best practices

### Use one color per category. {#use-one-color-per-category}

A color names a category; changing it inside one category reads as a different one.

Do: One color for one category.
Don't: Rainbow inside one category.

### Keep color for a category, never a status. {#keep-color-for-a-category-never-a-status}

Pick a color per category and keep it stable, or leave every tag gray. A condition that can change is a `StatusTag`.

Do: A stable color for a category.
Don't: Green reads as "went well" beside anything red.

### Show selection with the selected state. {#show-selection-with-the-selected-state}

Selection is a state of the tag, never a new color.

Do: Selected state.
Don't: A new color for selected.

### Add a swatch only when color is the way to find the tag. {#add-a-swatch-only-when-color-is-the-way-to-find-the-tag}

A plain tag is its outline and neutral words. Turn on `swatchBefore` for a tag that is a legend entry or a color-coded filter, where the reader matches the square to a chart or a key. An icon in `elemBefore` is for when the icon carries meaning of its own.

```jsx
<Tag color="blue">Lincoln Middle</Tag>                                  {/* plain: outline only */}
<Tag color="blue" swatchBefore>Lincoln Middle</Tag>                       {/* the tag's own color */}
<Tag swatchBefore="background-accent-orange-bolder">Week 3</Tag>   {/* a background color token */}
<Tag elemBefore={<Icon name="star" />}>Starred</Tag>                {/* an icon that means something */}
```

### Let the props pick the kind of tag. {#let-the-props-pick-the-kind-of-tag}

```jsx
// Read-only, the default: a value on show.
<Tag>Grade 4</Tag>

// Removable: a value the person can take out.
<Tag isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Grade 4</Tag>

// Selectable: a filter or an answer choice, with its result count.
<Tag isSelected={on} onClick={toggle} trailingMetric={12}>Science</Tag>

// Link, and a link with a separate ×.
<Tag href="/sites/lincoln-middle">Lincoln Middle</Tag>
<Tag href="/sites/lincoln-middle" isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Lincoln Middle</Tag>
```

`isSelected` is a boolean on purpose: `false` is an unselected toggle, and
leaving it out is a tag that is not selectable. `trailingMetric` is for
selectable tags only; anywhere else it is ignored with a warning.

### Use the type for who, not for what. {#use-the-type-for-who-not-for-what}

Person, agent and team tell people who something belongs to; topics stay plain.

Do: Types name the owner.
Don't: Plain tags hide the owner.

`avatar` takes an image source or a node. Leave it out, or let it fail, and
initials stand in without moving the tag. On a plain tag it is ignored with a
warning.

### Lift a tag onto an image with `isElevated`. {#lift-a-tag-onto-an-image-with-iselevated}

```jsx
<Tag color="blue" isElevated>Lincoln Middle</Tag>
<Tag href="/lessons/42" color="magenta" isElevated>Open lesson</Tag>
```

Read-only and link only: a value is edited off the image. On a removable or
selectable tag `isElevated` is ignored with a warning.

### Disable one tag, or the whole field. {#disable-one-tag-or-the-whole-field}

`isDisabled` disables one tag. A field or group that is disabled says so once,
and every tag inside follows:

```jsx
<Tag isDisabled>Grade 4</Tag>

<TagContext.Provider value={{ isDisabled: true }}>
    <Tag isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Grade 4</Tag>
</TagContext.Provider>
```

`useTagContext()` reads the same value from inside a custom tag.

### Let the group own the gaps. {#let-the-group-own-the-gaps}

`Tag` sets no margin of its own. A row of tags is a `TagGroup`, which sets
`gap` once for the set.

## Accessibility

- **A removable tag is not itself a control.** The × is, and a button inside a
  button is invalid, so the tag is a `span` with one button in it.
- **The × is named from the label.** It announces `Remove Science`;
  `removeButtonLabel` overrides that when the label is not text.
- **Selectable publishes `aria-pressed`**, so the state is not only visible.
  Selected also changes the border to the full hue, so it does not rest on a
  change of lightness alone. A selectable tag given `aria-expanded` is a button
  that opens something, such as `TagGroup`'s `+n`: it publishes the expanded
  state and no `aria-pressed`.
- **A link with a × is two tab stops**, link then ×, and pressing the × never
  follows the link.
- **Saving is announced once.** The spinner is hidden; a status region beside
  the tag, outside its name, says "Saving". The × and a link stay focusable
  but do nothing until the save lands.
- **A × needs a name.** When the label is not text, pass `removeButtonLabel`, or the
  × is named only "Remove" and development warns.
- **An elevated tag's focus ring has a surface gap.** The gap between the tag
  (or a link's ×) and the ring is filled in the surface color, so the ring
  reads on a dark picture.
- **Disabled tags take no focus, and say they are disabled.** They come from
  `isDisabled` or a disabled field. A selectable tag is a native disabled button, announced as
  disabled. Every other tag is a span, which has no disabled state a screen
  reader announces, so it ends with visually hidden text and is read as
  "Science, disabled".
- **A clipped label keeps its full text** in a tooltip that hover and keyboard
  focus both reach. On a control the control carries it; on a plain tag the
  label takes focus while, and only while, it is clipped.
- **The swatch and the avatar are decoration** and are hidden from assistive
  technology; an avatar image has empty alt text. The tag's words name the
  person, agent or team, so the initials are never read out or folded into the
  ×'s name.

## Related

- `TagGroup`: use when laying out a set of tags with shared spacing, alignment and overflow.
- `CompetencyTag`: use when tagging one of the five competency areas.
- `Suggestion`: use when offering proposed tags for the person to accept.

Same group: `ChangeTag` · `CompetencyTag` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `StatusTag` · `TagGroup`

## Parts

1. **Lead, optional.** Nothing by default. A `10` swatch (`swatchBefore`), an icon (`elemBefore`), or for a person, an agent or a team a `16` avatar.
2. **Label.** Neutral text; the hue never colors the words.
3. **Trailing metric.** Optional on a selectable tag: a `CountTag`, such as a filter's result count.
4. **Remove button.** Optional, with its own focus ring and a name that says what it removes.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Outlined, clear ground, the hue on the border. |
| Hovered, pressed | A link or a selectable tag takes the accent's subtlest and subtlest pressed steps; a link's words underline. On a removable tag only the × reacts. |
| Selected | The subtler ground with a full-hue border, held under hover and press. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring on the tag or on the ×; see Border. |
| Disabled | Disabled ground and words, no ×, no link, no focus; a selected tag keeps a bold edge. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Rest edge | `--ds-border-accent-blue-subtle`, and the same step for each hue. |
| Hovered, pressed | `--ds-background-accent-blue-subtlest` and `--ds-background-accent-blue-subtlest-pressed`. |
| Selected | `--ds-background-accent-blue-subtler` with a `--ds-border-accent-blue` edge. |
| Words | `--ds-text` on every hue. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled`, `--ds-text-disabled`, `--ds-icon-disabled`. |
| Padding, gap, corner | `--pad-x-xs`, `--stack-sm`, `--radius-md`; a person tag is `--radius-full`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the thing in a word or two: "Science", "Grade 6". | Write a sentence or a full instruction. |
| Use sentence case and the singular. | Use ALL CAPS or a trailing punctuation mark. |
| Give a × a name that says the value: "Remove Science". | Leave every × named "Remove". |
| Keep one wording for one category across the product. | Rename the same category per screen. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `text` | string | — | The label (alternative to children). |
| `children` | node | — | The label (takes precedence over `text`). |
| `color` | enum | `'gray'` | A category color: an accent family, on the border (and on the swatch when `swatchBefore` is on). Never a status. On an avatar type the border is neutral and the color fills the avatar; gray agents fill discovery (the AI purple) and gray teams the lightest blue. |
| `type` | oneOf | `'plain'` | What the tag names. `plain` leads with nothing unless `swatchBefore` or `elemBefore` is set; `person` (round), `agent` (hexagon) and `team` (square) lead with a 16 avatar. |
| `avatar` | string or node | — | The avatar of a person, agent or team tag: an image source, or a node. Missing or broken, it falls back to initials. Decorative. |
| `trailingMetric` | number or string | — | Selectable tags only: a neutral Count tag after the label, such as a filter's result count. Ignored with a warning elsewhere. |
| `elemBefore` | node | — | The leading icon slot, empty by default: an icon in front of the text, for when the icon carries meaning. Plain tags only: an avatar type leads with its avatar. Sits after `swatchBefore` when both are set. |
| `swatchBefore` | bool or string | — | A 10 color square in front of the text, off by default, for a tag that uses color for wayfinding such as a chart legend entry. `true` draws it in the tag's own color; a background color token (`background-accent-blue-bolder`, or `--ds-background-accent-blue-bolder`) draws a custom one. Never a raw CSS color. Plain tags only. |
| `maxWidth` | number or string | `180` | Caps the whole tag (default 180). A clipped label ellipsizes and shows its full text as a tooltip. |
| `href` | string | — | Makes the tag a link to this address. |
| `linkComponent` | elementType | — | Router link to render instead of `<a>` for a link tag. |
| `isSelected` | bool | — | Makes the tag a toggle, true or false: it publishes `aria-pressed` and fires `onClick`. Leave it out for a tag that is not selectable. |
| `isRemovable` | bool | `false` | Adds a Remove button, with the 2px focus ring on the button itself. Not shown while the tag is disabled. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | Disables this tag. A field disables all of its tags through `TagContext`. |
| `isLoading` | bool | `false` | Saving: a spinner replaces the swatch, icon or avatar and the tag ignores presses until it is done. |
| `isElevated` | bool | `false` | For a tag on an image or video: a solid surface fill, no border and the Elevation 2 shadow, with the hue kept on the swatch, when there is one, or the avatar's own fill. Disabled keeps the ground and shadow and turns the content Secondary (Text). Focus on the tag or a link's × has a surface gap inside the ring. Read-only and link tags only; ignored with a warning on removable and selectable ones. |
| `material` | enum | — | Colored material for a read-only tag over media or a material surface: a bold or subtle fill with the material edge. |
| `materialColor` | enum | `'brand'` | The color of the material: a status, brand or category identity. |
| `onClick` | func | — | Fires on a selectable tag and on a link. |
| `onAfterRemoveAction` | func | — | Called with the tag's text and the event after the Remove button is pressed. The caller removes the tag. |
| `removeButtonLabel` | string | — | Overrides the Remove button's accessible name. Defaults to `Remove <label>`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the tag element. |
| `id` | string | — | Id set on the tag element. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the tag element, merged over the `maxWidth` cap. |

## Variants

**`color`** — `gray` · `blue` · `green` · `purple` · `magenta` · `yellow` · `teal` · `orange` · `lime` · `brown`

**`type`** — `plain` · `person` · `agent` · `team`

**`material`** — `bold` · `subtle`

**`materialColor`** — `brand` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` · `information` · `discovery`

- **Is it a due or event date?** `DateTag`.
- **Is it the condition something is in, and can that condition change?** `StatusTag`.
- **Otherwise** (a subject, a focus area, a person, a category): `Tag`.

`color` is one of the ten tag hues (`gray`, `blue`, `green`, `purple`, `magenta`, `yellow`, `teal`, `orange`, `lime`, `brown`). `type` is `person`, `agent` or `team` for a tag that leads with an avatar. `isSelected` makes the tag a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); `isLoading` puts a spinner in the leading slot while a toggle or remove is saving.
rankedText.best:
### Use one color per category.

A color names a category; changing it inside one category reads as a different one.

Do: One color for one category.
Don't: Rainbow inside one category.

### Keep color for a category, never a status.

Pick a color per category and keep it stable, or leave every tag gray. A condition that can change is a `StatusTag`.

Do: A stable color for a category.
Don't: Green reads as "went well" beside anything red.

### Show selection with the selected state.

Selection is a state of the tag, never a new color.

Do: Selected state.
Don't: A new color for selected.

### Add a swatch only when color is the way to find the tag.

A plain tag is its outline and neutral words. Turn on `swatchBefore` for a tag that is a legend entry or a color-coded filter, where the reader matches the square to a chart or a key. An icon in `elemBefore` is for when the icon carries meaning of its own.

```jsx
<Tag color="blue">Lincoln Middle</Tag>                                  {/* plain: outline only */}
<Tag color="blue" swatchBefore>Lincoln Middle</Tag>                       {/* the tag's own color */}
<Tag swatchBefore="background-accent-orange-bolder">Week 3</Tag>   {/* a background color token */}
<Tag elemBefore={<Icon name="star" />}>Starred</Tag>                {/* an icon that means something */}
```

### Let the props pick the kind of tag.

```jsx
// Read-only, the default: a value on show.
<Tag>Grade 4</Tag>

// Removable: a value the person can take out.
<Tag isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Grade 4</Tag>

// Selectable: a filter or an answer choice, with its result count.
<Tag isSelected={on} onClick={toggle} trailingMetric={12}>Science</Tag>

// Link, and a link with a separate ×.
<Tag href="/sites/lincoln-middle">Lincoln Middle</Tag>
<Tag href="/sites/lincoln-middle" isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Lincoln Middle</Tag>
```

`isSelected` is a boolean on purpose: `false` is an unselected toggle, and
leaving it out is a tag that is not selectable. `trailingMetric` is for
selectable tags only; anywhere else it is ignored with a warning.

### Use the type for who, not for what.

Person, agent and team tell people who something belongs to; topics stay plain.

Do: Types name the owner.
Don't: Plain tags hide the owner.

`avatar` takes an image source or a node. Leave it out, or let it fail, and
initials stand in without moving the tag. On a plain tag it is ignored with a
warning.

### Lift a tag onto an image with `isElevated`.

```jsx
<Tag color="blue" isElevated>Lincoln Middle</Tag>
<Tag href="/lessons/42" color="magenta" isElevated>Open lesson</Tag>
```

Read-only and link only: a value is edited off the image. On a removable or
selectable tag `isElevated` is ignored with a warning.

### Disable one tag, or the whole field.

`isDisabled` disables one tag. A field or group that is disabled says so once,
and every tag inside follows:

```jsx
<Tag isDisabled>Grade 4</Tag>

<TagContext.Provider value={{ isDisabled: true }}>
    <Tag isRemovable onAfterRemoveAction={drop}>Grade 4</Tag>
</TagContext.Provider>
```

`useTagContext()` reads the same value from inside a custom tag.

### Let the group own the gaps.

`Tag` sets no margin of its own. A row of tags is a `TagGroup`, which sets
`gap` once for the set.

# TagGroup

TagGroup: the wrapper for more than one Tag together. It owns their spacing, wrapping, alignment and disabled state.

Also asked as: tag list.

**Import:** `import { TagGroup } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Overflow (`ds guide overflow`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/labels/TagGroup/TagGroup.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/labels/TagGroup/TagGroup.stories.jsx` — Wrapping, Collapse, CollapseMenu, CollapseWithSuggestions, MenuKeepsActions, MaxVisible, OneMoreTag, CapNeverSqueezes, WrappedSuggestionsAreNotCounted, NoOverflowWhenItFits, ConditionalChildrenAreNotCounted, OverflowTag, DigitBoundary, StableOnParentRender, SqueezedFirstReplaced, AlignmentRight, Disabled, RemovableSet, CustomOverflowAction, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused, DisabledSet

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/labels/TagGroup/TagGroup.mdx`

## Usage

Use `TagGroup` wherever more than one `Tag` appears together: the subjects on a
profile, the filters above a table, the recipients on a message. It is the
right wrapper even when the set is short, because the spacing, wrapping,
alignment and disabled state belong to the set rather than to any tag in it.
`Suggestion` items offered for the field go in the same group; they always sit
at the end of the row, after the tags and `+n`.

## Alternatives

- For one value rather than a set, use `Tag`.
- For a labeled field where the person picks and removes tags, use `TagInput`.
- For a long list that needs paging rather than an overflow count, use `Pagination`.

## Best practices

### Collapse long groups in tight rows. {#collapse-long-groups-in-tight-rows}

`overflow="collapse"` keeps one line and puts the rest behind `+n`, measured by the container's width: give the group a width to fit into, because a group that can grow shows everything. Use `maxVisible` only to show fewer than fit (`maxVisible={0}` puts every tag behind `+n`), and `+n` reserves room for the widest label at its digit count (`+88` when up to `99` tags are hidden).

`Suggestion` children are offers, not values: they are not counted into `+n`, never appear in its menu and always sit after it. Their width comes off the row before tags are counted, so a group with suggestions shows fewer tags, not fewer suggestions. Pass `Suggestion`s as direct children; a custom wrapper must copy the marker (`MySuggestion.isSuggestion = Suggestion.isSuggestion`) or it is counted as a tag. In the `+n` menu, a selectable tag toggles (`aria-pressed`) with the menu staying open, a link tag navigates, a saving tag is a disabled, busy row, a read-only or removable tag is a static row, and remove is only offered on the row, never from the menu.

Do: Collapse in a tight row.
Don't: Wrap pushes the row taller.

### Align to the surrounding text. {#align-to-the-surrounding-text}

`alignment="end"` belongs in a table column whose other cells are right-aligned. Everywhere else, tags read from the start.

Do: Start beside left-aligned text.
Don't: End beside left-aligned text.

### Disable the whole group when read-only. {#disable-the-whole-group-when-read-only}

Pass `isDisabled` on the group so every `Tag` and `Suggestion` inside follows as a unit; never disable one tag and leave its neighbors live.

Do: The whole group disabled.
Don't: A read-only group that looks editable.

### Let the group own the gap. {#let-the-group-own-the-gap}

`Tag` sets `margin: 0` and `TagGroup` sets `gap`, so spacing is defined in one place rather than on both the parent and each child.

## Accessibility

- **Named list.** The group renders `role="list"` named by `label`, wrapping each child in a `listitem` so `Tag` stays usable outside a group. `label` has no default, so a group without it is an unnamed list.
- **Hidden tags leave the list.** Collapsed tags stay out of the tab order and list count until the `+n` menu opens.
- **Suggestions stay reachable.** They are never behind `+n`, so a keyboard user reaches them on the row after `+n`.
- **Disabled is announced per tag.** A selectable tag, a Suggestion and `+n` are native disabled buttons; every other tag is a plain span that carries visually hidden text and reads as "Science, disabled". Nothing in a disabled group takes focus.
- **`+n` announces its count and menu state.** Its name starts with what it shows ("+3 more tags", "+1 more tag"). Enter or Space opens the menu, Tab reaches each interactive item inside, and Escape returns focus to `+n`. Selectable tags toggle in place (`aria-pressed`), links keep their `href`, and remove stays on the row.
- **Suggestions stay on the row.** They are never folded into `+n`, so keyboard users reach them directly.
- **Disabled is announced per item.** Interactive tags and `+n` become native disabled buttons; static tags append visually hidden ", disabled" text.

## Related

- `Tag`: use when configuring individual items inside the group.
- `CompetencyTag`: use when tagging competency areas inside the group.
- `Suggestion`: use when offering proposed tags at the end of the group.

Same group: `ChangeTag` · `CompetencyTag` · `CountTag` · `DateTag` · `StatusTag` · `Tag`

## Parts

1. **Tags and suggestions.** The group owns the gaps between them; a tag carries no margin.
2. **Overflow tag.** A `+n` that opens a menu of the hidden tags, or runs `onOverflowClick`.
3. **List.** A named `list` of `listitem`s; `label` is its accessible name.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | A wrapping row, or a collapsed row with a `+n` tag. |
| Hovered, pressed | None on the group. Each tag reacts as it would alone. |
| Focused | None on the list. Tab reaches the controls inside it in order: selectable tags, links, ×, suggestions, the overflow tag. |
| Disabled | `isDisabled` disables every tag and suggestion and the overflow menu, as a disabled field does. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Gap | `--stack-md` (8) between tags, and between rows. |
| Overflow tag | A selectable Tag, so its ground, ring and disabled tokens are Tag's. |
| Disabled | `--ds-background-disabled` and `--ds-text-disabled`, from `TagContext`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Give the group a `label` that names the set: "Focus areas". | Leave it out, or write "Tags". |
| Order tags by importance or by the order the person added them. | Sort them arbitrarily. |
| Name the overflow by what is hidden: "+3 focus areas". | Say "More" with no count. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `children` | node | — | The tags, and any Suggestions offered beside them. Suggestions always sit at the end, after `+n`, and are never counted or hidden; they must be direct children, or components that carry Suggestion's `isSuggestion` marker. `null` and `false` are skipped rather than counted. |
| `label` | string | — | The group's accessible name — what this set of tags is. |
| `overflow` | enum | `'wrap'` | `wrap` flows onto more lines; `collapse` keeps one line, shows as many tags as fit, and puts the rest behind `+n`. |
| `alignment` | enum | `'start'` | `end` lines the tags and the `+n` up on the end edge, for a right-aligned table column. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | — | Disables every Tag and Suggestion in the group, as a disabled field does. |
| `maxVisible` | number | — | `collapse` only: the most tags to show before `+n`, even when more would fit. By default, as many as fit. |
| `overflowLabel` | func | — | Formats the overflow tag's visible label. Defaults to `+n`; its accessible name starts with that label: "+3 more tags" ("+1 more tag"), or "<label>, 3 more tags" for a custom one. |
| `onOverflowClick` | func | — | Replaces the `+n` menu — for opening a picker or a panel instead. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |

## Variants

**`overflow`** — `wrap` · `collapse`

**`alignment`** — `start` · `end`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--stack-md`

From `design-system/src/components/labels/TagGroup/TagGroup.scss`. Override these through the token layer, never with a literal.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the field. Give every TagInput one.

props.name: labelMarker
props.description: Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form.

props.name: info
props.description: Text for an info tooltip beside the label.

props.name: caption
props.description: Standing help under the field. A validation message takes its place.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in the entry while there are no tags.

props.name: options
props.description: The options the list offers: strings, or objects with `value`, `label` (or `text`) and a Tag `color`. Required; the caller owns the list and adds what `onCreate` reports to it.

props.name: tags
props.description: The picked tags, controlled. Pass `onChange` with it.

props.name: defaultTags
props.description: The picked tags at first, uncontrolled.

props.name: spacing
props.description: `default` draws a 40 field and `compact` a 32 one.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables every tag and the entry.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Shows the tags with no × and no entry, on the read-only fill.

props.name: errorMessage
props.description: Shown under the field, and announced, while `isInvalid` is set.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: The longest a new value can be.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: The most tags the field holds. At the limit, Create hides and the list says so.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: `(tag)`: a tag was added, picked or created.

props.name: onCreate
props.description: `({ value, color })`: a new value was created, with the color it was given. Store both on the option. Return a promise of the stored id to hold the tag on a temporary id, saving, until it resolves; a rejection removes the tag and puts the text back.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: `(index, tag)`: a tag was removed.

props.name: onChange
props.description: `(tags)`: the new list, after any add or remove.

props.name: onRename
props.description: `(value, name)`: an option was renamed from its "…" menu. Store the new name on the option. A picked tag made from it takes the name too.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: `(value)`: an option was deleted from its "…" menu. Remove it from `options`; a picked tag made from it is removed with it.

props.name: onColorChange
props.description: `(value, color)`: an option was given another of Tag's ten colors from its "…" menu. Store it on the option.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: `(fromIndex, toIndex)`: an option was moved by its handle, by drag or by the keyboard. Both are places in `options`; move the option there.
