<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# TagInput

TagInput — a field of Tags with a text entry after them, modeled on Notion's multi-select. Focusing the field opens a list of the options. Typing filters it and highlights the first match; Enter or a click adds the highlighted option. A "Create *text*" row is offered when no option matches the text exactly, ignoring case. It previews the new tag as the Tag it will be, in the random Tag color it will get, and creating reports that color once through `onCreate`. Backspace in an empty entry removes the last tag, and Esc closes the list and clears only the typed text. People can tidy the options where they pick them, as in Notion. With `onRename`, `onDelete` or `onColorChange`, the highlighted row shows a "…" that opens the option's menu: its name, Delete, and Tag's ten colors. With `onReorder`, each row has a handle to drag, or to pick up with Space and move with the arrows. Without these handlers neither appears. Built on the shared parts: `_Field` is the box, `Listbox` the list and its rows, and the tags are Tags in a TagGroup. Without focus the tags collapse into "+n"; with focus they wrap, up to three rows, then scroll.

**Import:** `import { TagInput } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TagInput/TagInput.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TagInput/TagInput.stories.jsx` — TypingFilters, CreateWhenNothingMatches, MatchIgnoresCase, ClickPicks, BackspaceRemovesTheLastTag, EscClearsOnlyTheText, PasteSplitsOnCommas, PastedTagsGetTagColors, MaxLength, PickLimit, CollapsesWithoutFocus, SmallFitsItsTags, TemporaryIdUntilConfirmed, ReadOnly, Invalid, Disabled, Controlled, OptionMenuRenames, OptionMenuDeletes, OptionMenuChangesColor, KeyboardReorder, DragReorder, NoTidyingWithoutHandlers, OptionMenu, Reordering, Overview, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TagInput/TagInput.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TagInput` when a field's value is a set of short labels the person picks from a list and may create, rename, recolor or reorder in place, such as the topics a session covered. The field holds the picked values as `Tag`s in a `TagGroup`, with a text entry after them, and focusing it opens the option list under it.

## Motion

TagInput reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A tag is added or removed. |

## Alternatives

- For one value from a list, use `Select`.
- For several values from a fixed list nobody adds to, use `Select` with `isMulti`.
- For up to five multi-select options visible all at once, use `CheckboxGroup`.

## Best practices

### Label every tag input. {#label-every-tag-input}

A visible label says what the tags are; tags alone do not.

Do: A label names what is being tagged.
Don't: Tags with no label leave the field unnamed.

### Show an error on the field itself. {#show-an-error-on-the-field-itself}

The field carries the error state.

Do: The field shows the error state.
Don't: A default field gives no sign of the problem.

### Disable instead of hiding. {#disable-instead-of-hiding}

A disabled field tells people the option exists but is unavailable.

Do: Visible but disabled.
Don't: An enabled field that cannot take tags.

### The caller owns the options, and stores what is created. {#the-caller-owns-the-options-and-stores-what-is-created}

`options` is required. When the person creates a value, `onCreate` reports it
once, with the color it was given. Store both on a new option, so the color
stays the same everywhere the tag appears.

```jsx
// Incorrect — the created value is never stored, so its color is lost on the next render.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} />

// Correct — the new value joins the options with its color.
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onCreate={({ value, color }) => setTopics((list) => [...list, { value, label: value, color }])}
/>
```

### A value saved to a server holds a temporary id until it is confirmed. {#a-value-saved-to-a-server-holds-a-temporary-id-until-it-is-confirmed}

Return a promise from `onCreate` that resolves to the stored id. Until it
does, the tag is saving and its `value` is a temporary id starting `new-`. If
it rejects, the tag is removed, the text goes back in the entry, and the
failure is announced.

```jsx
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onCreate={({ value, color }) => api.createTopic({ name: value, color }).then((topic) => topic.id)}
/>
```

### A controlled field needs a handler to offer a ×. {#a-controlled-field-needs-a-handler-to-offer-a}

```jsx
// Incorrect — controlled with no handler, so no tag can be removed and none shows a ×.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} tags={picked} />

// Correct — onChange receives the new list.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} tags={picked} onChange={setPicked} />
```

### Let people tidy options where they pick them. {#let-people-tidy-options-where-they-pick-them}

Pass a handler for each change the screen can store. The caller owns the
options, so each handler updates the list. TagInput only reports the change.
A field with none of them works as before, with no "…" and no handle.

```jsx
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onRename={(value, name) => setTopics((list) => list.map((t) => (t.value === value ? { ...t, label: name } : t)))}
    onDelete={(value) => setTopics((list) => list.filter((t) => t.value !== value))}
    onColorChange={(value, color) => setTopics((list) => list.map((t) => (t.value === value ? { ...t, color } : t)))}
    onReorder={(from, to) => setTopics((list) => {
        const next = [...list];
        next.splice(to, 0, ...next.splice(from, 1));
        return next;
    })}
/>
```

- **Delete** also removes a picked tag made from that option, through
  `onChange` and `onRemove`. Rename and a color change update that tag too.
- **Reorder** works on the whole list, so the handles hide while text is
  typed. `onReorder(fromIndex, toIndex)` gives places in `options`.

### Use a `Tag` color for each option. {#use-a-tag-color-for-each-option}

A tag is a category, so it takes a `Tag` color. Any other name draws gray and warns in development.

## Accessibility

- **The label names the entry.** The text entry is a `combobox` that points at
  the list with `aria-controls` and at the highlighted row with
  `aria-activedescendant`, so focus stays in the field while the arrow keys
  move through the list.
- **The tags are a named list.** `TagGroup` is a list named "Selected:" and the
  label, and each × is named `Remove <tag>`.
- **Changes are announced.** Adding or removing a tag says so in a live
  region, such as "Music added".
- **Invalid is announced.** The message under the field has `role="alert"`,
  and the entry has `aria-invalid` and is described by it.
- **Read-only and disabled leave nothing to press.** Neither draws a × or opens
  the list.
- **A row's handle and "…" are real buttons.** They sit beside the listbox,
  laid over the highlighted row, because an option's content is presentational
  and a button inside one would be lost to a screen reader. They are named `Reorder <option>` and
  `Options for <option>`, and the handle is described by its keys.
- **Reordering is announced.** Picking up, each move, the drop and a cancel
  each say the row and its position, such as "Design judgment dropped,
  position 3 of 4".
- **The menu takes focus and gives it back.** Opening it moves focus to the
  name field. Closing it returns focus to the "…".

## Related

- `Tag`: use when rendering a single category or attribute label.
- `TagGroup`: use when displaying a read-only set of tags outside a form field.
- `Select`: use when choosing multiple values from a fixed list (`isMulti`).

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Field.** The box holding the tags and the text entry.
2. **Tags.** The picked values, each removable unless the field is read-only or disabled.
3. **Entry.** The text entry after the tags. Typing filters the list.
4. **List.** The options under the field, with a "Create" row when nothing matches.
5. **Caption.** Helper text, or the error that replaces it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge. Tags past one line collapse into "+n". |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box; the tags wrap and the list opens. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled`; every tag is disabled, with no × and no entry. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Read-only | The `--ds-background-neutral` fill at full contrast, no hover, in the tab order with `aria-readonly`, with no × and no list. |

### Keyboard

| Key | In the field |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the list and highlights the first match. |
| ↑ ↓ | Move the highlight; opens the list when it is closed. |
| Enter | Adds the highlighted option, or creates the typed text when Create is highlighted. Text matching an option, ignoring case, picks that option. |
| Backspace | In an empty entry, removes the last tag. |
| Esc | Closes the list and clears only the typed text. The tags stay. |
| Paste | Text with commas or line breaks becomes one tag per part, trimmed. |
| Tab | With a handler for the menu or reordering, moves from the entry to the highlighted row's handle, then its "…". |

On a row's handle and in its menu:

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space or Enter on the handle | Picks the row up. |
| ↑ ↓ | Move the picked-up row. |
| Space or Enter | Drops it there. |
| Esc | Cancels, and the row goes back. |
| Enter on the "…" | Opens the menu with focus in the name. |
| Enter in the name | Renames the option. After ↑ ↓, picks the highlighted row instead. |
| Esc in the menu | Closes it without renaming, and focus goes back to the "…". |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | Starts at 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. Grows as tags wrap. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Tags and entry | `--stack-md` between them; with focus, up to three rows of tags before the content scrolls. |
| Entry text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| List | `--ds-surface-overlay` with a `--ds-border` edge, `--popup-radius` and `--ds-shadow-overlay`. |
| List hint | `--body-sm` in `--ds-text-subtle`, `--pad-x-xs` `--pad-x-md`. |
| Row handle | `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Option menu | `--option-menu-width` wide; the name field `--pad-x-xs` `--pad-x-sm`; a `--border-width-default` rule in `--ds-border` above the colors. |

The tags take Tag's own tokens.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Write each tag as a short noun phrase: "Fractions". | A sentence as a tag. |
| Reuse existing tags before creating a new one. | Near-duplicates: "Fraction" and "Fractions". |
| Say what to do in an error: "Pick at least one topic". | "Required" or "Invalid". |
| Keep tags to a few words. | A tag that wraps. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `name` | string | — | — |
| `label` | node | — | Names the field. Give every TagInput one. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for an info tooltip beside the label. |
| `caption` | node | — | Standing help under the field. A validation message takes its place. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Select or create a tag'` | Shown in the entry while there are no tags. |
| `options` | arrayOf (required) | `[]` | The options the list offers: strings, or objects with `value`, `label` (or `text`) and a Tag `color`. Required; the caller owns the list and adds what `onCreate` reports to it. |
| `tags` | arrayOf | — | The picked tags, controlled. Pass `onChange` with it. |
| `defaultTags` | arrayOf | `[]` | The picked tags at first, uncontrolled. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws a 40 field and `compact` a 32 one. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables every tag and the entry. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the tags with no × and no entry, on the read-only fill. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | — |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | Shown under the field, and announced, while `isInvalid` is set. |
| `maxLength` | number | — | The longest a new value can be. |
| `maxTags` | number | — | The most tags the field holds. At the limit, Create hides and the list says so. |
| `onAdd` | func | — | `(tag)`: a tag was added, picked or created. |
| `onCreate` | func | — | `({ value, color })`: a new value was created, with the color it was given. Store both on the option. Return a promise of the stored id to hold the tag on a temporary id, saving, until it resolves; a rejection removes the tag and puts the text back. |
| `onRemove` | func | — | `(index, tag)`: a tag was removed. |
| `onChange` | func | — | `(tags)`: the new list, after any add or remove. |
| `onRename` | func | — | `(value, name)`: an option was renamed from its "…" menu. Store the new name on the option. A picked tag made from it takes the name too. |
| `onDelete` | func | — | `(value)`: an option was deleted from its "…" menu. Remove it from `options`; a picked tag made from it is removed with it. |
| `onColorChange` | func | — | `(value, color)`: an option was given another of Tag's ten colors from its "…" menu. Store it on the option. |
| `onReorder` | func | — | `(fromIndex, toIndex)`: an option was moved by its handle, by drag or by the keyboard. Both are places in `options`; move the option there. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

## Variants

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

rankedText.usage: Use `TagInput` when a field's value is a set of short labels the person picks from a list and may create, rename, recolor or reorder in place, such as the topics a session covered. The field holds the picked values as `Tag`s in a `TagGroup`, with a text entry after them, and focusing it opens the option list under it.
rankedText.best:
### Label every tag input.

A visible label says what the tags are; tags alone do not.

Do: A label names what is being tagged.
Don't: Tags with no label leave the field unnamed.

### Show an error on the field itself.

The field carries the error state.

Do: The field shows the error state.
Don't: A default field gives no sign of the problem.

### Disable instead of hiding.

A disabled field tells people the option exists but is unavailable.

Do: Visible but disabled.
Don't: An enabled field that cannot take tags.

### The caller owns the options, and stores what is created.

`options` is required. When the person creates a value, `onCreate` reports it
once, with the color it was given. Store both on a new option, so the color
stays the same everywhere the tag appears.

```jsx
// Incorrect — the created value is never stored, so its color is lost on the next render.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} />

// Correct — the new value joins the options with its color.
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onCreate={({ value, color }) => setTopics((list) => [...list, { value, label: value, color }])}
/>
```

### A value saved to a server holds a temporary id until it is confirmed.

Return a promise from `onCreate` that resolves to the stored id. Until it
does, the tag is saving and its `value` is a temporary id starting `new-`. If
it rejects, the tag is removed, the text goes back in the entry, and the
failure is announced.

```jsx
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onCreate={({ value, color }) => api.createTopic({ name: value, color }).then((topic) => topic.id)}
/>
```

### A controlled field needs a handler to offer a ×.

```jsx
// Incorrect — controlled with no handler, so no tag can be removed and none shows a ×.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} tags={picked} />

// Correct — onChange receives the new list.
<TagInput label="Topics" options={topics} tags={picked} onChange={setPicked} />
```

### Let people tidy options where they pick them.

Pass a handler for each change the screen can store. The caller owns the
options, so each handler updates the list. TagInput only reports the change.
A field with none of them works as before, with no "…" and no handle.

```jsx
<TagInput
    label="Topics"
    options={topics}
    onRename={(value, name) => setTopics((list) => list.map((t) => (t.value === value ? { ...t, label: name } : t)))}
    onDelete={(value) => setTopics((list) => list.filter((t) => t.value !== value))}
    onColorChange={(value, color) => setTopics((list) => list.map((t) => (t.value === value ? { ...t, color } : t)))}
    onReorder={(from, to) => setTopics((list) => {
        const next = [...list];
        next.splice(to, 0, ...next.splice(from, 1));
        return next;
    })}
/>
```

- **Delete** also removes a picked tag made from that option, through
  `onChange` and `onRemove`. Rename and a color change update that tag too.
- **Reorder** works on the whole list, so the handles hide while text is
  typed. `onReorder(fromIndex, toIndex)` gives places in `options`.

### Use a `Tag` color for each option.

A tag is a category, so it takes a `Tag` color. Any other name draws gray and warns in development.

# TextArea

Text area — free text over several lines, on `_Field`. The field is 80 high at least, and `rows` grows it from there. With `maxLength`, the caption counts characters on the right. With `appearance="subtle"`, it reads as plain text until hovered or edited, shows Save and Cancel while editing, and stays open when it loses focus.

Also asked as: multi-line, multiline text, long text input, notes field, comment box.

**Import:** `import { TextArea } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextArea/TextArea.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextArea/TextArea.stories.jsx` — Overview, Rows, Spacing, Rows1, Rows3, Rows6, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Filled, Success, Warning, FocusRing, Count, Subtle, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled, FieldInvalid, FieldReadOnly

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextArea/TextArea.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TextArea` for free-form plain text over several lines, such as session notes, feedback or a reason.

## Motion

TextArea reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Border color changes on focus and error. An error message makes room, then fades in; it fades, then the room closes, once the field is fixed. |

## Alternatives

- For a single-line answer, use `TextField`.
- For multi-line text that requires formatting such as lists or links, use `RichTextEditor`.

## Best practices

### Hint at the answer, not the control. {#hint-at-the-answer-not-the-control}

A placeholder shows what a good answer looks like.

Do: Hint names the answer.
Don't: Hint describes the control.

### Show an error on the field itself. {#show-an-error-on-the-field-itself}

The field carries the invalid state. Use `isInvalid` only when the form cannot go on.

Do: The field shows the invalid state.
Don't: A default field gives no sign of the problem.

### Disable instead of hiding. {#disable-instead-of-hiding}

A disabled field tells people the option exists but is unavailable.

Do: Visible but disabled.
Don't: An enabled field that cannot take input.

### Put help in the caption. {#put-help-in-the-caption}

Do: Put help in the caption, where it stays after the person types.
Don't: Help in the placeholder disappears when the person starts typing.

### Match `rows` to the expected answer. {#match-rows-to-the-expected-answer}

One or three rows fit a short note; six rows fit a longer paragraph. The box always starts at `--field-min-height-sm` (`80px`) regardless of `rows`.

### Set a count only for a real limit. {#set-a-count-only-for-a-real-limit}

Set `maxLength` when something downstream truncates; do not add a limit just to show a count.

### Use subtle for editing in place. {#use-subtle-for-editing-in-place}

`appearance="subtle"` shows Save and Cancel while editing and does not save when focus leaves the field, so a click elsewhere in the middle of a paragraph does not publish half a thought.

### Let a warning accept the value. {#let-a-warning-accept-the-value}

`warningMessage` draws the warning edge and `successMessage` the success edge, each with its message. The value is accepted in both.

### Use read-only for fixed values and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-values-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` shows a value someone could change but this person cannot right now: it stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, takes the neutral fill, has no hover and says `aria-readonly`. Say why in the caption. `isDisabled` is for a field that does not apply yet, and takes it out of the tab order. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value. Content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

## Accessibility

- **The label is associated whether you pass `id` or not**, and `isLabelHidden`
  clips it out of sight without removing the name.
- **An error is announced.** `isInvalid` sets `aria-invalid` and renders the
  message with `role="alert"`; a warning, a success message and standing help are
  described. A count is part of the description.
- **Focus is a ring**, with no change of fill.
- **Save and Cancel are real buttons**, reached in the tab order after the field.
  Esc cancels, and Ctrl or Cmd with Enter saves.

## Related

- `TextField`: use when collecting a single line of text.
- `RichTextEditor`: use when the text needs formatting such as lists or links.
- [Form](?path=/docs/components-forms-and-inputs-form--docs): use when reviewing label and caption rules across fields.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Label.** Names the field. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text, and an info tooltip sits beside it.
2. **Box.** 80 high at least, growing with `rows`, and scrolls past it.
3. **Control.** The native textarea. It resizes vertically.
4. **Caption.** A message on the left and, with `maxLength`, a count on the right.
5. **Save and Cancel** (subtle only). Shown below a subtle text area while it is edited.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge; the placeholder until there is text. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. A subtle text area takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Warning, success | The edge takes `--ds-border-warning` or `--ds-border-success`, with the message in the matching text color. |
| Read-only | The `--ds-background-neutral` fill, full contrast, ignoring the pointer. The value can be read, selected and copied. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | At least `--field-min-height-sm` (80). |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Padding | `--pad-y-md` top and bottom, `--pad-x-md` either side. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Label and caption | `--body-sm`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`; the count `--ds-text-subtle`, over the limit `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Save and Cancel | `--stack-sm` apart, aligned to the end. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the field with a short noun phrase: "Session notes". | An instruction where the name belongs: "Write your session notes here". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation on labels. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Say what to do about an error: "Add a note before you send." | "Invalid" or "Error". |
| Keep helper text to one short line. | Paragraphs in the caption. Link to help instead. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` of the `textarea`; the label points at it. Generated when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | The form key the text submits under. |
| `label` | node | — | The visible label above the field. Hide it with `isLabelHidden`. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the textarea. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `isLabelHidden` | bool | `false` | Hides the label without removing it. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for an info tooltip beside the label. |
| `caption` | node | — | Standing help under the field. A message takes its place. |
| `value` | string | — | The text. Pass it, with `onChange`, to control the field. |
| `defaultValue` | string | — | The text to start with when the field is uncontrolled. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | Hint text shown while the field is empty. |
| `rows` | number | `3` | Visible lines of text. One row is the short textarea. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` starts at 80 high with 10 corners; `compact` has 8 corners, to sit beside a 32 field. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'standard'` | `subtle` is borderless until hovered or edited, with Save and Cancel while editing. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Dims the field and blocks focus and editing. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the text and keeps it focusable, but it cannot be changed. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border and sets `aria-invalid`; `errorMessage` says why. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | The caption shown under the field while `isInvalid` is set. It replaces `caption`. |
| `warningMessage` | node | — | Draws the warning border. Does not set `aria-invalid`: the value is accepted. |
| `successMessage` | node | — | Draws the confirmation border. |
| `maxLength` | number | — | Limits the length and shows a count on the right of the caption. |
| `onSave` | func | — | Subtle only: called by Save (or Ctrl/⌘+Enter). Throw or reject to keep the field open in `invalid`. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called with the change event on each edit. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the field gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the field loses focus. |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Called with the keydown event. Call `preventDefault` to stop the subtle appearance's own key handling. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the field wrapper beside the component's own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline styles for the field wrapper. |

## Variants

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`

# TextField

Text field — a labeled single-line field on `_Field`, 40 high and 32 when `spacing="compact"`. Label, field and caption: the caption shows a message (or standing help) on the left and, when `maxLength` is set, a count on the right. `elemBeforeInput` and `elemAfterInput` fill the slots on either side of the control; a string is a text affix. With `appearance="subtle"`, the field reads as plain text until it is hovered or edited, and saves on blur or Enter through `onSave`. `type="number"` adds steppers after the control. Empty is not 0: an empty field stays empty, and stepping from it starts at 0 (or the nearest bound). A typed value outside `min`/`max` is clamped when the field loses focus, not while it is typed. The field is a text input, so the scroll wheel never changes the value.

Also asked as: search box, single-line, text box.

**Import:** `import { TextField } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextField/TextField.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextField/TextField.stories.jsx` — Overview, ElementBefore, TextAffix, HelperText, Filled, Success, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Spacing, FocusRing, Interactive, Anatomy, ErrorAndCount, Warning, Autofill, Search, ButtonsInside, Subtle, CaptionColors, NumberSteppers, NumberEmptyIsNotZero, NumberClampOnBlur, NumberWheelLeavesTheValue, NumberReadOnly, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled, FieldInvalid, FieldReadOnly

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TextField/TextField.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TextField` for single-line text entry: names, emails, search boxes and numbers. It owns its label, its validation state and its message, which makes it the right home for an error rather than a `SectionMessage` at the top of the form. Use `type="number"` only for stepped quantities; IDs, phone numbers and ZIP codes use `type="text"` with `inputMode`.

## Motion

TextField reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Border color changes on focus and error. An error message makes room, then fades in; it fades, then the room closes, once the field is fixed. |

## Alternatives

- For multi-line text, use `TextArea`.
- For finding a record in a list by typing, use `SearchField`.
- For picking a value from a list of options, use `Select`.
- For dates or times, use `DatePicker`, `TimePicker` or `DateTimePicker`.

## Best practices

### Name the field. {#name-the-field}

The label says what the field is, not what to do.

Do: The label names the field.
Don't: An instruction where the name should be reads badly in a list of fields.

### Put one element on each side, at most. {#put-one-element-on-each-side-at-most}

A leading icon or a trailing action, not both crowding the text.

Do: One element before the text.
Don't: Elements on both sides squeeze the value.

### Hint at the answer, not the control. {#hint-at-the-answer-not-the-control}

A placeholder shows what a good answer looks like.

Do: Hint shows the format.
Don't: Hint describes the control.

### Show an error on the field itself. {#show-an-error-on-the-field-itself}

The field carries the invalid state.

Do: The field shows the invalid state.
Don't: A default field gives no sign of the problem.

### Say what to do about an error. {#say-what-to-do-about-an-error}

Do: Say what to do about the error, in the field's own caption.
Don't: A fact that there is an error, with no way forward.

### Keep slots to decoration. {#keep-slots-to-decoration}

A string is a text affix; an icon is hidden from assistive technology. Anything the reader must know belongs in the label or the message, not in the glyph. Do not nest interactive elements in a slot, other than the Button the field is built for: a control with its own focus is announced apart from the field.

### Let the message follow the state. {#let-the-message-follow-the-state}

`errorMessage` shows with `isInvalid`; `warningMessage` and `successMessage` show on their own; otherwise `caption` shows. `maxLength` adds a count on the right beside any of them. A warning accepts the value: use it when the entry is allowed but worth a second look, and `isInvalid` only when the form cannot go on.

### Set `autoComplete` on every field the browser can fill. {#set-autocomplete-on-every-field-the-browser-can-fill}

Login email is `email`, the password is `current-password`, and an access code is `one-time-code`.

### Use subtle for editing in place. {#use-subtle-for-editing-in-place}

`appearance="subtle"` is for record and profile pages, never in a form someone fills from top to bottom. Pass `onSave`.

### Pick the spacing by the row it sits in. {#pick-the-spacing-by-the-row-it-sits-in}

Use `default` in forms and `compact` in toolbars, filter bars and table rows.

### Use `type="number"` for quantities you step. {#use-type-number-for-quantities-you-step}

Use `type="number"` for stepped quantities such as seats; for an ID, phone number or ZIP code, use `type="text"` with `inputMode`.

### Use read-only for fixed values and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-values-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` shows a value someone could change but this person cannot right now: it stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, takes the neutral fill, has no hover and says `aria-readonly`. Say why in the caption. `isDisabled` is for a field that does not apply yet, and takes it out of the tab order. Never swap one for the other, and never clip a read-only value. Content nobody can edit is plain text, not a field. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Read-only keeps the value readable, and the caption says why.
Don't: Disabled fades a value people need to read.

## Accessibility

- **The label is associated whether you pass `id` or not.** One id is derived
  once and used for both the label's `htmlFor` and the input.
- **`isLabelHidden` hides the label, it does not remove it.** The label is
  rendered either way and clipped out of sight. A field that has a `label` has an
  accessible name whether or not you show it. If the visible label is rendered
  by the caller instead, point it at the input with `htmlFor`; if there is no
  text anywhere, pass `aria-label`.
- **`isRequired` sets `aria-required` regardless of the label marker.** Pair it
  with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in
  the form; when most fields are required, mark the optional ones with
  `labelMarker="optional"` instead.
- **An error is announced.** The message gets an id, the input points at it with
  `aria-describedby`, and `isInvalid` sets `aria-invalid` and renders the message
  with `role="alert"`. A warning, a success message and standing help are
  described without being announced. Your own `aria-describedby` is kept and the
  message id is appended.
- **Focus is a ring**, with no change of fill, so it reads in Light, Dark and
  More contrast.
- **The number field is a text input**, so the scroll wheel never changes the
  value. The steppers are named for the field they change: "Decrease Seats" and "Increase Seats".

## Related

- `TextArea`: use when collecting several lines of plain text.
- `SearchField`: use when searching a list or table by typing.
- `Select`: use when choosing a value from a list of options.
- `DatePicker`: use when selecting a date or date range.
- [Form](?path=/docs/components-forms-and-inputs-form--docs): use when reviewing label and caption rules across fields.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Label.** Names the field. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text, and an info tooltip sits beside it.
2. **Before.** An icon, a text affix or a Button before the control.
3. **Control.** The native input.
4. **After.** An icon, a text affix, a Button or the number steppers.
5. **Caption.** A message on the left and, with `maxLength`, a count on the right.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge; the placeholder until there is text. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. A subtle field takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Warning, success | The edge takes `--ds-border-warning` or `--ds-border-success`, with the message in the matching text color. |
| Read-only | The `--ds-background-neutral` fill, full contrast, no hover. The value can be read, selected and copied; number steppers are not drawn. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Side padding | `--pad-x-md`; a Button in a slot sits `--pad-x-xs` from the edge. |
| Slot button | `--control-md` in the 40 field, `--control-sm` in the 32 field. |
| Slots | `--ds-text-subtle`, `--stack-sm` apart; `--radius-control-lg` between slot and control. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Label and caption | `--body-sm`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`; the count `--ds-text-subtle`, over the limit `--ds-text-danger`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the field with a short noun: "Email address". | An instruction where the name belongs: "Enter your email address here". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation on labels. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Say what to do about an error: "Enter a 10-digit number." | "Invalid" or "Error". |
| Keep helper text to one short line. | Paragraphs in the caption. Link to help instead. |
| Put the unit in an affix: "kg". | The unit in the label or the value. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Id of the input, which the label points at. A generated id is used when omitted. |
| `name` | string | — | Form key of the input. Number steppers also report it in the `onChange` event. |
| `label` | node | — | Visible label above the field. A string label also names the number steppers, as "Increase" and "Decrease" followed by the label. |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the input. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `isLabelHidden` | bool | `false` | Hides the label visually. It is still rendered and still names the input. |
| `info` | node | — | Text for an info tooltip beside the label. |
| `caption` | node | — | Standing help under the field. A message takes its place. |
| `placeholder` | string | — | Hint text shown while the input is empty. It does not replace a label. |
| `value` | string or number | — | With `type="number"`, empty (`''` or `null`) stays empty; it is never read as 0. |
| `defaultValue` | string or number | — | Starting value of an uncontrolled field. Use `value` to control it instead. |
| `inputRef` | func or shape or any | — | Ref to the underlying `<input>`, as a callback or a ref object. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` is 40; `compact` is 32. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'standard'` | `subtle` is borderless until hovered or edited, for editing in place. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Disables the input and its number steppers and dims the field. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | With `type="number"`, also hides the steppers; the value can be read and copied. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border and sets `aria-invalid`; `errorMessage` says why. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | Shown in the caption in place of `caption` when `isInvalid` is true. |
| `warningMessage` | node | — | Draws the warning border. Does not set `aria-invalid`: the value is accepted. |
| `successMessage` | node | — | Draws the confirmation border. |
| `elemBeforeInput` | node | — | Before the control. A string is a text affix; a node is rendered as given. |
| `elemAfterInput` | node | — | After the control. A string is a text affix; a node is rendered as given. |
| `type` | string | `'text'` | `number` shows steppers and holds the value as text. |
| `maxLength` | number | — | Limits the length and shows a count on the right of the caption. |
| `min` | number | — | `type="number"`: lower bound. A typed value below it is raised to it when the field loses focus. |
| `max` | number | — | `type="number"`: upper bound. A typed value above it is lowered to it when the field loses focus. |
| `step` | number | `1` | `type="number"`: how much a stepper changes the value. |
| `onSave` | func | — | Subtle only: called on blur or Enter with the new value. Throw or reject to keep the field open in `invalid`. |
| `autoComplete` | string | — | Browser autofill token, e.g. `email`, `current-password`, `one-time-code`. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class on the outer field wrapper, beside `plus-text-field`. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the outer field wrapper. |
| `onChange` | func | — | Called on every edit with the change event. Stepper presses and clamping call it with `{ target: { name, value, type: "number" } }`, the value as text. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Called with the focus event when the input gains focus. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Called with the blur event when the input loses focus. A number field is clamped to `min` and `max` first. |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Called with the keydown event before the field handles it. Call `event.preventDefault()` to skip a subtle field's own key handling. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`appearance`** — `standard` · `subtle`

entries.summary: Tile: a small square frame that holds a logo, thumbnail or icon standing for a thing.

props.name: content
props.description: What the tile frames. Icons and logos are inset; an image fills and crops.

props.name: size
props.description: 16, 20, 24, 32, 40 or 48, for every kind of content.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Icons only. `subtle` is the color's container; `bold` is the solid color.

props.name: color
props.description: A category color from the Tag set. `white` is for logos. Defaults to white for a logo, gray otherwise.

props.name: icon
props.description: `icon` only: a Font Awesome Free name (`book-open`), a class list, or a node.

props.name: src

# Tile

Tile: a small square frame that holds a logo, thumbnail or icon standing for a thing.

**Import:** `import { Tile } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Tile/Tile.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Tile/Tile.stories.jsx` — Sizes, DefaultSize, IconSubtle, IconBold, Logos, LogoDefaultsToWhite, Images, WithBorder, Decorative, Labeled, Interactive, Rest

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/images-and-icons/Tile/Tile.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Tile` wherever a small square picture stands for a thing: a tool's logo in
a list of integrations, a school's crest beside its name, a lesson's thumbnail,
or an icon marking the kind of item in a row. Putting all of them in one frame
keeps them the same size and shape wherever they appear.

## Alternatives

- For a person or an agent, use `Avatar`.
- For an unframed glyph inline with text, use `Icon`.
- For a value someone picked with a text label, use `Tag`.

## Best practices

### Pick the content, then the color. {#pick-the-content-then-the-color}

Icons take `appearance` and `color`. Logos take a ground color only, since the
logo keeps its own. Images cover the whole tile, so color does not apply.

Do: Icons take appearance and color; logos keep their own.
Don't: A bold appearance on a logo, which does nothing.

### Use colors as categories, never statuses. {#use-colors-as-categories-never-statuses}

`color` takes the Tag color set: plain names, never a status. Keep one color per kind of
item across the app, or leave tiles gray.

Do: One color for each kind of item, across the app.
Don't: The same kind of item in two colors.

### Give a logo its own ground. {#give-a-logo-its-own-ground}

Logos default to white. Set a ground color only to match a surface; never recolor the logo.

Do: A logo on the default white ground.
Don't: A bold ground on the logo, which keeps its own.

## Accessibility

- **Decorative by default.** A tile usually sits beside a name that already
  says what it is, so it is hidden from assistive technology
  (`aria-hidden="true"`) unless it has a `label`.
- **`label` makes it one image with a name.** The tile becomes `role="img"`
  with that name, and the picture inside it stays hidden, so the square is
  announced once. Give a tile a label whenever it stands alone, such as a
  logo with no name beside it.
- **Not a control.** A tile has no hover or focus state. To make one clickable,
  wrap it in a button or link that carries the accessible name.

## Related

- `Avatar`: use when representing a person, team or agent.
- `Object`: use when placing a compact record-kind glyph inline with a title.

Same group: `Avatar` · `AvatarGroup` · `Icon` · `Illustration` · `Image` · `Object`

## Parts

1. **Square.** The Media size of the step, `16` to `48`, with a radius of a quarter of its size.
2. **Content.** An icon, a logo or an image. An icon is inset to the Font Awesome size of the same step; an image covers the square.
3. **Border.** Optional, drawn inside the square so the tile keeps its size.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The only state. A tile is a picture, not a control. |
| Hovered, pressed, focused | None. Wrap the tile in a button or link that carries the name and the focus. |
| Disabled | None. Dim the control around it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Square | `--image-xxs` to `--image-xl` for 16 to 48. |
| Icon size | `--icon-sm` to `--icon-lg`, by step. |
| Radius | A quarter of the square; `--radius-control-lg` at 40. Logo inset `--radius-sm`. |
| Icon ground and glyph, subtle | Per color: the subtler accent background and the accent icon of that color; gray uses `--ds-background-neutral` and `--ds-icon-subtle`. |
| Icon ground and glyph, bold | Per color: the bolder accent background and `--ds-icon-inverse`; gray uses `--ds-background-neutral-bold` and `--ds-icon-inverse`. |
| Logo ground | The color's subtler accent background; white is `--ds-surface`. |
| Border | `--border-width-default` in `--ds-border`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label a tile that stands alone with the thing it shows: "Khan Academy". | "Logo" or "Icon", which names the picture. |
| Leave the label off a tile beside its name. | Repeat the name in both places. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `content` | enum | `'icon'` | What the tile frames. Icons and logos are inset; an image fills and crops. |
| `size` | enum | `32` | 16, 20, 24, 32, 40 or 48, for every kind of content. |
| `appearance` | enum | `'subtle'` | Icons only. `subtle` is the color's container; `bold` is the solid color. |
| `color` | enum | — | A category color from the Tag set. `white` is for logos. Defaults to white for a logo, gray otherwise. |
| `icon` | string or node | — | `icon` only: a Font Awesome Free name (`book-open`), a class list, or a node. |
| `src` | string | — | `logo` or `image`: the picture's URL. |
| `children` | node | — | `logo` or `image`: the picture as a node, in place of `src`. |
| `hasBorder` | bool | `false` | Adds a 1px border inside the tile. |
| `label` | string | — | Makes the tile an image with this name. Without it the tile is decorative and hidden. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |

## Variants

**`content`** — `icon` · `logo` · `image`

**`size`** — `16` · `20` · `24` · `32` · `40` · `48`

**`appearance`** — `subtle` · `bold`

**`color`** — `gray` · `blue` · `green` · `purple` · `magenta` · `yellow` · `teal` · `white`

# TimePicker

TimePicker — a time field: type a time, or pick one from the list of the day's times under it (Figma `Time picker`). It is the PLUS Select, searchable: the field is the shared `FieldBox`, the list is the shared `Listbox`, so the box, the list, the keyboard and every state are Select's. There is no separate AM/PM control: each time in the list carries its own period, and typing "2:30p" or "1430" finds it. - **List:** `times`, 24-hour `HH:mm` strings, every half hour by default, shown as "2:30 PM". Typing filters it. - **Typing a time that is not in the list** (`timeIsEditable`, on by default): Enter on the "Create" row reads it — "9:05", "905a", "21:05" — and picks it. Text that is not a real time is refused and the field is marked invalid. - **Value:** a 12-hour string, "02:30 PM", or null once cleared. A 24-hour `value` ("14:30") is accepted and read the same way. Props it does not name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `data-*`) go to the combobox, which is the control a screen reader lands on: TimePicker has no `label` prop, so that is how a caller names it.

Also asked as: time input, clock, time field, time selector.

**Import:** `import { TimePicker } from '@/components';`

**Governed by:** Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TimePicker/TimePicker.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TimePicker/TimePicker.stories.jsx` — Overview, Spacing, InteractionStates, PickTime, TwentyFourHourValueIsSplit, Default, WithValue, Compact, Invalid, ReadOnly, Disabled, HoveredState, KeyboardFocus, Interactive

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TimePicker/TimePicker.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.default`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TimePicker` to enter or choose a time of day, such as a reminder time or a recurring slot's start.

## Motion

TimePicker reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades. |
| change | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | A month change slides the grid flat. |

## Alternatives

- For a date or date range with no time, use `DatePicker`.
- For a combined date and time answer, use `DateTimePicker`.

## Best practices

### The field always reports a 12-hour value. {#the-field-always-reports-a-12-hour-value}

`onChange` fires with a string like `"02:30 PM"` regardless of how `value` was given, or `null` once the field is cleared. A 24-hour `value` is accepted and read as the same time, but what it hands back is always 12-hour.

```jsx
<TimePicker value={time} onChange={setTime} />
```

### Show the format in the placeholder. {#show-the-format-in-the-placeholder}

The placeholder shows hours and minutes with a colon (`__ : __`), so an empty field says what it holds. The field also parses compact typed digits (`1430` or `930a`) into the chosen time.

Do: The placeholder shows hours and minutes with a colon.
Don't: The placeholder has no colon.

### Offer round steps. {#offer-round-steps}

Half-hour or quarter-hour steps match how sessions are booked; pass custom intervals as `times`. Odd minutes nobody books only add noise.

Do: A round start time.
Don't: An odd minute.

### Pick the period with the time. {#pick-the-period-with-the-time}

Every option in the list carries `AM` or `PM` (`9:30 AM` and `9:30 PM` are separate rows). A typed time without `AM` or `PM` is read on the twenty-four-hour clock (`9:30` as morning, `21:30` as evening).

### Show a set time as read-only, not disabled. {#show-a-set-time-as-read-only-not-disabled}

`isReadOnly` shows a time the person may read but not change; `isDisabled` fades a field that does not apply right now and removes it from the tab order. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs) and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: A set time, read-only and easy to read.
Don't: The same time disabled, faded as if it did not apply.

## Accessibility

- **There is no `label` prop.** Name the field with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, forwarded straight to the combobox a screen reader lands on, same as `aria-describedby` and `data-*`.
- **It is a combobox with a listbox**, the same as Select: arrow keys move through the times, Enter picks, Escape closes the list.
- **A refused typed time marks the field invalid** with `aria-invalid`, so the person hears that it was not taken.

## Related

- `DatePicker`: use when selecting a date or date range without a time.
- `DateTimePicker`: use when selecting a date and a time together.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `Toggle` · `TreeSelect`

## Parts

1. **Field.** A 40 box (32 at compact) on the input fill. It holds the chosen time, and takes typing.
2. **List.** The day's times, every half hour by default (`times` changes them), each with its period. It opens under the field and filters as you type.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `--ds-background-input` fill with a `--ds-border-input` border. |
| Hovered | The border takes `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Focused | A 2px ring in `--ds-border-focused`, 2px off the box. |
| Invalid | The border takes `--ds-border-danger`. |
| Read-only | The box takes `--ds-background-neutral`, at full contrast with no hover. The chevron is not drawn and a press opens no list. |
| Disabled | The box fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Fill | `--ds-background-input`; read-only `--ds-background-neutral`. |
| Border | `--ds-border-input`; hovered `--ds-border-focused`; invalid `--ds-border-danger`. |
| Text | `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Focus ring | `--ds-border-focused`, 2px, 2px offset. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the time by its role: "Reminder time", "Session start". | A generic name: "Time". |
| Say what is expected when invalid: "Enter a time such as 2:30 PM". | "Invalid time". |
| Show the period with every time: "2:30 PM". | A bare "2:30" that could be either half of the day. |
| Use sentence case in labels and messages. | Title case: "Reminder Time". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | The `id` of the combobox input. |
| `name` | string | — | Submitted with a form, as the 12-hour value. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'__ : __'` | Defaults to `__ : __`. |
| `value` | string | — | A 12-hour string ("02:30 PM") or a 24-hour one ("14:30"). |
| `times` | arrayOf | `DEFAULT_TIMES` | The times the list offers, as 24-hour `HH:mm`. Every half hour of the day by default. |
| `timeIsEditable` | bool | `true` | Lets a typed time that is not in the list be picked. On by default. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` is 40; `compact` is 32. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | Dims the field and blocks opening and changing it. |
| `isReadOnly` | bool | `false` | Shows the time without letting the user change it. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the field invalid; a typed text that is not a time does too. |
| `isValid` | bool | `false` | Draws the field valid. |
| `onChange` | func | — | `(value)` — a 12-hour string, "02:30 PM", or null once cleared. |
| `onFocus` | func | — | Focus entering the field from outside it. |
| `onBlur` | func | — | Focus leaving the field and its list. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names on the field's wrapper, beside its own. |
| `style` | object | — | Inline style on the field's wrapper. |

## Variants

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

# Toggle

Toggle — turns one setting on or off, and the change takes effect at once. Controlled with `isChecked` or uncontrolled with `defaultChecked`. Built on Base UI's Switch: a `role="switch"` span with a hidden checkbox beside it for form submission. `readOnly` blocks the change at the root, so no hand-rolled click guard is needed. Extra attributes (`aria-label`, `aria-describedby`) go to the switch root.

Also asked as: enable disable, on/off setting.

**Import:** `import { Toggle } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`)

**Governed by:** Forms (`ds guide forms`); Read-only (`ds guide read-only`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Toggle/Toggle.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Toggle/Toggle.stories.jsx` — Motion, Overview, Sizes, States, Loading, Content, Interactive, ReadOnly, KeyboardFocus, TrackColors, Unchecked, Checked, Hovered, HoveredOn, Focused, Disabled, DisabledWithReason

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/Toggle/Toggle.mdx`

**Motion:** change `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `Toggle` to let a person turn a single setting on or off with immediate effect, such as making a resource public.

Pick the size by the page: `size={16}` (default) where a page has many toggles, such as a settings list, and `size={20}` to call attention to a single prominent setting.

## Motion

Toggle reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Color carries the feedback; the thumb follows. |

## Alternatives

- For an option in a form that waits for a Save or Submit button to apply, use `Checkbox`.
- For choosing one option from a short set of labeled choices, use `RadioGroup`.
- For choosing one option from a list of six or more, use `Select`.

## Best practices

### Label what turns on. {#label-what-turns-on}

The label names the setting, not the toggle position. It stays the same whether the toggle is on or off.

Do: The label names the setting.
Don't: "On" says nothing about what is on.

### Keep the label neutral across both positions. {#keep-the-label-neutral-across-both-positions}

A label that reads as a state, such as "Reminders on", contradicts the control when the toggle is off; a noun phrase such as "Session reminders" reads accurately in both positions.

Do: Off, and the setting's name still reads right.
Don't: Off, but the label says on.

### Say why a toggle is disabled. {#say-why-a-toggle-is-disabled}

Disable a toggle only for something the person can fix on the same screen, and state the reason in text next to it, never in a tooltip. A setting a role can never use is hidden. See [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs).

Do: Disabled, with the reason beside it.
Don't: Disabled with no reason, so nothing says what to fix.

### Apply the change immediately. {#apply-the-change-immediately}

A toggle changes the setting as soon as it is flipped. If the change needs confirming or saving with a form button, use `Checkbox`.

### Name, value and id. {#name-value-and-id}

`name` is a form key, not an id; two toggles may share a name. `isChecked` controls the value and needs an `onChange`; `defaultChecked` sets the start.

### Use read-only for fixed settings and disabled for unavailable ones. {#use-read-only-for-fixed-settings-and-disabled-for-unavailable-ones}

`isReadOnly` shows a setting the person may read but not change: the toggle stays in the tab order at full contrast, has no hover, says `aria-readonly` and ignores clicks. Say why beside it. `isDisabled` takes it out of the tab order and grays it, for a setting that does not apply right now. See [Read-only](?path=/docs/patterns-states-read-only--docs).

## Accessibility

- **Label every toggle.** Use a visible `label`, or pass `aria-label` when the layout already names the setting.
- **Native checkbox with `role="switch"`.** The platform maps the checked state, so no `aria-checked` is written; a `role` prop on the toggle replaces it. Space flips the toggle.
- **Keyboard focus is a 2px ring on `border.focused`, 2px off the track.**
- **Explain a disabled toggle** in visible text beside it rather than a tooltip.

## Related

- `Checkbox`: use when an option requires a form button press to apply.
- `RadioGroup`: use when choosing one option from a short visible set.
- `Select`: use when choosing one option from a longer list.
- `Tooltip`: use to explain what flipping a toggle does.

## Parts

1. **Track.** A pill, 32 by 16 or 40 by 20. Off it is the neutral bold fill; on it is the selected bold fill.
2. **Thumb.** An inverse circle inset 2 from the track. It slides to the end when the toggle is on.
3. **Label.** 14/20 text beside the track in a 24 row. It names the setting and stays the same in both states.
4. **Spinner.** Optional, between the track and the label while a change is saved.

| Rest | Off: `--ds-background-neutral-bold`. On: `--ds-background-selected-bold`. |
| Hovered | Off: `--ds-background-neutral-bold-hovered`. On: `--ds-background-selected-bold-hovered`. |

| Read-only | Full contrast, in the tab order, no hover, `aria-readonly`. Not changeable. |
| Loading | A spinner sits between the track and the label; input is ignored. |

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the setting as a noun phrase: "Session reminders". | An instruction or a status: "Turn on reminders", "Reminders are on". |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation. | Title case, or a period after the label. |
| Keep the label to a few words. | A sentence that explains the setting. Put the explanation in a caption or a Tooltip. |
| Write the label so it reads right in both positions. | "Enable" or "Disable" in the label, which the position already says. |

rankedText.best:
### Let the component drive hover and focus rather than passing `show`.

```jsx
// Incorrect — once `show` is defined, `trigger`, `delayShow` and `delayHide`
// are ignored, and the tooltip is only as visible as `show` says.
<Tooltip text="Saved" show={justSaved} trigger="hover" delayHide={2000}>
  <Button appearance="primary" text="Save" />
</Tooltip>

// Correct — let the component drive itself for hover, and use Flag for a
// transient confirmation.
<Tooltip text="Save this draft"><Button appearance="primary" text="Save" /></Tooltip>
```

### Say what the control does.

Do: A few words on what the control does.

Don't: Repeats the label the control already shows.

### Keep it to one short line.

Do: One line, sentence case, no closing period.

Don't: Two sentences that wrap, with a closing period.

### Never put a tooltip on a disabled control.

A disabled control takes no hover and no focus, so a tooltip on it never opens, and touch has no hover at all. Explain why in text on the page; see Disabled.

```jsx
// Incorrect: the disabled button cannot show the tooltip.
<Tooltip text="Add the session notes first">
  <Button appearance="primary" text="Save notes" isDisabled />
</Tooltip>

// Correct: the button stays enabled and the reason is text on the page.
<Button appearance="primary" text="Save notes" onClick={explainWhatIsMissing} />
```

### Put anything the user can click in a `Popup`.

Do: A popup holds content the user can reach.

Don't: A link in a tooltip: moving toward it leaves the trigger, and the tooltip hides.

# TreeSelect

TreeSelect: a field that picks from options that nest, at any level of the tree.

**Import:** `import { TreeSelect } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TreeSelect/TreeSelect.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TreeSelect/TreeSelect.stories.jsx` — Overview, SingleSelect, MultiSelect, SpacingDefault, SpacingCompact, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Focused, FieldDisabled, FieldInvalid, OpensWithAFade, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced, MotionKeyboardOpen

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/TreeSelect/TreeSelect.mdx`

**Motion:** enter `appearance.fast` · exit `appearance.fast` · change `spatial.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TreeSelect` when options nest in a hierarchy and someone needs to expand branches in place or pick nodes across multiple branches, such as curriculum units and lessons.

## Motion

TreeSelect reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens as a Popup: a fade in place. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place on appearance.fast, the same as the enter; stays mounted until the exit completes. |
| change | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Columns and branches expand. |

## Alternatives

- For a single hierarchical path chosen one column per level in sequence, use `Cascader`.
- For a flat list of options with no hierarchy, use `Select`.

## Best practices

### Use multi select for several branches. {#use-multi-select-for-several-branches}

With `isMulti` each chosen node is named in the field; a single value holds one.

Do: Each chosen node is named in the field.
Don't: A single value cannot hold several nodes.

### Open the tree to show nesting. {#open-the-tree-to-show-nesting}

The open tree shows how nodes nest before the choice is made. Arrow keys move through visible rows only: a collapsed branch's children are in the data but not on screen, so expand a branch first to reach what is inside it.

### Show the chosen node in the field. {#show-the-chosen-node-in-the-field}

A filled field shows the choice; an empty one cannot confirm it.

Do: The field names the chosen node.
Don't: An empty field after a choice cannot confirm it.

### Mark a failed pick on the field. {#mark-a-failed-pick-on-the-field}

With `isInvalid`, the field draws the danger border and `errorMessage` replaces the caption.

Do: A failed pick draws the danger border, so the error is seen at the field.
Don't: A failed pick still draws the normal border, so nothing marks the error.

### Checking a parent is shorthand for checking every descendant. {#checking-a-parent-is-shorthand-for-checking-every-descendant}

With `isMulti`, picking a parent node cascades the check to its whole
subtree, and a branch with only some descendants checked shows an
indeterminate mark rather than fully checked or unchecked. `value` always
reflects the actual set of checked nodes, parents included once their
subtree is complete.

```jsx
<TreeSelect
    label="Topics"
    isMulti
    value={topics}
    onChange={setTopics}
    options={[
        { value: 'roosevelt-k8', label: 'Roosevelt K-8', children: [
            { value: 'roosevelt-mon', label: 'Monday 3:30 PM' },
            { value: 'roosevelt-wed', label: 'Wednesday 3:30 PM' },
        ] },
    ]}
/>
```

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard matches what's visible.** Up/Down move between the currently
  expanded rows only, never into a collapsed branch's hidden children.
- **Checked state is explicit, including partial.** A parent with some but
  not all descendants checked is marked indeterminate, not silently rounded
  up or down to a checked or unchecked state.
- **Without a visible label, name the field explicitly** with `aria-label`
  or `aria-labelledby` — `label` is optional, but an accessible name isn't.

## Related

- `Cascader`: use when building a single path one level at a time across columns.
- `Select`: use when choosing from a flat list of options.

Same group: `Button` · `ButtonGroup` · `Calendar` · `Cascader` · `Checkbox` · `CheckboxGroup` · `ChoiceGrid` · `CloseButton` · `Comment` · `DatePicker` · `DateTimePicker` · `DropdownMenu` · `Fieldset` · `FileItem` · `FileUpload` · `FilterButton` · `FilterMenu` · `FooterActions` · `IconButton` · `InlineEditableTextfield` · `LinkButton` · `LinkIconButton` · `PopupSelect` · `Radio` · `RadioGroup` · `Range` · `Rating` · `RichTextEditor` · `SearchField` · `Select` · `SettingRow` · `SplitButton` · `TagInput` · `TextArea` · `TextField` · `TimePicker` · `Toggle`

## Parts

1. **Field.** The box that shows the picks, or the placeholder.
2. **Label.** Names the field. An optional minority marker (`"(optional)"` or `"(required)"`) follows it in plain text.
3. **Tree.** Rows that expand to their children. A parent checks its descendants.
4. **Caption.** Helper text, or the error that replaces it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The input fill with a `--border-width-default` input edge; the placeholder until a node is picked. |
| Hovered | The edge turns `--ds-border-focused`. |
| Pressed | No step of its own. The hovered edge holds while the pointer is down, and the press opens the tree. |
| Focused | A `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. No fill changes. |
| Disabled | The whole field fades to `--ds-opacity-disabled` and leaves the tab order. |
| Invalid | The edge takes `--ds-border-danger` and the message `--ds-text-danger`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Box | `--ds-background-input` fill, `--border-width-default` edge in `--ds-border-input`. |
| Height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--control-md`. |
| Radius | 10: `--radius-control-lg`. Compact 8: `--radius-control-md`. |
| Text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Label and caption | `--body-sm`; label `--ds-text`, caption `--ds-text-subtle`, error `--ds-text-danger`. |
| Tree panel | `--ds-surface-overlay` with a `--ds-border` edge, `--popup-radius` and `--ds-shadow-overlay`. |
| Row | `--control-md` high; hovered `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, picked `--ds-background-selected` with `--ds-text-selected`; the expand toggle `--ds-icon-subtle`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each node by what it is: "Lincoln Middle". | A node that only reads right under its parent. |
| Keep branches shallow, two or three levels. | A tree deeper than people can hold in mind. |
| Say what to do in an error: "Pick a topic". | "Required" or "Invalid". |
| Use the same label form at every level. | Mix a category name with a full sentence. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `name` | string | — | Submitted with a form through hidden inputs, one per value. |
| `label` | node | — | The visible label above the field. Without one, pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. |
| `caption` | node | — | Help under the field. With `isInvalid`, `errorMessage` takes its place and is announced. |

| `value` | string or number or arrayOf | — | — |
| `options` | arrayOf | `[]` | — |
| `onChange` | func | — | — |
| `isMulti` | bool | `false` | Several values, shown as checkboxes beside the toggle. |
| `placeholder` | string | `'Please select'` | Hint text shown in the field while nothing is selected. Defaults to `Please select`. |
| `spacing` | enum | `'default'` | `default` draws 40 and `compact` draws 32. |
| `isDisabled` | bool | `false` | — |
| `labelMarker` | enum | — | Marks the form's minority case in plain text after the label: `required` or `optional`. |
| `isRequired` | bool | `false` | Sets `aria-required` on the combobox. Pair with `labelMarker="required"` only when required fields are the minority in the form. |
| `isInvalid` | bool | `false` | Draws the error border, sets `aria-invalid`, and `errorMessage` becomes the announced caption. |
| `errorMessage` | node | — | — |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |

**`spacing`** — `default` · `compact`

**`labelMarker`** — `required` · `optional`
