<!-- DO NOT EDIT BY HAND. Generated by npm run generate:component-docs -->

# TreeTable

Tree table. Records that nest: a school, its classes, their students. Each level indents one step and keeps every column, so the nested rows can still be read across. Built on the table shell with `HeadCell`s and the shared `TableRow` and `TableCell` parts. - **Data.** `items` is one `{ id, cells, children, hasChildren, count }` per row; `cells` is one `{ content }` per column, and `children` nests the same shape. A row with `hasChildren` and no `children` gets them from `loadChildren(item)`, which returns them or a promise of them; until they arrive a loading message row sits under it, and an empty answer leaves an empty message row. - **Expand and collapse.** The chevron toggles a parent (12 tall in a 24 hit area). `shouldExpandOnClick` lets a press anywhere on the row toggle it too, but never a press on a control inside the row, so use it only on rows without controls. `defaultExpandedIds` seeds the open rows; `expandedIds` with `onExpandedChange` hands them to the page. - **Keyboard.** The WAI-ARIA treegrid pattern in row-focus mode, written here because Base UI has no treegrid part (an ADR-037 exception, like the Select keyboard):  the table is one tab stop; Down and Up move between rows, Home and End to the ends; Right opens a closed parent, then moves to its first child; Left closes an open parent, then moves to the parent row; Enter toggles. Every row carries `aria-level`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and a parent `aria-expanded`.

Also asked as: table tree, nested table.

**Import:** `import { TreeTable } from '@/components';`

**Used in:** Table (`ds guide table`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/TreeTable/TreeTable.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/TreeTable/TreeTable.stories.jsx` — Overview, LoadingChildren, Keyboard, ExpandOnRowPress, Rest, Focused, Interactive, MotionOpenClose, MotionReduced

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/TreeTable/TreeTable.mdx`

**Motion:** expand `spatial.fast` + `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use `TreeTable` for records that nest up to three levels: a curriculum of units
and lessons, a folder of sessions.

## Motion

TreeTable reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| expand | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Tree rows reveal from their parent by spring height; collapse completes before removal. Reduced motion holds the final size and fades. |

## Alternatives

- For a flat grid people read or sort or page, use `Table`.

## Best practices

### Keep every column at every level. {#keep-every-column-at-every-level}

Do: Each level indents one step and keeps both columns.
Don't: Levels that drop a column, so the type column goes ragged.

### Load children late for a long tree. {#load-children-late-for-a-long-tree}

Do: `hasChildren` with `loadChildren` fetches a branch the first time it opens.
Don't: `hasChildren` with nothing to load them, so the branch opens onto the empty message.

### Leave the row press for rows without controls. {#leave-the-row-press-for-rows-without-controls}

`shouldExpandOnClick` never fires from a button or link in the row. A row that carries controls reads better with the chevron alone.

Do: A row of plain text opens on a press anywhere.
Don't: A link in the row, where a press means two things.

## Accessibility

- **A treegrid.** Each row carries `aria-level`, `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize`, and a parent `aria-expanded`, so depth and state are announced.
- **One tab stop.** Arrow keys move, open and close rows; Home and End jump to the ends; Enter toggles.
- **The chevron is a pointer target only.** It is `aria-hidden`; the keyboard route is the arrow keys on the row.
- **Loading is busy.** A parent whose children are loading is `aria-busy`.

## Related

- `DynamicTable`: use when sorting, selecting or paging flat rows on the same table shell.
- Table: use when choosing between Static, Dynamic and Tree tables.

Same group: `Code` · `CodeBlock` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `StaticTable` · `VisuallyHidden`

## Parts

1. **Head cell.** A label, as in the other tables.
2. **Chevron.** `12` tall in a `24` hit area, leading a parent's title cell; a spinner while children load.
3. **Indent.** One `--table-indent` step per level, up to three levels.
4. **Count.** An optional count beside a parent's name.
5. **Message row.** Under an open parent that is loading or has nothing in it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Clear rows; depth shows as indentation. |
| Hovered, pressed | The row takes the subtle hovered and pressed steps. |
| Focused | Shows the focus ring inset on the row; focus is never a fill. |
| Expanded, collapsed, loading | The chevron points down or right, or turns into a spinner. |
| Disabled | Not applicable. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Indent per level | `--table-indent` |
| Chevron, hit area | `--icon-sm`, `--control-sm` |
| Ring | `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` |
| Row height | `--row-height-md` |
| Hairlines | `--ds-border` |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name each node for what it contains: "Linear equations". | Repeat the parent's name in every child. |
| Keep nesting to three levels. | Nest deeper than three levels. |
| Put a total in its own column; use `count` for how many children a row holds. | Put counts in the node name. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `head` | enum | — | One `{ key, content, width, align }` per column |
| `items` | arrayOf | `[]` | One `{ id, cells, children, hasChildren, count }` per row |
| `label` | string | — | The treegrid's accessible name. |
| `loadChildren` | func | — | Returns a row's children, or a promise of them, the first time it opens. |
| `shouldExpandOnClick` | bool | `false` | A press anywhere on a parent row toggles it; never a press on a control in the row. |
| `expandedIds` | arrayOf | — | The open rows' ids, owned by the page. |
| `defaultExpandedIds` | arrayOf | `[]` | The rows open at first when the table holds its own expansion. |
| `onExpandedChange` | func | — | Called with every open row's id when a row opens or closes. |
| `emptyMessage` | node | `'Nothing in here yet'` | The message under an open parent with nothing in it. |
| `size` | enum | `40` | Row height: 32, 40 or 48. |
| `className` | string | `''` | Extra class names added to the table's wrapper beside the component's own. |
| `testId` | string | — | Maps to `data-testid`, for test queries. |

## Variants

**`size`** — `32` · `40` · `48`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.

## Tokens touched

`--control-sm` · `--ds-text-subtle` · `--focus-ring-width` · `--icon-sm` · `--inline-md` · `--plus-table-row-height` · `--plus-tree-table-level` · `--table-indent` · `--type-weight-regular`

entries.text: # VisuallyHidden Text that assistive technology reads and nobody sees: a one-pixel, clipped span taken out of the flow. It is the `.visually-hidden` class `main.scss` defines, which the rest of the system already uses by class name, given a component so the caller never types the class. It paints nothing, so it takes no tokens. Also asked as: screen reader only, sr-only, assistive text, screen reader text. **Import:** `import { VisuallyHidden } from '@/components';` **Used in:** Section (`ds guide section`) **Governed by:** Loading (`ds guide loading`) **Source:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.jsx` **Stories:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.stories.jsx` — Overview, NamesAControl, HiddenColumnHeaders, RoleAndId, Interactive **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/text-and-data-display/VisuallyHidden/VisuallyHidden.mdx` ## Usage Use `VisuallyHidden` when the words a screen reader needs are not words a sighted person needs: the name of an icon-only button, the title of a table column that holds only checkboxes, the count in a status message, a table caption the layout already explains. It renders the `.visually-hidden` class on a `span`, which is one pixel square, clipped, out of the flow and kept in the accessibility tree. Existing markup that writes `className="visually-hidden"` is the same thing and can move to the component as it is touched. ## Alternatives - For an icon-only button that already takes a required `label` prop, use `IconButton`. - For a short visible label on hover and focus over a control, use `Tooltip`. ## Best practices ### Name icon-only controls. {#name-icon-only-controls} A control with no visible words still needs a name a screen reader can say. Do: Hidden text names the icon. Don't: An icon-only control left unnamed. ### Add context the layout implies. {#add-context-the-layout-implies} Sighted readers see the heading above a link; others need the words. Do: Hidden words complete the link. Don't: “Read more” repeated with no object. ### Do not repeat what is visible. {#do-not-repeat-what-is-visible} Hidden text that duplicates visible text is read twice. Do: The visible label speaks for itself. Don't: The label echoed in hidden text. ### Hide with `VisuallyHidden`, not with `display: none`. {#hide-with-visuallyhidden-not-with-display-none} `display: none` and the `hidden` attribute remove the text from the accessibility tree too, so nothing is announced. ```jsx // Incorrect: nothing is announced. Delete session // Correct: drawn nowhere, still read. Delete session ``` ### Do not hide what a sighted person also needs. {#do-not-hide-what-a-sighted-person-also-needs} An instruction that is invisible to people who can see is one they cannot find. Say it to everyone, and let the field point at it. ```jsx ``` ### Keep it out of the focus order. {#keep-it-out-of-the-focus-order} A hidden link or button can still be focused, and a keyboard user lands on something they cannot see. Hide text, not controls; a skip link needs to appear on focus. ## Accessibility - **Announced, not drawn.** The text stays in the accessibility tree, so it is part of the name, description or content of whatever contains it. This is the difference from `display: none`, `visibility: hidden` and `aria-hidden`, which remove it. - **Pair with `aria-hidden` on the visual.** An icon beside hidden text should be `aria-hidden="true"`, so the control is announced once, by its text. - **Live regions.** `role="status"` makes a polite announcement when its text changes. Render the region before the text changes, since a region that appears already filled is often not announced. - **No contrast or size to meet.** Nothing is painted, so there is no color requirement. The text should still be written for the ear: complete words, in the page's language. ## Related - `Tooltip`: use when pairing an icon-only control with a visible label on hover and focus. - `Spinner`: use when rendering a loading indicator, which already includes its own visually hidden label. Same group: `Code` · `CodeBlock` · `DynamicTable` · `Heading` · `InlineEdit` · `StaticTable` · `TreeTable` ## Parts 1. **Span.** The only part: a clipped `span` of text, out of the flow, that stays in the accessibility tree and paints nothing. ### States | State | What changes | | --- | --- | | Rest | The only state. Nothing is drawn; the text is read as part of whatever contains it. | | Hovered | None. There is nothing on screen to point at. | | Pressed | None. There is nothing on screen to press. | | Focused | None. It is not in the tab order; keep controls out of it. | | Disabled | None. It has no disabled state. | ### Tokens | Part | Token | | --- | --- | | Span | None. It paints nothing, so it takes no color, type or spacing tokens. | ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Name what the control does: "Delete session". | Leave an icon-only control with no name. | | Add only the words the layout implies: "Read more about the spring schedule". | Repeat words that are already visible. | | Write for the ear: complete words, in the page's language. | Hide instructions a sighted person also needs. | ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |------|------|---------|-------------| | `children` | node | — | The text screen readers announce. | | `id` | string | — | An id other elements can point at with `aria-labelledby` or `aria-describedby`. | | `role` | string | — | An ARIA role for the span, such as `status` for a live region. |

contextPages.intro: Which button, in which look, in which place, with which word. Cancel, Close, Clear, Reset, copy, edit, remove, the destructive tiers, and acting on many rows at once.
contextPages.name: Common actions
contextPages.text:
# Common actions

Which button, in which look, in which place, with which word. Cancel, Close, Clear, Reset, copy, edit, remove, the destructive tiers, and acting on many rows at once.

## Appearances

Primary, Default, Subtle, Warning, Danger, Discovery and AI. One Primary per area; one AI per region. The Button page holds every appearance and state; these are the places they go.

## Footers

One question picks the footer: what does it finish? An action that leaves is a link; an action that does something is a button.

| Where | Footer |
| --- | --- |
| Modal, Panel | FooterActions: four equal tracks, filled buttons 48 high, Primary last, no Cancel (the corner Close dismisses). A side action leads as a link, or as a danger link when it destroys. "Not now", "Skip" and "Keep editing" are Default buttons in the left half, never the leading slot. |
| Multi-step task (Frame) | The same FooterActions pinned under every step, one-question steps too: Save and exit as a link at the start, Back, then Next or Finish. No centered Back and Continue, no progress dots. |
| A form on a page | Buttons hug their labels at 32, at the start under the last field, Primary first: Save, then Cancel or Reset. Never pinned or full bleed. |
| Card | Buttons hug at the start. One action that goes somewhere is a link; two are a compact pair with no Primary; a card that is all one action is clickable and has no buttons. |
| Popup (filter menu, date picker) | Compact 24 at the end: Clear (Subtle), Apply (Default). No Primary. |

The place sets the alignment: a page form's buttons start under the fields; a layer's end where the eye does.

- **In a Modal.** Four tracks: Discard left, Primary right, no Cancel.
- **In a Modal, with a side action.** A danger link leads; a secondary and the Primary fill tracks 3 and 4.
- **In a multi-step task.** Save and exit as a link at the left edge; Back and Next in the right half.
- **In a page form.** Left-aligned under the fields, Primary first.
- **In a card.** A link for one action that leaves; a compact pair otherwise.
- **In a Popup.** Clear (Subtle) and Apply (Default), compact, at the end.

## Small actions

## Destructive tiers

Three tiers, picked by whether the change can be undone. No danger-outline combinations.

- **Active.** Reversible change: Discard and a Primary action.
- **Active with Danger.** A delete: Danger in place of Primary.
- **Danger, type the name.** Irreversible delete: Danger enables once the typed name matches.

## Acting on many rows

## Key cases

## Motion

## Usage

Choose a button's appearance by importance, placement by what it acts on, and label by what happens.

| Action | Appearance | Place | Word |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The main action of an area | Primary, one per area | Last in its group (on a page form: first, before Cancel) | Verb and object: "Add students" |
| Another action in the area | Default | Before the Primary | Verb and object: "Reschedule session" |
| Decline or postpone: "Not now", "Skip", "Keep editing", "Save for later" | Default | Left half of a two-action footer, beside the Primary | "Not now" |
| A side action that is not one of the footer's two outcomes | Link when it leaves, danger link when it destroys | The leading slot, at the left edge | "Save and exit"; "Delete draft" |
| Leave a page form without saving | Subtle | After Primary on a page form | "Cancel"; a link is allowed |
| Go somewhere from a card | Link, compact | The card's footer, at the start | "Open session" |
| Two actions on a card | Default pair, compact, no Primary | The card's footer, at the start | "Reschedule", "Add note" |
| Dismiss a Modal, Panel or Flag | Icon button | End of the header | Named "Close" |
| Empty a Popup's choices | Subtle, compact, before Apply (Default) | The end of the Popup's footer, or the top of a filter side | "Clear" in a Popup; "Reset filters" everywhere else |
| Empty one field | Icon button inside the field | End of the field | Named "Clear", "Clear search" |
| Copy a value | Icon button | Beside the value | Named "Copy"; "Copied" in a tooltip after |
| Change one value on a record | Inline edit on hover | On the value | Pencil named "Edit" |
| Change the whole record | Default, or Edit inside More | Title row or More menu | "Edit" |
| Take something out of a group | Default, or inside More | Row's More menu, or the bulk bar | "Remove from group" |
| Destroy something | Danger, after a confirm | A Modal's footer | "Delete note"; "Delete group" with the name typed when it cannot be undone |
| A change with a cost, not a delete | Warning | A Modal's footer | "Remove from this week" |
| The call to try something new | Discovery | Where the new thing starts | "Try the new schedule view" |
| The one AI action in a region | AI | With the region's actions | "Generate summary" |

## Alternatives

- For a set of choices the person picks between, use `RadioGroup`, not a row of buttons.
- For a menu of actions behind one trigger, use `DropdownMenu` from a More icon button.
- For a main action with variations, use `SplitButton`.
- For moving to another page, use `LinkButton`; a button acts on this page.
- For narrowing rows, follow Filtering: a filter is not an action.

## Best practices

### Give an area one Primary button.

The Primary is the main call to action or a form's submit. A second main action is Default beside it; a second Primary makes neither read as the next step. The AI appearance follows the same rule, one per region, and only for an action that calls AI.

Do: One Primary, with the other action Default beside it.
Don't: Two Primary buttons in one row: neither reads as the next step.

### Left-align buttons under a page form and right-align them in a Modal or a multi-step task.

On a page the Primary comes first, read in the same direction as the fields. In a layer the Primary is furthest right, where the eye ends. Stacked buttons put the Primary on top. Never top-aligned.

Do: Primary first, then Cancel, left-aligned under the fields.
Don't: The buttons at the far end of the page, away from the fields, with the Primary last.

### Fill the four tracks in a Modal footer and keep it 48 high.

FooterActions divides the footer into four equal tracks: filled buttons 48 high, Primary in the last track. One button takes the right half. A side action leads as a link and takes no track. A Panel's editing footer and a multi-step task's footer use the same component.

Do: Two buttons filling the footer's four tracks.
Don't: Small buttons in a group, with spare footer around them instead of filling the tracks.

### Keep the footer where it is.

Header and footer stay pinned while the body scrolls. A blocked submit, a server message and a sending button change the body or a button, never the footer's size or place. A sending button swaps its label for a spinner in place and keeps its width; only that button disables, and the secondary action stays live.

### Keep Close an icon button, and use Cancel only where there is no Close.

Close ends a layer and lives in its header, or by Save and exit in a multi-step task. In a Modal and Panel the corner Close dismisses, so their footers carry real actions (such as Discard or Keep) and no Cancel. A page form has no Close, so it keeps a subtle Cancel. A Popup holds no form, so it has no Cancel; Escape or a click outside dismisses it.

### Make Cancel Subtle on page forms.

Beside a Primary it is already clear the row is interactive, so Cancel steps back as Subtle. Cancel may be a link where a button would compete. In a Modal or Panel footer every filled track is a button, so the secondary action takes the Default fill to read as one. "Not now", "Skip" and "Keep editing" are that secondary action, never Subtle and never in the leading slot.

### Say Clear in a menu and Reset filters everywhere else.

The words and where they sit: Filtering › Say Clear in a menu and Reset filters everywhere else.

### Confirm a copy with a Copied tooltip, not a Flag.

The tooltip opens on the Copy button the moment the value is on the clipboard and leaves on its own. Flags stay for events that happened somewhere else.

### Edit one value inline and the whole record from More.

A value read far more than changed takes `InlineEdit`: a pencil on hover and focus, saved on its own. The record's More menu includes Edit, which opens the form host the Forms pattern picks. Never put inline edits inside a form that has its own Save.

### Name a destructive action by its tier.

Active: it can be undone, Discard (or a real alternative) and a Primary. Active with Danger: a delete, the action in Danger. Danger with the name typed: a delete that cannot be undone, the field caption asks for the name and the Danger button enables once it matches, with no tooltip. Remove, which takes something out of a group it can return to, is Default, not Danger. The Modal that raises the confirm: Modal.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected.

The bar and its words: Section › Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected.

### Link one action in a card, and pair two.

A card's buttons hug the start of its footer. One action that goes somewhere is a link; two actions are a compact Default pair with no Primary. A card that is all one action is clickable instead and has no inner buttons.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Verb and object: "Log session", "Add students", "Remove from group". | "Submit", "OK", "Yes", "Continue" with nothing after it. |
| "Cancel" on a page form; "Close" to dismiss a layer; real actions like "Discard" in Modal or Panel footers. | "Dismiss" on a form; "Cancel" on a Close icon or inside a Modal or Panel footer. |
| "Clear" in a menu; "Reset filters" everywhere else. | "Reset" in a menu; "Clear all", "Clear filters", "Reset all". |
| "Delete" for something destroyed; "Remove" for something taken out of a group. | "Delete" for leaving a group; "Remove" for erasing a record. |
| Sentence case: "Mark attendance". | Title Case: "Mark Attendance". |

## Accessibility

- A button performs an action and a link navigates; the element gives the role. An icon-only button is an `IconButton` with a `label`: "Close", "Copy", "Edit", "More".
- A sending button sets `aria-busy` and keeps its label in the tree; only that button disables, and the secondary action stays live.
- The Danger button in a type-the-name confirm is disabled until the name matches; the field caption carries the reason, never a tooltip.
- The bulk bar's count is a polite live region; the select-all checkbox reports its mixed state. Focus stays on the checkbox that was ticked.
- The focus ring takes `--ds-border-focused` on every appearance.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Action | Button | The nine appearances, `link` and `danger-link` among them; `isLoading` swaps the label for a spinner and keeps the width. |
| Icon action | Icon button | Close, Copy, Edit and More; its `label` names it. |
| Modal, Panel and task footer | FooterActions | Four equal tracks; a leading action is a link or a danger link. |
| Bulk bar | Section table head | The Dynamic table's head row, through `TableBulkActions`. |

## Related

- Forms: use when the buttons submit fields.
- Filtering: use for Clear and Apply inside a filter menu.
- Modal: use for the confirm a destructive action raises.
- Disabled: use when an action cannot run yet.

contextPages.intro: When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person: actions stay enabled and explain, and what a role can never use is hidden.
contextPages.name: Disabled
contextPages.text:
# Disabled

When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person: actions stay enabled and explain, and what a role can never use is hidden.

## The four answers

Try these options in order; disable only when the earlier options do not fit.

- **Enabled, and it explains.** An action stays pressable and says what is missing when pressed. It disables only while sending.
- **Disabled with a visible reason.** A field or option that waits on a prerequisite the person can fix here. The reason is the caption or the option's description line.
- **Read-only.** Content people must read but cannot change. It has its own pattern.
- **Hidden.** What this role can never use is left out, not dimmed. The one exception is the Toolkit, locked during onboarding and never hidden.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Disabled when something on the page cannot be used right now. Reach for it last: an enabled action that explains is better than a dimmed one, read-only is better for content people must read, and hiding is right for what a role can never use.

| The situation | Answer | Where the reason goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A submit with fields missing | Enabled; pressing it marks the fields | Field errors |
| A button while its action sends | Disabled with a spinner in place | None; it is self-evident |
| A field that waits on another field on this screen | Disabled | The caption: "Choose a school first" |
| An option that cannot apply | Disabled | The option's description line |
| A prerequisite that blocks the main action or several items | Disabled, plus a warning `SectionMessage` above | The message says how to turn it on |
| Back on step one; Danger until the name matches | Disabled | None, or the field caption |
| Content this person must read but cannot change | Read-only | The caption |
| An action this role can never take | Hidden | None |
| The Toolkit during onboarding | Locked, visible | The Sidebar line that says what unlocks it |

## Alternatives

- For a value this person cannot change but must read, follow Read-only.
- For what a role can never use, leave the control, page or Sidebar item out.
- For a submit that is not ready, keep it enabled and let validation explain; see Forms.

## Best practices

### Keep actions enabled and explain what is missing when pressed.

A disabled button gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing an action that cannot run yet marks what is missing. A button disables only while sending. A form's submit follows Forms.

### Disable a field or option only for a prerequisite the person can fix on the same screen.

Group waits on School; a time slot waits on a date. Anything blocked by something off this screen is enabled and explains, read-only, or hidden.

### Put the reason in visible text where the cause is.

The field caption or the option's description line. When the prerequisite blocks the main action or several items, a warning `SectionMessage` above says how to turn it on. Self-evident cases need no reason: Back on the first step.

### Keep the reason in text on the page, never in a tooltip on a disabled control.

A disabled control gets no events and is absent on touch, so a tooltip would never open for the people who need it most. A disabled control keeps its default behavior and leaves the tab order.

Do: The reason as the caption: "Choose a school first".
Don't: The reason in a tooltip on a faded field: it never opens on touch.

### Hide what a role can never use.

An action a tutor can never take, such as deleting a school, is left out, not dimmed. A breadcrumb level the person cannot open is left out. Only a change of role brings it back.

Do: An action a tutor can never take is left out of the menu.
Don't: A faded "Delete school" that a tutor will never be able to press.

### Lock the Toolkit during onboarding and keep it visible.

Tutors see what training unlocks. The Sidebar item shows a lock and a line that says what unlocks it; the line is Planned .

### Make content people must read read-only, not disabled.

Disabled fades and leaves the tab order; read-only stays readable at full contrast. The two are never swapped.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Caption: "Choose a school first." | "Disabled", "Not available". |
| Option description: "Ms. Ortiz has a session then." | A faded option with no line. |
| Warning message: "Add a school to this group to schedule sessions." with "Add school". | "Some actions are unavailable." |
| Toolkit: "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit." | "Locked". |

## Accessibility

- A disabled control leaves the tab order and gets no events; the reason beside it is ordinary text a screen reader reads with the field, tied through the caption.
- The warning `SectionMessage` is announced when it appears.
- Disabled controls fade; the caption keeps full contrast, so the reason stays readable.

## Related

- Read-only: use when the value must be read.
- Forms: use for the enabled submit.
- Common actions: use for the sending button.
- Navigation: use for the Sidebar's locked Toolkit.
- `Button`, `IconButton`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `SectionMessage`: the components.

contextPages.intro: What a view shows when it has nothing to show. It says what belongs here, why it is empty, and what to do next; it never leaves a blank area and never apologizes.
contextPages.name: Empty
contextPages.text:
# Empty

What a view shows when it has nothing to show. It says what belongs here, why it is empty, and what to do next; it never leaves a blank area and never apologizes.

## The types

Choose among four situations to set the wording and available action. See Empty state for props.

- **First use.** Nothing has been added yet. Say what will appear and give the one action that adds it, if this person can.
- **No matches.** A search or filter matched nothing. Name what is active and offer "Reset filters".
- **All done.** The person finished everything. Say so, and when more arrives. No action.
- **Can't show.** The data could not load, or this person has no access. Say why and give a way forward: Try again, or who can help.

## Where it sits

The place sets the spacing and the alignment. The words stay the same.

- **A full page.** The block lines up with the page title, left-aligned with no wide margin, the picture above the text. The block is centered today.
- **In a table.** The empty state replaces the whole table: no column headers, no footer. The block is centered and its text stays left-aligned. `EmptyState` centers the text today.
- **In a card.** Compact: a smaller picture and heading, the block centered in the card, the text left-aligned. Several cards at once drop their pictures and use Subtle actions. The text is centered today.
- **In a Panel.** The Details Panel when its record was removed: the block at the top of the body, with a way back.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Empty when a list, table, card, Panel or page has no records to show, a search or filter returns nothing, a queue is finished, or the content exists but cannot be shown to this person. Show Loading instead while content is on its way, and leave one blank field blank.

| Type | The view is empty because | Say | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First use | Nothing has been added yet: a new group with no students | What will appear here and how it gets here | One Primary, if this person can add something; otherwise none |
| No matches | A search or filter matched nothing | Which search or filters are active | "Reset filters" as a Default button; it also clears the search |
| All done | The person finished everything: every reflection is reviewed | That they are done, and when more arrives | None |
| Can't show | No access, or the data could not load | Why, in plain words | Try again, or who can help; never an action they cannot take |

## Alternatives

- For content still on its way, follow Loading: a skeleton, not an empty state.
- For a save or request that failed while the view still has content, use `SectionMessage`; the Errors pattern says where each failure shows.
- For one blank value in a record, show a dash, not an empty state.

## Best practices

### Show an `EmptyState` in any view that has no records.

Never a blank area or a bare "No results": a blank reads as broken or still loading.

Do: Say what belongs here and give the one action that fills it.
Don't: A bare string in an empty box: broken, loading or empty, nobody can tell.

### Lay the text out as a left-aligned block.

The picture above, then the heading, one line and the action, all on one left edge. On a full page the block lines up with the page title; inside a table or a card the block is centered and its text stays left-aligned. The text column never runs wide.  `EmptyState` centers its text today.

### Replace the whole table with the empty state.

No column headers and no footer while the table is empty; the Section's header rows above stay, so the person can change the view, search or reset. A "No matches" state offers "Reset filters".

Do: The whole table replaced; the header rows stay.
Don't: Column headers and a footer over nothing, with a centered paragraph.

### Give at most one Primary action.

The second action is Default and never stands alone. When two or more empty states can show on one screen, none of them uses a Primary; their actions are Subtle.

### Offer only an action this person can take.

If they cannot add anything, show no button. A button that leads to "You don't have permission" is a dead end.

### Write the heading as what belongs here.

"No students in this group yet". The view is empty, not wrong, so the heading carries no "Sorry", no "Oops" and no code.

### Mark the picture as decorative.

Screen readers skip it and read the heading first; the words carry the meaning. The `EmptyState` hides its picture and icon from assistive technology, and its heading sits one level below the section that holds it.

### Name the active search or filters in a No matches state.

The person may not remember a filter set last week. "No students match these filters" with "Reset filters" is the way out.

### Use an illustration once and an icon where it repeats.

An illustration for a full view a person meets once, such as a new tutor's first day; an icon on anything that repeats, such as a card on a home page. Illustrations arrive with the character work .

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Heading: "No students in this group yet". | "No data", "Nothing here", "Oops!". |
| One line: "Add students to schedule sessions and track their progress." | A paragraph about the feature. |
| Action names the next step: "Add students". | "Get started", "Continue". |
| No matches: "No students match these filters." with "Reset filters". | "Clear filters", "Clear all". |
| All done: "Every reflection is reviewed. New ones arrive after Friday's sessions." | "All caught up! 🎉" |
| Warmer for students, plainer for admins: "Your tutor will add notes after your session." and "No notes for this group." | One voice for everyone. |

## Accessibility

- The heading is one level below the section that holds it, so it joins the page outline.
- The picture is decorative: an empty alt, or `aria-hidden` on an icon.
- When a filter or search empties a list, the result count is announced in a polite live region ("0 students").
- Focus stays where it was. Never move it to the empty state's button.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The block | Empty state | Picture or icon, header, one line and the action; `spacing` is `default` for a view and `compact` for a table body or card. |
| The action | Button | `primaryAction` takes one Button; a No matches action is Default. |
| Table slot | Table | `emptyState` (the Table template) and `emptyView` / `noResultsView` (`DynamicTable`) take the block and replace the whole table, header and footer included. |
| In a Panel | Panel | The record-gone state at the top of the body. |

## Related

- Loading: use before you know the view is empty.
- Errors: use for the words in a Can't show state.
- Filtering: use for where No matches comes from, and the "Reset filters" wording.
- Search: use for a search that matches nothing.
- Section: use for the header rows that stay above a replaced table.

contextPages.intro: Where a failure shows and what it says: the place follows what failed, and the message is words, never a code or color alone.
contextPages.name: Errors
contextPages.text:
# Errors

Where a failure shows and what it says: the place follows what failed, and the message is words, never a code or color alone.

## By what failed

Give each failure one home near its cause. Key cases shows the two submit failures: blocked and rejected.

- **A field.** The error on the field, after blur. It clears once the rule is met: Forms.
- **A view that could not load.** The error in the empty-state slot, with Try again. The header rows stay.
- **No access.** The same slot, saying who can help. No action the person cannot take.
- **A background job.** A danger Flag that stays, with Try again.
- **The whole page.** A danger Banner for a condition that applies to everything on the page, for as long as it holds.
- **A menu's options.** A "Couldn't load options" row with Retry, in the menu itself.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Errors whenever something failed and the person needs to know. Put the message where the cause is, say what happened and what to do, and leave the rest of the page working. Severity comes from the component that carries the message, not from louder words.

| What failed | Where it shows | Stays until | Offers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One field's value | On the field, after blur | The rule is met | What to fix |
| A submit with fields missing | On each field; focus moves to the first; a Modal stays open | The fields are fixed | What to fix |
| A submit the server rejected | Danger `SectionMessage` at the top of the form, plus field errors | Dismissed or fixed | What happened, what to do |
| A view's content could not load | The empty-state slot | It loads | Try again |
| This person has no access | The empty-state slot | Access changes | Who can help |
| A job in the background | Danger `Flag`, top right, no autohide | Try again resolves it | Try again |
| A condition on the whole page | Danger `Banner` at its tier | The condition ends | A link if there is one |
| A menu's options | A "Couldn't load options" row in the menu | Retry succeeds | Retry |

## Alternatives

- For a caution before something goes wrong, use a warning `SectionMessage`; see Disabled.
- For a view that is simply empty, follow the Empty pattern; it holds the slot a load failure takes.
- For a decision the person must make before going on, use Modal, not an error.

## Best practices

### Validate a field when it loses focus and clear the error once the rule is met.

The error sits on the field and says what to fix. Forms holds when a field is checked.

### Say what to fix on the field, in words.

The message sits right under the invalid field and names the fix. The red border supports the words and never replaces them.

Do: Say what to fix, on the field, in words.
Don't: A red border alone, with its words in a tooltip.

### Keep a blocked submit in the same Modal.

Mark the field and move focus to it; never a second dialog for the error. A single shake is Planned . Forms holds the whole rule.

### Show a rejected submit as a danger SectionMessage at the top of the form.

It says what happened and what to do, and the field errors it names sit on their fields. It is announced when it appears. Scrolling it into view is Planned .

### Put a load failure in the empty-state slot with Try again.

Content that fails to load takes the place an empty view would, in the Section's body, so the header rows and the rest of the page keep working. No access uses the same slot and names who can help.

Do: The failure in the Section's slot; the rest of the page works.
Don't: A Modal over the whole page to report one Section's failure.

### Make a failed background job a danger Flag that stays.

The person has moved on, so the Flag finds them at the top right. A danger Flag does not hide on its own; it offers Try again and stays until Try again resolves it. `Flag` names the appearance `error`.

### Use a Banner only for a condition on the whole page.

An outage, a lost connection, an account-wide block: one Banner at its tier, danger only when action is needed now, mounted only while the condition holds. A Banner has no dismiss.

### Say what happened and what to do, with no codes.

Own the problem: "Couldn't add the student. Check the fields below and try again." The words carry the severity, because the icon is hidden from screen readers and color never carries the meaning alone.

### Keep every error in visible text where the cause is.

A tooltip is absent on touch and gone on blur. An error is text on the page, next to what failed.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Field: "Enter a full email, like name@school.org". | "Invalid", "Required field", "Error 422". |
| Rejected: "Couldn't add the student. Check the fields below and try again." | "Something went wrong." |
| Load: "Couldn't load this week's sessions." with "Try again". | "Failed to fetch /sessions". |
| No access: "Only Lincoln's supervisor can open these notes." | "403 Forbidden", "You don't have permission". |
| Flag: "Couldn't save your session note." with "Try again". | "Save failed!" |
| Own it: "We lost the connection." | "The connection was lost by the user." |

## Accessibility

- A field error is announced and sets `aria-invalid`; a group's one error is announced once.
- A `SectionMessage` announces assertively when it appears; a danger `Flag` is announced as an urgent message. A `Banner` is a status.
- Move focus to the first field that needs fixing when a submit is blocked.
- The error icon is decorative; the words say "couldn't", "missing" or "failed".

## Related

- Forms: use for when a field is checked.
- Empty: use for the slot a load failure takes.
- Notifications: use for the Flag and Banner tiers.
- Loading: use for a menu's Loading row before it fails.
- Disabled: use for a caution before something goes wrong.
- `SectionMessage`, `Flag`, `Banner`, `EmptyState`, `TextField`: the components.

contextPages.intro: How a person narrows a collection, with filters in the Section's header in one of five tiers.
contextPages.name: Filtering
contextPages.text:
# Filtering

How a person narrows a collection, with filters in the Section's header in one of five tiers.

## Tiers

Choose a tier by the number of categories and the length of their lists. See Best practices for when to move filters into a menu.

- **1 · Quick filters.** One to three categories, each a short list: a "Field: value" trigger per category opening its own list, applied as you pick.
- **2a · Menu, one category.** The Filter button opens one list, applied as you pick. No footer.
- **2b · Menu, side by side.** Two or three categories with short lists in columns, with Clear and Apply at the end.
- **2c · Menu, stacked.** Four or more categories, or long lists, stacked, with Clear and Apply at the end.
- **3 · Filter side.** Filtering is the main job: a side at the Section's start, "Reset filters" at its top and a count beside each category.

## What is on

The control that holds a filter shows it: the FilterButton's count, or the Filter button's own count on the selected fill. No row of tags under the header.

## Key cases

### Below 960, the filter side

The side hides and the Filter button returns with its count. Pressing it gives the filters the Section's whole width, and "Show results" goes back. The Section owns this behavior: Section › Width behavior.

### Widths

A one-list menu is auto: at least the trigger, 160 to 320, truncating with a tooltip. Side by side takes 3-col; stacked takes 3-col and never goes past 4-col. The widths are the Popup template's.

## Motion

## Usage

Use Filtering when a person narrows a collection by its attributes. Filters live in the Section header's third row, after Search: "Field: value" triggers, then More filters. Views in the second row are not filters: a view is one of a fixed set, and filters combine.

| Tier | Use when | Controls | Applies | Shows it is on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Quick filters | One to three categories, each a short list | A FilterButton per category | As you pick | The button's selected fill and count |
| 2a · Menu, one category | One category, and the bar has no room for a button | The Filter button, one list | As you pick | The Filter button's count |
| 2b · Menu, side by side | Two or three categories with short lists, applied together | The Filter button, columns, Clear and Apply | On Apply | The Filter button's count |
| 2c · Menu, stacked | Four or more categories, or long lists | The Filter button, stacked categories, Clear and Apply | On Apply | The Filter button's count |
| 3 · Filter side | Filtering is the main job, such as browsing a long catalog | A side at the Section's start | As you pick, or on "Apply filters" for a batch | A count beside each category |

## Alternatives

- For finding rows by name, use the Search pattern: its icon sits before the filters.
- For switching between fixed views of the rows, use `Tabs` as pill views.
- For sorting, use the `Table` column header: sorting is not a filter.

## Best practices

### Use one tier per bar.

Quick filters and a filter menu never share a bar: some filters outside and some inside read as two systems. When a Section outgrows tier 1, all of its filters move into the menu. Where the filters sit in the header, and the header's order: Section › Order the header.

Do: One tier: three quick filters, all in the bar.
Don't: Two quick filters plus a Filter button: two systems in one bar.

### Keep the filters in the third row.

The first two rows are for the title with its actions and for the views. The filters come after Search in the third row, so a person finds them in one place on every Section.

Do: Views in the second row; Search, then the filters, in the third.
Don't: The filters squeezed in beside the views.

### Show what is on through the control that holds it.

A FilterButton's count, the Filter button's count on the selected fill, or a count beside each category in a side. No separate count tag, and no row of tags under the bar.

Do: The count on the Filter button, on the selected fill.
Don't: A row of tags under the bar, repeating what is on.

### Apply one list as you pick and several categories on Apply.

A one-list menu is a Popup select: radios for one choice, not searchable for a short list. Checkboxes for several choices in one list are Planned on it . A multi-category menu is a Filter menu that holds values until Apply; Apply closes it and updates the content once, and Clear clears the choices without applying. Where a menu opens and how wide it is: Popup.

### Say Clear in a menu and Reset filters everywhere else.

A menu's footer says "Clear" and "Apply", compact at the end. "Reset filters" at the top of a side clears them all, and the "No matches" state offers it too; both clear the search. "Apply filters" appears only for batch filtering in a side.

### Hide the filter side below 960 and fold quick filters below 768.

Below 960 the side hides and the Filter button returns with its count; pressing it gives the filters the Section's whole width, with "Show results" to go back: Section › Drop the Filter button while a filter side shows. Below 768 quick filters become a stacked menu.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name categories as nouns: "Grade", "School", "Subject". | "Filter by grade", "Choose a school". |
| Label the menu footer "Clear" and "Apply". | "Reset", "OK", "Done". |
| Put "Reset filters" at the top of a side; "Apply filters" only for a batch. | "Clear all", "Submit". |
| Name the Filter button with filters on: "Filters 2". | "Filters (2)". |
| Count the results in words: "1 of 8 students". | "1 result". |
| Go back from the filters on a narrow Section with "Show results". | "Done", "Close". |

## Accessibility

- The Filter button's name is "Filters"; with a count it reads "Filters 2". Apply returns focus to it, so its new name is read.
- A FilterButton's name is its text plus its count. Its list is a listbox the arrow keys move through; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.
- The result count is a polite live region: it is read as the rows narrow.
- Clear and Apply are the last tab stops in a menu.
- A filter side is a region named "Filters", and each category is a group named by its legend.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quick filter | Filter button | A count only when a value is on; it hugs its label and opens its list at bottom-end. |
| Filter button | Filter button | Text "Filters" with the `filter` icon; its `trailingMetric` draws the count on the selected fill. The Section's `filters` entry hands it to the menu. |
| One list (tier 1 lists, 2a) | Popup select | Applies as you pick, radios for one. Checkboxes for several are Planned. |
| Filter menu (2b, 2c) | Filter menu | Holds values until Apply; columns side by side or stacked; Clear and Apply at the end. |
| Placement and width | Popup | bottom-end at the end of a bar, bottom-start at its start; 4 from the trigger. |
| Filter side | Section side | Composed at the start today. A start placement prop is Planned. |
| No matches | Empty state | Replaces the table and offers "Reset filters". |

## Related

- Section: use when the question is the header the filters sit in.
- Popup: use when the question is where a menu opens or how wide it is.
- Filter menu: use when building a tier 2b or 2c menu.
- Search: use for finding by name.
- Empty: use for No matches.
- Navigation: use for views.

contextPages.intro: The kinds of form and how a form takes and checks what someone types: when it validates, what a blocked submit does.
contextPages.name: Forms
contextPages.text:
# Forms

The kinds of form and how a form takes and checks what someone types: when it validates, what a blocked submit does.

## The kinds of form

There is no Form component or template. A form is a `Fieldset` of fields inside a host, and the host owns the title and the footer. Pick the kind by the task; its host page has the layout, the footer and the sizes.

- **Settings.** Values saved as a group, on their own page.
- **Create.** A rare, critical task with fewer than five fields.
- **Quick edit.** A short edit of a row, with the page still in view.
- **In steps.** A long form someone works through.

## Marks and help

## Validation

## Leaving with edits

## Bound inputs

## Motion

## Usage

Use Forms when a page asks for input that is saved together: adding a student, logging a session, a reflection, profile settings. Ask only what is needed, group fields under a `Fieldset` legend of two or three words, keep one column except for pairs that belong together (first and last name, date and time), and reveal a conditional field under the answer that needs it rather than adding a separate one.

| The form… | Kind | Host |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is saved as a group on its own page: settings, a profile | Settings | Section page header on the Page |
| is rare and critical, with fewer than five fields | Create | Modal, 8-col |
| is a short edit of a row, with the page still in view | Quick edit | Panel, Details |
| is long, or has sections someone works through | In steps | Multi-step task on Frame |
| asks for one value read far more than changed | None: inline edit | The record, which saves on its own |

Where the buttons sit and in which look is each host's footer, and Common actions for the rules across them. A Popup never holds a form.

## Alternatives

- For one value on a record page, use `InlineEdit`; it saves on its own.
- For settings that apply at once, group `SettingRow` items under section headings on the page; a `Toggle` never waits for Save.
- For a filter, follow Filtering: filters are not a form.
- For a decision with no fields, use Modal · Active.

## Best practices

### Validate a field when it loses focus and clear the error once the rule is met.

The error shows on the field, says what to fix, and goes away as soon as the value passes. Nothing is checked while typing. A warning accepts the value; a field is invalid only when the form cannot go on.

### Keep the submit button enabled and let it show what is missing.

A disabled submit gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing it marks every missing field and moves focus to the first; the body scrolls to it. The button disables only while sending, when it swaps its label for a spinner in place and keeps its width.

### Keep a blocked submit in the same Modal.

Mark the field, say what to fix inline, scroll the body to it, and shake once . Never a second dialog for the error. Reduced motion drops the shake; the color, icon, message and focus move carry it. A server failure: Errors.

Do: The message under the field, in the same Modal.
Don't: A second dialog over the first, with the field left unexplained.

### Mark only the minority case in the label, in plain text.

When most fields are required, mark the optional ones `"(optional)"` (`labelMarker="optional"`). When most fields are optional, mark the required ones `"(required)"` (`labelMarker="required"`). The marker is plain text in the label's type style, in `--ds-text-subtle`, never a symbol or legend. Required controls still set `isRequired`, so screen readers get `aria-required` and the visible `"(required)"` is hidden from them to avoid saying it twice. Choice flows (`RadioGroup` and `CheckboxGroup` across onboarding, quizzes, check-ins, and surveys) apply the same minority rule to selection controls: the majority selection type uses `appearance="soft"` (selected fill, border, and trailing check with no radio dot or checkbox box), while the minority selection type keeps its visible control (`card` or `plain`) so people notice when a question switches between single-select and multi-select.

Do: Two required fields stay unmarked; only the optional field says so.
Don't: Every field carries a marker, so none stands out.

### Put help in the caption, never in a tooltip.

A caption stays after the person types and is read by a screen reader with the field. A tooltip never carries the only copy of anything. An explanation most people will never need opens from an `InlineMessage` beside the field.

Do: Help in the caption, where it stays after typing.
Don't: Help only in a tooltip: gone on touch, gone after typing.

### Ask before leaving with unsaved edits.

Close, Discard, Cancel (on a page form) and navigating away raise a 4-col Modal: Back returns without losing anything typed; Discard is Danger. A form already in a Modal asks in that Modal's confirm view, so two layers never become three. A form with no edits leaves at once. In a multi-step task, Back in the inner sidebar asks first if anything is unsaved.

### Prefer a bound input to a free one.

Up to five choices: `RadioGroup` or checkboxes, visible at once. Six or more: `Select`. A date: `DatePicker`. A number: min and max. A radio group starts unanswered and never falls back to its first option. A `Toggle` applies at once, so anything that waits for Save is a `Checkbox`.

### Give the form a title from its host and a legend for each group.

The form's title is the page, Panel or Modal heading, never a generic "Form". Groups take a `Fieldset` legend, two or three words, a noun phrase. Labels are sentence case, one to three words, naming the field rather than what to do.

### Keep a form to one column.

Pair two fields side by side only when they belong together, such as first and last name, or date and time. Anything else reads down one column.

Do: One column, so the eye moves straight down.
Don't: Unrelated fields scattered across two columns.

### Keep a short edit beside the page.

Editing a row opens a Panel so the person keeps the page in view. A Modal is for a rare, critical task with fewer than five fields.

Do: A short edit in a Panel, the rows still in view.
Don't: The same short edit in a Modal that covers the rows.

### Set autofill on every field the browser can fill.

`autoComplete` on name, email, phone and address fields. Prefill what is already known, such as the student picked from a row.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label names the field: "School email". | Label gives an instruction: "Enter your school email:". |
| Error says what to fix: "Enter a full email, like name@school.org". | "Invalid input", "Error 422". |
| Caption says what the field is for: "Shared with the supervisor". | Caption repeats the label. |
| Placeholder shows a good answer: "name@school.org". | Placeholder names the control: "Text field". |
| Submit names the outcome: "Log session", "Add student". | "Submit", "Save" when the outcome has a name. |
| Dates and times as the person reads them: "Mar 4, 2026 · 4:00 PM". | "2026-03-04T16:00". |

## Accessibility

- Every input has a visible label. A group is a `fieldset` with a `legend`; its one error is announced once.
- A field error is announced and sets `aria-invalid`; the submit moves focus to the first invalid field. A server message is announced when it appears.
- A required field sets `aria-required` whether or not it carries a visible `"(required)"` marker; only the form's minority case is marked in the label text.
- A sending button keeps its name and sets `aria-busy`; the secondary action stays reachable.
- A dialog opens only from a person's action. Focus goes to the first input and stays trapped until it closes.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fields | `Fieldset` | There is no Form component: a Fieldset groups the fields inside a host. |
| Rejection at the top | `SectionMessage` | A danger message, scrolled into view. |
| Choices | `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Select`, `DatePicker` | A control that cannot be wrong; pictured tiles for one big question per step. |
| Settings rows | `SettingRow`, `Toggle`, `Select`, `StatusTag`, `Flag` | Divided rows under section headings with no card per row; flipping a toggle confirms via Flag. |
| Hosts | Section, Panel, Modal, Frame | A page (under its Section header, no Section around the fields), a Panel, a Modal, or the multi-step task on Frame. Each owns its footer. |
| Confirm view | Modal | Swapped in place today. A confirm view prop is Planned. |

## Related

- Common actions: use for where the buttons sit and which look they take.
- Modal, Panel, Frame: use for each host's layout and footer.
- Loading: use for a form that is sending.
- Disabled: use for a submit that cannot run yet.
- Errors: use for where a failed save shows.

contextPages.intro: The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved; the words carry the meaning.
contextPages.name: Indicators
contextPages.text:
# Indicators

The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved; the words carry the meaning.

## The three tags

Three jobs, three components. A category with a color is a Tag, not an indicator.

## Key cases

- **Status in a row.** Default spacing in a table cell. One status per object; the label is one or two words.
- **Status beside a heading.** Spacious beside the page title, after the text.
- **Counts on navigation.** A count beside an item's name. At zero the component renders nothing; bold asks for action now, at most one per area.
- **Where color is not enough.** A leading icon joins the color on a status that must be told apart at a glance, such as Missed.
- **Change where up is bad.** Absences rose by 3: the value is up and the tone is danger, because the good direction is down.
- **A roll-up.** A group's status shows the worst state among its children: danger over warning over information.

A checklist tracks setup or compliance steps in three layouts: a dismissible card on Home, a persistent card in a page, and a compact summary at the foot of the Sidebar.

## Motion

## Usage

Use Indicators when something needs a small label that says how it is. Ask what the label says: a number is a Count tag; a condition that can change is a Status tag; how much a number moved is a Change tag; a subject, a person or a category is a Tag. Skip an indicator when no action follows from it; past five or six states, use text.

| The label says | Component | Looks | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The condition something is in, and it can change | Status tag | Fill by meaning: neutral not started, information in progress, success done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery new | "Needs review" |
| How many | Count tag | Subtle neutral; bold for action now; nothing at 0; a cap past `max` with "+" | "12", "99+" |
| How much it moved | Change tag | Signed value, arrow, tone from the good direction; neutral when there is no judgment | "+3 vs last week" |
| A category, a subject, a person | Tag | Outline and text; a leading visual is optional | "Lincoln Middle" |
| Setup or compliance steps left to finish | Checklist (`Card` + `Section` + `Progress bar`) | Header count and bar aligned to one 128 action column; open steps above done steps | "2 of 5 done" |
| The shape of a trend | Sparkline | A word-sized line beside the number | Attendance over eight weeks |

## Alternatives

- For a message about the thing, use a Section message or a Flag; the Notifications pattern picks between them.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a competency area, use `CompetencyTag`.
- For something the AI proposes, use `Suggestion`.

## Best practices

### Never let color carry the meaning alone.

The words say the state; the fill repeats it. A state that must be told apart at a glance adds a leading icon. A Change tag's arrow is decorative and its hidden text reads "Up 3 vs last week". A dot with no label is announced as nothing.

### Give each appearance one meaning.

Neutral is not started, info is in progress, success is done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery is new. Success never labels a problem. There is no color prop; a category with a color is a Tag.

Do: Danger on a missed session: the word and the fill agree.
Don't: Success on a missed session: the fill says good about bad news.

### Show one status per object.

Two statuses force people to decide which is true. A roll-up shows the worst child state.

### Keep a status to one or two words.

A status is read at a glance; a sentence belongs in the row text. A Status tag truncates at 200 with its full text in a Tooltip.

### Keep most counts quiet and show nothing at zero.

Subtle neutral is the default. Bold asks for action now, so at most one bold count per area. Pass the raw number: the component renders nothing at 0 and caps past `max` with a "+". No skeleton on a count; it appears when the number arrives.

### Set the Change tag's good direction so up can be bad.

The sign gives the direction; the good direction gives the tone: up, down or none. Absences rising is danger; sessions held rising is success; a change with no judgment stays neutral. The value is always signed.

Do: A rise in absences in danger: the good direction is down.
Don't: A rise in absences in success: the color says good about bad news.

### Edit a status in the field, not on the label.

A Status tag never opens a menu. Where a status can be changed, the field around it becomes an inline Select.

### Nest a count in a status instead of placing one beside it.

"Needs review 3" reads as one label; two labels side by side read as unrelated.

### Line up checklist actions in one column and mark done steps with text.

Build the checklist from `Card` and `Section`:

1. Compose each row from an `Icon`, step text with one fact, and an action column. Use `--checklist-action-width` (128), with `--checklist-action-min-width` (120) as its floor. Buttons fill the column and align down the list.
2. Put the title at the header's start and the count ("2 of 5 done") with a `ProgressBar` at the end. Align the bar's start edge with the action column: 128 wide on a persistent card, or 96 when a 32 dismiss `IconButton` occupies the end.
3. Keep open steps in order above completed steps. Center a check icon and plain "Completed" text (Body small, subtle) in each completed row's action column.

Choose the layout by where the checklist appears:

| Layout | Use | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismissible card | Home | When complete, shrinks to one line for a day, then disappears. |
| Persistent card | Required work on a page | Keeps every completed row visible. |
| Compact card | Foot of the Sidebar | Shows the count, progress bar and next step, which opens the full list. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Status in one or two words: "Scheduled", "Needs review", "Missed". | "This session has been missed". |
| Count as the bare number: "4", "12", "99+". | "4 items", "Count: 4". |
| Change signed, with the comparison: "+3 vs last week", "−12%". | "3 more", "went up". |
| Hidden text reads the whole thing: "Up 3 vs last week". | Nothing for the screen reader. |

## Accessibility

- A tag is read as its text; nothing suggests it can be pressed. A clipped tag becomes a tab stop so the Tooltip opens on focus.
- A count's meaning is in the label it sits on: "Inbox, 3 unread". A bare number announces nothing useful.
- A Change tag's arrow and value are hidden from assistive technology and its words read the direction and the comparison.
- A Status tag, Tag and Change tag keep an inside border, so a pale fill stays visible on any background and in forced colors.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State | Status tag | Six appearances; `trailingMetric` nests a count inside it. |
| How many | Count tag | `max` caps it, `isBold` asks for action, `label` names it for a screen reader. |
| How much it moved | Change tag | `goodDirection` sets the tone; `comparison` names what it is measured against. |
| Checklist | Card, Section, Progress bar | Composed step rows (`Icon`, text, `Button` or "Completed" text) on `--checklist-action-width`; `Icon button` dismisses an optional card. |
| Category | Tag | Not an indicator: a subject, a person or a category. |

## Related

- Notifications: use for the count on the bell and the Inbox.
- Overflow: use for a tag that clips.
- Navigation: use for counts on Sidebar items and tabs.

contextPages.intro: What to show while PLUS fetches or saves something. Two inputs decide it: what is loading, and how long it has taken. The bands are 1 s and 10 s.
contextPages.name: Loading
contextPages.text:
# Loading

What to show while PLUS fetches or saves something. Two inputs decide it: what is loading, and how long it has taken. The bands are 1 s and 10 s.

## By what is loading

Four kinds of wait. Each has its own shape in the 1 to 10 s band; the time bands are the same for all.

- **A list or cards.** A skeleton in the real shape, so the layout stays still.
- **A button action.** A spinner inside the button that started it. The fields stay as they are.
- **A whole page.** The Frame and page header draw first; each Section fills as its data arrives.
- **A menu.** One "Loading options" row, never a skeleton. Fetch items before the click where you can.

## Across time

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Loading while someone waits for a fetch or save. Choose the indicator by what is loading and how long it has taken.

| What is loading | Under 1 s | 1 to 10 s | Over 10 s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A list or cards | Keep what was there; blank on first load | A skeleton in the real shape, `aria-busy`, "Loading students…" announced | The skeleton stays; a Flag explains the wait |
| A button action | Nothing yet; the button blocks a second press | A spinner inside the button; fields stay as they are | A Flag says it is still working and the person can leave; a Flag confirms when done |
| A whole page | Keep the previous page; blank screens wait | Frame and page header now, a skeleton in each Section | A labeled progress bar for a long job |
| A menu, Popup, Flag or Modal | Open complete; fetch before the click | One "Loading options" row; no skeleton | "Couldn't load options" with Retry, still one row |

## Alternatives

- For a wait whose length is known, use `ProgressBar`; it answers "how much longer".
- For a view that turns out to have nothing, follow Empty.
- For a load that failed, follow the Errors pattern: the error goes in the empty-state slot with Try again.

## Best practices

### Show nothing new under 1 s.

Keep the old content, or leave the area blank on a first load. A skeleton or spinner that appears and vanishes reads as a glitch rather than work. A button blocks a second press at once.

### Draw a skeleton in the real shape from 1 s.

The same rows, columns and cards the content will have, as plain text bars, so nothing jumps when it arrives. The container owns the skeleton; labels become text bars rather than label shapes. The shimmer stays on while loading.

Do: A skeleton in the table's own shape, text bars throughout.
Don't: One spinner in a blank area: the layout jumps when the rows arrive.

### Put the spinner inside the button that started the action.

The label swaps for a spinner in place and the button keeps its width. Only that button disables; the fields and Cancel stay live. One spinner per wait.

### Draw the Frame and page header first.

On a quick move keep the previous page until the next is ready. Past 1 s the Frame, Sidebar and page header draw at once and each Section fills as its data arrives. A full-screen blocking overlay has no place in a wait.

### Say so after 10 s.

A Flag, kept up with `autohide={false}` until the work ends, explains the wait and that the person can keep working or leave; a Flag confirms when the work finishes. A long job with a known length, such as importing a roster, gets a labeled progress bar instead.

### Keep a menu, Popup, Flag or Modal free of skeletons.

They open in answer to a click and open complete. A menu whose items must load shows one "Loading options" row, then "Couldn't load options" with Retry. A Modal's body may hold its content's own loading state.

Do: A menu shows one "Loading options" row.
Don't: A menu full of skeleton rows, promising items it may not have.

### Mark the loading region busy and announce it.

`aria-busy` on the container that is loading, and a visually hidden status beside it whose text is set after mount: "Loading students…", then "Students loaded". Skeletons themselves are hidden from assistive technology.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Announce what is loading: "Loading students…", then "Students loaded". | "Loading…" as the only text on a page. |
| Flag past 10 s: "Still loading students. This group is large; you can keep working." | "Please wait", "Hang tight!". |
| Progress bar label: "Importing roster · 40 of 120 students". | A bar with no words. |
| Menu rows: "Loading options" · "Couldn't load options" with "Retry". | "Error", "Failed to fetch". |

## Accessibility

- Every skeleton is `aria-hidden`, never takes focus and ignores the pointer.
- The busy region's live label sits beside the region, not inside it, because content inside a busy region may be held back.
- A spinner announces as a status with a label that says what is loading when it is not obvious.
- Reduced motion: the shimmer stops and the spinner becomes a static ring; the shape still reads as working.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Placeholder | Skeleton | Text bars in the content's own shape; `isShimmering` holds still under reduced motion. |
| Spinner | Spinner | Inside a Button through `isLoading`; the button keeps its width. |
| Long job | Progress bar | A value and a label that says what is happening. |
| Wait explained | Flag | Information appearance, held until the work finishes. |
| Menu rows | Dropdown menu | `loading` shows "Loading options"; `hasError` with `onRetry` shows "Couldn't load options". |

## Related

- Empty: use once the load finishes with nothing.
- Errors: use when the load fails.
- Notifications: use for the Flag past 10 s.

contextPages.intro: How a person moves: between areas, between views, and down into a record and back out, one control and one motion each.
contextPages.name: Navigation
contextPages.text:
# Navigation

How a person moves: between areas, between views, and down into a record and back out, one control and one motion each.

## The tiers

Four tiers, from the whole app down to one record. A quick look is a layer, not a tier; steps move within a level.

- **1 · Areas.** Go to: the Sidebar's fixed items. The selected row takes the selected fill.
- **1b · Open items.** Records the person opened, a session or a student, as temporary items in the Sidebar: add and remove, then go to.
- **2 · Views.** Pill views in a Section's header, or page tabs under the page title. Content swaps in place.
- **3 · Drill in and climb out.** A record page with a breadcrumb: the record's place, parents only. Climb out through the breadcrumb.

## Key cases

## Motion

## Usage

Choose the navigation tier first; it sets the control, placement and motion. Navigation belongs in the Sidebar and page. There is no global search.

| Tier | The move | Control | Motion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Areas | To another part of the app | A Sidebar item | Go to |
| 1b · Open items | To a session or student opened earlier | A temporary item in the Sidebar, named by when and who | Add and remove, then Go to |
| 2 · Views | Between views of one collection or record | Pill views in the Section header; page tabs under the title | Switch views: content in place, the indicator glides |
| 3 · Drill in and climb out | Into one record and back | A row, then the breadcrumb | Drill in, Climb out |
| Within a level | Through a task's steps | Back and Next in the bottom bar; the step rail | Step |
| A layer | A quick look without leaving | A Details Panel or a Modal | Open and Close |

### Opening a record

Least room to most. Pick the lowest step that fits. The picture is on Templates.

| Step | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| 1 · Expand the row | A few more lines, links at most. |
| 2 · Section detail | An inline expand inside a Section. |
| 3 · Details Panel | On a queue page (docked beside the list), or a quick look or short edit from a table. |
| 4 · Modal | A rare, critical task with fewer than five fields. |
| 5 · Its own page | Complex or stepped work, or anything worth a URL. The breadcrumb appears. |

## Alternatives

- For narrowing a collection rather than switching views, follow Filtering; filters combine, views do not.
- For more pills than fit, fold the extras into "More" ; keep page tabs to five.
- For a decision that blocks the page, use a Modal, not a page.

## Best practices

### Show the breadcrumb only after drilling into a record.

Never on an area page or a multi-step task. It sits above the title in the page header and shows the record's place: parents only, never history. It never wraps. Folding five or more items into "…" is Planned .

Do: A breadcrumb on the record page, parents only.
Don't: A breadcrumb on an area page: there is nothing to climb out of.

### Keep one tab system per page.

Either page tabs under the title, or pill views in a Section's bar, never both. Under page tabs a Section's views become one labeled PopupSelect at the start of its bar. It picks a view, not a filter.

Do: Under page tabs the Section's views are one labeled PopupSelect at the start of its bar.
Don't: Page tabs and pill views on the same page: two tab systems.

### Make views a fixed set the product defines.

Two to five views of the same rows, named by short parallel nouns. Nobody adds or edits views. One pill stays even with one view, so nothing moves when a second arrives.

### Swap content in place between views and tabs.

Only the selected indicator glides. Nothing slides between views.

### Open a record at the lowest step that fits.

Expand the row, then Section detail, then the Details Panel, then a Modal, then its own page. Section detail and the Details Panel both stay: Section detail expands in place (see Section), and the Details Panel docks beside the list on a queue page or opens from a table.

### Give a long task its steps in the inner sidebar.

The steps replace the Sidebar's rows and Back returns to them; no breadcrumb. How the steps, the page and the footer sit is on Frame.

### Name an open item by when and who.

"4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz", with the school in the Tooltip. Three show, then "Show n more". Removing one is Add and remove; opening one is Go to.

Do: Each item names the session by its time and the teacher.
Don't: Each item carries everything, and the time it is found by is cut off.

### Put the collection's add action in its Section's title row, not the page header.

"Add student" is the Primary at the end of the Students Section's title row. Page actions sit at the end of the page header and are only about the page.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Views as short parallel nouns: "Upcoming", "Past". | "Show upcoming sessions", "History". |
| Page tabs name views of one subject: "Overview", "Sessions", "Notes". | Counts or status in the tab label. |
| The labeled filter trigger names the view: "Status: Upcoming". | A bare "Upcoming". |
| Breadcrumb levels by the page's own title. | "Back", "Home" as a level. |
| Open item: "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz". | "Session #1028". |

## Accessibility

- The Sidebar is a navigation landmark; the selected item carries `aria-current="page"`. The selected row is a fill, not color on the icon alone.
- Views and page tabs are a real tab widget: one tab stop, Left and Right move selection, the panel is named by its tab.
- The breadcrumb is a `nav` around an `ol`; the last item is plain text with `aria-current="page"`.
- Leaving a multi-step task returns focus to the control that opened it .

## Related

- Overflow: use for the breadcrumb middle and open-item names.
- Search: use for narrowing as you type inside a view.
- Filtering: use for narrowing a view by attributes.
- Indicators: use for counts on Sidebar items.
- Frame, Page, Section: use for the drawn shells.
- `Sidebar`, `Breadcrumb`, `Tabs`, `PageHeader`, `PopupSelect`: the components.

contextPages.intro: What the product says back, and where: a Flag for what happened, a Banner for a condition, a SectionMessage for something to act on, and the Inbox for what arrived over time.
contextPages.name: Notifications
contextPages.text:
# Notifications
