What the product says back, and where: a Flag for what happened, a Banner for a condition, a SectionMessage for something to act on, and the Inbox for what arrived over time.

## The carriers

Four components carry every message. Each component page holds its appearances; this pattern picks the carrier and the place. A Modal is the fifth, for the one message that must be answered first.

- **Flag.** A passing notice at the top right, two lines at most. Routine ones leave on their own; warning and error stay until acted on.
- **Banner.** A condition that holds for the whole Frame, page or Section: one line, no dismiss, one at a time.
- **SectionMessage.** Something to read or act on that belongs to this part of the page and stays until resolved or dismissed.
- **The Inbox.** Updates that arrived over time, in a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel beside the Sidebar, opened from the bell beside your name, with `Unread` and `All` tabs and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day.

## Banner tiers

One banner at a time, scrolling with its content. The Frame tier is system news and pins only during an active outage. The Page tier is about this page. The Section tier is about this collection. The Frame and Page `banner` slots are Planned : today a Banner goes in the content, set where its tier says.

- **Frame.** System news across the whole width, above the Sidebar and the page.
- **Page.** Under the page header, about this page.
- **Section.** At the top of one collection, about that collection.

## Severity

## Key cases

## Motion

## Usage

Notify someone when an action finishes, a condition applies or a decision is needed. Match disruption to urgency using the carrier table below. Show only necessary notifications.

| The message is about… | Carrier | Where | Leaves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Something that already happened and needs no reply: saved, sent, copied | `Flag` | Top right | On its own after 8 s, or Dismiss on a default flag; a bold warning or error when its action resolves it |
| A job that finished after the person moved on | Default `Flag` with an action, `autohide={false}` | Top right | Dismiss, or the action |
| A job that failed after the person moved on | Bold error `Flag` with Try again | Top right | When Try again resolves it; no Dismiss |
| Something to read or act on in this part of the page | `SectionMessage` | Top of the Section or form | Resolved or dismissed |
| Guidance before a task that must not be missed | `SectionMessage`, dismiss off | By the action it informs | When it stops applying |
| A condition that holds for everything in a Frame, page or Section | `Banner` at that tier | Top of the tier | When the condition ends |
| A note beside one thing that most people never need | `InlineMessage` | Beside the field or value | On close |
| Something that must be answered before going on | `Modal`, Acknowledge or Active | Centered over a Blanket | On the button |
| What arrived over time | The Inbox, a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel, opened from the bell beside your name | Beside the Sidebar, over the page, no Blanket | Escape, outside click, or Close |

## Alternatives

- For an error about one field, put it on the field; see Errors.
- For a state on one object, use a `StatusTag`; see Indicators.
- For a copy confirmation, use the "Copied" tooltip; see Common actions.

## Best practices

### Place Flags at the top right, two lines at most.

A title that names the event and one line for the next step. A `FlagGroup` stacks them in the order you pass them, so pass the newest first, and renders with the page so each one is announced. `FlagGroup` sits at the top right (`top-end`) by default.

### Offer Undo on a Flag with a timer, and commit when it ends.

An archive or a delete confirms with a Flag that has `timer` and Undo as its first action, instead of a confirmation dialog first. The change commits in `onDismiss`, once. Pressing Undo replaces the Flag with a plain "restored" Flag. Hovering or focusing the Flag pauses the countdown, so reading it never costs the chance to undo.

### Put nothing important only in a Flag.

A Flag can be dismissed before it is read. A failure that needs a decision stays on the page in a SectionMessage; a decision that blocks the task is a Modal.

Do: A finished action on the default Flag: the event in the title, the next step below.
Don't: A decision in a Flag, which is gone before it is answered.

### Let routine Flags leave and keep warning and error until acted on.

Normal, information and success close after 8 s. Warning and error never close themselves and offer a next action. On a default, information or success Flag with an action, set `autohide={false}` when the person must act; warning and error ignore it. The × and the rest of the dismiss rule are on the Flag page.

### Show one Banner at a time, one line, at the tier it concerns, for as long as the condition holds.

Frame for system news, pinned only during an active outage ; Page for this page; Section for this collection. A Banner has no dismiss and no timeout, so it is mounted only while the condition is true, and it scrolls with the content.

Do: One Banner, one line, at the tier it concerns.
Don't: Two Banners stacked, pushing the page down.

### Keep a SectionMessage in the page until it is resolved or dismissed.

The fill and icon carry the appearance, with no border and no side stripe. A blocking message turns dismiss off. Put up to two actions after the body. Field errors stay on the field.

### Match the appearance to the meaning and say it in the words.

Success for a finished action, warning for a caution, danger only when something failed. The icon is hidden from screen readers, so the title says "saved", "couldn't", "due".

### Keep routine news on the default Flag.

A bold fill competes with the page; it is for what must be seen. Routine news stays on the default Flag, which the person can clear.

### Send what arrived over time to the Inbox.

A Flag is for now; the Inbox is for later. The Inbox opens from the bell beside the account name, docked beside the Sidebar at `--inbox-width` over the page with no Blanket, carrying `Mark all as read` and close in the header, `Unread` (with count) and `All` tabs, and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day. Clearing every unread item shows `"You are all caught up."` in `EmptyState`; pressing `Escape` or clicking outside closes the panel.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Flag title names the event: "Session logged." | "Success!" |
| Flag line gives the next step: "Maya's supervisor will see it Friday." | A bare title with no next step. |
| Banner is one sentence: "Scheduled maintenance Saturday 2–4 AM ET." | A paragraph in the Banner. |
| Own the problem: "We lost the connection. Your work is kept on this device." | "Connection lost by client." |
| Actions are verbs: "Undo", "View sessions". | "Click here", "OK". |

## Accessibility

- Warning and error Flags are alerts and interrupt; every other Flag is a polite status. Each is read as one message.
- A `SectionMessage` announces assertively when it appears; one present at first paint is ordinary content.
- A `Banner` is a status that never traps focus and sits in the reading order.
- The timeout on a Flag is a timing limit; the dismiss × on a default Flag satisfies it (see the Flag page).
- The appearance icon is decorative; the words carry the severity.
- Each `NotificationItem` in the Inbox is one link whose accessible name announces `"Unread"` while unread, with `"Mark as read"` as a sibling button outside the link.

## Related

- Errors: use for where a failure shows.
- Loading: use for the Flag past 10 s.
- Indicators: use for the count on the Bell.
- Panel: use for the Inbox.
- Modal: use for what must be answered first.
- Page: use for where a Page banner sits.
- `Flag`, `Banner`, `SectionMessage`, `InlineMessage`, `NotificationItem`, `Modal`: the components.

contextPages.intro: What happens when text or a list is longer than its room: titles wrap, cells truncate, lists fold, tables page.
contextPages.name: Overflow
contextPages.text:
# Overflow

What happens when text or a list is longer than its room: titles wrap, cells truncate, lists fold, tables page.

## The four answers

Pick by what the text is. Wrap when it must be read whole; truncate when the room is fixed and the full text can be reached; fold a list; page a table.

- **Wrap.** Titles, headers, labels, errors and notifications take more lines. They never end in an ellipsis.
- **Truncate with a Tooltip.** A cell ends in an ellipsis on one line. Its full text opens on hover and focus, only while it is clipped.
- **Fold a list.** A Tag group keeps one line and folds the rest behind +n. For other lists, "Show n more" and "Show less" are Planned .
- **Page a table.** A table pages instead of growing: the pager sits at the end of the Section footer.

## Key cases

The three cases below are Planned : no component carries them yet.

- **The breadcrumb middle.** Five or more levels fold the middle into a "…" that opens a menu of the hidden levels. The Breadcrumb never wraps.
- **An open item in the Sidebar.** Named by when and who, "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz", with the school in the Tooltip. Three show, then "Show n more".
- **A file name.** The one mid-line truncation: a file name or an id keeps its start and its end, because the end tells them apart.

## Motion

## Usage

Use Overflow when a value may exceed its space. Choose by element so it behaves consistently across pages, with the full text always reachable.

| Element | Answer | Full text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page title, Section title | Wrap | Always visible |
| Field error, Section message, Flag, Banner | Wrap | Always visible |
| Column header | Planned: wrap | Always visible |
| Table cell | Truncate at the end, one line | Tooltip on hover and focus when clipped |
| Tag (180), Status tag (200) | Truncate at the end | Tooltip when clipped; the tag becomes focusable |
| Tags in a group | Fold into +n | The +n menu lists the hidden tags |
| A table | Page | The range and the pager in the footer |
| Breadcrumb with five or more levels | Planned: fold the middle into "…" | The "…" opens a menu of the hidden levels |
| Open item in the Sidebar | Planned: truncate at the end | Tooltip with the school |
| Auto-width Popup row | Planned: truncate at the end at 320 | Tooltip when clipped |
| File name, id | Planned: truncate mid-line | Tooltip when clipped |
| A list of items, tags or notes | Planned: "Show n more", "Show less" | Expanded in place |

## Alternatives

- For a long paragraph, let it wrap; a paragraph is read, not scanned.
- For a trail too long to show, follow Navigation; the Breadcrumb's fold is described there.
- For more views than fit a row of pills, fold the extra pills into "More"; Navigation describes the views.
- For more controls than fit a bar, the extras go into the More icon button, five controls at most.
- For narrowing a long list of rows instead of folding it, follow Filtering.

## Best practices

### Wrap titles, headers, labels, errors and notifications.

They must be read whole, so they take more lines. Nothing that tells a person what something is, or what went wrong, is ever clipped.

Do: A long Section title takes a second line.
Don't: A clipped Section title: the one thing that names the content is the one thing cut.

### Truncate cells, tags and names at the end, on one line.

An ellipsis stands for three or more characters. A cell stays one line. Mid-line truncation is only for file names and ids, where the end tells them apart; it is Planned . Truncating from the front is not used.

### Open the full text in a Tooltip only when it is clipped.

The Tooltip opens on hover and on focus, and the clipped element becomes a tab stop only while it is clipped. Never the browser's `title` attribute. An unclipped value has no Tooltip.

Do: A clipped cell opens its full text in a Tooltip.
Don't: A clipped cell with nothing to open: the rest of the text cannot be read.

### Make a bare ellipsis open a menu.

A "…" that stands for hidden items, such as the breadcrumb middle, is a button that opens them. A "…" at the end of a value is not a control.

### Fold a list behind Show n more and page a table.

"Show n more" carries the count and "Show less" closes; both are Planned . A Tag group folds into +n today. A table pages in its footer instead of growing. No gradients, fades or inner scroll.

Do: A button under the list that names how many more it holds, and the list grows in place.
Don't: A fade over the list, hiding how much is there.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| "Show 4 more" and "Show less" (Planned). | "Load more", "See all", "…". |
| Open item: "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz"; the school in the Tooltip (Planned). | The whole title in the Sidebar. |
| Breadcrumb levels by the page's own title: "Lincoln Middle School". | "Back", "Up one level". |
| File name mid-line: "reflection_…_week12.pdf" (Planned). | "reflection_maya_rodrig…". |

## Accessibility

- The full text is always in the DOM, so a screen reader hears all of it whether or not it is clipped.
- A clipped element is a tab stop so a keyboard user can reach the Tooltip; an unclipped one is not.
- The +n button of a Tag group names how many tags it holds, "+3 more tags", and opens a menu the arrow keys move through.
- The breadcrumb's "…" button is named "Show hidden levels" .
- "Show n more" announces the new count when the list expands .

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full text | Tooltip | Switched on only while the text is clipped. |
| Label | Tag, Status tag | `maxWidth` caps the tag; a clipped label ends in an ellipsis. |
| Folded tags | Tag group | `overflow="collapse"` keeps one line and folds the rest into +n. |
| Cell | Dynamic table | A cell's `overflow` is `truncate` by default; `wrap` takes more lines. |
| Trail | Breadcrumb | The fold is Planned ; the component never folds its middle yet. |
| Pager | Pagination | Fills the Section's footer slot, aligned to the end. |

## Related

- Navigation: use for the breadcrumb and the Sidebar's open items.
- Indicators: use for tags that clip.
- Section: use for the footer a table pages in.

contextPages.intro: Choose an approach with code-free guidance and examples on templates you can use or adapt.
contextPages.name: Overview
contextPages.text:
# Patterns

Choose an approach with code-free guidance and examples on templates you can use or adapt.

## The patterns

Seven patterns and six States pages cover situations, examples on templates and usage. Consult them when choosing or reconsidering an approach. Templates and patterns explains how the layers fit together.

- **Navigation.** How a person moves between areas, views and records, with one control and one motion per move.
- **Common actions.** Which button, in which look, in which place, with which word, and acting on many rows at once.
- **Filtering.** How a person narrows a collection to the rows that matter, in five tiers.
- **Forms.** How a form takes and checks what someone types, and what happens on leaving with edits.
- **Search.** How a person finds a record by typing, in one of three modes.
- **Indicators.** The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved.
- **Notifications.** What the product says back, and where: a Flag, a Banner, a SectionMessage, the Inbox.
- **States · Empty.** What a view shows when it has nothing to show.
- **States · Overflow.** What happens when text or a list is longer than its room: titles wrap, cells truncate, lists fold, tables page.
- **States · Loading.** What to show while PLUS fetches or saves something.
- **States · Errors.** Where a failure shows and what it says.
- **States · Disabled.** When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person.
- **States · Read-only.** A value someone could change but this person cannot right now.

## Which pattern for which situation

Start from what is happening on the page. Each row names the pattern that answers it and the ones to read beside it.

| The situation | Pattern | Also read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choosing a button's look, words or place | Common actions | Forms |
| Acting on several rows at once | Common actions · the bulk bar | None |
| Taking and checking what someone types | Forms | Errors · Disabled |
| A view with nothing to show | Empty | Search · Filtering · Errors |
| Something is still fetching or saving | Loading | Notifications |
| Something failed | Errors | Forms · Notifications · Empty |
| Text or a list is longer than its room | Overflow | Navigation |
| A control cannot be used yet, or by this person | Disabled | Read-only · Forms |
| A value this person may see but not change | Read-only | Disabled |
| Telling someone what happened or what is wrong | Notifications | Errors |
| Showing a state, a number or a change on something | Indicators | Notifications |
| Moving between areas, views and records | Navigation | Overflow |
| Finding rows by what they are called | Search | Filtering · Empty |
| Narrowing rows by their attributes | Filtering | Search · Empty |

## Which state is it?

The six states told apart by what the view is doing. A filled dot means the pattern is built for it.

| The view… | Empty | Loading | Errors | Overflow | Disabled | Read-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| has no records to show | Yes | No | No | No | No | No |
| is still fetching or saving | No | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| could not load its content | Yes | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| could not save | No | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| has more than fits | No | No | No | Yes | No | No |
| has a control that waits on something the person can fix here | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |
| shows a value this person cannot change right now | No | No | No | No | No | Yes |
| hides what this role can never use | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |

A load failure fills two markers: Errors owns its words, and Empty owns the slot they show in. To choose a layer for a task, use the chooser on the Templates overview.

contextPages.intro: A value someone could change but this person cannot right now. It stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, and says why in its caption.
contextPages.name: Read-only
contextPages.text:
# Read-only

A value someone could change but this person cannot right now. It stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, and says why in its caption.

## The three cases

Choose how to show a value by who can change it and what prevents editing.

- **Read-only.** Someone can change it; this person cannot right now. Neutral fill, full contrast, the reason in the caption.
- **Plain text.** Nobody ever changes it here. It is a label and a value, not a field.

The third case is Disabled: the value waits on something fixable on this screen. It is faded and out of the tab order, and it is never swapped with read-only.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Read-only for a value someone could change but this person cannot right now: a session time the supervisor set, a field locked while a process runs, a record another person is editing. The common PLUS case is permission. Content that is never editable is plain text, not a read-only field.

| Who can change it | Show it as | Tab order | Looks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Someone else, or this person later | Read-only field | In | Neutral fill, full contrast, no chevron or calendar, no hover |
| Nobody, ever, here | Plain text: label and value | Out | Text |
| This person, once a prerequisite on this screen is met | Disabled field | Out | Faded, the reason in the caption |

## Alternatives

- For a value nobody changes here, show plain text in a details Section.
- For a field that waits on another on this screen, follow Disabled.
- For a value this person can change but rarely, use `InlineEdit`.

## Best practices

### Keep a read-only field in the tab order at full contrast.

It can be reached, read, selected and copied. `isReadOnly` sets `aria-readonly` on the controls that carry the role; the text keeps its color and the fill goes neutral. There is no hover change and the cursor is an arrow.

### Drop the interactive cues.

`Select` hides its chevron and `DatePicker` its calendar button. `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup` and `Toggle` keep their state and ignore clicks.

### Say why in the caption.

"Set by your supervisor." "Locked while the import runs." One caption on a group is enough when every field in it is read-only for the same reason.

Do: Read-only at full contrast, with "Set by your supervisor" in the caption.
Don't: A faded value with no reason: out of the tab order and hard to read.

### Show a read-only value whole.

A `Select` wraps to show its full value; for a `TextArea`, set `rows` to show it all. Automatic TextArea growth is Planned .

### Show never-editable content as plain text.

A field promises an input. A value nobody changes here is a label and a value in a details Section.

Do: A value nobody changes here is plain text.
Don't: A field for a value that was never editable: it promises an input.

### Keep read-only and disabled apart.

Disabled is for a prerequisite fixable on this screen and leaves the tab order. Read-only is for content people must read.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Caption: "Set by your supervisor." | "Read-only", "Locked". |
| Caption: "Locked while the import runs." | "Temporarily unavailable". |
| Group caption: "Session details are set by Lincoln's supervisor." | A caption repeated on every field. |

## Accessibility

- `aria-readonly` on every read-only control that carries the role; it is reachable and read by screen readers with its label and caption.
- Text contrast is unchanged from an editable field.
- The value can be selected and copied with the keyboard.
- The caption is tied to the field, so the reason is read with it.

## Related

- Disabled: use for a prerequisite fixable on this screen.
- Forms: use for the form the read-only field sits in.
- Overflow: use for everything else that may clip.
- `TextField`, `TextArea`, `Select`, `DatePicker`, `TimePicker`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Toggle`: the components with `isReadOnly`.

contextPages.intro: How a person finds a record by typing, with a Search field in one of three modes: active, focused or basic.
contextPages.name: Search
contextPages.text:
# Search

How a person finds a record by typing, with a Search field in one of three modes: active, focused or basic.

## Choosing a type

Three modes share one field. Choose by the amount of data and the cost of searching it.

- **Active.** Small or on-screen data. The rows narrow in place as the person types.
- **Focused.** A person's own work, found from the page they are on. A panel under the field lists recent searches, then matches grouped by type, and widens with "See all results".
- **Basic.** Large or costly data. Nothing runs while typing; Enter takes the person to a results page.

## Active search

The field starts the Section header's third row, compact, and collapses to an icon until it is needed. The results area under the header holds the count, the rows and the states; the header never moves.

## Focused search

Focus in the field opens the panel. With no text it lists recent searches; while typing it lists matches grouped by type, then a last "See all results" row that runs a basic search. An optional action row, such as "Add student", closes the panel.

## Basic search

The field alone. Typing runs nothing; Enter runs the search and a results page takes over. That page is its own template, outside this pattern.

## Scope filter and placement

## Motion

## Usage

Use Search when a person knows what a record is called. Search finds by name; Filtering narrows by attribute, so the two keep separate controls and separate counts.

| Mode | Use when | Where the answer lands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Active | The data is small or already on screen. | The rows in place, as you type. |
| Focused | A person finds their own work from the page they are on. | A panel under the field; "See all results" widens it. |
| Basic | The data is large or costly to search. | A results page, after Enter. |

| Key or action | With text | Empty |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type | Active: rows narrow and the count updates. Focused: the panel lists matches. | Focused: the panel lists recent searches. |
| Enter | Basic: runs the search. Focused: chooses the row under the cursor, or runs the search when none is. | Nothing to run. |
| Esc | Focused with the panel open: closes the panel and keeps the text. Otherwise clears the text. | A collapsible field closes and returns focus to the icon. |
| Arrow keys | Focused: move through the panel's rows. | Focused: move through recent searches. |
| Tab | Focused: closes the panel and moves on. | Moves on. |
| "Clear search" | Clears the text; the field stays open. | Not shown. |
| Leave the field | Stays open with its text. | A collapsible field shrinks back to the icon. |
| Switch views | The search is kept. | Nothing to keep. |
| "Reset filters" | Clears the search and every filter. | Nothing to clear. |

## Alternatives

- For narrowing by an attribute, follow Filtering.
- For picking one value from a long list, use a Select with its own search.
- For moving to another area, follow Navigation.

## Best practices

### Pick the mode by where the answer lands.

Active when the rows are in hand and few, focused when the person jumps to a record from the page they are on, basic when the search is heavy enough to wait for Enter. One mode per field.

### Name the scope in the placeholder.

"Search students". The label is hidden, so the placeholder is what a person reads and what names the collapsed icon.

### Add a scope filter when the search covers more than one kind of record.

The filter sits before the field with "All" first and selected, and each scope carries its count. A search over one kind of record has no scope filter.

### Show the count in the results header, zero included.

"2 of 6 students", "0 of 6 students". The count lives in the results header, in words, and updates as the rows narrow.

### Answer no matches in the results body.

An Empty state fills the results body, names what was searched and offers a next action: "Reset filters". The field stays where it is.

### Let loading mirror empty.

While results load, Skeleton bars take the results body, a Spinner takes the search icon's place and the count slot says what is happening. See Loading.

### Keep the bar still.

The field, the scope filter and the other bar controls hold their place in every state: typing, loading, no matches. Only the results area changes.

### Clear in two steps.

Esc empties the text and keeps the field. In focused, the first Esc closes the panel and keeps the text, and the next clears it. A collapsible field closes on the Esc after that and returns focus to the icon. "Clear search" empties the text and leaves the field open. Switching views keeps the search; "Reset filters" clears it.

### Place by context: compact in a bar, default in a page body.

The Section header holds controls of one height, 32, so the field takes `spacing="compact"` there. A search in a page body takes the default spacing and stays open.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Placeholder starts with a verb and names the scope: "Search students". | "Search…", "Type to search". |
| Count in words: "2 of 6 students", "0 of 6 students". | "2", "2 results". |
| Clear button: "Clear search". | "×", "Reset". |
| No matches: 'No students match "Zoe".' with "Reset filters". | "No results found." |
| Scope filter: "All" first, then the kinds: "Students", "Sessions". | "Everything", "Any". |
| Last panel row: "See all results for Ava". | "More", "Search". |

## Accessibility

- The hidden label still names the field: the collapsed icon and the field share the placeholder's words.
- The scope filter has its own name, "Search scope".
- In focused, the input is the combobox: focus stays in it, the highlighted row is its active descendant and the panel is a named listbox.
- The count in the results header is a polite live region, so "2 of 6 students" is announced as the rows narrow.
- Focus stays in the field when the results empty; it never jumps to the empty state.
- Loading is announced through the Spinner's status text.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Field | Search field | Mode `active`, `focused` or `basic`; compact in a bar, default in a page body. |
| Panel | Popup | Focused only: recent searches, grouped matches, "See all results" and an optional action row. |
| Rows | Dynamic table | Narrows as the text changes. |
| No matches | Empty state | Fills the results body; offers "Reset filters". |
| Loading | Skeleton | Takes the results body; a Spinner takes the search icon. |

## Related

- Filtering: use for narrowing by attributes; its Reset clears the search.
- Empty: use for the No matches state.
- Loading: use for the wait while results load.
- Section: use for where the header rows sit.

contextPages.intro: Arrange components by filling a template's slots. Use patterns to guide the choices.
contextPages.name: Overview
contextPages.text:
# Templates

Arrange components by filling a template's slots. Use patterns to guide the choices.

## The eight templates

Templates run from broadest to smallest. Each page covers types, anatomy, key states and usage. See Templates and patterns below for how the layers fit together.

## Templates and patterns

Templates define slots; patterns guide decisions across templates.

### Three layers

Fill a template's slots; consult a pattern when choosing or reconsidering an approach. Each layer owns one kind of guidance.

- **Components** are single pieces with props, imported by name. The question is "Am I using this piece right?" Anatomy is the piece's parts.
- **Templates** are arrangements of components with slots. They hold key scenarios and key states, and link to components for detail. The question is "Are the slots filled right?" Anatomy is the numbered slots.
- **Patterns** are code-free guidance for a situation, shown on annotated templates used as they are or tweaked. The question is "Is this the right approach?" A pattern has no anatomy and no code.

### The tie-break

Behavior splits out into a component, and a template that only redraws one component stays a component. One component's behavior goes on the component page. How pieces sit in one template goes on that template's page. Anything that holds across two or more templates is a pattern.

The step up from a quick look to its own page is under Opening a record, below. A rule lives in one place. A template page that needs a pattern's rule links to it and keeps its own words for the slots.

### Frame, Screen, Flow

- **Frame:** the template. Sidebar, Page and the AI panel slot, in its default and bare types; a multi-step task runs in its inner sidebar.
- **Screen:** a Frame with its slots filled for one page. Screens are documented under Flows in Figma.
- **Flow:** Screens in order, fulfilling one user story. Flows are documented under Flows in Figma as well.

## Which template for which job

A suggested starting point for each scenario, with the patterns to consult and the components it is built from. Never "always use". To start from the situation instead, use the Patterns overview.

| Scenario | Template | Patterns | Components |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An area page with one collection | Page · default, with a Section view bar alone | Filtering · Search · Common actions | `PageHeader`, `Tabs` (pill), `FilterButton`, `IconButton`, `Button`, `Table` |
| A home page with several Sections | Page · default, titled Sections, cards | Empty · Loading | `PageHeader`, `Card`, `Button` |
| A record page, one level down | Page with a breadcrumb and page tabs | Navigation · Indicators | `Breadcrumb`, `PageHeader`, `StatusTag`, `Tabs`, `PopupSelect` |
| Working through a queue | Panel · Details, docked beside the list | Navigation · Common actions | `Table`, `Panel`, `Button` |
| A quick look at one row | Panel · Details | Navigation | `Panel`, `Button` |
| A short decision before going on | Modal · Active, confirm width | Common actions · Errors | `Dialog`, `Button` |
| A long task with steps | Frame multi-step task, with a form in steps | Forms · Navigation | `Sidebar` (inner mode), `Fieldset`, `FooterActions`, `Button` |
| Settings saved as a group | A settings form on the Page under its page-level Section header; subsections for several groups | Forms · Read-only · Disabled | `Fieldset`, `TextField`, `PopupSelect`, `Toggle`, `Button` |
| Narrowing a long catalog | Section with a filter side | Filtering | `Checkbox`, `PopupSelect`, `Button` |
| Signing in | Frame · bare | Forms · Errors | `Logo`, `TextField`, `Button` |
| Notifications | Panel · Notifications (the Inbox) | Notifications | `Panel`, `Avatar`, `PopupSelect` |
| AI chat | Frame, the AI panel region | AI interaction guidelines | `AiChat`, `PromptInput`, `AiMessage` |

## Frame, Modal, Panel or Popup?

One chooser for the four layers that take over from the page or sit above it. A filled dot means the layer is built for it.

| The task… | Frame · multi-step | Modal | Panel | Popup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocks the page until it is done | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| keeps the page in view and usable | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| holds a long task, or five or more steps | Yes | No | No | No |
| holds a short sequence of steps | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| takes a form | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| is a destructive confirm | No | Yes | No | No |
| hangs off its trigger | No | No | No | Yes |
| dims the page under a Blanket | No | Yes | No | No |
| has its own URL | Yes | No | No | No |
| closes on Escape and returns focus | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal. Anything wider than 4-col, or that outlives a click, leaves the Popup for a Panel. Leaving a multi-step task goes through Save and exit, and unsaved work asks first, in a Modal.

## Opening a record

Least room to most. Pick the lowest step that fits; Navigation holds the rule.

Where a message sits, in a Frame, Page or Section banner, a Flag or a SectionMessage, is Notifications.

contextPages.intro:
A container for one student, session, metric or other object, with slots for an image, header, body and footer.

The examples on this page follow the toolbar's Color mode switch.
contextPages.name: Card
contextPages.text:
# Card

A container for one student, session, metric or other object, with slots for an image, header, body and footer.

The examples on this page follow the toolbar's Color mode switch.

## Size and layout

## Image placement

`imagePlacement` is `top` (default), `start` or `end`. Side placement applies when the card itself is at least the 480 minimum width, independently of the viewport. Below that width the image returns to the top and takes its `imageRatio` height. Use one placement per row of cards.

`imageSplit` is `1/3` (default) or `1/2`, for side placement only. A side image fills the card height, crops to cover, has no padding and takes the card's corners on its side only. The half split steps the title up to Heading md; top placement and narrow cards keep the regular card title.

## Behavior

## Surface

## State

## Interactive playground

## Motion

## Usage

Use a card when one object needs its own container on the page. Pick `surface` by the card's role: `sunken` (default) groups static content on `--ds-surface-sunken` without a shadow; `default` pairs `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border` on the Frame, on Sunken or colored areas, and for dense rows; `raised` pairs `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised` for the one primary card per view, first in reading order. A card holds a heading, content and an optional footer for actions. Fill its slots with your own parts.

1. Pick the size by what the card holds.
2. Choose a header, or omit it when the body carries its own title.
3. Fill the body slot. Add spacing only inside slot content, using Card stack tokens.
4. Add a footer only for actions that commit.

### Color

To give a card a semantic or accent fill, swap its surface token for a solid brand (`--ds-background-brand-subtlest`, or `--ds-background-brand-bold` with `--ds-text-inverse`), status (`--ds-background-information`, `--ds-background-success`), accent-subtlest (`--ds-background-accent-teal-subtlest`), or selected (`--ds-background-selected`) background token. `surface="raised"` keeps `--ds-shadow-raised`. On a clickable colored card, hovered and pressed states use that same token's `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps.

### Width guidance

Content picks the minimum width. Choose the narrowest card that holds the content without clipping, then let the row decide how many fit. Height always hugs the content, and a card in a row stretches to the tallest card.

| Minimum width | When to use | Pad | Radius | Token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224 | One number or one line. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-sm` |
| 304 | A short list or a few lines. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-md` |
| 480 | A summary with several parts. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-lg` |

`minWidth` sets the minimum width; every width uses `--card-pad` (16) and `--card-radius` (16). The text sets the height, and a top image takes its `imageRatio` height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4. Set a height cap with `style`'s `maxHeight`; the card clips what passes it.

### Cards in a row

In a row, place the most cards that keep each card at its minimum width. Each row is the content width of its mode, with a 16 gutter. The count switches between viewport widths of 1224 and 1256 with the sidebar docked.

| Mode | Content width | Min 224 | Min 304 | Min 480 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium, 768 | 720 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Large, 1024 | 736 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| X-Large, 1440 | 1152 | 4 | 3 | 2 |

## Parts

1. **Image** (optional). A slot above everything else, or beside the content in a side layout. It runs edge to edge, outside the pad, and the card radius clips its corners. On top, `imageRatio` (16:9 default, 4:3 or 1:1) sets its height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4, and the picture crops to cover; beside the content it fills the full height at one third or one half of the width and crops to cover.
2. **Header.** The title, an optional description and an optional actions slot. A custom `header` replaces all three. The title uses Heading xs at every heading level, stepping up to Heading md for a half side image. The description uses Body default. In Figma the title truncates to one line and the description's `text` variant truncates at three lines or wraps; code leaves wrapping to CSS.
3. **Body.** A slot for text, a list or media.
4. **Footer** (optional). A start-aligned slot for the card's actions: one link, or a compact pair with no Primary.

The image sits above (or, in a side layout, beside) a padded frame, and the header, body and footer sit inside it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `sunken` (default): `--ds-surface-sunken`, flat. `default`: `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border`, flat. `raised`: `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. Every surface keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) for forced colors. |
| Hovered | A clickable card only: `sunken` and `default` lift in place to `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`; `raised` lifts to `--ds-surface-raised-hovered` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`. A card with no `onClick` does not change. |
| Pressed | A clickable card only: settles to `--ds-surface-raised-pressed` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. |
| Focused | The card has no focus style of its own. A card made clickable as a whole takes `role` and `tabIndex` from you. |
| Disabled | A card is never disabled. Disable the controls inside it. |
| Dragging | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, held under hover and press. |
| Loading | Skeleton bars in the body, with `aria-busy` on the card. Figma's `loading?` has no prop in code. |

### Tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--card-pad` | 16 | Padding inside a card at every width. |
| `--card-radius` | 16 | Corner rounding of a card at every width. |
| `--card-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 4 · 8 · 12 | Title to description; header to body, set by `gap`; body to footer. |
| `--card-inline-md` | 8 | Items on a row, such as actions in the header. |
| `--card-min-width-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 224 · 304 · 480 | The minimum width of each card width. |
| `--card-surface-sunken`, `-default`, `-raised` | color | The card fill at rest (`--ds-surface-sunken`, `--ds-surface`, `--ds-surface-raised`). |
| `--card-border-default`, `--card-border-width` | border | The 1px `--ds-border` on `default` cards, and the 1px width kept on every card for forced colors. |
| `--card-shadow-raised`, `-overlay` | shadow | `--ds-shadow-raised` on raised and hovered clickable cards; `--ds-shadow-overlay` while dragged or hovering a raised card. |
| `--card-surface-raised-hovered`, `-pressed`, `-overlay` | color | Clickable hover/press steps and the dragged overlay surface. |
| `--heading-xs`, `--card-description-font` | type | The regular title and the description (`--body-default`). |
| `--card-title-font-lg` | type | The title beside a half-width side image (`--heading-md`). |
| `--card-text`, `--card-text-subtle` | color | The title and the description (`--ds-text`, `--ds-text-subtle`). |

## Best practices

### Fit the width to what the card holds.

Visible empty space inside the card means a narrower minimum width. A clipped or crowded body means a wider one.

Do: One number fits the 224 minimum; the card is only as wide as it needs, so a row of them stays tidy.
Don't: The same number at 480 leaves most of the card empty; narrow it instead of filling the space.

### Never put a card inside a card.

A card's fill and edge are its own object boundary. Group related cards in a Section instead.

Do: One card; three metrics stacked in its body, split by dividers.
Don't: Three mini cards inside the card; borders and shadows pile up and the hierarchy flattens.

### Keep the card in place while it loads.

Do: Loading keeps the card in place: a skeleton fills the body, so the layout does not jump when data arrives.
Don't: A bare loading line takes the card away; the row collapses and everything below it moves.

### Let the footer's job pick its buttons.

A card's footer actions hug the start, under the content. One action that goes somewhere, such as View session, is a link. Two actions are a compact Default pair with no Primary. A card that is all one action is clickable and has no buttons. Only a Modal or Panel footer, on FooterActions, fills tracks and ends in a Primary. The whole rule: Common actions.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the card with the object it holds, in sentence case: "Ana Ruiz", "Sessions this week". | A generic title such as "Details" or "Info". |
| Keep the description to one line that adds something, such as "Lincoln Middle · Thu 4:00 PM". | A description that repeats the title. |
| Name a footer action for what it does: "Save note", "View session". | "OK" or "Submit". |

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading one level below the section the card sits in: an h3 in a section, an h2 straight on a page. Nest the card in a Section rather than choosing a tag.
- A card that is clickable as a whole needs a role and a tab stop, and it must answer Enter and Space. When the card has one action, put a Button in the footer instead.
- Mark the card `aria-busy` while it loads. The skeleton bars are hidden from assistive technology.
- The hover lift is never the only cue that a card is clickable. Pair it with a visible action or a link in the card.
- Every card keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) so forced colors draw its edge.
- Text sits on each surface in `--ds-text` and `--ds-text-subtle`, which meet contrast in every color mode.
- The card sets `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` to its chosen surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

## Related

- Section for a region that holds cards under one heading.
- Table for many objects of the same shape that people compare across columns.
- Page for the content area's own fill, header and elevation.
- Modal for something that must be decided before the page can continue.

contextPages.intro: Every full page starts in the app frame: the Sidebar beside the Page, with the AI panel as its own region. Two types: default and bare. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.
contextPages.name: Frame
contextPages.text:
# Frame

Every full page starts in the app frame: the Sidebar beside the Page, with the AI panel as its own region. Two types: default and bare. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.

## Types

Choose one of two Frame types for every app page, shown here in browser windows. See Templates and patterns for how filled Frames become Screens and Flows, documented with the flows.

- **Default.** Pages people move among: the Sidebar, the Page, and the AI panel as its own region on the right.
- **Bare.** Sign-in, errors and welcome: one centered column, with no Sidebar and no header row.

## Anatomy

### Default

The default type at 1440 with the AI panel docked.

1. **Sidebar.** 240 wide, docked from 1024, with the toggle ending its logo row.
2. **Header row.** The Page's first row, 32 high on the logo row's center line: the breadcrumb, once a person has drilled into a record.
3. **Content.** The Page's content box: no corner radius, a 24 pad, and a 12-column grid capped at 1232 (864 at reading width, no cap at full width).
4. **AI panel.** A Frame region on the right, 320 to 640 and opening at 400, with its splitter on the left hairline. It docks from 1168 with a 400 panel, from 1408 beside an open Sidebar; under that it floats over the Page.

## Multi-step task

A task with several steps runs in the Sidebar's inner mode on a default Frame. A one-screen task stays a Modal. When a long task takes over the Sidebar is the Navigation pattern.

1. **Back.** The inner sidebar's first row names the area the task came from and returns to the main Sidebar.
2. **Steps.** Text-only rows, one noun each. The current step is marked, answered steps carry a tick, and steps past your answers are disabled with the reason in a tooltip.
3. **Page.** The task's name as the page's one h1, then the step's body at reading width, 864, centered.
4. **Footer**, fixed along the bottom and 48 high. Save and exit is a link at the left edge. Back (Default), then Next (Primary; Finish on the last step) take the right half. Both are FooterActions' filled buttons, 48 high, on the footer rule from Common actions. Back on the first step is disabled and needs no reason.

## Width behavior

The Frame decides what docks from its own width, so the content never drops under 720. Drag the width: the Sidebar and an open AI panel both dock from 1408 with a 400 panel; from 1168 the panel docks alone and the Sidebar collapses; below that, and under 1024, the panel floats over the Page with no Blanket. Under 768 the panel is full width. The Sidebar docks from 1024 (in Figma, the `Sidebar docked` variable); in code the Frame measures its own width through the layout resolver and has no token for it.

## Key states

- **Panel collapses the Sidebar, 1200.** The Sidebar, a 400 panel and 720 of content cannot all fit, so the Sidebar collapses and the toggle moves to the Page's top left. It comes back when the panel closes.

- **Under 1024.** The Sidebar never docks: opened by hand it floats over the Page. The panel floats over the Page with no Blanket, and one layer is open at a time.

A system banner, when one is needed, spans the whole width above the Sidebar and the Page: Notifications.

## Sizes

Lengths are in pixels. Where the layout mode changes a value, the columns read Medium (768), Large (1024) and X-Large (1440).

| Token | Medium | Large | X-Large | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Color and elevation token | Purpose |
| --- | --- |

## Motion

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `sidebar` | The Sidebar. Without it there is no Sidebar and no toggle. |
| `header` | The Page's header row: the breadcrumb. |
| `children` | The content: Sections in a 12-column grid. `width` sets the type: `default` caps it at 1232, `full` has no cap, `reading` caps it at 864. |
| `panel` · `panelLabel` · `panelOpen` | The AI panel region at the right, named for its content, filled with the Panel parts. |
| `surfaceDirect` | Children go straight into the Page with no content box, for a bare column or a full-bleed view. |
| `bar` | Planned. The multi-step footer, 48 high, with Save and exit, Back and Next. Today the page places the footer. |
| `banner` | Planned. System news across the whole width above the Sidebar and the Page. |

## Usage

Use Frame for every page of the app. It owns the frame sizes and the Sidebar's behavior, so a page only supplies its Sidebar, its breadcrumb and its content.

The Frame decides what docks from its own width, not the window's, through one layout resolver, so the content never drops under 720:

- **Sidebar.** Below its docking width, opened by hand, it floats over the Page and closes on an outside press or Escape. Hovering the toggle or the left edge peeks a collapsed Sidebar over the Page with no Blanket. Clicking the toggle, or pressing Ctrl+[, closes a docked Sidebar and opens a collapsed one.
- **AI panel.** It opens from anything inside the Frame through `usePanelControl()`. Both dock when the Sidebar, the panel and the content minimum fit. Otherwise a Sidebar left open by default collapses and comes back when the panel closes. Below that, the panel floats over the Page and the Sidebar on the overlay fill and shadow, with no Blanket.
- **Narrow Frames** hold one layer open at a time: opening the Sidebar closes the panel, and opening the panel closes the Sidebar.
- **Modals.** Opening a Modal closes a peeking or floating Sidebar, and a docked Sidebar stays. While a Modal is open the Sidebar does not peek, and Escape closes the Modal only. A Modal leaves the panel open under its Blanket.

Docked, the panel meets the Page at a hairline. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640, but never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar. The width and whether the panel is open are kept for the tab.

## Alternatives

- For a bare fill and elevation, use `Page`.
- For a region inside the content, use `Section`.
- For a short task that keeps the page in view behind it, use `Modal`. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.

## Best practices

### Give a multi-step task its steps in the inner sidebar.

The steps are the Sidebar's rows, so the Page holds only the task. Done steps tick and stay pressable; steps past your answers are off. The page places the footer along the bottom today; the Frame's `bar` slot is Planned.

Do: The steps as rows in the inner sidebar; the Page holds only the task.
Don't: The steps drawn again inside the Page: two lists for one task.

### Put Save and exit, Back and Next in the footer, with no Cancel.

The footer is fixed along the bottom, one row high, with its buttons on one line. Save and exit leaves the task and keeps the answers, so the footer holds only it, Back and the primary Next. Back on the first step is disabled and needs no reason.

Do: Save and exit as a link at the left edge; Back and the primary Next in the right half, on one line.
Don't: Cancel repeated in the footer beside Save and exit: two ways out of one task.

### Keep the AI panel docked as its own region.

The AI panel is a region of the Frame, not a floating Panel, so it stays put as a person moves between pages. The Page makes room for it; below `FRAME_LAYOUT.dockMin` it floats over the Page, with no Blanket.

Do: The panel docked at the right edge, the Page narrowing beside it.
Don't: The panel floating over the Page, hiding the rows beneath it.

### Keep a bare Frame to one column.

Sign-in, errors and welcome have one job and no account yet, so the Frame carries no Sidebar, header row or Panel.

Do: One centered column: the form and its button.
Don't: The Sidebar beside a sign-in: navigation for a person who has not signed in.

### Put the place in the header as a breadcrumb.

The header row is the breadcrumb, shown only after drilling into a record; area pages and multi-step tasks have none. A page's title belongs to its content, in a Section with `level="page"`.

Elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the multi-step task for what it does: "Plan a tutoring term". | A generic title such as "Wizard". |
| Name the panel for its content with `panelLabel`: "AI chat". | A generic name such as "Panel". |
| Name steps with one noun each: "Student", "Schedule", "Review". | A sentence for a step. |
| Keep Back and Next named for what they do. | Icon buttons with no name. |

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark, and the `nav` inside the Sidebar is the navigation landmark. Pass `contentAs="div"` when the page supplies its own `main`.
- The toggle is a button. Open, it ends the Sidebar's logo row as "Close sidebar"; closed, it sits at the Page's top left as "Open sidebar". It reports whether the Sidebar is showing and announces its shortcut, Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac).
- A peeking or floating Sidebar closes on Escape, and focus returns to the toggle.
- Docked, the AI panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`, after the Page in reading order. Below `FRAME_LAYOUT.dockMin` it is a Modal-style layer: focus moves to its first control, Tab stays inside it, the Page and the Sidebar under it are inert, and closing returns focus to what opened it.
- The splitter is a vertical separator named "Resize panel" that reports its width. The left arrow widens the panel by 16 and the right arrow narrows it, 64 with Shift; Home and End go to the narrowest and the widest.
- A multi-step task's steps are a list named "Steps" in the Sidebar's navigation; the current step is marked, a done step is named "Done", and an off step is not pressable. The footer's buttons follow the body in the tab order.

## Related

- Page: use when you need the bare fill-and-elevation the content box is built on.
- Sidebar: use when choosing what the Frame places beside the Page.
- Section: use when the content needs a region under its own heading.
- Modal: use when the task is short and the page should stay in view behind it.
- Panel: use when the work should float beside the page, not replace it.
- Grid: use when you need the column math the Frame is sized by.

contextPages.intro: A dialog for one task before anything else can happen, centered over a Blanket. Four types: Passive, Active, Acknowledge and Steps.
contextPages.name: Modal
contextPages.text:
# Modal

A dialog for one task before anything else can happen, centered over a Blanket. Four types: Passive, Active, Acknowledge and Steps.

## Types

Picked by what the person has to do. The Dialog component page holds the panel's props and states; these are the filled Modal layouts.

- **Passive.** Information only, with Close. No footer.
- **Active.** A choice, a confirm or a short form. Discard (or a real alternative) and the action; no Cancel.
- **Acknowledge.** One thing to read and one button that fills the footer.
- **Steps.** A short sequence at 10-col: Back and Next, split 50/50.

## Anatomy

An Active Modal at 8-col with a short form. Every part once; the pad is 20 on every side, the radius 16, and the parts sit 16 apart.

1. **Blanket.** Dims the page and holds the Modal centered.
2. **Header.** The title at 20/24, whatever the level around it, and the Close icon button. With tabs, the tab group sits 8 under the title.
3. **Body.** Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap and never draws under 96 tall.
4. **Footer** (optional). Full-bleed buttons; secondary (Default) left, Primary right. A declining action such as "Not now" is the secondary. Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel.

## Widths

A width is a step of the screen grid plus 20 on each side: 4, 6, 8 and 10 columns, here at 1024. It grows with the window and never shrinks; the Sidebar never changes it.

## Width behavior

Drag the screen's width. The Modal grows with it and never shrinks.

| Width | 768 | 1024 | 1440 | Made of |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4-col | 269 | 355 | 440 | 4 screen-grid columns + 2 × 20 |
| 6-col | 392 | 520 | 648 | 6 columns + 2 × 20 |
| 8-col | 515 | 685 | 856 | 8 columns + 2 × 20 |
| 10-col | 637 | 851 | 1064 | 10 columns + 2 × 20 |

## Destructive tiers

Which tier, and its words: Common actions.

## Footers

The rule for 4-track placement, real actions and Close: Common actions.

## Key states

- **Long content.** Each width has a maximum height. Past it the body scrolls between the pinned header and footer; the footer never moves.

- **Loading.** No skeleton on the Modal itself; the body shows its content's own loading state: Loading.

- **With a form.** The fields in the body and the Modal's own footer. A blocked submit keeps the Modal open and marks the field: Forms.

A Modal that confirms inside itself is under Stacking.

## Stacking

A confirm Modal may open over a Panel, a Popup or a multi-step task, and brings its own Blanket. A Modal never opens on another Modal.

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--modal-pad` | 20 | Pad on every side. |
| `--modal-radius` | 16 | Corner radius at every width. |
| `--modal-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 8, 16, 24 | Title to tabs; header, body and footer; groups of fields. |
| `--modal-body-min-height` | 80 | The least the body draws. |
| `--ds-surface-material-overlay`, `--ds-border-material`, `--ds-shadow-blocking` | pair | The Modal's fill, edge and elevation, the one surface that lifts above a Blanket. The fill is translucent with no blur, and turns solid under reduced transparency and increased contrast. |
| `--ds-blanket` | color | The Blanket's fill. |

The Modal's maximum height is the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below.

## Blanket

The Blanket is the full-screen layer inside the Modal template that holds the dimming fill and the Dialog above it, so the Dialog is placed, not drawn. It fills with the blanket token, pads 16 at the sides and 64 above and below, and centers the Dialog. It is part of this template, not exported on its own. The examples in this section follow the toolbar's Color mode switch.

A Blanket interrupts the page for one task. It dims everything behind it with one fill, so the person sees only the layer on top. It never draws content of its own.

A task that keeps the page in view is a Panel, which floats with no Blanket. `inline` draws the Blanket and Dialog in the page flow at a stand-in screen of `screenWidth` and `screenHeight`, for docs and previews.

### Layers

Figma has no z-index, so the order is written here and lives in code.

| Layer | Number | Token | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Navigation | 200 | `--layer-navigation` | The floating sidebar. It has a shadow and no blanket, and an outside click closes it. |
| Menu and Popup | 400 | `--layer-popup` | The Menu and the Popup. One opened from a Modal mounts in it and takes the Modal layer, 510. |
| Blanket | 500 | `--layer-blanket` | The Blanket and its fill. |
| Modal | 510 | `--layer-modal` | A Modal. |
| Flag | 600 | `--layer-flag` | Flags, above a modal. |
| Tooltip | 800 | `--layer-tooltip` | Tooltips, above everything. |

### Parts

1. **Blanket.** The screen-size layer with the blanket fill, the screen grid and the pads.
2. **Dialog.** The panel centered inside it with header, body and footer slots.

The Blanket carries the screen grid; page frames carry the content grid. Height, hug or fill, lives on the Dialog inside it.

### States

The Blanket is shown while the Modal is open and gone when it closes. `blanket` decides whether a press on the Blanket outside the Dialog closes the Modal (`true` by default; `static` or `false` keeps it open).

### Tokens

| Token | Value | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-blanket` | 32% in Light, 60% in Dark | The fill, under every modal. |
| `--blanket-pad-x` | 16 | The closest a modal gets to the sides. |
| `--blanket-pad-y` | 64 | The closest a modal gets to the top and bottom. It drops to 24 under 640 tall. |
| `--blanket-max-height-modal` | screen height less 2 × pad-y: 128, or 48 under 640 tall | The tallest a modal or confirm gets. Its body scrolls past it. |
| `--grid-gutter` | 16 | The gutter between screen-grid columns. |
| `--grid-width-column-screen` | 45.33, 66.67, 88 | One screen-grid column at 768, 1024 and 1440. |
| `--content-max-width` | 1232 | The cap on the screen grid. |
| `--layer-blanket`, `--layer-modal` | 500, 510 | The Blanket and the layer it holds. |

### Place a modal in the Blanket.

Let the Blanket place the modal. Do not detach it to move things around: the pads are the closest a modal gets to the screen edge.

Do: Center the Dialog on the Blanket with the built-in pads.

Don't: Detach or shift the panel past the Blanket edge pads.

### Blanket content guidelines

The Blanket holds no text of its own. The words belong to the Dialog it holds.

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Discard changes?" | A second dialog that repeats the first one's title. |
| Name the confirm's primary action for what it does: "Discard changes". | "OK" or "Yes". |

### Blanket accessibility

- The Blanket is a layout layer with no role. The Dialog inside it is the `dialog`.
- The blanket is a pointer shortcut, not a control. A keyboard closes a dialog from inside it, so the blanket takes no role and no key handler.
- The blanket at `--ds-blanket` keeps the dialog legible in Light and Dark. The toolbar's Contrast switch changes it with the rest of the page.
- A layer wider than a narrow screen keeps its width, and the Blanket scrolls.

### Blanket playground

### Blanket related

- Panel floats beside the page for a task that needs it in view, with no Blanket.
- Frame shows the floating Sidebar and the floating AI panel, which take a shadow and no blanket.

### Blanket motion

## Motion

## Slots

```jsx
import { Modal } from '@/templates';
import { Button } from '@/components';
```

`Modal` places `Dialog` (`@/components`) on the Blanket with Base UI portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return.

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `onClose` | The h1 and the Close icon button. |
| `width` | `4-col` · `6-col` · `8-col` · `10-col`. |
| `body` | Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap. |
| `footer` or `primaryButton` · `secondaryButton` | The footer's buttons. Leave them out for Passive. |
| `blanket` · `keyboard` | Whether a Blanket press or Escape closes the Modal (`true` by default; `blanket="static"` keeps it open). |
| Full-bleed footer | Planned. Cells that fill the footer edge to edge and never change the Modal's height, with the inner corners squared. Today the page composes it from Button. |
| `tabs` | Two to five views of one thing under the title. |
| `confirmView` | Planned. The swapped title, body and footer for a confirm about the Modal itself. Today the caller swaps them in place. |
| Blocked-submit shake | Planned. The Modal's single shake when a submit is blocked. |

## Usage

Use a Modal when the next step has to happen before anything else can: a confirm, a rare critical task with fewer than five fields, something to read before going on. It is always centered over a Blanket. A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal.

| Type | Use when | Footer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Passive | Something to read, with nothing to decide | None; Close only |
| Active | A choice, a confirm or a short form | Secondary (such as Discard or Keep) and the action; no Cancel |
| Acknowledge | One thing to read and accept | One button |
| Steps | A short ordered sequence | Back and Next |

## Alternatives

- For the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, use `Dialog` (`@/components`).
- For content read beside the page, use `Panel`.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For a long or stepped task, use `Frame`.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Open a Modal only from a person's action.

A button, a link, an icon. Never on its own.

Do: Open a Modal when a person clicks an action or trigger.

Don't: Open a Modal automatically on page load.

### Size a confirm at the smallest step and step up with a detail line or a field.

A confirm takes 4-col or 6-col; a short form is 8-col; a table, editor or steps is 10-col. Choose width by task.

Do: A confirm at the narrow step: the title, one line and two buttons.
Don't: The same confirm at a wide step: empty width around one line, picked to make it look a certain way.

### Confirm inside the Modal, and never open a Modal on another Modal.

Stacking holds the rule. The overlay module keeps a second Modal closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: One Modal that confirms inside itself, with a message and its own buttons.
Don't: A Modal opened on another Modal, a second Blanket dimming the first.

### Scroll the body between a fixed header and footer.

Each width has a maximum height, the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below. Header and footer are pinned and the footer never moves. Actions never sit in the body, which scrolls away; a missing-field error shows on the field and the body scrolls to it, and a rejected submit shows its message at the top of the body.

Do: Past the cap the body scrolls; the footer stays pinned with its buttons.
Don't: The button inside the scrolling body: it scrolls out of reach.

### Use tabs for views, not steps.

Two to five views of one thing opened in any order; one footer saves them all. Views in order are Steps, with Back and Next in the footer.

Do: Views in order are Steps: Back and Next split across the footer.
Don't: Numbered tabs as steps: any order, one Save, nothing to go back to.

Footer buttons, real actions and Close, and which destructive tier, including type the name: Common actions. A blocked submit: Forms. The sending button: Loading.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Delete this session?" | "Are you sure?" or "Warning". |
| Give the consequence in one line: "This cannot be undone." | A paragraph that repeats the title. |
| Name the action after the question: "Delete session". | "OK" or "Yes". |
| On the last step, name Next after the outcome: "Schedule". | "Finish". |

## Accessibility

- The Modal is a dialog named by its title, which is its h1; a Section inside opens at h2. A Modal with a custom header needs its own name.
- Focus moves into the Dialog on open (to the first input or control) and stays trapped until it closes, while the page behind stops scrolling. Escape, Close and the Blanket close it, and focus returns to what opened it.
- Set `blanket="static"` (or `false`) for an inline confirmation of a destructive action so a stray click outside does not abandon it.
- A body that scrolls is a tab stop. With tabs, Left and Right move between tabs and the panel is named by its tab.
- A blocked submit announces the first error; with reduced motion the color, icon, message and focus move carry it without the shake.
- Close is named "Close". The Danger button in a type-the-name confirm stays disabled until the name matches, and the caption carries the reason.

## Related

- Dialog: use when drawing the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, such as in docs and mockups.
- Forms: use when the Modal holds fields.
- Panel: use when the page must stay usable.
- Popup: use when the content is a menu or a short list.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules across Modals: Common actions, Forms, Errors, Loading.

contextPages.intro: The content inside a Frame: a page header, then Sections on the 12-column grid. Three types: default, full width and reading.
contextPages.name: Page
contextPages.text:
# Page

The content inside a Frame: a page header, then Sections on the 12-column grid. Three types: default, full width and reading.

## Types

- **Default.** The content grid, centered and capped at its content width. Nearly every page.
- **Full width.** The content runs to the pad with no cap, for a page that fills it, such as chat, a board or a wide table.
- **Reading.** The grid capped at 864, the readable measure: training lessons, help articles and policies. A multi-step task and sign-in use it too.

The Frame's `width` sets the type: `default`, `full` or `reading`.

## Anatomy

A record page one level down shows every header slot, with markers in the gutter beside each part.

1. **Breadcrumb** (optional). The record's parents on their own row, above the title.
2. **Title.** The page's one h1, with its StatusTag after the text when the page is one record.
3. **Description** (optional). One line under the title.
4. **Page actions** (optional). At the end of the title row, about the page only.
5. **Page tabs** (optional). At the bottom of the header; they switch the whole page.
6. **Banner** (optional). Under the header, one at a time.
7. **Content.** Sections on the grid, under the header.

## Key scenarios

## Width behavior

Drag the width control. Above the content cap, content centers at the cap; below it, content fills the available width. The header keeps one h1 at every width.

## Key states

- **Page banner.** A message about this page sits under the page header and scrolls with the content. Which tier a message belongs to is the Notifications pattern, listed in the Patterns overview.

- **Header and banner slots.** Page owns the spacing from its header to the banner and content, including when the banner is removed.

## Reference screens

Two whole screens built from the templates: a list that keeps search and quick filters in the Section header, and a detail page with its editing Panel docked beside it.

## Sizes

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--page-header-stack` | Between the breadcrumb, the title row and the page tabs. |
| `--page-header-gap` | Between the title and the page actions. |
| `--page-stack-md` | Header to the banner and the first Section; between Sections. |
| `--heading-lg`, `--body-default`, `--body-sm` | The title, the description, the breadcrumb. |
| `--content-max-width`, `--content-max-width-reading`, `--content-min-width` | The default cap, the reading cap and the floor of the content grid. Full width has no cap. |
| `--grid-columns`, `--grid-gutter`, `--page-pad` | The 12-column grid, its gutter and the pad. |
| `--ds-surface` | The Page's one fill, with no shadow. |

## Heading outline

Headings step down one size per nesting level, and their tags follow the nesting. The page's one h1 is Heading lg (24), a section's h2 is Heading md (20), and a subsection's h3 is Heading sm (16).

The outline keeps a page's headings in one order, so a reader and assistive technology see the same structure the sizes show. It applies across the Page, Section, Card, Modal, Popup and Flag.

### Page, Section and Subsection

Use one h1 per page. Each Section opens with an h2, and a subsection inside it with an h3. Do not skip a level to get a different size: the size follows from the level. Container titles keep their own sizes on their templates: Card, Modal and Popup.

### Group labels

A menu's label names a group, and a table's labels are column headers. Neither joins the outline.

### Heading outline accessibility

- **Tags follow nesting.** Heading levels are real `h1` to `h3` elements, not styled text, so screen reader users can move by heading.

## Motion

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | The page's one h1, at the heading-lg size, above the content. |
| `children` | The Sections and other page content. Existing pages may still supply the header and banner here. |
| `header` | One `PageHeader`: the h1 with `breadcrumbs` after a drill-in, `actions` and page tabs in `bottomBar`. Replaces `title`. |
| `description` · `status` | Planned. `PageHeader` has neither slot yet, so the examples here compose both in its `title` block: the `Heading`, a StatusTag after it, then one description line. |
| `banner` | One page `Banner`, below the header. Page separates the slots and content with `--page-stack-md`. |
| Type | Set on the Frame's `width`: `default` (1232), `full` (no cap) or `reading` (864). |
| Scrolled header | Planned. The sticky one-row header. |
| `as` | The container element. |

## Usage

Use Page for the content of every default Frame. It carries the page header, the one h1, and the Sections under it. The default type caps the grid at 1232; full width is for a page that fills the window, such as chat, a board or a wide table; reading caps it at 864 for text people read through.

## Alternatives

- For one task that takes the whole window, use `Frame`.
- For a region of the page with its own heading, use `Section`.
- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.

## Best practices

### Make the page header the page's one h1.

A Section never stands in for it. Sections inside open at h2.

Do: The page header is the one h1; the Section under it opens at h2.
Don't: Sections standing in for the page title: two page-title-sized headings and no page header.

### Show the breadcrumb by the Navigation pattern.

When it shows and what it holds: the Navigation pattern.

Do: An area page: the title alone.
Don't: A breadcrumb on a top-level area page, repeating the Sidebar's place.

### Place page actions and the add action by the Navigation pattern.

Page actions sit at the end of the title row and are about the page only. Where an add action goes: the Navigation pattern.

Do: "Add" is the Section's one action, in its title row; the page header carries only page actions.
Don't: The same Primary twice: in the page header and in the Section's title row.

### Keep the description to one line.

Anything longer moves into the first Section.

Do: One detail line under the title.
Don't: A paragraph under the title pushes the first Section down.

### Keep one tab system per page.

The rule and its reasons: the Navigation pattern. Page tabs name views of one subject; the Section's views become one labeled PopupSelect.

Do: Under page tabs the Section's views are one labeled PopupSelect in its views row.
Don't: Pill views under page tabs: two tab systems on one page.

### Shrink the scrolled header to one sticky row.

The breadcrumb with the title at its end, then the page actions; page tabs stick under it. The Section header rows scroll away. This state is planned.

### Show one banner at a time, scrolling with the content.

Which tier a message belongs to: the Notifications pattern.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title an area with what it holds, in sentence case: "Sessions". | Title case, or a title that repeats the breadcrumb. |
| Title a record with its name: "Maya Rodriguez". | "Student details". |
| One detail line: "Grade 8 · Math · Lincoln Middle School". | A paragraph under the title. |
| Page tab labels of one or two words: "Overview", "Sessions". | Numbered tabs, or tabs that wrap. |

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark. Its header's title is the one h1; Sections open at h2.
- The breadcrumb is a `nav` named "Breadcrumb".
- Page tabs are a tablist; the selected tab names its panel. Views swap in place and are announced.
- The StatusTag is text, never color alone.
- A title that truncates keeps its full text in a Tooltip on hover and focus.
- Text on a Page uses `--ds-text` at every level, in every color mode.

## Related

- Frame: use when deciding which type the page sits in.
- Section: use when a region needs its own heading, views or detail.
- Card: use when one object has a shape already agreed.
- Patterns: use when deciding where a breadcrumb or a tab belongs (Navigation), or choosing the StatusTag beside the title (Indicators).

contextPages.intro:
A full-height layer with no Blanket. Details sits on the right, docked beside the Page when it fits and floating over it when it does not; Notifications, the Inbox, sits at the start beside the Sidebar. Two types: Details and Notifications. The AI panel is a region of the Frame.
