contextPages.name: Panel
contextPages.text:
# Panel

A full-height layer with no Blanket. Details sits on the right, docked beside the Page when it fits and floating over it when it does not; Notifications, the Inbox, sits at the start beside the Sidebar. Two types: Details and Notifications. The AI panel is a region of the Frame.

Import the Panel and its parts from `@/templates`. This template documents the parts and its layout within the Frame.

## Types

Neither has a Blanket. Details opens on the right, docked beside the Page when it fits and floating over it when it does not (Width behavior has the widths); floating at every width is Planned. Notifications opens at the start, beside the Sidebar.

- **Details.** A quick look at a row, docked beside the Page or floating over its right by width. The picked row stays highlighted.
- **Notifications.** The Inbox, opened from the bell beside your name. It docks beside the Sidebar, 360 wide, and stays open as you pick one.

## Anatomy

### Details

Opened from a session row. The page behind stays usable.

1. **Splitter.** On the Page-facing edge; it resizes from 320 to 640.
2. **Header.** The title names the record, with its status in the Subheader row under it; then Edit and the fixed actions: Up, Down, More, Close.
3. **Body.** The record's Sections. It scrolls between the header and the footer.

The picked row stays highlighted on the page while the Panel is open.

### Notifications

Picking an item opens its page behind the Panel and marks it read. The Inbox stays open.

1. **Header.** The title, Mark all as read and Close.
2. **Tabs.** Unread, with its count, and All.
3. **Items.** One `NotificationItem` per update, grouped by day. An unread item says "Unread" to a screen reader.

The bell at the end of the Sidebar's account row, with its unread count, opens the Inbox. The Inbox docks beside the Sidebar at `--inbox-width` (360) over the page, never covers the Sidebar, and closes on Escape, with focus back on the bell, on an outside click or on Close.

## Width behavior

Drag the Frame's width. From 1168 a 400 Panel docks beside the Page at an edge line with no shadow. Under it the Panel floats on the overlay material and shadow, capped at 320 under 1024 and full width under 768. It never has a Blanket.

## Composition

The parts on their own, outside a Frame, at the width they are given.

## Key states

- **Editing.** The same Panel with the form open and its full-bleed footer: Discard (Default) left and Save (Primary) right; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. Save returns to reading, which has no footer.

- **With a form.** A short edit of a row with the page still in view: the fields in the body and the Panel's own footer. Validation and leaving with edits: Forms.

- **Record gone.** When the row no longer exists the body shows its empty state with a way back: Empty.

- **Under 1024.** Too narrow to dock beside the table: the Panel floats on the overlay material and shadow, capped as Width behavior says, still with no Blanket.

### Beside the AI panel

A floating Panel and the docked AI panel sit side by side, and the AI panel is never covered. The Frame has one Panel area today, so this pair is Planned.

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--panel-width-default` | 400 | The width a Panel opens at. |
| `--inbox-width` | 360 | The width the Inbox opens at, beside the Sidebar. |
| `--panel-min-width` | 320 | The narrowest, and the cap under 1024. |
| `--ds-surface-material-overlay`, `--ds-border-material`, `--ds-shadow-overlay` | pair | The floating Panel's fill, edge and elevation. The fill is translucent with no blur, and turns solid under reduced transparency and increased contrast. A docked or standalone Panel uses `--ds-surface` and an edge line. |
| `--ds-border` | 1 | The edge line where a docked Panel meets the Page. |

The Panel resizes from 320 to 640 by drag or keys, never past what keeps 720 of content beside it.

## Motion

## Slots

```jsx
import { Frame, PanelContainer, PanelHeader, PanelBody, PanelFooter } from '@/templates';
```

The Panel components are the parts: header with its fixed actions, subheader, body, footer and disclaimer. The Frame hosts one, decides whether it docks or floats, and closes it on Escape. The template is its filled layout, one per type. The AI panel is the Frame's `panel`.

| Slot | Details | Notifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | The record's name, with its StatusTag under it | "Inbox" |
| `actions` | Edit, then Up, Down, More and Close | Mark all as read and Close |
| `backAction` · `titleIcon` | Optional, in the header before the title: a back action (`PanelBackAction`) and an icon. Pick the one the task needs. | None |
| `subheader` (`PanelSubheader`) | The record's StatusTag under the title | None: the Unread and All tabs sit under the header |
| `body` | Sections of the record; the form while editing | Items grouped by day, in Unread and All tabs |
| `footer` · `disclaimer` (`PanelFooter`, `PanelDisclaimer`) | Only while editing: Discard and Save, full bleed; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. The page composes it from Button. Planned as a prop. A `PanelDisclaimer` carries small print beside the actions. | None |
| Placement | Right. Docked from 1168; floating under it. Floating at every width is Planned. | Start, beside the Sidebar, 360 wide (`--inbox-width`), over the page with no Blanket. It opens from the Sidebar's bell, not from the Frame's Panel area. |
| Beside the AI panel | Planned. The Frame has one Panel area. | Planned. |

## Usage

Use a Panel when content is read beside the page and outlives a click: a quick look at a row, a short edit with the table in view, the Inbox. It never has a Blanket, so the page behind stays usable. Details sits on the right, docked beside the Page from 1168 and floating over it under that. The Inbox opens from the Sidebar's bell and docks beside the Sidebar at the start, 360 wide, over the page. One floating Panel is open at a time; opening another replaces it.

The AI panel is not a floating Panel. It is a region of the Frame, docked where there is room, so it persists across pages.

## Alternatives

- For a decision that must happen before the page continues, use `Modal`.
- For a queue page, use `Panel` docked beside the list; the record opens on demand.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For complex or multistep work, give the record its own page with a multi-step task on `Frame`.

## Parts

1. **Container** (`PanelContainer`). The outer surface. Its `width` falls back to the nearest `PanelProvider`'s width, then to `--panel-width-default`; inside the Frame's Panel area it fills the area instead.
2. **Header** (`PanelHeader`). An optional back action, an optional title icon, the title, and an action group (`PanelCloseAction`, `PanelMoreAction`).
3. **Subheader** (`PanelSubheader`). An optional row of secondary content under the header: tabs, a filter summary.
4. **Body** (`PanelBody`). The main content, which scrolls.
5. **Footer** (`PanelFooter`). Actions that commit a change, with an optional `PanelDisclaimer` for small print beside them.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The page ground with a leading edge. |
| Hovered | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Focused | Not focusable. Focus goes to the fixed actions and the content. |
| Disabled | A panel has no disabled state. Disable the controls in it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Ground and edge | `--ds-surface`; `--ds-border` at `--border-width-default` on the leading edge. |
| Header | Padding `--panel-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`; `--panel-inline-md` between its parts; `--border-width-default` rule below. |
| Action group | `--panel-inline-sm` between actions. |
| Subheader | Padding `--panel-subheader-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`; `--border-width-default` rule below. |
| Body | Padding `--panel-pad`. |
| Footer | Padding `--panel-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`, `--panel-inline-lg` between its parts; rule above; disclaimer in `--body-sm`, `--ds-text-subtle`. |

## Best practices

### Float a Panel with no Blanket.

The page keeps scrolling and stays clickable. A press on the page outside the Panel, or Escape, closes it. Narrow, it is capped and then full width, still with no Blanket. A confirm Modal over a Panel brings its own Blanket.

Do: The Panel floats on its shadow and the page beside it stays undimmed.
Don't: The same Panel with a Blanket dimming the whole page.

### Open one floating Panel at a time.

Another row swaps the content; the Inbox replaces Details. The overlay module keeps a second overlay closed.

Do: One Panel; another row swaps what it shows.
Don't: Two Panels open at once, the second covering the first.

### Keep the picked row highlighted while Details is open.

Picking the same row again closes it; Up and Down step through the rows.

### Show a footer only while editing.

Discard (Default) and Save (Primary), full bleed; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. A declining action such as "Keep editing" is Default, in the left half. Reading needs no footer.

Do: Reading: a header and a body, nothing to save.
Don't: A footer of buttons on a Panel that is only read.

### Leave the AI panel uncovered.

A floating Panel and the docked AI panel sit side by side. The AI panel is never covered. This pair is Planned.

The docked AI panel here is a second Panel in the docked slot; its own placement beside a floating Panel is not built yet.

Do: The floating Panel beside the docked AI panel, both fully visible.
Don't: The floating Panel drawn over the AI panel, hiding part of it.

### Move a Panel that needs full attention into a Modal.

If the person must not look at anything outside it, it is a Modal.

### Grow the Inbox out of the Sidebar.

Its left edge sits against the Sidebar, over the left of the Page. Picking an item opens its page behind the Inbox, which stays open. Flags still show at the top right. This placement is Planned.

### Give the Panel room to read.

Below its default width the title wraps and the body stops being scannable.

Do: Default width.
Don't: Squeezed to a narrow strip.

### Keep the header to one cue.

An icon, a back action and a subheader together bury the title; pick the one the task needs.

### Share one width across a page's Panels with `PanelProvider`.

Wrap the region that can open Panels in a `PanelProvider`, and read or change the shared width with `usePanelManager`, so Panels opened over time stay the same size instead of each picking its own.

```jsx
<PanelProvider>
    <PanelContainer>
        <PanelHeader title="Student detail" actions={<PanelCloseAction onClick={close} />} />
        <PanelBody>...</PanelBody>
    </PanelContainer>
</PanelProvider>
```

### Reach for the fixed action components before building your own.

`PanelBackAction`, `PanelCloseAction` and the rest already carry the right icon, label and compact spacing; a custom `IconButton` for the same job risks a different icon or label than the rest of the system uses.

### Title the Panel with the object.

"Session · Mar 4", not "Details", so someone who opened it from elsewhere still knows.

### Offer "Open as page" in More.

For the step up when the quick look is not enough.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title Details with the record: "Ana Ruiz · Thu 4:00 PM". | "Details". |
| Name the filter by what it keeps: "Unread". | "Filter". |
| Give the empty state a way back: "Back to sessions". | "Nothing here". |
| Keep the disclaimer to one line. | Put instructions in the footer that belong in the body. |
| Name the footer's actions: "Discard" and "Save". | "OK" and "Done". |

## Accessibility

- Floating, the Panel is a complementary landmark named by its title, after the Page in reading order. Focus moves to its title on open and returns to the row, or the Bell, on close.
- Floating at a narrow width it is a dialog: focus is trapped, and Escape, a press outside or Close return it.
- The Frame closes the Panel on Escape unless an inner control handles it, such as an open menu.
- Up and Down are named "Previous" and "Next" and announce the record that opens.
- **`usePanelManager` outside a provider fails loudly.** Calling it without a `PanelProvider` ancestor throws, rather than silently falling back, so a missing provider is caught during development.
- An unread dot is paired with the text "unread" for a screen reader.

## Related

- Frame: use when the question is the AI panel, which is a Frame region.
- Section: use when a row or card opens in place inside its Section.
- Modal: use when the task needs full attention.
- Forms: use when the Panel edits a record.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules around a Panel: Navigation, Empty, Notifications.


The Panel components are the parts: header with its fixed actions, subheader, body, footer and disclaimer. The Frame hosts one, decides whether it docks or floats, and closes it on Escape. The template is its filled layout, one per type. The AI panel is the Frame's `panel`.

| Slot | Details | Notifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | The record's name, with its StatusTag under it | "Inbox" |
| `actions` | Edit, then Up, Down, More and Close | Mark all as read and Close |
| `backAction` · `titleIcon` | Optional, in the header before the title: a back action (`PanelBackAction`) and an icon. Pick the one the task needs. | None |
| `subheader` (`PanelSubheader`) | The record's StatusTag under the title | None: the Unread and All tabs sit under the header |
| `body` | Sections of the record; the form while editing | Items grouped by day, in Unread and All tabs |
| `footer` · `disclaimer` (`PanelFooter`, `PanelDisclaimer`) | Only while editing: Discard and Save, full bleed; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. The page composes it from Button. Planned as a prop. A `PanelDisclaimer` carries small print beside the actions. | None |
| Placement | Right. Docked from 1168; floating under it. Floating at every width is Planned. | Start, beside the Sidebar, 360 wide (`--inbox-width`), over the page with no Blanket. It opens from the Sidebar's bell, not from the Frame's Panel area. |
| Beside the AI panel | Planned. The Frame has one Panel area. | Planned. |

contextPages.intro: A floating layer that hangs off its trigger and closes on an outside click. Six types: menu, profile menu, select list, content, filter menu and stacked filter menu.
contextPages.name: Popup
contextPages.text:
# Popup

A floating layer that hangs off its trigger and closes on an outside click. Six types: menu, profile menu, select list, content, filter menu and stacked filter menu.

## Types

Each type composes the Popup component, which handles placement, outside clicks and Escape.

- **Menu.** Actions from a More button, at auto width. Applies on pick.
- **Profile menu.** From the account row: who is signed in, then links and Sign out. The 3-col width is Planned: today the menu hugs its rows.
- **Select list.** One list that applies as you pick: radios for one choice, checkboxes for several.
- **Content.** A preview or a short explanation. Anything wider is a Panel or a Modal.
- **Filter menu.** Two or three categories, held until Apply. Clear and Apply sit compact at the end.
- **Filter menu, stacked.** Four or more categories, or long lists, stacked at 3-col, or 4-col when the options need it. The categories scroll between the pinned header and footer.

## Anatomy

A filter menu off the Filter icon. Every part once; the layer is padded 16 and rounded 12 on the overlay pair.

1. **Trigger.** The control it hangs off. It shows the open state and, for the Filter icon, the count.
2. **Layer.** Hangs 4 below the trigger, aligned to the trigger's end edge because the trigger sits at the end of the bar. A titled layer's title is 14, whatever level the page around it is at.
3. **Rows or categories.** Menu rows; a list of checkboxes or radios; columns or stacked categories.
4. **Footer** (filter menu only). Clear (Subtle) and Apply (Default), compact, at the end. No Primary.

## Widths

Auto and the column steps of the screen grid, here at 1024. Auto follows the words: at least the trigger, 160 to 320. The steps follow the grid. The 2-col step, with a 200 floor, is Planned.

## Placement

Aligned to the edge of the trigger on the side where it sits. A trigger at the start of a bar, such as the view picker under page tabs, gets a layer aligned to its start edge. A trigger at the end, such as Filter or More, gets one aligned to its end edge. Both open 4 below.

## Key states

- **Long label.** A menu stops at 320. Past that a row ends in an ellipsis, and the full text opens in a Tooltip when clipped: Overflow. The Tooltip on a clipped row is Planned.

- **Loading a list.** One “Loading options” row, with no skeleton: Loading.

- **Load failed.** “Couldn't load options” with Retry; the menu stays open.

- **Flipped.** With no room below, the layer opens above the trigger and stays 8 from the screen edge.

- **Filter applied.** After Apply the menu closes and the count sits on the Filter icon's selected fill, read “Filters, 2 applied”. No tag row: Filtering.

## Sizes

| Width | 768 | 1024 | 1280 | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | 160 to 320 | 160 to 320 | 160 to 320 | Menus and select lists; at least the trigger |
| 2-col | 200 (floor) | 200 (floor) | about 224 | A short choice list, a small date or time picker |
| 3-col | 200 | 264 | 328 | A filter menu; the profile menu once DropdownMenu takes a width |
| 4-col | 261 | 347 | 432 | Content, and a stacked filter menu whose options need it; the cap |

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--popup-min-width`, `--popup-max-width` | 160, 320 | The auto range. |
| `--popup-offset`, `--popup-gap-screen` | 4, 8 | Below the trigger; from the screen edge. |
| `--popup-pad`, `--popup-radius` | 16, 12 | The layer's pad and its corner radius (12, `--popup-radius`). |
| `--dropdown-menu-max-height` | 320 | A menu's rows scroll past this height. |
| `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay` | pair | The layer's fill and its one edge, the shadow's ring. |
| `--layer-popup` | 400 | The layer's place in the stack. |

## Motion

## Slots

```jsx
import { Popup, DropdownMenu, PopupSelect, FilterMenu, IconButton } from '@/components';
```

Popup is the component: placement, offset, outside click and Escape. Each type is a composition on it: DropdownMenu for the menu and the profile menu, PopupSelect for one list, FilterMenu for several categories.

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `trigger` | The control it hangs off: an IconButton, a FilterButton, the labeled view trigger, the account row. |
| `placement` | `Popup` itself opens `top`. Under a bar, set `bottom-start` for a trigger at the start and `bottom-end` for one at the end; DropdownMenu and PopupSelect default to `bottom-start` and FilterMenu to `bottom-end`. It flips when there is no room. |
| `width` | `auto` (default) · `3-col` · `4-col`. |
| `width="2-col"` | Planned. The short-list step with a 200 floor. |
| `children` | Menu rows, a list, filter categories, or a short aside. |
| Filter footer | Clear and Apply, compact, at the end. It belongs to FilterMenu. |
| Profile menu width | Planned. DropdownMenu hugs its rows today; it takes the 3-col step once it takes a width. |
| Tooltip on a clipped row | Planned. The full text of a row that ends in an ellipsis. |

## Usage

Use a Popup for content anchored to a trigger that leaves on an outside click or Escape: a menu of actions, a list to pick from, the filter menu behind the Filter icon, the profile menu, a short aside. It brings no Blanket and the page stays usable.

| Type | Use when | Width | Applies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Menu | Choosing one action from a short list | auto | On pick |
| Select list | One category, picked as you go; the view picker under page tabs | auto | As you pick |
| Filter menu | Two or more categories applied together | 3-col; stacked, 3-col or 4-col | On Apply |
| Profile menu | The account row | auto today, 3-col once DropdownMenu takes a width | On pick |
| Content | A preview, a definition, a short explanation | 4-col at most | — |

## Alternatives

- For a decision before going on, use `Modal`.
- For content read alongside the page, use `Panel`.
- For one line that names a control, use `Tooltip`.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Hang a Popup 4 below its trigger, aligned to the trigger's edge on the side where it sits.

A trigger at the start of a bar, such as the view picker under page tabs, gets a layer aligned to its start edge; a trigger at the end, such as Filter or More, gets one aligned to its end edge. So it grows into the page and stays on it. It flips above when there is no room below and stays 8 from the screen edge.

Do: More sits at the end of the bar, so its menu aligns to its end edge and grows into the page.
Don't: An end trigger with a start-aligned menu: it runs off the edge of the page.

### Make a menu at least as wide as its trigger, from 160 up to 320.

It hugs the longest item. The width is set once, on open, so it holds still while someone types. A long or loading list opens at 320. A long row: Overflow.

Do: The menu is at least as wide as its trigger, so their edges line up.
Don't: A menu narrower than the trigger it hangs off: the edges no longer line up.

### Cap a Popup at 4-col, and keep it a short aside.

Anything wider or longer is a Panel or a Modal. Anything with inputs the person must finish, steps or a long scroll belongs in a Modal. An auto-width Popup grows past 320 only to match a trigger wider than 320, never for its content.

Do: A content Popup at 4-col, the cap, holding a short explanation.
Don't: A long read in a Popup: anything this long is a Panel or a Modal.

### Put fields the person must finish in a Modal.

An outside click closes a Popup and loses what was typed.

Do: Fields to finish go in a Modal, over its Blanket.
Don't: A form in a Popup: an outside click loses what was typed.

### Open one Popup at a time, each off its own trigger.

A confirm Modal may open over a Popup and brings its own Blanket. A Popup opened from a Modal sits above it; a Tooltip sits above everything.

Do: One flat menu; a choice with two forms is two rows.
Don't: A menu opening a second Popup beside it: two layers off one trigger.

### Leave the Blanket to the Modal.

A Popup floats on the overlay pair, `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, and the page behind it stays usable.

### Keep a menu's label short and move the detail to its description.

Start with the verb: "Reschedule", "Export notes". An option that waits on something says why in its description line, as visible text.

When a list applies, and the words Clear and Reset filters: Filtering.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| A menu label that starts with the verb: "Reschedule". | A sentence as the label. |
| A category title in a filter menu: "Grade", "Tutor". | "Filter by grade". |
| A Filter Tooltip that names the control: "Filters". | "Click to filter the table". |
| Say Clear in a menu: Clear, Apply. | "Reset" or "Reset filters" inside the menu. |

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries `aria-haspopup` and an `aria-expanded` that tracks the open state. A Filter icon's name says what is on: "Filters, 2 applied".
- A menu moves focus to its first row; Up and Down move, and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. A content Popup opened by a click or a key takes focus too: its first focusable element, or the popup itself when there is none. Tab reaches what is inside, and Escape or a click away returns focus to the trigger.
- A select list is a listbox or a group of checkboxes, and the chosen state is announced. The labeled view trigger reads "Status, Upcoming".
- In a filter menu, Clear and Apply are reachable after the categories. Apply announces the new count in words.
- A "Loading options" row is announced once, and "Couldn't load options" offers a Retry button.

## Related

- Section: use when placing the Filter icon, the view picker or More in the view bar.
- Modal: use when the content must be finished before going on.
- Panel: use when the content is wider than 4-col or outlives a click.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules around a Popup: Filtering, Overflow, Loading, Disabled.
- Popup: use when you need its props and states.

contextPages.intro: A span of the page grid under one heading: a header, a body, and an optional side, detail and footer. The header owns the title row, the views and the filters.
contextPages.name: Section
contextPages.text:
# Section

A span of the page grid under one heading: a header, a body, and an optional side, detail and footer. The header owns the title row, the views and the filters.

## Types

Each Section type combines a header and body, with an optional side or detail. These are starting layouts of the same component.

- **List.** The views alone, one table, paging. The default for an area page.
- **Detail.** A list with a detail that opens an item in place.
- **Cards.** Title and actions, a grid of cards three across.
- **Stats.** A row of cards, each one number and its label, four at most.
- **Details.** Label and value pairs in two columns, with Edit in the title row.
- **Main and side.** A split with the side at the end and no fill: facts beside the main content.
- **Form.** Fields in a card, with the card's own Save and Cancel at its bottom.
- **Subsections.** Sections nested one level, each an h3, for a long settings page.

## Anatomy

A Section with its header rows, a detail and a footer. The title, the first pill and the first column share one left edge.

1. **Title row.** The h2, an optional one-line description, and the actions at the end: More and the labeled Primary.
2. **Header rows** (optional). Row 2 holds the pill views at the start and the format switch at the end. Row 3 holds Search, then the filter triggers.
3. **Body.** A Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. A Table's head row follows the header rows with nothing between.
4. **Detail** (optional). An inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel` beside the list.
5. **Footer** (optional). Paging or "View all".

## Header rows

A starting set, picked by what the Section holds. Every control state lives on its component: Icon button, Filter button and Tabs. Which filters the header takes is Filtering; how the search field behaves is the Search pattern, listed in Patterns.

A header has up to three rows, all on one 32 line. Row 1 is the title with its actions: usually one Primary standing alone, with a `…` Icon button or a secondary button beside it. Row 2 is the views at the start and the format switch at the end. Row 3 is Search, then the filter triggers, each reading "Field: value". A Section with no views drops row 2 and the format switch moves to the end of row 3; one with nothing to search or filter drops row 3.

Every control in a header row is 32: Buttons, Icon buttons and Filter buttons at default spacing, Search and text fields at compact spacing. A Tag beside them is 20. Applied filters take the selected state, and the row ends with the count and Clear all. Three triggers show and the rest go in More filters with a count. Under 768 Search takes the row and the triggers fold into one Filter button with a count; the count and Clear all stay at the end of the Search row. When the triggers no longer fit beside Search they wrap to their own row, end-aligned. A trigger can open a list: give its `filters` entry a `menu` that hands the trigger to a Popup select or a Filter menu.

- **Full.** Title and actions, views and the format switch, then Search and three triggers.
- **Filters applied.** Applied triggers take the selected state; the row ends with the count and Clear all.
- **No views.** Row 2 goes; the format switch joins the end of row 3.
- **Views only.** Nothing to search or filter, so row 3 goes.
- **Many filters.** Three triggers show; the rest sit in More filters with a count.
- **Wrapped filters.** When the triggers do not fit beside Search they take their own row, end-aligned.
- **Rows selected.** The header stays; the table's head row becomes the bulk bar.
- **Narrow.** Search takes the row; the triggers fold into one Filter button with a count.
- **Subsection.** A smaller title; its primary acts on it alone.

## Side and detail

## Width behavior

Drag the width through 960 and 768. From 960 the filter side sits at the start. Below it the side hides and the Filter button returns with its count; pressing it gives the filters the Section's whole width, and "Show results" goes back. The title row and the header rows stay separate rows at every width.

## Key states

- **Empty, in a table.** The empty state replaces the whole table, column headers and footer too, and offers "Reset filters". The rule is the Empty pattern's.

Loading, errors and the search field follow their patterns and components: Loading, Errors and Search, listed in Patterns.

## Sizes

| Token | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| `--section-stack-sm` | Title row to header rows. |
| `--section-stack-md` | Header to body; body to footer. |
| `--section-stack-lg` | Between subsections. |
| `--section-min-width-main`, `--section-min-width-side` | The main and side columns of a split. |
| `--card-pad`, `--card-radius` | The detail, which is a sunken Card, on `--ds-surface-sunken`. |
| `--heading-md`, `--heading-sm` | A Section title and a subsection title. |

## Motion

## Slots

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `title` · `description` · `actions` | The title row. |
| `views` · `format` · `search` · `filters` · `count` | Rows 2 and 3 of the header: pill Tabs and the format switch, then a compact Search and the "Field: value" triggers. A `filters` entry takes an optional `menu`, `(trigger) => node`, that wraps its trigger in a Popup select or a Filter menu. |
| `header` · `type` | With `type="custom"` the `header` slot replaces the title and description; `title` stays as the visually hidden heading. `type` is `default` or `custom`, and is read from the slots when left off. |
| `isLoading` | Swaps the header for skeleton bars while the Section loads. |
| `level` | `page` makes the Section the page header: an h1, and the Sections it holds are h2s. Left off, the title is one level below what holds it. |
| `named` | Makes the Section a region named by its title, for one that stands apart as a landmark. |
| `onClearAll` · `onMoreFilters` · `onOpenFilters` | Clear all, More filters, and the Filter button of a narrow Section. |
| `id` · `className` · `style` | Passed to the Section's root. |
| `spacing` | `compact`, `default` or `spacious`: the space between the header, the body and the footer. |
| `children` | The body: a Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. |
| `layout="split"` · `side` | A second column at the end, for a summary. |
| `sidePlacement` | Planned. `start` puts the side first, for a filter side or a step rail. |
| `detail` · `detailTitle` · `detailDescription` · `detailFooter` | An inline expand that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel`. |
| `detailOpen` · `defaultDetailOpen` · `onDetailOpenChange` | Open state of the inline detail expand. |
| `footer` | Paging or "View all". |

The bulk bar lives in the Dynamic table's head row, through its `bulkActions`, and the Section holds nothing for it: Dynamic table.

## Usage

Use `Section` when content has a heading, shares actions, shows or hides as a unit, or takes its own span of the grid; otherwise the content belongs to the Section above it. The header is the Section's, not the Table's: the title row names it and carries its actions, and the header rows under it hold the views, then Search and the filters, so switching views can swap a table for cards while the rows stay put.

A Section takes no fill and no pad, and has five parts: header, body, side, detail and footer. The detail is an inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down.

## Alternatives

- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.
- For a queue page or a quick look at a row from a table, use `Panel`.
- For the page's own title, use `PageHeader`; a Section stands under it.

## Best practices

### Make a Section only when it earns one.

A Section earns its own heading, its own actions or its own place in the grid. When its heading would repeat its only card's title, drop the Section and let the card stand on its own.

Do: A card with its own title stands on its own in the page.
Don't: A Section whose heading repeats its only card's title: two headings for one thing.

### Put the title row first and the header rows under it.

The title row sits `--section-stack-sm` above the header rows, and the header sits `--section-stack-md` above the body. The title, the first pill's label and the first column's text share one left edge. Actions that do not fit beside the heading drop under it, still at the end of the row. At every width the two stay separate rows. In a narrow Section the filters fold into one Filter button and the views scroll sideways.

Do: The title row first, the header rows under it, sharing one left edge.
Don't: The title pushed into the views row: the heading and the pills fight for the start, and the description has nowhere to go.

### Give each action one home: the title row.

Actions sit at the end of the title row, More then the labeled Primary, whether or not the Section has views. The views row is for views and the format switch, the third for Search and filters, so an action there is a second home.

Do: The actions at the end of the title row, with the views under it.
Don't: Add students in the title row and again in the views row: one action, two homes.

### Keep views at the start as pills that hug their labels.

Views are a fixed set the product defines, and one pill stays even with one view. The strip stays on one line and scrolls sideways when the pills do not fit. Under page tabs, the views become one labeled PopupSelect, so the page keeps one tab system.

### Order the header: actions, then views and format, then Search and filters.

The title row ends with More, then the labeled Primary, which is last. The views row holds the views at the start and the format switch at the end. The filters row holds a compact `SearchField` (`spacing="compact"`, and `isCollapsible` where the row is tight), then the filter triggers; a trigger that opens a list takes a `menu`. More is an Icon button with a Tooltip. Fold extras into More.

Do: More and the labeled Primary in the title row; the format switch ends the views row; Search, then the filter, lead the filters row.
Don't: Five controls in no order, the Primary first, a second labeled button and a Filter icon in the title row: fold extras into More and give the filter its own row.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected.

The part-ticked select-all, the count of selected rows, then the actions, all at the start. The checkboxes clear the selection, so the bar carries no Cancel. Selected rows take the selected fill and the header rows stay put. Only the Dynamic table selects rows.

### Drop the Filter icon while a filter side shows.

Each control has one home. The Filter button returns with its count once the side hides, below `SECTION_DETAIL_FLOOR`.

### Use a Section detail as an inline expand, never on a queue page.

A **Section detail** is an inline expand: a row or card opens in place inside its Section and pushes the content below it down. It is never the detail view on a queue page — a queue page docks a `Panel` beside the list instead, and the record opens on demand.

### Keep the footer for paging and "View all".

Actions that commit changes belong in the card or form that holds the fields.

Do: The form card holds its own Save; the Section footer is for paging and "View all".
Don't: Cancel and Save in the Section footer, away from the fields they commit.

### Give a part a fill with a Card, not a Section.

A padded box with a fill is a Card. A Section takes no fill and no pad, so a part that stands apart from its neighbor, such as a detail, is a sunken Card.

### Nest a Section once at most.

A subsection is an h3. A Section that already has views holds subsections without them.

The table's empty state replaces the whole table, by the Empty pattern; elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the Section with what it holds, in sentence case: "Upcoming sessions". | A title that repeats the only card inside it. |
| Keep the description to one line: "Lincoln Middle · 24 students". | A paragraph under the title. |
| Name views by the rows they show: "All students", "Needs follow-up". | Views of different things in one strip. |
| Name the scope in Search: "Search students". | A bare "Search". |

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading whose level follows nesting: h2 for a Section, h3 for a subsection. With a custom header the title stays in the page, hidden from sight.
- The pill views are a tablist; the selected tab says which rows the body shows. Views swap in place.
- Search, the filter triggers and More carry their names: "Search students", "Status: Upcoming", "More section actions". A trigger's selected state is announced as pressed.
- The table announces a selection politely, "2 selected", and the bulk bar's actions follow the select-all checkbox in the tab order.
- The detail is a collapsible region named by its title: the disclosure button toggles it with Enter or Space, and Escape inside the open detail closes it and returns focus to the button.

## Related

- Page: use when the heading is the page's own.
- Panel: use when a queue page docks the Panel beside the list, or for a quick look from a table.
- Popup: use when choosing the menu the labeled view trigger (`PopupSelect`) or a filter trigger opens.
- Table: use when the body is rows and columns.
- Filtering: use when picking a filter tier for the header.
- Patterns: use when the question is the search field's behavior (Search) or an empty body (Empty).

`StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` and `TreeTable` are the components for the three table kinds; the template takes any of them.

The examples on this page follow the toolbar's Color mode switch.

## Appearance

## State

## Interactive playground

## Motion

## Usage

A table sits in a Section and spans it. Its first and last cells sit flush with the section edge. The Section header carries the views, then Search and the "Field: value" filters, and once a filter is applied, the record count. The bulk bar is never in the Section header: while rows are selected, a Dynamic table's head row becomes it, so the header rows stay put. Empty and no results replace the whole table so the Section header stays usable; loading and error states happen inside the table, under its header. Paging stays under the rows, inside the same Section.

### Type guidance

Choose by what people do with the rows. Read the questions in order and stop at the first yes.

| Question | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Does any row nest under another? Nesting wins, even when the table is interactive. | Tree table |
| Can people act on the table: sort, filter, select, page, expand rows or use row actions? | Dynamic table |
| Otherwise, people only read it. | Static table |

Search, filters and actions sit in the Section header: `<Table title="Students" views={...} search={...} filters={[...]} count="340 students" kind="dynamic" tableProps={...} />`. Pass the table as `children` instead of `kind` when you build it yourself.

## Parts

1. **Head row.** Names the columns. Its rule is the bold border.
2. **Rows.** The data you pass as `tbody`. Each draws a thin rule, and there is no zebra striping.
3. **Footer** (optional). The `footer` slot under the rows, aligned to the end: the range, the page-size Select and Pagination. The template draws no default footer: the slot is the contract. On a narrow screen its parts wrap onto lines of their own, and the pager stays at the end. It hides while the empty state shows. A Dynamic or Tree table draws its own footer and empty state, so the template's `footer`, `emptyState` and `empty` are for a Static table.
4. **Empty state.** The `emptyState` slot, which replaces the whole table (head row, caption and footer included) when `empty` is true; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally.

### States

Row states are layered over each cell's fill, never swapped for it.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill of its own: the table shows what it sits on. |
| Hovered | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Focused | A scroll region takes keyboard focus and draws the `--ds-border-focused` ring. |
| Disabled | A table has no disabled state. Disable the controls in a row. |
| Selected | A row with `aria-selected="true"` takes `--ds-background-selected` across the whole row, with `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps and no stripe on its leading edge. |
| Empty | The empty state replaces the whole table; no head row or footer stays. |

### Tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-border`, `--border-width-default` | color, 1 | The rule under each row. |
| `--ds-border-bold` | color | The rule under the head row. |
| `--ds-text`, `--body-default` | 14/20 | Body cells. |
| `--ds-text-subtle`, `--heading-xxs` | color, type | Head cells, message rows, and empty-state wrapper text. |
| `--table-pad-x-cell`, `--table-pad-y-cell` | length | Cell padding, message row padding, and plain empty-state wrapper padding. |
| Footer slot (Table template): `--table-inline`, `--table-footer-height` | 8, 48 | The gap between the table and the footer slot, the gap between controls in the footer, and the footer row height. |
| `--table-empty-surface`, `--table-empty-radius` | color, 16 | The sunken background and card-rounded corners of the empty state box. |
| `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`, `-pressed` | color | A hovered and a pressed row. |
| `--ds-background-selected`, `-hovered`, `-pressed` | color | A selected row. |
| `--ds-shadow-overflow` | shadow | A sticky edge, only while content is scrolled under it. |
| `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` | color | The fill of sticky cells, so they match what the table sits on. |
| `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` | focus ring | The ring of a scroll region. |
| `--row-height-md` | 40 | The least height of the message row. |
| Footer the shell draws (Dynamic/Tree): `--stack-md`, `--stack-sm` | 8, 4 | Gap between a Dynamic or Tree table and the footer it draws itself, and inside message and empty-state wrappers. |

## Best practices

### Put a plain table in a Section.

Do: The table spans the Section under its header: no frame, no card, no padding of its own.
Don't: The table sits inside its own frame with padding; it stops lining up with the Section and the Section header.

### Put nothing between the header and the head row.

Do: Search and filters live in the Section header rows, with the record count once a filter is applied; the head row follows directly.
Don't: A second toolbar sits between the Section header and the head row; the table has no toolbar of its own.

### One table per block.

Never mix a Static, Dynamic or Tree table in one Section either.

Do: One table per Section, with its own header, so people always know which rows its Search and filters act on.
Don't: Two tables share one Section and one header; search and filters no longer say which table they act on.

### Use a Dynamic table for rows people act on.

Do: A roster people act on as a Dynamic table: sortable heads, checkboxes, a pager, and bulk actions in the head row while rows are selected.
Don't: A roster people act on as a Static table; with no sort, selection or paging, 340 students become one long scroll.

### Use a Tree table for a hierarchy.

Do: Classes nest under their school and students under their class; each level indents and keeps the columns.
Don't: A hierarchy faked with expandable rows: the classes and students lose their columns and can't be sorted or selected.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name every column with a short head, in sentence case: "Last session". | A blank head, or one in all caps. |
| Give the count in words in the header once a filter is applied: "340 students". | A count in the head row or under the table. |
| An empty message that says what will appear and the first action: "No members yet", "Invite a member". | An empty table body with no message. |

## Accessibility

- Name every column with a head cell. Head cells are labels for a column, so they use Heading/xxs rather than a heading level.
- Mark the sorted column with `aria-sort`, and give every icon-only control a name, such as "Actions for Ava Thompson".
- Mark a selected row with `aria-selected="true"`. That attribute belongs to a row of a table with `role="grid"`.
- Selection is never color alone. The row's checkbox is checked, and the head row says "2 selected".
- A region that scrolls takes keyboard focus, so people can scroll it without a pointer. That covers a region with `maxHeight` and one with a sticky column.
- When empty, the empty state replaces the table with no table roles left behind, and keeps the table's accessible name when one was provided.
- Name the table with its `label`, or `label` on the template for the empty state box, when no caption names it.

## Related

- Section: the header rows that sit above every table.
- Static table, Dynamic table and Tree table: the three table components the template takes.
- Pagination: the pager that fills the footer slot.
- Card: a table never sits inside a card.

# Accessibility

The rules every PLUS screen meets, built into the tokens and patterns.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Accessibility.mdx`

## Overview

WCAG 2.1 AA is the minimum bar for every PLUS screen. Tutors use PLUS on laptops during live sessions, often while sharing their screen with a student, so a screen stays legible at any zoom level and works under assistive technology.

Each foundation page owns the rules for its subject: contrast in [Color](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-color--docs), heading levels in [Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-typography--docs#foundation-heading-levels), the focus ring in [Border](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-border--docs#foundation-focus-ring) and [Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-radius--docs#foundation-focus-ring), and reduced motion in [Motion](?path=/docs/foundations-expression-motion-physics--docs#foundation-reduced-motion). Each component page adds the rules for its own name, role and keyboard behavior.

## Heading levels

Every page's outline starts with one `h1`, and a heading's tag is its place in the outline, never its size. A page whose name sits only in the Sidebar or a tab strip still has an `h1`, hidden visually with `VisuallyHidden` (never `display: none`). [Typography](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-typography--docs#foundation-heading-levels) and [Page](?path=/docs/templates-page--docs) own the outline rules.

## Contrast

Text clears 4.5:1 and icons, borders and the focus ring clear 3:1 against what they sit on, in light and dark (7:1 and 4.5:1 under increased contrast). Each text and icon token pairs with a surface or fill. Never put a neutral text token on a bold fill, or an inverse token on a surface; [Color](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-color--docs) shows every measured pair.

## Focus

Focus is shown by the focus ring, never by a fill: the control's fill and opacity stay unchanged. The ring is the same on every interactive element, including cards, table rows and list items. [Border](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-border--docs#foundation-focus-ring) owns the ring's color, width and offset, and [Radius](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-radius--docs#foundation-focus-ring) owns its corner.

### Focus in overlays

Opening a `Modal` or a floating `Panel` moves focus inside it and keeps Tab there; closing it returns focus to the control that opened it. Both do this themselves, and a new overlay gets the same behavior by building on Base UI.

## Keyboard

Every interactive element can be reached and operated from the keyboard.

- Tab order follows the visual reading order: left to right, top to bottom.
- Widgets follow standard keyboard patterns: arrow keys move through a menu or radio group, and Escape closes an overlay.
- New interactive behavior is built on [Base UI](?path=/docs/tech-stack-base-ui--docs) (`@base-ui/react`), which supplies these patterns.

## Screen readers

- Use semantic elements first (`button`, `nav`, `main`, `table`), and ARIA only when no element fits.
- Name any control that has no visible text with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.
- Announce content that changes without a page load through a live region (`role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"`), as the `Table` bulk-action count does.

## Disabled

A disabled component keeps its label so people can tell what is unavailable. [Color](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-color--docs) owns how disabled looks, and [Disabled](?path=/docs/patterns-states-disabled--docs) owns when to use it.

- Disabled elements are not focus targets, and none uses `aria-disabled` to stay focusable.
- State the reason a field or option is disabled in visible text beside it at full contrast, never in a tooltip on the disabled control.
- Keep submit actions enabled and explain what is missing when pressed; disable a button only while it is sending.

## Forms

[Forms](?path=/docs/patterns-forms--docs) and [Errors](?path=/docs/patterns-states-errors--docs) own form layout and validation.

- Every field has a visible label tied to its control: a field that renders its own label wires `htmlFor` to the control's `id` itself, and `Select` and `DatePicker` render none, so the form supplies it.
- An error states what went wrong and how to fix it on the field through `errorMessage`.
- A required field sets `aria-required` (or native `required`) regardless of visual markers; the form marks only the minority case in plain text on the label — "(optional)" when most fields are required, "(required)" when most are optional.
- Related fields sit in a `Fieldset`, which renders a `fieldset` and its `legend`.

## Charts

Every chart describes its type, axes, series and points to screen readers, and its data can be read from the keyboard. A chart is a labeled group inside its section, not a landmark of its own. Give every chart a title or label, and never carry a series by color alone; see [Chart color](?path=/docs/data-visualizations-color--docs).

## Automated checks

Every story runs axe in the Storybook test suite, and a story may not add a violation, so a component that breaks a rule here is caught before it ships.

## Do and don't

### Show focus with a ring

The control's fill stays as it is.

### Never carry meaning in color alone

Pair a status color with an icon and a word.

# Border

A border is a width token paired with a color token.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Border.mdx`

## Overview

Borders mark a boundary, separate neighbors and show state. The width token sets how heavy the line is and the color token says what it means, so always choose them as a pair.

```css
border-width: var(--border-width-default);
border-width: var(--border-width-selected);
border-width: var(--border-width-focused);
```

Figma holds `Border/default`, `Border/selected` and `Border/focused` in `spacing / semantics`, paired with `color/border/*` in `color / semantics`.

## Width tokens

Three widths cover every border. Pick by what the line says, never by how heavy you want it to look. Values are indicative; the tokens are the contract.

- `--border-width-default` (Border/default): Every standard border and divider: field edges, table lines, section rules.
- `--border-width-selected` (Border/selected): The chosen option in a group: an active tab, a selected tile or row.
- `--border-width-focused` (Border/focused): The focus ring that shows keyboard users where they are.

## Pair width with color

Take both width and color from this table.

| Width | Color | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/default` | Edges and dividers that only separate. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/input` | A field’s outline. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/danger` | An invalid field. |
| `Border/default` | `color/border/disabled` | A disabled control. |
| `Border/selected` | `color/border/selected` | The selected option in a group. |
| `Border/focused` | `color/border/focused` | The focus ring. Use `color/border/focused/inverse` on a dark surface. |

## Focus ring

The focus ring shows keyboard users where they are. It is a ring, never a fill: a filled field looks selected or disabled.

| Fact | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Width | 2 px, `--border-width-focused` |
| Distance | 2 px away from the control (`--focus-ring-width`) |
| Color | `color/border/focused` (`--ds-border-focused`); `color/border/focused/inverse` on a dark surface |
| Radius | The control’s radius plus 2 px. Radius owns the pairs. |
| Containers | Cards and modals draw no ring of their own |

Do: The field keeps its fill and gains the ring.

Don't: A filled field reads as selected and hides what is typed.

## Selected states

A selected option, active tab or chosen tile takes `Border/selected` (2 px) in `color/border/selected` on every side, paired with a second cue such as a check or a fill. State and emphasis use the whole shape, never a colored stripe on one edge.

## Dividers

- Space comes first. Add a 1 px line (`Border/default` in `color/border/default`) only when spacing alone does not separate two groups.
- A horizontal rule spans the content width of its container. A vertical rule sits between controls and takes their height.
- A heavier or colored line is a state, not a divider.

## Borders in patterns

Take pattern borders from this table rather than adding one of your own.

| Pattern | Line | Token | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Table | Grid lines and the head rule | `color/border/default` · `color/border/bold` | The selected row fills the whole row with color/background/selected. The checkbox is the second cue. |
| Docked sidebar | One 1 px divider on the edge that faces the Page | `color/border/default` | The Page carries no border of its own. |
| Banner | None | — | Meaning comes from the fill and the icon. |
| Card | None | — | The edge comes from elevation, not a border. |

### Give the sidebar one edge and the page header none

The sidebar ends in a 1 px divider in `color/border/default`. The page header has no border.

Do: One hairline on the sidebar edge.

Don't: A line under the page header adds a second edge the Frame does not use.

## Do and don't

### Show selection with the whole outline

A selected row takes the 2 px selected border on every side, in `color/border/selected`.

Do: The 2 px outline wraps the whole row.

Don't: A colored stripe on one edge marks nothing the system recognizes. Use the full outline, a fill or an icon.

### Use the selected width only for selection

`Border/default` is the width for everything that is not a state.

Do: Resting rows and cards keep Border/default.

Don't: The 2 px width on a resting row reads as selected, so users cannot tell what is chosen.

## Accessibility

- A border that is the only cue for a control's edge clears 3:1 against its surround (WCAG 1.4.11). Use `color/border/input` for fields.
- The focus ring is the one signal for keyboard focus and clears 3:1 against what it sits on.
- Selection never rests on color alone: the 2 px width is the second cue beside `color/border/selected`.
- A subtle accent background needs an accent border to reach 3:1 against the surface.

# Color

Every color is a --ds token named for its job.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Colors.mdx`

## Overview

Every color is a semantic token named for the job it does: page text, field edge, or primary button fill. Each token resolves per mode, so components adapt to light, dark and increased contrast automatically.

```css
color: var(--ds-text-danger);
background: var(--ds-background-danger-subtler);
```

Figma holds them in `color / semantics` (modes Light, Dark, Light IC and Dark IC); `color / primitives` stay hidden. See Tokens: Color for the full collection.

## How the tokens are built

Primitives hold raw ramps and stay hidden; bind only semantic tokens. Names read from general to specific: property, role, emphasis, state. In Figma, parts join with slashes (`color/background/danger/bold/hovered`); in CSS, drop `color` and join with dashes behind `--ds-` (`--ds-background-danger-bold-hovered`).

| Part | In `color/background/danger/bold/hovered` | Values | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| color | Namespace | `color` | Dropped in CSS. Surface and shadow tokens start with elevation. |
| background | Property | `text` · `icon` · `border` · `background` · `link` · `surface` · `shadow` · `blanket` · `skeleton` · `interaction` · `chart` | What the color paints. |
| danger | Role | `brand` · `neutral` · `selected` · `input` · `inverse` · `disabled` · `focused` · `danger` · `warning` · `success` · `information` · `discovery` · `accent-*` · `competency-*` | What it means. Omitted for default neutral. |
| bold | Emphasis | `subtlest` · `subtler` · `subtle` · (default) · `bold` · `bolder` · `boldest` | Contrast against the surface. |
| hovered | State | `hovered` · `pressed` · `visited` | Interactive backgrounds and links only. |

`--ds-border-<role>-subtle` is the pale edge of an outlined label, such as a Tag or a date Status.

## Modes

PLUS ships four modes: light and dark, each at standard and increased contrast. `auto` follows OS `prefers-color-scheme` and `prefers-contrast`.

- **Dark mode** is not light inverted: raised and overlay surfaces step lighter as they rise, because shadows are subtle on dark grounds. Design in dark mode by choosing the same token; never map your own values.
- **Increased contrast** pushes text to 7:1 and borders, icons and the focus ring to 4.5:1. Tints, surfaces and the Blanket stay unchanged.
- **In code**, set `data-color-mode` (`light`, `dark`, `auto`) and `data-contrast-mode` (`no-preference`, `more`, `auto`) on `<html>`. No attribute means light at standard contrast.
- **In Figma**, set the frame mode to Light, Dark, Light IC or Dark IC.

## Roles

Pick the role for the intention, then the emphasis. Never pick a role by how the hue looks or by a matching value: a danger fill, its border and its icon are three tokens even when two of them share a value today.

| Role | Default fill | Text | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `neutral` | `--ds-background-neutral` | `--ds-text-subtle` | Default text, secondary buttons and navigation. |
| `brand` | `--ds-background-brand-bold` | `--ds-text-brand` | Primary actions and brand marks. |
| `information` | `--ds-background-information-bold` | `--ds-text-information` | Informative UI or work in progress. |
| `success` | `--ds-background-success-bold` | `--ds-text-success` | A completed or favorable outcome, such as a booked session. |
| `warning` | `--ds-background-warning-bold` | `--ds-text-warning` | Caution before a mistake happens. Bold warning uses --ds-text-warning-inverse. |
| `danger` | `--ds-background-danger-bold` | `--ds-text-danger` | Errors or destructive actions, such as a failed payment. |
| `discovery` | `--ds-background-discovery-bold` | `--ds-text-discovery` | New features, onboarding or a Suggestion. |
| `accent` | `--ds-background-accent-teal-subtle` | `--ds-text-accent-teal` | Categorization without status meaning. |
| `inverse` | — | `--ds-text-inverse` | Text, icons and borders on bold backgrounds. |
| `input` | `--ds-background-input` | `--ds-text` | Form fields. |

Danger, warning, success, information and discovery each ship four emphasis levels: default tint for a Banner, `subtler` for a Status tag, `subtle` for a non-interactive Tag, and `bold` for a filled Count tag or button.

## Accent hues

Eleven hues decorate tags, charts, avatars and illustrations. An accent hue carries no status meaning; when color carries meaning, use a role.

## Competency areas

The five competency areas each have their own role (`social-emotional` orange, `mastering-content` teal, `advocacy` lime, `relationship` magenta, `technology-tools` brown): `background/competency/<subject>` with `text/competency/<subject>` and `border/competency/<subject>` for a Tag, `subtle` for illustration bodies, and `bold` for filled marks. Use a competency color only for its area.

## Surfaces and border

| Token | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `--ds-surface` | The page |
| `--ds-surface-sunken` | Grouped grounds: sidebar column, sunken well |
| `--ds-surface-raised` | Cards, paired with `--ds-shadow-raised` |
| `--ds-surface-overlay` | Modals, menus, popups, tooltips and flags, paired with `--ds-shadow-overlay` |
| `--ds-border` | Standard dividers; `--ds-border-bold` bounds controls |

A surface lifts by shadow, never by a different gray. Surface levels and shadows are owned by Elevation; stroke widths and the focus ring are owned by Border.

## States

Hover and press step along the token's own ladder. Focus is always a ring, never a fill (Border). AI color tokens live on AI UI › Color.

- **Rows, menu items and sidebar items** take `color/background/neutral/subtle/hovered` and `/pressed`.
- **Selected elements** take `color/background/selected` (`selected/hovered` and `/pressed` on interaction), paired with a second cue such as a check mark or border. Never use brand, link or focused tokens for selection. Keep selected and focused distinct: selected persists to show a current choice, focus shows where the keyboard is, and a selected item stays recognizable while hovered or pressed.
- **Fields** take `color/background/input/hovered` with `color/border/input` on hover; on focus they keep their fill and add the focus ring.
- **Icons** have no hovered or pressed color tokens; show interaction with a subtle neutral background behind the icon.
- **Avatars and images** whose fill cannot change use `color/interaction/hovered` and `color/interaction/pressed` overlays.

```css
.my-element:hover {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered);
}
.my-element:active {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed);
}
.my-element.is-selected {
  background-color: var(--ds-background-selected);
}
```

## Partner pairs and contrast

Every foreground token pairs with a ground that clears WCAG AA across all four modes: 4.5:1 for text (7:1 in IC) and 3:1 for icons, borders and the focus ring (4.5:1 in IC).

- **Bold fills** take `color/text/inverse` and `color/icon/inverse`, except bold warning which takes dark `color/text/warning/inverse`.
- **Status tints** take the role's text token, or its `-bolder` step on `-subtler` and `-subtle` grounds.
- **Surfaces** take `color/text/default`, `subtle` or `subtlest`.
- Never carry meaning by color alone: a status has an icon or a word, and a chart has a legend or direct labels. Use 3:1 for UI essential to understanding.

## Data-viz color

Charts use `--chart-*` tokens (`chartPalette` from `@/components`). Never reach for an accent hue or a UI role token to draw a series. Color is the one foundation with chart rules of its own; charts take spacing, radius, elevation, stroke, type, layers and motion from the same component tokens as the rest of the system.

| Job | What it encodes | Tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One series | Single measure | `--chart-brand`; reference line takes `--chart-neutral` |
| Categorical | Distinct series | `--chart-categorical-1` to `-8`, in order |
| Sequential | Magnitude | One hue from `subtler` to `bold`, `bolder`, `boldest` (darkest = largest) |
| Diverging | Direction from a baseline | Two hues around `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler` (orange and blue by default; never red and green) |
| Status | On track, at risk, off track | `--chart-success`, `-warning`, `-danger`, `-information`, `-discovery` (plus `-bold` for the more extreme level) |
| SMART subject | SMART area | `--chart-smart-<subject>` |

- Use five or six categories at most and group the rest into "Other".
- Never mix categorical and status colors in one chart, and give every series or state a second cue (label, shape, pattern, icon or backing table).
- Titles, axes, gridlines, tooltips and threshold lines wear text and border tokens, never a chart color.

### Categorical order

Assign series in slot order without skipping.

| Slot | Hue | Light | Dark | Light IC | Dark IC |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 (brand) | lagoon | 600 | 500 | 850 | 300 |
| 2 | orange | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |
| 3 | blue | 500 | 500 | 800 | 300 |
| 4 | magenta | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |
| 5 | lime | 500 | 400 | 800 | 250 |
| 6 | purple | 700 | 700 | 900 | 500 |
| 7 | orange | 500 | 500 | 800 | 300 |
| 8 | blue | 800 | 700 | 1000 | 500 |

Three rules govern this sequence:

- **Brand leads:** slot 1 is lagoon (`--chart-brand`), so a one-series chart and the first series of a multi-series chart share their lead color.
- **Neighbors alternate light and dark steps:** slot 2 (orange-800) sits between slot 1 (lagoon-600) and slot 3 (blue-500), alternating through slot 6 so adjacent series remain distinct in grayscale and under color-vision deficiency.
- **Hues spread across the wheel:** lagoon, orange, blue, magenta, lime and purple never place two adjacent slots in the same hue family. Yellow (warning), red (danger) and teal (too close to brand) stay out; lime and purple-500 double as success and discovery, which is why categorical and status colors never mix.
- **Overflow and dark mode:** slots 7 and 8 reprise orange and blue for overflow past six series. Dark mode steps one lighter except blue (3) and orange (7), which hold at 500 to preserve lightness alternation, and purple (6), which holds at 700 so it does not crowd its neighbors.

### Separators, ramps, SMART subjects and hover

- **Separators:** keep a gap or `--ds-border-inverse` line where marks touch (stacked bars, histogram bins, waterfall steps). Lightness alternation identifies the series; the separator marks the boundary.
- **Sequential and diverging ramps:** sequential runs `--ds-background-accent-<hue>-subtler` through `--chart-<hue>-bold`, `-bolder` and `-boldest` (strongest tone = largest value). Diverging runs two hues around `--ds-background-accent-gray-subtler` (orange and blue by default; never red and green).
- **SMART subjects:** each subject uses the emphasis that keeps S-M-A-R-T neighbors apart: social-emotional orange (`bold`), mastering content teal (`boldest`), advocacy lime (`bold`), relationship magenta (`boldest`), technology tools brown (`bold`). Label directly or keep the legend beside the chart.
- **Labels and hover:** place labels beside marks; when a label must sit on a fill (heatmap cell, stacked segment), use `--ds-text` or `--ds-text-inverse`. Hovered marks take their `-hovered` token, and unselected series fade with `--ds-opacity-disabled`.

## Chart order, targets and ranges

Sort categories from most to least (an ordinal set such as grades takes one hue ramp), put the strongest tone on the largest value, and mark targets and ranges without shading bands or repeating tooltip numbers beside the bar.

### Sort biggest first and darken with the value

Students by grade in the tutoring cohort.

Do: Biggest at the top, darkest tone on the biggest value.
Don't: Grades in any order, one tone; the eye has to read every number to find the biggest.

### Mark the target with a tick and the range with an outline

Attendance for one class against a 90% target.

Do: A green tick at 90 and a green outline on the track.
Don't: A shaded band and a value beside the bar; the band hides the bar's own end and the text repeats the tooltip.

## Disabled

Disabled is a dedicated color token (`color/text/disabled`, `color/background/disabled`, `color/border/disabled`), not an opacity fade. `--ds-opacity-disabled` is reserved for dimmed images and de-emphasized chart series. State the reason a control is disabled in nearby text (see Accessibility).

### Disable with color tokens

The Reschedule button after the session has ended.

Do: Disabled takes color/text/disabled on color/background/disabled.
Don't: Opacity on the primary button; it still looks clickable and the gray is not the system one.

## Links

Links take `color/link/default` (`--ds-link`, with `--ds-link-pressed` on press and no hovered color step). Underline links in running text at rest and on hover; standalone navigation links, menus, buttons and card titles may omit the underline. Never use brand, selected or focused colors for a link.

### Underline links in running text

Do: Link color and underline together.
Don't: The color alone is too close to the body text, so the link is easy to miss.

## Pattern colors

| Pattern | Part | Tokens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tile | Rest · hovered · selected | `color/background/neutral/subtle` · `…/subtle/hovered` · `color/background/selected` with `color/border/selected` |
| Input | Field · edge · placeholder · helper | `color/background/input` · `color/border/input` · `color/text/subtlest` · `color/text/subtle` |
| Progress and meter | Track · fill | `color/background/neutral` · `color/background/brand/bold` (success or warning bold for status) |
| Empty state | Icon · message | `color/icon/subtlest` · `color/text/subtle` |
| Skeleton | Blocks | `color/skeleton/default` · `color/skeleton/subtle` |
| Table | Grid lines · head rule · selected row | `color/border/default` · `color/border/bold` · `color/background/selected` across the whole row |
| Sidebar item | Hovered · selected | `color/background/neutral/subtle/hovered` · `color/background/selected` with `color/text/selected` and `color/icon/selected` |

## Do and don't

### Use the right role

Pick the role for the job. A failed payment is danger; an accent has no meaning, so it should not carry one.

Do: Danger for a failed payment.
Don't: A purple accent where the color has semantic meaning.

### Pair text with its ground

Take the text color from the same role as the ground. Gray text on a bold ground falls well below 4.5:1 in both modes.

Do: Danger text on the subtle danger ground.
Don't: Gray text on the bold danger ground; the role is right and the pair is wrong.

### Use inverse tokens on bold backgrounds

On a bold fill, text and icons take `color/text/inverse` and `color/icon/inverse` (`color/text/warning/inverse` on bold warning).

Do: color/text/inverse on a bold danger fill.
Don't: color/text/default on a bold fill loses contrast.

### Show focus with a ring, never a fill

A filled field looks selected or disabled. The focus ring is the one signal for keyboard focus.

Do: The field keeps its fill and gains the focus ring, color/border/focused.
Don't: A brand fill on the field to show focus; it reads as a selected value and hides what is typed.

### Keep selected and focused distinct

Selection uses the selected tokens and another cue such as a check mark. The focus ring is only for keyboard focus.

Do: Selected tokens plus a check mark.
Don't: The focus ring used to mean selected.

### One series, one color

A single series is drawn in the brand chart color. Reaching for the categorical set makes a legend that says nothing.

Do: Five weeks of one measure, all in color/chart/brand.
Don't: A rainbow on one measure suggests five series; the color does no job, and a reader looks for a legend that is not there.

## Accessibility

- Foreground/background partner pairs clear WCAG 2.1 AA in all four modes: 4.5:1 for text smaller than 24 px (1.4.3) and 3:1 for essential UI, icons, borders, the focus ring and text 24 px or larger (1.4.11), rising to 7:1 and 4.5:1 in increased contrast.
- Never convey meaning by color alone: pair status colors with an icon or text, selection with a check mark or 2 px border, and chart series with labels, shapes or a table.
- Warning icons and borders use `color/icon/warning` and `color/border/warning` rather than the yellow fill (2.87:1 on the darkest surface) so they clear 3:1.
- Check new screens in all four modes with the toolbar's Color mode and Contrast switches, and see Accessibility for cross-cutting rules.

# Language

How we write every word, for everyone PLUS reaches.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ContentLanguage.mdx`

## Words

Use the word a tutor would say out loud.

### Pick everyday words

Verbs over nouns. Short words over long ones.

Do: A verb the reader can act on.
Don't: Correct, but “availability” is an abstract noun to decode.

### Spell out team terms

New tutors don’t know our shorthand yet. Write the full name.

Do: Clear on day one.
Don't: Fine for a lead tutor; a new tutor has to ask.

| Say | Not |
| --- | --- |
| session | meeting, class |
| call off | cancel |
| fill-in | sub |
| lead tutor | TA, captain |
| reflection | survey |
| student | kid, tutee |

## People

PLUS reaches students, families and schools who never open the app. Write so every one of them is included.

### Describe the work

Say what a student is learning. Leave out labels about who they are.

Do: Specific, and it points forward.
Don't: True, but it labels Leo and doesn’t say which skill.

### Don’t assume a household

Families look different. So do devices and quiet rooms.

Do: Works for every family.
Don't: Close, but leaves out a grandparent or older sibling.

### Show the least you need

On shared screens, first name and last initial. No names in research exports.

Do: Enough to find her.
Don't: Fine in a private record; too much on a projected screen.

## Sentences

### Say who acted

Name the person behind a change. Passive voice hides them.

Do: The tutor knows who to thank or ask.
Don't: Fine in a tight flag; in a notice, it hides who decided.

### Write as “we” and “you”

PLUS is “we”. The reader is “you”. Use contractions.

Do: A promise from someone.
Don't: Accurate, but no one is making the promise.

## Mechanics

One way to write each thing, so every screen reads the same.

| Topic | Rule | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capitalization | Sentence case everywhere | Open session notes |
| Punctuation | No period in titles, buttons or labels. No exclamation marks in errors. | Reflection submitted |
| Numbers | Digits in the UI. Spell out one to nine in a sentence. | 3 sessions left |
| Dates | Shortest clear format. Add the year only in records. | Wed, Nov 13 |
| Times | 12-hour, with the time zone | 3:30 PM ET |
| Ranges | En dash, no spaces | 3:30–4:15 PM ET |
| Recent | Relative under a week, then the date | 10 min ago · Yesterday · Nov 4 |
| School calendar | Terms, not quarters | Fall term |

### Always add the time zone

Tutors and schools sit in different zones.

Do: Means the same thing everywhere.
Don't: Reads fine, until a tutor in another zone joins an hour late.

# Messages

What to say when something happens.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ContentMessages.mdx`

## Anatomy

Every message has the same three parts.

| Part | What it says | Length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Title | What happened. | 2 to 5 words |
| Body | Why, and what it means for the reader. | 1 or 2 sentences |
| Action | A verb that says what the button does. | One verb |

## Choose a type

Pick by what the reader needs. Each type has a home component.

| Type | When | Component |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Error | Something failed and the reader can act | Flag, Section message, Inline message |
| Warning | Before a step that’s hard to undo | Modal, Section message |
| Success | A task finished | Flag |
| Info | Context that helps, then gets out of the way | Banner, Section message |
| Empty state | Nothing to show yet | Empty state |
| Feature discovery | Something new and useful | Spotlight |

## Writing each type

### Errors: reassure, then fix

Say what broke, what’s safe, and the next step.

Do: Answers the first worry: did I lose my work?

Don't: Polite and short, but the tutor still wonders if the notes are gone.

### Warnings: name who it affects

Say what happens to other people, then name both buttons.

Do: The tutor sees the ripple before deciding.

Don't: Clear action, but it hides the people it touches.

### Success: say what’s next

Name what finished, then what happens with it.

Do: The tutor knows their work lands somewhere.

Don't: Warm, but the tutor doesn’t know who reads it.

### Empty states: say how it fills

Say why it’s empty and what will fill it.

Do: Sets the expectation and names who acts.

Don't: Calm, but later when, and why?

### Field errors: write the fix

One line, under the field, phrased as what to do.

Do: An instruction, with the unit.

Don't: Correct, but reads like a rule, and drops the unit.
