# Voice and tone

How PLUS sounds to everyone it serves.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ContentVoiceAndTone.mdx`

## Voice

Our voice is helpful, honest, warm and clear. Who we are stays the same; how we say it fits who is reading.

| Word | The idea | What it asks of the writer |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | The purpose · Productivity | Point to the next step. Tell people what is coming, then show them how to get there. |
|  | The truth · Learning | Say what happened. Give feedback straight, with the reason. Own our mistakes. |
|  | The feeling · Uplift | Write the way a colleague talks. Notice the effort. Skip the jargon. |
|  | The words · Simplicity | Keep it short. Use everyday words. Lead with the verb. One idea per sentence. |

## When to dial

The four words never change. How hard we lean on each one does.

| Word | Lean in | Pull back |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | A tutor is about to start a session. | The reader is browsing, not doing. |
|  | Something failed, or a student is stuck. | Never. Soften how you say it, not what you say. |
|  | A student did well. A tutor showed up. | Money, policy, or an error. |
|  | A live session, a phone, a hurry. | Never. Clear is always on. |

### Warm, pulled back

When money is late, warm means calm and specific. The date is the kindest part.

Do: Kind, because it answers “when?”.
Don't: Polite, but the tutor still has to ask when.

## Tone

One moment, told five ways: Maya, a sixth-grade student, can now solve fractions on her own. However the tone shifts, it always sounds like PLUS.

| Reader | Where | Tone | The line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tutor | Product | Quick, warm, like a teammate | “Maya solved her first fraction on her own. Nice work this week.” |
| Supervisor | Product | Brief, factual, ranked | “Maya mastered fractions in four sessions with her tutor, Priya.” |
| Researcher | Product | Precise, neutral, numbers first | “Fractions: mastered at session 4. School B, grade 6.” |
| Teacher | Service | Respectful, free of product terms | “Maya can now solve fractions on her own. Next, her tutor moves on to decimals.” |
| Student | Service | Short, kind, about effort | “You did it, Maya. Fractions are yours.” |

One card for each person who uses PLUS. The voice holds; the tone shifts with the job. In each card the headline is the action, what to do next, and the body says why it matters in that reader’s terms.

| Reader | Context | Headline (the action) | Body (why it matters) | Actions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tutor | Today · 3:30 PM · Breakout room 3 · Starts in 10 min | Prep for Maya’s session | Last week you tagged her Stuck on fractions. Start with a warm-up problem to build her confidence. | Open session · View notes |
| Lead tutor | Room 3 · Attendance · 2 of 6 joined | Mark attendance for Room 3 | Four students haven’t joined yet. Marking them absent frees their tutors for students who are here. | Mark attendance · Wait 5 min |
| Supervisor | Reviews · This week · 2 urgent | Start with 2 urgent reflections | Priya flagged a session where a student seemed upset. Reading it first lets you check in before her next session. | Open review · See all 5 |
| Researcher | Exports · Fall term · Ready | Your export is ready | 1,240 sessions from three schools, with student names removed. It matches the filters you saved on Monday. | Download CSV · Edit filters |

# Dimensions

One rem ladder that every gap, size, radius and stroke reads from. Heights land on a multiple of 4 px (025).

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Dimensions.mdx`

## Overview

Dimension is the ruler. Spacing, sizing, radius and stroke are what you measure with it, the way color roles read from the palette. Every length on a page is a dimension primitive, or is computed from them (a column width, a fill).

| Use | Measures | Page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sizing | How big a thing is: control, row, label, media, field | Dimensions |
| Spacing | Empty space: pad, stack, inline, gutter | Spacing |
| Layout | Where boxes go: columns, breakpoints, content widths | Grid |
| Radius · Stroke | Corners and lines | Radius · Border |

In Figma the ladder is the hidden `spacing / primitives` collection; nothing binds a primitive directly. Bind the semantic, template or component token that names the job.

## Primitives

Primitives are named in basis points of a rem: `100` is 1 rem, 16 px at the default root; `025` is 0.25 rem, 4 px. The quarter primitives below step by 4 px (`025`). Above 80, the size ladder continues for widths: 120 · 160 · 224 · 240 · 304 · 320 · 400 · 480 · 640 · 720 · 864 · 1232.

### Fine primitives

Below `100`, four values are not a multiple of 4 px (`025`): 1, 2, 6 and 10. They live inside components only: a stroke, a radius, a focus offset, an icon gap, or the pad-y that lands a control’s height on the grid. Templates read quarter primitives only.

| Primitive | px | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `00625` | 1 | stroke-1 |
| `0125` | 2 | stroke-2, focus ring, pad-y-sm |
| `0375` | 6 | pad-y-md, radius-control-sm, tag gap |
| `0625` | 10 | radius-control-lg |

## Heights snap to 4 px (025)

Every line-height, control, row, label and fixed-height box is a multiple of 4 px (025 rem). A box that hugs its content stays on the grid because its lines and pads are on it. The line box snaps, not the glyph: 14 px text sits in a 20 line. Sizes are rem, so a reader who sets a larger default font gets a larger grid, and everything still lands on it.

| Measured | Values |
| --- | --- |
| Line-heights | 16 · 20 · 24 · 28 · 32 · 36 |
| Controls | `size-150 · size-200 · size-250 · size-300` |
| Rows | `size-200 · size-250 · size-300` |
| Labels | `size-100 · size-125` |
| Media | 16 · 20 · 24 · 32 · 40 · 48 · 96 · 128 |

## Core sizes

Five box sizes, every `050` from `100` to `300`: 16 · 24 · 32 · 40 · 48. Reach for these first; any other multiple of 025 is still allowed. An empty cell is a rule: no control below the 24 target, no row under 32.

## Size roles

Pick the role, then its size; the pixel leads and the token is the binding. Icon sizes (12 · 16 · 24) live on Iconography; frame sizes on Grid; template sizes on Spacing.

| Role | Sizes | Tokens | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Button | compact 24 · default 32 · spacious 48 | `--control-sm · -md · -xl` | Spacious only in a footer |
| Field (text, search, select) | compact 32 · default 40 | `--control-md · -lg` | One family: search and select take the field sizes |
| Row | compact 32 · default 40 · spacious 48 | `--row-height-sm · -md · -lg` | A minimum; rows grow with content |
| Tag | `size-125` | `--label-height-md` | One size: read-only, removable, or in a field |
| Count · Change | `size-100` | `--label-height-sm` | A number, beside or inside a label; one size |
| Status · Date · Competency | 20 · spacious 32 | `--label-height-md · --control-md` | Spacious beside a page, panel or module title |
| Label max width | 160 | `--label-max-width` | Truncates past it |
| Media | `size-100 · size-125 · size-150 · size-200 · size-250 · size-300` | `--image-xxs … -xl` | Avatar, Tile, logo; profile 96 · 128 |
| Field width | 80 · 160 · 240 · 320 · 480 | `--field-width-xs … -xl` | Fields fill their column by default |
| Field min height | 80 · 120 | `--field-min-height-sm · -lg` | Text area, rich text |

## Controls side by side

Controls that share a row share a height. Fields (text, search, select) are one family at 32 and 40; buttons are 24, 32 and 48. A row picks its height first, then each control’s size that reaches it.

| Row | Height | Field · Search · Select | Button | Tag |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Toolbar, Section header, view bar | `size-200` | compact | default | `size-125` |
| Field with its own button (add, send) | `size-200` | compact | default | — |
| Table row | `size-250` | compact when editing | compact 24 | `size-125` |
| Form | 40 per field | default | footer default 32 | — |

### Toolbar: 32 throughout

### Field with its own button: 32

### Table rows: compact 24 actions, 20 tags

Each row draws one rule along its bottom edge, inside its 40; the head row’s rule is stronger. The last row drops its rule when the table sits in a frame, so the frame’s edge is never doubled.

### Tags in a field: 20, inside 40 and 32 fields

## Building a control

Height first, then pad. A Button is a 20 line plus 6 above and below, with 12 at each side. A Tag is a 16 line plus 2 above and below, with 4 at each side: 20. A fine primitive exists so the height lands on the grid.

## Do and don’t

### Land every height on 4 px

Do: A 32 Button: on the grid.
Don't: A 22 label: off the grid.

### Pick a core size first

Do: A 40 avatar.
Don't: A 36 avatar no component ships.

### One height per row

Do: Search, Select and buttons at 32.
Don't: 40, 32 and 24 in one toolbar.

## Accessibility

- A control is never smaller than 24 × 24, the minimum pointer target; 32 or more outside a table row or inline toolbar.
- Sizes are rem, so they follow the reader’s font setting.
- A tag is never the only way to act: a removable tag’s remove button has a name.

## Related

| Page | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Spacing | Pad, stack and inline, each a dimension primitive |
| Grid | Columns, breakpoints, content widths |
| Radius | Corners: control height ÷ 4 |
| Border | Stroke widths |
| Iconography | Icon sizes 12 · 16 · 24 |
| Tokens: Spacing and size | Every token |

# Accessibility

A boundary someone needs to find a control or read its state meets 3:1 in every mode, drawn with a border or a surface color, never a shadow alone.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationAccessibility.mdx`

## Cards in forced colors

Forced colors drop background fills and shadows but keep borders. Every card carries a 1px transparent border, so its edge still shows there.

## Material

| Case | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Text contrast | Text on material meets 4.5:1 against the busiest content it can float over, and icons 3:1. Check against the darkest and the lightest picture, not the average. |
| Reduced transparency | Under `prefers-reduced-transparency`, every material falls back to solid `--ds-surface-overlay`. Shape, edge and shadow stay. |
| Increased contrast | Under `prefers-contrast: more`, solid as above, and the edge becomes the 3:1 border. |
| Forced colors | The fill is replaced by the system color; the 1px border stays and draws the edge. |

# Color

Each layer has its surface color. A surface tone separates before any shadow; Sunken marks a different surface, never a recess. In dark mode only floating and blocking surfaces step lighter.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationColor.mdx`

## States and adaptive fills

| Token | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `-hovered · -pressed` | Every surface has both. A clickable surface changes tone on hover and press; a clickable Sunken card lifts to Raised on hover instead. Never both at once. |
| `--ds-background-neutral` | Translucent: darkens in light, lightens in dark. For a fill that must adapt to whatever surface it sits on (a button, a tag). Not a container. |

## Colored surfaces

A surface token may be swapped for a solid background token when the color means something: brand, status or selection.

### Swap the surface; never stack it

### Keep the shadow with the color

### Solid color only

### Color means brand, status or selection

## Dark mode

Shadows read weakly on dark surfaces, so floating and blocking surfaces step lighter. Which ones step lighter is rule 9 under Usage; here is how.

Raised is the exception: in dark it keeps the page tone (`--ds-surface-raised` equals `--ds-surface`), so a Raised card separates by its shadow alone and never steps lighter.

### Pair a lighter surface with its shadow

# Layer system

Every surface sits in one of five layers. Layers 0 and 1 are flat; 2 to 4 are elevated. Then, within the page, three surfaces set what groups and what stands out.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationLayerSystem.mdx`

## The five layers

### Layer 0 · Frame

The ground the app sits on, and the docked Sidebar on it.

#### Usage & styling

- **Flat.** Never a shadow, never floats.
- **Docked Sidebar** shares the Frame; floating, it moves to Layer 3.

### Layer 1 · Page

The page and everything in its flow. What sits on it is broken down below, in Within the page.

#### Usage & styling

- **Flat by default.** Set off from the Frame by tone alone.
- **One surface, one pad.** The Page paints `--ds-surface` edge to edge with `--page-pad` on every side, and takes no radius, border or shadow. See Templates › Page.
- **A standalone Panel** sits on Default: `--ds-surface` with an edge line, and no shadow. Only a floating Panel moves to Layer 3. See Templates › Panel.

### Layer 2 · Navigation

Edges that stay put while content scrolls under them: a sticky table header and column.

#### Usage & styling

- **Border first;** the overflow shadow appears only once content scrolls beneath.

#### Stacking

`--layer-card`

### Layer 3 · Non-blocking overlay

Floats while the page stays usable: the floating Sidebar and Panel, Popup types, Inline edit, Flag, Spotlight, a dragged Card.

#### Usage & styling

- **Overlay pair,** no border. The floating Sidebar and Panel wear the overlay material instead of the solid fill: translucent, no blur, with a 1px material edge, and solid under reduced transparency and increased contrast.
- **Dark mode:** steps lighter.

#### Stacking

`--layer-navigation` · `--layer-popup` · `--layer-flag` · `--layer-spotlight`

### Layer 4 · Blocking overlay

The Modal, and nothing else.

#### Usage & styling

- **Always on the Blanket;** nothing else dims the page.
- **Wears the overlay material** over the Blanket, with a 1px material edge, and keeps the blocking shadow.
- **One at a time;** a Flag may sit above it.
- **A confirm Modal may open over a Panel or a Popup,** with its own Blanket.
- **Popups and Tooltips open over a Modal.**
- **`--layer-*` tokens are set in code only.** Components name the token, never a number.

#### Stacking

`--layer-blanket` · `--layer-modal`

### Not a layer

A **Tooltip** labels a control: no shadow, `--layer-tooltip`.

## Within the page

Layer 1 has three surfaces: Default, Sunken and Raised.

### Default

Most of the page: a Section and its side, tables, lists, forms; rows are hairlines. A Default card is this surface with a border.

#### Usage & styling

- **A Section takes no surface:** no fill, no padding, no border.
- **A Default card** (`surface="default"`) takes `--ds-border`: on the Frame, on Sunken or colored areas, or when dense with its own rows.

### Sunken

A backdrop that groups static content: a Card (the default surface), the table’s empty box (`--ds-surface-sunken`, card radius), a clickable card at rest.

#### Usage & styling

- **Only on the Default surface;** one step only, never a Card inside a Card.
- **Flat:** no shadow, and a transparent 1px border that shows only in forced colors.
- **The default card surface** (`surface="sunken"`). A clickable one lifts to Raised on hover, in place.

### Raised

The one card a view is about, a clickable card on hover, a grabbed control.

#### Usage & styling

- **One per view at rest,** placed first in reading order.
- **Always the pair:** raised surface with raised shadow. In dark its fill is the page tone, so the shadow does the lifting.
- **Hover lifts in place;** the card never moves.
- **Dragged,** it takes the overlay pair.

### By template

How a Section, its side and its detail sit on the page is in Templates › Section; the table and its empty box are in Templates › Table; the Card and its three surfaces are in Templates › Card. Elevation sets only their surface: a Section takes none.

# Material

Translucent surfaces for things that float above other UI and stay connected to what is behind them: a Tag on an illustration, a floating button, a floating Panel, a Modal on the Blanket. Material varies the surface a layer uses, never the layer.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationMaterial.mdx`

## Material ramp

Three materials, from most to least see-through. The bigger the surface and the longer its text, the less it lets through.

## Material tokens

A material surface is three tokens together. The fill alone dissolves on busy content.

## Choose a material

## Colored material

Color identity for small accents on media or on a material surface: a Tag or a Status tag. Two treatments, and each carries the material edge.

### Tokens

One bold token per color. Text uses the on-bold text tokens that already exist.

### In use

A Tag takes `material` and `materialColor`, and a Status tag takes `material` with its own appearance. Neutral has no colored material.

### How it composes

### Accessibility

Every colored material has a solid fallback.

- **Text contrast.** On-bold text meets 4.5:1 composited over white and over black. That is why light is 95%: at 92% white text over white measures 4.3:1.
- **Reduced transparency.** Bold becomes solid `--ds-background-{color}-bold`; subtle becomes solid `--ds-surface-overlay` with the same text.
- **Increased contrast.** Solid as above, and the edge becomes the 3:1 border.
- **Forced colors.** System colors replace the fill; the 1px border stays and draws the edge.

## Do and don’t

Each rule as a Do and a Don’t.

### Over media, use media material

### Match the material to the surface

### Give every material its edge

### Use material only on what floats

### Transparency only, no blur

### Apply the token as it is

### Neutral material only

### A blocking material sits on the Blanket

### Keep colored material small

### Pair the fill with its on-bold text

### Give colored material the edge

# Overview

Elevation says what sits above what, and what you can act on. Surface color, shadow and material are the three cues that show it.

It is never decoration: each cue answers what floats, what groups and what you can press.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationOverview.mdx`

## Terms

| Term | Means |
| --- | --- |
| Layer | Where a surface sits in the stack: Layer 0 · Frame, Layer 1 · Page, Layer 2 · Navigation, Layer 3 · Non-blocking overlay, Layer 4 · Blocking overlay. A higher layer is always above a lower one. |
| Surface | The color a layer or element sits on: `--ds-surface` (Default), `--ds-surface-sunken`, `--ds-surface-raised`, `--ds-surface-overlay`. |
| Shadow | How high a surface floats: `--ds-shadow-raised`, `--ds-shadow-overflow`, `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-blocking`. |
| Material | A translucent surface for what floats and stays connected to what is behind it: `--ds-surface-material-media`, `--ds-surface-material-control`, `--ds-surface-material-overlay`. |
| Blanket | The dimmed layer under a blocking overlay: `--ds-blanket`. |
| Flat | No shadow, whatever the surface. |

## Golden rules

1. Flat by default.
2. Lift means you can act on it.
3. Raise one thing per view.
4. Group with a surface color or a border, never a shadow.
5. A blocking overlay sits on the Blanket.
6. One blocking overlay at a time.
7. No stroke on an elevated surface.
8. Pair the surface with its shadow.
9. Dark mode lightens only what floats.
10. A control’s boundary meets 3:1.

Each rule is drawn as a Do and a Don’t under Usage.

# Shadow ramp

Four shadows, in layer order. The higher ones are stronger on purpose, so a floating surface separates clearly from what is under it.

| Token | Layer | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--ds-shadow-raised` | Page · Raised | The primary card, a grabbed control |
| `--ds-shadow-overflow` | Layer 2 · Navigation | A sticky header or column once content scrolls under it |
| `--ds-shadow-overlay` | Layer 3 · Non-blocking overlay | Popups, Flag, floating Sidebar and Panel, a hovered clickable Card, a dragged Card |
| `--ds-shadow-blocking` | Layer 4 · Blocking overlay | The Modal, on the Blanket |

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationShadowRamp.mdx`

## Shadow tokens

Each token adds three layers: an edge, a key and an ambient shadow. Overflow is a scroll-edge shadow only.

## Using the tokens

### Keep the token a component ships with

## Shadow anatomy

### Interactive composer

Every shadow is three slots: **edge**, **key** and **ambient**. A new shadow fills all three, or says why one is empty. Switch each slot off to see what it carries on a live surface.

### Cross-section

How dark the ground is at each px below a surface's edge, computed from the tokens on this page. The tick on the axis is each shadow's reach.

### Every slot

Each value reads offset x and y, blur, spread, then ink opacity. In dark the ambient is a tight dark halo: a wide soft shadow does not show on a dark ground.

# Usage

Choose elevation by what a surface does, never by how strong a shadow looks.

| What it does | Where it sits | Templates and components |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Blocks the page | **Layer 4 · Blocking** | Modal on the Blanket |
| Floats, page stays usable | **Layer 3 · Non-blocking** | Floating Sidebar and Panel, Popup types, Inline edit, Flag, Spotlight, a dragged Card |
| Stays put while content scrolls | **Layer 2 · Navigation** | Sticky table header and column |
| The one object the view is about | **Page · Raised** | Primary card, a clickable card on hover, Range thumb, current Carousel slide |
| Groups static content | **Page · Sunken** | Card (default), empty box, a clickable card at rest |
| Everything else in the flow | **Page · Default** | Section and its side, table, list, form; a Default card, bordered |
| Holds the app | **Layer 0 · Frame** | The Frame and the docked Sidebar |
| Labels a control | **Not a layer** | Tooltip, no shadow |

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/ElevationUsage.mdx`

## Golden rules

Ten rules, each as a Do and a Don’t.

### 1. Flat by default

### 2. Lift means you can act on it

### 3. Raise one thing per view

The one focal card is Raised and placed first in reading order. Every other card is Sunken, the default surface, or Default with a border. A clickable card lifts in place on hover.

### 4. Group with a surface color or a border, never a shadow

Every card keeps a 1px border, transparent on Sunken and Raised, so forced colors draw its edge.

### 5. A blocking overlay sits on the Blanket

### 6. One blocking overlay at a time

### 7. No stroke on an elevated surface

### 8. Pair the surface with its shadow

### 9. Dark mode lightens only what floats

### 10. A control’s boundary meets 3:1

### In motion

Elevation changes on a spring and never jumps. A clip never cuts a shadow: a scrolling area leaves room for the shadow of what floats inside it.

# Overview

Foundations create consistent experiences across the tutor and student apps.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/FoundationsOverview.mdx`

## Framework

## Overview

Foundations are the tokens, guidelines and visual styles that every pattern and component builds on: color, spacing, typography and more.

- Repo: `design-system/guidelines/foundations/` holds the written guidance for each foundation.
- Figma: one page per foundation under Foundations.
- Storybook: one page per foundation under Foundations.

## The foundations

Grouped as tokens, brand, visual, layout, expression and accessibility.

### Design tokens

- **Tokens.** Named values that store a design decision once, for every theme.

### Brand

- **Voice and tone.** How PLUS sounds to everyone it serves.
- **Language.** How we write every word, for everyone PLUS reaches.
- **Messages.** What to say when something happens.
- **Logos.** The PLUS mark, with or without the wordmark.
- **Illustrations.** Hand-drawn characters for moments with room to breathe.

### Visual

- **Color.** Every color as a token named for its job.
- **Typography.** Heading, Body, Metric and Code text styles.
- **Iconography.** Font Awesome Free icons at three sizes.
- **Elevation.** Surface and shadow pairs that lift a layer.
- **Radius.** Corner roundness: height ÷ 4, with buttons at 6 and 4.
- **Border.** A width token paired with a color token.

### Layout

- **Dimensions.** The one ladder every size, gap, radius and stroke reads from.
- **Spacing.** Empty space named by the job it does: pad, stack, inline and gutter.
- **Grid.** Two 12-column grids, the breakpoints and the content widths.

### Expression

- **Motion.** Springs, transitions and what moves.
- **Sound.** Synthesized sounds for the few moments worth hearing.

### Accessibility

- **Accessibility.** The rules every PLUS screen meets, built into the tokens and patterns.

## Page anatomy

Every foundation page follows the same shape:

- A landing opens the page: the foundation's name, one-line purpose, quick links, and hero.
- The right rail lists every section, Overview and Related included.
- The foundation's sections come next, then Accessibility, then Related last.
- Examples read live tokens and follow the toolbar's Color mode and Contrast switches.

## Accessibility

Each foundation page ends with the accessibility rules it owns. [Accessibility](?path=/docs/foundations-accessibility--docs) holds the cross-cutting rules.

# Grid

Two 12-column grids with a 16 gutter at every width; page content caps at 1232.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Grid.mdx`

## Overview

PLUS is desktop only, from 768 up. Two grids share 12 columns and a 16 gutter. The content grid sits inside the Page: cards, tables, forms and text align to it. The screen grid is for overlays only: modals and floating Panels size from it. The grid decides where containers sit; spacing decides everything inside them.

The content grid: 24 Page pad, 12 columns, 16 gutters, two cards spanning six columns each.

## Breakpoints

Each breakpoint is a minimum width with its own mode. Columns stay 12 and the gutter 16 at every width. The Sidebar opens over the page below 1024 and docks from 1024.

| Mode | From | Code | Sidebar | Page pad | Content | Column |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium | 768 | `:root` | opens over the page | `space-150` | 720 | 45.33 |
| Large | 1024 | `min-width: 1024px` | docked, 240 | `space-150` | 736 | 46.67 |
| X-Large | 1440 | `min-width: 1440px` | docked, 240 | `space-150` | 1152 | 81.33 |

Nothing switches above 1440 or below 768. Design at Medium and X-Large at least, by switching the frame’s mode, never by resizing by hand.

## Two grids

Both grids have 12 columns and a 16 gutter. They never show together: the content grid lays out the Page, and the screen grid only places what floats over it.

### Content grid: the Page

Sits inside the Page, after the Sidebar, a docked Panel and the Page pad. Cards, tables, forms and text align to it. Its width is what the frame leaves, never under 720.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--grid-columns` | `Grid/columns` | `space-075` | Both grids |
| `--grid-gutter` | `Grid/gutter` | `space-100` | Both grids, every width |
| `--content-width` | `Content/width-content` | 720 · 736 · 1152 | Per mode |
| `--grid-width-column` | `Grid/width-column` | 45.33 · 46.67 · 81.33 | Computed |

### Screen grid: overlays only

Spans the whole screen inside the screen pad and ignores the Sidebar. Only modals, floating Panels and the Blanket size from it, so an overlay sits in the same place whether the Sidebar is open or not. Nothing on the Page aligns to it.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--screen-width` | `Screen/width-screen` | 768 · 1024 · 1440 | Per mode |
| `--screen-pad-x` | `Screen/pad-x-screen` | `space-150 · space-150 · space-200` | The screen grid’s margin |
| `--grid-width-column-screen` | `Grid/width-column-screen` | 45.33 · 66.67 · 88 | Computed |

Column widths are computed, not dimension primitives: the gutter and the pads are the steps.

## Content widths

Page content stops growing at a cap. Pick the cap by what the page holds.

| Mode | Width | Token | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fixed-wide (default) | 1232 | `--content-max-width` | Dashboards, directories, tables |
| Fixed-narrow | 864 | `--content-max-width-reading` | Long-form reading |
| Fluid | no cap | — | Canvases, boards, timelines |
| Minimum | 720 | `--content-min-width` | Narrower than this, the page scrolls sideways |

## The frame

Sidebar 240, Page pad 24. The Page runs to the top of the screen. A Panel opens at 400 and its splitter holds it between 320 and 640. The frame has no seams: the Page meets the Sidebar and the Panel at a hairline, and the content grid recomputes from the width that is left.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--frame-sidebar-width` | `Sidebar/width-sidebar` | 240 | Docked from 1024 |
| `--page-pad` | `Page/pad` | `space-150` | Every side of the Page |
| `--panel-width-default` | — | 400 | Where a Panel opens |
| `--panel-min-width · max-width` | — | 320 · 640 | The splitter’s reach |

## Column spans

A region takes whole columns: span n = n × column + (n − 1) × 16. Cards per row is the most of 4, 3, 2 or 1 that keeps each card at its minimum width (224 · 304 · 480). In a region narrower than 12 columns, only counts that divide its span apply. A split keeps its main column at 480 or more and its side at 224 or more; below that, they stack.

## Card widths

A card size sets a minimum width, and each row holds as many cards as stay at or above it. Since the content width changes by breakpoint, each size spans a range of columns: sm 3 to 4, md 4 to 6, lg 6 to 12. The card never sets a fixed width; it fills its columns.

| Card size | Pad | Minimum | Medium · 720 | Large · 736 | X-Large · 1152 | Columns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sm | `space-100` | 224 | 3 per row · 4 cols · 229 | 3 per row · 4 cols · 235 | 4 per row · 3 cols · 276 | 3–4 |
| md | `space-100` | 304 | 2 per row · 6 cols · 352 | 2 per row · 6 cols · 360 | 3 per row · 4 cols · 373 | 4–6 |
| lg | `space-100` | 480 | 1 per row · 12 cols · 720 | 1 per row · 12 cols · 736 | 2 per row · 6 cols · 568 | 6–12 |

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--card-min-width-sm` | — | 224 | Small cards, four per row at X-Large |
| `--card-min-width-md` | — | 304 | Most cards |
| `--card-min-width-lg` | — | 480 | A featured card; side images start here |

Between breakpoints the content width is fluid, so a card lands anywhere from its minimum up to the next count’s switch point.

## Modal widths

A modal’s content area spans 4, 6, 8 or 10 screen-grid columns, and its pad (--modal-pad, 20) sits outside them on each side, so the box bleeds one pad past the columns. The tinted band is that pad, outside the columns. It grows with the screen between breakpoints, stops past a 1280 screen, never shrinks below its Medium width, and ignores the Sidebar, so it sits in the same place either way.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--modal-width-4-col` | `Modal/width-4-col` | 269 · 355 · 440 | 4 columns |
| `--modal-width-6-col` | `Modal/width-6-col` | 392 · 520 · 648 | 6 columns |
| `--modal-width-8-col` | `Modal/width-8-col` | 515 · 685 · 856 | 8 columns |
| `--modal-width-10-col` | `Modal/width-10-col` | 637 · 851 · 1064 | 10 columns |
| `--popup-width-3-col · 4-col` | — | 200 · 264 · 328 · 261 · 347 · 432 | Popups on the screen grid |

## Hug and fill

Every component either hugs its content or fills the space it is given, and the template it sits in decides which. Text fills; a Button, an icon and a tag hug and never stretch to a column.

## Do and don’t

Do: One gutter at every width.
Don't: A gutter that changes with the screen.

Do: Span whole columns.
Don't: Stop halfway across a column.

Do: Center a modal on the screen grid.
Don't: Center it on the content grid: it shifts with the sidebar.

Do: Cap reading text at the reading width.
Don't: Run a paragraph across the full width.

Do: Align the cards; their content follows their pad.
Don't: Pull content to the card’s edge to meet a column line.

Do: Keep the grid on the Page.
Don't: Run columns under the sidebar.

Do: Build with auto layout and gaps.
Don't: Place by hand: it drifts.

Do: Design from the Medium breakpoint up, on 12 columns.
Don't: Design a phone layout on 2 columns.

## Accessibility

- Content never sits under the Sidebar. Below 1024 the Sidebar opens over the page, closes on an outside click or Escape, and returns focus to its toggle.
- Cap long-form text at 864, so a line stays readable.
- Keep DOM order the same as visual order on the grid.
- Content holds a 720 minimum; narrower than that, the page scrolls sideways instead of squeezing columns. PLUS is a desktop tool, so it does not reflow to a single column at 400% zoom: a known exception to WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow.

## Related

| Page | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Dimensions | The ladder, and every height and width |
| Spacing | Pad, stack and inline inside each template |
| Templates | Frame, Page, Section, Card, Modal on these grids |
| Elevation | Which surface each layer sits on |

# Iconography

Icons are small symbols that help people find their way and act faster.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Icons.mdx`

## Overview

The Icon component renders a single glyph; components with icon slots (`Button`'s `iconBefore` and `iconAfter`) pass the glyph name through `Icon` (`fa-regular fa-<name>`, falling back to `fa-solid` where Font Awesome Free has no regular weight). A React node in place of the name renders as given.

```jsx
<Icon name="calendar-days" size={16} color="subtle" />
<Button appearance="primary" text="Add tutor" iconBefore="plus" />
```

## Principles

### Use one recognized symbol per meaning

Pick the plainest glyph most people read the same way (calendar for dates, bell for notifications, gear for settings) and keep one glyph per meaning across the product.

### Pair icons with text labels

A label states what the icon does and names it for screen readers. Leave an icon unlabeled only for a familiar action in a tight space, and give the control an accessible `label` in code.

## Sizes: 12, 16 and 24

Icons ship at three sizes bound to `Size/Icon` tokens. `--fa-width: 1em` is set globally so every glyph fills its square box without adding line height. Chevrons are always 12. Add breathing room with spacing tokens, never a larger icon size.

| Size (px) | Figma token | Code | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | `Size/Icon/sm` | `--icon-sm` | Chevrons, field validation, and compact controls such as tags, Count tags, statuses, secondary actions and table headers. |
| 16 | `Size/Icon/md` | `--icon-md` | Default beside 14 and 16 text in buttons, menus, fields and lists. |
| 24 | `Size/Icon/lg` | `--icon-lg` | Empty states, section headers and standalone status marks. Above 24, use a Tile. |

## Above 24, use a Tile

24 is the top of the icon scale. A larger mark, tool logo or empty-state symbol belongs in a Tile, which sets its size, radius and fill together.

## Font Awesome Free and color tokens

Use Font Awesome Free 7.2 only: `fa-solid`, `fa-regular` and `fa-brands` (such as `fa-brands fa-figma` and `fa-brands fa-github`). Pro families (`fa-light`, `fa-thin`, `fa-sharp`, `fa-duotone`) and Pro-only names are unlicensed and render blank, so check a glyph name against the Free set first. Regular is the default weight; solid is used where Free has no regular glyph. Where one set of icons needs a glyph Free draws only in solid, that one glyph is solid and the rest stay regular. Always use current glyph names rather than legacy aliases (`calendar-days`, not `calendar-alt`).

Color icons with `--ds-icon-*` tokens (`--ds-icon-success`, `--ds-icon-danger`, or the text color beside the icon), never a raw hex value.

## Usage

| Component | Job |
| --- | --- |
| Icon | Backs up a text label at 12, 16 or 24. |
| Tile | Frames an icon, partner/tool logo or picture at 16 to 48. |
| Logo | Marks PLUS itself. |
| Image | Places a photo or graphic in content. |

Before proposing a new glyph through Intake, verify that no existing glyph fits, that it will not conflict with another icon in the same view, and that a text label alone would not be clearer. A design lead approves new glyphs. Zoom has no Font Awesome Free glyph: a Zoom link is not an icon, and partner and tool marks go in a `Tile`, never in `Logo`.

## Common icons

| Glyph | Name | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | `plus` | Add |
|  | `minus` | Remove |
|  | `check` | Confirm |
|  | `xmark` | Close, cancel or dismiss |
|  | `trash` | Delete |
|  | `pen` | Edit |
|  | `magnifying-glass` | Search |
|  | `gear` | Settings |
|  | `calendar-days` | Session or schedule |
|  | `user` | Person or profile |
|  | `clipboard` | Session note |
|  | `bell` | Notification |
|  | `circle-info` | Information |
|  | `arrow-right` | Next or forward |
|  | `arrow-left` | Back or previous |
|  | `chevron-down` | Expand or open a menu |
|  | `chevron-up` | Collapse |
|  | `star` | Favorite or rating |

## Do and don't

### Use Free families and Free names only

Solid, regular and brands are licensed here, including brand glyphs.

Do: Free families (fa-regular, fa-solid, fa-brands) render everywhere.

Don't: Pro families (fa-light, fa-thin, fa-sharp, fa-duotone) render blank.

### Use 16 by default, 12 sparingly

Icons are 16 beside body text. Keep 12 for chevrons, validation and compact parts.

Do: A 16 icon leads the label; the trailing chevron is 12.

Don't: A 12 leading icon is too small beside 14 body text.

### Use a symbol people recognize

Pick the glyph most people read the same way.

Do: A bell for notifications.

Don't: A gear reads as settings, so it misleads here.

## Accessibility

- Decorative icons and icons beside a visible text label carry `aria-hidden="true"`.

The logomark ships in fixed heights: 16, 20, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 96. At 24 and below it uses a heavier small-size drawing so the plus stays open. Pick a step; never scale an instance by hand.

## Construction

The logomark is drawn on a 12 by 12 unit square (1 unit = 8 of the 96 drawing coordinates). Two circles of 6 and 4.5 units share its center, two 2-unit corner circles sit at the top right and bottom left, and the 3-unit plus is centered 8.5 units from the left and 3.5 from the top. Choose the color option for the ground the logo sits on.

| Color option | Ground | When to use |

| Dark | Dark grounds | Solid deep teal tile with a white plus and light wordmark. |

# Choreography

How several moving parts stay coherent: one direction, no collisions, a set order, and a clear cause.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/MotionChoreography.mdx`

## How to read the figures

Every transition is built from three blocks (something enters, something leaves, something changes) and a short list of atoms. The rules below decide direction, space, order and cause; where there is a wrong way, it is the same scene with one rule broken, played beside the right way. Before a move plays, the screen dims and the path each part takes is drawn from start (a dot) to landing (an arrowhead). Where the lesson is order, a strip under the screen shows when each part starts. Use a figure's speed control to watch at ½× or ¼×.

## Direction

### Unify direction

When several parts move together, they move along one axis so no path crosses another and none scatters. What cannot share that axis fades in place instead of traveling. Position indicators (such as a tab indicator) track the place while the content makes its own move; step indicators change state in place.

### Move along the grid

Across, then up or down, round the corner. Never diagonal. A size change is the same: width, then height.

### Direction follows where it lives

Everything comes from where it lives and goes back there.

- A menu grows out of its trigger and shrinks back into it.
- A row grows into its page, and the page shrinks back into the row.
- A Panel and the Sidebar slide from and to their own edge.
- A section collapses up into the header that stays.
- A Flag slides in from the top-right corner along x and leaves the same way.
- On a bar anchored to the right, a control that grows (Search, the Filter count) grows to the left.
- A chevron points where the view will move.

### Back the way it came

Closing retraces the opening in reverse, one speed faster. A round trip draws one line, not two.

## Space

### Keep space

Nothing collides with a neighbor or shares its place mid-move. What leaves fades out first; only then does anything move into its space.

### Clean fades

New content begins when the old is about 90% out (`appearance.fast`, about ). A true crossfade is kept for non-text content: an image, the Blanket, or content arriving over a Skeleton.

### Stable layouts

A Skeleton holds the layout while content loads, so nothing shifts when it arrives.

### Transition every change

Every change is shown, at a volume set by how often it happens. The floor is a quiet fade, never a cut.

### Continuity

A shared container connects two views: the row becomes the record, or a quick look in a floating Panel grows into its record page. If the content is ready before the container settles, the content wins.

## Order

### Sequence and stagger

When several items arrive, they stagger 20 ms apart (or 500 ms ÷ items if shorter), so the whole set lands within half a second and reads as one arrival. The gap stays tight: the fifth row lands 80 ms after the first, while at 150 ms apart each row becomes its own event. The stagger and the clean-fade gap live in the composites, not as tokens.

### Opening a page, by moment

Stable parts arrive first, important last, top to bottom. Nothing arrives by rising; a settle of 4 px or less downward is fine, and so is a chart mark growing to its value.

- **Routine** (dozens a day): the old page fades out, the new one fades in, in place, all at once.
- **Hero** (a milestone): stable parts first, 20 ms apart, each settling 4 px or less downward. Expressive on the one Card.

### Load order

Shell and navigation, then headings and text, then data, then the primary action, then charts (which may wait until scrolled to).

### Many or one

When a few items change, each one moves (Add or remove, Reorder). When about a third or more change, swap the whole list (Swap content).

## Cause

### Same meaning, same motion

A row expanding is a reveal from its seam, and size sets the speed. A menu or a Select opening is not: it fades in place. That fade is instant from the keyboard and absent under the in-app Reduced setting; the system's reduced-motion setting keeps it. Visually similar things that live on different layers get different motion: a Panel on the page's layer pushes; one above it slides over. When one element changes both position and opacity, spatial and appearance run together.

### Forward is confirm, reverse is cancel

Cancel reverses the entrance one speed faster. Confirm fades the layer and carries the change forward: a status changes, a Flag confirms, a new record opens.

### Who started it

Input is answered at once. A system change is quieter, arrives where the system speaks (the top-right corner, a message slot above the work), and never moves what a person is touching.

### Breakpoints

A resize follows the hand: each layout change is a single jump the instant the edge crosses a breakpoint, with no animation afterward. A filter side hides at 960, quick filters fold into a menu at 768, and a rotating tablet does the same.

## Atoms

Every motion is built from these atoms, each on a family.

| Atom | Family | Where PLUS uses it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opacity | `appearance` | Fades everywhere; Swap content; Tooltip |
| Scale | `spatial` | Floating layers only: a Modal entering, and shrinking 2% as it leaves |
| Position | `spatial` | Panel, Sidebar, Step, indicators, Reorder |
| Mask (clip) | `spatial` | A row opening from its seam |
| Position and mask | `spatial` | A number rolling once, downward; use sparingly |
| Scale and opacity | spatial with appearance | Modal |
| Reveal from under another element | `spatial` | Breadcrumb row opening above the title |
| Position and opacity | spatial with appearance | Flag; a milestone settle |
| Corner radius, moving with size | `spatial` | Drill into and climb back out (Transitions): corners square off as the row becomes a page |

# Physics

Every motion in PLUS is a spring, picked by name from one token table.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/MotionPhysics.mdx`

## Springs

A spring has no fixed duration. It is pulled toward its target and settles when it arrives, so it can be interrupted, reversed and handed the speed of a hand at any moment. Linear motion is the one exception: it is for things that follow time or the pointer one to one.

### Three families

Pick the family by the property that changes. The page header on scroll is `linear` too: its small title, actions and tabs follow the scroll position one to one and stay put when scrolling stops.

| Family | Changes | Overshoot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `spatial` | Position, size, scale, rotation, corner radius, clip | Only in Expressive |
| `appearance` | Opacity, color, blur, shadow | Never: a spring with no bounce, so it can still be interrupted |
| `linear` | Anything that follows time or the pointer one to one: progress, countdowns, Skeleton shimmer, scrolling, dragging | Never: it is not a spring |

### How quick and how bouncy

A spring has two settings: stiffness (how quick it is) and damping ratio (how bouncy it is). At ratio 1 it lands on its target and stays; at 0.8 it passes by about 1.5%; at 0.6 by about 9.5%. Each time is given twice: to 90% (when the motion reads as arrived) and to settled (within 1% of the target).

### Modes and tokens

Elsewhere in the docs a token drops its `motion.` prefix (`spatial.fast`), and "Expressive `spatial.fast`" means that token in Expressive mode. All tokens are mass 1. Figma has no motion tokens; a Figma prototype uses the nearest spring with Smart Animate, splitting any move into x then y.

**Productive** is the mode for everything. **Expressive** is switched on for one container at a time (`data-motion="expressive"`) for these moments only:

- **Finish:** every completed reflection. The confirmation Flag lands with one overshoot on Expressive `spatial.fast`.
- **Milestone:** onboarding complete, first session done, a student's goal reached, a recognition earned, term start and term end. The one card in the hero entrance is Expressive. A goal shows once per person: the student sees it the moment it happens, the tutor the next time they open that student.

Inside an Expressive container, controls, fields, page transitions and data marks stay Productive. This is the only list of Expressive moments; other pages point here.

**The shake** is the one other bounce. A blocked submit shakes its container once: a loose spring (stiffness 1187.5, damping 15, mass 1) kicked sideways at 420 px/s, peaking at 9 px after 40 ms. It is one pattern used by Modal, a field with its own button and InlineEdit, not a token.

### Speed follows size and distance

| Speed | For | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fast` | Small things, short distances | Toggle thumb, Popup, a row, a tab indicator |
| `default` | Mid-size layers, short travel | Modal, Flag, content changing in place, the Sidebar opening, a row growing into its record (Drill, because it repeats all day) |
| `slow` | Large layers, long travel | A floating Panel, a docking Panel, a whole page that slides; anything traveling more than about 600 px |

### Exits

Two questions decide how something leaves.

1. **Can it come back?** If yes (a floating Panel, the Sidebar, a docked Panel), it reverses its entrance one speed faster (`fast` stays `fast`) and settles at the edge.
2. **If it is gone for good, who started it?**
   - **The system** (a Flag timing out): `spatial.exit`, aimed 3.8 times past the edge so it leaves at full speed.
   - **The person, with a click** (a close button, a deleted row): `appearance.fast` in place; surrounding rows close the gap on `spatial.fast`.
   - **The person, with a flick:** `spatial.exit` started from the hand's velocity.

An exit is shorter than its entrance and lands without a bounce. A floating layer may shrink 2% as it fades (a Modal to 98%). Every component names an enter and exit pair, and the exit is the entrance one speed faster, so there is no second token set.

### Loops

`motion.loop` is an undamped spring that swings as a sine wave (one cycle every 1.2 s). A three-pulse typing Progress indicator runs the same loop, each pulse an eighth of a cycle behind the one before; turning damping back on settles it at rest.

- A loop runs only while work runs (loading, thinking, typing) and stops the moment the work ends.
- A decorative loop stops by 5 s, and every loop has a pause.
- In Reduced mode a loop becomes a static label, such as "Thinking".

## Velocity

What a hand moves keeps the hand's speed.

- **Dragging, splitters, swipes and scrubbing run a live spring** started from the release velocity (projected rest = velocity ÷ 1000 × 0.998 ÷ 0.002; 3 px slop before drag starts, pointer capture, `touch-action: none`).
- **Opening, closing and selecting use the token as CSS.** There is no velocity to carry.
- **Past a limit, it resists, then returns** with the hand's speed (√overshoot × 4 px, returning on `spatial.fast`).
- **A throw is decided by where it would land,** and shows an armed state before release so the person can still take it back.
- **Gestures stay contained:** a press is not a drag, and the page never scrolls under the hand.

### A throw keeps the hand's speed

The same throw twice: only whether the spring receives the hand's speed changes.

### Where it would land decides

A short, fast flick carries past halfway, so it is armed and leaves; a longer, slower drag comes to rest short of halfway and returns.

### Interruption

A spring can be reversed at any moment from where it is and at the speed it has. Nothing waits for an animation to end before it answers.

## Weight

Weight in PLUS is chosen by token, never by mass (every token is mass 1).

### Size and carry

Bigger things travel on slower tokens (`fast`, `default`, `slow`). Something dragged follows the pointer on a spring: a tag or name stays right under the pointer on `spatial.fast`; a card trails slightly on `spatial.default` and settles a beat after the drop. Neither bounces: weight shows as lag, never wobble. Keep the lag small; a carried thing that falls far behind the hand reads as slow, not heavy.

### What it costs

A destructive action gets friction, not slower motion: deleting something that cannot be undone asks for a confirmation Modal while keeping its normal motion token.

## Damping

These four share `spatial.default`'s stiffness and differ only in damping ratio. Productive motion uses ratio 1 everywhere; Expressive uses 0.8 and, for small things thrown with energy, 0.6. Every token stays at 0.6 or above so it never rings.

### Damping at a limit

Dragged past where it can go, a surface moves by √overshoot × 4 px and springs back on `spatial.fast` on release.

## Choosing a spring

Size and distance set the speed. How often it happens decides whether it travels.

| How often | What moves |
| --- | --- |
| Dozens a day | Color and parts only; a page fades in place on `appearance.fast` |
| Once a session | It travels on its size’s token |
| A milestone | Expressive, on the one card only |

- A page never cuts.
- From the keyboard, controls and Popups open with no animation; layers and pages keep their motion.
- Focus rings never animate.

## Reduced motion

When someone turns on reduce motion in their system settings, PLUS switches to Reduced mode. It is a mapping, not a fourth set of springs.

| Family | In Reduced mode |
| --- | --- |
| `spatial` | Replaced by an `appearance.fast` fade in the final place and size. Never a cut |
| `appearance` | One short fade on `appearance.fast` (about ), so a change is still noticed |
| `linear` | Progress and countdowns keep moving, because they carry information. Skeleton shimmer stops |
| Loops | Stop, and become a static label |
| Decorative motion | Removed, not shortened: Expressive overshoot (the card and the Flag simply fade in), shape morphing, parallax |
| Shake | None. Color, icon, message and focus carry the error |

Nothing flashes more than three times a second, and anything that moves for more than 5 s on its own has a pause.

## One spring, five ways

One token, written for each target it ships to (`damping = 2 × ratio × √(stiffness × mass)`, `response = 2π ÷ √stiffness`). Because CSS cannot repeat a generated `linear()` easing, `motion.loop` ships in CSS as an alternating 600 ms half-cycle sine curve.

## In code

CSS reads a semantic token as a `linear()` easing plus its settle time. Components bind `--ds-motion-*` semantics only, never a `--motion-spring-*` primitive, and reduced motion is handled once, in the token layer.

```css
transition: transform var(--ds-motion-spatial-default-duration) var(--ds-motion-spatial-default);
```

JS motion (drag, throw, interruption, height) reads `SPRINGS`:

```js
import { animate } from 'motion';
import { SPRINGS } from '@/tokens/ladder/springs.generated.js';

animate(panel, { x: 0 }, SPRINGS['spatial.default'].productive);
```

# Principles

Motion in PLUS explains a change. If it explains nothing, it is not there.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/MotionPrinciples.mdx`

## How motion carries the framework

Our motion is responsive, clear about how things work, kind in the moments that matter, and quiet everywhere else.

## Four principles

Nearly everything a tutor does in a day is Productive; one moment in a term is Expressive. Every Do and Don't below plays the same scene with one rule broken, drawing its path from start to landing before it moves.

### Always responsive

**Keep up, never hold up.**

Every press answers in the same frame through its color or press state (90% done by about ). A moving part, such as a Toggle thumb, follows on `spatial.fast`. Any motion can be interrupted mid-way, switched to Reduced mode by the system setting, and paused if it runs longer than 5 s.

### Build understanding

**Show how, not just what.**

Motion shows where something came from, where it went, and where you are now. It keeps the speed of the hand that started it, carries the weight of the thing that moves, and settles where it belongs.

### Lead with empathy

**Cheer the wins, cushion the misses.**

Expressive marks the end of something worth finishing, a few times a week at most. A blocked submit shakes once; a failed save eases in and stays until it is fixed.

### Cut the noise

**One story at a time.**

Only what explains the change moves. How often something happens sets how loud its motion is, never to zero at page level. From the keyboard, controls and Popups open with no animation; layers and pages keep their motion. Never use Expressive on a control, a field, or anything done dozens of times a day.

## Sound

Sound is rare and never the only signal: see Sound · When to play and Settings and accessibility.

## Before you add motion

1. **What does it explain?** Where something came from, where it went, or what is new. If the answer is "nothing", leave it out.
2. **How often will someone see it?** Dozens a day means quiet.
3. **Does it answer at once, and can it be interrupted?** Nothing waits for an animation to finish.
4. **Does the weight fit the object and the input?**
5. **Does it fit the moment?** Cheer a win once; keep a failed save calm.
6. **Does every moving part explain the change?** Cut the rest, or move it as one group.

A new kind of motion is a question for the design team.

| Tapped row | grows into the record (position, size, corner radius together) | `spatial.default` | 0 |

| List | fades out in place; it doesn't move, and nothing dims | `appearance.fast` | 0 |
| Record header, tabs and content | opacity in, together, in place | `appearance.default` | Once the container is well on its way |

The row becomes the page: its own bars fade as it grows, and the record's content fades in once the container shows where it is going. Nothing inside travels; the container is the only mover. Because people drill many times a day, the grow runs on `spatial.default`, and Back reverses it one speed faster on `spatial.fast`, returning the list at the same scroll position with that row briefly lit.

PLUS is at most three levels deep (area, record, one record inside it), so the same container transform holds at every level. A flow that needs a fourth level is a hierarchy to flatten, not a fourth grow. On a desktop with a fixed Sidebar a page never slides in: a slide reads as a floating Panel opening.

Climbing back one level shrinks the page into the row it came from. Jumping back two or more levels, past a page no longer on screen, fades in place with the Breadcrumb already shorter.

**Used in:** Record page, Table rows, Card, Breadcrumb.

### Switch views

| Tells the person | When | Not | Breadcrumb | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The same thing, seen another way. | Page tabs, such as a session’s Overview, Notes and Reflection. | An ordered set is Step; pill filters and format switches are Swap content in place. | Unchanged. | Tab bar click or arrow keys. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tab indicator | position, width | `spatial.fast` | 0 |
| Both tab bodies | slide together toward the chosen tab, as one flat sheet, no fade | `spatial.slow` for a page-size body, `spatial.default` for a panel | 0 |
| Tab labels | color | `appearance.fast` | 0 |

Because the views are peers in a row, the bodies move sideways as a group without fading; in Reduced mode the slide becomes an `appearance.fast` fade.

### Step to the next or previous

| Tells the person | When | Not | Breadcrumb | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The next one in line, and where you are in the set. | An ordered set: form steps, paging, one week to the next, reflection questions. | Going deeper is Drill; another area is Go to. | Unchanged; position label changes ("2 of 4"). | Reflection 1 of 4; Schedule week to week. Triggered by Next and Back, arrow keys, swipe on touch. |

| Steps sit | Body | Token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Across the top (horizontal ProgressTracker, ≤4 steps, paging, Schedule weeks, Carousel) | Old and new slide together sideways, no fade | By size; step states change in place on appearance.fast |
| Down a side (vertical ProgressTracker, ≥5 steps, reflection questions in a side list) | Old and new slide together vertically, no fade: Next brings the new step up from below | By size; step states change in place on appearance.fast |

The body moves on the same axis as the step list. Step states change in place on `appearance.fast`, the moment the body starts: the step just left becomes visited and the next becomes current, and nothing travels along the ProgressTracker. Placement (top for four steps or fewer, side for five or more) is set once, when the task opens, by the longest path the flow can take, so a branch never changes the slide axis mid-task. Fit can push top to side, never the reverse: four steps whose labels would truncate go down the side. The position label swaps on `appearance.fast`; the header, Sidebar and step list never move.

**Used in:** Form steps, Table paging, Schedule weeks, Carousel, multi-step tasks.

## Within a place

The person stays where they are; something on the page changes.

### Scroll to a spot on the page

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| You’re still on this page; here is the spot. | A heading outline link or a link to one comment on the current page. | Another page is Go to or Drill. | Heading outline "Escalation" link scrolls and marks the heading. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | scroll position | `spatial.slow` | 0 |
| Destination | Call attention (below) | as Call attention | On arrival |

In Reduced mode the page does not travel: the content at the new position fades in on `appearance.fast` and the destination is marked.

### Swap content in place

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The frame is the same; what’s inside it changed. | A view pill, a filter that replaces most of a list, a confirm replacing a form in a Modal, Previous/Next in a Panel. | If one item changes, it is Add or remove, or Update a value. | Sessions filter from This week to Last month. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame, headers, stable labels | stay still | — | — |
| Selected view pill fill | glides to the new pill | `spatial.fast` | 0 |
| Old content | opacity out | `appearance.fast` | 0 |
| New content | opacity in | `appearance.fast` | After the clean-fade gap |

The old content is gone before the new arrives, so one clean frame sits between them. A cross-fade shows both at half strength and reads as mud.

### Add or remove an item

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One thing joined or left, and the others made room. | One item joins or leaves a list or grid in the page (rows, SectionMessage, Banner). | Above the page is Open an overlay; replacing most of a list is Swap content. | Adding a session; opening a record adds it to Sidebar open items. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rows below | make room | `spatial.fast` | 0 |
| New row | opens from the seam (height) | `spatial.fast` | 0 |
| New row content | opacity in, in place, no scale | `appearance.fast` | Once there is room |
| Removed row | opacity out | `appearance.fast` | 0 |
| Rows below a removed row | close the gap | `spatial.fast` | As it fades |

In a grid, the others slide along their row and wrap.

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The same items, in a new order. | Sorting, or dragging an item to a new place in the same set. | If items join or leave, it is Add or remove. | Sorting Students by last session; dragging a session to another slot. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Each item | moves to its new place: straight along the column in a list, x then y in a grid | `spatial.default` | Staggered: 20 ms apart, or 500 ms ÷ items if shorter |

Between two lists the dropped item takes the place it lands on and both lists close up. Under Reduced motion nothing travels: what moved fades in place on `appearance.fast`, in the same order.

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| More of the same thing, revealed from where it was hidden. | A disclosure row, Search icon opening into a field, Filter button widening for its count. | If new content arrives from elsewhere, it is Load content. | "Escalate this session" reveals the reason field. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Container | height, from the seam | `spatial.fast` for a row, `spatial.default` for a section | 0 |
| Rows below | move down | Same as the container | 0 |
| Revealed content | opacity in | `appearance.fast` | Once there is room |
| Chevron | rotates with the height | Same as the container | 0 |

Closing reverses the reveal on the same token, with the detail fading first.

### Load content

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Something is coming, and the page won’t jump when it arrives. | Content is fetched, then arrives. | Saving is Update a value or state. | The Admin dashboard loading. |

| Wait | Signal |
| --- | --- |
| Under 200 ms | Nothing |
| 200 ms to 5 s | A Skeleton or Spinner, inside the thing that is loading |
| In a menu or Popup | Never a Skeleton: one "Loading options" row, then "Couldn't load options" with Retry. New options fade in 20 ms apart; the list grows on spatial.fast |
| Over 5 s | Progress with a number |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skeleton | shimmer, top-left to bottom-right | `linear` | While waiting |
| Content | opacity in, in place, in load order | `appearance.default` | Staggered: 20 ms apart, or 500 ms ÷ items if shorter |
| Skeleton | opacity out under it | `appearance.fast` | As content arrives |

## Above a place

Something joins the page from above or beside it.

### Open and close an overlay

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This sits on top for now; the page underneath is untouched. | A Modal, Popup, floating Panel, Flag or Tooltip appears. | Taking space beside the page is Dock and undock; a deeper Breadcrumb level is Drill. | Call-off confirm Modal: Cancel reverses, Confirm carries on. |

| Flag | slides in from the top-right corner | leaves the way it came, by the exit rules in Physics |

A menu is opened dozens of times a day, so it changes opacity and nothing else: the same fade in and out for every member of the family, instant when opened from the keyboard. The in-app Reduced setting shows it with no animation, and the system's reduced-motion setting keeps the fade. Only the floating layers above (Modal, Panel, Flag) move.

A Modal opens only from user action, moves focus to its first input as the motion starts, and never stacks a second Modal (a confirm swaps content in place). Scale is for floating layers only.

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This sits beside your work, and your work made room for it. | A panel takes space beside the page. | Floating above the page is Open an overlay. | The AI Panel docks on the right of Sessions and the table narrows. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | width, making room | `spatial.slow` | 0 |
| Panel | slides in from its edge | `spatial.slow` | 0 |
| Panel content | opacity in | `appearance.fast` | When the page is about 90% done making room |

Below the docking width the Panel slides over with a Blanket.

## Feedback

Nothing moves place. One element answers, or asks to be looked at.

### Update a value or state

| Tells the person | When | Not | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This value changed. | A status, Saving to Saved, or a count. | If the element joins or leaves, it is Add or remove. | Shift swap accepted: session goes from Called off to Covered. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Status | color | `appearance.default` | 0 |
| Number, first view | rolls once | `spatial.fast` | 0 |
| Number, later updates | fades to the new value | `appearance.fast` | 0 |

A number never overshoots.

| Tells the person | When | PLUS case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Look here. | The row you jumped to, a warning that appeared, a field that needs fixing. | Scroll to "Escalation" marks the heading. |

| What | Property | Token | Starts |

In a field, check when focus leaves and never flag the person while they type.

A failure that is the system's gets a message that makes room, never a shake.

A page gets a summary at the top and focus on the first error, never a shake.

# Radius

How round a corner is, and which rule decides it. Every corner reads a token.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Radius.mdx`

## Overview

Nine rules decide a corner. Take the first one that matches. A radius comes only from a token.

1. **Window edge:** 0. A Page in the Frame, and a Modal footer that runs to the Modal's sides.
2. **Pill:** `--radius-full`. A pill keeps its shape wherever it sits.
3. **Joined group:** the outer corners round; the seams inside stay square.
4. **Tight grid:** `--radius-md` (4).
5. **Nested:** inner radius = outer radius − padding. Fix an uneven corner with padding, not a new radius.
6. **Button in a field:** the field's radius − 4, so 6 default and 4 compact.
7. **Other controls:** the control's height ÷ 4 (`Radius / Control`).
8. **Templates:** Modal and Card 16; Popup, Table and boxes inside a page 12; the smallest nested visual 8.
9. **Focus ring:** the element's radius + the ring's offset.

## Scale

Semantic radius and control-radius tokens point directly at their matching Space step (`--radius-control-lg` is 0.625rem, 10). The scale below shows the resulting values; `--radius-full` is the only literal. Components bind the semantic tokens below.

## Controls

A control rounds at a quarter of its height, so the corner reads the same at every size.

| Control height (px) | Radius (px) | Token | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24 | 6 | `--radius-control-sm` | Tooltip, compact tab |
| 32 | 8 | `--radius-control-md` | Compact field, tab, option row, Sidebar row |
| 40 | 10 | `--radius-control-lg` | Default field |

A Tile follows the same quarter: 20 rounds at 5 and 40 at 10. A square Avatar rounds at a quarter of its size, up to 16.

## Buttons

A button sits 4 inside a field, so it rounds at the field's radius minus 4: 6 at 32 (in a 40 field) and 4 at 24 (in a 32 compact field).

`--button-radius-default` and `--button-radius-compact` apply whether the button sits in a field or not. This covers Button, Icon button, Split button and every button built on them.

A button group rounds its outer corners and keeps the inner seams square.

## Templates

Each template owns a token. A Page sits square in the Frame; a Card rounds at 16.

| Template | Radius (px) | Token |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page in the Frame | 0 | — |
| Modal | 16 | `--modal-radius` |
| Card | 16 | `--card-radius` |
| Popup, menu, Flag | 12 | `--popup-radius` |
| Table | 12 | `--table-radius` |

A box inside a page (Comment, Code block, Section message, File upload) takes `--card-radius`, 16, like a Card. The smallest nested visual (a choice card, a spacious Status tag) rounds at 8 (`--radius-lg`).

### Window edge

Where a box meets the window or its parent's side, it takes 0. The Page runs to the Frame's edge, and a filled Modal footer runs to the Modal's sides, so its seam is square and the Modal's corner clips it.

## Nesting

A shape inset in a rounded box rounds at the box's radius minus the inset, so the gap between the curves stays even. Rows inset 4 in a 12 Popup take 8.

If the corners look uneven, change the padding, not the radius, so the inner radius lands on a step. A part flush with its parent's edge (a Table head row, a Card image) takes no radius of its own; the parent clips it.

### Pills

A pill is exempt from nesting and keeps `--radius-full` inside a Card, field or row.

## Small details

Small parts keep the two smallest steps wherever they sit. A tight grid, such as the days of a Calendar, rounds at 4 so a larger curve does not pinch the gap between neighbors.

| Radius (px) | Token | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | `--radius-sm` | Logo in a Tile, team avatar in a Tag |
| 4 | `--radius-md` | Count tag, Status tag, Checkbox, Link, Calendar day, Table loading bar |

## Focus ring

The focus ring sits 2 px outside the element (`--focus-ring-width`), so its radius is the element's radius + 2. [Border](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-border--docs#foundation-focus-ring) owns the ring's color and width. Radius is decoration: never let a corner alone signal state or meaning.

| Element | Radius (px) | Focus ring radius (px) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default button (32) | 6 | 8 |
| Compact button (24) | 4 | 6 |
| 24 control | 6 | 8 |
| 32 control | 8 | 10 |
| 40 field | 10 | 12 |
| Checkbox | 4 | 6 |

## Tokens

The `Radius` group names a step by size; `Radius / Control` names it by control height. `--frame-sidebar-row-radius` (8) rounds a Sidebar row. Template and component radius tokens sit in the tables above, and [Tokens: Spacing and size](?path=/docs/foundations-tokens-spacing-and-size--docs) lists the full ladder.

- `--radius-sm` (Radius/sm): Small details.
- `--radius-md` (Radius/md): Tight grids and small tags.
- `--radius-lg` (Radius/lg): The smallest nested visual.
- `--radius-xl` (Radius/xl): Popup, menu, Flag and Table.
- `--radius-xxl` (Radius/xxl): The largest templates.
- `--radius-full` (Radius/full): Pills.
- `--radius-control-sm` (Radius/Control/sm): 24 high controls.
- `--radius-control-md` (Radius/Control/md): 32 high controls.
- `--radius-control-lg` (Radius/Control/lg): 40 high controls.

## Do and don't

### Round an inner corner smaller than its parent

Do: Rows inset 4 in a 12 Popup take 8, so the gap between the curves stays even.
Don't: Rows at the Popup's own 12; their corners bulge toward its edge, and the inset looks uneven.

### Keep a component's own radius

Do: Both buttons keep the button radius, 6.
Don't: One button overridden to a pill; one component now has two shapes.

### Stay on the scale

Do: The Card at 16 and the tag at 4, both steps on the scale.
Don't: A Card at 14 and a tag at 5; off-scale values drift from every neighbor.

### Round a tight group at 4

Do: Tiles 2 apart at 4; the gaps stay straight.
Don't: The same tiles at 12; every gap pinches where the curves meet.

### Close with an Icon button

Use a subtle Icon button for close controls instead of a hand-built circle, whose corner, its states and its focus ring are all guesses.

Do: The subtle Icon button: the button radius, the ring and the states come with it.

Don't: A hand-built circle. Its corner, its states and its focus ring are all guesses.

### Read a token, never a px value

Do: The token follows the rules when a value moves.
Don't: A literal radius is right today and wrong after the next change, and the radius lint fails it.

# Sound

Sound marks the few moments worth hearing, and lands with the motion that shows them.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/SoundOverview.mdx`

## Overview

A sound plays where a moment matters and a tutor may be looking elsewhere: a Flag arriving, a step done, a sign-up confirmed. Every sound is synthesized in the browser from one material, a dry abacus bead, so there are no audio files.

## Principles

### Rare

Most moments are silent. A sound plays only where its registry row names one: When to play.

### Paired

Every sound has an on-screen change that says the same thing, so turning sound off loses nothing: Settings and accessibility.

### Landed

A sound lands when its motion lands: With motion.

### In key

Every sound is in one key, so any two can play back to back: Sounds.

## The nine sounds

Press one to hear it. The switch is the same setting the app reads; Sounds adds the three AI feedback sounds.

One switch turns all sound off, and no one misses anything when it is off.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/SoundSettings.mdx`

One setting turns every sound off. It is on by default and kept across visits. Nothing is opt-in, and reduced motion does not mute sound. Sound follows the device's volume.

## Pairing

Every sound pairs with an on-screen change that says the same thing: a Flag, a step checked, a message. Sound is never the only signal, so turning it off loses nothing.

## The student rule

A sound a student can hear is good news only. A concern never plays while a student can hear, and a shared moment, such as a goal reached, plays for both.

Every sound is in C major, tuned to whole-number ratios on . Milestone is tuned a fourth lower, on . Any two sounds can play back to back without clashing.

Length runs from the first notch to the last note falling silent. Tokens drop their `sound.` prefix elsewhere in the docs.

Each token sits on one of three levels, measured offline as its loudest 50 ms.

The registry names every moment that plays. Everything else is silent.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/SoundWhenToPlay.mdx`

- **Severity:** Error follows only a person's own submit or a job they started. Most confirmations stay silent; the registry names the ones that play.

Each row is a motion registry row with a `sound` cell: the token, when it plays and any condition. These moments are silent too, and have no registry row of their own:

A sound starts at its motion token's 90% time minus its pickup, so its first note lands as the motion reads as arrived. Under reduced motion it lands with the reduced motion instead.
