# Spacing

Four words space everything: pad, stack, inline and gutter. The template you are in picks the size.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/Spacing.mdx`

## Overview

Spacing is the empty space inside a component or template and between the things it holds. Its tokens name a job, not a size. Pick the template you are in (Page, Section, Card, Modal, Popup, Table or a control), then the job (pad around the content, stack between rows, inline between things side by side, gutter between cards on the grid), then the size. Every value is a dimension primitive; bind the token, never a primitive or a typed number.

```css
padding: var(--card-pad);           /* space-100 */
gap: var(--card-stack-md);          /* space-050 */
```

In Figma the same tokens live in `spacing / semantics` (Pad, Stack, Inline, Grid, Screen, Content) and `spacing / templates`; primitives are hidden from the picker.

## Principles

Space tells people what belongs together. Five ideas decide every gap on a page.

### Similarity

Things of equal weight sit close, one stack apart.

### Differentiation

When content changes kind, step up a tier so the change reads.

### Rhythm

Gaps grow from the inside out: smallest between a label and its field, larger inside a card, largest inside a section.

### Hierarchy

A heading takes the larger stack of its tier; never add space by hand.

### White space

Pad a modal on every side, so nothing touches its edge.

## Tokens

A token reads as template, then job, then size: Section/stack-md in Figma is --section-stack-md in code. A template with one job skips the size (--page-pad).

| Word | Means | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pad | Space between an edge and the content inside it, the same on all four sides | --card-pad · space-100 |
| pad-x · pad-y | Only when the axes differ, as on a control | --pad-x-md · space-075, --pad-y-md · space-0375 |
| stack | Vertical gap between rows, chosen by use, never by the size of what holds them | --section-stack-md · space-100 |
| inline | Horizontal gap between things side by side | --modal-inline-sm · space-050 |
| gutter | Gap between grid columns, and between cards side by side on the grid | --grid-gutter · space-100 |

Margin, slot and viewport are never token words: a page margin is the Page pad. Corners live on Radius; heights and widths live on Dimensions.

## Pad

Pad is the space between an edge and the content inside it. A template pads the same on every side. A control pads wider than tall, because its height comes first: the label is a 20 line and the pad fills what is left.

### A control

pad-y = (height − 20) ÷ 2, so space-0125 at a 24 control and space-0375 at 32. A 40 field centers its content. Pad-x is always the larger.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--pad-x-xs` | `Pad/pad-x-xs` | `space-025` | Tag, Status, Count |
| `--pad-x-sm` | `Pad/pad-x-sm` | `space-050` | Compact 24 controls |
| `--pad-x-md` | `Pad/pad-x-md` | `space-075` | Default 32 controls, fields |
| `--pad-x-lg` | `Pad/pad-x-lg` | `space-100` | Spacious 48 controls |
| `--pad-y-sm` | `Pad/pad-y-sm` | `space-0125` | Compact 24 controls |
| `--pad-y-md` | `Pad/pad-y-md` | `space-0375` | Default 32 controls |
| `--pad-y-lg` | `Pad/pad-y-lg` | `space-050` | Spacious controls |

### A template

A Card, Modal or Popup carries its own pad on every side. Every Card pads space-100 at every size, so cards differ by width, not by pad. A component that pads like a card but is not a template, such as a Section message or a File upload, takes the compact Card pad, space-100. A Section has no pad.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--card-pad` | `Card/pad` | `space-100` | Every side of every Card, at every size |
| `--modal-pad` | `Modal/pad` | `space-125` | Every side of a Modal |
| `--popup-pad` | `Popup/pad` | `space-100` | Popup, Flag |
| `--frame-sidebar-pad` | — | `space-075` | The Sidebar, every side |
| `--page-pad` | `Page/pad` | `space-150` | Every side of the Page |

### A table cell

Cells pad space-025 top and bottom and space-050 across. In a plain table the first cell sits flush with the table edge, so its text lines up with the heading above.

## Stack

Stack is the vertical gap between rows. It comes in tiers that grow from a control out to the page, and each tier has sm, md and lg. Pick the tier from the template the rows sit in, then the step from how closely they relate.

| Tier | sm | md | lg | Used between |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control | `space-025` | `space-050` | `space-075` | Label and field, field and help text |
| Card | `space-025` | `space-050` | `space-075` | Title, body and footer inside a card |
| Modal | `space-050` | `space-100` | `space-150` | Header, body and footer; fields and groups |
| Section | `space-050` | `space-100` | `space-150` | Heading, body and footer of a section |
| Page | `space-100` | `space-150` | `space-250` | Sections; space-250 before a new topic |

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--stack-sm · md · lg · xl · 2xl · 3xl` | `Stack/stack-sm · md · lg · xl · 2xl · 3xl` | `space-025 · space-050 · space-075 · space-100 · space-150 · space-200` | Inside a control; xl, 2xl and 3xl for the larger general gaps |
| `--card-stack-sm · md · lg` | `Card/stack-…` | `space-025 · space-050 · space-075` | Inside a card |
| `--modal-stack-sm · md · lg` | `Modal/stack-…` | `space-050 · space-100 · space-150` | Inside a modal |
| `--section-stack-sm · md · lg` | `Section/stack-…` | `space-050 · space-100 · space-150` | Inside a section |
| `--page-stack-sm · md · lg` | `Page/stack-…` | `space-100 · space-150 · space-250` | Between sections |

## Inline

Inline is the horizontal gap between things side by side: an icon and its label, two buttons, a tag and the text after it. It follows the same tiers as stack: inside one card, an icon sits space-025 from a Button’s label, space-025 from the card title, and the actions sit space-050 apart.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--inline-sm · md · lg · xl · 2xl · 3xl` | `Inline/inline-sm · md · lg · xl · 2xl · 3xl` | `space-025 · space-050 · space-075 · space-100 · space-150 · space-200` | Inside a control: icon and label; xl, 2xl and 3xl for the larger general gaps |
| `--card-inline-sm · md · lg` | `Card/inline-…` | `space-025 · space-050 · space-075` | Side by side inside a card |
| `--modal-inline-sm · md · lg` | `Modal/inline-…` | `space-050 · space-100 · space-150` | Footer actions, side by side |

## Gutter

Gutter is the gap between grid columns, and so between cards side by side on the grid. It is one value at every width, space-100, so cards stay on the columns when the screen changes. Inside a card the grid stops and stack and inline take over.

| Token | Figma | Value | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--grid-gutter` | `Grid/gutter` | `space-100` | Between columns, and between cards on the grid |

## Template tokens

Every template has its own tokens, so a value is read from where it sits.

| Template | Token | Value | What it spaces |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame | `--frame-sidebar-pad` | `space-075` | The Sidebar, every side |
|  | `--frame-sidebar-row-gap` | `space-0125` | Between Sidebar rows (32 tall), so hover fills never touch |
|  | `--frame-sidebar-group-gap` | `space-100` | Between Sidebar groups |
| Page | `--page-pad` | `space-150` | The Page, every side; the content grid’s margin |
|  | `--page-stack-sm · md · lg` | `space-100 · space-150 · space-250` | Between sections |
| Section | `--section-stack-sm · md · lg` | `space-050 · space-100 · space-150` | Heading, body, footer. A Section has no fill and no pad. |
|  | `--section-min-width-main · side` | 480 · 224 | The narrowest a split’s columns get before they stack |
| Card | `--card-pad` | `space-100` | Every side, every card size |
|  | `--card-stack · --card-inline (sm · md · lg)` | `space-025 · space-050 · space-075` | Inside the card |
|  | `--card-min-width-sm · md · lg` | 224 · 304 · 480 | Decides cards per row |
| Table | `--table-pad-x-cell · pad-y-cell` | `space-050 · space-025` | Every cell |
|  | `--table-indent` | `space-150` | A nested row’s first cell |
|  | `--table-pad-x-footer` | `space-100` | The table footer |
| Blanket | `--blanket-pad-x · pad-y` | `space-100 · space-400` | Around a modal; pad-y drops to 24 on screens under 640 tall |
| Modal | `--modal-pad` | `space-125` | Every side |
|  | `--modal-stack · --modal-inline (sm · md · lg)` | `space-050 · space-100 · space-150` | Inside the modal |
| Popup | `--popup-pad` | `space-100` | Popup, Flag |
|  | `--popup-gap-screen` | `space-050` | The nearest a popup comes to the screen edge |
|  | `--dropdown-menu-pad` | `space-025` | Around the rows of a menu |
|  | `--tooltip-pad-y` | `space-025` | Above and below a tooltip’s text |

Template pads and gaps step by 4. A value finer than 4 stays inside a component; the one template exception is the Sidebar row gap of 2.

## Usage

### Group first, then assign tokens

Group from the inside out; each step out is one tier up. In a modal form: a label and its field space-050 (--stack-md); related fields space-100 (--modal-stack-md); a new group space-150 (--modal-stack-lg); header, body and footer space-100 (--modal-stack-md); actions side by side space-050 (--modal-inline-sm).

### Be consistent first

Use the same token for the same relationship everywhere. A slightly-off value used consistently reads better than a perfect value used once.

### Start generous, then tighten

When a gap is unclear, start a step larger and step down until related things read together. A little too much space reads better than a little too little.

### Space between groups is never smaller than space inside them

The gap between two groups is at least the gap within each, or the groups blur together.

### The gap inside never exceeds the pad

Things inside a card, a modal or a control sit no further apart than that card, modal or control pads, or the content looks loose inside a tight edge.

### Pick by context, not by number

A Card token inside a card, a Section token inside a section, a Stack or Inline token inside a control. Two gaps with the same value can still be different tokens. Never type a number.

## Do and don’t

Do: Group by proximity: related rows close, a tier between groups.
Don't: One gap everywhere: nothing groups.

Do: Inside a Card, read a Card token.
Don't: A Page token inside a Card: a gap from the wrong tier.

Do: Bind a token.
Don't: Type a number: off the ladder, and it drifts.

Do: Keep the gap inside a card no larger than its pad, so the content holds together.
Don't: A gap bigger than the pad: the content drifts apart and the edge feels tight.

Do: Pad a control wider than tall, about two to one, so it reads as one line.
Don't: Equal pad on every side: the control turns into a block.

## Accessibility

- Spacing never carries meaning alone: name every group with a heading, label or legend.
- Keep one stack tier per context across a template, so the structure reads the same everywhere.
- Leave room for the focus ring: a control never sits flush against an edge that clips it.
- Sizes are rem, so every gap grows with the reader’s font setting.

## Related

| Page | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Dimensions | The ladder every gap reads from; heights and widths |
| Grid | Columns, gutters, content caps, modal widths |
| Radius | Corners, and how a menu’s rows round inside it |
| Border | Stroke widths |
| Typography | The 20 line that sets every control’s pad |
| Elevation | Which surface each layer sits on |

Roles such as text, surface and border give a palette step a job and switch with the Light, Dark and high-contrast modes ([Color](?path=/docs/foundations-visual-color--docs)). A screen binds a role, never a palette step.

Shadow and opacity for how high a surface sits, and the layer order for what stacks over what.

Every token in one place: search by name, narrow by collection, tier and scope, and copy a name.

**Kind:** Foundation

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/styles/TokensLibrary.mdx`

Tokens form a ladder. A screen binds the semantic token whose job matches, never a primitive, so one decision is made once and every mode follows.

| Primitive | Raw palette hues, rem scales and spring curves | Semantic tokens only; hidden from features |

All motion in PLUS is a spring ([Physics](?path=/docs/foundations-expression-motion-physics--docs)). A primitive is a stiffness and damping pair; a semantic token names the job, such as a fast spatial move or an appearance fade, and aliases one primitive.

Space, radius, stroke and size steps, from the raw scale to what a page, a card or a control reads.

Never type a raw size or detach a style. ### Body, metric and weights - **Body/large (16/24):** long-form reading such as lessons, help articles and quotes (quotes use the body family; never add a decorative face). - **Body/default (14/20):** default interface text and control labels (sets the 24, 32 and 40 control heights). Do not use heading styles inside components; use body with a heavier weight instead. - **Body/small (12/16):** secondary meta text, tags, statuses, counts and tooltips. - **Metric (large, medium, small):** featured numbers such as session counts or scores. - **Paragraph spacing:** space blocks with Section and stack tokens (Spacing), never a paragraph-spacing style. | Style | Size/line | Weight | Role | Sample | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Body/default/regular | 14/20 | 400 | Paragraphs and descriptions | | | Body/default/medium | 14/20 | 500 | Control labels and text beside an icon | | | Body/default/bold | 14/20 | 600 | Inline emphasis, used sparingly | | ## In code Set component text with `font: var(--heading-sm)` or `font: var(--body-default)`, and icon glyphs with `--icon-sm`, `--icon-md` or `--icon-lg` (Iconography). The metric classes also set tabular figures. Component stylesheets use `font: var(--…)` directly, and add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` to a metric. ```jsx

Helper text

Section title

``` ## Heading levels Headings step down one size per nesting level; containers use a fixed title size. Reserve `Heading/xxlarge` (32) and `Heading/xlarge` (28) for heroes, empty states and metric-heavy dashboards, never a page title. Use a heading style rather than bold text or a size change, because heading styles carry the structure assistive technology reads. | Level | Style | | --- | --- | | Page title | Heading/large · 24 · the page's one h1 | | Section title | Heading/medium · 20 · h2 | | Subsection title | Heading/small · 16 · h3 | | Modal title | Heading/medium · 20 · the modal's h1, named by aria-labelledby | | Card, popup and flag title | Heading/xsmall · 14 · one level below its section | | Group label (menu group, table head) | Heading/xxsmall · 12 · a group or head cell, never a heading tag | Every page has one `h1` (visually hidden when a tab strip replaces a visible page header). Never set regular or bold weight, or a heading style, on a button or tab label. A Sidebar tab is a navigation row: its label is regular weight at rest and medium when selected. Do: Body/default/medium on a button or tab label. Don't: Regular or bold weight, or a heading style, on a button or tab label. ## Code `Code/default` (12/16, Noto Sans Mono) sets code samples, token names and property values. In CSS, `var(--code-default)` sets `0.875em` of the parent size so inline code scales with surrounding text. ## Truncate and wrap Names and titles truncate; primary content wraps. Never shrink font size to fit a long string. - **Titles and names** truncate to one line with an ellipsis; expose the full text on hover or in the detail view. - **Descriptions** clamp at 3 lines unless configured to wrap. - **Session notes and help answers** wrap in full. Table cells truncate by default and opt into wrap per column. ### Truncate a long name to one line A student name in a roster row. Do: One line with an ellipsis. The Status keeps its place. Don't: The name wraps onto extra lines and makes the row taller than its neighbors. ## Do and don't ### Use a heading style Introduce a section with a heading style, not with bold body text. Do: Heading/small, tagged as the section's heading. Don't: Bold body text looks like a heading but carries no structure. ### Do not skip heading levels Headings step down one level at a time. Do: h1, then h2, then h3. Don't: An h3 straight after the h1 skips the h2. ## Headings, numbers and mono ### Headings Every heading level is Noto Sans at weight 600. Size, line height and tracking step down together (sizes are in the type scale above, tracking in the tokens table, and the level for each role in Heading levels). Semibold at 28 and 32 sits close to bold body text. Keep 600 and do not add a 700 weight. ### Numbers Metric styles are Noto Sans 600 with tabular figures. Use the `.num` class, or `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, for numbers that line up vertically: table columns, times in schedules and timelines, and counts in lists. Running text keeps proportional figures. A time or duration ("3:30 to 4:30", "12 min") takes the body or heading style of its context, never mono. Do: Metric/large for the figure. Don't: Heading/medium for a number. ### Mono Noto Sans Mono is for code, token names, property values and machine IDs such as a session ID or a URL. Never use it for metrics, times or counts: mono digits are wide and read as a data dump. `Code/default` is 0.875em of its parent, and in a table it pairs with `Body/small`. Do: Metric/large for the count, mono for the session ID. The view bar above never moves. | | | confirm | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A destructive action opens a Modal. Confirm fades it and carries on: the row's status changes color, and a Flag confirms. | `sound.done.sent` on land: only a call-off or lead request sent; other confirms stay silent | | cancel | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Cancel reverses the Modal's entrance one speed faster. | | | undo | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Keep and Undo sit beside the change, tinted, until the person moves on. Undo reverses the Add or remove that made the change. | | ## Best practices ### Give an area one Primary button. {#give-an-area-one-primary-button} **Checked:** Automatic The Primary is the main call to action or a form's submit. A second main action is Default beside it; a second Primary makes neither read as the next step. The AI appearance follows the same rule, one per region, and only for an action that calls AI. Do: One Primary, with the other action Default beside it. Don't: Two Primary buttons in one row: neither reads as the next step. ### Left-align buttons under a page form and right-align them in a Modal or a multi-step task. {#left-align-buttons-under-a-page-form-and-right-align-them-in-a-modal-or-a-multi-step-task} **Checked:** Automatic On a page the Primary comes first, read in the same direction as the fields. In a layer the Primary is furthest right, where the eye ends. Stacked buttons put the Primary on top. Never top-aligned. Do: Primary first, then Cancel, left-aligned under the fields. Don't: The buttons at the far end of the page, away from the fields, with the Primary last. ### Fill the four tracks in a Modal footer and keep it 48 high. {#fill-the-four-tracks-in-a-modal-footer-and-keep-it-48-high} **Checked:** Automatic FooterActions divides the footer into four equal tracks: filled buttons 48 high, Primary in the last track. One button takes the right half. A side action leads as a link and takes no track. A Panel's editing footer and a multi-step task's footer use the same component. Do: Two buttons filling the footer's four tracks. Don't: Small buttons in a group, with spare footer around them instead of filling the tracks. ### Keep the footer where it is. {#keep-the-footer-where-it-is} **Checked:** Automatic Header and footer stay pinned while the body scrolls. A blocked submit, a server message and a sending button change the body or a button, never the footer's size or place. A sending button swaps its label for a spinner in place and keeps its width; only that button disables, and the secondary action stays live. ### Keep Close an icon button, and use Cancel only where there is no Close. {#keep-close-an-icon-button-and-use-cancel-only-where-there-is-no-close} **Checked:** Automatic Close ends a layer and lives in its header, or by Save and exit in a multi-step task. In a Modal and Panel the corner Close dismisses, so their footers carry real actions (such as Discard or Keep) and no Cancel. A page form has no Close, so it keeps a subtle Cancel. A Popup holds no form, so it has no Cancel; Escape or a click outside dismisses it. ### Make Cancel Subtle on page forms. {#make-cancel-subtle-on-page-forms} **Checked:** Automatic Beside a Primary it is already clear the row is interactive, so Cancel steps back as Subtle. Cancel may be a link where a button would compete. In a Modal or Panel footer every filled track is a button, so the secondary action takes the Default fill to read as one. "Not now", "Skip" and "Keep editing" are that secondary action, never Subtle and never in the leading slot. ### Say Clear in a menu and Reset filters everywhere else. {#say-clear-in-a-menu-and-reset-filters-everywhere-else} **Checked:** Automatic The words and where they sit: Filtering › Say Clear in a menu and Reset filters everywhere else. ### Confirm a copy with a Copied tooltip, not a Flag. {#confirm-a-copy-with-a-copied-tooltip-not-a-flag} **Checked:** Automatic The tooltip opens on the Copy button the moment the value is on the clipboard and leaves on its own. Flags stay for events that happened somewhere else. ### Edit one value inline and the whole record from More. {#edit-one-value-inline-and-the-whole-record-from-more} **Checked:** Review A value read far more than changed takes `InlineEdit`: a pencil on hover and focus, saved on its own. The record's More menu includes Edit, which opens the form host the Forms pattern picks. Never put inline edits inside a form that has its own Save. ### Name a destructive action by its tier. {#name-a-destructive-action-by-its-tier} **Checked:** Review Active: it can be undone, Discard (or a real alternative) and a Primary. Active with Danger: a delete, the action in Danger. Danger with the name typed: a delete that cannot be undone, the field caption asks for the name and the Danger button enables once it matches, with no tooltip. Remove, which takes something out of a group it can return to, is Default, not Danger. The Modal that raises the confirm: Modal. ### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected. {#turn-the-head-row-into-the-bulk-bar-when-rows-are-selected} **Checked:** Automatic The bar and its words: Section › Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected. ### Link one action in a card, and pair two. {#link-one-action-in-a-card-and-pair-two} **Checked:** Review A card's buttons hug the start of its footer. One action that goes somewhere is a link; two actions are a compact Default pair with no Primary. # Disabled When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person: actions stay enabled and explain, and what a role can never use is hidden. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Disabled/Disabled.mdx` ## The four answers Try these options in order; disable only when the earlier options do not fit. - **Enabled, and it explains.** An action stays pressable and says what is missing when pressed. It disables only while sending. - **Disabled with a visible reason.** A field or option that waits on a prerequisite the person can fix here. The reason is the caption or the option's description line. - **Read-only.** Content people must read but cannot change. It has its own pattern. - **Hidden.** What this role can never use is left out, not dimmed. The one exception is the Toolkit, locked during onboarding and never hidden. ## Key cases ## Usage Use Disabled when something on the page cannot be used right now. Reach for it last: an enabled action that explains is better than a dimmed one, read-only is better for content people must read, and hiding is right for what a role can never use. | The situation | Answer | Where the reason goes | | --- | --- | --- | | A submit with fields missing | Enabled; pressing it marks the fields | Field errors | | A button while its action sends | Disabled with a spinner in place | None; it is self-evident | | A field that waits on another field on this screen | Disabled | The caption: "Choose a school first" | | An option that cannot apply | Disabled | The option's description line | | A prerequisite that blocks the main action or several items | Disabled, plus a warning `SectionMessage` above | The message says how to turn it on | | Back on step one; Danger until the name matches | Disabled | None, or the field caption | | Content this person must read but cannot change | Read-only | The caption | | An action this role can never take | Hidden | None | | The Toolkit during onboarding | Locked, visible | The Sidebar line that says what unlocks it | ## Alternatives - For a value this person cannot change but must read, follow Read-only. - For what a role can never use, leave the control, page or Sidebar item out. - For a submit that is not ready, keep it enabled and let validation explain; see Forms. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Caption: "Choose a school first." | "Disabled", "Not available". | | Option description: "Ms. Ortiz has a session then." | A faded option with no line. | | Warning message: "Add a school to this group to schedule sessions." with "Add school". | "Some actions are unavailable." | | Toolkit: "Complete your assigned training to unlock the Toolkit." | "Locked". | ## Accessibility - A disabled control leaves the tab order and gets no events; the reason beside it is ordinary text a screen reader reads with the field, tied through the caption. - The warning `SectionMessage` is announced when it appears. - Disabled controls fade; the caption keeps full contrast, so the reason stays readable. ## Related - Read-only: use when the value must be read. - Forms: use for the enabled submit. - Common actions: use for the sending button. - Navigation: use for the Sidebar's locked Toolkit. - `Button`, `IconButton`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `DropdownMenu`, `SectionMessage`: the components. ## Best practices ### Keep actions enabled and explain what is missing when pressed. {#keep-actions-enabled-and-explain-what-is-missing-when-pressed} **Checked:** Automatic A disabled button gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing an action that cannot run yet marks what is missing. A button disables only while sending. A form's submit follows Forms. ### Disable a field or option only for a prerequisite the person can fix on the same screen. {#disable-a-field-or-option-only-for-a-prerequisite-the-person-can-fix-on-the-same-screen} **Checked:** Review Group waits on School; a time slot waits on a date. Anything blocked by something off this screen is enabled and explains, read-only, or hidden. ### Put the reason in visible text where the cause is. {#put-the-reason-in-visible-text-where-the-cause-is} **Checked:** Automatic The field caption or the option's description line. When the prerequisite blocks the main action or several items, a warning `SectionMessage` above says how to turn it on. Self-evident cases need no reason: Back on the first step. ### Keep the reason in text on the page, never in a tooltip on a disabled control. {#keep-the-reason-in-text-on-the-page-never-in-a-tooltip-on-a-disabled-control} **Checked:** Automatic A disabled control gets no events and is absent on touch, so a tooltip would never open for the people who need it most. A disabled control keeps its default behavior and leaves the tab order. Do: The reason as the caption: "Choose a school first". Don't: The reason in a tooltip on a faded field: it never opens on touch. ### Hide what a role can never use. {#hide-what-a-role-can-never-use} **Checked:** Review An action a tutor can never take, such as deleting a school, is left out, not dimmed. A breadcrumb level the person cannot open is left out. Only a change of role brings it back. Do: An action a tutor can never take is left out of the menu. Don't: A faded "Delete school" that a tutor will never be able to press. ### Lock the Toolkit during onboarding and keep it visible. {#lock-the-toolkit-during-onboarding-and-keep-it-visible} **Checked:** Review Tutors see what training unlocks. The Sidebar item shows a lock and a line that says what unlocks it; the line is Planned . ### Make content people must read read-only, not disabled. {#make-content-people-must-read-read-only-not-disabled} **Checked:** Automatic Disabled fades and leaves the tab order; read-only stays readable at full contrast. The two are never swapped. ## In code From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Disabled`. ```jsx import { Button } from '@/components'; function DisabledExample() { return (

# Empty What a view shows when it has nothing to show. It says what belongs here, why it is empty, and what to do next; it never leaves a blank area and never apologizes. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Empty/Empty.mdx` ## The types Choose among four situations to set the wording and available action. See Empty state for props. - **First use.** Nothing has been added yet. Say what will appear and give the one action that adds it, if this person can. - **No matches.** A search or filter matched nothing. Name what is active and offer "Reset filters". - **All done.** The person finished everything. Say so, and when more arrives. No action. - **Can't show.** The data could not load, or this person has no access. Say why and give a way forward: Try again, or who can help. ## Where it sits The place sets the spacing and the alignment. The words stay the same. - **A full page.** The block lines up with the page title, left-aligned with no wide margin, the picture above the text. The block is centered today. - **In a table.** The empty state replaces the whole table: no column headers, no footer. The block is centered and its text stays left-aligned. `EmptyState` centers the text today. - **In a card.** Compact: a smaller picture and heading, the block centered in the card, the text left-aligned. Several cards at once drop their pictures and use Subtle actions. The text is centered today. - **In a Panel.** The Details Panel when its record was removed: the block at the top of the body, with a way back. ## Key cases ## Usage Use Empty when a list, table, card, Panel or page has no records to show, a search or filter returns nothing, a queue is finished, or the content exists but cannot be shown to this person. Show Loading instead while content is on its way, and leave one blank field blank. | Type | The view is empty because | Say | Action | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | First use | Nothing has been added yet: a new group with no students | What will appear here and how it gets here | One Primary, if this person can add something; otherwise none | | No matches | A search or filter matched nothing | Which search or filters are active | "Reset filters" as a Default button; it also clears the search | | All done | The person finished everything: every reflection is reviewed | That they are done, and when more arrives | None | | Can't show | No access, or the data could not load | Why, in plain words | Try again, or who can help; never an action they cannot take | ## Alternatives - For content still on its way, follow Loading: a skeleton, not an empty state. - For a save or request that failed while the view still has content, use `SectionMessage`; the Errors pattern says where each failure shows. - For one blank value in a record, show a dash, not an empty state. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Heading: "No students in this group yet". | "No data", "Nothing here", "Oops!". | | One line: "Add students to schedule sessions and track their progress." | A paragraph about the feature. | | Action names the next step: "Add students". | "Get started", "Continue". | | No matches: "No students match these filters." with "Reset filters". | "Clear filters", "Clear all". | | All done: "Every reflection is reviewed. New ones arrive after Friday's sessions." | "All caught up! 🎉" | | Warmer for students, plainer for admins: "Your tutor will add notes after your session." and "No notes for this group." | One voice for everyone. | ## Accessibility - The heading is one level below the section that holds it, so it joins the page outline. - The picture is decorative: an empty alt, or `aria-hidden` on an icon. - When a filter or search empties a list, the result count is announced in a polite live region ("0 students"). - Focus stays where it was. Never move it to the empty state's button. ## Parts | Part | Component | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | The block | Empty state | Picture or icon, header, one line and the action; `spacing` is `default` for a view and `compact` for a table body or card. | | The action | Button | `primaryAction` takes one Button; a No matches action is Default. | | Table slot | Table | `emptyState` (the Table template) and `emptyView` / `noResultsView` (`DynamicTable`) take the block and replace the whole table, header and footer included. | | In a Panel | Panel | The record-gone state at the top of the body. | ## Related - Loading: use before you know the view is empty. - Errors: use for the words in a Can't show state. - Filtering: use for where No matches comes from, and the "Reset filters" wording. - Search: use for a search that matches nothing. - Section: use for the header rows that stay above a replaced table. ## Best practices ### Show an `EmptyState` in any view that has no records. {#show-an-emptystate-in-any-view-that-has-no-records} **Checked:** Review Never a blank area or a bare "No results": a blank reads as broken or still loading. Do: Say what belongs here and give the one action that fills it. Don't: A bare string in an empty box: broken, loading or empty, nobody can tell. ### Lay the text out as a left-aligned block. {#lay-the-text-out-as-a-left-aligned-block} **Checked:** Review The picture above, then the heading, one line and the action, all on one left edge. On a full page the block lines up with the page title; inside a table or a card the block is centered and its text stays left-aligned. The text column never runs wide. `EmptyState` centers its text today. ### Replace the whole table with the empty state. {#replace-the-whole-table-with-the-empty-state} **Checked:** Review No column headers and no footer while the table is empty; the Section's header rows above stay, so the person can change the view, search or reset. A "No matches" state offers "Reset filters". Do: The whole table replaced; the header rows stay. Don't: Column headers and a footer over nothing, with a centered paragraph. ### Give at most one Primary action. {#give-at-most-one-primary-action} **Checked:** Review The second action is Default and never stands alone. When two or more empty states can show on one screen, none of them uses a Primary; their actions are Subtle. ### Offer only an action this person can take. {#offer-only-an-action-this-person-can-take} **Checked:** Review If they cannot add anything, show no button. A button that leads to "You don't have permission" is a dead end. ### Write the heading as what belongs here. {#write-the-heading-as-what-belongs-here} **Checked:** Review "No students in this group yet". The view is empty, not wrong, so the heading carries no "Sorry", no "Oops" and no code. ### Mark the picture as decorative. {#mark-the-picture-as-decorative} **Checked:** Automatic Screen readers skip it and read the heading first; the words carry the meaning. The `EmptyState` hides its picture and icon from assistive technology, and its heading sits one level below the section that holds it. ### Name the active search or filters in a No matches state. {#name-the-active-search-or-filters-in-a-no-matches-state} **Checked:** Review The person may not remember a filter set last week. "No students match these filters" with "Reset filters" is the way out. ### Use an illustration once and an icon where it repeats. {#use-an-illustration-once-and-an-icon-where-it-repeats} **Checked:** Review An illustration for a full view a person meets once, such as a new tutor's first day; an icon on anything that repeats, such as a card on a home page. Illustrations arrive with the character work . ## In code From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Empty`. ```jsx import { Button, EmptyState, StaticTable } from '@/components'; import { Table } from '@/templates'; function EmptyExample() { return ( } /> }>
); } ```
guides.design-system/agent-views/patterns/Error:
# Errors

Where a failure shows and what it says: the place follows what failed, and the message is words, never a code or color alone.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Errors/Errors.mdx`

## By what failed

Give each failure one home near its cause. Key cases shows the two submit failures: blocked and rejected.

- **A field.** The error on the field, after blur. It clears once the rule is met: Forms.
- **A view that could not load.** The error in the empty-state slot, with Try again. The header rows stay.
- **No access.** The same slot, saying who can help. No action the person cannot take.
- **A background job.** A danger Flag that stays, with Try again.
- **The whole page.** A danger Banner for a condition that applies to everything on the page, for as long as it holds.
- **A menu's options.** A "Couldn't load options" row with Retry, in the menu itself.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Errors whenever something failed and the person needs to know. Put the message where the cause is, say what happened and what to do, and leave the rest of the page working. Severity comes from the component that carries the message, not from louder words.

| What failed | Where it shows | Stays until | Offers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One field's value | On the field, after blur | The rule is met | What to fix |
| A submit with fields missing | On each field; focus moves to the first; a Modal stays open | The fields are fixed | What to fix |
| A submit the server rejected | Danger `SectionMessage` at the top of the form, plus field errors | Dismissed or fixed | What happened, what to do |
| A view's content could not load | The empty-state slot | It loads | Try again |
| This person has no access | The empty-state slot | Access changes | Who can help |
| A job in the background | Danger `Flag`, top right, no autohide | Try again resolves it | Try again |
| A condition on the whole page | Danger `Banner` at its tier | The condition ends | A link if there is one |
| A menu's options | A "Couldn't load options" row in the menu | Retry succeeds | Retry |

## Alternatives

- For a caution before something goes wrong, use a warning `SectionMessage`; see Disabled.
- For a view that is simply empty, follow the Empty pattern; it holds the slot a load failure takes.
- For a decision the person must make before going on, use Modal, not an error.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Field: "Enter a full email, like name@school.org". | "Invalid", "Required field", "Error 422". |
| Rejected: "Couldn't add the student. Check the fields below and try again." | "Something went wrong." |
| Load: "Couldn't load this week's sessions." with "Try again". | "Failed to fetch /sessions". |
| No access: "Only Lincoln's supervisor can open these notes." | "403 Forbidden", "You don't have permission". |
| Flag: "Couldn't save your session note." with "Try again". | "Save failed!" |
| Own it: "We lost the connection." | "The connection was lost by the user." |

## Accessibility

- A field error is announced and sets `aria-invalid`; a group's one error is announced once.
- A `SectionMessage` announces assertively when it appears; a danger `Flag` is announced as an urgent message. A `Banner` is a status.
- Move focus to the first field that needs fixing when a submit is blocked.
- The error icon is decorative; the words say "couldn't", "missing" or "failed".

## Related

- Forms: use for when a field is checked.
- Empty: use for the slot a load failure takes.
- Notifications: use for the Flag and Banner tiers.
- Loading: use for a menu's Loading row before it fails.
- Disabled: use for a caution before something goes wrong.
- `SectionMessage`, `Flag`, `Banner`, `EmptyState`, `TextField`: the components.

## Best practices

### Validate a field when it loses focus and clear the error once the rule is met. {#validate-a-field-when-it-loses-focus-and-clear-the-error-once-the-rule-is-met}

**Checked:** Automatic

The error sits on the field and says what to fix. Forms holds when a field is checked.

### Say what to fix on the field, in words. {#say-what-to-fix-on-the-field-in-words}

**Checked:** Automatic

The message sits right under the invalid field and names the fix. The red border supports the words and never replaces them.

Do: Say what to fix, on the field, in words.
Don't: A red border alone, with its words in a tooltip.

### Keep a blocked submit in the same Modal. {#keep-a-blocked-submit-in-the-same-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Mark the field and move focus to it; never a second dialog for the error. A single shake is Planned . Forms holds the whole rule.

### Show a rejected submit as a danger SectionMessage at the top of the form. {#show-a-rejected-submit-as-a-danger-sectionmessage-at-the-top-of-the-form}

**Checked:** Automatic

It says what happened and what to do, and the field errors it names sit on their fields. It is announced when it appears. Scrolling it into view is Planned .

### Put a load failure in the empty-state slot with Try again. {#put-a-load-failure-in-the-empty-state-slot-with-try-again}

**Checked:** Automatic

Content that fails to load takes the place an empty view would, in the Section's body, so the header rows and the rest of the page keep working. No access uses the same slot and names who can help.

Do: The failure in the Section's slot; the rest of the page works.
Don't: A Modal over the whole page to report one Section's failure.

### Make a failed background job a danger Flag that stays. {#make-a-failed-background-job-a-danger-flag-that-stays}

**Checked:** Automatic

The person has moved on, so the Flag finds them at the top right. A danger Flag does not hide on its own; it offers Try again and stays until Try again resolves it. `Flag` names the appearance `error`.

### Use a Banner only for a condition on the whole page. {#use-a-banner-only-for-a-condition-on-the-whole-page}

**Checked:** Review

An outage, a lost connection, an account-wide block: one Banner at its tier, danger only when action is needed now, mounted only while the condition holds. A Banner has no dismiss.

### Say what happened and what to do, with no codes. {#say-what-happened-and-what-to-do-with-no-codes}

**Checked:** Review

Own the problem: "Couldn't add the student. Check the fields below and try again." The words carry the severity, because the icon is hidden from screen readers and color never carries the meaning alone.

### Keep every error in visible text where the cause is. {#keep-every-error-in-visible-text-where-the-cause-is}

**Checked:** Automatic

A tooltip is absent on touch and gone on blur. An error is text on the page, next to what failed.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Errors`.

```jsx
import { TextField } from '@/components';

function ErrorExample() {
    return <TextField label="Student name" isInvalid errorMessage="Enter the student name." />;
}
```

# Filtering How a person narrows a collection, with filters in the Section's header in one of five tiers. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Filtering/Filtering.mdx` ## Tiers Choose a tier by the number of categories and the length of their lists. See Best practices for when to move filters into a menu. - **1 · Quick filters.** One to three categories, each a short list: a "Field: value" trigger per category opening its own list, applied as you pick. - **2a · Menu, one category.** The Filter button opens one list, applied as you pick. No footer. - **2b · Menu, side by side.** Two or three categories with short lists in columns, with Clear and Apply at the end. - **2c · Menu, stacked.** Four or more categories, or long lists, stacked, with Clear and Apply at the end. - **3 · Filter side.** Filtering is the main job: a side at the Section's start, "Reset filters" at its top and a count beside each category. ## What is on The control that holds a filter shows it: the FilterButton's count, or the Filter button's own count on the selected fill. No row of tags under the header. ## Key cases ### Below 960, the filter side The side hides and the Filter button returns with its count. Pressing it gives the filters the Section's whole width, and "Show results" goes back. The Section owns this behavior: Section › Width behavior. ### Widths A one-list menu is auto: at least the trigger, 160 to 320, truncating with a tooltip. Side by side takes 3-col; stacked takes 3-col and never goes past 4-col. The widths are the Popup template's. ## Usage Use Filtering when a person narrows a collection by its attributes. Filters live in the Section header's third row, after Search: "Field: value" triggers, then More filters. Views in the second row are not filters: a view is one of a fixed set, and filters combine. | Tier | Use when | Controls | Applies | Shows it is on | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 · Quick filters | One to three categories, each a short list | A FilterButton per category | As you pick | The button's selected fill and count | | 2a · Menu, one category | One category, and the bar has no room for a button | The Filter button, one list | As you pick | The Filter button's count | | 2b · Menu, side by side | Two or three categories with short lists, applied together | The Filter button, columns, Clear and Apply | On Apply | The Filter button's count | | 2c · Menu, stacked | Four or more categories, or long lists | The Filter button, stacked categories, Clear and Apply | On Apply | The Filter button's count | | 3 · Filter side | Filtering is the main job, such as browsing a long catalog | A side at the Section's start | As you pick, or on "Apply filters" for a batch | A count beside each category | ## Alternatives - For finding rows by name, use the Search pattern: its icon sits before the filters. - For switching between fixed views of the rows, use `Tabs` as pill views. - For sorting, use the `Table` column header: sorting is not a filter. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Name categories as nouns: "Grade", "School", "Subject". | "Filter by grade", "Choose a school". | | Label the menu footer "Clear" and "Apply". | "Reset", "OK", "Done". | | Put "Reset filters" at the top of a side; "Apply filters" only for a batch. | "Clear all", "Submit". | | Name the Filter button with filters on: "Filters 2". | "Filters (2)". | | Count the results in words: "1 of 8 students". | "1 result". | | Go back from the filters on a narrow Section with "Show results". | "Done", "Close". | ## Accessibility - The Filter button's name is "Filters"; with a count it reads "Filters 2". Apply returns focus to it, so its new name is read. - A FilterButton's name is its text plus its count. Its list is a listbox the arrow keys move through; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button. - The result count is a polite live region: it is read as the rows narrow. - Clear and Apply are the last tab stops in a menu. - A filter side is a region named "Filters", and each category is a group named by its legend. ## Parts | Part | Component | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Quick filter | Filter button | A count only when a value is on; it hugs its label and opens its list at bottom-end. | | Filter button | Filter button | Text "Filters" with the `filter` icon; its `trailingMetric` draws the count on the selected fill. The Section's `filters` entry hands it to the menu. | | One list (tier 1 lists, 2a) | Popup select | Applies as you pick, radios for one. # Forms

The kinds of form and how a form takes and checks what someone types: when it validates, what a blocked submit does.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Forms/Forms.mdx`

## The kinds of form

There is no Form component or template. A form is a `Fieldset` of fields inside a host, and the host owns the title and the footer. Pick the kind by the task; its host page has the layout, the footer and the sizes.

- **Settings.** Values saved as a group, on their own page.
- **Create.** A rare, critical task with fewer than five fields.
- **Quick edit.** A short edit of a row, with the page still in view.
- **In steps.** A long form someone works through.

## Marks and help

## Validation

## Leaving with edits

## Bound inputs

## Usage

Use Forms when a page asks for input that is saved together: adding a student, logging a session, a reflection, profile settings. Ask only what is needed, group fields under a `Fieldset` legend of two or three words, keep one column except for pairs that belong together (first and last name, date and time), and reveal a conditional field under the answer that needs it rather than adding a separate one.

| The form… | Kind | Host |
| --- | --- | --- |
| is saved as a group on its own page: settings, a profile | Settings | Section page header on the Page |
| is rare and critical, with fewer than five fields | Create | Modal, 8-col |
| is a short edit of a row, with the page still in view | Quick edit | Panel, Details |
| is long, or has sections someone works through | In steps | Multi-step task on Frame |
| asks for one value read far more than changed | None: inline edit | The record, which saves on its own |

Where the buttons sit and in which look is each host's footer, and Common actions for the rules across them. A Popup never holds a form.

## Alternatives

- For one value on a record page, use `InlineEdit`; it saves on its own.
- For settings that apply at once, group `SettingRow` items under section headings on the page; a `Toggle` never waits for Save.
- For a filter, follow Filtering: filters are not a form.
- For a decision with no fields, use Modal · Active.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label names the field: "School email". | Label gives an instruction: "Enter your school email:". |
| Error says what to fix: "Enter a full email, like name@school.org". | "Invalid input", "Error 422". |
| Caption says what the field is for: "Shared with the supervisor". | Caption repeats the label. |
| Placeholder shows a good answer: "name@school.org". | Placeholder names the control: "Text field". |
| Submit names the outcome: "Log session", "Add student". | "Submit", "Save" when the outcome has a name. |
| Dates and times as the person reads them: "Mar 4, 2026 · 4:00 PM". | "2026-03-04T16:00". |

## Accessibility

- Every input has a visible label. A group is a `fieldset` with a `legend`; its one error is announced once.
- A field error is announced and sets `aria-invalid`; the submit moves focus to the first invalid field. A server message is announced when it appears.
- A required field sets `aria-required` whether or not it carries a visible `"(required)"` marker; only the form's minority case is marked in the label text.
- A sending button keeps its name and sets `aria-busy`; the secondary action stays reachable.
- A dialog opens only from a person's action. Focus goes to the first input and stays trapped until it closes.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fields | `Fieldset` | There is no Form component: a Fieldset groups the fields inside a host. |
| Rejection at the top | `SectionMessage` | A danger message, scrolled into view. |
| Choices | `RadioGroup`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Select`, `DatePicker` | A control that cannot be wrong; pictured tiles for one big question per step. |
| Settings rows | `SettingRow`, `Toggle`, `Select`, `StatusTag`, `Flag` | Divided rows under section headings with no card per row; flipping a toggle confirms via Flag. |
| Hosts | Section, Panel, Modal, Frame | A page (under its Section header, no Section around the fields), a Panel, a Modal, or the multi-step task on Frame. Each owns its footer. |
| Confirm view | Modal | Swapped in place today. A confirm view prop is Planned. |

## Related

- Common actions: use for where the buttons sit and which look they take.
- Modal, Panel, Frame: use for each host's layout and footer.
- Loading: use for a form that is sending.
- Disabled: use for a submit that cannot run yet.
- Errors: use for where a failed save shows.

## Motion

Forms reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| focus | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Border color on appearance.fast. The focus ring never animates. |  |
| error | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | An error on leaving a field makes room on spatial.fast, then fades in; it fades and the room closes once the field is fixed. |  |
| blocked | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | A blocked submit shakes the Modal, or the field with its own button, once. Never bigger on repeat; never in Reduced mode. |  |
| failed | Call attention | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | When the system failed, a message makes room at the top of the Modal or form, then fades in. No shake: the person did nothing wrong. A page-level error is a one-line summary that makes room at the top; focus goes to the first error. | `sound.error` on land: the person's own submit was rejected (a danger SectionMessage) |
| steps | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Step states change in place. |  |
| saving | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The button keeps its width: its label fades out, a Spinner fades in, and the same button confirms when done. |  |
| success | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The same button confirms: its Spinner fades out and the done label fades in, at the same width. | `sound.commit` on land: a sign-up is confirmed: one-time, recurring or fill-in |

## Best practices

### Validate a field when it loses focus and clear the error once the rule is met. {#validate-a-field-when-it-loses-focus-and-clear-the-error-once-the-rule-is-met}

**Checked:** Automatic

The error shows on the field, says what to fix, and goes away as soon as the value passes. Nothing is checked while typing. A warning accepts the value; a field is invalid only when the form cannot go on.

### Keep the submit button enabled and let it show what is missing. {#keep-the-submit-button-enabled-and-let-it-show-what-is-missing}

**Checked:** Automatic

A disabled submit gives no direction and leaves the tab order. Pressing it marks every missing field and moves focus to the first; the body scrolls to it. The button disables only while sending, when it swaps its label for a spinner in place and keeps its width.

### Keep a blocked submit in the same Modal. {#keep-a-blocked-submit-in-the-same-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Mark the field, say what to fix inline, scroll the body to it, and shake once . Never a second dialog for the error. Reduced motion drops the shake; the color, icon, message and focus move carry it. A server failure: Errors.

Do: The message under the field, in the same Modal.
Don't: A second dialog over the first, with the field left unexplained.

### Mark only the minority case in the label, in plain text. {#mark-only-the-minority-case-in-the-label-in-plain-text}

**Checked:** Review

When most fields are required, mark the optional ones `"(optional)"` (`labelMarker="optional"`). When most fields are optional, mark the required ones `"(required)"` (`labelMarker="required"`). The marker is plain text in the label's type style, in `--ds-text-subtle`, never a symbol or legend. Required controls still set `isRequired`, so screen readers get `aria-required` and the visible `"(required)"` is hidden from them to avoid saying it twice. Choice flows (`RadioGroup` and `CheckboxGroup` across onboarding, quizzes, check-ins, and surveys) apply the same minority rule to selection controls: the majority selection type uses `appearance="soft"` (selected fill, border, and trailing check with no radio dot or checkbox box), while the minority selection type keeps its visible control (`card` or `plain`) so people notice when a question switches between single-select and multi-select.

Do: Two required fields stay unmarked; only the optional field says so.
Don't: Every field carries a marker, so none stands out.

### Put help in the caption, never in a tooltip. {#put-help-in-the-caption-never-in-a-tooltip}

**Checked:** Automatic

A caption stays after the person types and is read by a screen reader with the field. A tooltip never carries the only copy of anything. An explanation most people will never need opens from an `InlineMessage` beside the field.

Do: Help in the caption, where it stays after typing.
Don't: Help only in a tooltip: gone on touch, gone after typing.

### Ask before leaving with unsaved edits. {#ask-before-leaving-with-unsaved-edits}

**Checked:** Automatic

Close, Discard, Cancel (on a page form) and navigating away raise a 4-col Modal: Back returns without losing anything typed; Discard is Danger. A form already in a Modal asks in that Modal's confirm view, so two layers never become three. A form with no edits leaves at once. In a multi-step task, Back in the inner sidebar asks first if anything is unsaved.

### Prefer a bound input to a free one. {#prefer-a-bound-input-to-a-free-one}

**Checked:** Review

Up to five choices: `RadioGroup` or checkboxes, visible at once. Six or more: `Select`. A date: `DatePicker`. A number: min and max. A radio group starts unanswered and never falls back to its first option. A `Toggle` applies at once, so anything that waits for Save is a `Checkbox`.

### Give the form a title from its host and a legend for each group. {#give-the-form-a-title-from-its-host-and-a-legend-for-each-group}

**Checked:** Review

The form's title is the page, Panel or Modal heading, never a generic "Form". Groups take a `Fieldset` legend, two or three words, a noun phrase. Labels are sentence case, one to three words, naming the field rather than what to do.

### Keep a form to one column. {#keep-a-form-to-one-column}

**Checked:** Review

Pair two fields side by side only when they belong together, such as first and last name, or date and time. Anything else reads down one column.

Do: One column, so the eye moves straight down.
Don't: Unrelated fields scattered across two columns.

### Keep a short edit beside the page. {#keep-a-short-edit-beside-the-page}

**Checked:** Review

Editing a row opens a Panel so the person keeps the page in view. A Modal is for a rare, critical task with fewer than five fields.

Do: A short edit in a Panel, the rows still in view.
Don't: The same short edit in a Modal that covers the rows.

### Set autofill on every field the browser can fill. {#set-autofill-on-every-field-the-browser-can-fill}

**Checked:** Automatic

`autoComplete` on name, email, phone and address fields. Prefill what is already known, such as the student picked from a row.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Forms`.

```jsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button, TextField } from '@/components';

function FormExample() {
    const [name, setName] = useState('');
    return (
        <form onSubmit={(event) => event.preventDefault()}>
            <TextField label="Student name" value={name} onChange={(event) => setName(event.target.value)}
                caption="Use the name the student goes by." />
            <Button text="Add student" appearance="primary" type="submit" />
        </form>
    );
}
```
guides.design-system/agent-views/patterns/Indic:
# Indicators

The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved; the words carry the meaning.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Indicators/Indicators.mdx`

## The three tags

Three jobs, three components. A category with a color is a Tag, not an indicator.

## Key cases

- **Status in a row.** Default spacing in a table cell. One status per object; the label is one or two words.
- **Status beside a heading.** Spacious beside the page title, after the text.
- **Counts on navigation.** A count beside an item's name. At zero the component renders nothing; bold asks for action now, at most one per area.
- **Where color is not enough.** A leading icon joins the color on a status that must be told apart at a glance, such as Missed.
- **Change where up is bad.** Absences rose by 3: the value is up and the tone is danger, because the good direction is down.
- **A roll-up.** A group's status shows the worst state among its children: danger over warning over information.

A checklist tracks setup or compliance steps in three layouts: a dismissible card on Home, a persistent card in a page, and a compact summary at the foot of the Sidebar.

## Usage

Use Indicators when something needs a small label that says how it is. Ask what the label says: a number is a Count tag; a condition that can change is a Status tag; how much a number moved is a Change tag; a subject, a person or a category is a Tag. Skip an indicator when no action follows from it; past five or six states, use text.

| The label says | Component | Looks | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The condition something is in, and it can change | Status tag | Fill by meaning: neutral not started, information in progress, success done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery new | "Needs review" |
| How many | Count tag | Subtle neutral; bold for action now; nothing at 0; a cap past `max` with "+" | "12", "99+" |
| How much it moved | Change tag | Signed value, arrow, tone from the good direction; neutral when there is no judgment | "+3 vs last week" |
| A category, a subject, a person | Tag | Outline and text; a leading visual is optional | "Lincoln Middle" |
| Setup or compliance steps left to finish | Checklist (`Card` + `Section` + `Progress bar`) | Header count and bar aligned to one 128 action column; open steps above done steps | "2 of 5 done" |
| The shape of a trend | Sparkline | A word-sized line beside the number | Attendance over eight weeks |

## Alternatives

- For a message about the thing, use a Section message or a Flag; the Notifications pattern picks between them.
- For a due or event date, use `DateTag`.
- For a competency area, use `CompetencyTag`.
- For something the AI proposes, use `Suggestion`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Status in one or two words: "Scheduled", "Needs review", "Missed". | "This session has been missed". |
| Count as the bare number: "4", "12", "99+". | "4 items", "Count: 4". |
| Change signed, with the comparison: "+3 vs last week", "−12%". | "3 more", "went up". |
| Hidden text reads the whole thing: "Up 3 vs last week". | Nothing for the screen reader. |

## Accessibility

- A tag is read as its text; nothing suggests it can be pressed. A clipped tag becomes a tab stop so the Tooltip opens on focus.
- A count's meaning is in the label it sits on: "Inbox, 3 unread". A bare number announces nothing useful.
- A Change tag's arrow and value are hidden from assistive technology and its words read the direction and the comparison.
- A Status tag, Tag and Change tag keep an inside border, so a pale fill stays visible on any background and in forced colors.

## Parts

| Part | Component | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| State | Status tag | Six appearances; `trailingMetric` nests a count inside it. |
| How many | Count tag | `max` caps it, `isBold` asks for action, `label` names it for a screen reader. |
| How much it moved | Change tag | `goodDirection` sets the tone; `comparison` names what it is measured against. |
| Checklist | Card, Section, Progress bar | Composed step rows (`Icon`, text, `Button` or "Completed" text) on `--checklist-action-width`; `Icon button` dismisses an optional card. |
| Category | Tag | Not an indicator: a subject, a person or a category. |

## Related

- Notifications: use for the count on the bell and the Inbox.
- Overflow: use for a tag that clips.
- Navigation: use for counts on Sidebar items and tabs.

## Motion

Indicators reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| status | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A status that changes fades to its new word and fill on appearance.default; nothing bounces. |
| count-first | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A count rolls once on first view, downward, and then fades to later values on appearance.fast. |
| progress | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-linear` | Progress fills on linear with the work, never ahead. Nothing bounces. |

## Best practices

### Never let color carry the meaning alone. {#never-let-color-carry-the-meaning-alone}

**Checked:** Review

The words say the state; the fill repeats it. A state that must be told apart at a glance adds a leading icon. A Change tag's arrow is decorative and its hidden text reads "Up 3 vs last week". A dot with no label is announced as nothing.

### Give each appearance one meaning. {#give-each-appearance-one-meaning}

**Checked:** Review

Neutral is not started, info is in progress, success is done, warning needs attention, danger failed or missed, discovery is new. Success never labels a problem. There is no color prop; a category with a color is a Tag.

Do: Danger on a missed session: the word and the fill agree.
Don't: Success on a missed session: the fill says good about bad news.

### Show one status per object. {#show-one-status-per-object}

**Checked:** Review

Two statuses force people to decide which is true. A roll-up shows the worst child state.

### Keep a status to one or two words. {#keep-a-status-to-one-or-two-words}

**Checked:** Review

A status is read at a glance; a sentence belongs in the row text. A Status tag truncates at 200 with its full text in a Tooltip.

### Keep most counts quiet and show nothing at zero. {#keep-most-counts-quiet-and-show-nothing-at-zero}

**Checked:** Automatic

Subtle neutral is the default. Bold asks for action now, so at most one bold count per area. Pass the raw number: the component renders nothing at 0 and caps past `max` with a "+". No skeleton on a count; it appears when the number arrives.

### Set the Change tag's good direction so up can be bad. {#set-the-change-tag-s-good-direction-so-up-can-be-bad}

**Checked:** Automatic

The sign gives the direction; the good direction gives the tone: up, down or none. Absences rising is danger; sessions held rising is success; a change with no judgment stays neutral. The value is always signed.

Do: A rise in absences in danger: the good direction is down.
Don't: A rise in absences in success: the color says good about bad news.

### Edit a status in the field, not on the label. {#edit-a-status-in-the-field-not-on-the-label}

**Checked:** Review

A Status tag never opens a menu. Where a status can be changed, the field around it becomes an inline Select.

### Nest a count in a status instead of placing one beside it. {#nest-a-count-in-a-status-instead-of-placing-one-beside-it}

**Checked:** Review

"Needs review 3" reads as one label; two labels side by side read as unrelated.

### Line up checklist actions in one column and mark done steps with text. {#line-up-checklist-actions-in-one-column-and-mark-done-steps-with-text}

**Checked:** Review

Build the checklist from `Card` and `Section`:

1. Compose each row from an `Icon`, step text with one fact, and an action column. Use `--checklist-action-width` (128), with `--checklist-action-min-width` (120) as its floor. Buttons fill the column and align down the list.
2. Put the title at the header's start and the count ("2 of 5 done") with a `ProgressBar` at the end. Align the bar's start edge with the action column: 128 wide on a persistent card, or 96 when a 32 dismiss `IconButton` occupies the end.
3. Keep open steps in order above completed steps. Center a check icon and plain "Completed" text (Body small, subtle) in each completed row's action column.

Choose the layout by where the checklist appears:

| Layout | Use | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dismissible card | Home | When complete, shrinks to one line for a day, then disappears. |
| Persistent card | Required work on a page | Keeps every completed row visible. |
| Compact card | Foot of the Sidebar | Shows the count, progress bar and next step, which opens the full list. |

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Indicators`.

```jsx
import { StatusTag } from '@/components';

function IndicatorExample() {
    return <StatusTag appearance="warning">Needs review</StatusTag>;
}
```
