# Loading What to show while PLUS fetches or saves something. Two inputs decide it: what is loading, and how long it has taken. The bands are 1 s and 10 s. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Loading/Loading.mdx` ## By what is loading Four kinds of wait. Each has its own shape in the 1 to 10 s band; the time bands are the same for all. - **A list or cards.** A skeleton in the real shape, so the layout stays still. - **A button action.** A spinner inside the button that started it. The fields stay as they are. - **A whole page.** The Frame and page header draw first; each Section fills as its data arrives. - **A menu.** One "Loading options" row, never a skeleton. Fetch items before the click where you can. ## Across time ## Key cases ## Usage Use Loading while someone waits for a fetch or save. Choose the indicator by what is loading and how long it has taken. | What is loading | Under 1 s | 1 to 10 s | Over 10 s | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A list or cards | Keep what was there; blank on first load | A skeleton in the real shape, `aria-busy`, "Loading students…" announced | The skeleton stays; a Flag explains the wait | | A button action | Nothing yet; the button blocks a second press | A spinner inside the button; fields stay as they are | A Flag says it is still working and the person can leave; a Flag confirms when done | | A whole page | Keep the previous page; blank screens wait | Frame and page header now, a skeleton in each Section | A labeled progress bar for a long job | | A menu, Popup, Flag or Modal | Open complete; fetch before the click | One "Loading options" row; no skeleton | "Couldn't load options" with Retry, still one row | ## Alternatives - For a wait whose length is known, use `ProgressBar`; it answers "how much longer". - For a view that turns out to have nothing, follow Empty. - For a load that failed, follow the Errors pattern: the error goes in the empty-state slot with Try again. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Announce what is loading: "Loading students…", then "Students loaded". | "Loading…" as the only text on a page. | | Flag past 10 s: "Still loading students. This group is large; you can keep working." | "Please wait", "Hang tight!". | | Progress bar label: "Importing roster · 40 of 120 students". | A bar with no words. | | Menu rows: "Loading options" · "Couldn't load options" with "Retry". | "Error", "Failed to fetch". | ## Accessibility - Every skeleton is `aria-hidden`, never takes focus and ignores the pointer. - The busy region's live label sits beside the region, not inside it, because content inside a busy region may be held back. - A spinner announces as a status with a label that says what is loading when it is not obvious. - Reduced motion: the shimmer stops and the spinner becomes a static ring; the shape still reads as working. ## Parts | Part | Component | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Placeholder | Skeleton | Text bars in the content's own shape; `isShimmering` holds still under reduced motion. | | Spinner | Spinner | Inside a Button through `isLoading`; the button keeps its width. | | Long job | Progress bar | A value and a label that says what is happening. | | Wait explained | Flag | Information appearance, held until the work finishes. | | Menu rows | Dropdown menu | `loading` shows "Loading options"; `hasError` with `onRetry` shows "Couldn't load options". | ## Related - Empty: use once the load finishes with nothing. - Errors: use when the load fails. - Notifications: use for the Flag past 10 s. ## Best practices ### Show nothing new under 1 s. {#show-nothing-new-under-1-s} **Checked:** Review Keep the old content, or leave the area blank on a first load. A skeleton or spinner that appears and vanishes reads as a glitch rather than work. A button blocks a second press at once. ### Draw a skeleton in the real shape from 1 s. {#draw-a-skeleton-in-the-real-shape-from-1-s} **Checked:** Review The same rows, columns and cards the content will have, as plain text bars, so nothing jumps when it arrives. The container owns the skeleton; labels become text bars rather than label shapes. The shimmer stays on while loading. Do: A skeleton in the table's own shape, text bars throughout. Don't: One spinner in a blank area: the layout jumps when the rows arrive. ### Put the spinner inside the button that started the action. {#put-the-spinner-inside-the-button-that-started-the-action} **Checked:** Automatic The label swaps for a spinner in place and the button keeps its width. Only that button disables; the fields and Cancel stay live. One spinner per wait. ### Draw the Frame and page header first. {#draw-the-frame-and-page-header-first} **Checked:** Review On a quick move keep the previous page until the next is ready. Past 1 s the Frame, Sidebar and page header draw at once and each Section fills as its data arrives. A full-screen blocking overlay has no place in a wait. ### Say so after 10 s. {#say-so-after-10-s} **Checked:** Review A Flag, kept up with `autohide={false}` until the work ends, explains the wait and that the person can keep working or leave; a Flag confirms when the work finishes. A long job with a known length, such as importing a roster, gets a labeled progress bar instead. ### Keep a menu, Popup, Flag or Modal free of skeletons. {#keep-a-menu-popup-flag-or-modal-free-of-skeletons} **Checked:** Review They open in answer to a click and open complete. A menu whose items must load shows one "Loading options" row, then "Couldn't load options" with Retry. A Modal's body may hold its content's own loading state. Do: A menu shows one "Loading options" row. Don't: A menu full of skeleton rows, promising items it may not have. ### Mark the loading region busy and announce it. {#mark-the-loading-region-busy-and-announce-it} **Checked:** Review `aria-busy` on the container that is loading, and a visually hidden status beside it whose text is set after mount: "Loading students…", then "Students loaded". Skeletons themselves are hidden from assistive technology. ## In code From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Loading`. ```jsx import { Skeleton } from '@/components'; function LoadingExample() { return
; } ```
guides.design-system/agent-views/patterns/Navig:
# Navigation

How a person moves: between areas, between views, and down into a record and back out, one control and one motion each.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Navigation/Navigation.mdx`

## The tiers

Four tiers, from the whole app down to one record. A quick look is a layer, not a tier; steps move within a level.

- **1 · Areas.** Go to: the Sidebar's fixed items. The selected row takes the selected fill.
- **1b · Open items.** Records the person opened, a session or a student, as temporary items in the Sidebar: add and remove, then go to.
- **2 · Views.** Pill views in a Section's header, or page tabs under the page title. Content swaps in place.
- **3 · Drill in and climb out.** A record page with a breadcrumb: the record's place, parents only. Climb out through the breadcrumb.

## Key cases

## Usage

Choose the navigation tier first; it sets the control, placement and motion. Navigation belongs in the Sidebar and page. There is no global search.

| Tier | The move | Control | Motion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 · Areas | To another part of the app | A Sidebar item | Go to |
| 1b · Open items | To a session or student opened earlier | A temporary item in the Sidebar, named by when and who | Add and remove, then Go to |
| 2 · Views | Between views of one collection or record | Pill views in the Section header; page tabs under the title | Switch views: content in place, the indicator glides |
| 3 · Drill in and climb out | Into one record and back | A row, then the breadcrumb | Drill in, Climb out |
| Within a level | Through a task's steps | Back and Next in the bottom bar; the step rail | Step |
| A layer | A quick look without leaving | A Details Panel or a Modal | Open and Close |

### Opening a record

Least room to most. Pick the lowest step that fits. The picture is on Templates.

| Step | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| 1 · Expand the row | A few more lines, links at most. |
| 2 · Section detail | An inline expand inside a Section. |
| 3 · Details Panel | On a queue page (docked beside the list), or a quick look or short edit from a table. |
| 4 · Modal | A rare, critical task with fewer than five fields. |
| 5 · Its own page | Complex or stepped work, or anything worth a URL. The breadcrumb appears. |

## Alternatives

- For narrowing a collection rather than switching views, follow Filtering; filters combine, views do not.
- For more pills than fit, fold the extras into "More" ; keep page tabs to five.
- For a decision that blocks the page, use a Modal, not a page.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Views as short parallel nouns: "Upcoming", "Past". | "Show upcoming sessions", "History". |
| Page tabs name views of one subject: "Overview", "Sessions", "Notes". | Counts or status in the tab label. |
| The labeled filter trigger names the view: "Status: Upcoming". | A bare "Upcoming". |
| Breadcrumb levels by the page's own title. | "Back", "Home" as a level. |
| Open item: "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz". | "Session #1028". |

## Accessibility

- The Sidebar is a navigation landmark; the selected item carries `aria-current="page"`. The selected row is a fill, not color on the icon alone.
- Views and page tabs are a real tab widget: one tab stop, Left and Right move selection, the panel is named by its tab.
- The breadcrumb is a `nav` around an `ol`; the last item is plain text with `aria-current="page"`.
- Leaving a multi-step task returns focus to the control that opened it .

## Related

- Overflow: use for the breadcrumb middle and open-item names.
- Search: use for narrowing as you type inside a view.
- Filtering: use for narrowing a view by attributes.
- Indicators: use for counts on Sidebar items.
- Frame, Page, Section: use for the drawn shells.
- `Sidebar`, `Breadcrumb`, `Tabs`, `PageHeader`, `PopupSelect`: the components.

## Motion

Navigation reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| area | Go to another area | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | The Sidebar highlight glides on spatial.fast; the page fades through on appearance.default. |
| open-item | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opening a record adds an open item to the Sidebar; closing one removes it. Picking one is Go to another area. |
| view | Switch views | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Only the selected indicator glides; the content swaps in place. |
| swap | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Filters swap the content in place. |
| drill | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Drilling into a record moves on spatial.default. |
| climb | Drill into and climb back out | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Climbing out moves on spatial.fast. The Breadcrumb never animates on its own. |

## Best practices

### Show the breadcrumb only after drilling into a record. {#show-the-breadcrumb-only-after-drilling-into-a-record}

**Checked:** Automatic

Never on an area page or a multi-step task. It sits above the title in the page header and shows the record's place: parents only, never history. It never wraps. Folding five or more items into "…" is Planned .

Do: A breadcrumb on the record page, parents only.
Don't: A breadcrumb on an area page: there is nothing to climb out of.

### Keep one tab system per page. {#keep-one-tab-system-per-page}

**Checked:** Automatic

Either page tabs under the title, or pill views in a Section's bar, never both. Under page tabs a Section's views become one labeled PopupSelect at the start of its bar. It picks a view, not a filter.

Do: Under page tabs the Section's views are one labeled PopupSelect at the start of its bar.
Don't: Page tabs and pill views on the same page: two tab systems.

### Make views a fixed set the product defines. {#make-views-a-fixed-set-the-product-defines}

**Checked:** Review

Two to five views of the same rows, named by short parallel nouns. Nobody adds or edits views. One pill stays even with one view, so nothing moves when a second arrives.

### Swap content in place between views and tabs. {#swap-content-in-place-between-views-and-tabs}

**Checked:** Automatic

Only the selected indicator glides. Nothing slides between views.

### Open a record at the lowest step that fits. {#open-a-record-at-the-lowest-step-that-fits}

**Checked:** Review

Expand the row, then Section detail, then the Details Panel, then a Modal, then its own page. Section detail and the Details Panel both stay: Section detail expands in place (see Section), and the Details Panel docks beside the list on a queue page or opens from a table.

### Give a long task its steps in the inner sidebar. {#give-a-long-task-its-steps-in-the-inner-sidebar}

**Checked:** Automatic

The steps replace the Sidebar's rows and Back returns to them; no breadcrumb. How the steps, the page and the footer sit is on Frame.

### Name an open item by when and who. {#name-an-open-item-by-when-and-who}

**Checked:** Automatic

"4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz", with the school in the Tooltip. Three show, then "Show n more". Removing one is Add and remove; opening one is Go to.

Do: Each item names the session by its time and the teacher.
Don't: Each item carries everything, and the time it is found by is cut off.

### Put the collection's add action in its Section's title row, not the page header. {#put-the-collection-s-add-action-in-its-section-s-title-row-not-the-page-header}

**Checked:** Automatic

"Add student" is the Primary at the end of the Students Section's title row. Page actions sit at the end of the page header and are only about the page.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Navigation`.

```jsx
import { Breadcrumb } from '@/components';

function NavigationExample() {
    return <Breadcrumb items={[{ text: 'Sessions', href: '#sessions' }, { text: 'Session review' }]} />;
}
```
guides.design-system/agent-views/patterns/Notif:
# Notifications

What the product says back, and where: a Flag for what happened, a Banner for a condition, a SectionMessage for something to act on, and the Inbox for what arrived over time.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Notifications/Notifications.mdx`

## The carriers

Four components carry every message. Each component page holds its appearances; this pattern picks the carrier and the place. A Modal is the fifth, for the one message that must be answered first.

- **Flag.** A passing notice at the top right, two lines at most. Routine ones leave on their own; warning and error stay until acted on.
- **Banner.** A condition that holds for the whole Frame, page or Section: one line, no dismiss, one at a time.
- **SectionMessage.** Something to read or act on that belongs to this part of the page and stays until resolved or dismissed.
- **The Inbox.** Updates that arrived over time, in a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel beside the Sidebar, opened from the bell beside your name, with `Unread` and `All` tabs and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day.

## Banner tiers

One banner at a time, scrolling with its content. The Frame tier is system news and pins only during an active outage. The Page tier is about this page. The Section tier is about this collection. The Frame and Page `banner` slots are Planned : today a Banner goes in the content, set where its tier says.

- **Frame.** System news across the whole width, above the Sidebar and the page.
- **Page.** Under the page header, about this page.
- **Section.** At the top of one collection, about that collection.

## Severity

## Key cases

## Usage

Notify someone when an action finishes, a condition applies or a decision is needed. Match disruption to urgency using the carrier table below. Show only necessary notifications.

| The message is about… | Carrier | Where | Leaves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Something that already happened and needs no reply: saved, sent, copied | `Flag` | Top right | On its own after 8 s, or Dismiss on a default flag; a bold warning or error when its action resolves it |
| A job that finished after the person moved on | Default `Flag` with an action, `autohide={false}` | Top right | Dismiss, or the action |
| A job that failed after the person moved on | Bold error `Flag` with Try again | Top right | When Try again resolves it; no Dismiss |
| Something to read or act on in this part of the page | `SectionMessage` | Top of the Section or form | Resolved or dismissed |
| Guidance before a task that must not be missed | `SectionMessage`, dismiss off | By the action it informs | When it stops applying |
| A condition that holds for everything in a Frame, page or Section | `Banner` at that tier | Top of the tier | When the condition ends |
| A note beside one thing that most people never need | `InlineMessage` | Beside the field or value | On close |
| Something that must be answered before going on | `Modal`, Acknowledge or Active | Centered over a Blanket | On the button |
| What arrived over time | The Inbox, a 360-wide (`--inbox-width`) Panel, opened from the bell beside your name | Beside the Sidebar, over the page, no Blanket | Escape, outside click, or Close |

## Alternatives

- For an error about one field, put it on the field; see Errors.
- For a state on one object, use a `StatusTag`; see Indicators.
- For a copy confirmation, use the "Copied" tooltip; see Common actions.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Flag title names the event: "Session logged." | "Success!" |
| Flag line gives the next step: "Maya's supervisor will see it Friday." | A bare title with no next step. |
| Banner is one sentence: "Scheduled maintenance Saturday 2–4 AM ET." | A paragraph in the Banner. |
| Own the problem: "We lost the connection. Your work is kept on this device." | "Connection lost by client." |
| Actions are verbs: "Undo", "View sessions". | "Click here", "OK". |

## Accessibility

- Warning and error Flags are alerts and interrupt; every other Flag is a polite status. Each is read as one message.
- A `SectionMessage` announces assertively when it appears; one present at first paint is ordinary content.
- A `Banner` is a status that never traps focus and sits in the reading order.
- The timeout on a Flag is a timing limit; the dismiss × on a default Flag satisfies it (see the Flag page).
- The appearance icon is decorative; the words carry the severity.
- Each `NotificationItem` in the Inbox is one link whose accessible name announces `"Unread"` while unread, with `"Mark as read"` as a sibling button outside the link.

## Related

- Errors: use for where a failure shows.
- Loading: use for the Flag past 10 s.
- Indicators: use for the count on the Bell.
- Panel: use for the Inbox.
- Modal: use for what must be answered first.
- Page: use for where a Page banner sits.
- `Flag`, `Banner`, `SectionMessage`, `InlineMessage`, `NotificationItem`, `Modal`: the components.

## Motion

Notifications reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flag-enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-default` | A Flag enters from the top right. |
| flag-timeout | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-exit` | A Flag that times out exits the way it came. |
| flag-dismiss | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A Flag closed by hand does a quick fade in place. |
| stack | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The stack closes up when a Flag leaves. |
| message | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A SectionMessage or InlineMessage makes room on spatial.fast, then fades in; it reverses on exit. |
| banner | Add or remove an item | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A Banner pushes the page down on spatial.default, then fades in. |

## Best practices

### Place Flags at the top right, two lines at most. {#place-flags-at-the-top-right-two-lines-at-most}

**Checked:** Review

A title that names the event and one line for the next step. A `FlagGroup` stacks them in the order you pass them, so pass the newest first, and renders with the page so each one is announced. `FlagGroup` sits at the top right (`top-end`) by default.

### Offer Undo on a Flag with a timer, and commit when it ends. {#offer-undo-on-a-flag-with-a-timer-and-commit-when-it-ends}

**Checked:** Review

An archive or a delete confirms with a Flag that has `timer` and Undo as its first action, instead of a confirmation dialog first. The change commits in `onDismiss`, once. Pressing Undo replaces the Flag with a plain "restored" Flag. Hovering or focusing the Flag pauses the countdown, so reading it never costs the chance to undo.

### Put nothing important only in a Flag. {#put-nothing-important-only-in-a-flag}

**Checked:** Review

A Flag can be dismissed before it is read. A failure that needs a decision stays on the page in a SectionMessage; a decision that blocks the task is a Modal.

Do: A finished action on the default Flag: the event in the title, the next step below.
Don't: A decision in a Flag, which is gone before it is answered.

### Let routine Flags leave and keep warning and error until acted on. {#let-routine-flags-leave-and-keep-warning-and-error-until-acted-on}

**Checked:** Automatic

Normal, information and success close after 8 s. Warning and error never close themselves and offer a next action. On a default, information or success Flag with an action, set `autohide={false}` when the person must act; warning and error ignore it. The × and the rest of the dismiss rule are on the Flag page.

### Show one Banner at a time, one line, at the tier it concerns, for as long as the condition holds. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time-one-line-at-the-tier-it-concerns-for-as-long-as-the-condition-holds}

**Checked:** Automatic

Frame for system news, pinned only during an active outage ; Page for this page; Section for this collection. A Banner has no dismiss and no timeout, so it is mounted only while the condition is true, and it scrolls with the content.

Do: One Banner, one line, at the tier it concerns.
Don't: Two Banners stacked, pushing the page down.

### Keep a SectionMessage in the page until it is resolved or dismissed. {#keep-a-sectionmessage-in-the-page-until-it-is-resolved-or-dismissed}

**Checked:** Automatic

The fill and icon carry the appearance, with no border and no side stripe. A blocking message turns dismiss off. Put up to two actions after the body. Field errors stay on the field.

### Match the appearance to the meaning and say it in the words. {#match-the-appearance-to-the-meaning-and-say-it-in-the-words}

**Checked:** Review

Success for a finished action, warning for a caution, danger only when something failed. The icon is hidden from screen readers, so the title says "saved", "couldn't", "due".

### Keep routine news on the default Flag. {#keep-routine-news-on-the-default-flag}

**Checked:** Review

A bold fill competes with the page; it is for what must be seen. Routine news stays on the default Flag, which the person can clear.

### Send what arrived over time to the Inbox. {#send-what-arrived-over-time-to-the-inbox}

**Checked:** Review

A Flag is for now; the Inbox is for later. The Inbox opens from the bell beside the account name, docked beside the Sidebar at `--inbox-width` over the page with no Blanket, carrying `Mark all as read` and close in the header, `Unread` (with count) and `All` tabs, and `NotificationItem` rows grouped by day. Clearing every unread item shows `"You are all caught up."` in `EmptyState`; pressing `Escape` or clicking outside closes the panel.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Notifications`.

```jsx
import { Banner } from '@/components';

function NotificationExample() {
    return <Banner appearance="announcement">Session reports will be available Friday.</Banner>;
}
```
guides.design-system/agent-views/patterns/Overf:
# Overflow What happens when text or a list is longer than its room: titles wrap, cells truncate, lists fold, tables page. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Overflow/Overflow.mdx` ## The four answers Pick by what the text is. Wrap when it must be read whole; truncate when the room is fixed and the full text can be reached; fold a list; page a table. - **Wrap.** Titles, headers, labels, errors and notifications take more lines. They never end in an ellipsis. - **Truncate with a Tooltip.** A cell ends in an ellipsis on one line. Its full text opens on hover and focus, only while it is clipped. - **Fold a list.** A Tag group keeps one line and folds the rest behind +n. For other lists, "Show n more" and "Show less" are Planned . - **Page a table.** A table pages instead of growing: the pager sits at the end of the Section footer. ## Key cases The three cases below are Planned : no component carries them yet. - **The breadcrumb middle.** Five or more levels fold the middle into a "…" that opens a menu of the hidden levels. The Breadcrumb never wraps. - **An open item in the Sidebar.** Named by when and who, "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz", with the school in the Tooltip. Three show, then "Show n more". - **A file name.** The one mid-line truncation: a file name or an id keeps its start and its end, because the end tells them apart. ## Usage Use Overflow when a value may exceed its space. Choose by element so it behaves consistently across pages, with the full text always reachable. | Element | Answer | Full text | | --- | --- | --- | | Page title, Section title | Wrap | Always visible | | Field error, Section message, Flag, Banner | Wrap | Always visible | | Column header | Planned: wrap | Always visible | | Table cell | Truncate at the end, one line | Tooltip on hover and focus when clipped | | Tag (180), Status tag (200) | Truncate at the end | Tooltip when clipped; the tag becomes focusable | | Tags in a group | Fold into +n | The +n menu lists the hidden tags | | A table | Page | The range and the pager in the footer | | Breadcrumb with five or more levels | Planned: fold the middle into "…" | The "…" opens a menu of the hidden levels | | Open item in the Sidebar | Planned: truncate at the end | Tooltip with the school | | Auto-width Popup row | Planned: truncate at the end at 320 | Tooltip when clipped | | File name, id | Planned: truncate mid-line | Tooltip when clipped | | A list of items, tags or notes | Planned: "Show n more", "Show less" | Expanded in place | ## Alternatives - For a long paragraph, let it wrap; a paragraph is read, not scanned. - For a trail too long to show, follow Navigation; the Breadcrumb's fold is described there. - For more views than fit a row of pills, fold the extra pills into "More"; Navigation describes the views. - For more controls than fit a bar, the extras go into the More icon button, five controls at most. - For narrowing a long list of rows instead of folding it, follow Filtering. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | "Show 4 more" and "Show less" (Planned). | "Load more", "See all", "…". | | Open item: "4:00 PM · Ms. Ortiz"; the school in the Tooltip (Planned). | The whole title in the Sidebar. | | Breadcrumb levels by the page's own title: "Lincoln Middle School". | "Back", "Up one level". | | File name mid-line: "reflection_…_week12.pdf" (Planned). | "reflection_maya_rodrig…". | ## Accessibility - The full text is always in the DOM, so a screen reader hears all of it whether or not it is clipped. - A clipped element is a tab stop so a keyboard user can reach the Tooltip; an unclipped one is not. - The +n button of a Tag group names how many tags it holds, "+3 more tags", and opens a menu the arrow keys move through. - The breadcrumb's "…" button is named "Show hidden levels" . - "Show n more" announces the new count when the list expands . ## Parts | Part | Component | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Full text | Tooltip | Switched on only while the text is clipped. | | Label | Tag, Status tag | `maxWidth` caps the tag; a clipped label ends in an ellipsis. | | Folded tags | Tag group | `overflow="collapse"` keeps one line and folds the rest into +n. | | Cell | Dynamic table | A cell's `overflow` is `truncate` by default; `wrap` takes more lines. | | Trail | Breadcrumb | The fold is Planned ; the component never folds its middle yet. | | Pager | Pagination | Fills the Section's footer slot, aligned to the end. | ## Related - Navigation: use for the breadcrumb and the Sidebar's open items. - Indicators: use for tags that clip. - Section: use for the footer a table pages in. ## Motion Overflow reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve. | Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | fold-open | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The +n menu is a Popup: it fades in place on appearance.fast. | | fold-close | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The +n menu fades out on appearance.fast. | | truncate | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A clipped value's Tooltip opens on hover and focus; # Patterns

Choose an approach with code-free guidance and examples on templates you can use or adapt.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/PatternsOverview.mdx`

## The patterns

Seven patterns and six States pages cover situations, examples on templates and usage. Consult them when choosing or reconsidering an approach. Templates and patterns explains how the layers fit together.

- **Navigation.** How a person moves between areas, views and records, with one control and one motion per move.
- **Common actions.** Which button, in which look, in which place, with which word, and acting on many rows at once.
- **Filtering.** How a person narrows a collection to the rows that matter, in five tiers.
- **Forms.** How a form takes and checks what someone types, and what happens on leaving with edits.
- **Search.** How a person finds a record by typing, in one of three modes.
- **Indicators.** The small labels that say how something is: its state, how many, how much it moved.
- **Notifications.** What the product says back, and where: a Flag, a Banner, a SectionMessage, the Inbox.
- **States · Empty.** What a view shows when it has nothing to show.
- **States · Overflow.** What happens when text or a list is longer than its room: titles wrap, cells truncate, lists fold, tables page.
- **States · Loading.** What to show while PLUS fetches or saves something.
- **States · Errors.** Where a failure shows and what it says.
- **States · Disabled.** When a control cannot be used yet, or by this person.
- **States · Read-only.** A value someone could change but this person cannot right now.

## Which pattern for which situation

Start from what is happening on the page. Each row names the pattern that answers it and the ones to read beside it.

| The situation | Pattern | Also read |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Choosing a button's look, words or place | Common actions | Forms |
| Acting on several rows at once | Common actions · the bulk bar | None |
| Taking and checking what someone types | Forms | Errors · Disabled |
| A view with nothing to show | Empty | Search · Filtering · Errors |
| Something is still fetching or saving | Loading | Notifications |
| Something failed | Errors | Forms · Notifications · Empty |
| Text or a list is longer than its room | Overflow | Navigation |
| A control cannot be used yet, or by this person | Disabled | Read-only · Forms |
| A value this person may see but not change | Read-only | Disabled |
| Telling someone what happened or what is wrong | Notifications | Errors |
| Showing a state, a number or a change on something | Indicators | Notifications |
| Moving between areas, views and records | Navigation | Overflow |
| Finding rows by what they are called | Search | Filtering · Empty |
| Narrowing rows by their attributes | Filtering | Search · Empty |

## Which state is it?

The six states told apart by what the view is doing. A filled dot means the pattern is built for it.

| The view… | Empty | Loading | Errors | Overflow | Disabled | Read-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| has no records to show | Yes | No | No | No | No | No |
| is still fetching or saving | No | Yes | No | No | No | No |
| could not load its content | Yes | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| could not save | No | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| has more than fits | No | No | No | Yes | No | No |
| has a control that waits on something the person can fix here | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |
| shows a value this person cannot change right now | No | No | No | No | No | Yes |
| hides what this role can never use | No | No | No | No | Yes | No |

A load failure fills two markers: Errors owns its words, and Empty owns the slot they show in. To choose a layer for a task, use the chooser on the Templates overview.

# Read-only

A value someone could change but this person cannot right now. It stays in the tab order at full contrast, can be selected and copied, and says why in its caption.

**Kind:** Pattern

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/ReadOnly/ReadOnly.mdx`

## The three cases

Choose how to show a value by who can change it and what prevents editing.

- **Read-only.** Someone can change it; this person cannot right now. Neutral fill, full contrast, the reason in the caption.
- **Plain text.** Nobody ever changes it here. It is a label and a value, not a field.

The third case is Disabled: the value waits on something fixable on this screen. It is faded and out of the tab order, and it is never swapped with read-only.

## Key cases

## Usage

Use Read-only for a value someone could change but this person cannot right now: a session time the supervisor set, a field locked while a process runs, a record another person is editing. The common PLUS case is permission. Content that is never editable is plain text, not a read-only field.

| Who can change it | Show it as | Tab order | Looks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Someone else, or this person later | Read-only field | In | Neutral fill, full contrast, no chevron or calendar, no hover |
| Nobody, ever, here | Plain text: label and value | Out | Text |
| This person, once a prerequisite on this screen is met | Disabled field | Out | Faded, the reason in the caption |

## Alternatives

- For a value nobody changes here, show plain text in a details Section.
- For a field that waits on another on this screen, follow Disabled.
- For a value this person can change but rarely, use `InlineEdit`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Caption: "Set by your supervisor." | "Read-only", "Locked". |
| Caption: "Locked while the import runs." | "Temporarily unavailable". |
| Group caption: "Session details are set by Lincoln's supervisor." | A caption repeated on every field. |

## Accessibility

- `aria-readonly` on every read-only control that carries the role; it is reachable and read by screen readers with its label and caption.
- Text contrast is unchanged from an editable field.
- The value can be selected and copied with the keyboard.
- The caption is tied to the field, so the reason is read with it.

## Related

- Disabled: use for a prerequisite fixable on this screen.
- Forms: use for the form the read-only field sits in.
- Overflow: use for everything else that may clip.
- `TextField`, `TextArea`, `Select`, `DatePicker`, `TimePicker`, `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup`, `Toggle`: the components with `isReadOnly`.

## Best practices

### Keep a read-only field in the tab order at full contrast. {#keep-a-read-only-field-in-the-tab-order-at-full-contrast}

**Checked:** Automatic

It can be reached, read, selected and copied. `isReadOnly` sets `aria-readonly` on the controls that carry the role; the text keeps its color and the fill goes neutral. There is no hover change and the cursor is an arrow.

### Drop the interactive cues. {#drop-the-interactive-cues}

**Checked:** Automatic

`Select` hides its chevron and `DatePicker` its calendar button. `Checkbox`, `RadioGroup` and `Toggle` keep their state and ignore clicks.

### Say why in the caption. {#say-why-in-the-caption}

**Checked:** Review

"Set by your supervisor." "Locked while the import runs." One caption on a group is enough when every field in it is read-only for the same reason.

Do: Read-only at full contrast, with "Set by your supervisor" in the caption.
Don't: A faded value with no reason: out of the tab order and hard to read.

### Show a read-only value whole. {#show-a-read-only-value-whole}

**Checked:** Review

A `Select` wraps to show its full value; for a `TextArea`, set `rows` to show it all. Automatic TextArea growth is Planned .

### Show never-editable content as plain text. {#show-never-editable-content-as-plain-text}

**Checked:** Review

A field promises an input. A value nobody changes here is a label and a value in a details Section.

Do: A value nobody changes here is plain text.
Don't: A field for a value that was never editable: it promises an input.

### Keep read-only and disabled apart. {#keep-read-only-and-disabled-apart}

**Checked:** Automatic

Disabled is for a prerequisite fixable on this screen and leaves the tab order. Read-only is for content people must read.

## In code

From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#ReadOnly`.

```jsx
import { TextField } from '@/components';

function ReadOnlyExample() {
    return <TextField label="Student ID" value="S-1042" isReadOnly caption="Assigned by the school." />;
}
```

# Search How a person finds a record by typing, with a Search field in one of three modes: active, focused or basic. **Kind:** Pattern **Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/Search/Search.mdx` ## Choosing a type Three modes share one field. Choose by the amount of data and the cost of searching it. - **Active.** Small or on-screen data. The rows narrow in place as the person types. - **Focused.** A person's own work, found from the page they are on. A panel under the field lists recent searches, then matches grouped by type, and widens with "See all results". - **Basic.** Large or costly data. Nothing runs while typing; Enter takes the person to a results page. ## Active search The field starts the Section header's third row, compact, and collapses to an icon until it is needed. The results area under the header holds the count, the rows and the states; the header never moves. ## Focused search Focus in the field opens the panel. With no text it lists recent searches; while typing it lists matches grouped by type, then a last "See all results" row that runs a basic search. An optional action row, such as "Add student", closes the panel. ## Basic search The field alone. Typing runs nothing; Enter runs the search and a results page takes over. That page is its own template, outside this pattern. ## Scope filter and placement ## Usage Use Search when a person knows what a record is called. Search finds by name; Filtering narrows by attribute, so the two keep separate controls and separate counts. | Mode | Use when | Where the answer lands | | --- | --- | --- | | Active | The data is small or already on screen. | The rows in place, as you type. | | Focused | A person finds their own work from the page they are on. | A panel under the field; "See all results" widens it. | | Basic | The data is large or costly to search. | A results page, after Enter. | | Key or action | With text | Empty | | --- | --- | --- | | Type | Active: rows narrow and the count updates. Focused: the panel lists matches. | Focused: the panel lists recent searches. | | Enter | Basic: runs the search. Focused: chooses the row under the cursor, or runs the search when none is. | Nothing to run. | | Esc | Focused with the panel open: closes the panel and keeps the text. Otherwise clears the text. | A collapsible field closes and returns focus to the icon. | | Arrow keys | Focused: move through the panel's rows. | Focused: move through recent searches. | | Tab | Focused: closes the panel and moves on. | Moves on. | | "Clear search" | Clears the text; the field stays open. | Not shown. | | Leave the field | Stays open with its text. | A collapsible field shrinks back to the icon. | | Switch views | The search is kept. | Nothing to keep. | | "Reset filters" | Clears the search and every filter. | Nothing to clear. | ## Alternatives - For narrowing by an attribute, follow Filtering. - For picking one value from a long list, use a Select with its own search. - For moving to another area, follow Navigation. ## Content guidelines | Do | Don't | | --- | --- | | Placeholder starts with a verb and names the scope: "Search students". | "Search…", "Type to search". | | Count in words: "2 of 6 students", "0 of 6 students". | "2", "2 results". | | Clear button: "Clear search". | "×", "Reset". | | No matches: 'No students match "Zoe".' with "Reset filters". | "No results found." | | Scope filter: "All" first, then the kinds: "Students", "Sessions". | "Everything", "Any". | | Last panel row: "See all results for Ava". | "More", "Search". | ## Accessibility - The hidden label still names the field: the collapsed icon and the field share the placeholder's words. - The scope filter has its own name, "Search scope". - In focused, the input is the combobox: focus stays in it, the highlighted row is its active descendant and the panel is a named listbox. - The count in the results header is a polite live region, so "2 of 6 students" is announced as the rows narrow. - Focus stays in the field when the results empty; it never jumps to the empty state. - Loading is announced through the Spinner's status text. ## Parts | Part | Component | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Field | Search field | Mode `active`, `focused` or `basic`; compact in a bar, default in a page body. | | Panel | Popup | Focused only: recent searches, grouped matches, "See all results" and an optional action row. | | Rows | Dynamic table | Narrows as the text changes. | | No matches | Empty state | Fills the results body; offers "Reset filters". | | Loading | Skeleton | Takes the results body; a Spinner takes the search icon. | ## Related - Filtering: use for narrowing by attributes; its Reset clears the search. - Empty: use for the No matches state. - Loading: use for the wait while results load. - Section: use for where the header rows sit. ## Motion Search reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve. | Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | grow | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | The Search icon grows into a field to the left on spatial.fast, its right edge fixed. | | narrow | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Typing swaps the rows in place as they narrow. | | shrink | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Escape, or an empty blur, shrinks the field back to the icon on spatial.fast. | | panel | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | A focused search opens its panel the way a Popup opens: it fades in place under the field, and closing is the same fade. | ## Best practices ### Pick the mode by where the answer lands. {#pick-the-mode-by-where-the-answer-lands} **Checked:** Review Active when the rows are in hand and few, focused when the person jumps to a record from the page they are on, basic when the search is heavy enough to wait for Enter. One mode per field. ### Name the scope in the placeholder. {#name-the-scope-in-the-placeholder} **Checked:** Review "Search students". The label is hidden, so the placeholder is what a person reads and what names the collapsed icon. ### Add a scope filter when the search covers more than one kind of record. {#add-a-scope-filter-when-the-search-covers-more-than-one-kind-of-record} **Checked:** Review The filter sits before the field with "All" first and selected, and each scope carries its count. A search over one kind of record has no scope filter. ### Show the count in the results header, zero included. {#show-the-count-in-the-results-header-zero-included} **Checked:** Review "2 of 6 students", "0 of 6 students". The count lives in the results header, in words, and updates as the rows narrow. ### Answer no matches in the results body. {#answer-no-matches-in-the-results-body} **Checked:** Review An Empty state fills the results body, names what was searched and offers a next action: "Reset filters". The field stays where it is. ### Let loading mirror empty. {#let-loading-mirror-empty} **Checked:** Review While results load, Skeleton bars take the results body, a Spinner takes the search icon's place and the count slot says what is happening. See Loading. ### Keep the bar still. {#keep-the-bar-still} **Checked:** Review The field, the scope filter and the other bar controls hold their place in every state: typing, loading, no matches. Only the results area changes. ### Clear in two steps. {#clear-in-two-steps} **Checked:** Review Esc empties the text and keeps the field. In focused, the first Esc closes the panel and keeps the text, and the next clears it. A collapsible field closes on the Esc after that and returns focus to the icon. "Clear search" empties the text and leaves the field open. Switching views keeps the search; "Reset filters" clears it. ### Place by context: compact in a bar, default in a page body. {#place-by-context-compact-in-a-bar-default-in-a-page-body} **Checked:** Review The Section header holds controls of one height, 32, so the field takes `spacing="compact"` there. A search in a page body takes the default spacing and stays open. ## In code From `design-system/src/storybook-docs/patterns/CodeExamples.stories.jsx#Search`. ```jsx import { useState } from 'react'; import { SearchField } from '@/components'; import { Section } from '@/templates'; function SearchExample() { const [query, setQuery] = useState(''); return (
} >

{['Ana Ruiz', 'Ben Okafor'].filter((name) => name.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase())).join(', ')}

); } ```
guides.design-system/agent-views/templates/Pane:
# Panel

A full-height layer with no Blanket. Details sits on the right, docked beside the Page when it fits and floating over it when it does not; Notifications, the Inbox, sits at the start beside the Sidebar. Two types: Details and Notifications. The AI panel is a region of the Frame.

Import the Panel and its parts from `@/templates`. This template documents the parts and its layout within the Frame.

**Kind:** Template

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Panel/Panel.mdx`

## Types

Neither has a Blanket. Details opens on the right, docked beside the Page when it fits and floating over it when it does not (Width behavior has the widths); floating at every width is Planned. Notifications opens at the start, beside the Sidebar.

- **Details.** A quick look at a row, docked beside the Page or floating over its right by width. The picked row stays highlighted.
- **Notifications.** The Inbox, opened from the bell beside your name. It docks beside the Sidebar, 360 wide, and stays open as you pick one.

## Anatomy

### Details

Opened from a session row. The page behind stays usable.

1. **Splitter.** On the Page-facing edge; it resizes from 320 to 640.
2. **Header.** The title names the record, with its status in the Subheader row under it; then Edit and the fixed actions: Up, Down, More, Close.
3. **Body.** The record's Sections. It scrolls between the header and the footer.

The picked row stays highlighted on the page while the Panel is open.

### Notifications

Picking an item opens its page behind the Panel and marks it read. The Inbox stays open.

1. **Header.** The title, Mark all as read and Close.
2. **Tabs.** Unread, with its count, and All.
3. **Items.** One `NotificationItem` per update, grouped by day. An unread item says "Unread" to a screen reader.

The bell at the end of the Sidebar's account row, with its unread count, opens the Inbox. The Inbox docks beside the Sidebar at `--inbox-width` (360) over the page, never covers the Sidebar, and closes on Escape, with focus back on the bell, on an outside click or on Close.

## Width behavior

Drag the Frame's width. From 1168 a 400 Panel docks beside the Page at an edge line with no shadow. Under it the Panel floats on the overlay material and shadow, capped at 320 under 1024 and full width under 768. It never has a Blanket.

## Composition

The parts on their own, outside a Frame, at the width they are given.

## Key states

- **Editing.** The same Panel with the form open and its full-bleed footer: Discard (Default) left and Save (Primary) right; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. Save returns to reading, which has no footer.

- **With a form.** A short edit of a row with the page still in view: the fields in the body and the Panel's own footer. Validation and leaving with edits: Forms.

- **Record gone.** When the row no longer exists the body shows its empty state with a way back: Empty.

- **Under 1024.** Too narrow to dock beside the table: the Panel floats on the overlay material and shadow, capped as Width behavior says, still with no Blanket.

### Beside the AI panel

A floating Panel and the docked AI panel sit side by side, and the AI panel is never covered. The Frame has one Panel area today, so this pair is Planned.

## Sizes

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--panel-width-default` | 400 | The width a Panel opens at. |
| `--inbox-width` | 360 | The width the Inbox opens at, beside the Sidebar. |
| `--panel-min-width` | 320 | The narrowest, and the cap under 1024. |
| `--ds-surface-material-overlay`, `--ds-border-material`, `--ds-shadow-overlay` | pair | The floating Panel's fill, edge and elevation. The fill is translucent with no blur, and turns solid under reduced transparency and increased contrast. A docked or standalone Panel uses `--ds-surface` and an edge line. |
| `--ds-border` | 1 | The edge line where a docked Panel meets the Page. |

The Panel resizes from 320 to 640 by drag or keys, never past what keeps 720 of content beside it.

## Slots

```jsx
import { Frame, PanelContainer, PanelHeader, PanelBody, PanelFooter } from '@/templates';
```

The Panel components are the parts: header with its fixed actions, subheader, body, footer and disclaimer. The Frame hosts one, decides whether it docks or floats, and closes it on Escape. The template is its filled layout, one per type. The AI panel is the Frame's `panel`.

| Slot | Details | Notifications |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | The record's name, with its StatusTag under it | "Inbox" |
| `actions` | Edit, then Up, Down, More and Close | Mark all as read and Close |
| `backAction` · `titleIcon` | Optional, in the header before the title: a back action (`PanelBackAction`) and an icon. Pick the one the task needs. | None |
| `subheader` (`PanelSubheader`) | The record's StatusTag under the title | None: the Unread and All tabs sit under the header |
| `body` | Sections of the record; the form while editing | Items grouped by day, in Unread and All tabs |
| `footer` · `disclaimer` (`PanelFooter`, `PanelDisclaimer`) | Only while editing: Discard and Save, full bleed; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. The page composes it from Button. Planned as a prop. A `PanelDisclaimer` carries small print beside the actions. | None |
| Placement | Right. Docked from 1168; floating under it. Floating at every width is Planned. | Start, beside the Sidebar, 360 wide (`--inbox-width`), over the page with no Blanket. It opens from the Sidebar's bell, not from the Frame's Panel area. |
| Beside the AI panel | Planned. The Frame has one Panel area. | Planned. |

## Usage

Use a Panel when content is read beside the page and outlives a click: a quick look at a row, a short edit with the table in view, the Inbox. It never has a Blanket, so the page behind stays usable. Details sits on the right, docked beside the Page from 1168 and floating over it under that. The Inbox opens from the Sidebar's bell and docks beside the Sidebar at the start, 360 wide, over the page. One floating Panel is open at a time; opening another replaces it.

The AI panel is not a floating Panel. It is a region of the Frame, docked where there is room, so it persists across pages.

## Alternatives

- For a decision that must happen before the page continues, use `Modal`.
- For a queue page, use `Panel` docked beside the list; the record opens on demand.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For complex or multistep work, give the record its own page with a multi-step task on `Frame`.

## Parts

1. **Container** (`PanelContainer`). The outer surface. Its `width` falls back to the nearest `PanelProvider`'s width, then to `--panel-width-default`; inside the Frame's Panel area it fills the area instead.
2. **Header** (`PanelHeader`). An optional back action, an optional title icon, the title, and an action group (`PanelCloseAction`, `PanelMoreAction`).
3. **Subheader** (`PanelSubheader`). An optional row of secondary content under the header: tabs, a filter summary.
4. **Body** (`PanelBody`). The main content, which scrolls.
5. **Footer** (`PanelFooter`). Actions that commit a change, with an optional `PanelDisclaimer` for small print beside them.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The page ground with a leading edge. |
| Hovered | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Pressed | Nothing changes on the panel. |
| Focused | Not focusable. Focus goes to the fixed actions and the content. |
| Disabled | A panel has no disabled state. Disable the controls in it. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Ground and edge | `--ds-surface`; `--ds-border` at `--border-width-default` on the leading edge. |
| Header | Padding `--panel-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`; `--panel-inline-md` between its parts; `--border-width-default` rule below. |
| Action group | `--panel-inline-sm` between actions. |
| Subheader | Padding `--panel-subheader-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`; `--border-width-default` rule below. |
| Body | Padding `--panel-pad`. |
| Footer | Padding `--panel-pad-y` and `--panel-pad`, `--panel-inline-lg` between its parts; rule above; disclaimer in `--body-sm`, `--ds-text-subtle`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title Details with the record: "Ana Ruiz · Thu 4:00 PM". | "Details". |
| Name the filter by what it keeps: "Unread". | "Filter". |
| Give the empty state a way back: "Back to sessions". | "Nothing here". |
| Keep the disclaimer to one line. | Put instructions in the footer that belong in the body. |
| Name the footer's actions: "Discard" and "Save". | "OK" and "Done". |

## Accessibility

- Floating, the Panel is a complementary landmark named by its title, after the Page in reading order. Focus moves to its title on open and returns to the row, or the Bell, on close.
- Floating at a narrow width it is a dialog: focus is trapped, and Escape, a press outside or Close return it.
- The Frame closes the Panel on Escape unless an inner control handles it, such as an open menu.
- Up and Down are named "Previous" and "Next" and announce the record that opens.
- **`usePanelManager` outside a provider fails loudly.** Calling it without a `PanelProvider` ancestor throws, rather than silently falling back, so a missing provider is caught during development.
- An unread dot is paired with the text "unread" for a screen reader.

## Related

- Frame: use when the question is the AI panel, which is a Frame region.
- Section: use when a row or card opens in place inside its Section.
- Modal: use when the task needs full attention.
- Forms: use when the Panel edits a record.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules around a Panel: Navigation, Empty, Notifications.

## Motion

Panel reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| docked-enter | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-slow` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The AI Panel slides in from its edge while the page makes room; its content fades in once the page is about 90% done. A docked Panel never has a Blanket. |
| docked-exit | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Reverses and stays at the edge. |
| floating-enter | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Details and the Inbox slide in from their edge over the page; the Inbox grows out of the Sidebar from the left. A quick look promoted to its record grows from the Panel itself. |
| floating-exit | Dock and undock a panel | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` | Reverses. |
| narrow-enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-slow` | At narrow widths it slides over with a Blanket. |
| narrow-exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The same way back. |

## Best practices

### Float a Panel with no Blanket. {#float-a-panel-with-no-blanket}

**Checked:** Automatic

The page keeps scrolling and stays clickable. A press on the page outside the Panel, or Escape, closes it. Narrow, it is capped and then full width, still with no Blanket. A confirm Modal over a Panel brings its own Blanket.

Do: The Panel floats on its shadow and the page beside it stays undimmed.
Don't: The same Panel with a Blanket dimming the whole page.

### Open one floating Panel at a time. {#open-one-floating-panel-at-a-time}

**Checked:** Automatic

Another row swaps the content; the Inbox replaces Details. The overlay module keeps a second overlay closed.

Do: One Panel; another row swaps what it shows.
Don't: Two Panels open at once, the second covering the first.

### Keep the picked row highlighted while Details is open. {#keep-the-picked-row-highlighted-while-details-is-open}

**Checked:** Review

Picking the same row again closes it; Up and Down step through the rows.

### Show a footer only while editing. {#show-a-footer-only-while-editing}

**Checked:** Review

Discard (Default) and Save (Primary), full bleed; Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel. A declining action such as "Keep editing" is Default, in the left half. Reading needs no footer.

Do: Reading: a header and a body, nothing to save.
Don't: A footer of buttons on a Panel that is only read.

### Leave the AI panel uncovered. {#leave-the-ai-panel-uncovered}

**Checked:** Review

A floating Panel and the docked AI panel sit side by side. The AI panel is never covered. This pair is Planned.

The docked AI panel here is a second Panel in the docked slot; its own placement beside a floating Panel is not built yet.

Do: The floating Panel beside the docked AI panel, both fully visible.
Don't: The floating Panel drawn over the AI panel, hiding part of it.

### Move a Panel that needs full attention into a Modal. {#move-a-panel-that-needs-full-attention-into-a-modal}

**Checked:** Review

If the person must not look at anything outside it, it is a Modal.

### Grow the Inbox out of the Sidebar. {#grow-the-inbox-out-of-the-sidebar}

**Checked:** Review

Its left edge sits against the Sidebar, over the left of the Page. Picking an item opens its page behind the Inbox, which stays open. Flags still show at the top right. This placement is Planned.

### Give the Panel room to read. {#give-the-panel-room-to-read}

**Checked:** Review

Below its default width the title wraps and the body stops being scannable.

Do: Default width.
Don't: Squeezed to a narrow strip.

### Keep the header to one cue. {#keep-the-header-to-one-cue}

**Checked:** Review

An icon, a back action and a subheader together bury the title; pick the one the task needs.

### Share one width across a page's Panels with `PanelProvider`. {#share-one-width-across-a-page-s-panels-with-panelprovider}

**Checked:** Review

Wrap the region that can open Panels in a `PanelProvider`, and read or change the shared width with `usePanelManager`, so Panels opened over time stay the same size instead of each picking its own.

```jsx
<PanelProvider>
    <PanelContainer>
        <PanelHeader title="Student detail" actions={<PanelCloseAction onClick={close} />} />
        <PanelBody>...</PanelBody>
    </PanelContainer>
</PanelProvider>
```

### Reach for the fixed action components before building your own. {#reach-for-the-fixed-action-components-before-building-your-own}

**Checked:** Review

`PanelBackAction`, `PanelCloseAction` and the rest already carry the right icon, label and compact spacing; a custom `IconButton` for the same job risks a different icon or label than the rest of the system uses.

### Title the Panel with the object. {#title-the-panel-with-the-object}

**Checked:** Review

"Session · Mar 4", not "Details", so someone who opened it from elsewhere still knows.

### Offer "Open as page" in More. {#offer-open-as-page-in-more}

**Checked:** Review

For the step up when the quick look is not enough.
guides.design-system/agent-views/templates/Popu:
# Popup

A floating layer that hangs off its trigger and closes on an outside click. Six types: menu, profile menu, select list, content, filter menu and stacked filter menu.

**Kind:** Template

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Popup/Popup.mdx`

## Types

Each type composes the Popup component, which handles placement, outside clicks and Escape.

- **Menu.** Actions from a More button, at auto width. Applies on pick.
- **Profile menu.** From the account row: who is signed in, then links and Sign out. The 3-col width is Planned: today the menu hugs its rows.
- **Select list.** One list that applies as you pick: radios for one choice, checkboxes for several.
- **Content.** A preview or a short explanation. Anything wider is a Panel or a Modal.
- **Filter menu.** Two or three categories, held until Apply. Clear and Apply sit compact at the end.
- **Filter menu, stacked.** Four or more categories, or long lists, stacked at 3-col, or 4-col when the options need it. The categories scroll between the pinned header and footer.

## Anatomy

A filter menu off the Filter icon. Every part once; the layer is padded 16 and rounded 12 on the overlay pair.

1. **Trigger.** The control it hangs off. It shows the open state and, for the Filter icon, the count.
2. **Layer.** Hangs 4 below the trigger, aligned to the trigger's end edge because the trigger sits at the end of the bar. A titled layer's title is 14, whatever level the page around it is at.
3. **Rows or categories.** Menu rows; a list of checkboxes or radios; columns or stacked categories.
4. **Footer** (filter menu only). Clear (Subtle) and Apply (Default), compact, at the end. No Primary.

## Widths

Auto and the column steps of the screen grid, here at 1024. Auto follows the words: at least the trigger, 160 to 320. The steps follow the grid. The 2-col step, with a 200 floor, is Planned.

## Placement

Aligned to the edge of the trigger on the side where it sits. A trigger at the start of a bar, such as the view picker under page tabs, gets a layer aligned to its start edge. A trigger at the end, such as Filter or More, gets one aligned to its end edge. Both open 4 below.

## Key states

- **Long label.** A menu stops at 320. Past that a row ends in an ellipsis, and the full text opens in a Tooltip when clipped: Overflow. The Tooltip on a clipped row is Planned.

- **Loading a list.** One “Loading options” row, with no skeleton: Loading.

- **Load failed.** “Couldn't load options” with Retry; the menu stays open.

- **Flipped.** With no room below, the layer opens above the trigger and stays 8 from the screen edge.

- **Filter applied.** After Apply the menu closes and the count sits on the Filter icon's selected fill, read “Filters, 2 applied”. No tag row: Filtering.

## Sizes

| Width | 768 | 1024 | 1280 | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `auto` (default) | 160 to 320 | 160 to 320 | 160 to 320 | Menus and select lists; at least the trigger |
| 2-col | 200 (floor) | 200 (floor) | about 224 | A short choice list, a small date or time picker |
| 3-col | 200 | 264 | 328 | A filter menu; the profile menu once DropdownMenu takes a width |
| 4-col | 261 | 347 | 432 | Content, and a stacked filter menu whose options need it; the cap |

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--popup-min-width`, `--popup-max-width` | 160, 320 | The auto range. |
| `--popup-offset`, `--popup-gap-screen` | 4, 8 | Below the trigger; from the screen edge. |
| `--popup-pad`, `--popup-radius` | 16, 12 | The layer's pad and its corner radius (12, `--popup-radius`). |
| `--dropdown-menu-max-height` | 320 | A menu's rows scroll past this height. |
| `--ds-surface-overlay`, `--ds-shadow-overlay` | pair | The layer's fill and its one edge, the shadow's ring. |
| `--layer-popup` | 400 | The layer's place in the stack. |

## Slots

```jsx
import { Popup, DropdownMenu, PopupSelect, FilterMenu, IconButton } from '@/components';
```

Popup is the component: placement, offset, outside click and Escape. Each type is a composition on it: DropdownMenu for the menu and the profile menu, PopupSelect for one list, FilterMenu for several categories.

| Slot or prop | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `trigger` | The control it hangs off: an IconButton, a FilterButton, the labeled view trigger, the account row. |
| `placement` | `Popup` itself opens `top`. Under a bar, set `bottom-start` for a trigger at the start and `bottom-end` for one at the end; DropdownMenu and PopupSelect default to `bottom-start` and FilterMenu to `bottom-end`. It flips when there is no room. |
| `width` | `auto` (default) · `3-col` · `4-col`. |
| `width="2-col"` | Planned. The short-list step with a 200 floor. |
| `children` | Menu rows, a list, filter categories, or a short aside. |
| Filter footer | Clear and Apply, compact, at the end. It belongs to FilterMenu. |
| Profile menu width | Planned. DropdownMenu hugs its rows today; it takes the 3-col step once it takes a width. |
| Tooltip on a clipped row | Planned. The full text of a row that ends in an ellipsis. |

## Usage

Use a Popup for content anchored to a trigger that leaves on an outside click or Escape: a menu of actions, a list to pick from, the filter menu behind the Filter icon, the profile menu, a short aside. It brings no Blanket and the page stays usable.

| Type | Use when | Width | Applies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Menu | Choosing one action from a short list | auto | On pick |
| Select list | One category, picked as you go; the view picker under page tabs | auto | As you pick |
| Filter menu | Two or more categories applied together | 3-col; stacked, 3-col or 4-col | On Apply |
| Profile menu | The account row | auto today, 3-col once DropdownMenu takes a width | On pick |
| Content | A preview, a definition, a short explanation | 4-col at most | — |

## Alternatives

- For a decision before going on, use `Modal`.
- For content read alongside the page, use `Panel`.
- For one line that names a control, use `Tooltip`.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| A menu label that starts with the verb: "Reschedule". | A sentence as the label. |
| A category title in a filter menu: "Grade", "Tutor". | "Filter by grade". |
| A Filter Tooltip that names the control: "Filters". | "Click to filter the table". |
| Say Clear in a menu: Clear, Apply. | "Reset" or "Reset filters" inside the menu. |

## Accessibility

- The trigger carries `aria-haspopup` and an `aria-expanded` that tracks the open state. A Filter icon's name says what is on: "Filters, 2 applied".
- A menu moves focus to its first row; Up and Down move, and Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. A content Popup opened by a click or a key takes focus too: its first focusable element, or the popup itself when there is none. Tab reaches what is inside, and Escape or a click away returns focus to the trigger.
- A select list is a listbox or a group of checkboxes, and the chosen state is announced. The labeled view trigger reads "Status, Upcoming".
- In a filter menu, Clear and Apply are reachable after the categories. Apply announces the new count in words.
- A "Loading options" row is announced once, and "Couldn't load options" offers a Retry button.

## Related

- Section: use when placing the Filter icon, the view picker or More in the view bar.
- Modal: use when the content must be finished before going on.
- Panel: use when the content is wider than 4-col or outlives a click.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules around a Popup: Filtering, Overflow, Loading, Disabled.
- Popup: use when you need its props and states.

## Motion

Popup reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enter | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place; no clip, no travel. From the keyboard it opens with no animation. In-app Reduced mode shows it with no animation; the system reduced-motion setting keeps the fade. |
| exit | Open and close an overlay | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Fades in place, the same as the enter. |

## Best practices

### Hang a Popup 4 below its trigger, aligned to the trigger's edge on the side where it sits. {#hang-a-popup-4-below-its-trigger-aligned-to-the-trigger-s-edge-on-the-side-where-it-sits}

**Checked:** Automatic

A trigger at the start of a bar, such as the view picker under page tabs, gets a layer aligned to its start edge; a trigger at the end, such as Filter or More, gets one aligned to its end edge. So it grows into the page and stays on it. It flips above when there is no room below and stays 8 from the screen edge.

Do: More sits at the end of the bar, so its menu aligns to its end edge and grows into the page.
Don't: An end trigger with a start-aligned menu: it runs off the edge of the page.

### Make a menu at least as wide as its trigger, from 160 up to 320. {#make-a-menu-at-least-as-wide-as-its-trigger-from-160-up-to-320}

**Checked:** Automatic

It hugs the longest item. The width is set once, on open, so it holds still while someone types. A long or loading list opens at 320. A long row: Overflow.

Do: The menu is at least as wide as its trigger, so their edges line up.
Don't: A menu narrower than the trigger it hangs off: the edges no longer line up.

### Cap a Popup at 4-col, and keep it a short aside. {#cap-a-popup-at-4-col-and-keep-it-a-short-aside}

**Checked:** Review

Anything wider or longer is a Panel or a Modal. Anything with inputs the person must finish, steps or a long scroll belongs in a Modal. An auto-width Popup grows past 320 only to match a trigger wider than 320, never for its content.

Do: A content Popup at 4-col, the cap, holding a short explanation.
Don't: A long read in a Popup: anything this long is a Panel or a Modal.

### Put fields the person must finish in a Modal. {#put-fields-the-person-must-finish-in-a-modal}

**Checked:** Review

An outside click closes a Popup and loses what was typed.

Do: Fields to finish go in a Modal, over its Blanket.
Don't: A form in a Popup: an outside click loses what was typed.

### Open one Popup at a time, each off its own trigger. {#open-one-popup-at-a-time-each-off-its-own-trigger}

**Checked:** Automatic

A confirm Modal may open over a Popup and brings its own Blanket. A Popup opened from a Modal sits above it; a Tooltip sits above everything.

Do: One flat menu; a choice with two forms is two rows.
Don't: A menu opening a second Popup beside it: two layers off one trigger.

### Leave the Blanket to the Modal. {#leave-the-blanket-to-the-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

A Popup floats on the overlay pair, `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, and the page behind it stays usable.

### Keep a menu's label short and move the detail to its description. {#keep-a-menu-s-label-short-and-move-the-detail-to-its-description}

**Checked:** Review

Start with the verb: "Reschedule", "Export notes". An option that waits on something says why in its description line, as visible text.

When a list applies, and the words Clear and Reset filters: Filtering.

# Templates

Arrange components by filling a template's slots. Use patterns to guide the choices.

**Kind:** Template

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/storybook-docs/templates/TemplatesOverview.mdx`

## The eight templates

Templates run from broadest to smallest. Each page covers types, anatomy, key states and usage. See Templates and patterns below for how the layers fit together.

## Templates and patterns

Templates define slots; patterns guide decisions across templates.

### Three layers

Fill a template's slots; consult a pattern when choosing or reconsidering an approach. Each layer owns one kind of guidance.

- **Components** are single pieces with props, imported by name. The question is "Am I using this piece right?" Anatomy is the piece's parts.
- **Templates** are arrangements of components with slots. They hold key scenarios and key states, and link to components for detail. The question is "Are the slots filled right?" Anatomy is the numbered slots.
- **Patterns** are code-free guidance for a situation, shown on annotated templates used as they are or tweaked. The question is "Is this the right approach?" A pattern has no anatomy and no code.

### The tie-break

Behavior splits out into a component, and a template that only redraws one component stays a component. One component's behavior goes on the component page. How pieces sit in one template goes on that template's page. Anything that holds across two or more templates is a pattern.

The step up from a quick look to its own page is under Opening a record, below. A rule lives in one place. A template page that needs a pattern's rule links to it and keeps its own words for the slots.

### Frame, Screen, Flow

- **Frame:** the template. Sidebar, Page and the AI panel slot, in its default and bare types; a multi-step task runs in its inner sidebar.
- **Screen:** a Frame with its slots filled for one page. Screens are documented under Flows in Figma.
- **Flow:** Screens in order, fulfilling one user story. Flows are documented under Flows in Figma as well.

## Which template for which job

A suggested starting point for each scenario, with the patterns to consult and the components it is built from. Never "always use". To start from the situation instead, use the Patterns overview.

| Scenario | Template | Patterns | Components |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An area page with one collection | Page · default, with a Section view bar alone | Filtering · Search · Common actions | `PageHeader`, `Tabs` (pill), `FilterButton`, `IconButton`, `Button`, `Table` |
| A home page with several Sections | Page · default, titled Sections, cards | Empty · Loading | `PageHeader`, `Card`, `Button` |
| A record page, one level down | Page with a breadcrumb and page tabs | Navigation · Indicators | `Breadcrumb`, `PageHeader`, `StatusTag`, `Tabs`, `PopupSelect` |
| Working through a queue | Panel · Details, docked beside the list | Navigation · Common actions | `Table`, `Panel`, `Button` |
| A quick look at one row | Panel · Details | Navigation | `Panel`, `Button` |
| A short decision before going on | Modal · Active, confirm width | Common actions · Errors | `Dialog`, `Button` |
| A long task with steps | Frame multi-step task, with a form in steps | Forms · Navigation | `Sidebar` (inner mode), `Fieldset`, `FooterActions`, `Button` |
| Settings saved as a group | A settings form on the Page under its page-level Section header; subsections for several groups | Forms · Read-only · Disabled | `Fieldset`, `TextField`, `PopupSelect`, `Toggle`, `Button` |
| Narrowing a long catalog | Section with a filter side | Filtering | `Checkbox`, `PopupSelect`, `Button` |
| Signing in | Frame · bare | Forms · Errors | `Logo`, `TextField`, `Button` |
| Notifications | Panel · Notifications (the Inbox) | Notifications | `Panel`, `Avatar`, `PopupSelect` |
| AI chat | Frame, the AI panel region | AI interaction guidelines | `AiChat`, `PromptInput`, `AiMessage` |

## Frame, Modal, Panel or Popup?

One chooser for the four layers that take over from the page or sit above it. A filled dot means the layer is built for it.

| The task… | Frame · multi-step | Modal | Panel | Popup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| blocks the page until it is done | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| keeps the page in view and usable | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| holds a long task, or five or more steps | Yes | No | No | No |
| holds a short sequence of steps | Yes | Yes | No | No |
| takes a form | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| is a destructive confirm | No | Yes | No | No |
| hangs off its trigger | No | No | No | Yes |
| dims the page under a Blanket | No | Yes | No | No |
| has its own URL | Yes | No | No | No |
| closes on Escape and returns focus | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |

A Panel that needs full attention becomes a Modal. Anything wider than 4-col, or that outlives a click, leaves the Popup for a Panel. Leaving a multi-step task goes through Save and exit, and unsaved work asks first, in a Modal.

## Opening a record

Least room to most. Pick the lowest step that fits; Navigation holds the rule.

Where a message sits, in a Frame, Page or Section banner, a Flag or a SectionMessage, is Notifications.
