<!-- Tier: 2 -->

# Figma

Machine-readable contracts and human runbooks so Cursor prototypes, Storybook, and the Figma design system stay aligned on **tokens** and **components**.

## Canonical Figma file

| Field | Value |
|-------|--------|
| Name | Design System - BS4 Foundation Component Library |
| `fileKey` | `zAecJNRdvJzAUOcjV32tRX` |
| URL | https://www.figma.com/design/zAecJNRdvJzAUOcjV32tRX/Design-System---BS4-Foundation--Component-LIbrary- |

## What lives where

Protocol is authored here in `design-system/guidelines/figma/`; the registries it
governs are generated and stay beside the source they describe in
`design-system/figma/`.

| File | Where | State |
|------|-------|-------|
| `registry-load-gate.md` | this folder | **MANDATORY** — load both registries before any implement, write-back, or design-to-code mapping |
| `component-alignment.md` | this folder | Workflow for agents and contributors (implement + write-back) |
| `mcp-guide.md` | this folder | Figma MCP tool reference + implement-design workflows |
| `token-mapping.md` | this folder | Figma ↔ CSS token mapping (authoritative) |
| `page-documentation.md` | this folder | The page standard: Sections, layout and reflow, annotations, the Docs frame, naming, and the done test |
| `parity-2026-07.md` | this folder | Dated Figma ↔ Storybook parity snapshot |
| `component-registry.json` | `design-system/figma/` | **Generated** — import ↔ Figma component set ↔ props |
| `token-registry.json` | `design-system/figma/` | **Generated** — Figma variable ↔ CSS custom property, validated against SCSS |
| `component-figma-links.md` | `design-system/figma/` | **Generated** — Figma node links per component |
| `knowledge-audit.md` | `design-system/figma/` | **Generated** — verification status (edit `knowledge-audit.json` beside it) |
| `patterns.json` | `design-system/figma/` | Hand-authored source for the `patterns` section of `component-registry.json` |

## Source of truth: per-component MDX

The Figma mapping for each component lives in that component's MDX file as a non-rendered ESM export:

```jsx
export const figmaMeta = {
  fileKey: "zAecJNRdvJzAUOcjV32tRX",
  props: { /* optional code-side enum/boolean props */ },
  sets: [
    {
      id: "primary-buttons",
      name: "Primary buttons",
      componentSetNodeId: "123:456",
      codeDefaults: { appearance: "primary" },
      variantProps: { spacing: "spacing", appearance: "appearance", state: "state" },
      variantValueMap: { /* Figma enum label → code value */ },
      status: "verified"
    }
  ],
  deliberate: { /* optional: code prop → one-line reason it differs from the library on purpose */ }
};
```

- To change a mapping (node ID, variants, props), **edit the component's MDX `figmaMeta`**, not the registry.
- `deliberate` is where a person settles a DS precedence row as intended: one entry per code prop, its value the reason in one line, e.g. `deliberate: { "size": "Code sizes the textarea; the library sizes it by its frame." }`. The registry carries it as `figma.deliberate`, and the weekly DS precedence check skips every disagreement on that prop while the entry stands; delete the entry and the row comes back.
- `status` is `verified` when the node was read from Core and matches, or `missing` when Core has no main component for this code component yet. A `missing` entry carries no `componentSetNodeId` and its `notes` say what was searched and when. Treat it as a gap to report, never as permission to use a Deprecated or Archive set. Before you mark one missing, search the page's Updated section for a COMPONENT as well as a COMPONENT_SET: a single component (Footer, Tooltip, Panel) is not a set, and it is mapped with `isComponentSet: false`.
- `component-registry.json` is regenerated from all `figmaMeta` exports.
- `export const figmaMeta` is placed after imports and before `<Meta>`; Storybook does not render it.

### Token source of truth: `token-mapping.md`

`token-registry.json` is generated from `design-system/guidelines/figma/token-mapping.md`. Every `var(--*)` is validated against `design-system/src/tokens/*.scss`, so a mapping to a non-existent token fails the check.

- To change a token mapping, **edit `design-system/guidelines/figma/token-mapping.md`**, not the registry.
- Spacing is **contextual** (per layer: element / card / section / modal / surface / table) — there is no single `Spacing/N` → one token.

## Regenerating agent + Figma artifacts

```bash
# One command after editing MDX figmaMeta, token-mapping, or tokens SCSS
npm run generate:agent

# Or individually:
npm run generate:component-registry
npm run check:component-registry

npm run generate:token-registry
npm run check:token-registry
```

## Code-side source of truth

- Components: `design-system/src/components/` (forms live in `components/forms-and-inputs/`), `specs/`
- Tokens: `design-system/src/tokens/` (most families synced from a manual Figma export; the token ladder and motion in `tokens/ladder/` generate the other way, code → Figma, per ADR-038)
- Agent knowledge entry: `design-system/guidelines/overview.md`
- Agent views (generated): `design-system/agent-views/`

## Pilot status (Button)

- [x] Button page in Core → `3497:19482` → `Button` with `appearance` and `spacing`
- [ ] Button component-set `node-id` — read from the Updated section on the Core Button page
- [ ] Round-trip validated on prototypes page

## Quick commands

```bash
# Regenerate component registry from per-component MDX figmaMeta (59 components)
npm run generate:component-registry
npm run check:component-registry

# Regenerate token registry from token-mapping.md (validated vs SCSS)
npm run generate:token-registry
npm run check:token-registry

# Sync tokens from Figma (requires .env)
npm run generate:tokens  # exported Figma JSON under tokens/source/ -> SCSS
```

---
summary: Words, people, sentences and mechanics for product copy
---

<!-- Tier: 2 -->

<!-- Human twin: Brand › Content › Language (Storybook). The two change together. -->

# Language

One way to write each thing, so every screen reads the same. A Do/Don't pair
appears only where a rule is ambiguous.

## Words

- Use the word a tutor would say out loud: verbs over abstract nouns, short words over long ones.
  - Do: "Pick a time that works for you."
  - Don't: "Choose your availability."
- Spell out team terms. A new tutor doesn't know the shorthand yet.
  - Do: "Your tutor improvement plan is ready."
  - Don't: "Your TIP is ready."

PLUS word list:

| Say | Not |
|-----|-----|
| session | meeting, class |
| call off | cancel |
| fill-in | sub |
| lead tutor | TA, captain |
| reflection | survey |
| student | kid, tutee |

`GLOSSARY.md` holds the canonical product terms.

## People

Write so every student, family and school is included, including those who never open the app.

- Describe the work, not who the student is.
  - Do: "Leo is working on two-step equations."
  - Don't: "Leo is struggling with equations."
- Write for any household; families, devices and quiet rooms differ.
  - Do: "Ask someone at home to sign the form."
  - Don't: "Ask a parent or guardian to sign the form."
- Show the least you need. Shared screens get first name and last initial; research exports carry no names.
  - Do: "Ana P. · Grade 7" on a projected screen.
  - Don't: "Ana Pérez · Grade 7" on a projected screen.

## Sentences

- Say who acted; use passive only in a tight flag.
  - Do: "Your lead tutor approved the swap."
  - Don't: "Swap approved." in a notice
- PLUS is "we", the reader is "you". Use contractions.
  - Do: "We'll remind you 30 min before."
  - Don't: "A reminder will be sent 30 min before."

## Mechanics

| Topic | Rule | Example |
|-------|------|---------|
| Capitalization | Sentence case everywhere: titles, headings, navigation, buttons, labels | Open session notes |
| Punctuation | No period in titles, buttons or labels; no exclamation marks in errors | Reflection submitted |
| Numbers | Digits in the UI; spell out one to nine in a sentence | 3 sessions left |
| Dates | Shortest clear format; add the year only in records | Wed, Nov 13 |
| Times | 12-hour, always with the time zone: tutors and schools sit in different zones | 3:30 PM ET |
| Ranges | En dash, no spaces | 3:30–4:15 PM ET |
| Recent | Relative under a week, then the date | 10 min ago · Yesterday · Nov 4 |
| School calendar | Terms, not quarters | Fall term |

Do/Don't for times:
- Do: "Wed, Nov 13 · 3:30 PM ET"
- Don't: "Wed, Nov 13 at 3:30 PM"

---
summary: Message anatomy, type to component, and how to write each type
---

<!-- Tier: 2 -->

<!-- Human twin: Brand › Content › Messages (Storybook). The two change together. -->

# Messages

## Anatomy

Every message has three parts.

1. **Title.** What happened, in 2 to 5 words.
2. **Body.** Why, and what it means for the reader, in 1 or 2 sentences.
3. **Action.** A verb that says what the button does.

## Type to component

| Type | When | Component |
|------|------|-----------|
| Error | Something failed and the reader can act | Flag, SectionMessage, InlineMessage |
| Warning | Before a step that is hard to undo | Modal, SectionMessage |
| Success | A task finished | Flag |
| Info | Context that helps, then gets out of the way | Banner, SectionMessage |
| Empty | Nothing to show yet | EmptyState |
| Discovery | Something new and useful | Spotlight |

Props and variants come from each component's own file.

## Writing each type

- **Error: reassure, then fix.** Say what broke, what is safe, and the next step.
  - Do: "Notes didn't save" · "Your connection dropped. Your draft is safe on this device." · Try again
  - Don't: "Notes didn't save" · "Something went wrong. Try again."
- **Warning: name who it affects.** Say what happens to other people, then name both buttons.
  - Do: "Call off Thursday's session?" · "Jordan's teacher gets a note, and we look for a fill-in." · Keep session / Call off
  - Don't: "Call off this session?" · "You can't undo this." · Cancel / Call off
- **Success: say what's next.** Name what finished, then what happens with it.
  - Do: "Reflection submitted" · "Your lead tutor reads it before Friday's check-in."
  - Don't: "Reflection submitted" · "Thanks for sharing."
- **Empty: say how it fills.** Say why it's empty and what fills it.
  - Do: "No sessions this week" · "Sessions show up here once your lead tutor schedules them."
  - Don't: "No sessions this week" · "Check back later."
- **Field error: write the fix.** One line under the field, phrased as what to do, with the unit.
  - Do: "Enter 30 to 90 minutes."
  - Don't: "Must be between 30 and 90."
- **Info and discovery:** lead with what the reader gains; one action, or none.

Wording follows [language.md](language.md); tone follows [voice-and-tone.md](voice-and-tone.md).

---
summary: Product copy rules, one file per Brand › Content page
---

<!-- Tier: 2 -->

# Content

What a tutor, student or school reads inside the app. A button label is as much
a component decision as its padding, so the rules sit with the design system.
Each file mirrors one human page in Storybook (Brand › Content) and the two
change together.

| Reach for | When the copy is |
|-----------|------------------|
| [voice-and-tone.md](voice-and-tone.md) | Choosing how it sounds, or how that shifts for the reader |
| [language.md](language.md) | Any word, name, sentence, date, time or number |
| [messages.md](messages.md) | An error, warning, success, info, empty or discovery message |

**Not this folder:** how *agents* write — commit messages, PRDs, Slack replies,
long-form articles. That is `docs/conventions/`.

---
summary: The four voice words, when to dial them, and tone by reader
---

<!-- Tier: 2 -->

<!-- Human twin: Brand › Content › Voice and tone (Storybook). The two change together. -->

# Voice and tone

PLUS sounds like a supportive teammate, not a policy manual. Tutors are college
students between classes and sessions. Write the way they talk.

## Voice

Four words, each serving one thing the product promises.

| Word | Serves | In practice |
|------|--------|-------------|
| Helpful | Productivity | Lead with the next step. Name the action, then the reason. |
| Honest | Learning | Say what happened and what is still unknown. Name skills, leave out labels. |
| Warm | Uplift | Acknowledge the person's effort. Promise only what we will do. |
| Clear | Simplicity | Everyday words, short sentences, one idea each. |

## Dial

The voice stays; the volume moves with the moment.

- Dial warm up after a finished task. Dial it down when something failed.
- Dial honest up when work is at risk or hard to undo.
- Dial helpful up in onboarding and empty states.
- Dial clear up in every error, and in anything with a deadline.

## Tone by reader

| Reader | Tone | Example |
|--------|------|---------|
| New tutor, onboarding | Instructional, encouraging | Finish these three steps before your first session. |
| Tutor, live session | Supportive, brief | Nice — Leo answered correctly. Move on when you're ready. |
| Tutor, admin and scheduling | Professional, neutral | Your October payout has been processed. |
| Lead tutor | Direct, specific | Two reflections are due before Friday's check-in. |
| Student | Plain, encouraging, no jargon | You finished two-step equations. |
| School or family | Respectful, plain, no team terms | Sessions start at 10:30 AM ET on Monday. |

Word choices follow [language.md](language.md); message structure follows
[messages.md](messages.md).

summary: A chart's foundations other than color come from the same component tokens as the rest of the design system
---

<!-- Tier: 2 -->

# Data visualization

Chart color has rules of its own (the Storybook Color page,
[`Colors.mdx`](../../src/styles/Colors.mdx) § Data-viz color). For every other foundation — spacing, radius, elevation,
stroke, type, layers, motion — there is no chart-specific exception: a chart
takes the same component tokens the rest of the design system does. This page
names which token does which job, and why, for `design-system/src/dataviz/`
(theme, helpers, 42 charts, stories, MDX).

## Chart container

The chart container is a Card: its surface and its padding, not a chart-drawn
box. `chartTheme.js`'s `chart.spacing` reads `--card-pad` — the
density this component already rendered at — not a literal `16`. Highcharts'
`chart.spacing` is a layout number, not a CSS property, so it can't take a
`var()` string directly; `chartTheme.js` resolves the token to a pixel number
once, at module load, via `getComputedStyle`, so a ladder change still reaches
the chart without a code edit. The chart itself draws no padding of its own
beyond that.

## Tooltip

The tooltip is a floating layer: the Popup template's surface
(`--ds-surface-overlay`), overlay shadow (`--ds-shadow-overlay`), radius
(`--popup-radius`) and padding (`--popup-pad`), plus the shared
`--layer-popup` z-index. `useHTML` alone only moves the tooltip's TEXT into a
foreignObject — the box Highcharts draws around it is always its own SVG
`<path>`, and `background`/`border-radius`/`box-shadow` are no-ops there, so
styling `.highcharts-tooltip` (that path's `<g>`) never painted anything.
`chartTheme.js` also sets `tooltip.outside: true`, which moves the whole
tooltip into `.highcharts-tooltip-container` — a real `<div>` — and turns the
SVG box fully transparent (`backgroundColor: 'transparent'`, `borderWidth: 0`,
`shadow: false`) so the container's CSS surface (`chartTheme.css`) is the only
thing a reader sees. Every chart that sets its own `tooltip` block spreads
`chartTheme.tooltip` so it inherits this; `foundations.test.js` fails a chart
that doesn't.

## Sorting

Category charts with no inherent axis order sort categories from most to least by default (`sort = true`), with `sort={false}` as the opt-out for ordinal, temporal or profile axes (such as grades A–E, weekdays or radar spokes). Sorting and sequential toning are two separate, explicit steps in `design-system/src/dataviz/palette.js`:

- **Step 1 — sort:** `mostToLeast(items, value = (d) => d.y)` returns a new, stable array ordered from biggest to smallest. When categories and series live in separate arrays, `sortCategories({ categories, series, value = (d) => d.y })` reorders both (pass `value: (d) => d` for plain numeric data) and returns `{ categories, series, order }` so callers can reorder parallel arrays (such as icons or colors) with `order`.
- **Step 2 — optionally tone by rank:** `toneByRank(items, hue, value = (d) => d.y)` ranks items by `value` while keeping their input order and sets `color` on each item from `sequentialTone(rank, items.length, hue)`, placing the darkest ramp step (`--chart-<hue>-boldest`) on the largest value (rank `0`) and spreading `items.length` items across the ramp down to `subtler`.

A single series uses one color, `--chart-brand` (`BRAND`), so the chart never implies multiple categories where there is only one measure.

## Mark radius

Bars and columns round only the value end — the one end a bar is allowed to
round without distorting the length comparison it exists to support; rounding
both ends, or a radius bigger than a couple of pixels, reads as "this bar is
shorter than it is." `--chart-bar-radius` (`chartTheme.css`, aliasing
`--space-0125`, ~2px) is the one component-tier token for it, applied via
Highcharts' `borderRadius: { radius, where: 'end' }` — `where: 'end'` is what
keeps a stacked column from rounding every segment, only the stack's outer
end. Pies, donuts and areas take no radius at all.

## Strokes

Gridlines, axis lines, series lines, chart-only separators (e.g. the gap
between stacked bar segments) and markers take one of two component-tier
tokens, declared in `chartTheme.css`, aliasing the same stroke-width
primitives `--focus-ring-width` reads:

- `--chart-line-width` (2px) — a series line, a box-plot whisker, a marker
  ring, a stacked-segment separator.
- `--chart-grid-width` (1px) — a gridline or an axis line.

Like `chart.spacing`, these feed Highcharts options that render as SVG
presentation attributes rather than CSS properties, so `chartTheme.js`
resolves each to a number once and exports it (`CHART_LINE_WIDTH_NUMBER`,
`CHART_GRID_WIDTH_NUMBER`) for a chart to use directly. A `0` (removing a
default Highcharts border or line entirely) needs no token — it draws nothing.

## Type and numbers

Every text slot in a chart — title, subtitle, caption, axis labels and titles,
legend items, data labels, tooltips and empty-data notices — takes the Noto Sans
body family (`--type-family-body`) and the current text tokens
(`--type-size-075`, `--type-weight-semibold`, `--type-weight-medium`, and so on) — never a
`'12px'` literal, never a token `var()` paired with a literal fallback
value, and never a system-font fallback or a monospace
font. Titles and emphasized values use semibold (`--type-weight-semibold`, 600);
labels and supporting copy use medium (`--type-weight-medium`, 500). Nothing
renders at 700 or 300, and data-label text outlines stay off.

Number slots (axis tick labels, data labels, tooltips, legend items and
emphasized values) set tabular figures (`tabular-nums`) so columns of numbers
and live readouts align digit for digit. Inside a tooltip, text stays in
`--ds-text` while only the leading dot swatch (`●`) takes the series color. A
chart's title comes from the surrounding Section or Card header, not from Highcharts'
own `title` option (every chart sets `title: { text: null }`).

## States

Interactive states are declared once in the shared theme:

- **Hover:** a hovered mark shifts to its `-hovered` chart token (such as
  `--chart-categorical-1-hovered` or `--chart-brand-hovered`) on
  `appearance.fast`.
- **Inactive series:** while one series is hovered, the other series fade to
  `--ds-opacity-disabled` on `appearance.fast`.
- **Selected:** a selected mark takes `--ds-background-selected` with a 1px
  (`--chart-grid-width`) `--ds-border-selected` outline, never `--chart-brand`.

## Motion

Charts follow the same spring physics and choreography as the rest of the design system:

- **Entrance:** charts grow to their value on the default spatial spring (`spatial.default`). Charts inside a `ChartMotionArea expressive` take the expressive spring instead; the page's `data-motion="expressive"` attribute does not reach Highcharts, which animates in JavaScript.
- **State changes:** hover and inactive series transitions fade on `appearance.fast`.
- **Reduced motion:** reduced motion makes every entrance a fade (`appearance.fast`), even inside a `ChartMotionArea expressive`.
- **One orchestrated moment per area:** charts in one area arrive 20 ms apart within half a second (500 ms cap); a standalone chart enters with no delay.
- **No replay:** a chart animates on its first render only; nothing replays on redraw, resize or data update, and micro-charts such as a sparkline opt out of entrance motion altogether.

## Token checks

`foundations.test.js` and `chartText.test.js` hold `design-system/src/dataviz/`
to the tier tokens and enforce a hard ban (with a self-test) against eased
curves, animation millisecond literals and removed animation props, `<b>` or
`bold` or numeric font weights and weights other than 500 and 600,
series-color text, pixel offsets, control radii on non-controls, and number
slots without tabular figures; `design-system/tests/dataviz-tokens.test.js`
does the same for color.
guides.design-system/src/templates/Card/index.m:
# Card

PLUS card: an optional image, content and footer on a `sunken`, `default`, or `raised` surface. - **Surface**: `sunken` (default, flat), `default` (page surface with a 1px border, flat), or `raised` (raised surface and shadow). Every card carries a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) so forced colors draw its edge. - **Image placement**: `top` (default), `start` or `end`. Side images apply at the 480 minimum width and fill the height. `imageSplit` chooses one third (default) or one half; half uses Heading md on a side card. Below the 480 minimum width, the image returns to the top with its own ratio. - **Image ratio**: `imageRatio` is `16:9` (default), `4:3` or `1:1`. A top image's height is the card width times the ratio, rounded to a multiple of 4 so the card stays on the 4 px grid; the picture crops to cover and the text sets the rest of the height. - **Header** (`_Card header`): `title` (the card title type, shared with Card in `styles/_card-title.scss`, one heading level below its section) over an optional `description` (Body/default 14), with `actions` at the end of the row. `header` replaces that block with custom content, like the header's `custom` type, for tabs or a toolbar. - **Spacing** comes from the Card tokens: padding uses `--card-pad` and radius uses `--card-radius` at every size, the header sits Card/stack-md above the body (`gap` picks the stack step), and the footer sits Card/stack-lg below. The footer hugs the start: one action that goes somewhere is a link (`appearance="link"`), two are a compact pair with no Primary, and a card that is all one action is clickable with no buttons. - The card hugs its content; in a row it stretches to the tallest card. - **Elevation**: a clickable `sunken` or `default` card lifts to Raised on hover in place and settles to the raised shadow while pressed; a clickable `raised` card lifts to the raised hovered step under the overlay shadow and settles back onto the raised shadow while pressed; `dragging` puts any card on the overlay pair while it moves. The card also sets the current surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

Also asked as: summary card, object card.

**Import:** `import { Card } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Card (`ds guide card`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`)

**Source:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.stories.jsx` — Overview, Interactive, Elevation, Anatomy, Jobs, MinWidth224, MinWidth304, MinWidth480, ImageWide, ImageStandard, ImageSquare, ImageRatioGrid, ImageRatioDefault, ImageTop, ImageTopHovered, ImageTopPressed, ImageTopDragging, ImageStart, ImageStartHovered, ImageStartPressed, ImageStartDragging, ImageEnd, ImageEndHovered, ImageEndPressed, ImageEndDragging, ImageStartHalf, ImageEndHalf, ImageTopIgnoresSplit, BodyOnly, WithFooter, CustomHeader, SurfaceSunken, SurfaceDefault, SurfaceRaised, Static, Clickable, Dragging, ForcedColors, LoadingCard, Rows, PlacementBoundary

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Card/Card.mdx`

**Motion:** change `appearance.fast` · milestone `spatial.default`, sound `sound.done.milestone`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

Use a card when one object needs its own container on the page. Pick `surface` by the card's role: `sunken` (default) groups static content on `--ds-surface-sunken` without a shadow; `default` pairs `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border` on the Frame, on Sunken or colored areas, and for dense rows; `raised` pairs `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised` for the one primary card per view, first in reading order. A card holds a heading, content and an optional footer for actions. Fill its slots with your own parts.

1. Pick the size by what the card holds.
2. Choose a header, or omit it when the body carries its own title.
3. Fill the body slot. Add spacing only inside slot content, using Card stack tokens.
4. Add a footer only for actions that commit.

### Color

To give a card a semantic or accent fill, swap its surface token for a solid brand (`--ds-background-brand-subtlest`, or `--ds-background-brand-bold` with `--ds-text-inverse`), status (`--ds-background-information`, `--ds-background-success`), accent-subtlest (`--ds-background-accent-teal-subtlest`), or selected (`--ds-background-selected`) background token. `surface="raised"` keeps `--ds-shadow-raised`. On a clickable colored card, hovered and pressed states use that same token's `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps.

### Width guidance

Content picks the minimum width. Choose the narrowest card that holds the content without clipping, then let the row decide how many fit. Height always hugs the content, and a card in a row stretches to the tallest card.

| Minimum width | When to use | Pad | Radius | Token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 224 | One number or one line. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-sm` |
| 304 | A short list or a few lines. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-md` |
| 480 | A summary with several parts. | 16 | 16 | `--card-min-width-lg` |

`minWidth` sets the minimum width; every width uses `--card-pad` (16) and `--card-radius` (16). The text sets the height, and a top image takes its `imageRatio` height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4. Set a height cap with `style`'s `maxHeight`; the card clips what passes it.

### Cards in a row

In a row, place the most cards that keep each card at its minimum width. Each row is the content width of its mode, with a 16 gutter. The count switches between viewport widths of 1224 and 1256 with the sidebar docked.

| Mode | Content width | Min 224 | Min 304 | Min 480 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium, 768 | 720 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Large, 1024 | 736 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| X-Large, 1440 | 1152 | 4 | 3 | 2 |

## Motion

Card reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | It changes color on hover and press like a Button. Opening a clickable card is Drill. |  |
| milestone | Load content | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The one card in a milestone page entrance is Expressive and leaves by the exit rules. | `sound.done.milestone` on land: onboarding complete, first session, goal reached, term start or end, achievement claimed; goal reached is shared, so the student hears it |

## Best practices

### Fit the width to what the card holds. {#fit-the-width-to-what-the-card-holds}

Visible empty space inside the card means a narrower minimum width. A clipped or crowded body means a wider one.

Do: One number fits the 224 minimum; the card is only as wide as it needs, so a row of them stays tidy.
Don't: The same number at 480 leaves most of the card empty; narrow it instead of filling the space.

### Never put a card inside a card. {#never-put-a-card-inside-a-card}

A card's fill and edge are its own object boundary. Group related cards in a Section instead.

Do: One card; three metrics stacked in its body, split by dividers.
Don't: Three mini cards inside the card; borders and shadows pile up and the hierarchy flattens.

### Keep the card in place while it loads. {#keep-the-card-in-place-while-it-loads}

Do: Loading keeps the card in place: a skeleton fills the body, so the layout does not jump when data arrives.
Don't: A bare loading line takes the card away; the row collapses and everything below it moves.

### Let the footer's job pick its buttons. {#let-the-footer-s-job-pick-its-buttons}

A card's footer actions hug the start, under the content. One action that goes somewhere, such as View session, is a link. Two actions are a compact Default pair with no Primary. A card that is all one action is clickable and has no buttons. Only a Modal or Panel footer, on FooterActions, fills tracks and ends in a Primary. The whole rule: Common actions.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading one level below the section the card sits in: an h3 in a section, an h2 straight on a page. Nest the card in a Section rather than choosing a tag.
- A card that is clickable as a whole needs a role and a tab stop, and it must answer Enter and Space. When the card has one action, put a Button in the footer instead.
- Mark the card `aria-busy` while it loads. The skeleton bars are hidden from assistive technology.
- The hover lift is never the only cue that a card is clickable. Pair it with a visible action or a link in the card.
- Every card keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) so forced colors draw its edge.
- Text sits on each surface in `--ds-text` and `--ds-text-subtle`, which meet contrast in every color mode.
- The card sets `--ds-utility-elevation-surface-current` to its chosen surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

## Related

- Section for a region that holds cards under one heading.
- Table for many objects of the same shape that people compare across columns.
- Page for the content area's own fill, header and elevation.
- Modal for something that must be decided before the page can continue.

Same group: `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Parts

1. **Image** (optional). A slot above everything else, or beside the content in a side layout. It runs edge to edge, outside the pad, and the card radius clips its corners. On top, `imageRatio` (16:9 default, 4:3 or 1:1) sets its height from the card width, rounded to a multiple of 4, and the picture crops to cover; beside the content it fills the full height at one third or one half of the width and crops to cover.
2. **Header.** The title, an optional description and an optional actions slot. A custom `header` replaces all three. The title uses Heading xs at every heading level, stepping up to Heading md for a half side image. The description uses Body default. In Figma the title truncates to one line and the description's `text` variant truncates at three lines or wraps; code leaves wrapping to CSS.
3. **Body.** A slot for text, a list or media.
4. **Footer** (optional). A start-aligned slot for the card's actions: one link, or a compact pair with no Primary.

The image sits above (or, in a side layout, beside) a padded frame, and the header, body and footer sit inside it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | `sunken` (default): `--ds-surface-sunken`, flat. `default`: `--ds-surface` with a 1px `--ds-border`, flat. `raised`: `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. Every surface keeps a 1px border (transparent on sunken and raised) for forced colors. |
| Hovered | A clickable card only: `sunken` and `default` lift in place to `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`; `raised` lifts to `--ds-surface-raised-hovered` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`. A card with no `onClick` does not change. |
| Pressed | A clickable card only: settles to `--ds-surface-raised-pressed` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. |
| Focused | The card has no focus style of its own. A card made clickable as a whole takes `role` and `tabIndex` from you. |
| Disabled | A card is never disabled. Disable the controls inside it. |
| Dragging | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, held under hover and press. |
| Loading | Skeleton bars in the body, with `aria-busy` on the card. Figma's `loading?` has no prop in code. |

### Tokens

| Token | Value | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--card-pad` | 16 | Padding inside a card at every width. |
| `--card-radius` | 16 | Corner rounding of a card at every width. |
| `--card-stack-sm`, `-md`, `-lg` | 4 · 8 · 12 | Title to description; header to body, set by `gap`; body to footer. |
| `--card-inline-md` | 8 | Items on a row, such as actions in the header. |

# Frame

The Page runs the full height, and meets a docked Sidebar at its 1px edge. - The Frame owns the Sidebar state and hands it to the Sidebar through `SidebarControlContext`. Open, the toggle (`angles-left`) ends the Sidebar's logo row; closed, the Frame draws it (`bars`) at the Page's top left, centered on x 32, and the Page's header row (`header`, the breadcrumb) follows it on the same center line from x 56. - What docks is decided by the layout resolver (`./frameLayout`) from the Frame's own width: from 1024 the Sidebar docks (240, in flow); under 1024 it never docks. - Docked, the Sidebar sits on the sunken fill with a 1px `--ds-border` on its Page-facing edge. Floating (a peek, or opened by hand under 1024) it lies over the Page on `--ds-surface-material-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay` and no Blanket. - Hovering the left edge peeks a closed Sidebar. An outside press, Escape, or the pointer leaving closes the peek. - Either toggle, or Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac), closes a showing Sidebar and opens a closed one; focus follows to the toggle that is left. - Opening a modal closes a floating Sidebar and leaves a docked one alone, and while one is open the Sidebar does not peek. The frame hears it from the shared overlay module (`@/lib/overlay`), so a page does not wire its modals to the frame. A modal opened from inside the floating Sidebar hands focus to the toggle when it closes, since its trigger left with the Sidebar. - The Panel area (`panel`) is the Frame's right-hand area. The resolver docks it beside the Page at a hairline when the content keeps 720, collapsing a default Sidebar first (and restoring it when the Panel closes); otherwise it floats over the Page on the overlay material and shadow, with no Blanket, and a press outside or Escape closes it. Under 1024 it is an overlay capped at 320, and only one overlay is open at a time; under 768 it is full width. As an overlay the Panel is modal: focus moves into it and stays there, the Page and the Sidebar under it are inert, and closing it hands focus back to what opened it. Docked or peeking it is not modal and leaves focus where it is. Its open state, dismissal and focus run on Base UI's `Dialog`, portaled into the Frame's row so a dock or overlay switch never remounts the Panel's content. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640 (never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar) by drag or keys. Width and open state are kept in sessionStorage. A modal leaves it open. Anything inside the Frame opens it through `usePanelControl`. - A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode: its steps are the rows, and the Page's footer holds the task's actions. - Landmarks: the Page is `main`; the Sidebar's `nav` is the navigation; the Panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`. - The Page pads `--page-pad` (24 at every width) and caps its content at `--content-max-width` (1232), centered (`width="full"` lifts the cap, `width="reading"` caps it at 864), on a 12-column grid with a 16 gutter. Children span all 12 columns unless they set `grid-column`.

## Usage

Use Frame for every page of the app. It owns the frame sizes and the Sidebar's behavior, so a page only supplies its Sidebar, its breadcrumb and its content.

The Frame decides what docks from its own width, not the window's, through one layout resolver, so the content never drops under 720:

- **Sidebar.** Below its docking width, opened by hand, it floats over the Page and closes on an outside press or Escape. Hovering the toggle or the left edge peeks a collapsed Sidebar over the Page with no Blanket. Clicking the toggle, or pressing Ctrl+[, closes a docked Sidebar and opens a collapsed one.
- **AI panel.** It opens from anything inside the Frame through `usePanelControl()`. Both dock when the Sidebar, the panel and the content minimum fit. Otherwise a Sidebar left open by default collapses and comes back when the panel closes. Below that, the panel floats over the Page and the Sidebar on the overlay fill and shadow, with no Blanket.
- **Narrow Frames** hold one layer open at a time: opening the Sidebar closes the panel, and opening the panel closes the Sidebar.
- **Modals.** Opening a Modal closes a peeking or floating Sidebar, and a docked Sidebar stays. While a Modal is open the Sidebar does not peek, and Escape closes the Modal only. A Modal leaves the panel open under its Blanket.

Docked, the panel meets the Page at a hairline. Its splitter resizes it from 320 to 640, but never past what keeps 720 beside a docked Sidebar. The width and whether the panel is open are kept for the tab.

## Alternatives

- For a bare fill and elevation, use `Page`.
- For a region inside the content, use `Section`.
- For a short task that keeps the page in view behind it, use `Modal`. A multi-step task runs in the Sidebar's inner mode.

## Best practices

### Give a multi-step task its steps in the inner sidebar. {#give-a-multi-step-task-its-steps-in-the-inner-sidebar}

**Checked:** Review

The steps are the Sidebar's rows, so the Page holds only the task. Done steps tick and stay pressable; steps past your answers are off. The page places the footer along the bottom today; the Frame's `bar` slot is Planned.

Do: The steps as rows in the inner sidebar; the Page holds only the task.
Don't: The steps drawn again inside the Page: two lists for one task.

### Put Save and exit, Back and Next in the footer, with no Cancel. {#put-save-and-exit-back-and-next-in-the-footer-with-no-cancel}

**Checked:** Review

The footer is fixed along the bottom, one row high, with its buttons on one line. Save and exit leaves the task and keeps the answers, so the footer holds only it, Back and the primary Next. Back on the first step is disabled and needs no reason.

Do: Save and exit as a link at the left edge; Back and the primary Next in the right half, on one line.
Don't: Cancel repeated in the footer beside Save and exit: two ways out of one task.

### Keep the AI panel docked as its own region. {#keep-the-ai-panel-docked-as-its-own-region}

**Checked:** Review

The AI panel is a region of the Frame, not a floating Panel, so it stays put as a person moves between pages. The Page makes room for it; below `FRAME_LAYOUT.dockMin` it floats over the Page, with no Blanket.

Do: The panel docked at the right edge, the Page narrowing beside it.
Don't: The panel floating over the Page, hiding the rows beneath it.

### Keep a bare Frame to one column. {#keep-a-bare-frame-to-one-column}

**Checked:** Review

Sign-in, errors and welcome have one job and no account yet, so the Frame carries no Sidebar, header row or Panel.

Do: One centered column: the form and its button.
Don't: The Sidebar beside a sign-in: navigation for a person who has not signed in.

### Put the place in the header as a breadcrumb. {#put-the-place-in-the-header-as-a-breadcrumb}

**Checked:** Review

The header row is the breadcrumb, shown only after drilling into a record; area pages and multi-step tasks have none. A page's title belongs to its content, in a Section with `level="page"`.

Elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark, and the `nav` inside the Sidebar is the navigation landmark. Pass `contentAs="div"` when the page supplies its own `main`.
- The toggle is a button. Open, it ends the Sidebar's logo row as "Close sidebar"; closed, it sits at the Page's top left as "Open sidebar". It reports whether the Sidebar is showing and announces its shortcut, Ctrl+[ (Cmd+[ on a Mac).
- A peeking or floating Sidebar closes on Escape, and focus returns to the toggle.
- Docked, the AI panel is a complementary landmark named by `panelLabel`, after the Page in reading order. Below `FRAME_LAYOUT.dockMin` it is a Modal-style layer: focus moves to its first control, Tab stays inside it, the Page and the Sidebar under it are inert, and closing returns focus to what opened it.
- The splitter is a vertical separator named "Resize panel" that reports its width. The left arrow widens the panel by 16 and the right arrow narrows it, 64 with Shift; Home and End go to the narrowest and the widest.
- A multi-step task's steps are a list named "Steps" in the Sidebar's navigation; the current step is marked, a done step is named "Done", and an off step is not pressable. The footer's buttons follow the body in the tab order.

### Default

The default type at 1440 with the AI panel docked.

1. **Sidebar.** 240 wide, docked from 1024, with the toggle ending its logo row.

- For content read beside the page, use `Panel`.
- For a short aside off a control, use `Popup`.
- For a long or stepped task, use `Frame`.
- For a passing notice, use `Flag`.

## Best practices

### Open a Modal only from a person's action. {#open-a-modal-only-from-a-person-s-action}

**Checked:** Review

A button, a link, an icon. Never on its own.

Do: Open a Modal when a person clicks an action or trigger.

Don't: Open a Modal automatically on page load.

### Size a confirm at the smallest step and step up with a detail line or a field. {#size-a-confirm-at-the-smallest-step-and-step-up-with-a-detail-line-or-a-field}

**Checked:** Review

A confirm takes 4-col or 6-col; a short form is 8-col; a table, editor or steps is 10-col. Choose width by task.

Do: A confirm at the narrow step: the title, one line and two buttons.
Don't: The same confirm at a wide step: empty width around one line, picked to make it look a certain way.

### Confirm inside the Modal, and never open a Modal on another Modal. {#confirm-inside-the-modal-and-never-open-a-modal-on-another-modal}

**Checked:** Automatic

Stacking holds the rule. The overlay module keeps a second Modal closed and calls its `onClose`.

Do: One Modal that confirms inside itself, with a message and its own buttons.
Don't: A Modal opened on another Modal, a second Blanket dimming the first.

### Scroll the body between a fixed header and footer. {#scroll-the-body-between-a-fixed-header-and-footer}

**Checked:** Automatic

Each width has a maximum height, the screen less `--blanket-pad-y` above and below. Header and footer are pinned and the footer never moves. Actions never sit in the body, which scrolls away; a missing-field error shows on the field and the body scrolls to it, and a rejected submit shows its message at the top of the body.

Do: Past the cap the body scrolls; the footer stays pinned with its buttons.
Don't: The button inside the scrolling body: it scrolls out of reach.

### Use tabs for views, not steps. {#use-tabs-for-views-not-steps}

**Checked:** Review

Two to five views of one thing opened in any order; one footer saves them all. Views in order are Steps, with Back and Next in the footer.

Do: Views in order are Steps: Back and Next split across the footer.
Don't: Numbered tabs as steps: any order, one Save, nothing to go back to.

Footer buttons, real actions and Close, and which destructive tier, including type the name: Common actions. A blocked submit: Forms. The sending button: Loading.

## Accessibility

- The Modal is a dialog named by its title, which is its h1; a Section inside opens at h2. A Modal with a custom header needs its own name.
- Focus moves into the Dialog on open (to the first input or control) and stays trapped until it closes, while the page behind stops scrolling. Escape, Close and the Blanket close it, and focus returns to what opened it.
- Set `blanket="static"` (or `false`) for an inline confirmation of a destructive action so a stray click outside does not abandon it.
- A body that scrolls is a tab stop. With tabs, Left and Right move between tabs and the panel is named by its tab.
- A blocked submit announces the first error; with reduced motion the color, icon, message and focus move carry it without the shake.
- Close is named "Close". The Danger button in a type-the-name confirm stays disabled until the name matches, and the caption carries the reason.

## Related

- Dialog: use when drawing the dialog panel itself with no Blanket or modal behavior, such as in docs and mockups.
- Forms: use when the Modal holds fields.
- Panel: use when the page must stay usable.
- Popup: use when the content is a menu or a short list.
- Patterns: use when you need the rules across Modals: Common actions, Forms, Errors, Loading.

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Section` · `Table`

## Types

Picked by what the person has to do. The Dialog component page holds the panel's props and states; these are the filled Modal layouts.

- **Passive.** Information only, with Close. No footer.
- **Active.** A choice, a confirm or a short form. Discard (or a real alternative) and the action; no Cancel.
- **Acknowledge.** One thing to read and one button that fills the footer.
- **Steps.** A short sequence at 10-col: Back and Next, split 50/50.

## Anatomy

An Active Modal at 8-col with a short form. Every part once; the pad is 20 on every side, the radius 16, and the parts sit 16 apart.

1. **Blanket.** Dims the page and holds the Modal centered.
2. **Header.** The title at 20/24, whatever the level around it, and the Close icon button. With tabs, the tab group sits 8 under the title.
3. **Body.** Text, a list, fields or a table. It scrolls past the cap and never draws under 96 tall.
4. **Footer** (optional). Full-bleed buttons; secondary (Default) left, Primary right. A declining action such as "Not now" is the secondary. Close in the header dismisses, so no Cancel.

## Slots

```jsx
import { Modal } from '@/templates';
import { Button } from '@/components';
```

`Modal` places `Dialog` (`@/components`) on the Blanket with Base UI portal, focus trap, Escape, scroll lock and focus return.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title a confirm with the question: "Delete this session?" | "Are you sure?" or "Warning". |
| Give the consequence in one line: "This cannot be undone." | A paragraph that repeats the title. |
| Name the action after the question: "Delete session". | "OK" or "Yes". |
| On the last step, name Next after the outcome: "Schedule". | "Finish". |

# Page

The Page surface: paints `--ds-surface` edge to edge with `--page-pad` (24) on every side and no radius, border, or shadow; children fill the content slot. A Page can carry its `title`: the page's one h1, at Heading/large 24, above the content. Sections inside it open at h2.

Also asked as: surface.

**Import:** `import { Page } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Frame (`ds guide frame`); Modal (`ds guide modal`); Page (`ds guide page`); Panel (`ds guide panel`); Popup (`ds guide popup`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Disabled (`ds guide disabled`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Errors (`ds guide errors`); Forms (`ds guide forms`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); +1 more

## Usage

Use Page for the content of every default Frame. It carries the page header, the one h1, and the Sections under it. The default type caps the grid at 1232; full width is for a page that fills the window, such as chat, a board or a wide table; reading caps it at 864 for text people read through.

## Motion

Page reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| title | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The header is scroll-linked: the small title fades in at the end of the Breadcrumb row, its opacity mapped to the next 24 px of scroll. No spring, no timer, no snap when scrolling stops. |
| anchor | Scroll to a spot on the page | `--ds-motion-linear` | The actions and the tabs ride up with the page and anchor: the actions at the end of the Breadcrumb row, the tabs under it. One copy of every control. |
| tabs-shadow | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The tabs' shadow appears when they stick, a single moment. In Reduced mode nothing changes: every movement is the person's own scroll. |

## Alternatives

- For one task that takes the whole window, use `Frame`.
- For a region of the page with its own heading, use `Section`.
- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.

## Best practices

### Make the page header the page's one h1. {#make-the-page-header-the-page-s-one-h1}

**Checked:** Automatic

A Section never stands in for it. Sections inside open at h2.

Do: The page header is the one h1; the Section under it opens at h2.
Don't: Sections standing in for the page title: two page-title-sized headings and no page header.

### Show the breadcrumb by the Navigation pattern. {#show-the-breadcrumb-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

When it shows and what it holds: the Navigation pattern.

Do: An area page: the title alone.
Don't: A breadcrumb on a top-level area page, repeating the Sidebar's place.

### Place page actions and the add action by the Navigation pattern. {#place-page-actions-and-the-add-action-by-the-navigation-pattern}

**Checked:** Review

Page actions sit at the end of the title row and are about the page only. Where an add action goes: the Navigation pattern.

Do: "Add" is the Section's one action, in its title row; the page header carries only page actions.
Don't: The same Primary twice: in the page header and in the Section's title row.

### Keep the description to one line. {#keep-the-description-to-one-line}

**Checked:** Review

Anything longer moves into the first Section.

Do: One detail line under the title.
Don't: A paragraph under the title pushes the first Section down.

### Keep one tab system per page. {#keep-one-tab-system-per-page}

**Checked:** Review

The rule and its reasons: the Navigation pattern. Page tabs name views of one subject; the Section's views become one labeled PopupSelect.

Do: Under page tabs the Section's views are one labeled PopupSelect in its views row.
Don't: Pill views under page tabs: two tab systems on one page.

### Shrink the scrolled header to one sticky row. {#shrink-the-scrolled-header-to-one-sticky-row}

**Checked:** Review

The breadcrumb with the title at its end, then the page actions; page tabs stick under it. The Section header rows scroll away. This state is planned.

### Show one banner at a time, scrolling with the content. {#show-one-banner-at-a-time-scrolling-with-the-content}

**Checked:** Review

Which tier a message belongs to: the Notifications pattern.

## Accessibility

- The Page is the `main` landmark. Its header's title is the one h1; Sections open at h2.
- The breadcrumb is a `nav` named "Breadcrumb".
- Page tabs are a tablist; the selected tab names its panel. Views swap in place and are announced.
- The StatusTag is text, never color alone.
- A title that truncates keeps its full text in a Tooltip on hover and focus.
- Text on a Page uses `--ds-text` at every level, in every color mode.

## Related

- Frame: use when deciding which type the page sits in.
- Section: use when a region needs its own heading, views or detail.
- Card: use when one object has a shape already agreed.
- Patterns: use when deciding where a breadcrumb or a tab belongs (Navigation), or choosing the StatusTag beside the title (Indicators).

## Types

- **Default.** The content grid, centered and capped at its content width. Nearly every page.
- **Full width.** The content runs to the pad with no cap, for a page that fills it, such as chat, a board or a wide table.
- **Reading.** The grid capped at 864, the readable measure: training lessons, help articles and policies. A multi-step task and sign-in use it too.

The Frame's `width` sets the type: `default`, `full` or `reading`.

## Anatomy

A record page one level down shows every header slot, with markers in the gutter beside each part.

1. **Breadcrumb** (optional). The record's parents on their own row, above the title.
2. **Title.** The page's one h1, with its StatusTag after the text when the page is one record.
3. **Description** (optional). One line under the title.
4. **Page actions** (optional). At the end of the title row, about the page only.
5. **Page tabs** (optional). At the bottom of the header; they switch the whole page.
6. **Banner** (optional). Under the header, one at a time.
7. **Content.** Sections on the grid, under the header.

## Usage

Use `Section` when content has a heading, shares actions, shows or hides as a unit, or takes its own span of the grid; otherwise the content belongs to the Section above it. The header is the Section's, not the Table's: the title row names it and carries its actions, and the header rows under it hold the views, then Search and the filters, so switching views can swap a table for cards while the rows stay put.

A Section takes no fill and no pad, and has five parts: header, body, side, detail and footer. The detail is an inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down.

## Motion

Section reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| view-bar | Swap content in place | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Title row: nothing moves. The selected pill's fill and the format switch's indicator glide while the content swaps in place. Search and the Filter count grow to the left. |
| side-open | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The side opens and collapses as a section. Below 960 it hides with no animation. |
| side-close | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Collapses back the same way. Below 960 the side is gone in the same frame, with no animation. |
| detail | Expand and collapse | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. |
| body | Load content | `--ds-motion-spatial-fast` · `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Content loads on arrival; add or remove, reorder and swap content as it changes. |
| footer | Step to the next or previous | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | Paging is Step. |

## Alternatives

- For one object with an agreed shape, use `Card` inside a Section.
- For a queue page or a quick look at a row from a table, use `Panel`.
- For the page's own title, use `PageHeader`; a Section stands under it.

## Best practices

### Make a Section only when it earns one. {#make-a-section-only-when-it-earns-one}

**Checked:** Review

A Section earns its own heading, its own actions or its own place in the grid. When its heading would repeat its only card's title, drop the Section and let the card stand on its own.

Do: A card with its own title stands on its own in the page.
Don't: A Section whose heading repeats its only card's title: two headings for one thing.

### Put the title row first and the header rows under it. {#put-the-title-row-first-and-the-header-rows-under-it}

**Checked:** Automatic

The title row sits `--section-stack-sm` above the header rows, and the header sits `--section-stack-md` above the body. The title, the first pill's label and the first column's text share one left edge. Actions that do not fit beside the heading drop under it, still at the end of the row. At every width the two stay separate rows. In a narrow Section the filters fold into one Filter button and the views scroll sideways.

Do: The title row first, the header rows under it, sharing one left edge.
Don't: The title pushed into the views row: the heading and the pills fight for the start, and the description has nowhere to go.

### Give each action one home: the title row. {#give-each-action-one-home-the-title-row}

**Checked:** Review

Actions sit at the end of the title row, More then the labeled Primary, whether or not the Section has views. The views row is for views and the format switch, the third for Search and filters, so an action there is a second home.

Do: The actions at the end of the title row, with the views under it.
Don't: Add students in the title row and again in the views row: one action, two homes.

### Keep views at the start as pills that hug their labels. {#keep-views-at-the-start-as-pills-that-hug-their-labels}

**Checked:** Review

Views are a fixed set the product defines, and one pill stays even with one view. The strip stays on one line and scrolls sideways when the pills do not fit. Under page tabs, the views become one labeled PopupSelect, so the page keeps one tab system.

### Order the header: actions, then views and format, then Search and filters. {#order-the-header-actions-then-views-and-format-then-search-and-filters}

**Checked:** Review

The title row ends with More, then the labeled Primary, which is last. The views row holds the views at the start and the format switch at the end. The filters row holds a compact `SearchField` (`spacing="compact"`, and `isCollapsible` where the row is tight), then the filter triggers; a trigger that opens a list takes a `menu`. More is an Icon button with a Tooltip. Fold extras into More.

Do: More and the labeled Primary in the title row; the format switch ends the views row; Search, then the filter, lead the filters row.
Don't: Five controls in no order, the Primary first, a second labeled button and a Filter icon in the title row: fold extras into More and give the filter its own row.

### Turn the head row into the bulk bar when rows are selected. {#turn-the-head-row-into-the-bulk-bar-when-rows-are-selected}

**Checked:** Automatic

The part-ticked select-all, the count of selected rows, then the actions, all at the start. The checkboxes clear the selection, so the bar carries no Cancel. Selected rows take the selected fill and the header rows stay put. Only the Dynamic table selects rows.

### Drop the Filter icon while a filter side shows. {#drop-the-filter-icon-while-a-filter-side-shows}

**Checked:** Review

Each control has one home. The Filter button returns with its count once the side hides, below `SECTION_DETAIL_FLOOR`.

### Use a Section detail as an inline expand, never on a queue page. {#use-a-section-detail-as-an-inline-expand-never-on-a-queue-page}

**Checked:** Review

A **Section detail** is an inline expand: a row or card opens in place inside its Section and pushes the content below it down. It is never the detail view on a queue page — a queue page docks a `Panel` beside the list instead, and the record opens on demand.

### Keep the footer for paging and "View all". {#keep-the-footer-for-paging-and-view-all}

**Checked:** Review

Actions that commit changes belong in the card or form that holds the fields.

Do: The form card holds its own Save; the Section footer is for paging and "View all".
Don't: Cancel and Save in the Section footer, away from the fields they commit.

### Give a part a fill with a Card, not a Section. {#give-a-part-a-fill-with-a-card-not-a-section}

**Checked:** Review

A padded box with a fill is a Card. A Section takes no fill and no pad, so a part that stands apart from its neighbor, such as a detail, is a sunken Card.

### Nest a Section once at most. {#nest-a-section-once-at-most}

**Checked:** Review

A subsection is an h3. A Section that already has views holds subsections without them.

The table's empty state replaces the whole table, by the Empty pattern; elevation and fills follow Elevation.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading whose level follows nesting: h2 for a Section, h3 for a subsection. With a custom header the title stays in the page, hidden from sight.
- The pill views are a tablist; the selected tab says which rows the body shows. Views swap in place.
- Search, the filter triggers and More carry their names: "Search students", "Status: Upcoming", "More section actions". A trigger's selected state is announced as pressed.
- The table announces a selection politely, "2 selected", and the bulk bar's actions follow the select-all checkbox in the tab order.
- The detail is a collapsible region named by its title: the disclosure button toggles it with Enter or Space, and Escape inside the open detail closes it and returns focus to the button.

## Related

- Page: use when the heading is the page's own.
- Panel: use when a queue page docks the Panel beside the list, or for a quick look from a table.
- Popup: use when choosing the menu the labeled view trigger (`PopupSelect`) or a filter trigger opens.
- Table: use when the body is rows and columns.
- Filtering: use when picking a filter tier for the header.
- Patterns: use when the question is the search field's behavior (Search) or an empty body (Empty).

Same group: `Card` · `Frame` · `Modal` · `Page` · `Panel` · `Table`

## Types

Each Section type combines a header and body, with an optional side or detail. These are starting layouts of the same component.

- **List.** The views alone, one table, paging. The default for an area page.
- **Detail.** A list with a detail that opens an item in place.
- **Cards.** Title and actions, a grid of cards three across.
- **Stats.** A row of cards, each one number and its label, four at most.
- **Details.** Label and value pairs in two columns, with Edit in the title row.
- **Main and side.** A split with the side at the end and no fill: facts beside the main content.
- **Form.** Fields in a card, with the card's own Save and Cancel at its bottom.
- **Subsections.** Sections nested one level, each an h3, for a long settings page.

## Anatomy

A Section with its header rows, a detail and a footer. The title, the first pill and the first column share one left edge.

1. **Title row.** The h2, an optional one-line description, and the actions at the end: More and the labeled Primary.
2. **Header rows** (optional). Row 2 holds the pill views at the start and the format switch at the end. Row 3 holds Search, then the filter triggers.
3. **Body.** A Table, a card grid, a list, a form or subsections. A Table's head row follows the header rows with nothing between.
4. **Detail** (optional). An inline expand, drawn as a sunken Card, that opens in place inside the Section and pushes the content below it down. Never use it for a queue page, which docks a `Panel` beside the list.
5. **Footer** (optional). Paging or "View all".

# Table

Section header carries the title and the toolbar. Under the header come the table, then the `footer` slot (range, page size, Pagination), and the empty state box in place of both when there are no rows. The template draws no default footer: the slot is the contract. Pass the table as `children` (a `StaticTable`, `DynamicTable` or `TreeTable`), or name a `kind` and pass its props as `tableProps`. Choose the kind by what people do with the rows: nesting is a Tree table; sort, filter, select, page, expand or row actions is a Dynamic table; otherwise it is a Static table. A Dynamic or Tree table already draws its own footer and empty state, so the template's `footer`, `emptyState` and `empty` serve a Static table and are not drawn around the other two. Every other prop goes to the Section (`title`, `description`, `actions`, `views`, `search`, `filters`).

Also asked as: list of records, data table on a page, sortable list, records with filters, rows and columns, grid, table pattern.

**Import:** `import { Table } from '@/templates';`

**Used in:** Modal (`ds guide modal`); Section (`ds guide section`); Table (`ds guide table`)

**Governed by:** Common actions (`ds guide common-actions`); Empty (`ds guide empty`); Filtering (`ds guide filtering`); Indicators (`ds guide indicators`); Loading (`ds guide loading`); Navigation (`ds guide navigation`); Notifications (`ds guide notifications`); Overflow (`ds guide overflow`); Search (`ds guide search`)

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/templates/Table/Table.mdx`

**Motion:** selection `appearance.fast`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations › Expression › Motion.

## Usage

A table sits in a Section and spans it. Its first and last cells sit flush with the section edge. The Section header carries the views, then Search and the "Field: value" filters, and once a filter is applied, the record count. The bulk bar is never in the Section header: while rows are selected, a Dynamic table's head row becomes it, so the header rows stay put. Empty and no results replace the whole table so the Section header stays usable; loading and error states happen inside the table, under its header. Paging stays under the rows, inside the same Section.

### Type guidance

Choose by what people do with the rows. Read the questions in order and stop at the first yes.

| Question | Type |
| --- | --- |
| Does any row nest under another? Nesting wins, even when the table is interactive. | Tree table |
| Can people act on the table: sort, filter, select, page, expand rows or use row actions? | Dynamic table |
| Otherwise, people only read it. | Static table |

Search, filters and actions sit in the Section header: `<Table title="Students" views={...} search={...} filters={[...]} count="340 students" kind="dynamic" tableProps={...} />`. Pass the table as `children` instead of `kind` when you build it yourself.

## Motion

Table reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| selection | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | Ticking a row turns the head row into the bulk bar: labels cross-fade, same row, same height, nothing slides. Selected rows take the selected fill. The view bar above never moves. |

## Best practices

### Put a plain table in a Section. {#put-a-plain-table-in-a-section}

Do: The table spans the Section under its header: no frame, no card, no padding of its own.
Don't: The table sits inside its own frame with padding; it stops lining up with the Section and the Section header.

### Put nothing between the header and the head row. {#put-nothing-between-the-header-and-the-head-row}

Do: Search and filters live in the Section header rows, with the record count once a filter is applied; the head row follows directly.
Don't: A second toolbar sits between the Section header and the head row; the table has no toolbar of its own.

### One table per block. {#one-table-per-block}

Never mix a Static, Dynamic or Tree table in one Section either.

Do: One table per Section, with its own header, so people always know which rows its Search and filters act on.
Don't: Two tables share one Section and one header; search and filters no longer say which table they act on.

### Use a Dynamic table for rows people act on. {#use-a-dynamic-table-for-rows-people-act-on}

Do: A roster people act on as a Dynamic table: sortable heads, checkboxes, a pager, and bulk actions in the head row while rows are selected.
Don't: A roster people act on as a Static table; with no sort, selection or paging, 340 students become one long scroll.

### Use a Tree table for a hierarchy. {#use-a-tree-table-for-a-hierarchy}

Do: Classes nest under their school and students under their class; each level indents and keeps the columns.
Don't: A hierarchy faked with expandable rows: the classes and students lose their columns and can't be sorted or selected.

## Accessibility

- Name every column with a head cell. Head cells are labels for a column, so they use Heading/xxs rather than a heading level.
- Mark the sorted column with `aria-sort`, and give every icon-only control a name, such as "Actions for Ava Thompson".
- Mark a selected row with `aria-selected="true"`. That attribute belongs to a row of a table with `role="grid"`.
- Selection is never color alone. The row's checkbox is checked, and the head row says "2 selected".
- A region that scrolls takes keyboard focus, so people can scroll it without a pointer. That covers a region with `maxHeight` and one with a sticky column.
- When empty, the empty state replaces the table with no table roles left behind, and keeps the table's accessible name when one was provided.
- Name the table with its `label`, or `label` on the template for the empty state box, when no caption names it.

## Related

## Parts

1. **Head row.** Names the columns. Its rule is the bold border.
2. **Rows.** The data you pass as `tbody`. Each draws a thin rule, and there is no zebra striping.
3. **Footer** (optional). The `footer` slot under the rows, aligned to the end: the range, the page-size Select and Pagination. The template draws no default footer: the slot is the contract. On a narrow screen its parts wrap onto lines of their own, and the pager stays at the end. It hides while the empty state shows. A Dynamic or Tree table draws its own footer and empty state, so the template's `footer`, `emptyState` and `empty` are for a Static table.
4. **Empty state.** The `emptyState` slot, which replaces the whole table (head row, caption and footer included) when `empty` is true; with `empty` and no `emptyState`, the table renders normally.

### States

Row states are layered over each cell's fill, never swapped for it.

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | No fill of its own: the table shows what it sits on. |
| Hovered | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | The row takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-pressed`. |
| Focused | A scroll region takes keyboard focus and draws the `--ds-border-focused` ring. |
| Disabled | A table has no disabled state. Disable the controls in a row. |
| Selected | A row with `aria-selected="true"` takes `--ds-background-selected` across the whole row, with `-hovered` and `-pressed` steps and no stripe on its leading edge. |
| Empty | The empty state replaces the whole table; no head row or footer stays. |

rules.ds/no-unknown-component:
## ds/no-unknown-component

**fail.** A name imported from a public barrel (`@/components` or `@/templates`) that the barrel does not export, or `<DS.Name>` through a namespace import of one. A real component or template imported from the wrong barrel fails too, and its fix is the import line it belongs on.

Write a component listed in `design-system/agent-views/components/index.md`. When none fits, propose a new component instead of naming one.
rules.ds/no-unknown-prop:
## ds/no-unknown-prop

**fail.** On a design-system component or template (`Card`, `Frame` and the rest), a prop its manifest record does not list, or a literal value for an enum prop outside its list.

Use a prop from the record in `components.json` (or the component's generated doc, or the template's Storybook page). Every component also takes `key`, `ref`, `children`, `className`, `style`, `id`, `role`, `title`, `tabIndex`, `aria-*` and `data-*`. A value written as an expression (`appearance={tone}`) is not judged, and neither is a component whose record has `props: null`.
rules.ds/no-unknown-token:
## ds/no-unknown-token

**fail.** A `var(--name)` that no token, and no file under `design-system/src`, `prototypes` or `src`, declares; or a retired token name nothing declares any more.

Use the suggested token. A prototype may declare its own custom property (`--my-gap: var(--stack-md);`) and read it.
rules.ds/placement:
## ds/placement

**fail.** A component placed inside a slot or container where a template specifies a different control. Rows derive from slot acceptance metadata (`design-system/agent-views/_slots.json`): a row names the components a slot rejects and the ones it takes instead. No template registers such a row today, so `_slots.json` is empty and the only rows are the hand-kept ones below.

Hand-kept rows with `before` (`_placements.json`) check direct JSX siblings: a `Banner` before a `PageHeader` belongs in Page's `banner` slot, below its `header` (Notifications). This row remains **warn**.

Use the component the template names and read the guide the fix points to.
